dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Chemistry appears at three points in an Al Sufouh family's school life, and each sits differently in the week. The notes below separate them by how much weekly time each actually demands, because that is the planning constraint rather than difficulty.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: The current chemistry guide organises content into structure and reactivity units: models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, classification of matter, what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Standard and Higher Level share a core with Higher Level extending several units. Assessment is Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, and the scientific investigation at twenty.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Sufouh the Diploma chemistry set is often small enough that Standard and Higher Level students share a teacher and the Higher Level extension is delivered in extra sessions. That matters for scheduling: a Higher Level student may already be giving up a lunch hour or an after-school slot to the school, and a tutoring session has to sit outside that rather than compete with it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than papers: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science, each marked out of eight. MYP 4 and 5 chemistry introduces the quantitative work that the Diploma builds on, and the inquiring-and-designing criterion is the direct ancestor of the Diploma investigation's research design.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in this catchment finish the school day at a similar hour to Diploma students but carry fewer evening commitments, which makes a four or half past four slot genuinely available. That is the age at which a weekly chemistry habit is easiest to establish, and it is also the cheapest time to establish it.

programmes.name: IGCSE chemistry into Diploma chemistry
programmes.description: Students arriving from Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 have met moles, bonding, rates and organic chemistry in a form rewarding recall and single-step calculation. Diploma chemistry asks for multi-step reasoning, uncertainty treatment and explanation that connects a model to an observation. The gap shows first in energetics and in anything requiring a mechanism rather than a product.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's UK-curriculum schools hold 37 per cent of private enrolment against 7 per cent for the International Baccalaureate, so the IGCSE-to-Diploma crossover is routine here. Year 11 students have a lighter evening than Diploma students, which is why the transition is best supported in the summer before Year 12 rather than during it.

programmes.name: The Diploma core competing for the same evenings
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service run alongside the six subjects and occupy exactly the hours a tutoring session wants. A student writing a chemistry Extended Essay is carrying independent research on top of the scientific investigation, and the two have separate school deadlines that rarely sit kindly together.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh Diploma students typically hold an activity commitment immediately after school. Mapping the core deadlines onto the tutoring calendar in the first month of Year 12 is what prevents a family paying for sessions in weeks when the student has three other submissions due.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the subject here, and the entries below are what Al Sufouh families most often request alongside it, with a note on the weekly time each actually takes. Timetable load is the deciding factor in whether one tutor or two is sensible.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity units assessed by two papers and a scientific investigation. The reliable losses are energetics sign conventions, equilibrium questions answered qualitatively where a calculation was wanted, and organic responses that name a product without giving a mechanism. Higher Level depth in reactivity and in the mechanisms unit is where generalist science tutors most often stop.

subjects.name: Chemistry Paper 1, data-based section
subjects.description: Presents unfamiliar data and asks for processing and interpretation rather than recall. Students who revise content alone meet it unprepared. It is also among the most trainable parts of the course, because the required moves recur: identify the variable, read a gradient with units, decide whether a point is anomalous, and state what the uncertainty does to the conclusion.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Frequently taken with chemistry by students heading towards medicine or life sciences. It shares the investigation structure and the four assessment criteria, so good practice transfers. Content overlap is thin, so two subjects normally means two tutors, and the weekly load of two science investigations in the same term is a real scheduling problem.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Taken with chemistry by engineering-bound students. The shared ground is uncertainty handling, graph work and proportional reasoning rather than content. A student losing marks to units and precision in both subjects has one problem appearing twice, which can be closed once if the tutor teaches both.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Chemistry assumes logarithms for pH work, rearrangement for the gas and equilibrium expressions, and comfort with proportional reasoning throughout. A student fluent in a maths lesson who stalls when the same manipulation appears inside a chemistry question has a transfer problem, and that is a specific and short piece of work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A workable pairing with chemistry, though it spends less time on algebraic manipulation than the chemistry calculations assume. Students on this route taking Higher Level chemistry usually need some explicit algebra support that the mathematics course itself will not supply.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Taken alongside or instead of a second science by some Al Sufouh students. It carries its own internal assessment and its own deadlines, which is relevant to the calendar rather than to the chemistry. Where a student holds this and chemistry, the two coursework cycles should be mapped before either begins.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The natural sciences are one of the areas of knowledge TOK examines, and chemistry students are often asked to write about models and evidence. A tutor can discuss knowledge questions and interrogate an argument's structure, and cannot write the essay or the exhibition commentary. That boundary is stated before any work starts.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in chemistry
subjects.description: Independent research with its own criteria and word limit, supervised by a school-appointed supervisor. A tutor may discuss feasibility, question the scope of a research question and give feedback on the student's own draft, and may not write, draft or complete it. The student signs any authenticity declaration the school requires.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school alongside the licensed international curriculum, including IB Diploma schools. KHDA calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes, which is part of why the school day ends when it does.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-sufouh.regionsTitle: The communities Al Sufouh chemistry students commute from
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-sufouh.regionsIntro: Each note below is about the journey and the hour, because those are what decide whether a weekly chemistry slot survives a term in this part of Dubai.

Students attending a school in the same strip can be home within fifteen minutes, which makes a half past four start genuinely workable once an activity commitment is accounted for.

regions.note: Apartments and university campuses, with households where both parents commonly work past five. The practical slot here is seven or later, fixed to the same evening each week, because an inconsistent time is what ends arrangements rather than difficulty with the subject.

regions.note: Workday-dominated apartment blocks immediately inland. Students travelling back here after an after-school commitment are rarely settled before six. A half past six slot is realistic; a four o'clock slot is theoretical and should not be agreed just because it is offered.

regions.note: Similar to Media City in rhythm, with the added friction of the Sheikh Zayed Road interchanges at the evening peak. Families here benefit most from a fixed online slot, because a session that depends on a journey depends on the junction.

regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, with the American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy and Kings' School Al Barsha. The ten-minute hop looks trivial and is not at five o'clock on a Sunday, which is the slot families most often try first and abandon.

regions.note: Compact low-rise communities with Regent International School inside the Greens. Short internal journeys make an early slot possible, so this is one of the few parts of the catchment where a five o'clock chemistry session is realistic on most weeks.

regions.note: Dense towers with limited access roads and heavy evening congestion. The failure mode here is a lost session rather than an unavailable tutor, and a session lost to traffic is frequently still a session billed when a tutor has already travelled.

regions.note: Inland villa districts served by Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. Distances between villas cap a visiting tutor at two students an evening, which is why a late slot here is both scarce and expensive when bought in person.

American and British curricula dominate, with several schools running the IB Diploma alongside the main pathway. schoolClusters.note: Inland of the Greens, drawing from the Springs, the Meadows, the Lakes and Emirates Hills. Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills has run the Diploma for many years. Journey times from here into the coastal strip are the longest in this catchment at the evening peak.

This is the format chemistry needs most, because the subject is cumulative and a fortnight lost mid-topic is not a fortnight's worth of damage. Choosing a later, defendable hour beats choosing an earlier, optimistic one.

sections.heading: The Al Sufouh school run, mapped onto bookable hours
paragraphs: The table below is the practical core of this page. It maps the communities an Al Sufouh chemistry student travels between against the hour a session can realistically begin. End-of-day times vary by school, by phase and by term, so the finish column is a typical band for a Dubai secondary day rather than a statement about a named school, and your own school's calendar is the authority. What does not vary much is the shape: the bell, then an activity or clinic, then the journey, then food, then a usable hour.

Reading the table, two things become obvious. The first is that the slot most families try first, somewhere around four o'clock, works properly only for students who finish early and live within the coastal strip. Everyone else is agreeing to a time that will hold for a few weeks and then start slipping. The second is that the hour which actually works for most of this catchment, between half past six and eight, is exactly the hour a visiting tutor is least able to supply, because their day has already ended with a drive.

The right way to use this is to pick the latest hour the student will still be functional at, not the earliest hour that is free. A Diploma student doing chemistry at four o'clock after a full day and a fixture is present but not learning, and the session gets paid for anyway. A student doing chemistry at half past seven, having eaten, with the school's own notes open, is a different student. Families often resist the later slot because it feels like it intrudes on the evening, and then lose the arrangement entirely two months later.

Ramadan reshapes this whole table for a month, and it falls inside the UAE academic year. School hours shorten and evening study migrates to after Iftar. Sessions can move to a post-Iftar time for the month and move back afterwards, and agreeing that in advance rather than improvising it mid-month is what protects the investigation timetable, which is the part of Diploma chemistry least able to absorb three disrupted weeks.

sections.heading: Which schools Al Sufouh feeds, and what they actually sit
paragraphs: Al Sufouh is a narrow strip with an unusually dense school supply for its size. Dubai College sits inside it, running the British pathway. GEMS Wellington International School sits inside it, offering the IB Diploma alongside a British route. Regent International School sits just along in the Greens, and Emirates International School in Jumeirah draws from the same side of town. Across Sheikh Zayed Road, within fifteen minutes in reasonable traffic, are the American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Al Mawakeb School Al Barsha. Inland sit Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills.

That mix matters for a chemistry parent in a specific way. The schools in this catchment sit students for different qualifications, so a neighbour's chemistry experience may not be your child's. One street can contain a Diploma Higher Level chemistry student, an A Level chemistry student and an American-track student taking a different course entirely. Asking what a neighbour's tutor is like is useful; assuming the tutor is teaching your child's course is not.

The Diploma sets in this area tend to be small, which has two consequences worth planning for. The first is that Standard and Higher Level chemistry students often share a teacher, with the Higher Level extension content delivered in additional sessions outside the main timetable. A Higher Level student may therefore already be giving up a lunchtime or an after-school hour to the school. A tutoring slot has to sit outside that rather than compete with it.

The second is that a small set can be short of a specialism in any given year. A school may be strong across the sciences and thin in one unit of the chemistry guide, usually the mechanisms or the energetics material, simply because of who is teaching it that year. That is the situation in which private support is genuinely useful, and it is also a situation a parent can check cheaply by asking the student which topic the class as a whole found hardest. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment, so Diploma sets everywhere in the emirate are smaller than British-curriculum sets.

sections.heading: The chemistry topics that need consecutive weeks
paragraphs: Chemistry is not uniformly cumulative. Some topics can be picked up in a single session and parked: naming conventions, basic stoichiometry practice, a specific calculation type. Others collapse if the weekly slot is unreliable, because each session depends on the previous one being fresh. Knowing which is which is how a family decides whether a four o'clock slot that holds two weeks in three is acceptable, and for the topics in the table below it is not.

Energetics is the clearest case. Sign conventions, enthalpy cycles and the relationship between bond enthalpies and reaction enthalpies form a single chain of reasoning, and a student who meets the second half of it a fortnight after the first half will reconstruct the wrong version. Equilibrium behaves the same way: the qualitative reasoning and the quantitative expression have to be learned together, or a student ends up able to predict a shift and unable to calculate one.

Organic mechanisms are the most unforgiving. The difference between a student who can name a product and one who can explain a mechanism is a set of habits built over consecutive attempts: identifying the electron-rich and electron-poor sites, drawing curly arrows that start and end in defensible places, and recognising a reaction type rather than memorising a transformation. Spread that over interrupted weeks and the student retains a list of names, which is what most Standard Level candidates arrive at the paper with.

The planning consequence is practical. Book the consecutive-week topics into a clear stretch of the school calendar, away from mock weeks and away from the scientific investigation's internal deadline, and protect them. Leave the single-session topics for the weeks when the calendar is messy. A tutor who will not plan with you at this level of detail is a tutor who will be surprised by February, and so will you.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys in this catchment
paragraphs: Al Sufouh families comparing an in-home chemistry quote with an online one are usually comparing similar money. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel at Bestimate, with independently advertised home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. The online specialist band is AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted from AED 200 for IB at Unitors. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED, and the budget end of the market advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Every one of those is a market figure published by the provider named and read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price.

Since the bands overlap, the useful question is what the travel component is purchasing. Honestly: a person in the room, and the last hour of the tutor's working day. That is the trade. A visiting tutor who finishes at Al Barsha at six is not starting in Al Sufouh at half past six, and the slot that most of this catchment can actually protect, between half past six and eight, is the slot their day has already spent. The premium therefore buys presence at an hour that is often not the hour you need.

There is a second cost that does not appear in the rate at all: fragility. One closure on Al Sufouh Road, one long evening at the Sheikh Zayed interchanges, and the session is cancelled, shortened or rescheduled, and when a tutor has already travelled a cancelled session is frequently still billed. Across a two-year chemistry course a family losing four sessions a term to logistics loses a topic, and for the topics in the previous table losing a topic is not a linear loss.

Presence is still worth buying for some students, and that should be said plainly rather than argued away. A younger student who will not engage with a screen, or a household where supervision is the real requirement, is buying something real. For a sixteen or seventeen year old working through an enthalpy cycle, a shared screen holding the question, the markscheme and the student's own working is frequently the better tool. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai and does not dispatch tutors to UAE addresses; home visiting is an India-only service, and families who need presence should hire locally for it.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and when it has to happen
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent of the chemistry grade and is assessed on four criteria, each worth six marks for a total of twenty-four: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Its deadlines are set by the school, not by a published general calendar, which is why the first thing to ask the DP coordinator is when the internal deadlines fall. A support plan built against a guessed date collides with the school's calendar in the worst possible term.

The equal weighting across the four criteria is what students most often fail to act on. Effort concentrates on getting data, which sits inside one criterion, while evaluation carries exactly the same six marks and is far more improvable. In chemistry specifically, evaluation marks go begging because students write about equipment accuracy and ignore the chemistry: whether the reaction went to completion, whether a side reaction competed, whether the assumption that heat loss was negligible actually held in their set-up.

Research design is the other criterion where chemistry students lose avoidable marks, usually by choosing a research question that cannot be answered with the equipment a school laboratory holds. A tutor can test that before any data is collected, which is a short conversation that saves a term. Laboratory work itself belongs to the school, with its equipment, technician support and supervision requirement, and no tutoring arrangement should claim to replace it.

The boundary is firm and it should be stated to the student before any work starts. A tutor may discuss candidate research questions and say which will not generate enough usable data, question whether a method controls what it claims to, ask what the uncertainty implies for the conclusion, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or produce the investigation, and should not edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. Where a school requires an authenticity declaration, the candidate signs it. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which places a malpractice exposure on the student rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: Mock weeks, the UAE calendar and the weeks not to book
paragraphs: A chemistry support plan that ignores the school calendar will buy sessions in the worst weeks of the year. There are three predictable collisions in this catchment and all three are avoidable with one conversation in September.

The first is mock weeks. A school running mocks across two weeks will take the student's evenings for revision across four subjects at once, and a chemistry session dropped into the middle of that is a session the student cannot prepare for. The sensible pattern is to front-load chemistry work in the fortnight before mocks and to pause or lighten during them, rather than to pay the same weekly fee for a session nobody can use.

The second is Ramadan, which falls within the UAE academic year. School hours shorten, and evening study moves to after Iftar. Sessions can shift to a post-Iftar slot for the month. What breaks plans is improvising this in the second week rather than agreeing it in advance, because a month of missed or half-attended sessions in the middle of the course lands exactly where the consecutive-week topics sit.

The third is the scientific investigation's internal deadline, which the school sets. In the three or four weeks before it, a Diploma chemistry student is doing coursework rather than content, and a tutoring session should follow them into the coursework rather than continuing to deliver the syllabus. Families who do not plan for this end up paying for content sessions the student is too busy to absorb, and then paying again for coursework support after the deadline has passed, which is the most avoidable double cost in the whole arrangement.
bullets: Front-load before mock weeks; pause or lighten during them
Agree post-Iftar timing before Ramadan rather than during it

sections.heading: Checking a chemistry tutor before the first session
paragraphs: Three checks, none of which costs anything, and all of which matter more than a credential list. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

A linked point about school staff, which matters in a catchment where everybody knows which teacher is strong. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against current policy, but the direction is clear: arranging for your child's own chemistry teacher to tutor them privately for money is arranging something the teacher may not be permitted to do.

The second check is the guide. Ask whether the tutor is teaching the current chemistry guide with its structure and reactivity organisation, or the previous syllabus with its separate options. A tutor planning against a structure that no longer exists will cover material the papers no longer ask for, and that is a term of paid sessions pointed at the wrong target. A tutor who has taught the current guide will describe the units without being prompted.

The third is the claim set. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB, from Cambridge, from Pearson, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and claims none. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Any provider calling itself approved by a regulator or a board should be asked to produce the permit or centre number. Nobody should be described as an IB examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be presented as access to marking or boundaries.

sections.heading: Why the slot matters more than the tutor's rate
paragraphs: This page has argued the timetable before the chemistry, and the reason is arithmetic rather than preference. A weekly session that holds for thirty-two weeks of an academic year delivers thirty-two hours. The same session at an optimistic four o'clock, holding two weeks in three once fixtures and traffic are counted, delivers twenty-one. The difference is eleven hours, which at the mid-market band is between AED 1,650 and AED 3,300 of value either delivered or not, and the price per hour was identical in both cases.

Chemistry punishes that unreliability more than most subjects because of the consecutive-week topics. Energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases and organic mechanisms each need three to six sessions in successive weeks, and a plan that drops one week in three will never complete any of them cleanly. The student ends up with partial versions of four chains of reasoning, which is a worse position than having completed two of them properly.

So the sequence a family should follow is: find the hour, then find the tutor. Pick the latest hour the student will still function at, after the activity commitment and the journey and food. Protect it in the calendar the way a school lesson is protected. Then look for somebody who teaches the current guide at the right level and is free at that hour. Doing it the other way round produces a good tutor in an impossible slot, which is the commonest failure in this catchment.

Online delivery is simply what makes the right hour purchasable. Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and an eight o'clock session costs nothing extra to supply because nobody is driving to it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is offered only in India. For a Diploma chemistry student in Al Sufouh, that is less a feature than the reason the plan survives to May.

process.title: Write down the real end of the school day
process.description: Note when the bell goes, what happens in the hour afterwards, how long the journey home takes at the peak, and when the student has eaten. That sequence, not the earliest free hour a tutor offers, is what determines the slot. Five minutes with a pen saves an arrangement that would otherwise quietly stop in December.

process.title: Ask the coordinator for the internal deadlines
process.description: The DP coordinator can confirm the level your child is entered at and when the school's own internal deadlines for the scientific investigation fall. Half past seven, after food, with the school's notes open, is a different session. Families resist this and then lose the arrangement two months later.

Book it at the hour you intend to use every week, so the trial tests the real arrangement rather than a best-case version of it. If the student cannot concentrate at that hour, better to find out in the free session than in January.

faqs.question: What time does the school day end for an Al Sufouh chemistry student?
faqs.answer: Dubai secondary school days typically finish between two o'clock and half past three, varying by school, phase and term, and your own school's calendar is the authority. A Diploma student's day rarely ends at the bell: a creativity, activity and service commitment, a clinic, music or a fixture usually takes the next hour. A student living in the Al Sufouh coastal strip can be at a desk by half past four. A household in Media City or Internet City is realistically available from half past six.

faqs.question: Which hour should we actually book for a weekly chemistry session?
faqs.answer: The latest hour the student will still function at, not the earliest one available. For most of this catchment that is between half past six and eight, after the journey and after food. A four o'clock session following a full day and a fixture is attended rather than used, and it is billed either way. Online slots in Gulf Standard Time run into the evening, which is precisely the window a visiting tutor cannot usually supply because their day has ended with a drive.

faqs.question: Why does an unreliable chemistry slot cost more than a cheaper tutor would save?
faqs.answer: Because chemistry is cumulative in blocks. A weekly session holding thirty-two weeks of the year delivers thirty-two hours; the same session at an optimistic hour holding two weeks in three delivers twenty-one. At mid-market rates that gap is between AED 1,650 and AED 3,300 of value not received, at an identical hourly price. Worse, the consecutive-week topics never complete cleanly on that pattern, so the student ends with partial versions of several chains of reasoning.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics cannot survive a missed week?
faqs.answer: Energetics needs three or four successive weeks, because sign conventions and enthalpy cycles form one chain. Equilibrium needs three or four, because the qualitative and quantitative sides must be learned together. Acids, bases and pH need three to five as the logarithmic work compounds across weak acid, buffer and titration cases. Organic mechanisms need four to six, because the habits build across attempts. Stoichiometry practice and data-based technique, by contrast, survive gaps and can be parked in messy weeks.

faqs.question: Which schools does Al Sufouh feed, and do they all sit the same chemistry course?
faqs.answer: Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School sit inside Al Sufouh, with Regent International School in the Greens and Emirates International School in Jumeirah nearby. Across Sheikh Zayed Road are the American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Al Mawakeb School Al Barsha. They do not all sit the same course: one street can hold a Diploma Higher Level student, an A Level student and an American-track student. No affiliation with any named school is implied.

faqs.question: How is IB chemistry assessed under the current guide?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent and holds the extended-response work. The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent. Content is organised into structure and reactivity units rather than the separate options of the previous syllabus, which is worth checking with a prospective tutor: one planning against the retired structure will cover material the papers no longer ask for. Confirm the current detail with your school, which holds the documentation.

faqs.question: When should chemistry investigation work be scheduled?
faqs.answer: Backwards from the school's own internal deadline, which the DP coordinator sets and can confirm. In the three or four weeks before it the student is doing coursework rather than content, and sessions should follow them into the coursework. Families who do not plan for this pay for content sessions the student cannot absorb and then pay again for coursework help afterwards, which is the most avoidable double cost in the arrangement. Equal weighting across the four criteria means evaluation deserves planned time too.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium buy for a chemistry student in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: A person in the room, and the last hour of that tutor's working day. The in-home band is AED 180 to AED 350 an hour including travel at Bestimate, with independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, against AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an online specialist. Since the bands overlap, the premium is not buying better teaching. It is buying presence at an earlier hour than most of this catchment can use, plus fragility, because a cancelled session after a tutor has travelled is often still billed.

faqs.question: Can online chemistry tuition really help with an enthalpy cycle or a mechanism?
faqs.answer: Usually better than a kitchen table does. A shared screen holds the question, the markscheme and the student's own working simultaneously, curly arrows can be drawn and redrawn without reprinting, and the session can be recorded so the chain of reasoning is revisitable in revision week. What online tuition does not do is laboratory work, which belongs to the school with its equipment, technician support and supervision. Tutoring covers the design before the practical and the analysis afterwards.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan for an Al Sufouh family?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and evening study moves to after Iftar, so sessions move to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards. The thing that breaks plans is improvising this in the second week rather than agreeing it in advance, because a month of half-attended sessions lands wherever the consecutive-week topics happen to sit. Agree the Ramadan arrangement in the first month of the year, and place the energetics or mechanisms blocks away from it.

faqs.question: Should we pause chemistry tutoring during mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Usually lighten rather than continue as normal. A school running mocks over two weeks takes the student's evenings for revision across four subjects at once, and a full content session dropped into that is a session nobody can prepare for. The better pattern is to front-load chemistry in the fortnight before mocks, then use the mock period for short paper-technique work or pause entirely. Paying a normal weekly fee for an unusable session is a quiet and recurring waste.

faqs.question: Can my child's own chemistry teacher tutor them privately in the evenings?
faqs.answer: Treat it as prohibited rather than available. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported, so verify against current policy, but the direction is unambiguous. A permit-holding teacher from a different school is a straightforward arrangement.

faqs.question: Does a chemistry tutor in Dubai need a permit, and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

faqs.question: Is a Higher Level chemistry tutor different from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is worth asking directly. Standard and Higher Level share a core, so a tutor comfortable with the core teaches Standard Level well. Higher Level extends several units, with the mechanisms and the energetics material being where generalist science tutors most often stop. In a small Al Sufouh Diploma set the Higher Level extension is sometimes taught outside the main timetable, so a tutoring slot must sit outside that extra school session rather than competing with it.

faqs.question: My child can name organic products but cannot explain mechanisms. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a habit problem rather than a knowledge gap, which is why it needs consecutive weeks rather than extra reading. The work is identifying electron-rich and electron-poor sites, drawing arrows that start and end in defensible places, and recognising reaction types instead of memorising transformations. Four to six successive sessions is typical. Spread the same hours across interrupted weeks and the student returns to a list of names, which is where most candidates arrive at the paper.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free at the evening slot we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a timescale, rather than matched to a worse hour and left to discover the problem. The later Gulf Standard Time slots are the most requested in this catchment for exactly the reasons set out above. Where no suitable Higher Level match is free at that hour, the realistic options are a tutor in another time zone covering the evening, a short wait with a named date, or a single diagnostic session with a generalist to establish precisely what the specialist will be needed for.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingHeading: Fix the hour first, then book the chemistry
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: If you want an IB chemistry tutor in Al Sufouh, start with the calendar rather than the shortlist. Write down when the bell goes, what takes the hour afterwards, how long the journey home runs at the peak, and when the student has eaten. Pick the latest hour they will still function at. Ask the coordinator for the level and the investigation deadlines. Then book the free trial lesson in that exact slot, one subject, no payment taken beforehand. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: When does chemistry actually get studied in an Al Twar week?
paragraphs: Chemistry work does not arrive at a steady rate, and that is the fact most tutoring arrangements in this district ignore. School sets a problem sheet one week, a topic test the next, and a lab write-up the week after, and the lab write-up lands on top of everything else because practical work is timetabled when the laboratory is free rather than when the student has time. A fixed weekly tutoring hour dropped into that pattern is sometimes exactly what is needed and sometimes the last thing the student can face.

Layer the Al Twar geography on top. Schools in this cluster finish between roughly 2pm and 3.30pm, and Al Twar sits towards the end of most bus loops, so add thirty to forty-five minutes before counting. Changing, eating and the school's own set work take until around a quarter to five. That leaves an early window of roughly ninety minutes before the evening meal and a shorter one afterwards running to about nine. Households with a cross-district school place in Mirdif, Al Garhoud or Festival City should assume the early window does not exist.

The practical answer is to sequence rather than schedule. A chemistry tutor who knows the school's topic order can be a week ahead of the class rather than a week behind it, which converts a session from remedial into preparatory and makes the school lesson land better. That requires one piece of information most families never pass on: the scheme of work. Ask the chemistry teacher for the term's topic order. It is usually a single sheet and it changes what a tutoring hour is worth. Without it a tutor is guessing at which half of the course your child is currently in, and in this cluster that guess is wrong about as often as it is right.

The second thing worth timing deliberately is the Scientific Investigation. It carries about a fifth of the grade at both levels, it has internal deadlines set by the school rather than by the IB, and it is produced over months in a period that also contains mocks. Counting those deadlines backwards in September, rather than discovering them in February, is the difference between supervision that helps and supervision that cannot legitimately do much.

One thing to state plainly. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Chemistry tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for mechanisms, worked stoichiometry and annotated drafts. For a plan that has to flex around lab weeks and mock timetables, that matters: a session can be moved by a day at no cost to anyone, which is impossible when somebody has already set off across the city.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Two written papers plus one Scientific Investigation. Content sits under Structure, covering models of the particulate nature of matter, bonding and classification, and under Reactivity, covering energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acid-base and redox behaviour and organic mechanisms. Higher Level adds depth rather than another paper.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences before chemistry
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than by paper: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Chemistry separates into its own subject in the later years at most schools.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students arriving in DP1 chemistry in this cluster are typically strong at designing an investigation and short of calculation volume. The useful intervention is a summer block on quantitative work before DP1 starts, not a term of remedial sessions in October.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 give a sound grounding in bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases and the first organic families. Neither covers entropy, Gibbs energy, buffer calculations or mechanism arrow-pushing, which is why the first term of DP1 feels like a new subject.
programmes.countryNote: Al Twar and Al Qusais have a dense IGCSE market, so most Diploma chemistry students here arrive from Extended-tier courses. The gap that shows is quantitative rather than conceptual, and six to eight weeks of bridging work before DP1 closes most of it.

programmes.name: The Scientific Investigation
programmes.description: One independent investigation designed, performed, analysed and written up by the student, internally assessed and externally moderated, worth about a fifth of the grade at both levels. Uncertainty treatment and the evaluation drive the mark more than the topic does.
programmes.countryNote: Its deadlines are set by your school, not by the IB, and they fall in a term that already contains mocks. Getting those dates in September and working backwards is the single most useful piece of planning available to a chemistry family in this district.

subjects.name: Chemistry

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A common third subject in this cluster. Its internal assessment commentaries fall in the same window as the chemistry investigation, which is a workload fact worth planning around.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay. Chemistry supplies good material on the status of models: why the periodic table is a classification rather than a law.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: A supervised research essay whose deadlines overlap the investigation's. Scope is the usual failure: a question school apparatus cannot answer produces a literature review with measurements attached.

subjects.name: Lab report writing
subjects.description: Method, data, uncertainty, graphs and evaluation. Taught once properly it serves every write-up for two years, which makes it one of the better uses of an early session.

sections.heading: The Al Twar chemistry week, hour by hour
paragraphs: The usable window here is narrower than families plan for, and it closes from both ends. A 2.30pm finish plus a bus route through Al Qusais and Al Twar puts a student at the door around 3.15pm. Changing and eating is not optional and the school's own set work usually gets a first pass. By a quarter to five the student is available and genuinely tired, with about ninety minutes before the evening meal and a blunter window afterwards running to roughly nine.

Within that, chemistry divides neatly by task. New content and mechanism work belong in the early window, because they ask the student to construct rather than recall. Past-paper questions, stoichiometry drilling and command-term practice survive the later window perfectly well. Lab report writing sits awkwardly in both and is best handled on a weekend morning, when there is enough continuous time to do the data properly rather than in two interrupted halves.

Saturday morning is the slot almost nobody books and the one that works best. In Al Twar households Friday and Saturday afternoon carry most of the week's commitments, which leaves Saturday from nine until noon free with the student at their freshest. A ninety-minute Saturday session for new content, paired with a short weekday slot for practice, is the pattern we propose most often in this district, and it is the one that survives an unexpected school event.

The table sets out the afternoon as a sequence rather than a timetable. The spread across this cluster is the thing to notice: finishing times differ by up to ninety minutes between schools, so two students on the same Al Twar street can have usable windows an hour apart. That is why we ask for the school by name and the actual arrival time in the first conversation, before anybody is matched.

sections.heading: Why chemistry homework arrives in bursts, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Chemistry is timetabled around a laboratory, and a laboratory is a shared resource. Practical work therefore happens when the room is free rather than when it fits the teaching sequence or the student's week, and the write-up follows a few days later regardless of what else is due. Add a topic test at the end of a unit and a problem sheet in between, and the subject's workload arrives in peaks separated by quiet weeks rather than as a steady stream.

A rigid weekly tutoring slot interacts badly with that. In a quiet week the session has nothing urgent to attach to and drifts into general review, which is the least valuable thing a tutor can do. In a peak week the student arrives having already written for two hours and has no capacity left. Both outcomes look like a tutor problem and are actually a planning problem, and families conclude after a term that tutoring did not help.

The fix is a standing slot with an agreed right to move it by a day or two. That sounds minor and it changes the arrangement materially: in a lab week the session becomes support on the write-up, held after the practical rather than before it, and in a quiet week it moves forward to prepare the topic the class is about to meet. Over a term the same number of hours does considerably more work.

The other half of the fix is to teach the report structure once, properly, early. Method, data table, uncertainty treatment, graph conventions and a real evaluation are the same every time, and a student who has been taught them in September writes every subsequent report faster and better. It is one session and it pays for itself several times over, which makes it one of the first things we do rather than something we get to eventually.

sections.heading: Sequencing a tutor against the school's own scheme of work
paragraphs: Two Al Twar students in different schools can be studying opposite halves of the chemistry course in the same term, because schools sequence the guide differently. Some open with Structure and the particulate model; others begin with stoichiometry and quantitative work on the grounds that everything later depends on it. A tutor working from a generic topic order will be out of step with at least one of them, and being out of step is worse than it sounds: the student is asked to hold two different frames at once.

So the single most useful document a family can pass to a tutor is the term's scheme of work, which the chemistry teacher will usually provide as one sheet. With it, a tutor can be deliberately a week ahead of the class rather than a week behind. That converts the session from remedial to preparatory, which is a better purchase: the student meets the topic in school already knowing where it is going, and the school lesson does more work for free.

There is a judgement about when to abandon that. After a poor topic test the right move is to drop back and repair rather than press ahead, because a gap in the foundation of Reactivity will undermine everything built on it. The tutor should say so rather than keeping to a plan, and a family should expect the sequence to change two or three times across a year without that being a sign of disorganisation.

sections.heading: The investigation deadline, counted backwards from your school's calendar
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation carries about a fifth of the chemistry grade, and its deadlines are set by your school rather than by the IB. That is the detail families miss. Nobody publishes a universal date, so the only way to plan is to ask the chemistry teacher or the IB coordinator for the school's internal milestones in September and then work backwards from them. Two emails, and the whole component stops being a surprise.

Counting backwards produces a timetable most students would not arrive at alone. The slowest stage is narrowing the question, because a question that school apparatus cannot answer produces a literature summary with a few measurements attached, and that is the commonest reason a competent student scores poorly here. Allow a fortnight for that, with a tutor or teacher pushing back on each version. Then trialling the method, which exposes the variable nobody controlled. Then collection, processing and writing.

The complication specific to DP1 into DP2 is that this period also contains mock season and, in several subjects, other internal assessment deadlines. Economics commentaries, the Extended Essay and the chemistry investigation can land within weeks of each other. A family that has mapped those dates in September can space the chemistry work sensibly; a family that has not will meet all of them at once in a single fortnight.

The table gives the milestones with who controls each one. The dates are yours to fill in from the school's calendar. The one worth putting on the fridge is the first internal deadline, because everything downstream compresses against it and because the useful supervision all happens before it.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry wants little and often, not a block
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where Diploma students decide they are bad at chemistry, and the decision is almost always a consequence of how it was learned rather than how hard it is. Held as a list of thirty unrelated reactions, every synthesis question is a fresh memory test. Held as a map, with functional groups at the nodes, reagents on the arrows between them and conditions as labels, a multi-step synthesis becomes route-finding, which most students are considerably better at.

The scheduling consequence is specific and it matters in a week as tight as the Al Twar one. The map is built in about three sessions and then maintained in five minutes a week. It cannot be crammed: a student who meets the whole of organic chemistry in a single intensive block before a mock will hold it for a fortnight and lose it. Little and often is not a preference here, it is how the material behaves.

Mechanisms are the second half, and the error is nearly always the same: the arrow starts in the wrong place. An arrow represents the movement of an electron pair, so it must begin at a lone pair or at a bond, never at an atom and never at a positive charge. Students who internalise that single rule stop losing mechanism marks because the remaining steps follow. A tutor who marks mechanisms weekly spots this in one session; one who meets organic chemistry twice a year does not.

For students arriving from Indian-curriculum schools, which in Al Qusais and Al Nahda is a substantial share of the cohort, there is an extra wrinkle. That preparation emphasises named reactions and memorised conversions, which is excellent for recall and poor preparation for a question asking for a mechanism to be drawn and justified. The transition takes a few weeks of deliberate arrow discipline, and a tutor who knows both systems anticipates it rather than discovering it in a mock.

sections.heading: Ramadan, mock season and the chemistry weeks you lose
paragraphs: The UAE year does not distribute study time evenly, and two periods remove more of it than families plan for. The first is mock season, when the school week fills with timed papers and revision sessions and the early evening window effectively disappears. The second is Ramadan, when school days shorten, household rhythms change and the useful study window moves to after Iftar. Between them they can account for six or seven weeks of a chemistry year.

The adjustments are straightforward once planned. During mock season teaching moves to Saturday morning and the weekday slot becomes a short marking session on a timed paper, because the student's own revision is already taking the evenings. During Ramadan sessions shift to a post-Iftar start, typically from around 8.30pm, and get shorter and more focused: forty-five minutes of past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new mechanism teaching, with new content moved to weekend mornings.

Prayer times shape the ordinary week too and are worth settling at the booking stage rather than working around later. A session that reliably runs into Maghrib gets cut short or cancelled; one scheduled to end before it or start after it simply holds. Because lessons run over live video, moving a slot by thirty or forty minutes for a whole term is an administrative change rather than a logistical one, which is not true of an arrangement that depends on somebody driving.

Travel is the third factor in this district. Many Al Twar households are away for part of the long break and part of the winter holiday. Over video a session can follow the family rather than pausing and restarting cold, which is particularly useful in chemistry where organic chemistry decays quickly without maintenance. Tell us the travel dates when the plan is made and they get built in rather than breaking it.

sections.heading: What unreliable timing does to the price
paragraphs: Timing and cost are the same conversation in a villa district. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, against qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 and Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The gap is the tutor's drive, which from central Dubai to Al Twar is forty to sixty minutes each way at the evening peak. That part is visible on the invoice.

The invisible part is reliability, and chemistry is unusually sensitive to it. A plan that depends on a session happening in the same week as a lab write-up only works if the session can move. An in-home arrangement cannot move cheaply, because moving it wastes somebody's journey, so in practice it does not move and the session is spent on the wrong thing. Over a term that is a meaningful share of the value, lost for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching.

For completeness, the rest of the market as published in October 2026: budget and university-student online tutors from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's survey agreeing; and BartyED advertising AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages appear at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of these is an IB Gram price; the trial lesson is free and the consultation sets out what a plan would involve.

One piece of context for an Al Twar household. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the school line flat, this is a year in which a family can decide a tutoring figure and a schedule deliberately and hold both for two years, which chemistry rewards more than most subjects.

sections.heading: Three chemistry schedules that survive an Al Twar term
paragraphs: The first is for a DP1 student in the local cluster who gets home by 3.15pm. One session a week in the early window, sequenced a week ahead of the class from the scheme of work, with the right to move by a day in a lab week. Add a single Saturday morning session in September to teach the report structure once, and that is the whole arrangement for the first two terms. It is less than most families expect to buy and it is the shape that works.

The second is for a household with a cross-district school place, where the child is not home before six. Teaching moves to Saturday morning, ninety minutes, and the weekday contact becomes a short late-window slot for marked practice. This is not a reduced version of the first schedule; it is a different design, and trying to force a 5pm weekday session into this household is the error that gets made most often.

The third is for a DP2 student heading into mock season. One weekly session on current content plus a monthly full timed paper, marked properly and discussed, with Paper 2 taken first because it carries about 44 per cent of the grade. Then a separate short block on the data-based section of Paper 1, which is rarely drilled at school and is the cheapest set of marks available in the course.

Two rules hold across all three. Protect the evening meal, because sessions scheduled across it get cancelled and cancellation breaks the weekly rhythm that makes chemistry stick. And settle the Ramadan and mock-season arrangements in advance rather than improvising, moving teaching to weekend mornings and shortening the weekday slot. A schedule built for the year it has to survive beats one that is ideal in October.

process.title: Send the school, the finish time and the scheme of work
process.description: Those three decide the plan. The scheme of work is usually one sheet from the chemistry teacher, and with it a tutor can work a week ahead of the class instead of a week behind, which is a better use of the same hour.

process.description: They are set by your school, not by the IB, and everything downstream compresses against the first one. Two emails to the teacher or the IB coordinator, and the component stops arriving as a surprise in February.

process.title: Agree the right to move a session
process.description: Chemistry work comes in bursts around lab write-ups and topic tests. A standing slot that can shift by a day does far more with the same hours than a rigid one that gets abandoned in November.

process.description: A full session at no cost and no card details, scheduled in the real slot rather than a convenient one, so you find out whether 5pm on a Tuesday works for your child in practice.

process.description: We expect the plan to change two or three times a year: after a poor topic test the right move is to drop back and repair rather than press ahead, and we will say so rather than keeping to a schedule.

whyPoints.description: Schools in this cluster teach the chemistry guide in different orders, so a generic topic sequence puts a tutor out of step with at least some students. We work from the school's own scheme of work, a week ahead of the class where possible.

whyPoints.title: Built to flex around lab weeks

faqs.question: What time can a chemistry session start on a weekday in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: Usually not before 5pm, and for some households not before six. Schools in this cluster finish between about 2pm and 3.30pm, Al Twar sits late on most bus loops so add thirty to forty-five minutes, and changing, eating and the school's own set work take until around a quarter to five. Families with a cross-district place in Mirdif, Al Garhoud or Festival City should assume the early window does not exist, and plan Saturday morning teaching with a short late weekday slot instead.

faqs.question: Why does chemistry homework seem to arrive all at once?
faqs.answer: Because practical work is timetabled around laboratory availability rather than around the teaching sequence or your child's week. The write-up then follows a few days later whatever else is due, and a topic test at the end of a unit lands on top. The result is peaks separated by quiet weeks. A rigid weekly tutoring slot handles that badly: it drifts in the quiet weeks and overloads the student in the peaks. Agree a standing slot that can move by a day or two.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to our villa in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Chemistry tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for mechanisms, worked stoichiometry and annotated drafts. For a plan that has to flex around lab weeks and mock timetables that is the practical advantage: a session moves by a day at no cost to anybody, which is not true when someone has already set off across the city.

faqs.question: What is a scheme of work and why should I ask for it?
faqs.answer: It is the term's topic order, usually a single sheet the chemistry teacher can send you. It matters because schools in this cluster sequence the Diploma chemistry guide differently: some open with Structure and the particulate model, others start with stoichiometry. With that sheet a tutor can deliberately work a week ahead of the class rather than a week behind, which turns the session from remedial into preparatory and makes the school lesson land on prepared ground.

faqs.question: Should a tutor be ahead of the class or catching up?
faqs.answer: Ahead, where the student can cope with it, because preparing a topic makes the school lesson do more work for the same tutoring hour. The exception is a poor topic test, where the right move is to drop back and repair, since a gap in the foundation of Reactivity undermines everything built on it. Expect the sequence to change two or three times across a year. A tutor who never deviates from the plan is following a document rather than teaching a student.

faqs.question: When should my daughter start the chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's internal deadline implies, because the slowest stage is narrowing the question rather than running the experiment. Ask the chemistry teacher or IB coordinator for the school's internal milestones in September, then work backwards: a fortnight to settle a question the available apparatus can actually answer, time to trial the method and find the uncontrolled variable, then collection, processing and writing. Starting at the deadline produces a literature summary with measurements attached, which is the usual reason a strong student scores poorly.

faqs.question: Who sets the deadlines for the Scientific Investigation?
faqs.answer: Your school does, not the IB, which is the detail most families miss. There is no universal published date, so the only reliable plan comes from the school's own calendar. That also means the deadlines land in a term that contains mock examinations and, in several subjects, other internal assessment work. A family that maps those dates in September can space the chemistry write-up sensibly; one that does not will meet all of them inside a single fortnight in the spring.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade comes from outside the exam hall?
faqs.answer: About a fifth, through the Scientific Investigation, at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 2 carries about 44 per cent and Paper 1 about 36 per cent across its multiple-choice and data-based sections. Confirm the exact figures with your child's subject guide or the IB coordinator, since assessment detail is revised between guides and the IB publishes the authoritative version. The practical consequence is that a component worth a fifth of the grade deserves scheduled time rather than the fortnight before a deadline.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my son's lab write-ups?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the best version of that help happens once, early. Method, data table, uncertainty treatment, graph conventions and a real evaluation are the same every time, so teaching the structure properly in September makes every subsequent report faster and better. Beyond that, a tutor can give feedback on the student's own write-up and point out where a claim is not supported by the data. A tutor may not supply a method, process data the student did not collect, or write any section.

faqs.question: Why is organic chemistry so hard to revise in one block?
faqs.answer: Because it behaves like a map rather than a list, and a map has to be maintained. Built properly, with functional groups at the nodes and reagents on the arrows between them, it takes about three sessions and then five minutes a week to keep. Crammed into an intensive block before a mock it holds for a fortnight and then goes. Little and often is not a preference in this topic, it is how the material works, which has direct consequences for how a term is scheduled.

faqs.question: My child draws mechanism arrows from the wrong place. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Quickly, and it is one of the most satisfying things to fix. An arrow represents the movement of an electron pair, so it must begin at a lone pair or at a bond, never at an atom and never at a positive charge. Students who internalise that single rule stop losing mechanism marks, because the remaining steps follow from it. A tutor who marks mechanisms weekly identifies this in one session; one who meets organic chemistry twice a year will read it as carelessness.

faqs.question: What happens to chemistry sessions during mock season?
faqs.answer: They invert. The school week fills with timed papers and revision, so the early evening window disappears and the student's own revision takes the evenings. The arrangement that works is teaching moved to Saturday morning, with the weekday slot becoming a short session marking one timed paper. Take Paper 2 first, because it carries about 44 per cent of the grade. Scope the block against the school's own mock dates and accept honestly what can move in the weeks available.

faqs.question: How should a chemistry plan change for the Ramadan weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to plan the shift than to defend the old slot. School days shorten, household rhythms change, and the useful study window moves to after Iftar, typically from around 8.30pm. Sessions get shorter and more focused, forty-five minutes of past-paper work rather than ninety minutes of new mechanism teaching, with new content moved to weekend mornings. Because lessons run over live video, changing a slot for a month is administrative rather than logistical.

faqs.question: We travel in the holidays. Does chemistry tutoring have to stop?
faqs.answer: No, and in chemistry that matters more than in most subjects, because organic chemistry decays without maintenance. Since lessons are delivered over live video on Gulf Standard Time, a session can follow the family through a trip rather than stopping for three weeks and restarting cold. Tell us the travel dates when the plan is made and they get built in, including a reduced frequency across the break if that suits. An arrangement depending on a UAE address cannot do this at all.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a week does a Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, with the right to move it. One weekly session suits a student who is coping but losing marks on technique, because the learning happens in the practice between sessions. Two make sense for a real content gap, or for a Higher Level student whose Standard Level foundation needs repair before the extensions can land. Beyond two hours a week the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice rather than teaching time, so extra hours displace what makes the earlier ones work.

faqs.question: Does it cost more to have a tutor who can reschedule?
faqs.answer: Not in itself, but it costs considerably more to have one who cannot. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutors, and the gap pays for a drive of forty to sixty minutes each way to Al Twar. The quieter cost is that an in-home session cannot move cheaply, so in a lab week it happens anyway and gets spent on the wrong thing.

intro.heading: What an Al Warqa parent can check for themselves before paying
paragraphs: Chemistry tutoring in Dubai is sold on confidence, and confidence is unverifiable. So start with the three things you can verify without anyone's help. The IB Chemistry subject guide is a public document and your child's school will tell you which level and which theme they are in. Your child's marked scripts show exactly where the marks went. And the Dubai rate cards are published: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, Unitors from AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate at AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist work, and BartyED at AED 650.

Put those three together and you can price the job yourself. If the scripts show organic mechanisms failing, that is a known block of work with a known length. If they show the data-based questions on Paper 1 going wrong, that is a technique problem shared with every other science and fixable in a handful of sessions. If they show the right chemistry written in an answer shape the command term did not ask for, that is a term of enforcement rather than a content purchase. Each of those has a different hour count, and the hour count is what determines the bill, not the rate.

The one genuinely chemistry-specific cost driver is Higher Level depth. The current guide organises the whole course under two headings, Structure and Reactivity, with Higher Level content extending topics inside each rather than sitting in separate units. In practice that concentrates the difficulty in a few places: energetics and entropy, equilibrium quantitative treatment, acid-base calculations, and organic mechanisms with their electron movement. A tutor who is strong on the rest and vague on those four is not a Higher Level chemistry tutor, whatever the rate says.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Al Warqa chemistry lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. This matters practically rather than philosophically. Mechanism work is drawing: curly arrows in the right place, from the right lone pair, to the right atom. A shared screen where a tutor can annotate the student's own mechanism, with a mark scheme open beside it, is a better setting for that than a notebook on a kitchen table.

The rest of the page is the material for the check. The two themes and what sits in each. Higher Level content, named. The three topics that swallow most chemistry tutoring budgets and what each actually costs in hours. Paper weightings. The investigation criteria and the chemistry-specific way research questions fail. And an honest list of where money gets wasted in this subject, which includes at least one thing we could sell you and will not.
