programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Higher and Standard Level, with content organised under two themes, Structure and Reactivity, and assessed by two written papers plus the scientific investigation at twenty per cent. Higher Level content extends topics inside both themes rather than forming separate units, so the depth increases across the course rather than in one section a student could isolate.
programmes.countryNote: Al Warqa Diploma chemists travel to Mirdif or Festival City, so a session realistically starts at 17:15 or later. Chemistry tolerates that better than mathematics for recall and mechanism practice, and worse for quantitative equilibrium work, which is worth considering when choosing the evening.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Four criteria each marked 0 to 8: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. No external examination, with the report grade converted from criterion totals.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest chemistry intervention available to an Al Warqa family is fixing criterion B and C in MYP 4 or 5. They are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation's research design and data analysis criteria, and the same weakness costs ordinary rates now and specialist rates in Year 13.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry, as the other route in
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1, with Cambridge tiered Core and Extended and offering either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Many Al Warqa students reach Diploma Chemistry this way rather than through MYP.
programmes.countryNote: A 0620 Extended candidate arrives with solid moles calculations and nomenclature and no experience of mechanism reasoning or of extended explanation. Four to eight weeks of focused work covers it, and identifying that early is considerably cheaper than a year of general weekly support.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Diploma Chemistry can sit inside it, keeping the subject and its assessment while reducing the overall load.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant here because a student struggling with Higher Level Chemistry has options other than buying more chemistry hours, including moving to Standard Level. A provider who never mentions either is selling time, and the cost difference over eighteen months is substantial.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is one subject and a short list of genuinely expensive topics. Each note names what the topic demands and roughly what it costs in sessions to repair.

subjects.name: Structure 1: Models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Atomic structure, the mole concept, electron configuration and ionisation energy. Moles work is where weak foundations show, and it is cheap to fix: three to five sessions usually secures it, and nothing later in the course works without it.

subjects.name: Structure 2: Models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, shapes of molecules and, at Higher Level, further treatment including hybridisation. Students lose marks explaining boiling points by naming a force without saying how it affects energy required.

subjects.name: Structure 3: Classification of matter
subjects.description: The periodic table, periodicity, organic families and spectroscopic identification. Spectroscopy questions reward a methodical reading of the data rather than recall, which makes them recoverable marks for a student taught the method.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: What drives chemical reactions
subjects.description: Energetics, enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs energy. One of the four places Higher Level difficulty concentrates. Sign conventions and cycle construction account for most of the lost marks, and both are technique.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: How much, how fast and how far
subjects.description: Reaction rates, equilibrium and acid-base chemistry, with quantitative equilibrium and pH calculations extended substantially at Higher Level. This is the most expensive block in the subject to repair late, typically eight to twelve sessions.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: What are the mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.description: Redox, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms, with nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition developed at Higher Level. Mechanism marks are drawing marks: curly arrows from the correct lone pair to the correct atom, with charges shown.

subjects.name: Organic reasoning and synthesis routes
subjects.description: Multi-step synthesis and reasoning about why a reagent behaves as it does. Students who have memorised individual reactions cannot plan a route, which is the difference between a 5 and a 7 at Higher Level and takes six to eight sessions to build.

subjects.name: Calculations and significant figures
subjects.description: Titration arithmetic, limiting reagents, percentage yield and consistent significant figures. Rounding and figure discipline bleed single marks across a whole paper, invisibly on any one question and substantially in total.

subjects.name: Data-based and experimental questions
subjects.description: Reading tables, identifying controlled variables, spotting systematic error and interpreting graphs. Taught least at school because a class in a laboratory is doing something else, and among the most recoverable marks in the subject.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, one report, four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The student designs it, runs it, analyses it and writes it; a tutor teaches the criteria and reviews their drafts.

sections.heading: Pricing the job yourself from scripts and published rates
paragraphs: The rate is the easiest number to compare and the least useful. What decides the bill is hours, and hours come from the diagnosis. So begin with two recently marked chemistry scripts and read them for pattern rather than for score. A paper where moles calculations collapse is a different purchase from one where the chemistry is right and the answer shape is wrong, and both are different from one where organic mechanisms are drawn with arrows starting in the wrong place.

Then apply the published numbers. Dubai's budget tier runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, which buys supervision and question-answering. The qualified band is roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IB from AED 200. Specialist work runs AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's Dubai table, with TutorChase at AED 270. The premium end reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, where BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: how the course is actually organised
paragraphs: The current guide puts everything under two headings. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and what the mechanisms of chemical change are. That is the whole architecture, and a tutor who cannot describe it is working from a previous version of the course.

The organisation is not decorative. It groups content by the question being asked rather than by traditional topic, which means a student is expected to connect ideas across what used to be separate chapters. An energetics question can require bonding reasoning; an equilibrium question can require acid-base understanding. A tutor who teaches isolated topics will produce sessions that each make sense and a student who cannot answer a Paper 2 question that crosses two themes.

Higher Level content sits inside these themes rather than beside them, and the practical consequence is that there is no Higher Level section to skip to. Difficulty concentrates in four places: entropy and Gibbs energy within Reactivity 1, quantitative equilibrium and pH calculations within Reactivity 2, organic mechanism depth within Reactivity 3, and further bonding treatment within Structure 2. Those four are where a tutor's level genuinely shows.

For an Al Warqa family the practical step is one email. Ask the school which theme is being taught now and which comes next, and whether the student is Higher or Standard Level. A tutor consolidating the current theme is worth considerably more than one working through the guide in their own order and reaching equilibrium three months after the class did.

sections.heading: The three topics that swallow a chemistry budget
paragraphs: Quantitative equilibrium and pH calculations are the most expensive thing to repair late in this subject. They sit at the end of Reactivity 2, they assume moles work is already automatic, and they require a kind of layered reasoning that cannot be shortcut. A student arriving at them with shaky moles will fail twice: once in equilibrium, and once again when acid-base questions appear on a paper. Eight to twelve sessions is a realistic estimate, which is why the cheap version of this purchase is five sessions of moles work in the first term of Year 12.

Energetics with entropy and Gibbs energy is the second. The chemistry is not conceptually enormous; the losses come from sign conventions and from building enthalpy cycles correctly, both of which are technique. Six to eight sessions normally secures it. The common error families make is buying this as content teaching when the scripts show a technique fault, which takes half as long and costs half as much.

Organic mechanisms are the third, and they behave differently from the other two. Mechanism marks are drawing marks: the curly arrow has to start at the correct lone pair or bond and finish at the correct atom, with charges shown. A student who has memorised which reagent does what to which functional group can still lose every mechanism mark on a paper. This is why the work has to be done by drawing and correcting, not by explaining, and why a shared screen with live annotation is genuinely the right tool.

One further cost worth naming because it is invisible. Significant figures and rounding discipline bleed single marks across a whole paper. Neither student nor parent can see it without a marked script, each individual loss looks trivial, and the cumulative effect across two papers is large enough to move a grade. It takes one session to teach and a term to enforce, which makes it the best value in the subject.

sections.heading: Papers, weightings and what each rewards
paragraphs: Both levels sit two written papers plus the investigation. Paper 1 is thirty-six per cent and comes in two parts: a multiple-choice section and a data-based and experimental section. Paper 2 is forty-four per cent and carries the structured and extended-response questions. The investigation is the remaining twenty per cent. Higher Level papers are longer, with the same weightings at both levels.

Paper 2 deserves most of the attention because it carries most of the grade, and because command terms decide it. Deduce, explain, outline, describe, state, justify and compare each demand a different answer. A student who writes a paragraph when asked to state loses time they will need later in the paper; one who writes a sentence when asked to explain loses the marks outright. That is not a chemistry problem and it does not improve with content revision.

The data-based section of Paper 1 is the quietly recoverable part. It is a paper exercise: a table, a graph, a described method, questions about controlled variables and systematic error. Schools drill it least because a class of twenty in a laboratory is occupied with something else, and it overlaps almost entirely with the equivalent sections in physics and biology, which means a student taking two sciences gets double value from the same block of work.

A caution on dates rather than papers, and it applies to every page in this project. ibo.org returns an error to automated access, so no IB session or results date here has been confirmed from the IB itself, and secondary sources disagree with each other. UAE schools sit the May session. Any date your family acts on should come from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly, and not from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: The investigation, and the chemistry-specific way it fails
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in one report, assessed against four criteria worth six marks each for twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The four carry equal weight, which matters because students spend most of their effort on the practical work and almost none on evaluation, which is worth exactly as much as the design they agonised over.

The chemistry-specific failure is a research question whose reaction will not produce a measurable change. A student picks an interesting question, books the laboratory, and discovers that the concentration range available cannot shift the observable quantity enough to plot anything meaningful. In physics a badly scoped question usually produces too few data points; in chemistry it often produces data that are real but indistinguishable from noise, which is worse because it looks like data until it is analysed.

That is also why the design conversation has to happen before anything is measured. Once the data are collected, a question that could not produce a measurable change stays that way, and the student is left writing an honest evaluation of an investigation that never had a chance. Pressure-testing the question is one or two sessions, and it is the highest-value part of any investigation block.

The boundary on support is firm and stated in full. A tutor may teach the four criteria in the examiner's wording, explain what the twenty-four marks are made of, ask whether the proposed reaction will produce an analysable change, teach uncertainty and significant-figure discipline on the student's own measurements, and comment on a draft the student has written. No tutor at IB Gram designs an investigation, supplies or processes data, writes a section, or edits until authorship changes. Research for this project found a Dubai provider selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: Where chemistry money gets wasted in Al Warqa households
paragraphs: The first waste is buying content teaching for a technique fault. Scripts showing correct chemistry in the wrong answer shape point at command terms, and that is a session plus a term of enforcement. Buying twenty hours of energetics teaching for it is an expensive way to avoid a conversation about the word deduce. The marked work distinguishes the two in minutes, which is why it should arrive before any package is quoted.

The second is paying qualified or specialist rates for supervision. A student who understands chemistry and will not sit down to practise needs presence, and presence costs AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end of this market. Paying AED 250 for it across a year is a four-figure difference for an identical service, and it is among the most common avoidable expenses in Dubai tutoring. We will say this even though it costs us the booking.

The third is the travel premium, which in Al Warqa is larger than most families estimate. In-home rates run AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online, and the gap covers a round trip of eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes from central Dubai at exactly the hour your child is free. In teaching terms, AED 1,800 a month buys six to twelve online hours or three and a half to ten in-home. Over two Diploma years that difference is a whole second block of topic work.

The fourth is the one nobody calls waste: continuing. An arrangement with no review point becomes a standing order, and chemistry is particularly prone to it because there is always another topic coming. Six weeks, a check against the school's own assessment data, then extend or stop. Where the estimate said five sessions and twelve have passed without movement, the diagnosis was wrong, and that is useful information rather than a reason to buy more of the same.

sections.heading: From MYP Sciences or IGCSE Chemistry into the Diploma
paragraphs: Two different students arrive, and the cheap intervention differs for each. The MYP student has been marked against criterion B, inquiring and designing, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, which are direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation's research design and data analysis criteria. If those were weak in MYP 5 they will be weak in the investigation, and addressing them in MYP 4 or 5 costs ordinary rates while addressing them in Year 13 costs specialist rates under deadline.

The IGCSE student arrives from Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 with solid moles arithmetic, reliable nomenclature and no experience of mechanism reasoning or of extended explanation to a command term. Four to eight weeks of focused work usually covers it. Left unnamed, it presents as a general struggle with a harder course and gets treated with a year of weekly support, when what was needed was mechanism drawing and a command-term rule.

A third pattern recurs in this community because of the local school mix. Students from CBSE chemistry often arrive with stronger calculation and less practice at uncertainty treatment and at writing explanations in the shape a mark scheme wants. Again, short and specific. Treating it as a transition requiring a year of support is the expensive misreading, and it is the one most frequently made.

In all three cases, the diagnosis comes from marked work rather than from the previous curriculum. Two scripts from the first Diploma term show whether the problem is moles, mechanisms, command terms, figures or data interpretation. Each of those is a different purchase with a different session count, and the session count is what you are actually buying when you pay an hourly rate.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and the claims to refuse
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit, and the detail is quotable. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time via its app, website and e-services.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so none appears here; a figure circulating informally could not be verified against any official source and leaving it out is the correct choice rather than a cautious one. Because the permit is free and takes two days, asking for it is entirely reasonable and there is no good answer other than yes.

Two claims should be refused on sight in this market. Nobody should describe themselves as approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson without the specific permit number to show. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds none of these, runs no premises in the UAE, and claims nothing of the kind.

And nobody should promise a grade. A tutor can make a weakness visible, teach the technique that addresses it, and build the past-paper habit that converts knowledge into marks. What happens in an examination hall in May is not a product anyone can sell, and a provider who offers a guaranteed 7 in Higher Level Chemistry is telling you about their marketing rather than their teaching.

intro.heading: Chemistry is the subject where understanding and marks separate most
paragraphs: Diploma Chemistry produces a specific and frustrating pattern. Students who can describe a reaction mechanism accurately, who can explain why an equilibrium shifts, who clearly understand the chemistry, come back from a paper with a 4 or a 5. Their parents in Al Wasl reasonably conclude that something is wrong with the teaching or with the effort. Usually neither is true. The gap is in conversion: the student knows the chemistry and does not know what the mark scheme is paying for.

That is not a vague complaint. It is specific and it is diagnosable from a marked script in about twenty minutes. Paper 1 is multiple choice, and the losses there are overwhelmingly on the quantitative items, where a student who could do the calculation with working guesses it without. Paper 2 rewards answers that state the assumption the student has silently made, that give the sign on an enthalpy change, that carry units through and quote significant figures consistently. The scientific investigation is marked against criteria that students frequently have not read, with the heaviest losses in the evaluation.

The syllabus itself has a shape worth understanding too, because it changes how revision should be organised. Chemistry is built around two organising concepts, structure and reactivity, with the content threaded through them rather than presented as a list of separate topics. That structure is an advantage for a student who uses it: a question about why a reaction happens is usually a question about structure in disguise, and recognising that saves time under pressure.

This page therefore works through the subject rather than around it. Component by component, what each one is testing and where the marks go. The topics that cost most, with the specific error in each. The data booklet, which is provided in every paper and routinely ignored. Paper 1 and Paper 2 treated as separate skills. The investigation, criterion by criterion. How practical work is handled when tuition is online. And the cost picture in dirhams, with sources, because nobody else in this market publishes it.

On delivery and scheduling, two plain statements. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run in India only. Chemistry teaching for Al Wasl families happens one-to-one over live video with a shared workspace, which handles mechanisms, structures and calculations well because both people can draw. And the Al Wasl week has real constraints in it: schools in this cluster finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.15pm, Al Wasl Road is slow from four to six, and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons KHDA requires occupy periods and generate homework of their own. A session placed without accounting for any of that is the one that gets cancelled, and a cancelled session in a cumulative subject costs more than a missed hour.

programmes.countryNote: Families in the Al Wasl catchment often make this decision alongside the choice between A Levels and the Diploma, since several schools here offer both. Taking Higher Level Chemistry and two other Higher Level sciences is a heavy combination that a Year 11 student rarely has the information to assess.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, the year before
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed science covering the three disciplines, strong on investigation design and lighter on quantitative work than the Diploma assumes. Students arriving from MYP generally handle the scientific investigation well and find moles calculations and energetics harder than expected.
programmes.countryNote: MYP sciences are taught at the IB continuum schools within a short drive of Al Wasl. The useful intervention for an MYP student heading into Diploma Chemistry is quantitative: moles, concentration and stoichiometry practised to fluency over the summer before Diploma 1 begins.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry, the other entry route
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson Edexcel 4CH1, at Core or Extended tier. Students from this route arrive with solid calculation technique and structured exam habits, and meet two unfamiliar things in Diploma Chemistry: mechanisms explained rather than recalled, and a research investigation they design themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Most of the Jumeirah-side secondaries around Al Wasl run IGCSE Chemistry before the post-16 split. An Extended-tier grade with comfortable moles work is the realistic preparation for Higher Level Chemistry; a Core entry is not, and that is a Year 10 conversation rather than a Year 12 one.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: The Chemistry topics that produce the most tutoring requests from Al Wasl families, each with the error that actually costs the marks rather than a general note on difficulty.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole concept
subjects.description: The arithmetic foundation of the subject. Losses come from limiting-reagent questions answered on the wrong reactant and from percentage-yield work where the theoretical yield was computed from the excess rather than the limiting species.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy sign conventions and Hess cycles. The most common single error in the subject is an enthalpy change given with the wrong sign, which the scheme treats as a wrong answer however correct the magnitude.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.description: Rate equations, orders of reaction and the Arrhenius relationship at Higher Level. Students read graphs correctly and omit the statement of units on the rate constant, which is a required part of the answer.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning is usually sound; the equilibrium constant calculations are where marks go, particularly when initial rather than equilibrium concentrations are substituted into the expression.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.description: pH and weak-acid calculations, buffers and titration curves at Higher Level. Losses cluster in the approximations: students apply a weak-acid assumption without stating it, and the scheme wants the assumption named.

subjects.name: Redox processes and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Half-equations, cell potentials and electrolysis. Standard electrode potentials sit in the data booklet, and students who do not use it reliably lose marks on questions designed to be answered with it.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Nucleophilic substitution, elimination and electrophilic addition. Curly arrows must start and end in the right places, and a mechanism with correct products and sloppy arrows scores below one with careful arrows.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Ionisation energy trends and electron configuration. Explanation questions here are answered with a restated trend rather than a reason, which is the single most repeated pattern in Paper 2 across the sciences.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Intermolecular forces and shapes of molecules. Boiling-point comparison questions need the specific force named and the reason given, not simply an assertion that one molecule is more polar.

subjects.name: Data processing and uncertainties
subjects.description: Propagating uncertainty and quoting significant figures consistently. These marks appear in both papers and in the investigation, and they are among the easiest in the subject to recover with deliberate practice.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: A student-designed investigation marked against criteria. The research question is usually too broad, which quietly limits several criteria at once, and the evaluation is treated as an apology rather than an analysis.

subjects.name: Data booklet and periodic table technique
subjects.description: Provided in every paper and genuinely examinable. Students who have never practised finding a value under time pressure lose marks on questions written specifically to be answered from the booklet.

modes.title: Weekly work through the two years
modes.description: One tutor, one weekly slot, running across Diploma 1 and 2. A gap left in Diploma 1 reappears as an apparently unrelated failure a year later, which is why sustained work beats intensive rescue.

sections.heading: What an IB Chemistry grade is actually made of
paragraphs: Three components produce the grade, and they reward different things. Students and parents tend to treat Chemistry as one skill measured three ways. It is closer to three skills measured separately, and a student can be strong in one and weak in another without that being visible in an overall grade.

Paper 1 is multiple choice and allows no partial credit. A student who understands a calculation but works too slowly to complete it will mark an answer they have reasoned towards rather than computed, and will be wrong about a third of the time on precisely the items they could have got right. The remedy is speed on standard quantitative routines rather than more content, and it is one of the few genuinely quick wins in the subject.

Paper 2 is where the mark scheme becomes visible. It pays for stated assumptions, correct enthalpy signs, units carried through and significant figures used consistently. It penalises explanation questions answered by restating the trend the question gave you. A student can lose a band's worth of marks across this paper without getting a single piece of chemistry wrong, which is the single most important thing for an Al Wasl parent to understand before deciding what tutoring should work on.

The scientific investigation is the most controllable component, because it is produced over months with draft feedback available rather than in a sealed room. It is also the one students most often leave until the time available no longer permits doing it properly. The table sets the three out with where each one bleeds.

table.caption: THE THREE COMPONENTS AND WHERE EACH LOSES MARKS
rows: Speed drills on standard calculation routines
Unstated assumptions, signs, units, restated trends
Marking the student's own script to the scheme
Narrow the question early, read the criteria
Direct teaching of the HL-only material
Timed questions designed around the booklet

sections.heading: Structure and reactivity: how the syllabus is organised
paragraphs: Diploma Chemistry is organised around two unifying ideas rather than as a list of discrete topics. Structure covers the models of matter, bonding, and the classification of substances. Reactivity covers what drives reactions, how fast they go and how far. The content is threaded through those two, which is more useful than it sounds, because it tells a student where to look when a question seems unfamiliar.

Most apparently novel Paper 2 questions are a familiar idea in unfamiliar clothing. A question asking why one compound has a higher boiling point than another is a structure question, and the answer is a named intermolecular force plus a reason. A question asking why a reaction proceeds at one temperature and not another is a reactivity question, and the answer involves energy distribution. A student who reflexively classifies the question before answering it writes better answers, because the classification tells them which vocabulary the mark scheme expects.

Revision organised the same way also travels better than topic-by-topic revision. Working through bonding, intermolecular forces and physical properties as one block makes the connections explicit, and the connections are what Paper 2 tests. Working through them as three separate chapters a fortnight apart produces students who can recall each and cannot link them, which is exactly the student who understands chemistry and scores a 5.

The practical consequence for tutoring is the order of work. A tutor who starts with the topic the student names as hardest is often starting in the wrong place, because the difficulty usually sits one layer below. Organic mechanisms that will not stick are frequently a bonding problem. Equilibrium calculations that keep going wrong are frequently a stoichiometry problem. Finding the layer underneath is most of the diagnostic value of a first session.

sections.heading: The topics that cost Al Wasl students the most marks
paragraphs: Chemistry losses are not evenly distributed. A small number of topics account for a large share of the marks that go missing, and the error inside each is specific enough to be named. That specificity is what makes the subject tractable: a student is rarely bad at Chemistry in general and usually making four or five identifiable mistakes repeatedly.

Energetics leads the list, and the sign on an enthalpy change leads energetics. A correct magnitude with the wrong sign is a wrong answer, and students who understand exothermic and endothermic perfectly well still drop the sign under time pressure. Equilibrium follows, where initial concentrations find their way into an expression that wanted equilibrium concentrations. Acids and bases follow that, where a weak-acid approximation is applied without being stated and the scheme wanted it stated.

Organic chemistry behaves differently. Students usually know the products and lose marks on the mechanism presentation: curly arrows starting from the wrong place, or from an atom rather than from a bond or a lone pair. This is a drawing convention rather than chemistry, and it is learnable in two sessions, which makes it a high-return place to start.

Across all of them sits a layer of presentational loss: units omitted, significant figures inconsistent within one answer, uncertainties not propagated. Those marks appear in both papers and in the investigation, and recovering them requires no new chemistry at all. The table pairs the topic with the error and the fix.

table.caption: TOPIC AGAINST ERROR - IB CHEMISTRY
rows: Sign stated before the arithmetic, every time
Initial concentrations used in the expression
A written ICE layout as standard practice
Name the assumption in the answer
Curly arrows from the wrong origin
Units of the rate constant omitted
Units derived from the rate equation each time
A fixed routine applied to every calculation

sections.heading: The data booklet is part of the exam
paragraphs: A data booklet and a periodic table are provided in every Chemistry examination, and a meaningful number of questions are written to be answered from them. Students who have not practised using them under time pressure lose those marks, not because they do not know the chemistry but because they do not know where the value lives or trust themselves to find it quickly.

The specific skills are mundane and worth drilling. Locating a standard electrode potential and getting the sign convention the right way round. Finding a bond enthalpy and recognising that it is an average rather than a specific value, which matters in some answers. Reading an infrared absorption range and matching it to a functional group. Picking the right constant from several that look similar under pressure. Each of those takes seconds for a practised student and costs a minute or two for an unpractised one, and a minute or two multiplied across a paper is a grade.

The booklet also changes what revision should include. There is no value in memorising anything the booklet provides, and students waste real hours doing it. There is substantial value in knowing precisely what it does and does not contain, because that determines what must be learned and what can be looked up. Going through the booklet page by page once, early, is an hour that pays for itself repeatedly.

In an online session this is straightforward to practise, since both people can look at the same booklet page and the same question simultaneously. It is one of several places where screen-based teaching is at no disadvantage, and a shared workspace where a tutor can watch a student search for a value is arguably better than sitting beside them, because the search itself becomes visible and correctable.
bullets: Learn what the booklet contains before memorising anything
Practise locating values under time pressure, not at leisure
Electrode potential sign conventions are a recurring trap

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is a student-designed piece of practical research, marked against criteria with published descriptors and mark allocations. Students who have not read the descriptors are guessing at what is being rewarded, and in Chemistry specifically the guess is usually wrong, because the criteria reward design reasoning and evaluation far more heavily than students expect and reward the quantity of data much less.

The failure that does the most damage is a research question too broad for the apparatus and time available. It caps several criteria at once: the method cannot be focused, the data cannot support a clear conclusion, and the evaluation has nothing specific to evaluate. Narrowing the question is almost always the most valuable hour a tutor spends on an investigation, and it has to happen before the practical work rather than after it.

The second failure is the evaluation, which students write as a list of apologies. Limited time, small sample, imprecise equipment. That earns little. The descriptor wants the effect of a specific limitation on the specific conclusion drawn, and a realistic improvement that would address it. One sentence of that form outperforms a page of generic regret, and most students have never been shown the difference.

On the honesty boundary, which matters here as much as anywhere in the Diploma: a tutor may explain the criteria, model an investigation on an unrelated question, check whether a method can actually answer the question posed, and read a draft and respond with questions. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of it. Some operators in this market sell completed internal assessments outright; a student who buys one risks a malpractice finding and the Diploma itself, and no grade justifies that.

table.caption: INVESTIGATION CRITERIA - WHAT EACH CREDITS AND WHERE IT GOES WRONG
rows: A question answerable with the apparatus
Question the scope until it narrows
Ask why each choice was made
Point at the gap, not fill it
A conclusion stronger than the data
Ask what the data actually shows
Specific limitation tied to the conclusion
Generic apologies about time and equipment
Explain the descriptor, not write the line

sections.heading: Practical chemistry when the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection to online science tuition, and it deserves a direct answer rather than reassurance. Laboratory work stays at school, where the apparatus, the chemicals and the supervision are. No tutoring arrangement, in-home or online, substitutes for a school laboratory, and anyone implying otherwise is overselling.

What a tutor works on is the part of practical chemistry that is examined on paper, and that part is substantial. Variable control and why a particular control matters for a particular reaction. Uncertainty propagation through a calculation. Reading a results table for a trend and distinguishing it from noise. Identifying which source of error actually affected the conclusion rather than listing every possible one. Evaluating a method's fitness for a stated purpose. All of those are written skills assessed in both papers and in the investigation.

In practice this is where a large share of the recoverable marks sit, because practical reasoning is taught less explicitly than content. A student who has done the experiment and cannot write about its limitations precisely loses marks in a place that has nothing to do with manual skill. Working on exactly that is a reasonable use of a session and does not need a bench.

There is a documentation point too. The investigation requires raw data, processing and a written account, and students regularly return from a laboratory session with data recorded too thinly to work with: no uncertainties noted, no record of the apparatus used, no observation of anything that went wrong. Agreeing before the practical what to write down converts a laboratory hour into usable evidence, and that conversation is one of the most valuable things a tutor can have with a Chemistry student.

sections.heading: What Chemistry support costs in Dubai, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Chemistry is one of the subjects where the specialist premium is real, because the pool of people who can teach Higher Level to examiner depth is small. Here is the market picture with its sources, so that any quote you receive has a context. A qualified online subject tutor in Dubai is published at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work is quoted at AED 270 by TutorChase, with Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200-450 and above, and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end.

At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which generally means a university student. For Standard Level content catch-up that can be adequate. For Higher Level work the thing being bought is the diagnosis inside the hour rather than the hour itself, and diagnosis is what the cheaper tier usually lacks. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and AED 200-500 by independent home tutors, with travel inside that figure.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' own figures with their own dates, not an IB Gram price list.

Two things a parent can check independently in a single afternoon. Ask for a written hourly rate and whether travel sits inside it. And ask the provider to describe, before you pay, what they would look at first in your child's marked Paper 2. A provider who answers that question specifically is selling diagnosis; one who answers it with reassurance is selling hours. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson first and a fee discussed once the level and the problem are known.

sections.heading: Fitting Chemistry into an Al Wasl Diploma week
paragraphs: A Diploma student taking Higher Level Chemistry in this cluster is carrying a heavy week before any tutoring is added. Six subjects with homework, laboratory sessions with write-ups, the investigation, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, a Creativity Activity Service commitment, and the mandatory UAE subjects KHDA requires of all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

Those mandatory subjects are not a small factor. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies occupy real periods. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Separate classes are required for Arab and non-Arab students in several of them, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

On timing, schools in this cluster finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.15pm and arrival home along Al Wasl Road lands between about 3.30pm and 4.15pm, with the road at its slowest from four to six. For Chemistry specifically, later is worse than it is for a discussion subject: calculation work and mechanism drawing both degrade sharply when a student is tired. A 5pm start is the practical default, and a weekend morning is better than a 7pm weekday slot for anything quantitative.

Two further realities to plan for rather than discover. During Ramadan sessions typically move to after Iftar, which online delivery handles without anyone travelling, though quantitative work is better placed in the morning if the school day is shortened. And during the mock fortnight most students are better served pausing weekly sessions and sitting papers than adding an hour to an impossible week.

process.title: Name the level
process.description: Higher or Standard. It is the first question because Higher Level Chemistry carries additional content and a longer paper, and the gap between a 5 and a 7 at Higher Level sits almost entirely in material Standard Level never covers. A tutor comfortable at Standard Level is not automatically comfortable above it.

process.title: Send a marked Paper 2
process.description: Not a report. A marked Paper 2 shows whether the marks are going on unstated assumptions, enthalpy signs, missing units, inconsistent significant figures or genuinely absent content. Those need different work, and a report card cannot distinguish between them however carefully it is written.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: One full session online, no cost, no card, in a shared workspace where both people can draw structures and mechanisms. Afterwards you get a written view of where the marks are leaving. If the problem turns out to sit one layer below the topic your child named, we will say which layer.

process.title: Sequence against the school's laboratory and deadline calendar
process.description: The investigation has school deadlines, laboratory access is scheduled, and the May session is fixed. Work follows that order rather than a generic plan: investigation first in Diploma 1, papers first in the final term, and a conversation before each practical about what data to record.

process.title: Weekly notes and an error log by cause
process.description: A short note after each session on what was covered, and once paper work begins a running log of lost marks sorted into causes. The log makes the last two months efficient and gives you an independent way to judge whether the sessions are achieving anything.

whyPoints.title: Level-matched Chemistry specialists
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry cohorts at individual Dubai schools are small, so the specialist pool is small and city-wide. Matching by subject and level rather than by distance from Al Wasl Road is the only way to reach it, and an in-home requirement cuts it to whoever is both qualified and nearby.

whyPoints.title: Mark-scheme behaviour taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Stated assumptions, enthalpy signs, units carried through, consistent significant figures, and explanation questions answered with a reason rather than a restated trend. A student can lose a band across Paper 2 without getting any chemistry wrong, and that is recoverable without learning new content.

whyPoints.title: The data booklet practised, not ignored
whyPoints.description: It is provided in every paper and questions are written to be answered from it. We go through what it contains once, early, then practise finding values under time pressure, which also stops students memorising things the booklet would have given them.

whyPoints.title: A shared workspace that draws
whyPoints.description: Mechanisms, structures and energy profiles all need drawing, and both people drawing in the same space works well on screen. A tutor can also watch a student search the data booklet, which makes the search itself visible and correctable in a way sitting beside them does not.

whyPoints.title: The investigation handled within the rules
whyPoints.description: Criteria explained, scope questioned, drafts answered with marginal questions. No writing, no rewriting, no editing to completion. One operator in this market sells finished internal assessments; a student who buys one risks the Diploma, and we say so on the page.

whyPoints.title: Honest about limits and status
whyPoints.description: No UAE home visits, no Dubai office, no approval claimed from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, no grade promised, and no IB past papers or mark schemes supplied. Home visits are an India-only service. School laboratory work cannot be replaced by any tutor.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry and keeps getting a 5. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly conversion rather than comprehension, and a marked Paper 2 will show it in twenty minutes. The usual pattern is marks lost to an enthalpy sign, to an approximation applied without being stated, to units omitted from a rate constant, and to explanation questions answered by restating the trend the question supplied. None of that is a chemistry failure. A student can lose a band across Paper 2 without getting a single piece of chemistry wrong, and recovering those marks requires no new content at all.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Chemistry genuinely much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference is located rather than general. Higher Level carries additional content and a longer paper, and the extra material is where a 5 and a 7 separate: deeper kinetics with rate equations and the units that go with them, buffer and titration-curve work in acids and bases, and more demanding organic mechanisms. Standard Level is a serious qualification accepted for many courses. A student who takes Standard Level and performs strongly is usually better placed than one who takes Higher Level and cannot cope with the extension.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topics should a tutor start with?
faqs.answer: Usually not the one the student names as hardest, because the difficulty generally sits one layer below. Organic mechanisms that will not stick are often a bonding problem. Equilibrium calculations going wrong are often a stoichiometry problem. Energetics confusion is frequently a sign-convention habit rather than a conceptual gap. Finding the layer underneath is most of the diagnostic value of a first session, and it is why the session starts with a marked script rather than with a topic list.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep losing marks on Paper 1 multiple choice?
faqs.answer: On the quantitative items, almost always, and almost always because of speed. Paper 1 offers no partial credit, so a student who understands a calculation but works too slowly to finish it will mark the answer they reasoned towards rather than computed, and will be wrong a meaningful share of the time on exactly the questions they could have secured. The fix is speed on standard calculation routines rather than more content, and it is one of the quicker wins available in the subject.

faqs.question: How important is the Chemistry data booklet?
faqs.answer: More important than most students treat it. A data booklet and periodic table are provided in every Chemistry examination, and a meaningful number of questions are written to be answered from them. The skills are mundane and worth drilling: finding an electrode potential with the sign convention the right way round, locating a bond enthalpy and knowing it is an average, matching an infrared range to a functional group. Going through the booklet once, early, also stops students memorising things it would have given them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Chemistry scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, and the boundary should be stated to the student at the outset. A tutor may explain the criteria, model an investigation on an unrelated question, check whether the proposed method can actually answer the question, and read a draft and respond with questions. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of it. The most valuable legitimate help is early: narrowing the research question until the apparatus and time available can genuinely answer it, which is where most weak investigations were decided.

faqs.question: How are practical skills taught if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work stays at school, where the apparatus and supervision are, and no tutoring arrangement replaces that. What a tutor works on is the examined part: variable control and why a specific control matters, uncertainty propagation, reading a results table for trend against noise, identifying which error actually affected the conclusion, and evaluating a method against its stated purpose. Those are written skills assessed in both papers and in the investigation, and a large share of recoverable marks sits in them.

faqs.question: Will a Chemistry tutor come to our home in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. Chemistry sessions here are one-to-one over live video in a shared workspace where both people can draw mechanisms, structures and energy profiles. For this subject the format works well, and watching a student search the data booklet on a shared screen is arguably more useful than sitting beside them, because the search becomes visible and correctable.

faqs.question: What should my child write down during a school practical to use later?
faqs.answer: More than most students do. Raw data with uncertainties noted rather than rounded values. The apparatus actually used, including its precision. Anything that went wrong or behaved unexpectedly, because that is the material a good evaluation is built from. Any deviation from the planned method. Students regularly return from a laboratory session with data too thin to process properly, and agreeing in advance what to record converts a laboratory hour into usable evidence rather than a vague memory.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry sessions a week do Diploma families in Al Wasl start with?
faqs.answer: One is normal, moving to two in the final term or when the investigation and paper practice both need attention at once. The limit is the student's capacity to do the work between sessions rather than the budget. A full Paper 2 takes well over an hour to sit and roughly as long again to review properly, and a student booked three times a week has no space left to produce the evidence those sessions exist to diagnose. More contact hours past that point produces less progress.

faqs.question: What time of day suits a Chemistry session for a family near Safa Park?
faqs.answer: Earlier than you might think, because quantitative work degrades with tiredness faster than discussion does. Schools here finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.15pm and arrival home at the southern end of Al Wasl lands between 3.30pm and 4.15pm, with the road slowest from four to six. A 5pm start is the practical default. For anything calculation-heavy a weekend morning beats a 7pm weekday slot, and online delivery means no tutor's journey has to be accommodated either way.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Chemistry required for medicine or pharmacy?
faqs.answer: It is commonly specified or strongly preferred for medicine, pharmacy, chemical engineering and several biosciences, but requirements are set by each individual course and vary between universities and countries. The only reliable method is to build the shortlist and read each course's own stated entry requirements, including for UAE universities, rather than relying on a general rule. Do that in Year 11 while the level choice is still open, because discovering a requirement in Year 13 is an expensive way to learn it.

faqs.question: My child is coming into Diploma Chemistry from IGCSE. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Two things, both predictable. Mechanisms have to be explained rather than recalled, which is a different kind of thinking from the structured recall IGCSE rewards, and curly-arrow conventions have to be learned properly because the scheme marks the drawing as well as the products. And the scientific investigation is self-designed rather than prescribed, which is unfamiliar territory for a student used to following a method sheet. Both are addressable in the first term if they are identified then rather than in the spring.

faqs.question: Can you supply IB Chemistry past papers, mark schemes or the data booklet?
faqs.answer: No. Those documents belong to the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright problem rather than a grey area. Your child's school has legitimate access and can provide what is needed, and sessions work from material the student already holds. Be cautious with any site offering a downloadable bundle of IB assessment material, since distributing it is something they have no right to do, which is a reasonable signal about how the rest of the service is run.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Chemistry specialist is available?
faqs.answer: We tell you plainly rather than assigning a general science tutor and hoping. Higher Level Chemistry is one of the thinner categories in this market, and it tightens further during exam terms when specialists are fully committed. You get a clear statement that we do not currently have the right person, a realistic estimate of how long a match would take, and a suggestion for the interim, which is sometimes the school's own department. A mismatched science tutor costs a term.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any IB or KHDA accreditation for teaching Chemistry?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, has no office or centre in the UAE, and is not an IB World School. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing issued to a specific kind of business, and we do not hold one. Treat any provider claiming board accreditation as a provider making a checkable claim.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Chemistry at Higher and Standard Level on the 2023 guide. Each works from released assessment material rather than textbook summaries, marks student answers against the published command terms, and can take a student through organic mechanisms with the curly arrows drawn on a shared screen.

intro.heading: Chemistry marks are lost to the specification, not to the chemistry
paragraphs: A Diploma chemistry student in Arabian Ranches who sits a past Paper 2 and scores six out of eleven on an energetics question has usually understood the energetics. What went wrong was a sign, a unit, or a step the mark scheme wanted written down and the student thought was obvious. That is the characteristic shape of chemistry underperformance at Diploma level, and it is why a chemistry tutor is a different purchase from a chemistry textbook. The textbook explains the content. The tutor shows your child how the content is marked.

The 2023 guide reorganised the course into six strands, three under Structure and three under Reactivity, and removed the option topics and Paper 3 along with them. Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, from the nuclear atom and electron configurations to the mole and ideal gases. Structure 2 covers bonding and structure across the ionic, covalent and metallic models. Structure 3 classifies matter through the periodic table and through organic functional groups. Reactivity 1 asks what drives chemical reactions, Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far, and Reactivity 3 asks what the mechanisms of chemical change are.

That structure matters for tutoring because it decides where a weakness propagates. A student who is shaky on the mole in Structure 1.4 will lose marks in Reactivity 2.1 on amount of chemical change, in titration calculations, in percentage yield, and again in the data analysis of their own investigation. Fixing Structure 1.4 fixes four different question types. Fixing the symptom in one of them fixes nothing. A diagnosis-led tutor works out which strand the error lives in before deciding what to teach.

Arabian Ranches students reach DP Chemistry mainly through JESS Arabian Ranches, which runs the English National Curriculum to IGCSE and then the IB Diploma inside the community, or through the IB campuses a short drive out: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. KHDA inspects all of them annually and publishes the reports. Whichever campus your child attends, the examination is the same, the data booklet is the same, and the mark scheme is the same.

IB Gram delivers chemistry teaching live over video, one-to-one. We do not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches; home visits are an India-only service and no page on this site says otherwise. For a chemistry student the online format is not a compromise. Mechanisms are drawn on a shared screen where both people can annotate them, past-paper scripts are marked side by side with the published mark scheme open, and the spectroscopy data in the booklet is on the screen rather than in a textbook nobody brought.

programmes.description: Chemistry is taught inside integrated science units and assessed against four criteria out of eight each: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. programmes.countryNote: Families around the Ranches reach the MYP at Fairgreen International School, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 runs Core and Extended tiers, with Paper 1 and Paper 3 for Core, Paper 2 and Paper 4 for Extended, and either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 is untiered across two written papers. Neither includes entropy, electrode potentials or reaction mechanisms, which is precisely where DP1 students stall.
programmes.countryNote: JESS Arabian Ranches, Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole School in Motor City and South View School towards Remraam all run IGCSE chemistry. programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines DP courses with a career-related study, so DP Chemistry SL can be taken inside it. The chemistry content and assessment are identical to the full Diploma version. What changes is the amount of time available each week, which changes how many hours of support make sense and when the investigation can realistically be written.
programmes.countryNote: No campus inside Arabian Ranches runs the Career-related Programme, so families considering it look across Dubai. dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the focus of this page. The subject notes below describe the strands and the companion subjects in terms of what each one is assessed on, because that is the information a parent needs in order to judge whether a tutor is talking about the right thing.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL
subjects.description: Paper 1 runs two hours and Paper 2 two hours thirty. The HL-only material concentrates in energy cycles, entropy and spontaneity, the extent of chemical change, proton and electron transfer, and electron-pair sharing reactions. Born-Haber cycles and the Gibbs free energy relationship account for a disproportionate share of HL marks lost.

subjects.name: Chemistry SL
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 each run one hour thirty across the same six strands at reduced depth. SL candidates lose fewer marks to advanced content and more to presentation: unrounded answers, missing units, equations without state symbols, and explanation answers that stop one step short of the mark.

subjects.name: Structure 1: particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: The nuclear atom, electron configurations, counting particles by mass through the mole, and ideal gases. Everything quantitative in the course rests on 1.4. A student who cannot move confidently between mass, moles, concentration and volume will lose marks in four other strands without ever seeing the connection.

subjects.name: Structure 2 and 3: bonding and classification
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic models, the move from models to materials, the periodic table as classification, and organic functional groups. Explanation questions here are marked on the model invoked, so an answer that describes a property without naming the bonding responsible usually scores half of what it could.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: what drives chemical reactions
subjects.description: Measuring enthalpy changes, energy cycles, energy from fuels, and at Higher Level entropy and spontaneity. The arithmetic trap is constant: enthalpy in kilojoules per mole, entropy in joules per kelvin per mole, and a Gibbs calculation that silently fails if the units are not reconciled first.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: how much, how fast, how far
subjects.description: Amount of chemical change, rate of reaction, and the extent of reaction through equilibrium. Equilibrium constant expressions that wrongly include pure solids and liquids, and Le Chatelier answers that give a direction without an effect, are two of the most common repeated errors in the whole course.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.description: Proton transfer, electron transfer, electron sharing and electron-pair sharing reactions. This is where acids and bases, redox and organic chemistry live. Curly arrows are marked on where they start and where they point, so a mechanism drawn with the right products and the wrong arrow origins scores poorly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Useful rather than essential for chemistry. Logarithms matter for pH and pKa work, and comfort with rearranging multi-variable relationships matters for the Gibbs and equilibrium calculations. A chemistry student weak on logarithms will find Reactivity 3.1 harder than the chemistry itself warrants.

subjects.name: Biology HL and SL
subjects.description: The usual partner for medicine and life-science applications. Biology and chemistry share the 2023 assessment architecture exactly, so command-term technique transfers directly, and the two scientific investigations can be planned in the same DP1 term instead of colliding.

subjects.name: Physics HL and SL
subjects.description: The partner for engineering and physical-science routes. Physics uses the same Paper 1A and 1B structure and the same uncertainty conventions, so a student taking both only needs the data-analysis skill taught once, and the second subject then borrows it.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: A chemistry Extended Essay needs a research question answerable with school equipment and reagents a Dubai school can actually obtain. The school supervisor supervises it. Tutoring is confined to teaching the underlying chemistry, discussing method, and giving feedback on drafts the student has written.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK consumes DP1 and DP2 time in ways that collide with the chemistry investigation deadline. A tutor can help a student reason clearly about scientific knowledge claims. A tutor does not produce the essay or the exhibition commentary, which remain the student's own work throughout.

sections.heading: The six strands, and which one your child is actually failing
paragraphs: The 2023 Chemistry guide is organised as two themes with three strands each, and the single most useful thing a parent can do is find out which strand the lost marks are in. Schools report by assessment, not by strand, so a report card showing a four in chemistry says nothing about cause. A tutor reading two marked papers can usually name the strand within one session, because the error signature of each strand is distinctive.

Structure 1 problems look like arithmetic: wrong moles, wrong concentration, an answer to five significant figures when the data supports two. Structure 2 problems look like vocabulary: a property described without the bonding model that causes it. Structure 3 problems look like misclassification, usually of an organic functional group. Reactivity 1 problems are signs and units. Reactivity 2 problems are equilibrium expressions and Le Chatelier answers that stop halfway. Reactivity 3 problems are mechanisms, half-equations and electrode potentials with reversed signs.

The table below sets out each strand with its content and its characteristic failure. Use it as a diagnostic rather than a syllabus summary. A student who recognises their own mistakes in the right-hand column of one row has found the block of teaching worth paying for, and a student who recognises them in four rows has a quantitative problem in Structure 1 rather than four separate problems.

This is also how the teaching order gets decided. Arabian Ranches families often ask for help with organic chemistry because that is the topic the school is currently teaching, and the correct answer is frequently to spend the first fortnight on the mole and on titration arithmetic instead. Organic mechanisms are hard to learn while the quantitative foundation is still shifting underneath them, and the marks recovered from Structure 1 appear in the organic questions anyway.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and what the data booklet is for
paragraphs: Chemistry is assessed in three components and no more. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and is sat as one session containing a multiple-choice part and a data-based part. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent in short and extended response. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent. There is no Paper 3 and there are no options on the current guide, so a tutor or a revision guide still referring to them is working from material your child will never be examined on.

The data booklet is the component parents understand least and students waste most. It is provided in both papers and it contains the periodic table, physical constants, average bond enthalpies, standard electrode potentials and the spectroscopic data ranges for infrared, mass spectrometry and proton nuclear magnetic resonance. A student who has not used it in practice loses time hunting for a value. A student who has used it in practice knows which page carries which table and reads a wavenumber range without thinking about it.

The practical consequence is that data booklet fluency is a trainable skill with a measurable return, and it belongs in past-paper sessions from DP1 rather than in the final month. The same is true of the command terms. Deduce, determine, explain, state and suggest demand different answers, and the mark allocation tells the student how many linked steps the examiner expects. A three-mark explain question answered in one confident sentence scores one mark, however correct the sentence is.

The table sets the components out with their durations at each level. Note that Higher Level sits longer papers rather than extra ones, and that the investigation weighting is identical at both levels. For a DP1 student in Arabian Ranches that last point is the planning fact that matters: the fifth of the grade written at home is worth exactly as much to an SL candidate as to an HL candidate.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme traps that cost the most marks
paragraphs: Six errors account for most of the preventable loss in Diploma chemistry, and all six are presentation rather than understanding. Significant figures come first. An answer is expected to the precision the data supports, and a student who writes out the full calculator display loses the mark on an otherwise perfect calculation. The fix takes one session and holds for two years, which makes it the best value in the entire course.

State symbols come second, and they bite hardest in thermochemistry, where an enthalpy of solution or combustion written without the physical states is incomplete. Signs come third: exothermic enthalpy changes are negative, and the sign on a reversed half-equation reverses with it. Units come fourth, and the recurring disaster is the Gibbs free energy calculation, where an enthalpy term in kilojoules per mole meets an entropy term in joules per kelvin per mole and the student multiplies without converting.

Equilibrium language is fifth. A question that asks for the effect of increased pressure wants the direction of shift and what happens to the quantity named in the question, and an answer giving only the direction scores half. Pure solids and liquids do not appear in the equilibrium constant expression, and they appear in student answers constantly. Mechanisms are sixth. A curly arrow is marked on where it begins and where it points, so an arrow drawn from an atom rather than from a bond or a lone pair loses the mark even when the product is right.

None of this is taught by re-explaining the chemistry, which is why a tutor who only lectures will not move these marks. It is taught by marking the student's own script against the published scheme, naming each loss, and logging it. Most Ranches students who do this consistently for six weeks stop making four of the six errors entirely, and the remaining two become visible enough to catch in the examination hall.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: the mechanisms and how they are actually marked
paragraphs: Organic chemistry sits in Structure 3.2 for classification and in Reactivity 3.3 and 3.4 for mechanism, and it is the part of the course where Ranches students most often ask for help. The content is finite and learnable. The marking is unforgiving in a specific way: the examiner is looking at the arrows, the intermediates and the charges, not only at the product. A student who can predict the product of every reaction in the syllabus and cannot draw the arrows will score poorly on the mechanism questions and well on everything else.

Nucleophilic substitution is the clearest example. The choice between the two pathways is decided by the substrate class, with tertiary halogenoalkanes going through a carbocation and primary ones through a single concerted step, and the explanation marks come from the stability argument rather than from the label. Electrophilic addition to alkenes needs the intermediate drawn with its charge in the right place. Elimination, condensation and the reactions of carboxylic acids and their derivatives each have a small number of examinable mechanisms, and the set is small enough to drill properly.

Spectroscopy is the other half of the organic marks and the half most often neglected. Mass spectrometry fragments, infrared absorption ranges and proton nuclear magnetic resonance chemical shifts are all in the data booklet, and the question is almost always the same shape: identify the compound from three pieces of evidence. The technique is to narrow by functional group from the infrared data, count environments from the nuclear magnetic resonance integration and splitting, then confirm the molecular mass. Students who learn that order stop guessing.

An online session is a good place for this work because the structures can be drawn and annotated on a shared screen in a way a textbook diagram cannot be. The student draws the mechanism, the tutor marks the arrows in a second colour, and the error is visible rather than described. Over a six-week block most students move from drawing mechanisms from memory to constructing them from the substrate, which is the shift the examination rewards.

sections.heading: Past-paper work that actually changes a chemistry grade
paragraphs: Most students do past papers badly, and doing them badly is worse than not doing them, because it builds confidence on top of an unfixed error. The pattern that works has four steps and a tutor is useful at two of them. The student sits the paper under timed conditions without notes. The student marks it against the published scheme without mercy. The tutor reviews the marked script and classifies every loss as content, technique or presentation. The next block of teaching attacks the largest category.

Classification is the step that students cannot do alone, because a loss that feels like not knowing the chemistry is frequently a presentation error wearing a disguise. A student who wrote the right idea in two steps for a three-mark question did not fail to know the chemistry. A student who used the right method and lost the final mark to significant figures did not fail either. Separating those cases changes what the next month is spent on, and it is the single highest-value thing a chemistry tutor does.

The second place a tutor earns the fee is in choosing which papers to sit. Past material from the previous guide still contains useful questions on bonding, periodicity and organic chemistry, and is misleading on entropy, options and the removed Paper 3. Specimen and released material for the current guide is the only reliable source of question style for Paper 1B. A student working through a decade of old papers in syllabus order is spending real hours on components that no longer exist.

Reproduction is the boundary worth stating plainly. IB Gram does not host, copy or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. Those belong to the IB and to the examination boards, and the legitimate route is the school, the official store or the board's own site. A tutor works from material the student or the school already holds legally, and a provider offering a downloadable archive of papers is offering something it is not entitled to give away.
