sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks, four criteria, 3,000 words
paragraphs: The investigation is 20 per cent of the chemistry grade and it is assessed against four criteria worth six marks each. Research design covers the research question, the methodology and the handling of variables. Data analysis covers processing, uncertainty and presentation. Conclusion covers the interpretation against the research question and the comparison with accepted values. Evaluation covers the strengths, the limitations and realistic improvements. Twenty-four marks, with a report limit of 3,000 words.

Most lost marks sit in two places. The research question is too broad, so no amount of good data can answer it, and the evaluation is generic, listing human error and equipment accuracy rather than naming the specific limitation that affected this experiment. Both are preventable at the planning stage and almost impossible to repair once the data is collected, which is why the useful time to talk to a tutor about an investigation is before the laboratory work rather than after it.

The boundary on what a tutor may do is strict and it protects your child. Teaching is permitted: what a controlled variable is, why the examiner wants it justified, how to propagate an uncertainty, whether a relationship should be linearised, what a high-scoring evaluation contains. Feedback on a draft the student has written is permitted, and it is exactly what a school supervisor also gives. Writing, rewriting, editing to completion, handing over a research question to be adopted wholesale, or supplying data are not permitted, and IB Gram does not do them.

Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright, with a price list. Treat that as a warning rather than an option: the malpractice consequence falls on the student, not on the seller, and it can end a Diploma. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to the Theory of Knowledge essay. Your child's school supervisor stays in charge of the investigation throughout, and a tutor who suggests otherwise has told you something important about themselves.

sections.heading: From Cambridge 0620 to DP Chemistry: the measurable gap
paragraphs: A Ranches student arriving in DP1 from Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 or Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 meets five genuinely new things, and knowing which five turns a vague feeling of difficulty into a work plan. Entropy and spontaneity are new. Standard electrode potentials and quantitative electrochemistry are new. Reaction mechanisms with curly arrows are new. Spectroscopic identification is new. And the expectation that an explanation is constructed in linked steps, each worth a mark, is new in kind rather than in degree.

What is not new is most of the content. Bonding, periodicity, acids and bases, rates, equilibrium qualitatively, and organic functional groups all appear at IGCSE in recognisable form. The Diploma asks for the same ideas at greater depth and with quantitative treatment attached. That is why a student who was comfortable at IGCSE can be uncomfortable in DP1 without having forgotten anything: the questions have changed shape rather than subject.

The transition map below lists the gaps with an honest estimate of how much support each usually needs. Those estimates come from the pattern of enquiries rather than from a study, so treat them as planning figures and not as promises. A student who closes the quantitative gap in Structure 1 early tends to need less help with everything after it, which is the single most useful thing a Year 11 Ranches family can act on during the summer before DP1.

The double-award routes deserve a separate note. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Pearson Edexcel Double Award Science 4SD0 cover less chemistry than the separate syllabuses, so the gap into DP Chemistry from a double award is wider, especially in organic chemistry and in quantitative work. A student moving from 0654 into Chemistry HL should assume a term of catching up and should plan for it in Year 11 rather than discovering it in October.

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs for an Arabian Ranches family
paragraphs: Think in monthly terms first, because that is how a tuition decision is actually made inside a household budget. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 research puts the monthly cost of a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures are the publishers' own.

Converted to an hourly view the same research puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase lists AED 270, and BartyED's examiner-led tier sits at AED 650. At the budget end EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour online.

Two conclusions follow for a chemistry family. The first is that the specialist premium is modest in monthly terms and large in effect: the difference between a generalist and a chemistry specialist is a few hundred dirhams a month, and it decides whether anyone in the room understands why a curly arrow lost a mark. The second is that frequency costs more than quality. Going from one session a week to three triples the bill; going from a generalist to a specialist does not.

Set that against school fees for context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula. Tutoring is the part of the education budget that still moves year to year, which is why a family should decide what it is buying before deciding how much of it to buy. IB Gram does not publish a rate card here; the free trial and a short conversation establish the plan first.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and what IB Gram is not
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is legal and regulated. The route for an individual is a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website or e-services system.

Tutoring without that permit exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of fines has been published, so any specific amount quoted at a parent should be treated with suspicion. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct works the same way. A chemistry teacher offering to tutor their own class privately is not a convenience; it is a problem for both of you.

On regulators, the position is worth stating precisely because competitors blur it. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by any of them, nor by the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims no partnership with any school or school group.

There is also no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and no phone number outside the region is used as the route to reach us. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai would require a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation with an initial approval stage, a six-month window to complete the licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. We do not hold it, so we do not describe ourselves as though we did.

faqs.question: What does the 2023 IB Chemistry syllabus cover at HL that SL leaves out?
faqs.answer: Higher Level runs to 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra material concentrates in five places: energy cycles and Born-Haber treatment, entropy and spontaneity through Gibbs free energy, quantitative equilibrium, standard electrode potentials and cell calculations, and additional depth in organic mechanisms and spectroscopy. The assessment components are identical in kind; Higher Level simply sits longer papers. For a Ranches student the practical test of readiness for HL is not interest in chemistry but comfort with algebraic rearrangement and with logarithms.

faqs.question: How are marks split between Paper 1, Paper 2 and the investigation in IB Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and is sat as a single session containing a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent in short and extended response. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent and is written over roughly ten hours of class time, to a limit of 3,000 words. There is no Paper 3 on the current guide and there are no option topics. Paper 2 is therefore the largest single component, and the investigation is the only part written outside an examination hall.

faqs.question: Why do strong students still lose marks on IB Chemistry Paper 1B data questions?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1B tests the tools and inquiry skills that are taught across the course rather than in a unit of their own, so they are rarely drilled. The recurring losses are percentage uncertainty, combining uncertainties through a multiplication, obtaining an uncertainty on a gradient from maximum and minimum lines, and judging whether a stated conclusion is actually supported by the data. A student who is strong on content frequently has never practised any of it against a mark scheme. It is the most improvable component in the course.

faqs.question: Which organic mechanisms come up most often in IB Chemistry HL papers?
faqs.answer: Nucleophilic substitution in both pathways, electrophilic addition to alkenes, elimination, and the reactions of carboxylic acids and their derivatives including condensation. The examinable set is small enough to drill properly in a few weeks. The marks sit on the arrows and the intermediates rather than on the product: an arrow must start at a bond or a lone pair, an intermediate must carry its charge in the right place, and the choice of pathway must be justified by substrate class and carbocation stability rather than asserted.

faqs.question: How many marks does each criterion of the IB Chemistry investigation carry?
faqs.answer: Six each, across four criteria, giving 24 marks in total for 20 per cent of the grade. Research design covers the research question, methodology and variables. Data analysis covers processing, uncertainty and presentation. Conclusion covers interpretation against the research question and comparison with accepted values. Evaluation covers strengths, limitations and realistic improvements. The report limit is 3,000 words. Most lost marks sit in criterion A, where the research question is too broad, and criterion D, where the evaluation is generic rather than specific to this experiment.

faqs.question: Can my child practise chemistry past papers properly over a video lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for marking clinics the online format is better than sitting side by side. The student sits the paper in their own time, uploads the script, and the session is spent marking it against the published scheme with both people looking at the same screen. Errors are classified as content, technique or presentation and logged. Mechanisms are drawn by the student and annotated by the tutor in a second colour. The one thing that cannot happen online is the laboratory work, which belongs to the school in any case.

faqs.question: What is the chemistry data booklet allowed to do for my child in an exam?
faqs.answer: It is provided in both written papers and it carries the periodic table, physical constants, average bond enthalpies, standard electrode potentials and the spectroscopic data ranges for infrared, mass spectrometry and proton nuclear magnetic resonance. It does not carry worked methods or definitions. The value of practising with it is speed: a student who knows which page holds which table reads a wavenumber range without breaking concentration, while a student meeting it for the first time in the hall loses minutes they cannot recover.

faqs.question: How much does one-to-one IB Chemistry tuition cost for an Arabian Ranches family?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai research, with TutorChase listing AED 270, Unitors quoting IB from AED 200, and BartyED's examiner tier at AED 650. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300. In monthly terms the same research estimates AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support at one session a week. Those are other companies' published rates. IB Gram does not post a rate card here; the trial lesson comes first.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry HL necessary for medicine applications from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, but the requirement belongs to the university rather than to the IB, and it varies. Many medical schools in the United Kingdom, Ireland and the Gulf expect Chemistry at Higher Level, often with Biology, and some specify a minimum grade in each. The only reliable method is to read the entry requirements for each named university your child is considering, then work backwards into Year 12 subject choices. No tutoring provider can tell you what a given admissions office will require, and any that claims to should be read carefully.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a week does a DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session is the common pattern for a student who is broadly on track and losing marks to technique. Two becomes sensible where a whole strand is missing, typically entropy or electrochemistry, because new content needs teaching and then consolidating. Three is an intensive arrangement that makes sense for a defined block before mock examinations rather than as a standing commitment. Frequency is the expensive variable in a tuition budget, so it is worth being honest about whether the problem is coverage or technique before buying more hours.

faqs.question: What goes wrong when a student moves from IGCSE Chemistry 0620 into DP Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Five things are genuinely new: entropy and spontaneity, standard electrode potentials and quantitative electrochemistry, reaction mechanisms with curly arrows, spectroscopic identification, and the expectation that explanations are built in linked steps worth a mark each. Most of the remaining content is familiar at greater depth. Students from the double-award routes, Cambridge 0654 or Edexcel 4SD0, face a wider gap than students from 0620 or 4CH1, particularly in organic chemistry and quantitative work, and should plan for it during Year 11.

faqs.question: Does my child need equipment at home for chemistry practical work?
faqs.answer: No. The practical programme, the laboratory, the equipment for the scientific investigation and the supervision of experiments all belong to the school, whether that is JESS Arabian Ranches, Fairgreen International School or GEMS International School Al Khail. An online tutor works on theory, data handling, question technique and the written report. No apparatus is needed at home, and a tutor who offers to supply experimental data for an investigation is offering something that would put your child's Diploma at risk.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor mark my child's investigation draft for them?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft your child has written and give feedback on it, which is the same thing a school supervisor does. That includes pointing out that a conclusion is not supported by the data, that an evaluation is generic, or that the uncertainty treatment is incomplete. What a tutor must not do is write, rewrite or edit the report to completion, supply the research question to be adopted, or provide data. IB Gram works only on the feedback side of that line, and the school supervisor remains the supervisor.

faqs.question: Which Arabian Ranches schools teach IB Chemistry rather than A Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: JESS Arabian Ranches runs the IB Diploma after IGCSE, inside the community. Nearby, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills all offer the Diploma. Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills and GEMS Metropole School in Motor City follow the British route to A Level instead. Check the current KHDA inspection report for any campus you are considering rather than relying on a summary on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Should a Year 11 Ranches student start chemistry support before DP1 begins?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is the cheapest intervention available. The summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the right window to make quantitative work in Structure 1 automatic: moving between mass, moles, concentration and volume quickly and precisely, and getting significant figures right by habit. That foundation appears in every later strand and in the investigation. Two or three sessions in August do more for a Diploma chemistry grade than the same hours bought in a panic the following March, and they cost the same.

intro.heading: Why chemistry costs more here than any other Diploma subject
paragraphs: Chemistry is the most expensive Diploma subject to tutor in Dubai, and the explanation is boring: there are fewer people who can do it. A graduate chemist is not automatically a Diploma Chemistry teacher. The current guide, with its Structure and Reactivity organisation and its single scientific investigation replacing the old internal assessment, is recent enough that a tutor whose experience predates it will teach a course that no longer exists in that shape. Families pay the scarcity premium either knowingly or by accident, and this page is written so it is knowingly.

The published Dubai bands set the frame. Qualified online subject tutors are advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-track tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 depending on travel, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts ordinary in-home sessions at AED 180 to 350. Chemistry sits in the specialist band rather than the qualified-tutor band for most families, and pretending otherwise would be a quotation rather than information.

What the premium should buy is specific. A Diploma Chemistry specialist can tell you, without looking anything up, that Paper 1 is worth 36% of the grade and splits into a multiple-choice Paper 1A and a data-based Paper 1B; that Paper 2 carries 44%; that the scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% across four criteria worth six marks each; and that organic mechanisms and energetics are where Higher Level students lose most. A tutor who cannot do that is charging a specialist rate for general chemistry teaching.

Arabian Ranches 2 adds a geographic version of the same problem. There is no secondary school inside the community, so every Diploma student is bussed out towards Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Nad Al Sheba, Al Barsha South or the Sustainable City. The pool of Diploma Chemistry specialists living within a sensible drive of Casa, Rosa, Palma, Lila, Camelia, Azalea, Reem, Yasmin and Rasha is very small. Searching by proximity in this subject does not filter for quality; it filters quality out.

IB Gram delivers Diploma Chemistry support to this community one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The trade is straightforward: you give up a person at the table, and the specialist filter stops competing with a map. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the publisher named next to it and describes the market, never our own price list.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.programmesIntro: Three stages shape a chemistry spend in this community: what arrived from IGCSE or MYP, which level the Diploma student is sitting, and what the grade is being bought for after school.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Organised into Structure and Reactivity rather than the older topic list. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much, how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level extends each of these rather than adding separate topics.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the subject is usually taken at Higher Level by students aiming at medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, chemical engineering or materials science, and at Standard Level as a second science. The Higher Level cohort in this catchment is small enough that schools often run a single class, which is part of why private support is in demand.

programmes.name: Standard and Higher Level, as a buying decision
programmes.description: The assessment architecture is the same at both levels and the papers are longer at Higher Level: Paper 1 runs 1h30 at SL and 2h at HL; Paper 2 runs 1h30 at SL and 2h30 at HL. The weightings do not change - 36%, 44% and 20%. What changes is depth, and the depth lands heaviest in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms.
programmes.countryNote: Moving between levels is a registration decision handled by the school's Diploma coordinator and tied to a deadline. Any family in Arabian Ranches 2 with genuine doubts about an HL Chemistry placement should get that deadline in writing during DP1 rather than discovering in the final term that only the exam remains.

programmes.name: What arrives from IGCSE and MYP
programmes.description: Most students in this catchment arrive from Cambridge 0620 Extended, Pearson 4CH1 or MYP Sciences. None of those requires the quantitative fluency Diploma Chemistry assumes from term one, and the mole calculations that felt sufficient at IGCSE are the ones that fail in DP1 under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: The gap is narrow and specific: moles in multi-step calculations, limiting reagents, writing and balancing equations fast enough to be invisible, and reading a question for what it actually asks. Ten to fifteen hours in the summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the cheapest chemistry intervention available here and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: What the grade is being bought for
programmes.description: Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering are the usual destinations, and many of those programmes publish a requirement for Chemistry at Higher Level. Requirements are set per university and per programme and change between admission cycles, so the published requirement for the named course is the only reliable reference.
programmes.countryNote: For students applying inside the UAE, check whether Ministry of Education equivalency is required for the route and verify the current rules with the Ministry directly. No tutor performs or guarantees that process, and published summaries of it go out of date. Ask the admissions office in writing which level of chemistry they expect.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.subjectsIntro: A chemistry budget is spent on parts of the course, and those parts differ enormously in how many marks an hour returns. The list below is what sessions are actually built from.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.description: Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and radical substitution, with the Higher Level extension into electron-pair sharing reactions. The single largest source of lost marks in the subject, because mechanisms must be drawn precisely and a half-remembered arrow earns nothing. Responds well to repetition and badly to reading.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: what drives chemical reactions
subjects.description: Energetics, enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs energy. Students can usually recite the definitions and still lose marks on sign conventions and on reading an energy cycle in the direction the question requires. Six to ten hours shifts this reliably.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: how much, how fast and how far
subjects.description: Stoichiometric calculation, rates, equilibrium and acid-base chemistry, with the Higher Level work on equilibrium constants and buffers. Quantitative and therefore diagnosable from a marked script, which makes it one of the better-value blocks to buy early rather than late.

subjects.name: Structure 1: the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Models of the atom, electron configuration, ionisation and the quantitative treatment of amount of substance. The foundation the rest of the course assumes, and the place where an IGCSE-to-DP gap shows up first as slowness rather than as error.

subjects.name: Structure 2: models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic models, intermolecular forces, and the Higher Level work on formal charge and molecular orbital ideas. Explanation questions here reward precise language, and students lose marks for describing when the command term asked them to explain.

subjects.name: Structure 3: classification of matter
subjects.description: Periodicity, the periodic table as a predictive tool, organic nomenclature and functional groups, and spectroscopic identification at Higher Level. Nomenclature is cheap to fix and frequently left broken, which costs marks across every organic question in both papers.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data-based questions
subjects.description: The part of Paper 1 that is not multiple choice: interpreting data, spotting trends, handling uncertainty and explaining an anomaly. Almost nobody practises it separately, which makes it a reliable source of recoverable marks for a student already competent on content.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, around ten hours of work, 3,000 words maximum, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. sections.heading: What the chemistry premium actually pays for
paragraphs: Start with what is scarce rather than with a price. The scarce thing in Dubai is somebody who has taught Diploma Chemistry under the current guide, through a full two-year cycle, including the scientific investigation. Chemistry graduates are not scarce. Teachers who can explain electrophilic addition are not scarce. The combination of subject depth, current-guide familiarity and marked-script experience is, and in a market with a small Higher Level cohort per school it stays scarce.

That is what sits inside the specialist band. Published Dubai figures put IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; qualified online subject tutors sit lower at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; premium named or examiner-track tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. For Standard Level chemistry the qualified band is often enough. For Higher Level mechanisms and the investigation, it usually is not.

The in-home band is a separate question and should not be confused with quality. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts ordinary in-home sessions at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, and the increment over the online band is travel. For a family in Camelia or Azalea the drive from the city is long, so the premium is at its highest here while the teaching is identical. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at all, so no travel appears in any figure we quote.

Below all of this sits the budget band at roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. It has a legitimate use in chemistry: supervised study, keeping a student company while they work through questions they can already attempt. It has no useful role in organic mechanisms or in the investigation, and buying it for those is the most common way a chemistry budget produces nothing.

sections.heading: The course your child is sitting, in the shape the guide uses
paragraphs: Diploma Chemistry is now organised into two halves rather than a list of topics, and a tutor who talks about topic numbers from an older guide is a warning sign worth acting on. Structure covers three areas: models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level deepens each of these rather than bolting separate units onto the end.

That reorganisation has a practical consequence for tutoring. Questions now cut across the old boundaries deliberately, so a student who learned chemistry as separate chapters answers badly even when they know the content. A question about an organic reaction can demand nomenclature from Structure 3, a mechanism from Reactivity 3 and an energetic justification from Reactivity 1 in consecutive parts. Teaching has to follow the same connections, which is a skill, not a syllabus.

The tutoring implication for a family in Arabian Ranches 2 is about sequencing rather than volume. Working through the course in the order the school teaches it is sensible in DP1. In DP2 it stops being sensible, because the exam does not respect that order. Sessions should begin to run across areas, and the marked script is what tells you which combinations your child cannot handle.

One practical point that saves wasted hours. The chemistry data booklet is provided in the examination, so time spent memorising constants, ionisation data and bond enthalpies is time taken away from using them. A disconcerting number of students arrive at a first session with flashcards for information that will be printed in front of them, and redirecting that effort is often the quickest improvement available in the first fortnight.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: where the eighty per cent sits
paragraphs: Eighty per cent of a Diploma Chemistry grade is examined on two papers, and they reward different things. Paper 1 carries 36% and has two parts: Paper 1A, which is multiple choice, and Paper 1B, which is data-based. Paper 2 carries 44% and consists of short and extended response questions. At Standard Level Paper 1 runs an hour and a half and Paper 2 an hour and a half; at Higher Level Paper 1 runs two hours and Paper 2 two and a half.

Paper 1B is the component most often left unpractised, and it is the cheapest source of recoverable marks in the subject. It asks students to read data, identify a trend, handle uncertainty and account for an anomaly. None of that is content revision, and a student who is strong on content frequently loses marks here simply because they have never sat a set of these questions under time. Two or three sessions of deliberate Paper 1B work is some of the best value available at specialist rates.

Paper 2 is where command terms decide outcomes. A four-mark explain question wants four distinct creditable points, and a student who writes a paragraph of correct chemistry without separating them loses marks they have genuinely earned in their head. This is trainable, fast, and unglamorous: write the mark allocation next to each answer, count the points, repeat. It is also the work that most often lifts a grade that content teaching alone had stalled.

Multiple choice in Paper 1A has its own discipline. The commonest loss is not ignorance but rushing: reading three of four options, or missing a negative in the stem. Timed sets with the errors categorised afterwards sort this out in a handful of sessions, and it is work a student can do independently once a tutor has shown them how to mark and classify their own attempts.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: the block most families pay for twice
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is bought twice by a predictable number of families in this community, and the pattern is worth naming because avoiding it saves a four-figure sum. The first purchase happens in DP1, when mechanisms are first taught and a student finds them impossible. Six sessions produce apparent understanding, the topic test improves, and the tutoring stops. The second purchase happens in DP2, when the same student cannot reproduce any of it under exam conditions.

The reason is that mechanisms are a motor skill as much as a knowledge item. Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and radical substitution each have to be drawn correctly, with arrows starting and ending in the right places, quickly, without reference. Understanding them is a one-session job. Being able to produce them cold, nine months later, is a repetition job, and repetition does not happen in a session that ends with a satisfied student.

The cheap fix is structural rather than financial. After the DP1 block, the student should draw the mechanisms they have learned once a week for ten minutes, from memory, and check them. A tutor can set that up in one session and audit it monthly. Families who do this do not buy organic chemistry a second time; families who do not, reliably do, and the second purchase lands in the most expensive month of the two years.

The same principle applies to a shorter list of other items: enthalpy cycle conventions, equilibrium expressions, and the rules of organic nomenclature. These are all things a student can hold for a fortnight and lose by the spring. Identifying them early, and converting them into short recurring self-tests rather than repeat teaching, is how a chemistry budget stays inside what a family actually planned to spend.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 20%, four criteria and a hard boundary
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent of the Diploma Chemistry grade, takes around ten hours of student work and is limited to 3,000 words. It is assessed on four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. That structure is worth knowing as a parent, because it tells you what the work should look like at each stage and when outside help is genuinely useful.

Research design is where most of the damage is done, and it is done early. A question that cannot generate enough data, a variable that cannot be controlled in a school laboratory, or a method that produces a single measurement rather than a range will cap the other three criteria no matter how well the write-up is done. One session at the design stage is worth three at the write-up stage, and it is the point at which a specialist earns the specialist rate.

Evaluation is where marks are most commonly left on the table. It asks for a genuine assessment of the method's weaknesses and realistic improvements, and students write apologies instead: more repeats, better equipment, more time. A chemistry specialist can push a student towards the specific limitations of their own measurements, which is what the criterion rewards. This is feedback on the student's own work rather than contribution to it.

The boundary is absolute and worth stating in plain words before any booking. A tutor may teach the chemistry involved, explain a technique, question whether a conclusion is supported by the data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor may write the investigation, draft any section of it, or provide text that ends up in the submission. This is the IB's academic-honesty requirement, the consequence of breaching it falls on the student, and we would rather decline the work than blur it.

sections.heading: A two-year chemistry spend plan for this community
paragraphs: Laid out across two years, chemistry spending has a natural shape that is cheaper than the shape most families end up with. Cheapest first: a summer block between Year 11 and DP1, closing the quantitative gap from IGCSE chemistry. Then light weekly support through DP1 while mechanisms and energetics are taught. Then a short investigation block at the design stage. Then timed paper work in the final stretch, which is expensive but short.

The version families actually buy is the inverse: nothing until the first DP2 report, then specialist-band intensity for three months. It costs more and produces less, because the final months are the worst time to teach content and the best time to practise papers. A plan that front-loads the cheap work and reserves the expensive band for paper technique is the single biggest saving available in this subject.

Some context for the household budget while planning. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector is also expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

The figures in the table below are built from published market bands and are a planning tool, not a quotation. They assume one subject at Higher Level and a student who is doing the independent work between sessions. A family running chemistry and physics together should double the weekly rows and then ask seriously whether both are genuinely weak, because the commonest cause of two weak sciences is a single shared quantitative problem.

sections.heading: Practical chemistry when the lesson is on a screen
paragraphs: The fair question about online chemistry support is what happens to practical work. The honest answer has two halves. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school: your child does their practical programme and their investigation in their own school laboratory, with their own teacher supervising, and no tutoring arrangement changes that or should try to.

What a tutor can do is everything around it. Designing a method that will actually generate usable data. Deciding what to measure and how many times. Working out which uncertainties matter and which are noise. Reading a results table and identifying the anomaly worth discussing. Those are the skills Paper 1B and the investigation criteria reward, and they are discussion and analysis tasks that work as well on a shared screen as across a table - sometimes better, because the data is on the screen for both people.

Where online support needs deliberate effort is the mechanical side: apparatus handling, titration technique, recognising a colour change at the right moment. A tutor cannot teach the hands. What they can do is make sure the student knows what they are looking for before they walk into the laboratory, and debrief properly afterwards from the results. Ask any chemistry tutor how they handle that, because the answer distinguishes someone who has taught the subject from someone who has studied it.

The shared-screen advantage is real for the parts of chemistry that are drawing. A mechanism drawn by a student on a shared whiteboard, corrected arrow by arrow, is a better teaching episode than the same correction made on paper across a table, because the correction is visible, recordable and reviewable later. For the subject's single largest source of lost marks, the format is an advantage rather than a compromise.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry in the Gulf evening peak is one of the hardest intersections in this market to staff, and the honest response is to say so rather than to fill the slot. If no HL Chemistry specialist is free at your preferred time, we will tell you, set out the alternatives with the rate attached, and let you decide: a different weekday slot with the right person, a weekend slot, or a specialist whose hours sit outside the Gulf peak. What we will not do is put a general science tutor in front of an HL student because the hour was available.

On the legal framework, private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work and the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No official fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here, and figures circulating online should be treated with caution. One arrangement is ruled out regardless of availability: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Two further limits, stated so they are not discovered later. IB Gram does not hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the licence a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires, because we operate no premises in the UAE. And we do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference the official sources and link to them, and the papers your child practises on come from the school or the board's own site.

faqs.question: Why does an IB Chemistry tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 cost more than a maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Supply. The pool of people who have taught Diploma Chemistry under the current guide through a full two-year cycle, including the scientific investigation, is small in Dubai, and Higher Level cohorts in individual schools are often a single class. Published bands put IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. For Standard Level content the lower band is often enough; for Higher Level organic work it usually is not.

faqs.question: How are the marks split across the Diploma Chemistry components?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and contains two parts: Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, data-based questions. Paper 2 carries 44% and consists of short and extended response questions. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%. At Standard Level both papers run an hour and a half; at Higher Level Paper 1 runs two hours and Paper 2 two and a half. The weightings are identical at both levels - only the paper lengths and the depth change.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why is it worth paying attention to?
faqs.answer: Paper 1B is the data-based half of Paper 1. It asks a student to read data, identify a trend, handle uncertainty and account for an anomaly, and it is almost never practised separately. That makes it the cheapest recoverable marks in the subject: a student who is strong on content frequently loses marks here purely from unfamiliarity with the question style under time. Two or three sessions of deliberate Paper 1B work often returns more than the same hours spent on further content.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand organic mechanisms and then forget them completely?
faqs.answer: Because drawing a mechanism is closer to a motor skill than a fact. Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and radical substitution each need arrows that start and end in precise places, produced quickly and without reference. Understanding takes one session; retention takes weekly repetition. This is why families buy organic chemistry twice - once in DP1 when it is taught, once in DP2 when it cannot be reproduced. Ten minutes a week drawing from memory prevents the second purchase.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade is the scientific investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Standard and Higher Level. It involves around ten hours of student work, is limited to 3,000 words, and is assessed on four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is the highest-leverage stage because a question that cannot generate enough data, or a variable that cannot be controlled in a school laboratory, caps the three later criteria no matter how carefully the write-up is done.

faqs.question: What is a chemistry tutor allowed to do on the scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Teach the chemistry involved, explain a technique, question whether the conclusion is actually supported by the data, point out that an evaluation is generic, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. What no tutor may do is write the investigation, draft any section of it, or supply text that ends up in the submission. The rule is the IB's academic-honesty requirement rather than a company policy, and the penalty for breaching it lands on the student.

faqs.question: Where do students lose the most marks in Diploma Chemistry evaluation sections?
faqs.answer: In writing apologies instead of evaluations. The criterion asks for a genuine assessment of the method's specific weaknesses and realistic improvements, and students commonly offer more repeats, better equipment and more time. None of that engages with their own measurements. A specialist can push a student towards the particular limitations of the data they actually collected, which is what earns the marks, and that work is feedback on the student's own investigation rather than a contribution to it.

faqs.question: Should we buy chemistry help in the summer before DP1?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest effective purchase in the two years, and almost nobody makes it. Students arriving from Cambridge 0620 Extended, Pearson 4CH1 or MYP Sciences are rarely quantitatively fluent enough for Diploma pace: moles in multi-step calculations, limiting reagents and balancing equations fast enough to be invisible. Ten to fifteen hours in that summer closes a gap that otherwise shows up as apparent weakness across the whole of DP1 term one and costs far more to fix then.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Chemistry necessary for medicine?
faqs.answer: Many medical, dental and pharmacy programmes publish a requirement for Chemistry at Higher Level, but requirements are set per university and per programme and change between admission cycles. The only reliable reference is the published requirement for the specific course your child is applying to, confirmed in writing by the admissions office. Do not rely on a general rule, including this answer, and do not let any tutor imply that their support is needed for an admissions outcome.

faqs.question: Can my child do practical chemistry properly if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work stays with the school: the practical programme and the investigation are done in the school laboratory under the school's supervision, and no tutoring arrangement changes that. What a tutor adds is the thinking around it - method design, what to measure and how often, which uncertainties matter, how to read a results table and identify the anomaly worth discussing. Those are analysis tasks that work well on a shared screen, where the data is visible to both people at once.

faqs.question: Does moving from Higher to Standard Level chemistry save money?
faqs.answer: It can reduce the hours needed, but it is a registration decision handled by the school's Diploma coordinator with a deadline attached, not something to arrange quietly in the final term. Ask the coordinator for the actual deadline during DP1 and get it in writing. Also check what the change does to university applications first: if a published entry requirement names Chemistry at Higher Level, a cheaper two years may cost more later. Decide on the destination, then on the level.

faqs.question: Do we need to memorise constants and bond enthalpies for the chemistry exams?
faqs.answer: No, and time spent on it is time taken from using the information. The chemistry data booklet is provided in the examination, so constants, ionisation data and bond enthalpy values are printed in front of the candidate. A surprising number of students arrive at a first session with flashcards for data they will be given, and redirecting that effort into applying it is often the fastest improvement available in the first fortnight of support.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for chemistry across the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Plan it in stages rather than as a monthly subscription. Published bands suggest roughly AED 1,500 to 4,500 for a ten to fifteen hour summer block before DP1, AED 600 to 1,200 a month for weekly support during DP1 and DP2 term one, AED 800 to 1,800 for a short investigation block at the design stage, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for two sessions a week in the final six to eight weeks. Front-loading the cheap work is what keeps the total down.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level chemistry specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with the real alternatives and their rates: a different weekday time with the right specialist, a weekend slot, or a tutor whose working hours sit outside the Gulf evening peak. What we will not do is put a general science tutor in front of a Higher Level chemistry student because the hour was free. Higher Level Chemistry at peak Gulf time is one of the hardest intersections in this market to staff, and disclosing that is cheaper for everyone than concealing it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us IB past papers and mark schemes for chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to. IB, Cambridge and Pearson materials are copyright, and reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is not something a legitimate tutor does. The papers your child practises on should come from the school or from the board's own site. A tutor's job is to set work from legitimate sources, mark it properly and explain what the marks were awarded for.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach DP Chemistry rather than science in general. Each one is matched to a level first and a timetable second, because an IB Chemistry HL student eleven weeks from a mock and an IB Chemistry SL student starting their investigation need two different people and two different plans.

intro.heading: Chemistry is a timing problem before it is a content problem
paragraphs: Most families in Arabian Ranches 3 start looking for chemistry help after a specific event. A DP1 report comes home with a 4 where there used to be a 7 at MYP. A mock paper comes back with every structure drawn correctly and almost no marks for the explanation. A supervisor writes one line on an investigation proposal: not enough independent variable range. Whatever the trigger, it arrives mid-term, with a fixed number of weeks left before something is due. The question is never whether chemistry can be learned. It is what can be moved in the weeks that remain.

That is a scheduling question, so this page answers it as one. The DP Chemistry course is two years long, but the marks are decided in a small number of concentrated windows: the investigation draft deadline the school sets, the mock window in the winter term of DP2, the point at which predicted grades are written, and the examination session itself. Each of those has a different best use of tutoring time. Eight weeks before a mock, past-paper discipline outranks new content. Eight weeks before an investigation deadline, the opposite is true, because a weak research design cannot be rescued by revision later.

The content itself is not vast. Under the Chemistry guide for first examinations in 2025 the syllabus sits in two halves, Structure and Reactivity, each with three units. Structure covers the particulate model, bonding and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives a reaction, how much and how fast and how far it goes, and the mechanisms by which it happens. Higher Level adds depth to every one of those rather than adding a seventh topic, which is why an HL student who is shaky on a Standard Level idea does not simply lose HL marks. They lose the same mark twice.

The place matters less than parents expect, and more than the brochures admit. Arabian Ranches 3 has no Diploma school inside it, so children are bussed out to campuses in Arabian Ranches, the Sustainable City, Motor City, Nad Al Sheba or Al Barsha South. A tutor hired on the basis of living in the next community over is a tutor chosen by postcode, and a postcode has never once correlated with knowing why a student keeps losing the sign on an enthalpy change. Chemistry specialism is thin on the ground anywhere in Dubai. Choosing from one villa cluster makes it thinner.

So the rest of this page is a plan rather than a pitch. There is a calendar table you can count backwards on, a unit-by-unit view of where time actually goes, the component weightings written out, the investigation criteria with their mark allocations, the dirham rates the Dubai market charges with their sources, and a plain statement of how lessons are delivered. If the eight weeks you have left are the wrong eight weeks for what you want to achieve, this page should tell you that before you book anything.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.programmesIntro: Chemistry support starts well before the Diploma. The three stages below are the ones that actually feed into a DP Chemistry grade, plus the core components that sit alongside the subject and compete with it for a student's evenings.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria out of 8 each, and chemistry appears inside an integrated course rather than as a separate subject. The habits that decide a DP Chemistry grade are built here: writing a method somebody else could repeat, handling uncertainty in a measurement, and explaining a result rather than restating it. A student who reaches DP1 able to describe a trend but not account for it is usually carrying an MYP criterion C and D gap rather than a chemistry gap.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Arabian Ranches 3 whose children are in the MYP are typically at Fairgreen International School in the Sustainable City or at an IB continuum campus further in towards Al Barsha. The commute out of the community is long enough that MYP science support is almost always better placed on a weekend morning than on a weekday evening, which is a scheduling fact rather than a preference.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry SL
programmes.description: IB Chemistry SL carries the same six syllabus units as Higher Level at a reduced depth, with Paper 1 at 1 hour 30 minutes and Paper 2 at 1 hour 30 minutes under the current guide. Standard Level students are frequently the ones taking chemistry because a university course asks for it rather than because they chose it, which changes the tutoring. The work is less about extension and more about securing the predictable marks: definitions, equations balanced with state symbols, and data-booklet use under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of SL chemistry students around the Dubailand villa belt are aiming at health science, pharmacy or engineering foundation routes at UAE and UK universities. Those entry requirements are published by the individual university and change between intakes, so the sensible move is to read the current page for the specific programme rather than rely on what an older sibling needed three years ago.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry HL
programmes.description: IB Chemistry HL extends every unit rather than adding a new one: more quantitative treatment in Reactivity 2, more mechanism detail in Reactivity 3, and a broader range of bonding and structure ideas in Structure 2. Paper 1 runs to 2 hours and Paper 2 to 2 hours 30 minutes under the current guide, so stamina is a real component. The commonest HL profile we see is a student who understands the chemistry and cannot write it: correct reasoning, missing command-term response, marks lost in the gap.
programmes.countryNote: HL Chemistry is the subject Dubailand families most often ask for and the one with the thinnest local tutor supply, which is why hiring by distance from Arabian Ranches 3 goes wrong so often. Online delivery widens the pool to specialists outside the emirate, and we will say plainly when a particular HL slot cannot be covered in your preferred evening window rather than filling it with a generalist.

programmes.name: The scientific investigation, Extended Essay and TOK
programmes.description: The investigation is 20% of the Chemistry grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. A chemistry Extended Essay is a separate 4,000-word piece assessed against the Diploma core criteria, and Theory of Knowledge runs alongside both. Together they take DP2 evenings that a student assumed were revision time. Planning that collision is a legitimate use of tutoring; outsourcing any part of the writing is not, and we decline it.
programmes.countryNote: School-set internal deadlines for the investigation and the Extended Essay differ between the campuses Arabian Ranches 3 children attend, sometimes by six weeks. The only reliable version is the one on your child's own school calendar, confirmed with the Diploma coordinator. Every plan we build starts from that document rather than from a generic IB timeline, because the generic timeline is what causes the February panic.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-arabian-ranc.subjectsIntro: Chemistry rarely travels alone. The subjects below are the ones that share a timetable, a maths requirement or an investigation deadline with DP Chemistry, and the ones families in this part of Dubai most often add once the first subject is stable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six units across Structure and Reactivity, assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the investigation at 20%. Marks are lost most reliably in energetics sign conventions, equilibrium reasoning and the mechanism questions in Reactivity 3, where a student draws the right arrows and then describes the wrong step.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Shares the same four investigation criteria and the same 20% weighting as Chemistry, which makes a double science load in DP2 a scheduling problem as much as a content one. The commonest biology mark loss is in data-based questions that reward precise reading of a graph rather than recall.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Built on five themes from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics, with the same paper structure as Chemistry. Students taking Chemistry HL and Physics HL together usually need help with algebraic rearrangement before they need help with either subject's content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most often paired with Chemistry HL. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency, and a chemistry student who cannot manipulate logarithms will lose marks in pH and in rate equations that have nothing to do with chemistry understanding.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-heavy, and a legitimate pairing with Chemistry SL. It is a weaker fit with Chemistry HL for students targeting engineering, because some published entry requirements name Analysis and Approaches specifically. Check the individual university page rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Available as a Group 3 or Group 4 choice and often taken alongside Chemistry by students who want a second science without a second quantitative load. The assessment rewards systems diagrams and evaluation of competing viewpoints, which is a different skill from chemistry explanation.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A Group 4 option with real biochemistry content in it, which makes it a common second science for Chemistry students heading towards physiotherapy or sports medicine. The investigation criteria are identical to Chemistry's, so the two deadlines land in the same weeks.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Materials science overlaps directly with Structure 3 classification of matter, so Chemistry students often find the content familiar and the assessment unfamiliar. The design cycle documentation is where marks are won, and it is the part students treat as administration.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, and worth points in combination with the Extended Essay. Chemistry students usually find the exhibition easier than the essay, because the essay asks them to argue rather than to explain, and the two are marked quite differently.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece with a chemistry research question, supervised in school. Support means teaching research question framing, experimental feasibility and referencing discipline. It does not mean editing a draft to completion, and no tutor should write the Extended Essay or any part of it.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of IB Chemistry can and cannot change
paragraphs: Eight weeks of weekly one-to-one chemistry, used well, reliably changes three things: command-term accuracy, data-booklet speed, and the proportion of a paper a student attempts. Those three between them are usually worth a grade band at Standard Level and can be worth more at Higher Level, because HL papers punish slow working harder. What eight weeks does not do is rebuild a two-year foundation. If a DP2 student cannot balance a redox half-equation, eight weeks spent on exam technique will buy a smaller improvement than eight weeks spent on Reactivity 1, and the honest version of that conversation belongs in the first session rather than the sixth.

The diagnostic matters more than the teaching in week one. A student who scores 40% on a Paper 2 has not failed uniformly. They have usually failed in a shape: full marks on anything numerical, nothing on anything that asks them to explain; or correct explanations written for questions that asked them to deduce. Those two profiles need opposite interventions. Marking a full past paper against the published mark scheme, question by question, is the only way to see which one you have. Impressions from a school report will not show it, because a report grade is an average and the average hides the shape.

The second thing eight weeks exposes is how much of the loss is chemistry at all. A significant share of DP Chemistry marks go missing to arithmetic, to unit conversion, to significant figures and to reading the question. None of that is chemistry and all of it is fixable quickly, which is why a proper diagnostic often produces a better first-month result than a content plan would. It also tells you something about the longer run: a student losing marks to process will keep losing them in Physics and in Mathematics until the process is fixed, so the chemistry work pays for itself twice.

Where the eight weeks sits in the year decides the whole plan. Eight weeks before the winter mock in DP2, the work is paper discipline. Eight weeks before a school investigation deadline, the work is research design and the mock will have to wait. Eight weeks before the May session, nothing new gets taught. Parents who book without naming the date they are working towards generally get a sensible plan for the wrong eight weeks, and that is the single most common waste of money in this market.

sections.heading: The DP Chemistry year, counted backwards
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a calendar, and the absence is strange, because the calendar is the thing parents are actually trying to reconstruct when they search. The table below counts backwards from the May examination session that UAE Diploma schools sit, in relative terms rather than fixed dates. That choice is deliberate and worth explaining: specific IB examination and results dates for a given session are set by the IB and published through schools, and we will not print a date on 2,654 pages that we have not read on ibo.org ourselves. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative version.

Read the table from the bottom up, because that is the direction the year actually runs in. The dates that bite are not the examination dates. They are the internal school deadlines for the investigation and the Extended Essay, which sit a long way earlier, are set by the campus rather than by the IB, and differ by several weeks between the schools Arabian Ranches 3 children attend. A family planning around the examination window alone will discover the investigation deadline about three weeks before it lands, which is the standard February emergency in this community.

The second thing the table shows is where predicted grades come from. Predicted grades are written by teachers, usually off the back of the winter mock, and they go to universities long before the real result exists. A student who is going to be tutored at all is better tutored before the mock than after it, because the mock is the evidence the prediction is built on. Families who start in March have missed that lever entirely. It is still worth starting in March; it is simply worth knowing what has already been decided.

Cambridge and Pearson dates, for families with an IGCSE sibling in the same house, are published and can be planned against directly. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: the six units as a tutor reads them
paragraphs: The current Chemistry guide, for first examinations in 2025, organises the subject into Structure and Reactivity with three units each. Structure 1 is the particulate nature of matter, Structure 2 is bonding and structure, Structure 3 is classification of matter. Reactivity 1 asks what drives a chemical reaction, Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far, Reactivity 3 asks what the mechanisms of chemical change are. Higher Level extends each of the six rather than adding a seventh, which is the single most useful fact a parent can hold about the course.

That structure has a direct tutoring consequence. Because HL is depth rather than breadth, a Higher Level student with a Standard Level weakness pays for it twice: once in the SL-level question and again in the HL extension built on top of it. The practical effect is that HL remediation almost always has to go backwards before it goes forwards, and a tutor who starts at the HL material because that is what the student asked for will produce two months of apparent progress followed by a mock result that has not moved.

The table sets out where time actually goes. The hours column is not a promise; it is what we typically see for a student working from a secure Standard Level base towards a confident Higher Level answer in that unit, and a student starting lower will need more. What the table is genuinely useful for is ordering. Reactivity 2 and Reactivity 3 between them carry most of the marks that distinguish a 5 from a 7, and they are also the units students postpone, because equilibrium and mechanisms both feel harder than they are once the notation is secure.

One caution on syllabus material. The IB's subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. We reference them, cite them and teach from the student's own legitimately obtained copies; we do not reproduce or supply them. Any tutoring service offering a download pack of IB papers is distributing material it does not own, and the same applies to Cambridge and Pearson documents. The official route is your child's school or the board's own site.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: what each component rewards
paragraphs: Under the current guide, DP Chemistry is assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%, at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 splits into two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice. Paper 1B is data-based and set on the experimental programme, which means it tests the practical work a student has actually done rather than content recall. Paper 2 is short and extended response. Confirm the current durations and the exact split with your child's Diploma coordinator, because assessment detail is revised between guide cycles.

Paper 1B is the component with the largest gap between how much it is worth and how much it is practised. Students arrive having worked through dozens of multiple-choice questions and almost no data-based ones, because data-based questions are harder to self-mark and schools under time pressure set what can be marked quickly. The result is predictable: a student who can recall everything and cannot interpret a table of titration readings. Half of the Paper 1B work in a tutoring block is not chemistry teaching at all. It is teaching a student to read a column heading, including its units.

Paper 2 is where command terms decide the grade. State, outline, describe, explain, deduce, discuss and evaluate are not synonyms, and each one has a mark allocation shaped to it. A student who explains when asked to state wastes time they needed later in the paper; a student who states when asked to explain loses the marks outright. This is learnable in a handful of sessions and it is the single highest-return item on most DP Chemistry plans, which is why it sits near the front of any eight-week block we build.

Stamina is a real variable at Higher Level. The HL papers are materially longer than the SL ones, and a student who has only ever practised in thirty-minute chunks will lose marks in the final third of Paper 2 to fatigue rather than to chemistry. Full-length timed practice, at least three times before the session, is the fix. It is also the part of a plan that families most often skip, because a two-and-a-half-hour paper on a school night is genuinely difficult to schedule in a household that already commutes out of Dubailand twice a day.

sections.heading: Where chemistry marks actually go missing between October and March
paragraphs: The marks a DP Chemistry student loses are more repeatable than most parents expect. Across the diagnostic papers we mark, the same small set of losses accounts for most of the gap between a 5 and a 7, and almost none of it is exotic content. It is sign conventions in energetics, equilibrium answers that restate rather than explain, redox half-equations that do not balance, organic mechanism descriptions that do not match the arrows the student drew, and significant figures discarded somewhere in the middle of a correct calculation.

Energetics is the clearest example. A student calculates an enthalpy change of the right magnitude, writes it with the wrong sign, and loses the mark for a conclusion they actually understood. The fix is not more enthalpy teaching. It is a rule about where the sign comes from, applied to twenty questions in a row until it is automatic. That is a single session's work and it recurs on every paper, which makes it the highest-value hour in a typical block. Equilibrium is the same shape: students know Le Chatelier and write answers that describe the shift without naming the reason for it.

Mechanisms in Reactivity 3 are the most misdiagnosed. Students who get them wrong are usually told they need to learn mechanisms, and they have learned them, in the sense that they can draw the curly arrows from memory. What they cannot do is say what the arrow represents in words, which is what the mark scheme asks for. Teaching the verbal description alongside the diagram, rather than after it, closes that gap faster than any amount of redrawing. It also transfers: a student who can narrate a nucleophilic substitution can usually narrate an electrophilic addition without being taught it twice.

The last category is not chemistry. Arithmetic slips, unit conversions between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, significant figures and simple misreading of the question are, in our marking, a substantial share of lost marks at Standard Level. They are also the fastest to fix and the easiest to ignore, because they look like carelessness rather than a skill gap. Treating them as a skill gap, with their own practice and their own checklist, is what turns a student who understands chemistry into one whose paper shows it.
