sections.heading: Acids, bases and the logarithm problem at Higher Level
paragraphs: At Standard Level, acid-base chemistry is largely descriptive with straightforward pH work. At Higher Level it becomes the most mathematically demanding part of the course, and the mathematics rather than the chemistry is what costs students marks. Logarithms appear in pH, in pKa and pKb, and in buffer calculations, and a student who is uncomfortable with logarithms in mathematics will be uncomfortable with them here.

The asymmetry is worth naming. Calculating pH from a known concentration of a strong acid is routine and almost everyone can do it. Going the other way - finding a concentration from a pH - requires an inverse logarithm and a calculator operation that students fumble under pressure. Weak acid calculations require an approximation, namely that the dissociated amount is negligible compared with the initial concentration, and the marks are available for stating that assumption. Students who use the approximation without naming it lose the mark that was there for naming it.

Buffers and titration curves are the other recurring area. A titration curve question usually asks for the pH at a specified point - at the start, at half-equivalence, at equivalence, after excess - and each point needs a different method. Half-equivalence is the one worth memorising properly, because at that point the pH equals the pKa and a question can be answered in a single line by a student who knows it and in no lines at all by one who does not. The shape of the curve for a weak acid against a strong base, and which indicator suits it, is examined in most series.

The practical teaching point is that this area is best approached as applied mathematics taught by a chemist. A student working on logarithmic pH problems is doing algebra with chemical labels on it, and tutoring that treats it as chemistry content to be understood rather than as technique to be practised tends to produce a student who follows the explanation and then cannot do the next question. Practice, in volume, against past-paper questions is what fixes it.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: why memorising the reactions fails and the mechanisms do not
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is the topic Bur Dubai parents name most often, and the reason it feels impossible is usually the method being used on it. A student who treats it as a list of reactions to memorise faces an ever-growing list, forgets the middle of it, and panics. A student who understands a handful of mechanisms can generate most of the list from first principles and recognises a reaction they have never seen.

At Higher Level the mechanisms are explicitly examined with curly arrows, and they are marked precisely. An arrow must start at a lone pair or at a bond and must end where the electrons go. Arrows drawn from an atom rather than from its electrons lose marks even when the overall transformation is right. Nucleophilic substitution has two pathways with different conditions and different stereochemical consequences; elimination competes with substitution under conditions a question will specify; electrophilic addition follows a predictable pattern once the intermediate is understood. These are four or five ideas, not forty.

Nomenclature is the other half of the problem, and it is purely mechanical. Longest chain, lowest locants, substituents alphabetically, functional group priority. Students who lose nomenclature marks are almost always losing them to carelessness rather than ignorance, and the repair is a few dozen examples in a single session rather than a course of teaching. It is worth doing precisely because it is easy marks that strong students throw away.

Spectroscopy belongs with organic chemistry in practice, because structure determination questions combine them. Infrared, mass spectrometry and at Higher Level nuclear magnetic resonance are interpreted together to identify a compound, and every reference table needed sits in the data booklet. A student who knows where those tables are answers these questions quickly; one who does not loses both the marks and the minutes. This is a data booklet drill, not a chemistry lesson, and it is one of the cheapest sessions in the subject.

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation: four criteria and where the design caps the grade
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is 20 per cent of the chemistry grade, assessed on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. In chemistry the characteristic design failure is different from physics: it is choosing a dependent variable that cannot be measured precisely enough with the apparatus a school actually has. A colour change judged by eye, a mass change too small for the balance's resolution, a temperature change of two degrees measured with a thermometer reading to the nearest degree - all of these produce data whose uncertainty swamps the effect being studied, and no analysis rescues it.

That is why the useful hour happens before anything is booked in the laboratory. The questions are concrete: what exactly will you measure, with what instrument, to what resolution, and is the expected change large enough to be distinguishable from the uncertainty in that instrument? How many values across what range, and how many repeats at each? A fifteen-minute conversation at that stage prevents the most expensive mistake available in the component.

Data analysis and Conclusion then follow from what was actually collected. Enough values across enough of the range, with repeats and with uncertainties recorded at the point of measurement rather than estimated afterwards, give a student something to process. Five values collected once do not. The Conclusion can only be as strong as the analysis, and comparing the result with an accepted literature value - cited properly - is where many students stop short.

Evaluation gives away more marks than any other criterion in the component. It asks for limitations specific to what happened and improvements that would actually address them. Generic lists - more repeats, human error, better equipment - score nothing. A limitation that names a particular systematic error in that experiment, explains the direction in which it would skew the result, and proposes a realistic change, scores. On what we will and will not do: a tutor asks questions, teaches uncertainty and graph technique, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not design the experiment, process the data, or write any part of the report. That boundary is written down before any investigation work begins, because under IB academic honesty rules the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.
bullets: Research design is settled before any apparatus is booked
Check that the expected change exceeds the instrument's uncertainty
Enough values, across enough range, with repeats and recorded uncertainties
Evaluation needs specific limitations, not a generic list

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs in this part of Dubai, and what you can check yourself
paragraphs: A parent can verify every figure in this section without taking our word for anything, which is the point of publishing it. Three providers in this market publish no price at all; two publish in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family transacts in. The ranges below are in dirhams, each attributed to the provider that published it, read in October 2026.

At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For Diploma chemistry that band buys homework supervision and a second explanation, which is not what a student losing marks on logarithmic pH calculations needs. The next band is a qualified subject tutor online, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly packages in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What the bands actually buy, for chemistry specifically: the mid band is right for calculation chain work and for content teaching, because that is competent instruction of well-defined material and prestige adds nothing. The specialist band earns its premium for investigation design and for reading a script to find where marks are being lost, both of which are judgement rather than knowledge. Nothing in the market is worth a premium for the final fortnight's past-paper practice, because that work belongs to the student.

Two questions to ask any provider, including us. Is the quoted rate per hour or per lesson - a ninety-minute lesson at an hourly rate is a different number from a ninety-minute lesson at a lesson rate. And what happens if you stop after one session. Those two answers separate providers faster than any amount of marketing copy. None of the figures above are IB Gram prices; we do not publish a rate card on a landing page, we hold no office or centre in the UAE, and we are not accredited, approved or licensed by the International Baccalaureate, KHDA or anyone else.

sections.heading: A chemistry tutor in a Bur Dubai flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The in-home instinct is reasonable here. A tutor in the room can be observed, a parent can judge whether an hour was worked, and in a flat with younger children it avoids a journey entirely. We take those arguments seriously rather than dismissing them.

The position, stated before payment: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video. We put it on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and no family should learn that after paying a month's fees.

For chemistry the format fits the work unusually well. A multi-step calculation - a Hess cycle, a buffer problem, a three-row equilibrium layout - is best worked on a shared surface where the tutor can annotate the student's own working in place and the whole thing can be saved. The data booklet can be open on the same screen at the relevant page, which matters because navigating it is itself a taught skill. A sheet of paper slid across a table and taken away afterwards does none of that.

The supply argument is the decisive one, though. A teacher who knows precisely where a research question will cap the Evaluation criterion, who can read a Higher Level script fast enough to rank mark losses in an hour, and who has taught the current guide's treatment of reactivity properly is a narrow specialism. The chance that such a person lives within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mankhool and is free at 5pm on a Tuesday is small. Insisting on proximity means accepting a generalist, and the market data shows the in-home premium is paying for travel rather than for that expertise.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and the claims nobody in this market should make
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula. Abu Dhabi's regulator is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate; Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map, and most tutoring sites in this market name none of them.

Naming a regulator and claiming its approval are entirely different things. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified, licensed, authorised or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai - initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry - and we do not hold one. No tutoring platform without that permit should describe its tutors as KHDA-approved, and the phrase should be challenged wherever it appears.

On permits for individuals, the facts are checkable. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published officially, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

Two more things we will not do. We will not write, complete, draft or edit to completion any part of a Scientific Investigation, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or other assessed coursework - one competitor in this SERP sells completed internal assessments outright, which is an IB malpractice trigger for the student who submits one. And we will not publish a statistic without a sample size, a date and a method attached, which is why there is no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor headcount anywhere on this page.

process.title: Run the ten-minute mole diagnostic
process.description: Before booking anything, have your child talk through three conversions out loud: mass to moles, concentration and volume to moles, gas volume to moles. Hesitation, a remembered triangle instead of a relationship, or a unit slip tells you where to start, whatever topic the report card names.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a topic list
process.description: The most useful thing you can share is a marked past paper or a returned school assessment. Fifteen minutes with a script and the mark scheme locates the losses precisely; an hour spent discussing which topics feel hard usually locates them in the wrong place.

process.title: A free trial, worked on a real question
process.description: One session at no cost with the tutor you would continue with, spent working a multi-step past-paper calculation or interrogating an investigation research question. You get a written note of what was found, whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Fix the hour against the real commute
process.description: Choose a slot that survives a bad afternoon rather than a good one, and agree in advance that it shifts during Ramadan. Oud Metha and Al Mankhool households can often hold 4.30pm; Karama, Deira-side and Al Nahda families usually do better after six. All times are Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Check progress across topics, not within one
process.description: The test of calculation chain work is whether it holds in a thermochemistry question, then a gas question, then a titration. We set questions from different topics deliberately, because a student who can do the chain in one context and not another has not yet got it.

process.title: End the block
process.description: Calculation repair takes four to eight sessions and then it is done. Investigation support ends at submission. We would rather tell you a block is finished than keep a standing booking nobody is measuring, and if timed-paper marks have plateaued, that is information rather than a reason to buy more hours.

whyPoints.title: We diagnose upstream of the named topic
whyPoints.description: When a family says organic chemistry, we check the mole chain first, because the named topic is usually where a more basic problem becomes visible. Re-teaching the named topic without checking that is the most common way chemistry tutoring money gets wasted in this market.

whyPoints.title: The data booklet treated as a skill
whyPoints.description: Chemistry's booklet carries bond enthalpies, electrode potentials, pKa values and spectroscopic correlation tables. Navigating it under time pressure is trainable and examined, and students who quote remembered approximations instead of booklet values lose accuracy marks for no reason at all.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms before memorisation
whyPoints.description: A student who understands four or five organic mechanisms can generate most of the reaction list and recognise an unfamiliar reaction. A student memorising the list faces an ever-growing one. We teach the smaller thing, which is also the harder thing to teach and the reason specialists cost more.

whyPoints.title: A written boundary on the investigation
whyPoints.description: We ask questions, teach uncertainty and graph technique and give feedback on the student's own draft. We do not design the experiment, process the data or write any part of the report. That is written down before work starts, because under IB rules the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed and checkable
whyPoints.description: Each AED range on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, so you can verify it yourself. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor count, because we cannot attach a sample size, a date and a method to any of them.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claims
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no premises in the UAE. We name the regulators and explain what they do; we do not imply any of them endorses us, and nor should anyone else in this market.

faqs.question: Why does my child struggle with organic chemistry but seem fine elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Usually because of method rather than ability. Treating organic chemistry as a list of reactions to memorise produces an ever-growing list that nobody retains. Understanding four or five mechanisms - nucleophilic substitution by its two pathways, elimination, electrophilic addition - lets a student generate most of that list and recognise a reaction they have never seen. At Higher Level the mechanisms are examined directly with curly arrows, marked precisely on where each arrow starts and ends. The shift from memorising to mechanism typically takes four to six sessions.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful thing to check before hiring a chemistry tutor?
faqs.answer: Whether your child can do the mole chain without thinking. Ask three questions out loud: moles from a mass, moles from a concentration and volume, moles from a gas volume. Watch for hesitation, for reaching for a remembered triangle rather than stating a relationship, and for cubic centimetre conversions going the wrong way. If any of those shows up, that is where tutoring should start regardless of which topic the report names, because energetics, equilibrium, titration and electrochemistry all run through it.

faqs.question: How are the IB chemistry papers weighted?
faqs.answer: Paper 1, which combines a multiple-choice section with a data-based section, carries 36 per cent. Paper 2, extended response, carries 44 per cent. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent and is submitted at a school deadline months before the papers. That split matters for planning: the investigation is the component a DP1 student can still influence most cheaply, and a DP2 student in the spring term has 80 per cent of the grade left in the papers and nothing available in the other 20.

faqs.question: Why are sign errors so costly in IB chemistry energetics?
faqs.answer: Because the arithmetic can be entirely correct and the answer still wrong. An exothermic enthalpy change is negative; a Hess cycle step run in reverse reverses its sign; a calorimetry calculation uses the mass of the solution rather than of the solute. Each of those is a simple idea that fails under time pressure. The fix is mechanical rather than conceptual: draw the cycle, arrow every step, write each signed value next to its arrow, and state in words whether the process is exothermic before writing any number.

faqs.question: What does the equilibrium constant actually tell you?
faqs.answer: The position of equilibrium - how far a reaction proceeds - and nothing about how fast it gets there. Conflating the constant with reaction rate is the most common conceptual error in the topic and it appears in most series. Two further points students lose marks on: concentrations rather than amounts in moles go into the expression, which matters whenever the volume is not one cubic decimetre, and only a change in temperature alters the value of the constant. Changing concentration or pressure shifts the position without changing the constant.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level acid-base chemistry so much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Because it becomes applied mathematics. Logarithms appear in pH, in pKa and pKb, and in buffer calculations, and a student uncomfortable with logarithms in mathematics will struggle here for mathematical reasons rather than chemical ones. The asymmetry matters: pH from a known concentration is routine, while concentration from a pH needs an inverse logarithm that students fumble under pressure. Weak acid calculations also require an approximation, and there are marks available specifically for stating it rather than silently using it.

faqs.question: What should my child do about the chemistry investigation before going near a laboratory?
faqs.answer: Answer four questions on paper. What exactly will be measured, with which instrument, to what resolution, and is the expected change large enough to be distinguished from that instrument's uncertainty? Then: how many values across what range, and how many repeats at each. The characteristic chemistry design failure is a dependent variable that cannot be measured precisely enough with school apparatus - a colour judged by eye, a mass change below the balance resolution - and no analysis rescues data whose uncertainty swamps the effect.

faqs.question: How many marks does the chemistry Evaluation criterion give away?
faqs.answer: More than any other part of the investigation, because students write generic lists. More repeats, human error, better equipment - none of those score. What scores is a limitation specific to what actually happened, an explanation of the direction in which it would skew the result, and a realistic change that would address it. The marks are there for specificity. Keeping notes during data collection rather than reconstructing problems from memory afterwards is what makes a specific evaluation possible, and it costs nothing.

faqs.question: Does my child need separate IGCSE chemistry to cope with Diploma chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, but it changes the first term. Students from separate IGCSE chemistry - Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 - arrive having already met mole calculations and volumetric work. Students from a coordinated or combined award often have not, and the gap shows immediately in DP1. Neither route is a barrier. Which one your child took predicts the first term's difficulty better than their IGCSE grade does, and it is worth telling a tutor at the outset so the opening sessions are aimed correctly.

faqs.question: Do you send a chemistry tutor to our home in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, stated before you pay. For chemistry the format suits the work: a Hess cycle or a three-row equilibrium layout is best annotated on a shared surface and saved, and the data booklet can be open on the same screen. The stronger argument is supply - a Higher Level chemistry specialist free at 5pm and living near Al Mankhool is an unlikely pairing.

faqs.question: How much does an IB chemistry tutor cost in Dubai in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Figures read in October 2026 from each provider's own pages: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200; Bestimate's Dubai table places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to 350 at Bestimate and up to AED 500 with independent tutors. These are market rates and not our prices. Ask any provider whether the rate is per hour or per lesson.

faqs.question: Is a premium chemistry tutor worth the extra dirhams?
faqs.answer: It depends on the task. For the mole chain, energetics and content teaching, the mid band is sufficient - this is competent instruction of well-defined material and prestige adds nothing measurable. For investigation design and for reading a script to rank where marks are leaking, the specialist band earns its premium, because those are judgement skills rather than knowledge. For the final fortnight of past-paper practice, nothing in the market is worth a premium, because that work belongs to the student and no tutor can do it for them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give my child IB chemistry past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: We do not host or redistribute them. IB, Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright material, and reproducing them is somebody else's intellectual property rather than ours to share. We reference them, cite the official source and link out. In practice your child's chemistry teacher can usually supply past papers directly, and that is the right route. Any tutoring site offering a download library of official papers is taking a risk a family does not need to be part of.

faqs.question: Do some tutoring services really offer to produce a finished internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Some do advertise it, and one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments outright. It is an academic honesty breach under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student who submits the work, not on the service that produced it - potentially the loss of the diploma. We teach, question and give feedback on the student's own draft, and we do not design the experiment, process the data or write any part of the report. That boundary is written down before any investigation work begins.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring company be KHDA approved?
faqs.answer: A training institute with premises in Dubai can hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific authorisation for a specific kind of business. IB Gram does not hold one, has no premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Ask anyone claiming otherwise for the permit number.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix a chemistry calculation problem?
faqs.answer: Four to eight sessions for the mole chain to become automatic, which is the usual root cause. The work is deliberately spread across topics rather than within one: the same chain practised in a thermochemistry question, then a gas question, then a titration, so the student stops seeing them as different problems. Progress is checked against past-paper questions from several topics rather than one, because a student who can do the chain in a familiar context and not an unfamiliar one has not yet got it. Then the block ends.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingHeading: Start with the chain, not the topic
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingBody: Before you buy any chemistry tutoring, spend ten minutes on the mole diagnostic: three conversions, talked through out loud. If any of them is slow or uncertain, that is where the hours should go, whatever the report card names. If the chain is secure and the marks are still leaking, send us a marked script and we will tell you where from. Either way, the free trial lesson costs nothing - one hour with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a real multi-step past-paper question or on an investigation research question, with a written note of what was found. All lessons for Bur Dubai families are one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-business-bay.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Chemistry at Standard and Higher Level to students across Dubai's central corridor. Each works from the student's own school scheme of work, not a generic course, and the first lesson is a diagnostic rather than a sales call.

intro.heading: A Business Bay address is a commute, not a curriculum
paragraphs: Business Bay has towers, a canal, offices and almost no schools. The children who live here are driven or bussed out every morning — towards Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf, Al Quoz, Al Barsha or Jumeirah — and they come back somewhere between half past three and half past four depending on which direction the bus turned. That single fact explains most of what a parent here needs to know about arranging Chemistry support. The subject does not vary by district. The evening does.

Parents in this area often start by searching for someone close by, on the reasonable assumption that proximity makes a lesson easier. For most subjects at most levels there is something in that. For IB Chemistry at Higher Level it inverts. The pool of people within a twenty-minute drive of Business Bay who can confidently teach entropy, buffer calculations and the mechanisms of nucleophilic substitution is small. The pool of people who can teach those things well, somewhere on earth, at seven o'clock Gulf Standard Time, is much larger. Choosing the second pool is the whole argument for online delivery, and it is an argument about quality rather than convenience.

This page is written as a comparison, because that is the question Business Bay families actually ask: is my district better or worse placed than the next one over? Downtown Dubai sits a bridge away and has the same answer. DIFC, Al Jaddaf, Culture Village, Meydan and Sobha Hartland all have the same answer. The reason is that none of these districts contains the Chemistry specialist a Diploma student needs, so all of them are buying the same thing — a subject expert reached over live video. What differs between them is only the clock: how long the bus takes, and therefore whether a session can start at five, six or seven.

What follows is the Chemistry rather than the marketing. The current subject guide reorganised the course into Structure and Reactivity themes, and the assessment sits on two papers plus one internally assessed investigation. Each of those three components fails in a different way, and a tutor who treats them as one thing wastes a term. Below you will find the component weightings, the places marks genuinely go missing, the four criteria the investigation is marked against, what the Dubai market charges for this kind of help, and where the boundary sits between coaching a student's investigation and interfering with it.

One thing is stated plainly throughout. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Business Bay apartment; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered live online. The phrase parents type is often a home tutor, and the honest response is to answer that question properly — what the in-home market charges, what the travel premium buys, how families weigh it — and then show the comparison rather than hide behind it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-business-bay.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to a Business Bay family thinking about Chemistry: the Diploma, where Chemistry becomes a named course with papers and an investigation, the Middle Years Programme that feeds it, and the Career-related Programme that some Dubai schools run alongside the Diploma.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two years where Chemistry becomes a graded subject. A student takes it at Standard or Higher Level, sits two written papers and submits one scientific investigation of their own design. Higher Level adds depth to every theme rather than new isolated topics, which is why students who coped at Standard Level can still stall: the questions assume they can combine two ideas that were taught months apart.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma sits alongside the KHDA mandatory subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies — which occupy timetable hours a student in another country would spend on sciences. A Business Bay student commuting to Sobha Hartland or Al Jaddaf therefore has less free study time than the raw timetable suggests, and Chemistry tends to be the subject that absorbs the shortfall.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences are taught as one integrated subject assessed against four criteria rather than as separate Chemistry papers. Students arrive in the Diploma fluent in investigation design and the language of criteria, and often short of fluency in the calculation work that Chemistry Standard Level assumes from the first week — moles, concentrations, stoichiometric ratios done at speed and without a prompt.
programmes.countryNote: Several central Dubai schools run the MYP through to MYP 5 instead of IGCSE, so a Business Bay family choosing a school is also choosing which gap their child will have in September of DP1. That gap is predictable and is the cheapest thing to fix: a short block of arithmetic-of-chemistry work in the summer before the Diploma does more than a term of catch-up afterwards.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller route combining two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study and a core of its own. A student may take Chemistry Standard Level inside the Career-related Programme and be assessed on exactly the same papers and the same investigation as a full Diploma candidate, which means the tutoring need is identical even though the overall qualification is not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a handful of schools offering this route, usually attached to business, hospitality or engineering pathways. Business Bay parents sometimes discover it only after the Diploma has already proved too broad. Where Chemistry is one of the retained courses, the assessment calendar and the investigation deadline are set by the same school coordinator, so the support plan does not change.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the page's subject, but it is rarely the only one in the plan. These are the courses Business Bay families most often add once Chemistry is stabilised, with what each actually assesses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers plus the scientific investigation. Marks concentrate in energetics, equilibrium, acid-base calculations and the organic mechanisms, and Higher Level questions routinely require two of those at once. Paper 1B is data analysis under time pressure and is the component most students have never practised separately.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Shares the investigation structure and the command-term discipline with Chemistry, which makes the two cheap to tutor together. Students lose marks on explain and evaluate questions by describing a process accurately and never naming the mechanism the mark scheme wanted.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The science most dependent on algebraic fluency. A Business Bay student taking Chemistry and Physics together usually needs one shared repair — rearranging and substituting without arithmetic slips — rather than two separate subject plans.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Supplies the calculus and logarithm work that Chemistry HL assumes when it reaches rate equations and pH. Students on Applications and Interpretation can still take Chemistry HL comfortably, but the log work needs covering somewhere.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Heavier on statistics, modelling and technology use. Useful to a Chemistry student for the data-analysis half of Paper 1 and for the uncertainty treatment the investigation criteria expect.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed through an individual oral, a paper on unseen non-literary texts and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied work. The writing discipline transfers directly into the evaluation section of a science investigation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers plus a portfolio of commentaries on published news articles. A common Diploma pairing for students who want a science and a social science, and a frequent source of timetable collision in the investigation term.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that can satisfy either the sciences or the individuals-and-societies requirement. Business Bay students sometimes carry it alongside Chemistry, and the two share enough data-handling that one tutor can cover both.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. It is examined on its own terms and is a common reason a Diploma student has less revision time for Chemistry than the family expected.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Chemistry students often find the exhibition easier than peers because the investigation has already trained them to justify a method, but the essay rewards a different register entirely.

sections.heading: What a Business Bay search for a Chemistry tutor is really asking
paragraphs: The literal question is where is the nearest person. The useful question is who can teach this particular course. An IB Chemistry tutor in Business Bay is almost never a neighbour, because Business Bay is a commercial and residential district with no secondary campus inside it. Every Diploma student here already travels for school, and the Chemistry they are travelling to is set by a single international subject guide that is identical in every one of those schools.

That makes the proximity instinct expensive. A parent who filters for distance is filtering on the one variable that does not affect the teaching, and is discarding the variable that does. Higher Level Chemistry is a narrow specialism. A tutor who has taught it repeatedly knows that students lose predictable marks in buffer calculations and in the mechanisms, and knows which past-paper questions expose each. A capable general science tutor who lives nearby does not know that, and will spend four sessions discovering it.

There is one real advantage to living in this district, and it is worth naming. Business Bay evenings are flexible because the family is already organised around a commute. Parents are frequently working in the same tower cluster, the child is home by late afternoon, and nobody has to drive anywhere for a lesson at seven. Compared with a villa community further out, where a tutor's travel time would have to be paid for, an online session costs the family nothing in logistics at all.

sections.heading: Business Bay against the districts either side of it
paragraphs: A comparison is the fastest way to settle this. The table below sets Business Bay next to the districts its families most often weigh themselves against, on the four things that actually differ: which schools the district reaches, how long the afternoon return takes in term time, the earliest hour a weekday Chemistry session can realistically begin, and whether any of that changes the Chemistry itself.

The last column is the point of the exercise. It reads the same in every row. Content, papers, weightings and the investigation criteria do not vary by district, by school or by emirate, because they are set internationally. A family in Sobha Hartland with a five-minute school run and a family in Meydan with a forty-minute one are buying the same subject expertise; they are simply booking it at different times of the evening.

Commute figures here are term-time observations rather than published data, and they move with roadworks and bus routing. Treat them as the shape of the problem, not a timetable. The practical rule Business Bay parents end up applying is simple: hold a slot thirty minutes later than you think you need for the first fortnight, then pull it earlier once you know what the bus actually does.

The second column deserves a note of its own. Districts with a campus inside them are not automatically better placed for Diploma support. A child who walks to school in Sobha Hartland gains an hour of evening, which is real, but gains nothing in access to a Higher Level Chemistry teacher outside school hours. The regulator for all of these districts is the same body, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale. An inspection grade describes the school, not the availability of subject tutors near it, and parents frequently read it as though it did.

sections.heading: Where the Chemistry content actually sits now
paragraphs: The course was reorganised so that content is grouped under two headings rather than eleven numbered topics. Structure covers the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and the mechanisms by which change happens. Higher Level does not bolt on separate topics so much as deepen each of these, which is why the step up feels like the same syllabus asking harder questions.

Assessment sits on two written papers and one internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 has two parts that behave completely differently: 1A is multiple choice across the whole course, and 1B is data-based analysis of unfamiliar material. Paper 2 is short and extended response. The investigation is marked in school against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Any tutoring plan that does not treat those as three separate skills will improve one of them and leave the grade roughly where it was.

The weightings below are the shape most Dubai schools work to, and they are the reason a mock result can mislead. A student who is strong on recall and weak on unfamiliar data can look comfortable in a topic test and then lose a grade on Paper 1B. Confirm the current component structure and durations with your child's IB coordinator before planning a revision sequence around them, because subject guides are revised and the school holds the authoritative version.

sections.heading: Where Chemistry marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Four places account for most of the lost marks, and they are diagnosable in a single session with a marked paper in front of you. The first is the organic mechanisms. Students learn the names of the mechanism types and then cannot draw the arrows, because the arrows require a decision about which species is electron-rich and which is electron-poor. A student who has memorised a diagram reproduces it for the one case they memorised and fails the variant.

The second is equilibrium and the arithmetic around it. Setting up an expression is usually fine; the loss happens in interpreting what a change does to the position of equilibrium and then saying so in the vocabulary the mark scheme accepts. The third is energetics, where enthalpy cycles and entropy reasoning are both conceptually simple and procedurally unforgiving — one sign error and an otherwise correct answer earns nothing. The fourth is acid-base calculation, particularly buffers, where students apply a formula without noticing which species is in excess.

None of this is fixed by covering the syllabus again. It is fixed by working marked questions in each of the four areas, naming the specific error each time, and then returning to the same question type a fortnight later to confirm it has gone. That loop is what a specialist does automatically and what a general tutor takes a month to arrive at. It is also why the first session with a new student is spent reading their marked work rather than teaching.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is one piece of work the student designs, carries out and writes up, marked in school against four published criteria and moderated by the IB. It carries a fifth of the final Chemistry grade, which puts it on a par with a written paper, and it is the component Business Bay families most often leave until the deadline is visible. It is also the component where the boundary between help and malpractice matters most.

The table sets out the four criteria, what each is actually rewarding, and what a tutor may legitimately do in each. The pattern is the same in every row: the tutor may ask questions, name the standard, point at a gap and comment on a draft the student has written. The tutor may not supply the research question, write the method, process the data or draft the evaluation. Those are the things being assessed, and a student who submits them as their own is exposed to an academic-honesty investigation.

In practice the mark is usually decided before any data is collected. A research question with a measurable independent variable, a sensible range and a realistic apparatus list sets up every other criterion. A question that is too broad produces data nobody can analyse, and the student then writes an evaluation that is mostly an apology. The cheapest intervention available in this subject is two sessions on the research question, several weeks before the school's internal deadline.

sections.heading: What Chemistry support costs around the central corridor, counted by the month
paragraphs: Most published rates are hourly, which is the least useful unit for a decision. Families commit by the month, so start there. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include online blocks around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home blocks of AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Converting back to hourly, the cheapest end of the market is university-student and generalist online tuition: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits higher — Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB and IGCSE specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650.

Those figures are the market's, attributed to whoever published them, and they are not an IB Gram price list. What the spread tells a Business Bay parent is where the money actually goes. The gap between a generalist at AED 60 and a Higher Level Chemistry specialist at AED 270 is subject knowledge. The gap between an online specialist and an in-home one is travel, which in this district buys a tutor sitting on your sofa instead of on your screen and buys nothing at all in teaching quality. Start with the free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a package, and judge the first marked piece of work.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the permit question, and what a parent can check
paragraphs: Two things in this market are worth a parent's scepticism, and both are checkable. The first is any offer to help with assessed work in a way that crosses into producing it. The investigation, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own. There are providers in this SERP selling completed internal assessments at four-figure prices; that is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A tutor teaches, questions, and gives feedback on work the student has already written.

The second is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified.

A Business Bay parent can therefore ask three concrete questions and expect answers. Does the person teaching my child hold the permit, and can I see it? Will they put in writing that they will not write any part of the investigation? And in Abu Dhabi schools, the regulator's professional-ethics rules bar staff from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, so never arrange paid lessons with your child's own class teacher. IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not describe itself as if it did.

sections.heading: Getting started from a Business Bay tower, with the limits stated
paragraphs: The first step is a free trial lesson with a Chemistry specialist, booked at an hour that survives the school run. Bring the most recent marked paper, the school's topic order for the term, and the internal deadline for the investigation if one has been set. Those three documents let a tutor diagnose in forty minutes what would otherwise take a month of lessons to notice, and they turn the trial into a working session rather than an audition.

After the trial you will be told plainly whether weekly support is the right answer. Sometimes it is not. A student who is three weeks behind on one topic needs a short block, not a term's commitment, and saying so is more useful than selling the term. Where a two-year plan does make sense, it usually runs as one weekly session through DP1, two in the investigation term, and a concentrated past-paper sprint in the final run-up, with the weighting shifted according to what the mock exposes.

The limits are these. Lessons are delivered live online and nowhere else in the UAE — IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, because home visits are an India-only service. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist at a specific hour is not always available immediately, and when that happens you will be told what the wait is rather than offered a generalist described as a specialist. No grade is promised, by anybody, at any price. What is offered is a subject expert, a diagnosis you can read, and an honest account of what the next eight weeks can achieve.

Reading a student's actual errors is faster and more accurate than any questionnaire, and it means the trial lesson starts from evidence rather than from a conversation about confidence levels.

process.description: A full session with the specialist you would keep, timed around the Business Bay school run. The tutor works a past-paper question in each weak area and tells you which of the four classic loss points applies. You decide afterwards whether to continue, with nothing committed in advance.

process.description: Paper 1A, Paper 1B, Paper 2 and the investigation need different work. The plan states how many sessions go to each over the term and which comes first, so you can see what is being prioritised rather than discovering it later from an invoice.

process.description: Each lesson ends with a short written note: what was covered, what the student got wrong, and the single target before next week. That note is what lets a parent in a different time zone or a different tower know whether the arrangement is working.

process.title: Reassess after the mock
process.description: A marked mock is the only honest checkpoint. The plan is rebuilt around it — sometimes dropping a topic that is now secure, usually adding timed Paper 1B practice, occasionally recommending that the family stops because the student no longer needs paid support.

whyPoints.description: A Business Bay family is matched to someone who has taught this Chemistry course repeatedly, wherever they live. Filtering for a tutor within driving distance of the canal removes most of the people who can teach Higher Level mechanisms properly and improves nothing about the lesson.

whyPoints.title: The investigation handled early and honestly
whyPoints.description: Support concentrates on the research question weeks before the school deadline, because that is where the mark is decided. The student writes every word. Nobody drafts a method, processes data or supplies a conclusion, and that boundary is stated in writing at the start.

whyPoints.description: If no Higher Level Chemistry specialist is free at the hour you need, you are told the wait rather than matched to a generalist. Disclosing a coverage limit costs a booking occasionally and saves a wasted term regularly.

faqs.question: How much does IB Chemistry support cost a Business Bay family each month?
faqs.answer: Think in months rather than hours. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 monthly at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages in this market include around AED 799 monthly for eight online sessions. Those are market figures from the sources named, not an IB Gram price list. For a Higher Level Chemistry student in the investigation term, two sessions a week is common, so budget towards the specialist band rather than the generalist one.

faqs.question: Is a Chemistry tutor living in Downtown Dubai better placed than one teaching online?
faqs.answer: Not for this subject. Downtown is one bridge from Business Bay and contains no secondary campus either, so a tutor there is no closer to your child's school or syllabus. What matters is whether the person has taught Higher Level Chemistry repeatedly and can name where marks go missing in energetics and the mechanisms. The number of people who can do that within any one Dubai district is small; the number who can do it at seven o'clock Gulf Standard Time over video is much larger. Proximity is a filter that removes specialists without improving the teaching.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 at a Sobha Hartland school and failing Chemistry tests. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with the marked papers, not the syllabus. Three or four marked tests usually show one pattern rather than general weakness — most often sign errors in energetics, formula use in acid-base work without checking which species is in excess, or mechanism questions answered from memory. A single diagnostic session with those papers in front of the tutor identifies which. From there a short block on that one area, with the same question type revisited a fortnight later, does more than a term of general revision. Do not wait for the next report; reports describe the symptom.

faqs.question: What changed when the Chemistry subject guide was reorganised?
faqs.answer: Content is now grouped under Structure and Reactivity rather than a long list of numbered topics, and the assessment sits on two papers plus the scientific investigation. Paper 1 is split into a multiple-choice part and a data-analysis part that behave quite differently. The practical effect for a student is that questions more often require two ideas taught months apart to be combined, which is why recall-based revision stops working around the middle of DP1. Confirm the exact component structure, durations and weightings with your school's IB coordinator, who holds the authoritative current version.

faqs.question: How are Paper 1A and Paper 1B different, and does that change revision?
faqs.answer: Completely, and yes. Paper 1A is multiple choice across the whole course and rewards secure recall at speed. Paper 1B presents unfamiliar experimental data and rewards the ability to read a table, spot what is being varied, handle uncertainty and draw a defensible inference. Students who revise only by topic prepare for 1A and walk into 1B cold. The fix is to practise 1B as its own skill, timed, on data the student has never seen, several times before the mock rather than in the fortnight before the exam.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Chemistry need more maths than my child currently has?
faqs.answer: It needs confident logarithms, rearrangement and proportional reasoning rather than advanced mathematics. Students on Mathematics Analysis and Approaches usually have that already. Students on Applications and Interpretation can take Chemistry at Higher Level comfortably, but the logarithm work that appears in pH and rate questions has to be covered somewhere, and the school's maths course may not reach it at the right moment. One or two sessions on that specific arithmetic, early in DP1, prevents a recurring loss of marks that otherwise looks like a chemistry problem.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Chemistry scientific investigation worth, and who marks it?
faqs.answer: It is a 24-mark task assessed against four published criteria — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — marked by the school and moderated by the IB. It carries a fifth of the final grade, which puts it level with a written paper. Most of the mark is effectively decided by the research question: one that is narrow enough to measure sets up every later criterion, while one that is too broad produces data nobody can analyse. Confirm the internal deadline with the school early, because it usually falls in a term that is already crowded.

faqs.question: May a tutor suggest the research question for my child's investigation?
faqs.answer: No. The research question is part of what is being assessed, so supplying it is not help, it is substitution. A tutor may ask what the student is actually measuring, point out that a variable cannot be controlled, question whether the proposed range will produce usable data, and give feedback on a question the student has drafted. The student writes the question, the method, the analysis, the conclusion and the evaluation. Ask any provider to state that boundary in writing before the investigation term begins; providers who will not are telling you something.

faqs.question: Organic mechanisms are where my child collapses. Can that be repaired before the exams?
faqs.answer: Usually, because the failure is narrower than it looks. Most students have memorised mechanism diagrams rather than learned to decide which species is electron-rich and which is electron-poor, so they reproduce the case they memorised and fail every variant. Repair means working marked mechanism questions one at a time, naming the decision at each arrow, and returning to the same question type a fortnight later to confirm it holds. Four to six focused sessions typically shift this, provided the work is on marked past-paper questions rather than on re-reading notes.

faqs.question: How late can a Chemistry session start on a Business Bay school night?
faqs.answer: In term time a Business Bay student is usually home between 15:45 and 16:30, so a 17:30 start works for most families and 18:00 is comfortable. Students commuting from the Jumeirah direction return later and tend to settle on 18:30. Because lessons are online there is no travel to add at either end, which is the practical advantage of this district: the slot is set by the bus, not by a tutor's driving time. Hold a slightly later slot for the first fortnight and pull it earlier once you know what the route really does.

faqs.question: Do Chemistry lessons move during Ramadan for families here?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the shift should be planned rather than improvised. School days shorten, so an earlier afternoon slot becomes possible, and many families prefer to move a session to after iftar instead. Both work for online delivery because nothing depends on a tutor travelling. The point worth planning is the revision calendar rather than the clock: if the examination series falls close to or after Ramadan, the heavy past-paper work should be front-loaded into the weeks before it rather than squeezed into a month when concentration is genuinely harder.

faqs.question: Does a private Chemistry tutor in Dubai need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Ask the tutor to show you the permit. Anyone quoting you a fee for it is describing something other than the official route, and anyone quoting a specific fine amount is guessing, because no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level Chemistry to apply for medicine from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set by each university and vary by country, so the only reliable answer comes from the admissions page of the universities your child is actually considering. Many medical programmes in the United Kingdom and elsewhere expect Chemistry at Higher Level, and some specify a minimum grade; others accept different combinations. Check each one directly and early, in DP1 rather than DP2, because the subject choice is difficult to reverse after the first term. Tutoring does not change an entry requirement and nobody should suggest that it does.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Chemistry specialist is free at our hour?
faqs.answer: You are told. Coverage for a narrow Higher Level subject at one specific weekday hour is not guaranteed, and the honest options are a different slot, a short wait for a named specialist, or a different weekday. What should not happen is being matched to a general science tutor described as a Chemistry specialist, which costs a family four sessions before anyone admits it. Most providers in this market publish no coverage limit at all; asking directly what happens when nobody is available is a fair test of any of them.

faqs.question: Which schools do Business Bay Chemistry students usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no secondary campus inside Business Bay, so students travel. The commonest directions are the creek side towards Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf, where schools such as Hartland International, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Swiss International Scientific School sit; the Al Barsha and Al Khail corridor; and the Jumeirah and Al Safa route along Al Wasl Road. Those schools are named as context for the school run only — no affiliation or endorsement is implied. All of them teach Chemistry from the same international subject guide, which is the point.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-city-walk.tutorsIntro: The chemistry teachers below work from the published mark scheme and the student's own scripts. Each has taught the current course, knows that the options topics and the third paper are gone, and will start by establishing which of the six themes the school has already covered.

intro.heading: What the chemistry grade is made of, theme by theme
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry is a single structure with very few moving parts, and knowing the structure precisely is the difference between revision that works and revision that feels productive. There are six themes, organised under two headings. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. There is no options topic in the current course and no third paper, which catches out students revising from inherited notes and parents working from an older guide.

Assessment is three components. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is 44% and is extended response. The scientific investigation, marked out of 24 across four criteria, is 20%. Higher Level covers the same six themes with additional depth and sits longer papers, and the component weightings are identical to Standard Level, so the extra Higher Level load appears as breadth and algebra rather than as a different examination shape.

Where the marks actually go is more specific than that, and it is the reason a City Walk family should be asking a prospective tutor diagnostic questions rather than asking about experience in years. Students lose Paper 2 marks on four recurring things: command terms obeyed loosely, state symbols and units omitted, reasoning compressed so that the marker cannot see the step the mark is attached to, and the quantitative chain breaking somewhere between moles and the final answer. Each one is a repeatable error. Each one recurs on every paper until somebody names it and drills it out.

City Walk students mostly attend schools in Al Safa, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, and those schools teach the six themes in different orders. That matters for planning: a revision programme built on the published order will repair content the class covered in September while next week's assessment goes unprepared. Any useful plan starts from the school's own topic list, which is why we ask for it before the second session rather than assuming a sequence.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For chemistry specifically the online format has a concrete advantage: mechanisms are drawn on a shared screen where the annotation stays visible and can be replayed, and a student's own script can be marked against the published mark scheme in front of them rather than handed back a week later. What follows is the theme-to-paper map, the component breakdown, the command-term vocabulary, the quantitative chain, the mechanisms work, a twelve-week past-paper method and the honest limits on coursework help.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-city-walk.programmesIntro: Chemistry arrives on a student's timetable from one of three directions, and the gap to close depends on which. These are the routes City Walk families take into Diploma chemistry, with what each one leaves undone.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme chemistry
programmes.description: Six themes, two written papers and one scientific investigation. Paper 1 contains multiple-choice and data-based sections; Paper 2 is extended response; the investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Higher Level adds depth within the same themes and longer papers at identical weightings.
programmes.countryNote: Among the schools City Walk students attend, the order in which the six themes are taught varies widely, and some campuses teach structure and reactivity in parallel rather than in sequence. A tutor who assumes the published order will be a term out of step within a month. The first thing we ask for is the school's scheme of work, which almost every Dubai department will share on request.

programmes.name: From Year 11 chemistry into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1, taken separately or inside a combined award. The Diploma assumes Extended or Higher tier content: mole arithmetic, bonding, rates and the basics of organic nomenclature all reappear in Year 12 at pace, without reteaching. Core-tier or combined-science backgrounds are workable but need deliberate filling in.
programmes.countryNote: This is the dominant route in the City Walk corridor, where most nearby campuses are British curriculum. The specific gap that shows up in the first Year 12 term is quantitative: students arrive able to recall bonding and periodicity and unable to carry a mole calculation through three steps without losing a unit. Six weeks in the summer on exactly that is the highest-value chemistry work available to a family here.

programmes.name: From the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma
programmes.description: Criterion-marked sciences across four criteria, each out of eight. The processing and evaluating criterion is the one that predicts Diploma chemistry performance, because it assesses data handling, graphing and evaluation rather than recall, which is precisely what the data-based section of Paper 1 and the investigation go on to test.
programmes.countryNote: One IB continuum school sits in Al Safa within a short drive of City Walk and others are in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, so this route exists locally but serves a minority of families. Students arriving from it are usually stronger than their peers on the investigation and weaker on timed written papers and on fast content recall, and both deficits respond to a few weeks of deliberate work.

programmes.description: The scientific investigation carries 20% of the chemistry grade across four criteria of six marks each. An Extended Essay in chemistry runs to 4,000 words with a school supervisor. Both are the student's own work throughout. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a research question and challenge a conclusion, and may not write, edit or supply any part of either.
programmes.countryNote: This is the part of the Dubai market a City Walk parent should treat most carefully. One provider in this cluster has been documented selling completed internal assessments at AED 3,750, which is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger carried entirely by the student. Dubai schools run originality checks and supervisors sign declarations, so the risk is concrete rather than theoretical.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-city-walk.subjectsIntro: Chemistry sits inside a six-subject Diploma and competes with the rest of it for the same evenings. These are the subjects that interact with it most, and what each one takes from or gives to a chemistry grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six themes, two written papers, one investigation. The marks concentrate in Paper 2, where command-term discipline, state symbols, units and visible reasoning steps decide the grade as much as content knowledge does. The mechanisms theme and the quantitative chain are the two places where paid teaching time earns its rate most clearly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Supplies the logarithms that pH work needs, the proportional reasoning behind every mole calculation and the algebraic speed the papers assume. Chemistry errors that look conceptual are frequently arithmetic, which is why a chemistry tutor who can diagnose across both subjects shortens the plan rather than lengthening it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Compatible with chemistry at either level and common among students pairing chemistry with economics or business. It leans on graphing technology and leaves symbolic manipulation thinner than the chemistry papers assume, so a block of algebraic fluency work is often more useful than more chemistry content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual partner for medicine applicants. Marked against the same four investigation criteria and the same command-term vocabulary, so work done on answering 'explain' and 'outline' properly in chemistry transfers directly. The volume of recall is the differentiating workload rather than the reasoning.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares the data-based question style, the uncertainty arithmetic and the graph-reading skills, so one block of teaching on uncertainties serves both courses. Taken with chemistry by most engineering applicants, and the pair competes hard for the same evening hours in an exam year.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Offered at some Dubai campuses and occasionally taken instead of a second science. It uses the same investigation criteria, so the criterion teaching transfers. Families treating it as a lighter alternative to chemistry should check the published entry requirements of the universities on their list first.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Relevant to a chemistry page for one reason: it is where students learn to write to a brief, and the same discipline raises Paper 2 marks. A student who can identify what a question is actually asking in an English essay can be taught to do it in chemistry considerably faster than one who cannot.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in chemistry
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word piece with a school supervisor. The efficient intervention is one or two sessions narrowing the research question before any laboratory work begins, because an unbounded question cannot be rescued later. The student writes every word, takes every measurement and reaches every conclusion.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects, carrying points alongside the Extended Essay. Chemistry students often find the exhibition harder than the essay because it asks them to argue about knowledge rather than about content, and it tends to get neglected until Year 13.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: KHDA requirement · all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in every Dubai private school regardless of licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. They occupy timetable and homework time that any chemistry plan has to work around rather than pretend does not exist.

sections.heading: What this search needs answering before anything else
paragraphs: A City Walk parent searching for a chemistry tutor has usually been given a grade and no diagnosis. The report says 4 or 5, the student says they understand it, and the gap between those two statements is where all the useful information lives. Closing it takes three facts, none of which requires a tutor to obtain: which of the six themes the school has taught so far, what the student's most recent written paper actually lost marks on, and whether the scientific investigation has been started. With those three a plan is obvious. Without them any plan is decoration.

The reason this page leads with the syllabus rather than with reassurance is that chemistry rewards precision in a way that is almost invisible from outside the classroom. A student can hold a correct understanding of buffer behaviour and lose every mark on the question because they wrote a conclusion without the state symbols, or because they answered 'deduce' as though it said 'state'. Parents reasonably interpret that as not knowing the chemistry. It is not. It is a vocabulary and layout problem, and it is the single most common reason a capable Diploma chemistry student sits two grades below their understanding.

The third thing worth saying at the outset is what the course is not. There is no options topic in the current chemistry course and no third paper, and a great deal of material circulating among students in this corridor still assumes both. A student revising an options topic is revising something that will not be examined, and a student budgeting time for a Paper 3 is misallocating their final term. Establishing that early costs nothing and routinely recovers a fortnight of revision time.

sections.heading: The six themes mapped to the papers they are examined in
paragraphs: The course is organised under two headings. Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, including atomic structure and the mole concept. Structure 2 covers models of bonding and structure. Structure 3 covers classification of matter, including periodicity and the organic families. Reactivity 1 covers what drives chemical reactions, which is energetics. Reactivity 2 covers how much, how fast and how far, which is equilibrium, rates, acids and bases and redox. Reactivity 3 covers the mechanisms of chemical change.

Every theme can appear in every component, which is a point students find counterintuitive and which changes how revision should be organised. There is no theme that only appears in multiple choice and none that is examined exclusively in extended response. What differs is the characteristic way each theme is tested: the quantitative themes dominate the data-based section, the structural themes carry a disproportionate share of the multiple-choice marks, and the mechanisms theme produces the longest extended-response questions at Higher Level. The table below sets out that pattern alongside the typical loss in each theme.

Revision order should follow dependency rather than the published sequence. Structure 1 comes first regardless of what the school is currently teaching, because the mole concept and the quantitative relationships underneath it are reused in Reactivity 1 and Reactivity 2 and a weakness there reappears disguised as an equilibrium problem. Structure 2 and Structure 3 are the most self-contained and the safest to leave for a short block closer to the papers. Reactivity 3 needs the longest run-up, because it is a volume problem rather than an understanding problem.
