intro.heading: Why IB chemistry slips in Year 12, and what actually fixes it
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma science where a student can be working hard, revising diligently, and still watching the grade fall. The reason is that the course changes character partway through. IGCSE and MYP chemistry reward knowing things: formulae, reagents, trends, definitions. Diploma chemistry rewards explaining why, and particularly why a reaction goes the way it does. A student who revises by memorising runs out of road somewhere in the organic topic and often cannot say what happened.

There are two walls and they are reliably the same two. Organic mechanisms are the first. A student can recite that a halogenoalkane plus hydroxide gives an alcohol, and still lose every mark on a question asking them to explain the attack, because they have never been taught to reason about electron density, partial charge and where a nucleophile goes. The second is energetics and thermodynamics — enthalpy cycles, entropy, Gibbs free energy — where the arithmetic is manageable and the sign conventions quietly destroy answers.

Underneath both sits moles. Stoichiometry, concentration, limiting reagent, percentage yield, gas volumes. Students arrive from IGCSE able to balance an equation and not able to carry a multi-step calculation through unit conversions under time pressure, and because every topic uses it, a weakness in moles presents as a weakness in everything. Any diagnostic worth having checks this before it checks anything the student named.

Then the Internal Assessment, worth 20% of the grade, and lost far more often at the design stage than in the writing. A chemistry investigation needs a research question with a genuinely measurable variable, a method that can produce enough data to say something about uncertainty, and controlled variables that were actually controlled. Students typically ask for help once the data is collected, by which time the available mark has been set.

The practical realities out here shape the help. DAMAC Hills 2 sits along the Al Qudra corridor and almost every Diploma student travels out to school — Motor City, Dubai Sports City, deeper into the city. A half three finish becomes a 4:45pm arrival home in afternoon traffic, and a tutor who still has to drive here makes it half six. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only.

And the supply is thin. The IB accounts for roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, spread citywide, with only the final two years sitting the Diploma. Chemistry at Higher Level is a narrow specialism within that, and the probability that a qualified HL chemistry teacher lives near DAMAC Hills 2 with a free weekday evening is low. Online matching makes the question irrelevant.

The pairing is sensible, but the two subjects reward different habits: biology rewards recall structured by command term, chemistry rewards explanation, and students sometimes apply the biology habit to a chemistry paper.

programmes.name: Chemistry Higher Level
programmes.description: Additional depth across the course plus an extra written paper, with the Internal Assessment still at 20%. HL organic chemistry extends into reaction pathways and stereochemistry, and HL energetics into entropy and spontaneity. The level rewards students who can build an argument across several steps and penalises formula lookup.
programmes.countryNote: This is the level most medicine, dentistry and pharmacy applications require, which means DAMAC Hills 2 families often need precisely the specialist the neighbourhood cannot supply. It is also where local availability most often reaches zero, which is the whole case for matching online rather than by distance.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into Diploma chemistry
programmes.description: The step that catches strong students. IGCSE chemistry rewards recall and single-step calculation; Diploma chemistry expects mechanism-level explanation and multi-step quantitative work. A high IGCSE grade is not protection, and the slip usually shows by November of Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: The intervention that works is a short block on moles, concentration and multi-step calculation plus an introduction to reasoning about electron density, taken in the summer or early Year 12. Done then it is inexpensive; done in Year 13 it is a rescue with two years of content sitting on top of it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-damac-hills-.subjectsIntro: These are the chemistry topics and components DAMAC Hills 2 students most often need work on, with the specific place marks go. Availability varies by level and term and is confirmed at the trial lesson.

subjects.name: Moles, stoichiometry and concentration
subjects.description: The layer every other topic stands on. Multi-step conversions between mass, moles, volume and concentration, limiting reagent, percentage yield and gas calculations. A weakness here presents as a weakness in everything else, so it is the first thing a diagnostic should test.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry: mechanisms
subjects.description: Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and, at HL, longer pathways and stereochemistry. The marks are in explaining why a species attacks where it does, using electron density and partial charge. Reagent lists memorised without that reasoning collapse on an unfamiliar question.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.description: Enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies, and at HL entropy and Gibbs free energy. The chemistry is usually understood and the sign conventions are usually not, so answers are internally consistent and wrong. This is a technique fix rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Equilibrium and kinetics
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning, equilibrium constants, rate equations and, at HL, determining orders from data. Students often state what shifts rather than explaining why, and the HL rate-determination questions are where data-handling confidence shows.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH and pKa calculations, buffers, titration curves and electrochemical cells. Titration-curve interpretation and buffer reasoning are reliably examined and reliably weak, and both improve quickly with worked practice against the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and the explanations behind them. Students can state a trend and lose every explanation mark because the answer omits shielding, nuclear charge or atomic radius as the reason rather than the label.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Intermolecular forces, molecular geometry and the link between structure and physical property. Explaining a boiling point difference properly requires naming the force and comparing its strength, and partial answers lose most of the credit available.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainty in chemistry
subjects.description: Percentage uncertainty in titrations and mass measurements, significant figures justified by the apparatus, and whether a result supports a conclusion. Examined in the papers and decisive in the investigation's processing and evaluation marks.

subjects.name: The Chemistry Internal Assessment
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation against published criteria. Lost most often at design: no measurable variable, insufficient repeats, a range too narrow to show a trend, or a controlled variable that was not controlled. Criterion reading in week one beats draft reading in week ten.

subjects.name: Practical technique and the alternative to the bench
subjects.description: Titration precision, dilution, gravimetric technique and the reasoning behind them. Bench work happens at school; what one-to-one work adds is prediction, anomaly handling, uncertainty treatment and writing up to the expected standard.

subjects.name: Chemical language and command terms
subjects.description: State, outline, explain, deduce, discuss and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and chemistry punishes imprecision harder than most subjects. A knowledgeable student answering the wrong command term is a routine and entirely fixable loss.

sections.heading: The two walls: organic mechanisms and energetics
paragraphs: Almost every chemistry enquiry we take from DAMAC Hills 2 names one of these, and they fail for opposite reasons, which is why they need different teaching.

Organic chemistry fails because it is taught, and revised, as a catalogue. Reagent plus substrate gives product. Learn the list. That survives until a question gives an unfamiliar molecule or asks for an explanation of the mechanism, at which point a student with a perfect catalogue has nothing to say. What the marks actually reward is reasoning about electron density: where a molecule is electron-poor, why a nucleophile is attracted there, what happens to the intermediate, why one pathway dominates. Taught that way, organic chemistry becomes the most predictable topic in the course rather than the least.

Energetics fails for the opposite reason. The concepts are usually understood and the execution is unreliable. Sign conventions are the main culprit — an exothermic value entered as positive, a cycle traversed in the wrong direction, an entropy change whose sign contradicts the physical description the student just wrote. The arithmetic is not hard; the bookkeeping is, and it produces answers that are internally consistent and entirely wrong.

Both are fixable quickly once correctly identified, which is the argument for diagnosing rather than covering. The table below sets out each wall, the real cause, and the work that moves it. The useful column is the last one, because in both cases the remedy is not more content.

sections.heading: What a chemistry paper rewards that revision notes do not
paragraphs: Chemistry punishes imprecision harder than any other Diploma science, and the punishment is invisible in revision. A student reading their notes understands the content. The same student writing an answer loses marks because the sentence was nearly right, and nearly right scores nothing in a subject where the mark scheme specifies the explanation.

Command terms are the first mechanism. State wants an answer. Outline wants a brief account. Explain wants a cause. Deduce wants a conclusion drawn from given information. Discuss wants balance. Evaluate wants a supported judgement. A student who understands periodicity and answers explain with a statement of the trend has written something true and scored nothing, because the question asked why and the answer said what.

The second is the specificity of explanation. Asked why one compound has a higher boiling point, an answer naming intermolecular forces in general gets partial credit at best; an answer naming the specific force, comparing its strength and connecting that to the energy needed to separate molecules gets the marks. The difference is not knowledge. It is the habit of finishing the reasoning rather than gesturing at it.

The third is unshown working in quantitative questions. Marks are available for method, and a student who computes several steps mentally and writes one line forfeits credit they genuinely earned. This is a behaviour change rather than learning, takes a few weeks of marked practice with a rule that every step goes on paper, and is probably the cheapest grade movement available in the subject.
bullets: Command terms decide the shape of the answer, and the shape decides the mark
Name the specific force or factor, then complete the reasoning — do not gesture
Method marks are forfeited by mental arithmetic; every step goes on paper
Practise against the mark scheme rather than against a sense of having understood

sections.heading: The Chemistry Internal Assessment is decided before the data exists
paragraphs: A fifth of the chemistry grade comes from an individual investigation, and by the time most students ask for help the marks that mattered are already set — not in the write-up, but in the fortnight when the research question was chosen and the method planned.

The design faults recur. A research question whose independent variable cannot actually be varied systematically with school apparatus. A range so narrow that any trend sits inside the uncertainty. Too few repeats to say anything honest about reliability. A controlled variable that was not controlled, discovered at the evaluation stage when the only remaining option is to admit it. A titration-based investigation with an uncertainty larger than the effect being measured. None of these can be rescued by a better conclusion.

So the valuable intervention is early and it is permitted in full. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards and what it is worth, test whether a proposed question can be investigated with the equipment available, check that the planned range and number of repeats will generate analysable data, point out that a chosen method's uncertainty will swamp the result, and give criterion-level feedback on a draft the student has written.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work: no writing any section, no supplying data or calculations, no model investigation to adapt, no editing a draft to a finish. The student signs an authorship declaration and the supervisor signs alongside, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice. This search result contains operators selling completed Internal Assessments — one advertises them at AED 3,750 — which risks the entire Diploma rather than one component.

sections.heading: Chemistry Higher Level and the medicine route
paragraphs: A large share of the DAMAC Hills 2 chemistry enquiries we take are really about medicine, dentistry or pharmacy, and the honest framing matters because the subject is usually a hard requirement rather than a preference.

What we can say plainly: many medical, dental and pharmacy programmes specify chemistry, frequently at Higher Level, and often alongside a second science. What we will not do is publish a points threshold or an entry requirement for any named university, because those are set by the institution, change between cycles, and differ between UAE, UK, European and North American systems. Check the actual published requirement of the actual programmes your child is considering, including UAE institutions, and check it for the entry year rather than the current one.

Nor will we suggest that tutoring is required for any admissions outcome. That would be a false-urgency claim about a competitive process whose variables — interview performance, admissions testing, personal statement, school reference, the strength of a particular year's applicant pool — are mostly outside a chemistry tutor's reach. What chemistry support can do is narrower and real: make sure the HL chemistry grade is not the thing that removes the option.

For planning, the useful consequence is timing. A student aiming at a chemistry-requiring degree needs HL chemistry secure by the end of Year 12, not improving through Year 13, because applications and predicted grades are made before the final result exists. That pushes the sensible start date for support to early Year 12, which is also when it is cheapest and most effective.

sections.heading: Practical and data skills when the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection to online chemistry tuition, and it deserves an answer rather than a reassurance. Nobody on a screen can stand beside a burette and correct a student's technique at the meniscus.

What is true is that bench technique is a small share of the assessed marks and the part of it that is assessed happens at school. Titration precision, dilution, gravimetric handling — these are taught and practised in the laboratory, and no tutor, in person or online, substitutes for that. A provider claiming otherwise is overselling.

What one-to-one work does add is the reasoning around the bench, which is where most of the available marks live. Predicting what an experiment should produce before it is run. Deciding what to do with an anomalous result rather than discarding it silently. Calculating percentage uncertainty from the apparatus and judging whether the effect is larger than it. Writing up so that the processing and evaluation criteria are actually addressed. Every one of those is a paper-and-screen skill and improves faster one-to-one than in a class.

The same applies to the written papers, where experimental questions ask students to evaluate a method rather than perform one: identify the flaw, name the controlled variable that was missed, say whether the data supports the stated conclusion. That is examinable reasoning, and it is what we teach. Ask your child's school which practical components are assessed and how, and we will match a tutor who has prepared students for those specific components.
bullets: Bench technique happens at school and no tutor replaces it
Prediction, anomaly handling and uncertainty are where the marks concentrate

sections.heading: Fitting chemistry into a DAMAC Hills 2 week
paragraphs: Chemistry needs a particular kind of hour. Mechanism work especially requires a student to hold several things in mind at once — structure, charge, what moved where — and a tired student cannot do it. Booking whichever slot is available is a worse decision here than in a recall-heavy subject.

The timetable out here is tight. A half three finish in Motor City or Dubai Sports City means a 4:45pm arrival home once the afternoon traffic on Hessa Street and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is counted; from an inner-city IB school it is nearer five. Because nobody is driving to you, a session can begin at 4:45pm, which for a Year 12 student is often the best hour available. For Year 13 the better choice is usually 8pm for ninety minutes, when a full past-paper section plus marking fits without rushing.

Weekend mornings are the underused option, and for chemistry they are particularly effective during an Internal Assessment term: two hours of uninterrupted work on method design or data processing is worth more than three scattered weekday half-hours. It also competes with nothing else in the week.

Ramadan is planned rather than discovered. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so DAMAC Hills 2 families typically move to a late-morning, early-afternoon or post-Iftar slot, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block. Prayer times are built into the slot from the start. What we work to avoid is the drift of cancel, reschedule, cancel — in chemistry that breaks the thread quickly, because mechanism work builds directly on the previous session.
bullets: Mechanism work needs an alert hour; recall revision tolerates a tired one

sections.heading: What chemistry tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates, read from provider pages in October 2026. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai research giving the specialist band as AED 200-450 plus. Budget online advertises from AED 33-65, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. In-home visits are AED 180-500 including travel. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Chemistry at Higher Level is one of the subjects where the budget band fails most visibly. A capable graduate can teach periodic trends and balance equations. Teaching organic mechanism reasoning, and teaching it so a student can handle a molecule they have never seen, is a different competence, and so is knowing what the investigation's processing criterion actually rewards. A term at AED 50 an hour with somebody who has never supervised a chemistry investigation produces pleasant sessions and no movement.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for one weekly hour of budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits.

Each figure belongs to the provider named beside it. None is an IB Gram price — we publish no rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on level, the specific gap and the weeks remaining. Take the free trial lesson and get a quote after the diagnostic.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about a chemistry result
paragraphs: No grade guarantee. Not a 7, not a points improvement, not a particular paper score, and specifically not an admissions outcome. The variables — prior quantitative fluency, weeks remaining, whether the investigation was designed well, whether the student has ever been taught to finish an explanation — are not all under a tutor's control.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which means none at all. No average chemistry score achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never say how any of them was produced.

No regulator or awarding-body claim, and no examiner descriptions. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not describe tutors as IB examiners because current examiner status is not something we can evidence. Examiner status confers no access to marking, boundaries or paper content whatever is implied. We host no IB past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables; they belong to the IB and we link the official source.

What we will give you is a diagnostic verdict. After watching your child work real paper questions, a chemistry specialist will say whether the gap is the quantitative layer, mechanism reasoning, explanation technique or the investigation, roughly how long each takes to move, and whether the available time is enough. Occasionally the answer is that it is not, and that concentrating on two of those rather than four is the better plan.

faqs.question: Why has my child's chemistry grade dropped since starting the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Because the course changes character. IGCSE and MYP chemistry reward knowing things — formulae, reagents, trends, definitions. Diploma chemistry rewards explaining why, especially why a reaction proceeds as it does. A student who revises by memorising runs out of road in the organic topic and often cannot say what went wrong, because their method worked for two years. The fix is not covering the syllabus again; it is being taught to reason from electron density and to finish an explanation rather than gesture at it.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry feel impossible to my child?
faqs.answer: Almost always because it has been learned as a catalogue: this reagent plus that substrate gives this product, memorise the list. That survives until a question presents an unfamiliar molecule or asks for the mechanism, at which point a perfect catalogue provides nothing. The marks reward reasoning about where a molecule is electron-poor, why a nucleophile is attracted there, what the intermediate is and why one pathway dominates. Taught that way, organic chemistry becomes the most predictable topic in the course rather than the hardest.

faqs.question: What is the quickest chemistry improvement available before mocks?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order. First, sign conventions in energetics written down as a fixed rule and then drilled, because the chemistry is usually understood and the bookkeeping is what fails. Second, a rule that every step of a calculation goes on paper, since method marks are being forfeited by mental arithmetic. Third, command-term discipline: explain wants a cause, deduce wants a conclusion from given data, and a knowledgeable student answering the wrong command term scores nothing. All three are weeks rather than months.

faqs.question: How much is the chemistry Internal Assessment worth and when should we get help?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the grade at both levels, and the help is worth most in the fortnight when the research question and method are chosen. The recurring faults are an independent variable that cannot be varied with school apparatus, a range too narrow for a trend to exceed the uncertainty, too few repeats to say anything about reliability, and measurement apparatus whose uncertainty swamps the effect. None of those is rescuable by a better conclusion, which is why week-one criterion reading beats week-ten draft reading.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry investigation without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permitted ground is wide. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards and its mark allocation, test whether a proposed question is feasible with available equipment, check the planned range and repeats will produce analysable data, point out that an apparatus uncertainty will dominate the result, and give criterion-level feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any section, supply data or calculations, provide a model to adapt, or edit to a finish. The student signs an authorship declaration.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry at Higher Level required for a medicine application?
faqs.answer: Many medical, dental and pharmacy programmes specify chemistry, frequently at Higher Level and often alongside a second science, but the requirement belongs to the institution and the entry year rather than to a general rule. Check the actual published requirement of the actual programmes being considered, including UAE institutions, for the year of entry. We will not publish a threshold or imply tutoring is required for any admissions outcome. What support can do is narrower: make sure the chemistry grade is not what removes the option.

faqs.question: How are chemistry practicals handled if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Bench technique — titration precision, dilution, gravimetric handling — is taught and assessed at school, and no tutor, in person or online, substitutes for it. What one-to-one work adds is the reasoning around the bench, which is where most of the available marks live: predicting what an experiment should produce, deciding what to do with an anomaly, calculating percentage uncertainty from the apparatus, and writing up so the processing and evaluation criteria are actually addressed. Written experimental questions also test evaluating a method rather than performing one.

faqs.question: Is moles really the problem when my child says organic is?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is why our diagnostic starts there regardless of what was named. Stoichiometry, concentration, limiting reagent and percentage yield sit underneath every topic in the course, so a weakness in multi-step conversion presents as a weakness in everything. Students arrive from IGCSE able to balance an equation and unable to carry a calculation through unit conversions under time pressure. A short quantitative block fixes it, and every subsequent session in every other topic lands better afterwards.

faqs.question: Is there an HL chemistry specialist near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The IB is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, only the final two years sit the Diploma, and Chemistry at Higher Level is a narrow specialism inside that. The pool of people who have taught it to final grade is small citywide, and most are serving school staff whose permit code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Online matching removes distance from a problem where distance was never the constraint that mattered.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor come to our villa in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers chemistry tuition to DAMAC Hills 2 one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from the Al Qudra corridor a real share of that is driving. For Diploma chemistry the binding constraint is whether the tutor can teach mechanism reasoning and investigation design, which has nothing to do with proximity.

faqs.question: What do DAMAC Hills 2 families pay for IB chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate giving AED 200-450 plus, budget online from AED 33-65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and BartyED at AED 650 premium. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work. Those belong to the providers named; we quote after the diagnostic.

faqs.question: Can a cheap tutor cover Higher Level chemistry?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and HL chemistry shows the limits of the budget band clearly. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate can teach periodic trends and balance equations competently. What they generally cannot do is teach organic mechanism reasoning so a student can handle a molecule they have never seen, or tell you what the investigation's processing criterion actually rewards. A term with somebody who has never supervised a chemistry investigation produces agreeable sessions and no movement, and the low hourly rate is what stops anyone examining it.

faqs.question: When should chemistry support start for a Year 12 student here?
faqs.answer: Early Year 12, for two reasons. First, the quantitative layer and mechanism reasoning both need time, and everything taught afterwards sits on them, so securing them early makes the rest of the course cheaper. Second, if a chemistry-requiring degree is in view, the grade needs to be secure by the end of Year 12 because predicted grades are made before the final result exists. By March of Year 13 the only remaining lever is paper technique, which is worth real marks but is the smallest of the three.

faqs.question: Should chemistry and biology be taken with the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually not at Higher Level, and this is one pairing where we would rather match two specialists. The content depth pulls apart at HL, and the two subjects reward different habits: biology rewards recall structured by command term, chemistry rewards explanation built from mechanism. A tutor strong in one often imports the wrong habit into the other, which is a subtle but real cost. Chemistry and physics share the quantitative layer and pair more naturally where one tutor genuinely teaches both.

faqs.question: When do IB chemistry exams fall for DAMAC Hills 2 students?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no specific IB date, and the reason is worth saying: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we will not put an unverified date in front of a family who will plan around it. Get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For IGCSE siblings, Cambridge runs June and November series — February/March is India-only — and Pearson runs May/June and November.

intro.heading: What the course is, before anyone talks about tutoring
paragraphs: IB Chemistry is the Diploma subject where the gap between understanding and marks is widest. Students who can explain a concept out loud still lose marks in writing, because the mark scheme rewards a particular kind of precision: a direction and a reason, a correct unit, a state symbol, a named interaction rather than a vague force. A tutor who only teaches content will not close that gap. A tutor who works from mark schemes will.

The course itself is organised around two organising concepts, each with three themes. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level carries additional content within those themes rather than extra themes, and sits longer papers. Running alongside is a practical scheme of work and the internally assessed scientific investigation, which carries 20 per cent of the final grade on its own.

That last number is the one Deira families most often underrate. The scientific investigation is a single piece of work of up to 3,000 words, marked against four criteria worth six marks each, and it is worth as much as a substantial slice of the written examinations. A student who produces a strong investigation and an average set of papers finishes above a student with the reverse profile, and the investigation is the part a family can actually plan for, because its deadline is set by the school and known a year ahead.

Locally, the picture is this. Deira is dense apartment housing north of the Creek, and most Diploma students here travel across the water to Al Garhoud or Dubai Festival City, arriving home around 4pm to 4:30pm. The IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, and Chemistry at Higher Level is among the thinnest specialisms in the city, so a family needing one should ask early rather than urgently.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For chemistry the practical consequence is worth stating honestly: we can teach the theory, the calculations, the mechanisms, the data analysis and the investigation write-up, and we cannot handle apparatus for your child. Practical work is the school's job and is part of the course's required practical scheme; what tutoring adds is the ability to read a data set and write about it the way the mark scheme wants.

subjects.name: Structure 1: Models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with additional HL content

subjects.levels: SL and HL, with additional HL content

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: What drives chemical reactions?
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with additional HL content

subjects.levels: SL and HL, with additional HL content
subjects.description: The amount of chemical change, the rate of chemical change, and the extent of chemical change. subjects.levels: SL and HL, with additional HL content

sections.heading: The six themes, and what each demands in writing
paragraphs: The current Chemistry guide organises the course under two concepts, Structure and Reactivity, each with three themes. Naming them matters because it is the fastest way to establish whether a prospective tutor has taught the course as it currently stands rather than an older version of it, and because it lets a parent see where their child's marked work is actually failing.

Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter: the particulate model, the nuclear atom, electron configurations, counting particles by mass through the mole, and ideal gases. Structure 2 covers models of bonding and structure: the ionic, covalent and metallic models and how those models translate into materials. Structure 3 covers classification of matter: the periodic table as a classification of elements, and functional groups as a classification of organic compounds.

Reactivity 1 asks what drives chemical reactions, covering enthalpy changes, energy cycles, energy from fuels, and entropy and spontaneity. Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far: the amount of chemical change, the rate of chemical change, and the extent of chemical change. Reactivity 3 asks about mechanisms: proton transfer, electron transfer, and electron sharing and electron-pair sharing reactions. Higher Level adds content within these themes rather than appending new ones, which is precisely why a tutor who has only taught Standard Level is a weak match for Higher Level work.

The table sets each theme against what the mark scheme actually wants from a written answer in it. That column is the useful one, because a student who understands bonding and writes strong intermolecular forces will be marked as though they did not.

sections.heading: The assessment, component by component
paragraphs: Chemistry is assessed through two written papers and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 contains short-answer and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the final grade. Higher Level papers are longer and carry the additional higher level content. Confirm the exact weightings for your child's cohort with their teacher, since the subject guide has been revised and published weightings should come from the school rather than from any website.

Each component fails in its own way, which is why a single revision strategy underperforms. The multiple-choice section punishes misreading and rewards elimination technique, and students who have never practised it under time pressure lose marks they could not lose on content grounds. The data-based section rewards careful reading of axes, units and uncertainties, and students treat it as a reading exercise rather than a chemistry one. Paper 2 extended responses reward command-term discipline: an explain answer that describes, or a deduce answer with no reasoning shown, loses marks regardless of how correct the chemistry underneath is.

The investigation is different in kind. It is marked against four criteria — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — worth six marks each for twenty-four in total, within a 3,000-word limit. Nothing about it is time-pressured, which means every mark lost in it was lost to planning rather than to performance. That makes it the most controllable 20 per cent in the subject and the part most worth spending tutoring money on early.

A practical note for parents: ask to see which component your child's marked mocks actually dropped marks in, as a proportion rather than in total. Families frequently buy content teaching when the scripts show a multiple-choice or data-based technique problem, which is a different and much shorter piece of work.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme traps that recur every session
paragraphs: This is the most useful section on the page for a student already working hard. These traps cost marks in every examination series, they are the same traps every year, and they have nothing to do with how well a student understands chemistry. A tutor who works from mark schemes will name them in the first session; a tutor who works from a textbook will not see them at all.

The first is naming a general force where the scheme wants a specific interaction. Hydrogen bonding, London dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions — these are the credited terms. Strong intermolecular forces earns nothing, and students write it constantly because it feels like the right register. The second is a periodicity or trend answer that gives the trend without the reason and the comparison. The scheme usually wants three things and students supply one.

The third is sign convention in energetics. Bond enthalpies, Hess cycles and free energy relationships all turn on signs, and a dropped negative produces a numerically wrong answer that the scheme cannot credit even where the method was sound. The fourth is equilibrium language: the scheme wants the direction of shift and the reason tied to the change imposed, and students write that the equilibrium adjusts. The fifth is calculation presentation — missing units, wrong significant figures, or a final answer with no working, which forfeits the method marks that would otherwise have survived an arithmetic slip.

The sixth is mechanism drawing. Curly arrow marks are awarded for arrows beginning at the correct electron source — a lone pair, a pi bond, a bond being broken — and ending at the correct destination. A mechanism that is conceptually right and drawn loosely scores badly. All six are habits, all six are teachable in weeks rather than terms, and together they typically account for more lost marks than any content gap.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: pattern rather than memorisation
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where most Deira Chemistry students decide the subject is impossible, and the reason is almost always that they are memorising rather than learning the pattern. Learned as a list of named reactions, organic chemistry is an unbounded memory task and the first unfamiliar molecule defeats it. Learned as functional-group behaviour under given conditions, it is a small number of rules applied repeatedly.

The structure to teach is this. Each functional group has a characteristic reactivity: it is electron-rich or electron-poor, it has a site that attracts attack or a site that donates. Reagents and conditions determine which of its available reactions occurs. Pathways are then derivable rather than remembered, because the student asks what this group does to that group rather than recalling a diagram. At Higher Level, where mechanism work expands considerably, the same framing carries: a mechanism is a sequence of electron movements, each with a reason.

Mechanism marks follow from the drawing, which is why a chemistry session needs a working surface where both people can draw. Curly arrows are awarded for starting at the correct electron source and finishing at the correct destination, with intermediates shown where the scheme requires them. A student who knows what happens but draws the arrow from the wrong atom gets no credit, and that is a correctable drawing habit rather than a conceptual failure.

The practical sequence we would use with a student stuck in organic chemistry: two sessions establishing functional-group behaviour as a framework, two sessions deriving rather than recalling pathways, and two sessions drilling mechanism drawing against mark schemes. Six sessions, and the subject usually stops feeling like memory work.

sections.heading: Calculations: where the chemistry is right and the marks are not
paragraphs: Calculation questions in IB Chemistry are unusual in that most lost marks are not chemistry errors. A student who can set up a titration calculation correctly and then presents it without units, to the wrong number of significant figures, or with no working shown, loses marks that no amount of further content teaching will recover. This is the single easiest category of marks to get back.

The recurring cases are predictable. Titration and limiting-reagent problems, where the moles are computed correctly and the final answer is not rounded as the data allows. Percentage yield and atom economy, where the formula is misremembered under pressure. Enthalpy from bond enthalpies and from Hess cycles, where sign errors dominate. Equilibrium constant calculations, where students substitute initial rather than equilibrium concentrations. And pH and acid-base work, where the logarithmic relationship is applied in the wrong direction.

The method that fixes all of them is mechanical and slightly tedious: a fixed layout used every time. State the relationship, substitute with units carried through, compute, then round to the significant figures the least precise datum allows, and state the unit. Students resist this because it feels slower; it is slower for the first fortnight and then faster, because the layout prevents the error rather than catching it afterwards.

Worth noting for parents comparing tutors: ask a candidate what significant-figure rule they apply to a calculated answer and why. A specialist answers immediately, in terms of the precision of the supplied data. A generalist says to use three, which is a guess that happens to be right often enough to hide the fact that it is a guess.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in a single piece of work of up to 3,000 words, assessed against four criteria worth six marks each. Unlike the papers, nothing about it is time-pressured, which means every mark lost in it was lost to planning. That is why it belongs at the front of a tutoring plan rather than the back.

Research design, the first criterion, rewards a focused research question with identified and justified variables and a method capable of generating sufficient relevant data. The commonest failure is a question too broad to be answered with the apparatus available in a school laboratory, chosen because it sounded interesting. Data analysis rewards appropriate processing with uncertainties carried through and presented clearly; students process correctly and then omit uncertainty treatment entirely.

Conclusion rewards an interpretation justified by the data and compared against the accepted scientific context, which means a student has to find and cite a literature value rather than simply state what their graph showed. Evaluation is the criterion most consistently underscored across cohorts, because students list generic weaknesses — human error, more trials would help — instead of naming a specific limitation, explaining its effect on their particular data, and proposing a realistic improvement.

A workable timeline, allowing for the school's own internal deadline being earlier than families expect: topic candidates in DP1 term two, research question tested for feasibility by the end of DP1, data collected and processed over the following months, a complete draft early in DP2 term one, then revision after supervisor feedback. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline in writing at the start of DP1.

sections.heading: Using past papers properly
paragraphs: Most Chemistry students use past papers badly, in a specific and fixable way: they attempt questions, check the answers, feel reassured or discouraged, and move on. Nothing in that sequence tells them why a mark was lost, which is the only information that changes anything.

The method that works has three steps. First, attempt the question under time, without notes, and write the answer out in full even when it feels obvious, because the written form is what is marked. Second, mark it against the official mark scheme rather than against the answer, awarding marks point by point and noting which specific credited phrase was absent. Third, classify the loss: content not known, command term ignored, presentation fault, or question misread. Those four need different responses, and a student who does not classify ends up re-reading the textbook regardless of which one applies.

The classification is what a tutor adds most efficiently. A student cannot see a missing method step in their own work, because the omission is invisible to the person who made it. An hour spent on a marked script with somebody reading it in mark-scheme language usually produces one named behaviour to change, and changing one behaviour reliably recovers more marks than another pass through a theme.

On sourcing: reference the official specimen and past materials through the school and the board's own channels rather than collecting unofficial copies. Reproducing or distributing board material is a copyright matter, and the school already has legitimate access to what a student needs.

sections.heading: What chemistry support costs, and which component it should target
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates, read in October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, online and generally generalist. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table in the same range. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the named or examiner-level end. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500.

The useful question is not which band but which component the money should target, because chemistry fails in component-specific ways. A budget-band hour cannot teach command-term discipline or mark-scheme precision, because the person delivering it has not marked against a scheme. A qualified-band hour teaches theme content well and is the right place for most Standard Level work. A specialist-band hour is what diagnosis, investigation feasibility and Higher Level additional content actually require, and a family should buy fewer of those rather than cheaper ones.

Two chemistry-specific notes on value. The investigation is 20 per cent of the grade and its deadline is known a year ahead, so four specialist sessions aimed at it early is the highest-return purchase in the subject. And the in-home premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour buys proximity in a subject where a shared digital whiteboard is a better surface for mechanism drawing than paper, since both people can draw and the board is saved between sessions. Advertised monthly packages show roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures, not IB Gram's prices. We quote after a free trial lesson, before any payment, against a written plan with a total on it, because an investigation block and a year of Higher Level theme work are different purchases.

sections.heading: What an online chemistry tutor can and cannot do
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. In chemistry that limitation deserves a straight answer rather than a slogan, so here is the honest division of labour.

What online one-to-one teaching does well, and in some respects better than paper: mechanism drawing on a shared whiteboard where both people draw and the board is saved between sessions; data analysis with the student's own spreadsheet and graphs on screen; marking a written answer line by line against a scheme with the annotations retained; and working through a calculation while watching the student's layout appear, which is the moment the error becomes visible. For a subject whose marks turn on written precision, that is the right working surface.

What it cannot do is handle apparatus. Practical skills are developed in the school laboratory as part of the required practical scheme of work, including the collaborative sciences project, and no tutoring arrangement replaces that. What a tutor can do around it is make the practical work count for marks: interpreting results the student generated, teaching uncertainty treatment, and turning a laboratory session into an investigation write-up that satisfies the four criteria.

There is also the Deira-specific point. Students here travel across the Creek to school and arrive home late and variably, and in dense apartment housing the quiet hour moves from day to day. A session set from dismissal time fails; one set from arrival, or moved to a weekend morning when the flat is quieter, holds. Where a tutor in the room is genuinely needed for other reasons, the Dubai market supplies it at the rates above and a family should use it.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary on the investigation
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is among the most commonly outsourced pieces of Diploma coursework, and at least one operation competing for searches like this sells completed internal assessments. The asymmetry is stark: the fee is paid once, the malpractice finding attaches to the student, and the possible consequence is the loss of the Diploma. The seller carries nothing at all.

Legitimate paid help is substantial and clearly bounded. A tutor may challenge whether a research question is answerable with school apparatus and sufficient to generate usable quantitative data. They may teach the chemistry the investigation rests on. They may read the four criteria with the student so they know what evaluation actually means in marking terms. They may mark a complete draft against those criteria and explain what a supervisor's comment requires. They may insist on a timeline that fits the school's internal deadline.

A tutor may not write or draft any part of it, produce the data analysis for the student to insert, supply data the student did not collect, invent an uncertainty treatment, or edit the text until the prose is theirs rather than the student's. The working test is whether the student can explain, unprompted, why each decision and each sentence is in the document. If they cannot, it should not be there.

This is better teaching as well as safer. A student who has been made to defend their own research question and write their own evaluation has learned something that transfers to the Extended Essay and to university laboratory work. A student handed a finished investigation has learned nothing and carries a risk on their record until somebody notices.

process.title: Say the level and send a marked script
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, the year of study, and the most recent marked paper or investigation draft. The script is the brief: it usually shows within a page whether the problem is content, command terms, presentation or data-based technique.

process.title: Ask us about the themes
process.description: During the trial, ask the tutor to name the six syllabus themes and say what the mark scheme wants in a bonding question. A specialist does both without hesitation. It is the fastest way to establish that they have taught the course as it currently stands.

process.title: Free trial lesson before payment
process.description: One free trial lesson before any payment, with the marked work open and the investigation question to hand if there is one. Ask the tutor what significant-figure rule they apply to a calculated answer and why; the answer is diagnostic.

process.title: One target per block
process.description: The plan names one target — a theme, a trap, a component, or the investigation — the school assessment it is aimed at, and the evidence that will show it worked. If the investigation is still open, that is almost always where we would start.

process.title: Reviewed on marked writing
process.description: The review point is a written answer or a timed section marked against the scheme, not a session count. We say whether the target behaviour changed, and if it did not, whether we think the problem was the method, the pace or the match.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus named, not gestured at
whyPoints.description: Three Structure themes and three Reactivity themes, with the sub-topics set out. A parent can use that list to establish whether a prospective tutor has taught the current course, which no amount of profile reading will tell them.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes, not textbooks
whyPoints.description: Most lost marks in this subject are written-precision failures rather than content gaps: a vague force, a missing reason, a dropped sign, a mechanism arrow from the wrong atom. We publish the six recurring traps and work from scripts rather than chapters.

whyPoints.title: The investigation treated as 20 per cent
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade sits in a piece of work with no time pressure and a deadline known a year ahead, which makes every mark lost in it a planning failure. Four early specialist sessions aimed at it is the highest-return purchase in the subject.

whyPoints.title: Honest about practicals
whyPoints.description: We cannot handle apparatus for your child, and we say so. Laboratory work belongs to the school's required practical scheme. What we add is turning the data a student generated into a write-up that satisfies the four criteria.

whyPoints.title: Level-matched, not subject-matched
whyPoints.description: Higher Level content is woven through all six themes rather than appended, so a Standard Level tutor is a poor match for Higher Level work. We match on the level and will give you a date rather than substitute when a Higher Level specialist is not free.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources and a target
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names its publisher and is dated October 2026, and the spend table says which component each band should be aimed at. Buying the wrong band for the job is the commonest waste in this subject, in both directions.

faqs.question: What are the six themes in IB Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The course is organised under two concepts. Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, including the nuclear atom, electron configurations, the mole and ideal gases. Structure 2 covers the ionic, covalent and metallic bonding models and how they translate into materials. Structure 3 covers classification: the periodic table and functional groups. Reactivity 1 asks what drives reactions, through enthalpy, energy cycles, fuels and entropy. Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far. Reactivity 3 covers mechanisms: proton transfer, electron transfer and electron sharing.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand chemistry but still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme rewards written precision rather than understanding. Six traps account for most of it: writing strong intermolecular forces instead of naming hydrogen bonding or London dispersion forces; giving a trend without the reason and comparison; dropping a sign in an energetics calculation; writing that an equilibrium adjusts instead of naming the direction and the cause; omitting units or working from a calculation; and drawing mechanism arrows from the wrong atom. All six are habits, and all six are fixable in weeks.

faqs.question: How much is the chemistry internal assessment worth?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the final grade, marked against four criteria — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — worth six marks each for twenty-four in total, within a 3,000-word limit. Confirm the weighting for your child's cohort with their teacher. Unlike the papers nothing about it is time-pressured, so every mark lost in it was lost to planning. That makes it the most controllable fifth of the grade in the subject.

faqs.question: Which investigation criterion do students score worst on?
faqs.answer: Evaluation, consistently. It rewards naming a specific limitation, explaining its effect on that student's particular data, and proposing a realistic improvement. Students instead list generic weaknesses — human error, more trials would help — which earns very little. The second weakest is usually conclusion, where the criterion requires comparison against the accepted scientific context, meaning a literature value has to be found and cited rather than simply stating what the graph showed.

faqs.question: My child finds organic chemistry impossible. Is it fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and quickly, because the problem is nearly always method rather than ability. Students memorise named reactions, which is an unbounded memory task that collapses at the first unfamiliar molecule. Taught as functional-group behaviour — each group is electron-rich or electron-poor, and reagents and conditions select which reaction happens — pathways become derivable rather than recalled. Two sessions on the framework, two deriving pathways and two drilling mechanism arrows usually changes how the whole topic feels.

faqs.question: What exactly earns a mark in a mechanism question?
faqs.answer: Curly arrows that start at the correct electron source and end at the correct destination, with intermediates shown where the scheme requires them. The source is a lone pair, a pi bond or a bond being broken, and an arrow drawn loosely between two molecules earns nothing even where the student knows what is happening. This is why a chemistry session needs a surface both people can draw on, and it is a correctable drawing habit rather than a conceptual failure.

faqs.question: How should my child use past papers for chemistry?
faqs.answer: Three steps. Attempt the question under time and write the answer out in full, because the written form is what is marked. Mark it against the official mark scheme point by point, noting which credited phrase was absent, rather than checking the final answer. Then classify the loss as content, command term, presentation or misreading, because those four need different responses. Students who skip the classification re-read the textbook whichever applies. Get papers and schemes through the school's own legitimate access.

faqs.question: Can online chemistry tutoring work without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: For everything except handling apparatus, yes, and for some things better than paper. Mechanism drawing on a shared whiteboard where both people draw and the board is saved between sessions, data analysis with the student's own graphs on screen, and marking written answers line by line against a scheme all work well. Practical skills belong to the school's required practical scheme of work, including the collaborative sciences project, and no tutoring replaces that. What tutoring adds is making the data count for marks.

faqs.question: Is a Standard Level chemistry tutor suitable for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Generally not. Higher Level content is woven through all six themes rather than appended at the end, with the additional material concentrated in energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and organic chemistry. A tutor who has taught only Standard Level will not know where the Higher Level boundary sits and will over-teach some topics while missing others. Ask any candidate which level they have taught, by name, and do not accept the subject title as an answer.

faqs.question: What significant figures should a calculated chemistry answer use?
faqs.answer: As many as the least precise piece of supplied data allows, which is the rule the mark scheme applies and the answer a specialist gives immediately. A generalist tends to say three, which is right often enough to hide that it is a guess. This is worth asking any prospective tutor during a trial, because the answer indicates whether they have marked work against a scheme. Rounding faults are among the cheapest marks in the subject to recover.

faqs.question: When should the chemistry investigation question be settled?
faqs.answer: Topic candidates in DP1 term two and the research question tested for feasibility by the end of DP1, with data collection and processing over the following months and a complete draft early in DP2 term one. The school's internal deadline, not any external window, is the one that binds, and it is usually earlier than families expect, so ask the Diploma coordinator for it in writing at the start of DP1. A question too broad for school apparatus discovered late is the most expensive error available.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a Higher Level chemistry tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Up to a week or two in normal conditions and longer around mock season, because Higher Level Chemistry is one of the thinnest specialisms in the city. The IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, so science specialists who have actually taught the Higher Level course are scarce everywhere, not just in one district. Request early, and if the deadline is tight we will give you a date rather than substitute a Standard Level tutor.

faqs.question: Does my child need Chemistry HL for medicine?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry is the standard expectation for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering applications, and it is the main reason demand for it in Dubai outstrips supply. Requirements vary by institution and country, so check two or three specific target courses rather than relying on a general rule, and check whether a second Higher Level science is also expected. No tutoring is required for any admissions process, and nobody can promise a particular grade or outcome.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor come to our apartment in Deira?
faqs.answer: Not from us. All UAE lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is part of our India service. For chemistry the whiteboard genuinely suits the subject, since mechanism drawing and calculation layout need a surface both people can write on with the work preserved between sessions. In-home tutoring exists in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel for families who want it.

faqs.question: What does chemistry tutoring cost and what should it target?
faqs.answer: Published October 2026 figures: qualified subject tutors online AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, which suits Standard Level theme content and multiple-choice or data-based technique. Specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, which is what Higher Level content, diagnosis and investigation work actually require. Budget online generalists AED 33 to 65, suitable only for homework supervision. Buy fewer specialist hours aimed at the investigation rather than many cheap ones.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the investigation without risking malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may test whether a research question is answerable with school apparatus and can generate usable quantitative data, teach the chemistry it rests on, read the four criteria with the student, mark a complete draft against them, explain a supervisor comment and enforce a timeline. A tutor may not write or draft any part of it, produce the data analysis, supply data, invent an uncertainty treatment, or edit it into their own prose. The test is whether the student can explain every decision unprompted.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-deira.closingHeading: Send a marked script and the investigation question
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-deira.closingBody: Those two documents answer most of what a chemistry plan needs. The script shows whether marks are going to content, command terms, calculation presentation or data-based technique, and those are four different pieces of work. The investigation question shows whether a fifth of the grade is already secure or still at risk. Tell us the level and the year alongside them, and you will get one target and an honest statement of what the time available can achieve. The first lesson is free, before any payment. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video on a shared whiteboard, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-difc.tutorsIntro: These are chemistry teachers who work from mark schemes and from the student's own scripts rather than from a textbook chapter list. Each has taught the current Diploma chemistry course with its two written papers and single investigation, and each will tell you after one session whether paid hours are the right purchase at all.

intro.heading: What Diploma chemistry really costs a DIFC household
paragraphs: Start with a number rather than a promise. Across the Dubai market, a weekly one-hour session with a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised between AED 150 and 300 an hour, which annualises to somewhere between AED 5,400 and AED 10,800 across a thirty-six week school year. Specialist Diploma and IGCSE tutors sit higher, at AED 200 to 450 and above. One company in this market advertises AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are published figures from published rate cards, not an estimate, and they are the frame a DIFC family should be working inside before anyone discusses chemistry at all.

The reason this page leads with money is that chemistry is the subject where families most often buy the wrong thing. It has a reputation for difficulty, the reputation is partly earned, and the market responds with group revision courses, bulk hour bundles and crash intensives sold three weeks before the papers. Some of that is useful. Much of it is the equivalent of buying a gym membership in March: it addresses the anxiety rather than the deficit. A DIFC household with a long office day and a school run across the creek has limited evening hours and limited patience for a purchase that does not move a mark.

The structure of the course tells you where the money belongs. Diploma chemistry is assessed through two written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and splits into multiple-choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 is 44% and is extended response; the investigation is 20%. There is no third paper in the current course. Forty-four per cent of the grade therefore sits in one paper that rewards precision of language, correct use of command terms and reasoning laid out so a marker can follow it. Those are coachable in a one-to-one hour and essentially uncoachable in a group of eight.

There is a second cost nobody itemises, which is travel. Published Dubai rates for in-home one-to-one work run AED 180 to 350 at Bestimate's 2026 rate table and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutors. The spread between those bands is mostly a car crossing Dubai for an hour's lesson. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For a DIFC family the online route costs less and buys a wider shortlist, which is the argument made in full further down rather than asserted here.

What follows is the detail: the two-year bill counted in months rather than hours, the four places chemistry money is routinely wasted in this district, what the six themes actually contain and which of them need paid time, the free provision a Dubai school already gives you, the cost of the course in context against school fees and exam entry, where the honesty line sits on the investigation, and the limits on what we will claim.
