dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-difc.programmesIntro: Chemistry support gets bought at four different points, and the price of a useful intervention rises sharply the later it is bought. These are the four stages, with what each one costs in hours rather than in confidence.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme chemistry
programmes.description: Two years across six themes, assessed by two written papers and one scientific investigation. Higher Level adds depth within the same themes and longer papers, with identical component weightings to Standard Level. Students take chemistry alongside five other subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a service commitment, which is the real reason weekly hours are scarce rather than unaffordable.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest point to buy Diploma chemistry support in DIFC is the first half of Year 12, and almost nobody does. A family that starts in October pays for maintenance; a family that starts in February of Year 13 pays for triage, needs more hours per week, and has fewer weeks to spread them over. The published hourly band does not change, but the number of hours required roughly doubles, which is where the real cost difference sits.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated or separate sciences depending on the campus, assessed against four criteria each marked out of eight and reported as a level from one to seven. The criterion that predicts later chemistry difficulty is processing and evaluating, because it tests data handling rather than recall, and data handling is what the data-based half of Diploma Paper 1 will later demand.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years Programme support is the cheapest chemistry money a DIFC family can spend, because a criterion gap identified in MYP 4 costs a handful of sessions and the same gap discovered in Year 12 costs a term. Two of the campuses closest to DIFC run this route, and parents arriving from a percentage-marked system often cannot read the reports well enough to spot the gap at all.

programmes.name: Year 11 chemistry before the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge chemistry 0620 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE chemistry 4CH1, taken separately or within a combined award. Extended or Higher tier content is what the Diploma assumes: mole calculations, bonding, energetics and the basics of organic nomenclature all reappear in Year 12 at pace and are not retaught from scratch.
programmes.countryNote: The best-value chemistry purchase available in this district is six weeks of mole arithmetic and bonding revision in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, bought before anything has gone wrong. It costs a fraction of a rescue block in Year 13 and it removes the single most common cause of early Diploma chemistry failure, which is arithmetic rather than chemistry.

programmes.name: The scientific investigation and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The chemistry investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria and carries 20% of the grade. An Extended Essay in chemistry runs to 4,000 words with a school supervisor. Both are the student's own work. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the research design and challenge a conclusion; nothing may be written, edited or supplied.
programmes.countryNote: This is where families in every Dubai district get overcharged, and sometimes worse. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; one has been documented selling them at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach and an expulsion risk for the student, and it is the most expensive thing a parent can buy in this market because the downside is the diploma itself.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-difc.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is rarely bought alone. These are the courses that most often share the same budget and the same evening in a DIFC household, with what each one actually charges a student in time.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six themes across structure and reactivity, two written papers and one investigation. The expensive parts to fix late are organic mechanisms and the quantitative chain that runs from moles through concentration to titration arithmetic, because both need practice volume rather than explanation. Paper 2 language costs the most marks and the fewest hours to repair.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual partner subject for medicine applicants, marked against the same investigation criteria and the same command terms. A student who learns to answer 'explain' and 'outline' properly for chemistry gains biology marks without extra hours, which is a genuine saving when both subjects are in play.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Taken with chemistry by most engineering applicants. Shares the data-based question style and the uncertainty arithmetic, so one block of teaching on uncertainties serves both courses. Where a family must choose which science to fund, the deciding question is usually which paper the student is actually losing marks on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The quantitative spine under Higher Level chemistry. Logarithms arrive with pH, proportional reasoning underpins every mole calculation, and rearranging an expression quickly is assumed. Chemistry errors that look conceptual are frequently arithmetic, which is why a tutor who can diagnose across both subjects saves billable hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Compatible with both chemistry levels, and the more common choice among students taking chemistry with economics or business rather than with physics. Leaves symbolic manipulation thinner than the chemistry papers assume, so a term of algebraic fluency work is often the cheaper intervention than more chemistry content.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Offered at a minority of Dubai campuses and sometimes taken instead of a second science. It uses the same investigation criteria, so the criterion teaching transfers. Families considering it as a lighter alternative to chemistry should check the published entry requirements of the universities on their list first.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in chemistry
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word piece supervised at school. The cost-efficient intervention is one or two hours spent narrowing the research question before any laboratory work begins. The student writes every word, collects every measurement and reaches every conclusion; a tutor asks questions and teaches the assessment criteria.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum is licensed, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. They occupy timetable slots and occasionally clash with science options, and families funding extra chemistry hours should know these lessons are competing for the same week.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects, carrying points alongside the Extended Essay. Science students often underestimate it and then buy emergency support for it in Year 13, which is a predictable and avoidable line in the budget.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-difc.regionsTitle: Where DIFC chemistry students study, and what each area implies for the bill
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-difc.regionsIntro: School choice changes the cost of chemistry support more than most parents expect, because it changes how much the school itself provides and how much of the evening survives the drive home. These are the areas DIFC families commute into.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Two large campuses, ten to eighteen minutes from the Gate Village. Short commute, so a straight-after-school session is possible and a family can buy one weekly hour rather than paying for a weekend block to compensate for lost weekday time.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: A continuum campus running from early years into the Diploma. Families stay for years, which makes early-stage support the cheapest option available to them, and the later finish time pushes chemistry sessions towards 17:30 or a second slot at 20:00.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: No large secondary campus inside either district, so almost every household commutes. These are the areas where evening online slots fill first, and where a family that leaves booking until October finds the cheap early-evening hours already taken.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: Three campuses within a quarter of an hour on a good run, through a slow industrial grid. Several run strong internal revision provision, which means a parent should ask what the school already supplies before buying hours for the same content.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Twenty to thirty-five minutes back at pick-up time. Families here usually settle on 18:00 sessions, and that later slot is where a shorter, sharper hour matters, because an exhausted student at 18:00 absorbs less per dirham than an alert one at 17:00.

regions.name: Al Safa and Jumeirah
regions.note: The older British-curriculum belt, with several selective schools and well-developed internal support. Students from this cluster more often need pace and past-paper discipline than foundational repair, which is a cheaper purchase in hours.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and the coast
regions.note: Twenty-five to forty minutes each way. The journey is the outer limit most DIFC families accept, and it rules out weekday early-evening work for many of them, pushing chemistry support into weekend mornings where ninety-minute sessions are possible.

schoolClusters.note: These campuses are the ones DIFC families most often use, and all run either the Middle Years Programme or a Year 11 qualification into a Diploma or A Level sixth form. Internal chemistry provision varies widely between them, which is the first thing to establish before buying any hours.

modes.description: One session a week following the school's own scheme of work, so the hour repairs this week's content rather than last term's. This is the lowest total cost per grade of anything in this list, because it prevents the gaps that later need rescuing. It is also the hardest sell, because nothing has visibly gone wrong yet.

modes.description: Four to eight weeks of paired sessions, one on content and one purely on timed papers marked against the published mark scheme. Losses get categorised as recall, arithmetic, command term or layout, and the category that dominates decides the next session. This is the highest return per hour in the whole course because Paper 2 carries 44% of the grade.

modes.description: A short, front-loaded block around the research question and the design, before data exists. The criteria are taught explicitly, the question is interrogated hard, and the uncertainty and graphing arithmetic is drilled. The student designs, measures, analyses and writes. A tutor who offers anything beyond this is selling something that puts the diploma at risk.

modes.description: Winter and spring break blocks, or Saturday mornings, used to rebuild a theme properly rather than to patch it. sections.heading: The two-year chemistry bill, counted in months
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a decision that lasts two years. A family deciding whether to fund Diploma chemistry needs the monthly figure and the total, because that is how household budgets work. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget provision at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-market at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Set against the hourly bands published elsewhere in this market, those monthly figures are internally consistent and they are the honest frame for the conversation.

The table below converts those published bands into the shapes a DIFC family actually buys. It is not a price list and none of these are IB Gram's rates; they are the market, expressed as monthly and two-year ranges so that a parent can see the size of the commitment before anyone talks about chemistry. What the table shows is that the expensive plans are not the ones with the highest hourly rate. They are the ones that start late and therefore need two or three sessions a week compressed into a single term.

The practical reading is this. A weekly specialist session run from October of Year 12 through to the May session of Year 13 costs more in total than a six-week crash block and far less per grade moved, because it is spent on prevention rather than on rescue. The crash block has a place, and the last section of this page says what it can and cannot do, but a family that budgets for one and ends up needing the other will have spent more than if it had simply bought the weekly hour from the start.

sections.heading: Where chemistry money gets wasted in this district
paragraphs: The first waste is the group class. A chemistry revision course with eight students in it can deliver content, and for a student who simply has not been taught a theme that is sometimes enough. What it cannot deliver is the thing that moves a Paper 2 mark, which is somebody reading one student's own written answers and naming the specific habit costing them marks. Those habits are individual. One student loses marks on state symbols and significant figures, another on using 'because' where the mark scheme wants a mechanism. A group rate looks like a saving until you notice it has bought the half of the problem that was never the problem.

The second is the generalist. A science tutor who covers chemistry, biology and physics across four curricula will teach the content competently and will not know, without looking it up, that organic mechanism marks hinge on arrow placement or that the data-based section expects uncertainties propagated rather than quoted. The specialist costs more per hour in this market and fewer hours in total. The arithmetic favours the specialist in almost every case where the student is above a grade 3 and trying to reach a 6 or 7.

The third is timing. Hours bought in Year 13 cost the same as hours bought in Year 12 and do perhaps half as much, because the foundational repair that was possible in October is no longer possible in March and the work becomes triage. The fourth is buying support for content the school is about to reteach anyway: most Dubai schools run their own revision programmes, clinic hours and past-paper sessions, and a parent who has not asked what is already provided free is at risk of paying twice. Establish that first. It is one email to the head of science and it routinely removes a third of the intended spend.

sections.heading: What the six themes contain, and which of them need paid hours
paragraphs: The current Diploma chemistry course is organised around structure and reactivity: models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, classification of matter, what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Schools teach them in different sequences, which is why any plan has to start from the school's own topic list rather than from the published order. What generalises is which themes reward paid one-to-one time and which a diligent student can close alone with the textbook and the school's resources.

Classification of matter and much of the bonding content is largely learnable alone. It is descriptive, well covered by school resources and tested in ways that reward organised notes. The quantitative chain is not. Moles into concentration into titration arithmetic into yield and error analysis is a sequence where one weak link breaks every question downstream, and a student cannot usually find their own weak link. Half an hour with a tutor watching the working locates it; a week with a revision guide does not. Energetics and equilibrium sit in the middle, and the mechanisms theme is where the money goes.

The table below sorts the themes on exactly that basis. It is a spending guide, not a difficulty ranking: a theme can be hard and still be bad value to buy, because the difficulty is in volume of practice rather than in explanation. The column that matters most is the last one, which names what a paid hour does in each theme that a free hour cannot. Where that column is thin, do not buy the hour.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, and why it is the most expensive thing to fix late
paragraphs: Organic chemistry behaves differently from the rest of the course in a way that has direct financial consequences. Most chemistry topics can be explained once and then practised. Organic chemistry has to be practised into the hand. A student who understands nucleophilic substitution perfectly well can still lose every mechanism mark on a paper because the curly arrow starts at the wrong place, the lone pair is not shown, the charge is missing from the intermediate, or the conditions above the arrow are absent. None of that is a comprehension failure and none of it is repaired by another explanation.

What repairs it is volume, spaced over weeks, with somebody correcting the drawing each time. That is a slow purchase. Fifteen mechanisms drawn badly and corrected is worth more than three hours of lecture, and it cannot be compressed into the fortnight before the papers, which is exactly when most families in this district come looking for it. A parent who starts organic support in April is buying a worse version of a cheaper thing they could have bought in January, and the tutor who tells them so is being honest rather than unhelpful.

The synthesis question compounds the problem. Higher Level papers ask students to get from one compound to another in several steps, which requires the pathway map to be in recall rather than in notes. Building that map takes repeated retrieval over a term. There is a cheaper route, and it is worth stating because it costs nothing: twenty minutes of mechanism drawing three times a week, self-marked against the school's own materials, through the whole of Year 13. Families who do that need far fewer paid hours. Families who do not will buy them in March at the point where they do the least good.

sections.heading: The free hour your school already provides
paragraphs: Before any money changes hands, establish what the school supplies. Dubai private schools are fee-paying, well resourced and inspected annually, and most run some combination of subject clinics, lunchtime help, after-school revision, past-paper libraries and departmental intervention lists. Parents in this district frequently do not know what exists because it is communicated once, in September, in a newsletter nobody finished. One email to the head of science asking what chemistry support is available and whether their child is on any intervention list changes the budget more than any discount negotiation will.

The free provision has real limits, though, and it is worth knowing where they are. A school clinic is a group setting and a teacher's time is divided; a subject teacher marking thirty scripts cannot write the individual diagnosis a tutor writes after one session; and no school will mark unlimited past papers for one student. The free hour is excellent for content that was missed and poor for habits that need naming. The paid hour is the reverse. A family that buys in that order spends less and gets more.

The table below sets out the comparison honestly, including the cases where the answer is not to buy anything. There is no version of this page in which the recommendation is always to purchase tuition. A student who is on grade 6 and losing marks to carelessness in timed conditions needs a timer and a mark scheme, not a tutor. A student who has never been taught enthalpy cycles because of a staff absence in Year 12 needs teaching, and no amount of self-discipline substitutes for it.

sections.heading: Chemistry tutoring in context: fees, exam entry and the Dubai budget
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means nothing without the rest of the education budget around it. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with British-curriculum provision at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and International Baccalaureate programmes at 7%. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees, in other words, held still. Tutoring is the discretionary line that did not.

That makes the comparison worth putting in front of a parent plainly. A weekly specialist chemistry session across an exam year, at the published market band, is a recognisable fraction of a single term's school fees at a mid-market Dubai campus. Expressed that way, the decision usually stops being about affordability and becomes about whether the particular purchase will work, which is the right question. The table below assembles the items that make up the real cost of a Diploma chemistry year so that nothing arrives as a surprise in February.

Two items on it catch families out. The first is the private-candidate examination entry fee, which only applies if a student is sitting outside their school's registration, and which is set by the board and the centre rather than by any tutor. The second is the cost of the investigation itself in time: the weeks it occupies are weeks not available for revision, and a family planning an intensive block should check the investigation deadline before booking it. Both are planning facts rather than charges, and both are cheaper to know in September than to discover in January.

sections.heading: The honesty line on the investigation, and the most expensive purchase in this market
paragraphs: A fifth of the chemistry grade comes from one scientific investigation, marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. The commercial consequence of that 20% is that a market has grown up around it, and parts of that market sell work rather than teaching. One provider in this cluster has been documented offering completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is not expensive tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers IB malpractice procedures, and the person who carries the consequence is the student.

The line we hold, and that any provider should be asked to state in writing, is this. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, question whether a proposed research question can be answered with the data it would generate, explain uncertainty propagation and graph choice, and ask whether a conclusion is supported by the numbers. A tutor may not write, edit, restructure or supply any part of the document, may not select the research question, and may not produce the analysis. The student writes every word and owns every judgement. Dubai schools run originality checks and supervisors sign declarations, so the alternative is not a risk in the abstract.

Framed as a purchase, the legitimate version is also the better value one. Three to five sessions spent on criterion A before any apparatus is booked prevents the failure mode that costs the most marks, which is a question too broad to answer. Ten sessions spent rescuing an investigation after the data has been collected cannot fix it, because the design is what is being assessed. Front-load the spend, keep the work the student's, and the 20% behaves like the most predictable part of the grade rather than the most frightening.

sections.heading: Online delivery from DIFC, the permit, and the claims we decline to make
paragraphs: Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to a DIFC address: IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring exists only in the India side of the business. The cost argument for that was made at the top of this page and is worth restating in one line. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutors, and the gap is a vehicle rather than a better lesson. A DIFC family buying online pays less and chooses from everybody who has taught the current chemistry course instead of from the few who can reach the Gate Village by five o'clock.

On regulation, the position worth knowing is factual and most of this market avoids stating it. Private tuition in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is issued free of charge for two years through MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, available on the ministry's app, website and e-services system, and eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so none is quoted here. Ask to see the permit, whoever you buy from.

Finally, the things this page will not say in order to close a sale. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation, Cambridge or Pearson; a KHDA educational services permit belongs to training institutes with premises and we hold none. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. No grade, point total or university place can be guaranteed by any tutor, because boards mark the papers and set the boundaries afterwards. On VAT, we will state whether a quoted IB Gram price includes it and will not characterise the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees generally; that question belongs to the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance. Every AED figure above belongs to the company or rate table that published it.

process.title: A diagnostic lesson at no charge
process.description: Fifty-five minutes, no card details. The tutor works through recent class material and one unfamiliar past-paper question while watching the working rather than the answers, then writes a short note classifying the problem as arithmetic, content, technique or discipline. The note sometimes says that paid hours are not the right purchase.

process.description: Every session ends with two or three named priorities and the exact past-paper questions to attempt before the next one. Parents get that note rather than a progress score. It says what was fixed, what is still wrong, and what the student is expected to manage unaided this week.

process.title: Review the spend at the mock
process.description: January and March mocks are the point at which the budget gets re-examined honestly. The marked paper is categorised by loss type, and the plan either continues, changes shape, or stops. A tutor recommending more hours every single time is not reading the data; a plan that winds down because it worked is the intended outcome.

faqs.question: What does a full year of Diploma chemistry support cost a DIFC family in total?
faqs.answer: Using published Dubai figures rather than estimates: Bestimate's monthly bands for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Across a thirty-six week school year that is roughly AED 5,400 to AED 10,800 at the mid band and more where a second weekly session is added in Year 13. One company advertises AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published prices. IB Gram quotes its own rate per session in writing before anything is booked, and the first lesson carries no charge.

faqs.question: Is a group chemistry class in Dubai genuinely cheaper than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Per grade, usually not, and the reason is specific. A group can deliver content a student has not been taught, which is sometimes exactly the need. It cannot deliver the thing that moves a Paper 2 mark, which is somebody reading one student's own written answers and naming the habit costing them marks week after week. Those habits differ between students: state symbols for one, command-term discipline for another. Buying a group rate for technique work means paying for the half of the problem that was never the problem. Use groups for content gaps and one-to-one for the 44% paper.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics are worth paying for and which will the school cover anyway?
faqs.answer: Bonding, structure and much of the periodicity and nomenclature content is learnable from school resources by an organised student, so paid hours there are poor value. The quantitative chain is the opposite: moles into concentration into titration arithmetic into yield, where one broken link ruins every question downstream and a student cannot locate their own weak point. Energetics and equilibrium sit in between. Organic mechanisms need volume with correction, which is the clearest case for paid time. Ask the school what revision provision already exists before buying anything, because most Dubai campuses run more than parents realise.

faqs.question: Why is organic chemistry the most expensive part of the course to fix late?
faqs.answer: Because it has to be practised into the hand rather than understood once. A student who follows nucleophilic substitution perfectly can still lose every mechanism mark to an arrow starting in the wrong place, a missing lone pair, an absent charge on the intermediate or no conditions above the arrow. Another explanation fixes none of that. Fifteen mechanisms drawn and corrected over several weeks does. That cannot be compressed into the fortnight before the papers, which is when most families come looking. Twenty minutes of self-marked drawing three times a week through Year 13 replaces a surprising number of paid hours.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level chemistry cost more per hour than Standard Level in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published market bands do not usually separate the two, and the hourly figures quoted across this market apply to Diploma chemistry generally: roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 or more for a specialist. What differs is the number of hours. Higher Level covers the same six themes with additional depth and longer papers, and the algebraic load is heavier, so a Higher Level plan typically needs more weeks or a second weekly session in the exam year. Budget for hours rather than for a premium rate.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions should we book before deciding whether it is working?
faqs.answer: Four, after the free diagnostic. One session shows whether the tutor and the student can work together; it cannot show whether the plan moves marks. Four gives the tutor time to see the student's own written answers more than once, categorise the losses, and demonstrate a change in one of those categories. If after four sessions the written notes are still describing the same error, change something: the tutor, the shape of the session, or the assumption that tutoring is what this student needs. Do not commit to a term in advance, and be cautious of any package priced to require it.

faqs.question: Are monthly chemistry packages better value than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Only if the package matches what the student actually needs, and the discount is usually paying for the provider's cash flow rather than for your outcome. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Eight sessions a month is two a week, which is more than most Diploma students can absorb outside an exam-year push. A package that locks in a volume you will not use is more expensive than a higher per-session rate used sparingly. Check what happens to unused sessions before signing anything.

faqs.question: Does chemistry tutoring in Dubai get more expensive as the May session approaches?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than headline rates moving, and the practical effect on a family is the same. In February and March the specialist slots between 16:30 and 19:00 fill, the tutors with current Diploma chemistry experience are already committed, and what is left is either an awkward hour or a generalist. Families who book a weekly slot in September pay the ordinary rate and keep the good time; families who come looking in March pay the ordinary rate for a worse slot or a worse match. The scarce commodity in this market is not money, it is a specialist at seventeen hundred hours.

faqs.question: Does a quoted chemistry tutoring rate in the UAE include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing, because providers differ in how they quote. IB Gram states whether an IB Gram price is inclusive or exclusive when the rate is given, before anything is booked. What this page will not do is characterise the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees in general, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own published guidance rather than for a tutoring website, and several pages in this market state it as settled fact without a citation. If a quote arrives without a VAT position stated, treat the ambiguity as part of the price.

faqs.question: What does an in-home chemistry tutor in Dubai charge, and what is the extra paying for?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors working online. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear in this market. The difference is principally travel: an hour's lesson in DIFC can mean ninety minutes in a car, and that time is inside the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover chemistry and maths so we pay for fewer hours?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and where it works the saving is real. Higher Level chemistry leans on logarithms for pH, on proportional reasoning throughout the mole work and on quick algebraic rearrangement, and a tutor who can see that a chemistry error is actually a logarithm error fixes it in minutes rather than reteaching the chemistry. The limit is depth: a tutor strong enough in both to teach Higher Level Analysis and Approaches properly is rarer than one strong in either. Test it in the diagnostic lesson by giving the tutor a chemistry question whose difficulty is arithmetic and seeing whether they notice.

faqs.question: Is it allowed to pay for help with the chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teaching is allowed; producing the work is not. A tutor may explain what each of the four criteria rewards, interrogate a research question the student has proposed, teach uncertainty propagation and graph choice, and ask whether a conclusion follows from the data. A tutor may not write, edit, restructure or supply any part of the document, choose the research question or produce the analysis. One provider in this market has been documented selling completed internal assessments at AED 3,750; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student. Schools in Dubai run originality checks and supervisors sign declarations.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if we stop after two chemistry sessions?
faqs.answer: Nothing should be owed beyond the sessions taken, and that is the test to apply to any provider in this market. IB Gram quotes per session, the diagnostic lesson carries no charge and takes no card details, and there is no bundle that has to be bought in advance to reach the quoted rate. What you should expect from a provider when you stop is a short written note on where the student actually stands, so that the two sessions leave something behind. Be wary of discounts conditional on a term's commitment and of packages whose unused sessions expire silently.

faqs.question: How does a year of chemistry tutoring compare with Dubai school fees?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Against a mid-market Dubai campus fee, a weekly specialist chemistry session across an exam year at published market bands of AED 600 to 1,200 a month is a recognisable fraction of a single term. Framed that way the question usually stops being affordability and becomes whether this particular purchase will work, which is the better question and the one the diagnostic lesson exists to answer.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sequence of chemistry support that actually changes a mark?
faqs.answer: In order: email the school and use the free provision it already runs; set up twenty minutes of self-marked organic mechanism drawing three times a week; buy a diagnostic hour to locate where the mole and concentration chain breaks; then one weekly session focused on the student's own Paper 2 scripts marked against the published mark scheme, because that paper carries 44% of the grade. Add three to five sessions on the investigation criteria before any data is collected. That sequence costs less than a crash block in March and does considerably more, which is the whole argument of this page.

intro.heading: The comparisons a chemistry family is actually making
paragraphs: Most enquiries about chemistry tutoring arrive with several unresolved comparisons behind them. Should the student take chemistry at Higher Level or Standard. Is chemistry the right third science against physics or biology. Is the school's own support enough, or is paid help needed, and if so for what. Underneath all three sits a quieter one: whether living in an apartment community rather than a villa one changes the options available.

Those comparisons are not equally useful. Three of them have real answers that change outcomes, and one of them does not change anything at all. The level decision shapes two years of workload and some university applications. The subject choice shapes what a student can apply for. The school-against-private question decides where money goes. The neighbourhood question is a distraction, and this page says so directly rather than flattering it.

Discovery Gardens is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings laid out in themed districts beside Ibn Battuta, with its own Route 2020 metro station. Diploma students travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and chemistry sessions run at 18:00 or later. Study space is usually a shared desk rather than a room.

What makes chemistry particular is where its marks sit. The Scientific Investigation is twenty per cent of the grade, reported in up to three thousand words. Organic mechanism notation and energetics sign conventions account for a large share of the remaining gap between what a student understands and what they score. And the course is organised around structure and reactivity rather than a numbered topic list, which changes what good revision looks like.

IB Gram matches by level and delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. For chemistry that is less restrictive than it sounds, because a session is mechanisms drawn on a shared screen, a data booklet open, and marked answers annotated together.

On dates, we publish no specific IB exam or results dates anywhere on this site. UAE schools sit the May session and we write about it, but the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than none. The Diploma coordinator holds the internal calendar, including the investigation deadline, and that is the document to request in September. It also settles the most practical of the comparisons on this page, because whether the investigation is still open determines where support money should go before anything else is considered.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-discovery-ga.subjectsIntro: Chemistry comparisons are easier to make with the demands written down. These are the components and neighbouring subjects a Discovery Gardens family will weigh up.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL
subjects.description: The structure and reactivity framework at greater depth, with longer quantitative chains and extended explanations built from a named principle. The scarcest chemistry specialism in this corridor, and the level where a tutor comfortable only to Standard Level becomes visible within two sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry SL
subjects.description: The same framework with reduced depth, the same investigation at twenty per cent, and the same data booklet. Families under-buy here assuming Standard Level is light, and most Standard Level marks are lost in the investigation and the data-based paper rather than in advanced content.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: The clearest case in the subject where understanding and marks diverge. Curly arrows from the wrong atom, lone pairs omitted, charges unassigned and intermediates drawn loosely all cost marks a student believes they earned. Four to six sessions typically closes the gap.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.description: Enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy, where sign conventions cost marks silently in every calculation and in the investigation. A student confident with the chemistry and careless with signs loses marks consistently, and the fix is drilled convention work rather than more theory.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and quantitative chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas calculations. Everything quantitative routes through this, so weakness here presents as poor marks in topics the student genuinely understands. Two to four sessions of arithmetic practice usually settles it.

subjects.name: Kinetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Rate expressions, orders of reaction, equilibrium constants and Le Chatelier reasoning. Higher Level adds depth that catches students who learned the ideas qualitatively, and the reliable loss is explaining a shift without naming which quantity changes and in which direction.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH calculations, buffers, titration curves and electrochemistry. Titration curve questions reward reading the graph rather than recalling a shape, and redox rewards systematic half-equation work. Both are procedural and respond quickly to marked practice.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade on four criteria. Analysis and evaluation carry the marks most often left unclaimed: processed data with propagated uncertainty, and limitations assessed for their effect rather than listed as complaints.

subjects.name: The data booklet
subjects.description: Provided in the examination with constants, values and spectroscopic data. Students who meet it first in the exam lose minutes locating entries under pressure. Using it in every session from the start costs nothing and is a fair thing to ask a prospective tutor about.

subjects.name: Biology as the alternative third science
subjects.description: Shares the investigation structure but differs in demand: biology penalises imprecise language above all, while chemistry penalises notation and arithmetic. Students who write carefully and calculate shakily often fare better in biology, and the reverse is equally true.

subjects.name: Physics as the alternative third science
subjects.description: The most mathematically demanding of the three, with uncertainty propagation and algebraic rearrangement throughout. A student choosing between physics and chemistry at Higher Level is largely choosing between algebra under pressure and notation under pressure.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research. Chemistry essays fail on equipment access and scope rather than ambition, which is diagnosable in one early session. Support is questioning the question and written feedback on the student's own drafts.

sections.heading: Comparison one: Higher Level against Standard Level chemistry
paragraphs: Both levels share the structure and reactivity framework, the data booklet and the Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent. What differs is depth and the quantitative load. Higher Level extends the treatment across the same organising ideas, with longer calculation chains, more unfamiliar contexts and extended explanations that must be built from a named principle rather than described. It is not a different subject, it is the same subject with less slack.

The honest signal for Higher Level is quantitative fluency across a year of marked work rather than a strong interest in the subject. A student who enjoys chemistry and calculates hesitantly will find Higher Level punishing, because the arithmetic burden is relentless and time pressure compounds hesitation. A student who calculates confidently and finds the content demanding usually copes, because the content can be taught and the fluency cannot be installed quickly.

The university side matters for some applications and not for others. Several medicine and life science courses specify chemistry, sometimes at Higher Level, and the only reliable method is reading the admissions pages of the specific courses your child is considering in Diploma 1 while the choice is still open. General assumptions about what medicine requires are frequently wrong and always worth checking against the source.

Where families get this comparison wrong is by treating Higher Level as a statement of ambition. A good grade at Standard Level is worth more than a poor one at Higher Level for most purposes, and the decision should rest on marked evidence. A diagnostic session reading three marked pieces against Higher Level demands gives a more useful answer than a predicted grade does, and it can be done before the choice is locked.

sections.heading: Comparison two: chemistry against the other two sciences
paragraphs: Students choosing a third science, or deciding which science to take at Higher Level, are usually comparing on interest and difficulty. A more useful comparison is on the kind of precision each subject demands, because that predicts performance better than enjoyment does. All three share the investigation structure and the same uncertainty expectations, so the differences lie in what each penalises.

Chemistry penalises notation and arithmetic. Mechanism arrows drawn from the wrong atom, sign conventions reversed in energetics, moles calculations carried out carelessly. A student who understands chemistry and is loose with detail will lose marks steadily. Biology penalises imprecise language: naming a mechanism and a direction is required, and an answer stating that something increases earns nothing however sound the understanding behind it.

Physics penalises mathematical hesitancy. Rearranging relationships under pressure, handling indices and logarithms, propagating uncertainty and interpreting gradients are constant demands, and a student slow at algebra will be slow throughout the paper regardless of conceptual grasp. Of the three, physics is the most mathematically loaded and biology the most linguistically exacting, with chemistry sitting between them and demanding both in smaller doses.

So the comparison that helps is about a student's own failure mode. Careless with symbols and confident with words points towards biology. Fluent with algebra and impatient with phrasing points towards physics. Methodical, detail-tolerant and comfortable with arithmetic points towards chemistry. None of this overrides interest, which sustains two years of work, but it predicts the grade better than interest alone.

sections.heading: Structure and reactivity: how the course is actually organised
paragraphs: IB Chemistry is not a numbered topic list. It is built around two organising ideas: structure, covering models of the particulate nature of matter, bonding and classification; and reactivity, covering what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far they proceed, and the mechanisms by which they happen. Higher Level deepens the same framework rather than adding separate higher-level topics.

Asking a prospective tutor to describe that organisation takes ten seconds and is a useful filter. Someone working from an older guide will teach correct chemistry in a sequence that does not match the school's scheme of work, which leaves the student holding two mental maps of one subject. The content taught is not wrong; the planning around it is unreliable, and that is harder for a parent to detect.

The framework also changes what good revision looks like. Because structure underpins reactivity, revising them as separate blocks produces a student who can describe a bond and cannot predict a reaction. Examination questions routinely require both at once: why a particular structure produces a particular reactivity. Cross-cutting work on that link is what the assessment rewards and is rarely how a topic-based plan is built.

One feature of the course deserves mentioning because it is free and under-used. Chemistry is examined with a data booklet provided, containing constants, values and spectroscopic information. Students who meet it for the first time in the examination waste minutes locating entries. Using it in every session from the start costs nothing, and a tutor who only produces it occasionally is leaving marks available.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms: understanding against notation
paragraphs: If one comparison explains most chemistry underperformance it is this one. A student can understand a mechanism completely, be able to talk through it accurately, and still lose most of the marks for it, because mechanism questions are marked on notation. Curly arrows must originate from the correct lone pair or bond. Lone pairs must be shown where they participate. Charges must be assigned. Intermediates must be drawn, not implied.

Students find this unjust, which is a useful diagnostic in itself. The complaint that the chemistry was right and the mark was low is almost always a notation complaint, and it indicates a student who has learned mechanisms conceptually from diagrams rather than by drawing them repeatedly and having them marked. The repair is mechanical: draw, mark strictly, redraw, repeat.

That makes it the best-value block in the subject. Four to six sessions spent entirely on mechanism notation converts existing understanding into marks across both written papers, and the gain is permanent because notation is a habit rather than knowledge to be retained. By contrast, four to six sessions spent revisiting organic content a student already understands produces almost nothing.

The comparison for a parent is therefore between buying content teaching and buying marking. Content teaching feels like the obvious purchase and is often what a student asks for, because revisiting familiar material is comfortable. Marking is uncomfortable and is what moves the grade. A tutor who proposes a mechanism-drawing block rather than an organic revision block has read the evidence correctly.

sections.heading: Comparison three: where to spend, the investigation or the papers
paragraphs: Chemistry support money has two main destinations and the correct split depends entirely on timing. The Scientific Investigation is twenty per cent of the grade and its mark is decided by the research question and the data, both fixed months before the writing. The written papers are the other eighty per cent and remain reachable until the examinations. So the answer changes depending on whether the investigation is still open.

Where it is open, it takes priority, and the spending is small. One hour spent before the research question is fixed, asking what will be measured, with what precision, over what range and with how many repeats, protects a share of twenty per cent that no later session can recover. In chemistry the characteristic failure is a question with sound chemistry and no realistic measurement route using school equipment, and that is entirely preventable.

Where the investigation has been submitted, the comparison is simpler and the priorities are clear: mechanism notation first, energetics sign conventions second, stoichiometry fluency third, and the data-based section of Paper 1 fourth. All four are notational or procedural rather than conceptual, which is why they can be addressed in a defined number of sessions rather than requiring a term.

What should not win this comparison is a general content review across the whole course, which is the default purchase and the weakest one. It treats a notation and arithmetic problem as a knowledge problem, and a term passes with everyone working hard and the grade unchanged. A tutor who asks which deadlines are still open before proposing anything is making the right comparison on your behalf.

sections.heading: Comparison four: school support against paid support
paragraphs: Before paying anyone, it is worth comparing what the school already provides, because some of it is better than anything purchasable. The subject clinic is the clearest case: the teacher who set and marked an assessment explains its marking better than an outsider can, and in most schools in this corridor that time exists and is under-used. For a specific question about a specific marked answer it is both free and immediate.

The school also holds two documents families rarely request. The paper-level breakdown of the last internal assessment or mock, which shows whether losses sit in one component or across all of them. And the internal deadline calendar, which shows when the investigation and other internal work fall and where they cluster. Both are free, both change what support is worth buying, and both are usually given on request.

What a school structurally cannot provide is individual marking at volume. A chemistry teacher with several classes cannot mark every student's mechanism answers weekly, nor spend an hour interrogating each investigation research question. That is not a criticism of schools; it is an arithmetic limit on any teacher's time, and it happens to be exactly where chemistry marks are lost.

So the comparison resolves fairly cleanly. Use the school for marking explanations, for the documents, and for subject expertise on content. Buy private support for the things that need one student's work read closely and repeatedly: mechanism notation, sign-convention discipline, investigation design, and marked paper work. That split costs less than buying a general chemistry course and addresses more.

sections.heading: The comparison that does not move a grade
paragraphs: Which brings us to the neighbourhood question, which recurs in this corridor's parent groups and deserves a direct answer. Discovery Gardens is apartments and Al Furjan next door is villas, and families here frequently assume the villa side has better access to tutors. On chemistry specifically, that assumption is wrong in every respect that matters.

Neither community has a resident population of Diploma chemistry specialists. Both are reached on the same drive from the Al Barsha and Jumeirah areas where Dubai's tutors actually live and work. Visiting tutors quote them in the same band, with published Dubai in-home rates running AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Those are market figures read in October 2026 rather than our prices.

What does differ is study space, and it runs against Discovery Gardens: most flats here have no room with a door, and the realistic setup is a desk in a shared living area. That is manageable with over-ear headphones and a household agreement that the hour is a timetabled lesson. Travel runs slightly the other way, because the community is compact and pickup is quicker than Al Furjan's long bus loops.

The net difference for a chemistry student is close to zero, and the reason is that Higher Level chemistry is scarce everywhere in this corridor. Requiring a specialist who will also drive into either community for an evening slot narrows the pool to a handful of people. Removing the drive is what widens it, which is why we deliver online, and that applies identically on both sides of the road.

sections.heading: What no comparison should include, and our limits
paragraphs: One option available in this market should be excluded from every comparison on principle. At least one UAE provider advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. That transaction transfers risk rather than solving a problem: the IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student and their Diploma rather than on the seller.

The legitimate territory is wide and worth using fully. A tutor may read the four investigation criteria with the student, interrogate the research question and the measurement plan, teach the uncertainty and graphical treatment the data requires, show how published work structures an argument, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts against each criterion. Most of the recoverable marks sit inside that list.

What a tutor may not do is write or rewrite the report, process the student's data, supply the analysis, or outline the document for completion. IB Gram tutors state that boundary at the first session of any investigation block and give feedback in writing, so that a school asking what support was received gets an answer that holds up to scrutiny.

Our standing limits apply throughout. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; they are cited and linked. We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. We do not guarantee grades, we do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status, and no tutor attends a UAE address.

faqs.answer: It is the reference document provided in the chemistry examination, containing constants, values and spectroscopic information. Students who meet it for the first time in the exam lose minutes locating entries under pressure, which is a wholly avoidable loss. A tutor should have it open in every session from the start of the course so it is familiar by the time it matters. It is a fair and revealing question to ask a prospective tutor about.

faqs.question: Why do energetics sign conventions matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because they cost marks silently. A student can understand enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy perfectly and reverse a sign, which loses the mark every time without the student noticing a conceptual problem to address. It shows up as a scattering of lost marks across quantitative questions rather than as a visible weak topic. The fix is drilled convention work over two or three sessions rather than more theory, and it is one of the cheapest corrections available.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the investigation research question?
faqs.answer: A tutor can interrogate a question the student proposes, which is different from supplying one. The legitimate work is reading the four criteria with the student, asking what will be measured and with what precision, over what range and with how many repeats, teaching the uncertainty treatment the data will need, and giving written feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write the report, process the data, supply the analysis or outline it for completion.

faqs.question: What time do chemistry sessions run for Diploma students here?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00, and 19:00 on a day with a fixture or a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment. Students in Discovery Gardens travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30. Middle Years students are often home by 16:00. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and a missed session can move to the next evening rather than the next week, since nobody is travelling.

faqs.question: Does chemistry work well as an online session from an apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the work is mechanisms drawn on a shared screen, a data booklet open, and marked answers annotated together. What it needs is a desk, over-ear headphones with a microphone, paper for drawing structures, and the marked work to hand. The harder constraint in a flat is interruption rather than equipment, and the answer to that is a household agreement that the hour is a timetabled lesson rather than homework.

faqs.question: Does medicine require chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Some courses specify it and others do not, and general assumptions in parent groups are frequently wrong. The only reliable method is to read the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses your child is considering, in Diploma 1, while the subject and level choice is still open. Doing that in Diploma 2 produces information rather than a decision. IB Gram does not advise on admissions or guarantee any outcome in an application process.

faqs.question: Is a general chemistry revision course a good purchase?
faqs.answer: It is usually the default purchase and the weakest one, because it treats a notation and arithmetic problem as a knowledge problem. Four to six sessions revisiting organic content a student already understands produces very little; the same hours spent drawing mechanisms and having them marked converts understanding into marks across both papers. A tutor who proposes a mechanism-drawing block rather than a content review has read the evidence correctly.

faqs.question: What should never appear in a comparison of chemistry providers?
faqs.answer: A completed internal assessment. At least one UAE provider advertises them at a fixed price, and the transaction transfers risk rather than solving a problem: the IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student and their Diploma rather than on the seller. Any provider offering that should be excluded from the comparison entirely, whatever else they appear to offer.

intro.heading: The October problem, and why it lands hardest on a Downtown timetable
paragraphs: IB Chemistry has a predictable breaking point. For the first six or eight weeks of DP1 the course rewards the same habits that worked at IGCSE: learn the definition, apply the formula, check the units. Then Structure 3 arrives with functional groups, Reactivity 3 arrives with proton and electron transfer, and the subject starts asking students to explain why a reaction goes the way it goes. Students who memorised their way through 0620 or 4CH1 hit that wall in October and November of DP1, and that is when the searches start.

Downtown Dubai makes the timing worse rather than better, for a structural reason. There is no private school inside the district, so every child here is bussed out: to Sobha Hartland and Meydan in the south-east, to Oud Metha and Al Garhoud across the creek, or north to Al Safa and Al Satwa. The day that starts with a 6.50am lobby pickup ends with a return somewhere between 3.45pm and 5.00pm, and two afternoons a week are usually taken by a co-curricular commitment. By the time a DP1 student in a Boulevard tower sits down with chemistry homework, they have been awake for twelve hours.

That matters because chemistry homework is the least forgiving kind. A mechanism that is half-understood produces an answer that looks plausible and earns nothing. A student can write three curly arrows in the wrong places and feel they have done the work. The feedback loop is slow — the school marks it a week later, by which point the class has moved to the next sub-theme — and the gap compounds quietly until a mock paper makes it visible in February.

A weekly online session placed in the hour your child can actually think closes that loop to seven days. The tutor sees the mechanism being drawn, interrupts at the wrong arrow rather than after it, and uses the published mark scheme wording to show what a four-mark explanation contains. Because the lesson runs over live video from the apartment, nobody is budgeting 45 minutes each way on Al Khail Road, which is the only reason a 6.15pm start is realistic at all. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

This page is written around the shape of the Downtown week: which schools the district feeds, when a session fits, what the 2023 Chemistry guide actually examines, where the marks go, how Ramadan and the Dubai calendar move the plan, and what the market charges. The tables are the part worth printing. If you read only one of them, read the cost table, because the gap between the cheapest published rate in this market and the most expensive is a factor of nearly twenty, and the difference in what a Chemistry HL student actually gets for the money is nothing like that wide. Buying fewer, better-aimed hours beats buying more of them, and the theme table tells you where to aim.

sections.heading: Where the Downtown week leaves room for chemistry
paragraphs: A chemistry session that happens at the wrong hour is a session that achieves nothing, and parents in Downtown discover this the expensive way. The pattern across the district is a long bus day with two co-curricular afternoons, homework for five other Diploma subjects, and a student who is genuinely tired by 7pm. Fitting chemistry into that is a scheduling decision first and a tutoring decision second.

Year group changes the picture more than most people expect. An MYP 4 or MYP 5 student has a shorter school day and more flexibility, so a 5pm start works and a sixty-minute session is plenty. A DP1 student is carrying six subjects and the first Internal Assessment deadlines, and ninety minutes once a week beats sixty minutes twice. A DP2 student in the spring is managing mocks, several IA submissions and Extended Essay drafting at once, and the only format that survives that is a fixed slot nobody negotiates.

The table below is the shape families in this district report rather than any school's published timetable. Your bus operator will give you exact figures, and Ramadan compresses the whole day. The useful column is the last one, which is the session length that actually holds a tired student's attention at that age.

Online delivery is what makes a narrow window workable. A tutor who does not have to drive from Mirdif to the Boulevard at 5.30pm can hold a 6.15pm slot reliably, and a session can shift from Tuesday to Thursday without anyone writing off a journey. That flexibility is worth more in DP2 than it sounds in DP1.

sections.heading: What the 2023 Chemistry guide actually asks for
paragraphs: The 2023 subject guide reorganised chemistry around two organising concepts rather than a numbered topic list, and parents working from an older syllabus find the vocabulary unfamiliar. Structure covers three themes: models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers three more: what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. HL and SL share the themes, with HL carrying additional depth inside each.

Assessment is two written papers and one investigation. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and splits into Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, a data-based section. Paper 2 is 44% and runs from short structured questions into extended response. The Scientific Investigation is 20%. A data booklet is provided for both papers, which is a genuine opportunity and a genuine trap: students who have not practised with it spend exam minutes hunting for a constant they should be able to find in seconds.

The reorganisation matters for tuition because it changed where the difficulty sits. Under the current structure, the mechanism content in Reactivity 3 is no longer an option paper that some students avoid; proton transfer, electron transfer and electron sharing reactions are core for everyone. That is the single biggest reason chemistry requests from Dubai spike in DP1 autumn rather than DP2 spring.

sections.heading: The mechanism problem, and how it is actually fixed
paragraphs: Mechanism questions are the clearest example of a topic where effort and marks come apart. A student revises by reading a mechanism and following it, which feels like understanding and is not. The exam asks them to produce one, and production requires knowing where the electrons start, which bond breaks, what the intermediate looks like and why the arrow goes that way rather than the other. Reading never builds that. Drawing does.

The fix is mechanical and it works. The student draws the same small set of mechanisms repeatedly from a blank page, with the tutor watching the arrows as they are drawn rather than marking the finished product. Every wrong arrow is interrupted at the moment it is drawn and the student explains where the electron density was. Four sessions of that is usually enough for nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition to stop being guesswork. The remaining work is recognition: identifying from a question stem which mechanism is being asked for before drawing anything.

The second half of the problem is written explanation. Chemistry mark schemes reward specific chemical reasons, not narrative. A student writes "the bromine attacks the double bond" when the mark scheme wanted the pi electrons named as the nucleophile and the polarisation of the halogen explained. Both sentences are true. Only one scores. Command-term discipline is the same skill a physics student needs for explain questions, applied to different content, and it is coachable in the same way.

This is also where online delivery is genuinely better than a visit, not merely cheaper. A shared digital whiteboard keeps every attempt, so a student can see their own six attempts at the same mechanism in sequence and watch the arrows settle. A paper exercise book from an in-home session is in a bedroom by the following week.

sections.heading: Practical and data skills when the lessons are online
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a science subject can be tutored remotely when chemistry is a laboratory discipline. The honest answer is to separate the two things that word covers. Hands-on technique — titrating without overshooting, using a balance properly, making up a standard solution — is learned in your child's school laboratory and cannot be learned anywhere else. Nothing on this page pretends otherwise.

The examined skills are different. Paper 1B is a data-based section marked at a desk. The Scientific Investigation is graded on Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, three of which happen entirely away from the bench. Processing raw data, propagating uncertainty, choosing a graph that reveals the relationship, comparing a result against published values and writing a specific evaluation are desk skills, and they are where most of the available marks actually sit.

What online tuition does well, then, is the part that carries the marks. A tutor can work through your child's own raw data on a shared screen, show why a particular plot linearises the relationship, and point out before the write-up starts that an uncertainty has been ignored that will swallow the effect being measured. That intervention has to happen before data collection finishes, which is why the timing of investigation support matters more than its format.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the Dubai calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Any plan for an exam-year chemistry student in Dubai that ignores the academic calendar will fail in a specific and predictable way. The school year here runs roughly from late August or early September to the start of July, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break. Ramadan moves earlier by about eleven days each year, and during it school hours are reduced across the emirate. For a DP2 student, that compression lands in the middle of the most important revision period of the two-year course.

The practical consequence is that the weeks before Ramadan are worth more than the weeks during it. A chemistry plan built backwards from the May session should assume that Ramadan weeks deliver fewer productive study hours per day, not the same hours shifted. Families who schedule post-Iftar sessions find them genuinely effective, because the student is rested and the house is awake, but there are fewer of them and they start late. Planning for two sessions a week during Ramadan and getting one is a worse outcome than planning for one and keeping it.

The other calendar feature worth planning around is the spring break landing shortly before the exam window. For most DP2 students that break is the last block of uninterrupted time they will get. Using it for full timed papers rather than note-making is the single highest-return decision in the final term, and it needs the tutor booked in advance because every family in Dubai wants those same days.

We do not publish IB session or results dates here. The reason is that ibo.org blocks automated verification, so any IB date we printed would be second-hand, and a date a family plans around has to come from the school's IB coordinator. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the position is different: both publish timetables openly, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series.

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs across a term, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Pricing conversations in Dubai usually start at the premium end, which makes every other option look like a compromise. Start at the other end instead. The cheapest published rates in this market are EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Across a ten-week term at one hour a week, that is roughly AED 330 to AED 650 in total. For MYP homework supervision or a Year 9 student who needs company while working, that is a sensible purchase and nobody should be embarrassed by it.

The next step up is a qualified subject tutor working online, which Unitors publishes at IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. A ten-week term at one weekly hour costs AED 1,500 to AED 2,000, and that is the band where a DP1 chemistry student who needs Reactivity 3 explained properly belongs. Above it sit the specialist rates: TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, which is where a Chemistry HL candidate in DP2 with an investigation due realistically lands. Bestimate's monthly estimates run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. At the very top, BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour for named or examiner-linked tutors.

In-home tuition sits across those bands with travel loaded in: Bestimate records AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500. Advertised monthly packages in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is close to double per contact hour. Every figure in this section belongs to the provider named beside it; none is an IB Gram price. We quote after the free trial lesson, once level and frequency are known.

One piece of context parents find useful: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. School fees are flat this year; tuition is the discretionary line that is not, which is a reason to buy fewer, better hours rather than more cheap ones.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on a chemistry investigation and Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the line that separates a tutor from a problem, and it is worth being explicit because the Dubai search results for chemistry help include businesses that sell completed coursework. One competitor in this market advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying one is an academic honesty breach that puts the student's diploma at risk, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

What a chemistry tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and worth listing because vagueness here helps nobody. They may discuss candidate research questions and say which ones a school lab can actually answer. They may point out that the planned concentration range will not produce a measurable rate difference. They may teach uncertainty propagation, explain why a particular plot linearises a relationship, and read a completed draft and say which of the four criteria it is currently failing and why. They may coach the structure of an Extended Essay argument and check that the scope is achievable in 4,000 words.

What a tutor may never do is write, redraft to completion, produce the analysis, generate the data, or supply text that appears in the submission. The distinction is authorship. Feedback on the student's own work is teaching; producing work the student submits as their own is malpractice. IB Gram tutors are briefed on that boundary before they take an investigation request, and we would rather say no to a request than take the booking.

There is also a copyright line. We do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads. Those are published by the organisations that own them and we link to the official sources rather than reproducing them.
