sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what a Dubai chemistry student needs to show later
paragraphs: Chemistry is a gateway subject for medicine, pharmacy and engineering, and families in this corridor often start thinking about UAE university entry long before they think about equivalency. The two are connected. The Ministry of Education runs an equivalency process for secondary certificates, and the requirements differ by curriculum track in ways that surprise parents late in Year 13.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. One competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track, English proficiency is demonstrated by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to publish, because we have not read one on an official Ministry page and an unsourced number here is worse than no number. Ask the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly, or ask your school's university counsellor who processes this annually.

Nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it. The process belongs to the Ministry and the attestation authority. What a tutor can do is make sure the grades your child presents are the ones they are capable of, which is a different and more modest claim.

faqs.question: Why does my child suddenly struggle with IB Chemistry in the first term of DP1?
faqs.answer: Because the subject changes what it rewards. The opening weeks reward IGCSE habits: learn the definition, apply the formula. Then Structure 3 brings organic functional groups and Reactivity 3 brings proton, electron transfer and electron sharing mechanisms, and the course starts asking why a reaction proceeds the way it does. Memorisation stops working and reasoning has to replace it. That transition lands in October and November for most Dubai schools, which is exactly when chemistry tuition enquiries from Downtown and Business Bay rise. It is a predictable shift, not a sign your child has stopped being able.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry assessed under the current subject guide?
faqs.answer: Two written papers and one Scientific Investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and splits into Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, a data-based section. Paper 2 carries 44% and runs from short structured questions into extended response. The investigation carries the remaining 20% and is marked against four criteria worth six marks each. A data booklet is supplied for both papers. Content is organised into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3 rather than a numbered topic list, which is why older revision guides can feel mismatched to your child's class.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to fix organic mechanism questions?
faqs.answer: Drawing them from a blank page while someone watches the arrows appear. Reading a mechanism builds recognition, which feels like understanding but does not survive an exam that asks for production. The method that works is repetition of a small set of mechanisms, with the tutor interrupting at the moment a wrong arrow is drawn and asking where the electron density was. Four focused sessions usually settles nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition. The remaining work is recognising from the question stem which mechanism is wanted before any arrows are drawn at all.

faqs.question: Can chemistry really be tutored online when it is a laboratory subject?
faqs.answer: The practical technique cannot and we do not claim otherwise; titrating accurately and making up a standard solution are learned in your child's school laboratory. The examined skills are mostly elsewhere. Paper 1B is data analysis at a desk, and three of the four investigation criteria — Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation — are desk work. Processing data, propagating uncertainty, choosing a plot that reveals the relationship and writing a specific evaluation are where most of the available marks sit, and all of them are taught well over a shared screen.

faqs.question: What does a Chemistry HL tutor cost per term in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Counted across a ten-week term at one hour a week: the published entry rates of Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 come to roughly AED 330 to 650 in total, which suits homework supervision rather than HL chemistry. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour, so about AED 2,000 a term. TutorChase publishes AED 270, around AED 2,700. Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to AED 450 or more per hour. Those are the providers' own published figures, not IB Gram prices; we quote after the free trial.

faqs.question: How should a chemistry plan change during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Plan for fewer usable hours rather than the same hours moved later. School hours are reduced across the emirate during Ramadan, and for a DP2 student that compression lands squarely inside the revision period. Post-Iftar sessions work well — the student is rested and the household is awake — but they start late and there are fewer of them. The practical response is to front-load the weeks before Ramadan, hold one reliable session a week during it rather than attempting two, and treat the following weeks as recovery rather than acceleration.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics do Dubai students most often need help with in DP2?
faqs.answer: Three recur. Entropy and spontaneity in Reactivity 1, where signs and units go missing in otherwise correct arithmetic. Equilibrium and rate work in Reactivity 2, where the chemistry is understood but the calculation is laid out so badly that method marks are lost. And the mechanistic detail HL adds in Reactivity 3, which students meet last and practise least. None of the three needs a full re-teach; each responds to a short block of targeted past-paper work with the layout and notation drilled explicitly.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a chemistry Extended Essay without crossing the IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the boundary held firmly. A tutor can discuss candidate research questions, say which ones a school laboratory can realistically answer, check that the scope fits 4,000 words, coach the structure of the argument and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write any section, redraft to completion, produce the analysis or supply data. The dividing line is authorship. A chemistry Extended Essay that fails usually fails because the question was unanswerable in a school lab, and that is a conversation worth having in the first month.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL noticeably harder than Chemistry SL?
faqs.answer: They share the same six themes, so the difference is depth rather than breadth, and the depth concentrates in predictable places. HL adds full Gibbs energy calculations in Reactivity 1, quantitative rate equations and equilibrium constants in Reactivity 2, and more mechanistic and electrochemical detail in Reactivity 3. The papers are longer. In practice the HL student who struggles is usually struggling with the algebra underneath the chemistry rather than with the chemistry, which is why a student on Maths AI SL taking Chemistry HL often needs separate rearrangement work.

faqs.question: My child takes both Chemistry and Physics HL. Is that two investigations in one year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the scheduling of it is the risk rather than the work itself. Both subjects use the same four criteria — Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation — each worth six marks, so the skills transfer cleanly. What does not transfer is time. Two investigations with internal deadlines set independently by two departments can land within a fortnight of each other, and a student who starts both late has no capacity to repeat a measurement in either. Ask both subject teachers for their submission dates in the first term of DP1 and plan backwards from the earlier one.

faqs.question: Do I need to send my child's school data to book a chemistry tutor?
faqs.answer: We ask for the school name, the year group, the subject and level, and the realistic time your child is home, because those four facts determine which tutors can actually take the slot. We do not need grades, reports or photographs to make a match, and we do not ask for them. If you choose to send a marked paper, it helps the tutor diagnose faster and we use it for that purpose only. Lead data about a minor is held for matching and you can ask for it to be deleted at any point.

faqs.answer: The campuses Downtown families most often name sit in the creek-side and Hartland clusters and in the older Oud Metha and Al Garhoud belt: Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, North London Collegiate School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy, Deira International School and Jumeirah Baccalaureate School appear repeatedly in enquiries, alongside British-curriculum schools that run IGCSE into A Level rather than the Diploma. Check the current programme list on the school's own site, because offerings change between academic years. These names are local context only and imply no relationship with IB Gram.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Dubai legal, and what should I ask a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is legal and it is permitted rather than unregulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. Ask any tutor whether they hold the permit, and treat a claim of regulatory endorsement as a prompt for one more question.

Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. One ranking competitor in this market states six subjects are needed; the sourced figure is five. For the IB there is no points threshold we will publish, because we have not read one on an official Ministry page. Verify on moe.gov.ae.

When that window is full we say so and offer a different hour, a different day, or a named wait, rather than substituting a general science tutor for a Chemistry HL request. Some of our chemistry tutors are UAE residents and others teach from India over video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The same answer in Academic City, Silicon Oasis and Mirdif
paragraphs: Parents in this part of Dubai compare neighbourhoods constantly, and for chemistry the comparison is instructive because it collapses. Dubai International Academic City is a university free zone off Al Ain Road; its own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British route to A Level. One junction away in Silicon Oasis, GEMS Wellington Academy teaches the Diploma. Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the full IB continuum, Universal American School in Al Warqa carries IB programmes, and the Nad Al Sheba schools sit beyond.

So an Academic City family drives ten minutes, a Silicon Oasis family drives five, a Mirdif family walks their child to the gate, and an International City family drives half an hour. Those differences are real and they change what time a session can start. What they do not change is the supply of people who can teach Diploma chemistry at Higher Level, because that is set across the emirate rather than district by district, and in the eastern suburbs it is thin everywhere.

Chemistry has a second reason to ignore geography. The two things that decide a chemistry grade are mole calculations and mechanism conventions, and both are specific, teachable and almost entirely independent of where a tutor sits. A student who cannot convert between mass, moles and concentration reliably will lose marks in every one of the six themes, and a student who draws curly arrows from the wrong origin will lose organic marks regardless of how well they understand the reaction.

The current chemistry syllabus is organised around two concepts, Structure and Reactivity, each containing three themes. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and what happens when electrons are transferred. A tutor talking about numbered topics and option units is working from a superseded guide.

The third decisive element is the scientific investigation, worth twenty-four marks across four criteria. In chemistry the commonest failure is a design that the school's apparatus cannot support at the precision the question needs - a rates investigation with no way to time accurately, or a titration with no suitable indicator available. That is a feasibility conversation, and it should happen before any data is collected rather than after a wasted week.

IB Gram delivers all of this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For Higher Level chemistry in this cluster that is not a limitation but the reason the arrangement works, because the local pool a travelling tutor would come from barely exists, while the pool that can coach organic mechanisms and equilibrium calculations does.

programmes.name: MYP sciences into Diploma chemistry
programmes.description: Graded 1-8 against knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. programmes.description: The full set of themes at standard depth, with written papers and the scientific investigation. Standard Level chemistry is often taken as a third science or as a prerequisite for a non-chemistry degree, and the presenting problem is usually stoichiometry rather than concepts. Students understand the chemistry and lose marks on the arithmetic that expresses it.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level chemistry requests from Academic City and Silicon Oasis frequently turn out to need six sessions on moles rather than a year of general support. One diagnostic session settles which it is, and saying so honestly costs us revenue and saves the family several thousand dirhams.

programmes.name: Chemistry, Higher Level
programmes.description: Additional content across every theme, with substantially more organic synthesis, more quantitative equilibrium and acid-base work, and more demanding spectroscopic interpretation. Higher Level chemistry is the usual requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering, which makes it one of the highest-stakes subjects in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level chemistry demand in Dubai peaks in the same fortnight every year, around mock examinations, and that is when it is hardest to staff. Families in this cluster who book in the first term get a specialist; families who book in February get whoever is free. The rate is the same either way, which is the entire argument for planning ahead.

programmes.name: The chemistry scientific investigation
programmes.description: An independent investigation worth twenty-four marks across four criteria of six each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. In chemistry it most often takes the form of a rates study, a titration-based concentration determination, an energetics measurement or an electrochemistry investigation, each with its own characteristic pitfalls.
programmes.countryNote: The limiting factor in this cluster is laboratory provision, which varies considerably between schools a few kilometres apart. A rates investigation needs reliable timing and temperature control; a titration needs suitable glassware and indicator. Check what the school has before the research design is written, because redesigning after a failed week costs more than the whole coaching block.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-academ.subjectsIntro: Chemistry divides into themes and skills, and most lost marks are in the skills. These are the areas families in this cluster raise.

subjects.name: Mole calculations and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Mass to moles, concentration, gas volumes, limiting reagent, percentage yield and atom economy. The single highest-return topic in the subject, because it appears inside questions in every theme. A student who hesitates here loses marks throughout the paper rather than in one section.

subjects.name: Models of the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Atomic structure, electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and the mass spectrum. Marks go on explanations of trends that describe the pattern rather than attributing it to nuclear charge, shielding and sub-level occupancy in the order the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, shapes of molecules and hybridisation at Higher Level. The recurring error is explaining a physical property by naming a bond type without saying which forces are broken and why that requires more or less energy.

subjects.name: Classification of matter and spectroscopy
subjects.description: Periodicity, organic families and, at Higher Level, structural determination from spectroscopic data. Spectroscopy questions reward a systematic order of attack - molecular formula, then functional groups, then connectivity - which students rarely apply unprompted.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign conventions account for most of the lost marks, followed closely by using bond enthalpies and formation enthalpies in the same calculation.

subjects.name: Rates of reaction
subjects.description: Collision theory, rate expressions and, at Higher Level, rate-determining steps and activation energy from graphical data. A common investigation topic in this cluster, and one where the design usually fails on timing precision rather than on chemistry.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier reasoning and, at Higher Level, equilibrium constant calculations. Students apply Le Chatelier correctly and then lose marks by failing to state what happens to the value of the constant, which is a separate and frequently examined point.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and pH
subjects.description: Strong and weak acids, pH and pKa calculations, buffers and titration curves at Higher Level. Logarithmic arithmetic is where the marks go, along with answers that treat a weak acid as fully dissociated partway through a calculation.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrolysis and, at Higher Level, cell potentials and the Nernst-type reasoning the guide requires. Half-equation balancing in acidic and basic conditions is mechanical and reliably mishandled under time pressure.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction types and, at Higher Level, nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition mechanisms with curly arrows. Mechanism marks are lost on conventions - arrow origin, lone pairs, charges, partial charges - rather than on understanding the chemistry.

subjects.name: Investigation design for chemistry
subjects.description: Choosing between rates, titration, energetics and electrochemistry designs with an eye on what the school's laboratory can actually deliver, then controlling the variables that matter. Feasibility first, chemistry second, writing third.

subjects.name: Uncertainty in chemical measurement
subjects.description: Glassware tolerances, propagation through a concentration calculation, and uncertainty in a gradient for rates work. Examined in data-analysis questions and central to the investigation's evaluation criterion, and almost never taught as a lesson in its own right.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: the six themes and where each one bites
paragraphs: The current chemistry syllabus is built around two organising concepts rather than a numbered topic list. Structure contains models of the particulate nature of matter, bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity contains what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and what happens when electrons are transferred. If a prospective tutor describes the course in terms of numbered topics with optional units, they are working from the previous guide.

Each theme has a characteristic failure mode, and they are different in kind. In Structure the failures are explanatory: a trend described rather than attributed, a property named rather than accounted for. In Reactivity they are numerical: sign conventions in energetics, logarithms in acid-base work, half-equation balancing in redox. Knowing which kind of failure dominates tells you whether your child needs writing practice or arithmetic practice, and those are different sessions.

The table below pairs each theme with its characteristic failure and a diagnostic question that surfaces it quickly. Those diagnostics are the useful part: each takes a few minutes and separates a content gap from a habit, which is the distinction that decides what the next eight sessions should contain.

One scheduling note. In most schools in this cluster the organic content and the equilibrium and acid-base work land in the second half of the first Diploma year or early in the second, around the time the investigation is live. That overlap is why chemistry support booked in the first term is worth more than the same number of hours bought in February.

sections.heading: Mole calculations: the highest-return topic in the subject
paragraphs: If a chemistry student in this cluster is losing marks across the whole paper rather than in one section, the cause is almost always stoichiometry. Mass to moles, moles to concentration, concentration to volume, gas volumes, limiting reagent, percentage yield. These calculations sit inside questions in every theme, which means a hesitation here costs marks in energetics, in equilibrium, in acid-base work, in redox and in the investigation, all at once.

The diagnostic is quick. Give a student a three-step stoichiometry problem and watch where they stop. A student who has to reconstruct the relationship between mass, moles and molar mass each time is spending working memory on arithmetic that should be automatic, and has none left for the chemistry the question is actually about. That is not a conceptual problem and it is not fixed by re-explaining the concept.

What fixes it is volume and variety: short calculation sets at the start of every session, across all the forms the Diploma uses, until the conversions happen without thought. Six to eight sessions of this, run alongside whatever the class is covering, changes a student's performance across the whole subject rather than in one theme. It is the least interesting thing a chemistry tutor does and the most valuable.

For families arriving from Indian-curriculum schools - a large group in Al Warqa and International City - the position is often reversed. Stoichiometry is strong, and the gaps are in explanation writing and in mechanism conventions. The same diagnostic session identifies which of the two situations you are in, which is why we would rather run it than take a booking on assumption.
bullets: Mass to moles via molar mass, in both directions, without hesitation
Concentration, volume and amount interconverted fluently
Limiting reagent identified before any yield calculation
Gas volumes handled with the correct conditions stated
Percentage yield and atom economy distinguished and calculated separately

sections.heading: Mechanism conventions are marking criteria, not drawing style
paragraphs: Organic mechanism questions are where good chemistry students lose marks they cannot explain. The chemistry is understood, the product is right, and the mark is two out of four. The reason is almost always convention: the curly arrow starts from the bond or the lone pair rather than from the atom, lone pairs are shown where they matter, formal charges appear on intermediates, partial charges are marked on polarised bonds, and the arrow points at the atom receiving the electron pair.

Mark schemes credit these individually. An arrow from the wrong origin loses the arrow mark even when the overall mechanism is correct. A missing charge on a carbocation loses the intermediate mark. These are not stylistic preferences imposed by a fussy examiner; they are the evidence that the student understands which electrons move where, which is the entire point of drawing a mechanism rather than writing an equation.

The teaching is repetitive and quick. Draw nucleophilic substitution ten times, with the conventions checked each time, and the habits set. Draw electrophilic addition to an alkene another ten times. At Higher Level add the distinction between the two substitution pathways and the stereochemical consequences. Fifteen minutes a session for a month produces a student who scores full marks on mechanism questions as a matter of routine.

Spectroscopy belongs in the same section because it is also a procedure rather than a body of knowledge. Attack in a fixed order: molecular formula from the mass spectrum, functional groups from the infrared, connectivity and environments from the nuclear magnetic resonance. Students who work in that order reach the structure; students who look at everything at once usually do not.

sections.heading: Chemistry investigation designs and their characteristic pitfalls
paragraphs: Chemistry investigations in this cluster cluster into four or five familiar shapes, and each has a known way of going wrong. The single most common failure is not analytical but practical: a design that the school's laboratory cannot execute at the precision the research question requires. A rates investigation needs reliable timing and temperature control. A titration needs appropriate glassware and a suitable indicator. Discovering the gap after a week of data collection is the expensive route to finding out.

So the first coaching session is a feasibility session, and it is short. What apparatus does the school actually have? What is the smallest division on the glassware, and what uncertainty does that imply for the final result? Can the temperature be held constant, and how? Is there enough of the reagent for the number of repeats the design needs? Those questions take half an hour and save a fortnight.

Beyond feasibility, the marks sit where they sit in every science investigation: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. In chemistry the data-analysis criterion rewards uncertainty propagated properly through a concentration calculation, which means knowing glassware tolerances rather than guessing. The evaluation criterion rewards identifying the dominant uncertainty source and proposing a specific change, not a list of generic limitations.

The boundary on all of this is firm. The student chooses the research question, designs the method, takes the measurements, processes the data and writes the report. The tutor tests feasibility, explains the criteria, questions the design and comments on drafts. One operator competing for these searches sells completed investigations at a published price; a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Academic City, Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, International City: the comparison done properly
paragraphs: Since families here shop by comparison, here is the comparison with the columns that actually matter for chemistry. Where the subject is taught nearby. What laboratory access looks like for investigation work. When a weekday session can realistically begin. And what the local pool of Higher Level chemistry specialists contains, which is the column where the comparison collapses.

Mirdif and Silicon Oasis have Diploma teaching inside the district, which makes both the school run and investigation access easier - a student who can get back into the laboratory for an extra set of readings has a real advantage over one who cannot. Academic City families travel one junction. International City families travel considerably further, which pushes sessions past six and makes the weekend morning the slot where calculation-heavy work gets done.

The last column reads the same in every row, and that is the finding. None of these four neighbourhoods contains a usable local choice of tutors who teach Diploma chemistry at Higher Level, because the supply is emirate-wide and the eastern suburbs are not where it concentrates. A family in Mirdif has a marginally better chance than one in Al Khawaneej. Neither has a shortlist.

Which means the practical advice is the same from all four addresses: choose on whether the tutor teaches the level and can coach an investigation through uncertainty propagation, and let the delivery be online so that choice is available at all. The timing differences in the table are worth planning around; the geography differences are not worth paying for.

sections.heading: Higher Level chemistry and the courses it gates
paragraphs: Chemistry at Higher Level carries unusual weight because of which degrees it gates. It is the standard requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and chemical engineering, which means a student in this cluster considering any of those routes is making a decision in Year 11 that is extremely awkward to reverse later. Dropping from Higher to Standard Level is generally possible; moving the other way usually is not.

The additional content at Higher Level is not evenly distributed. Organic chemistry expands considerably, with more reaction types and synthesis route planning. Equilibrium and acid-base work becomes properly quantitative, with equilibrium constant and pKa calculations. Energetics adds entropy and free energy. Electrochemistry adds cell potentials. Spectroscopic structure determination appears. The mathematical demand rises throughout, which is why stoichiometry fluency matters even more here.

The load question is also worth asking honestly. Higher Level chemistry alongside Higher Level biology and Higher Level mathematics is a common medicine-track combination and a genuinely heavy two years. If your child is still choosing, map the assessment deadlines across both years rather than looking only at interest, and ask the Diploma coordinator which combinations the timetable actually supports.

For admissions specifically, read the published requirements for each university and course rather than relying on a general rule, and do it during the first Diploma year. UAE institutions and overseas ones differ, and some specify a minimum grade in Higher Level chemistry rather than merely requiring the subject. That number, not the equivalency floor, is what the tutoring plan should be built around.

paragraphs: Three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote United States dollars, which is not the currency families here transact in. So here are the bands in dirhams, each attributed to whoever published the figure, all read in October 2026, and none of them an IB Gram rate.

Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That band is usable for Standard Level content support and rarely contains anybody who can coach Higher Level organic mechanisms. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Monthly, published packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, while Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

Useful context for a family weighing tutoring against other education costs: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For our own rates, the free trial lesson comes first and the figure is quoted against your child's actual level and the work the diagnosis identifies.

sections.heading: The chemistry year counted backwards, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session. For chemistry the internal calendar is the binding one, because the investigation deadline usually lands in the second half of the first Diploma year or early in the second, where it collides with mock examinations, the Extended Essay submission and the Theory of Knowledge essay inside a few weeks in January and February.

Counting backwards produces a workable order. Stoichiometry fluency in the first term of the first year, before it starts costing marks in other themes. Mechanism conventions drilled as organic content is taught rather than revisited in revision. Investigation feasibility checked and data collected before mock preparation begins. Timed past-paper work started in the first term of the second year rather than after the mocks.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all, so confirm every IB date with the Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

And the limits, plainly. We make no promises about grades, publish no predicted scores and offer no guarantee. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we have no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. On regulation: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB chemistry tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your address, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. For chemistry the online route is a straightforward advantage here. Academic City's own secondary runs the British route, the nearest Diploma chemistry teaching is in Silicon Oasis, and the local pool of tutors who teach the subject at Higher Level is effectively empty. Matching online lets us choose on whether the tutor can coach organic mechanisms and investigation uncertainty.

faqs.question: Is Mirdif or Academic City better for a Diploma chemistry student?
faqs.answer: Mirdif marginally, for two logistical reasons: Uptown International School runs the IB continuum inside the district so the school run is short, and getting back into the laboratory for an extra set of investigation readings is easier. Neither advantage touches the thing that decides the grade. Neither neighbourhood - nor Silicon Oasis, nor International City - contains a usable local choice of Higher Level chemistry specialists, because that supply is set across the emirate rather than district by district.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose chemistry marks across the whole paper?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly stoichiometry. Mole calculations sit inside questions in every theme, so a student who has to reconstruct the relationship between mass, moles and molar mass each time is spending working memory on arithmetic instead of on the chemistry the question is about. The diagnostic takes two minutes: give a three-step mole problem and watch where he stops. The fix is short calculation sets every session for six to eight weeks, run alongside whatever the class is covering.

faqs.question: My daughter understands organic chemistry but loses mechanism marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Conventions, which mark schemes credit individually. The curly arrow must start from the bond or the lone pair rather than from the atom, lone pairs must be shown where they matter, formal charges must appear on intermediates, and partial charges must be marked on polarised bonds. An arrow from the wrong origin loses the arrow mark even when the product is right. Drawing nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition ten times each, with the conventions checked, fixes it in about a month.

faqs.question: How should a student approach a spectroscopy question?
faqs.answer: In a fixed order, which is the whole technique. Molecular formula from the mass spectrum first, then functional groups from the infrared, then connectivity and the number of environments from the nuclear magnetic resonance data. Students who work in that order arrive at the structure reliably; students who look at all three spectra simultaneously usually do not. It is a procedure rather than knowledge, which means it responds to a handful of worked examples rather than to more revision.

faqs.question: What goes wrong with chemistry investigations in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Feasibility, far more often than analysis. A rates design with no reliable way to time the endpoint. A temperature study with no water bath, so the temperature drifts during the run. A titration with no suitable indicator or with glassware whose tolerance makes the final uncertainty unacceptable. All of these are discovered after a week of data collection unless somebody asks what the school actually has beforehand. That conversation takes half an hour.

faqs.question: How do the 24 investigation marks work in chemistry?
faqs.answer: Four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The equal weighting matters because research design is settled before any measurement and cannot be rescued later. In chemistry the data-analysis criterion rewards uncertainty propagated properly through a concentration calculation, which means knowing the burette and pipette tolerances rather than estimating them, and the evaluation criterion rewards naming the dominant uncertainty source and proposing one specific change.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my child's chemistry investigation draft?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor can test whether the design is executable with the school's apparatus, explain what each criterion rewards, question the method, teach uncertainty treatment on your child's own measurements, and read and comment on drafts. A tutor cannot choose the research question, design the method, supply or process data, or provide text. The test is whether your child could explain, without notes, why every number and sentence is there. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level chemistry essential for a medicine application from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level chemistry is the standard requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary science and chemical engineering, and some universities specify a minimum grade in it rather than merely requiring the subject. Read the published requirements for each institution and course during the first Diploma year, including the UAE universities, because dropping from Higher to Standard Level is generally possible later while moving up usually is not. Also consider the load: Higher Level chemistry with Higher Level biology and mathematics is a demanding two years.

faqs.question: What extra content does Higher Level chemistry add?
faqs.answer: Not an even spread. Organic chemistry expands considerably with more reaction types and synthesis route planning. Equilibrium and acid-base work becomes quantitative, with equilibrium constant and pKa calculations. Energetics adds entropy and free energy. Electrochemistry adds cell potentials. Spectroscopic structure determination appears. The mathematical demand rises throughout, which is why stoichiometry fluency matters more at Higher Level than at Standard, not less, despite the content being more conceptually interesting.

faqs.question: My child came from a CBSE school in Al Warqa. What will be different?
faqs.answer: Usually the calculations are strong and the writing is not, which is a narrow and quickly addressed gap. Students arriving from Indian-curriculum schools tend to handle stoichiometry confidently and then lose marks by describing a trend rather than attributing it to nuclear charge and shielding, and by drawing mechanisms without the conventions the mark scheme credits. Three sessions on explanation structure and a month of mechanism practice usually closes most of the distance.

faqs.question: When should chemistry support start to avoid the February collision?
faqs.answer: The first term of the first Diploma year, for stoichiometry, before the gap starts costing marks in energetics and equilibrium. Mechanism work as the organic content is taught rather than in revision. Investigation feasibility checked and data collected before mock preparation begins. In most schools in this cluster the investigation deadline, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the mocks all land within a few weeks in January and February, and chemistry is rarely the piece that gets sacrificed happily.

faqs.question: How much does Higher Level chemistry tutoring cost in eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers publishing them: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650; in-home one-to-one with travel at AED 180 to 500. The band below AED 100 is usable for Standard Level content and rarely contains anybody who coaches Higher Level organic.

faqs.question: Does a chemistry tutor working in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level chemistry tutor is available?
faqs.answer: You hear it at the enquiry stage rather than discovering it in session three. Higher Level chemistry demand across Dubai concentrates in the fortnight either side of mock examinations, and that is when we are most likely to be unable to staff it well. In that case we give a realistic wait, or we decline. What we will not do is put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate and rely on a pleasant first lesson to carry the arrangement.

intro.heading: Chemistry tuition that fits the Creek Harbour afternoon
paragraphs: Dubai Creek Harbour is a commuter district for schooling. The master plan is still filling in, so secondary students leave the district every morning and come back in the late afternoon, and almost every tutoring decision a parent here makes is really a decision about the clock. A Chemistry session booked for 3.30pm will be missed, rescheduled and eventually abandoned. A Chemistry session booked for 5pm, after the bus has come in and a meal has happened, survives the term. That sounds trivial and it is the single biggest predictor of whether tutoring works for a family in this district.

The geography is specific enough to plan around. Most Creek Harbour families run their school day in one of three directions. North and west across the creek to Al Jaddaf, Culture Village and Al Garhoud, which is the shortest journey and the densest nearby school cluster. South along Ras Al Khor Road or Al Khail Road to Nad Al Sheba, Sobha Hartland and Meydan, which holds some of the emirate's largest Diploma cohorts. Or towards Downtown, Business Bay and Al Quoz, usually chosen because a parent works nearby rather than because the drive is short.

School days in those clusters finish between roughly 2.45pm and 3.15pm. The bus does not. Pick-up, loading and the run back across the Ras Al Khor approaches puts most Creek Harbour students through their own front door between 4pm and 4.30pm, and later on days when the Business Bay crossing is slow. Add the time it takes a seventeen-year-old to eat something and find their folder, and the first honest tutoring slot in this district is about 5pm. Weekends and the Friday short day open the morning up, which is why a lot of our Creek Harbour Chemistry work happens on Saturdays.

Chemistry has its own reason to care about timing. It is a subject where the work has to be done in sequence, because energetics depends on bonding, equilibrium depends on energetics, and organic mechanisms depend on understanding electron movement properly in the first term. A student who misses three weeks of DP1 Chemistry has not lost three weeks of content; they have lost the foundation for the next three months. Catching that early in a predictable weekly slot is far cheaper, in money and in stress, than catching it in a panic before mocks.

What IB Gram offers for Creek Harbour is Diploma Programme Chemistry taught one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, by a tutor matched to the level and the school's own sequence. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. That is a service we run only in India, and we say so here rather than after a booking. The practical benefit for this district is exactly the thing the school run exposes: a video lesson at 5pm costs the tutor no driving time, so the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching rather than an hour of teaching plus a share of someone's commute.

programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed on four criteria scored 1-8 rather than on papers: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. It builds strong investigation design early. What it does not build is the calculation stamina DP Chemistry assumes, particularly moles, concentration and limiting reagents, which arrive fast in the first DP term.
programmes.countryNote: For a Creek Harbour student in MYP 5 who intends to take Chemistry in the Diploma, the most useful term of tuition is the summer before DP1 rather than the panic term after. Three or four sessions on mole calculations and on balancing redox equations removes the problem that otherwise surfaces in October. We will say when this is not needed, which for a confident MYP mathematician it often is not.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is syllabus 0620 and Pearson's International GCSE Chemistry is 4CH1. Both split into core and extended or higher content and both assess practical skills on paper rather than in a laboratory. The transition into DP Chemistry is less about new topics than about depth: the same reaction a student described at IGCSE now has to be explained with enthalpy data, equilibrium position and a mechanism.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools around Al Jaddaf, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Sheba feed both A Level and the IB Diploma. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE centres; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. Every centre is allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

programmes.name: Chemistry internal investigation and extended essay
programmes.description: The Chemistry internal investigation is one independent experiment written up within the IB's word limit and marked at school against the IB's named criteria. A Chemistry extended essay is a separate 4,000-word research piece with a school supervisor. Both must be the student's own work throughout. Tutoring here means teaching method, interrogating the research question, explaining what each criterion rewards, and giving written feedback on drafts the student has written.
programmes.countryNote: Timing matters more than talent on this component. Most Dubai schools set the Chemistry investigation deadline in the second term of DP1 or the first term of DP2, which collides with the Creek Harbour exam and travel calendar. A short intensive block four to six weeks before the school's deadline is the arrangement that works; a block in the final fortnight rarely changes the criterion the student is losing marks under.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-creek-.subjectsIntro: Chemistry rarely travels alone. The combinations below are the ones Creek Harbour families actually request alongside it, described by what the assessment rewards rather than by topic list.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL
subjects.description: The full core plus additional higher-level material in every theme, with a markedly heavier quantitative load. Marks concentrate in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. HL students typically need 90-minute sessions to work a full extended-response question and review it against a mark scheme in the same sitting.

subjects.name: Chemistry SL
subjects.description: The same core with the higher-level extensions removed. SL marks are lost disproportionately on definitions and command terms rather than on difficult chemistry: answering 'outline' at the length of 'explain' costs time, and answering 'explain' at the length of 'state' costs marks outright.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most common pairing for Creek Harbour students aiming at medicine or life sciences. Heavy on terminology precision. Students who handle the clean variables of a Chemistry investigation often find the Biology investigation harder, because biological variables refuse to behave.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The engineering pairing. Shares Chemistry's structure of external papers plus a 20% investigation, and shares the data-booklet navigation skill. A student strong in Chemistry calculations usually transfers well, except on uncertainty propagation, which Physics tests harder.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus and algebra at the level DP Chemistry quietly assumes. A Chemistry student who stalls on logarithms will stall on pH and on rate equations, and the symptom shows up in Chemistry first. We often find the real Chemistry fix is three sessions of AA work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led with a graphical and technology emphasis. Workable with Chemistry SL. Check the prerequisite pages of any intended medicine or engineering degree before choosing this route, because several faculties specify the Analysis and Approaches course.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary option that satisfies both a science and an individuals-and-societies requirement. Chemistry students find the systems-thinking assessment unfamiliar at first, because it rewards argument structure rather than calculation accuracy.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Chosen by Chemistry students who want a second science with a physiological angle. Contains more biochemistry than most expect, so Chemistry knowledge transfers directly into the energy-systems material.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Includes an individual oral on extracts the student chooses. Science students commonly underestimate the guided analysis paper, where the marks follow structure and evidence selection rather than vocabulary range.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. A Chemistry student has usable material here from laboratory work, provided they can move past treating scientific method as self-evidently reliable.

sections.heading: The Creek Harbour afternoon, hour by hour
paragraphs: Here is the direct answer to when a Chemistry session can start in this district: about 5pm on a weekday for most families, 4.30pm for those at Sobha Hartland, and from mid-morning at the weekend. Everything else on this page follows from that, so it is worth setting out properly rather than as a footnote. The reason parents get this wrong is that they plan from the school's published end time, which is between 2.45pm and 3.15pm in the nearby clusters, and the school's end time is not when the child is home.

The gap between those two numbers is where tutoring arrangements die. Bus loading takes ten to fifteen minutes before a vehicle moves. The Ras Al Khor and Al Khail approaches to Creek Harbour are at their slowest exactly when the school buses use them. Towers in Creek Beach and Harbour Views have lift queues at that hour. A student who left a Nad Al Sheba campus at 3.05pm is commonly through their own front door at 4.25pm, and is not in a state to balance a redox equation for another half hour after that.

What follows is practical rather than theoretical. Book the slot you can keep. A 5pm Chemistry hour that runs for thirty weeks does far more for a grade than a 3.30pm hour that runs for six weeks and then collapses into rescheduling messages. Because the lesson is delivered over video, the tutor has no commute of their own to fit around yours, so a later start costs nothing and an evening slot is as available as an afternoon one. The table sets out what we see across the three school runs.

sections.heading: Where the DP Chemistry marks sit, and which ones the school already holds
paragraphs: A fifth of your child's Chemistry grade is decided before the examination session and is marked by their own teacher. The internal investigation is worth 20% at both Higher and Standard Level, assessed at school against criteria the IB names and publishes. Families find this out late with surprising regularity, usually when the mark comes back and the window for improving the work has closed. If you take one thing from this page besides the timetable, take that date off your child's school deadline sheet and put it somewhere you will see it.

The external papers divide differently from most national systems. One paper tests breadth across the whole course in a short-answer and multiple-choice format. Another is extended response, where the marks follow the structure of an explanation at least as much as its chemistry. A further component covers experimental technique and the course's optional material, and it exposes students who know the content but have never thought hard about why a particular apparatus choice limits precision. The data booklet supplies constants and equations throughout, which means examination performance depends on finding the right relationship quickly rather than on having memorised it.

For tutoring this has a direct consequence. The highest-yield work in the final term is almost never new content. It is command-term discipline, extended-response structure, data-booklet navigation speed, and the handful of calculation types that recur every session: enthalpy cycles, equilibrium expressions, pH and buffer calculations, titration arithmetic. Those are drillable in a defined number of hours, which is why we can give a straight answer after a trial lesson about what six or eight weeks will realistically reach.

sections.heading: Energetics, equilibrium and organic: the three places Chemistry grades go
paragraphs: Across the DP Chemistry students we support in Dubai's central corridor, lost marks cluster in three predictable areas, and they are not the areas parents expect. Atomic structure and periodicity look hard on a syllabus and are usually taught thoroughly, because every teacher knows they come first and sets the pace accordingly. The damage happens later, in material taught at speed during a crowded middle term.

Energetics is the first. Enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpy calculations and Hess's law reward a student who sets out their reasoning on paper and punish a student who tries to hold the signs in their head. Most errors here are sign errors, not conceptual failures, and they are fixed by a method rather than by more theory. Equilibrium is the second, and it is where the mathematics catches up with students: writing an expression correctly, handling a quadratic that arises from it, and reasoning about Le Chatelier shifts without contradicting the arithmetic.

Organic chemistry is the third and the most expensive. It is taught as mechanisms, but it is examined as pattern recognition under time pressure, and the two require different practice. A student who can follow a nucleophilic substitution when it is explained may still be unable to produce it from a blank page in an examination. The remedy is volume with feedback: a reasonable number of mechanisms written out from scratch, marked, and the errors logged. For a Creek Harbour student on a 5pm weekday hour, this is the material we most often move to a weekend block, because it needs sustained attention rather than a tired forty minutes.

Equilibrium: expression setup, quadratics, and Le Chatelier reasoning that matches the maths

sections.heading: What a Chemistry tutor costs per month in this market
paragraphs: Parents in this district generally budget monthly rather than hourly, so start there. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session come out at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upwards for specialist support in an examination year. Advertised packages in the market sit alongside those figures: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those monthly numbers are the ones worth comparing, because an hourly rate tells you nothing until you know how many hours a term actually contains.

Converted to the hour, the market divides into tiers that publish their own numbers. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialist tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors ranging up to AED 500. BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutoring. Every one of those figures was read from the provider's own page in October 2026.

The useful comparison for a Creek Harbour family is between the online specialist band and the in-home band, because the difference is largely travel. A tutor driving to a Creek Harbour tower at 5pm spends a meaningful part of their working evening on the Ras Al Khor approaches, and that time is inside the hourly rate whether or not anyone itemises it. IB Gram publishes no hourly price list on these pages, because the right arrangement depends on level, subject and frequency, and quoting a single number would be less honest than quoting none. What we publish is the market, so that you can judge any quote including ours, and a free trial lesson so you see the teaching before any payment. It is also worth putting tutoring in the context of school fees: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects, Ramadan and the rest of the Creek Harbour calendar
paragraphs: Two things squeeze a Chemistry timetable in Dubai that have nothing to do with Chemistry. The first is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must also organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited.

Read that as timetable arithmetic. Those hours sit inside the same school week as Chemistry, and they are not optional for a Diploma student. It is a large part of why a DP2 student can have less Chemistry contact time than a parent assumes from the subject's weight in the diploma, and why evening tutoring so often ends up consolidating material the school week could not fit properly. For the mandatory subjects themselves, note that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring material for those subjects may be described.

The second squeeze is the UAE calendar itself. Ramadan shortens the school day and moves family routines later, and for most of our Creek Harbour families the practical answer is to shift weekday Chemistry sessions to after Iftar and lean harder on weekend mornings. Because there is no tutor commute involved, a post-Iftar slot is genuinely available rather than theoretically available. Winter and spring breaks, Eid holidays and the long summer all fall in places that interact badly with internal assessment deadlines, and families in this district travel more than most. A session timetable that follows the family rather than the address is worth more here than it would be in a district where nobody leaves.

sections.heading: The Chemistry investigation, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: This needs stating because the same search results that brought you here include services selling finished IB coursework at a published price. A parent three weeks from a school deadline, with a child who has not started, can talk themselves into that purchase quickly. It is the most damaging thing available in this market. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student's diploma rather than on the vendor's business.

What legitimate Chemistry tutoring looks like is specific. A tutor may teach experimental method and apparatus choice. A tutor may ask questions until a student narrows a vague research question themselves. A tutor may explain what each published criterion rewards and how marks are allocated across them. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and identify, in writing, which criterion is losing marks and why. A tutor may teach uncertainty treatment, graph choice and the arithmetic of error propagation that the report will need.

What a tutor may not do is choose the research question, supply data, write any section including the conclusion, edit a draft to completion, or hand over a template to be filled in, which is ghost-writing with extra steps. We also do not reproduce or circulate IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. If any provider offers your family something from the second list, that is the moment to walk away from them rather than to negotiate.
bullets: Permitted: method teaching, questioning the design, explaining criteria, written feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: choosing the question, supplying data, drafting, editing to completion, templates

sections.heading: Chemistry HL or SL, and what each route leaves open
paragraphs: Level choice is the decision with the longest shadow, and it is usually made in a single conversation during the term before DP1 begins. The honest position is that Chemistry HL is substantially more work than SL, not marginally more, and that the right answer depends on the degree route rather than on ambition in the abstract. A student who takes HL to keep options open and then loses points across three subjects has not kept options open.

The practical test is the prerequisite page of the courses your child might actually apply to. Medicine, dentistry, veterinary science, pharmacy, chemical engineering and most chemistry degrees commonly specify Chemistry at Higher Level, and many pair it with a second science or with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Biomedical and life-science routes vary more than families expect, with some accepting SL Chemistry alongside HL Biology. Engineering routes outside chemical engineering frequently prefer Physics HL and Maths AA HL, with Chemistry SL sufficient. These are prerequisite pages to read, not rules to infer.

For tutoring the level decision changes what a session looks like rather than whether one is needed. HL students need longer sessions to work full extended-response questions and review them properly; the additional higher-level content in energetics, equilibrium and organic is where the HL marks concentrate. SL students make faster progress in shorter sessions concentrating on definitions, command terms and the recurring calculation types. The table compares the two on the measures that matter when a family is deciding, rather than on the content lists a school prospectus already provides.

sections.heading: Starting from Creek Harbour, and what goes wrong when it does
paragraphs: The first thing we ask for is the school deadline sheet, which is unusual enough to explain. Every Dubai school sets its own internal assessment dates, and in this district two students in neighbouring towers are frequently on completely different Chemistry timelines. A mentoring block booked for the wrong month is money spent on the wrong month. Alongside it we ask for the school, the level, and one recently marked Chemistry script, because a marked paper locates the real problem in ten minutes where a description of it cannot.

Then a free trial lesson of about 45 minutes, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel if you stop there. The trial is diagnostic. The tutor works a real question with your child and afterwards tells you what they found, in specific terms, including the cases where the answer is that Chemistry is not the problem. It happens more often than you would think: a student failing Chemistry calculations is sometimes a student who needs three sessions on logarithms and indices, and we would rather say that than sell a term of Chemistry.

Failure modes are worth naming in advance. Sometimes the specialist your child needs is not free at the hour you want, and we offer a date rather than quietly substituting someone else. Sometimes the personality match is wrong, which is nobody's fault and is fixed by changing tutor at no extra cost rather than by persevering. And sometimes expectations do not match arithmetic: four sessions in April will not recover a year of unsecured foundations, and we will say so at the start rather than take the booking. No tutor can promise a grade, and we do not publish figures about outcomes that we cannot show you the method behind.

process.title: Send the school's deadline sheet
process.description: Dubai schools set their own internal assessment dates, and in Creek Harbour neighbouring students are often months apart. The deadline sheet tells us when a Chemistry investigation block needs to run. Without it we would be guessing, and a block timed for the wrong month changes nothing about the mark.

process.description: We schedule from when your child is actually through the door. For a Nad Al Sheba run that is about 4.30pm, for Sobha Hartland nearer 3.15pm. Getting this right at the start is what makes a slot survive thirty weeks instead of six.

process.title: Add one marked Chemistry script
process.description: A recent marked test with the teacher's annotations shows whether the loss is content, command terms, calculation method or timing. Those four have four different remedies, and a marked paper distinguishes them in minutes. A parent's description, however careful, usually cannot.

process.title: Meet the matched tutor on a free trial
process.description: About 45 minutes, live over video, no card details. The tutor works a real Chemistry problem with your child rather than presenting credentials, then tells you what they diagnosed in plain language, including the occasions when our view is that tutoring is not the right intervention.

process.description: One recurring weekly hour after the bus, or a weekend morning block, or both during an examination run. We send annotated whiteboards and worked solutions after each session so the work is reviewable. Timing shifts during Ramadan to post-Iftar and over the summer to follow travel.

process.title: Judge it on the next marked piece
process.description: Not on a feeling and not on a parent's sense of mood. If the next school test or investigation draft has not moved and the tutor cannot explain why in diagnosable terms, we change the tutor rather than extend the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around your actual afternoon
whyPoints.description: We set Chemistry slots from the bus return rather than the school bell, which in Creek Harbour means 5pm for most runs and 4.30pm for Sobha Hartland. A tutor crossing the Ras Al Khor approaches at 5pm is paid for that crossing whether anyone itemises it or not. A video lesson removes it and makes an evening slot as available as an afternoon one.
