sections.heading: Dubai Hills Estate, Arabian Ranches and Motor City: the same Chemistry problem with a different postcode
paragraphs: Set the communities side by side and the pattern is immediate. They do not differ in the Chemistry their children study, the campuses those children attend, or the topics that cost marks in February. They differ in commute. A Dubai Hills Estate family looking for Diploma Chemistry help and a Town Square family looking for the same thing are competing for the same handful of Group 4 specialists, and the Town Square family is competing with a longer drive attached to the offer.

The table below is built from where these communities actually send children to school and what the local tutoring supply looks like at Diploma level. The bus windows are indicative rather than a timetable; every campus runs its own routes and your school's transport office is the only reliable source. What matters is the shape: the further out the community, the later a weekday session can realistically start, and the thinner the pool of people who will teach it.

Read the final column carefully, because it is the point of the comparison. An earliest workable session of 17:30 is not a scheduling inconvenience; it is the reason a tutor who has to drive quotes more and arrives tired. Remove the drive and the same column reads the same in every row. That is the whole argument, and it does not require anybody to pretend that one of these communities is better served than another.

Families sometimes push back that a tutor who lives nearby will know the school. Occasionally true, and rarely decisive. What changes a Chemistry grade is whether the person in front of your child can take an unfamiliar data set apart under time pressure and explain where the mark scheme puts the marks. Proximity does not predict that, and in a city with 227 private schools running 17 curricula, local knowledge about one campus transfers badly to the next one.

sections.heading: What the current Diploma Chemistry course actually asks for
paragraphs: Diploma Chemistry is assessed on two external papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 carries short-response and extended-response questions. The investigation is one independent piece of practical work, written up by the student, marked by the school against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Higher Level and Standard Level share the same themes, with Higher Level going further into each rather than adding a separate topic list.

That structure matters because it tells you where tutoring hours pay back. A student who knows the content and loses marks on Paper 1B is not a student who needs more content; they need twenty data questions with the command term underlined before they touch a calculator. A student who writes fluent prose and scores poorly on Paper 2 extended response usually has never compared their own answer to a mark scheme line by line. These are different problems with different fixes, and buying generic Chemistry hours addresses neither reliably.

The table sets out the components and what each one tends to cost students. Confirm every weighting and duration against your child's current IB subject guide or with the school's DP coordinator before you plan around it: the IB revises subject guides on a cycle, and we do not publish assessment percentages we cannot show you a source for. What is stable, and what the table is really about, is the failure mode in each column three entry.

One recurring misunderstanding deserves naming. Parents often ask whether Higher Level Chemistry is 'the same course with harder exams'. It is not. The additional depth changes the kind of question that can be asked, so a student coasting at Standard Level pace through DP1 can meet Higher Level questions in DP2 and find the whole framing unfamiliar. Diagnosing that early is cheap. Diagnosing it after the mocks is not.

sections.heading: Where Chemistry marks go missing between October and the May session
paragraphs: The topics that cost Dubai students marks are predictable enough to list. Energetics is first: enthalpy cycles are drawn carelessly, signs are dropped, and a correct arithmetic answer arrives with the wrong sign attached. Equilibrium is second, because students learn to recite Le Chatelier and then cannot apply it to a question that changes two variables at once. Acids and bases is third, where the pH calculations are fine until a weak acid appears and the approximation is used without being stated.

Organic chemistry is the topic parents mention most often, and it is the one where the complaint is usually misdiagnosed. A student who says they cannot do organic chemistry is normally a student who has memorised individual reactions rather than learned to read a mechanism as a sequence of electron movements. Once the arrows mean something, the memorisation load collapses. That shift takes a handful of sessions with somebody who draws it properly, and it does not happen by doing more past papers alone.

Then there is the category that is not a topic at all. Significant figures, units, state symbols and the habit of answering the question that was asked rather than the question the student wishes had been asked. Across a full paper these are worth more than any single topic, and they are the cheapest marks in Chemistry to recover. We start here on almost every page of a first diagnostic, because it changes a grade boundary faster than new content does.

The timing matters. Between October of DP2 and the mocks, there is room to rebuild a topic properly. After the mocks, there is room to fix technique and to drill the question types that keep appearing. By April, the honest work is triage: identify the three highest-value gaps and leave the rest alone. A tutor who tells a Dubai Hills Estate family in April that everything can be covered is either misreading the calendar or selling hours.

sections.heading: Chemistry Higher Level and the medicine route from a Dubai school
paragraphs: A large share of the Diploma Chemistry Higher Level demand in these communities comes from students aiming at medicine, dentistry or pharmacy, in the UAE or abroad. The subject requirement is set by the receiving university, not by the school and not by us, and it varies enough that guessing is expensive. Some faculties ask for Chemistry at Higher Level specifically. Others accept Standard Level alongside a second science. Some admissions pages name a minimum subject grade rather than only a total.

The practical advice is unglamorous. Open the admissions page of each target university, find the Diploma entry requirements, and write the subject and level requirement into a single document before Year 11 ends. Where a UAE university is on the list, check what the Ministry of Education equivalency route requires as well, because recognition of the qualification and admission to the programme are two separate processes and families routinely conflate them. We describe both; we do not perform either, and no amount of tutoring is a substitute for a regulatory step.

Where Chemistry Higher Level is genuinely required, the tutoring question becomes a scheduling question. Higher Level Chemistry alongside Higher Level Biology or Higher Level Mathematics is a heavy combination, and the internal assessments for each land in overlapping windows. Students who plan the investigation calendar in DP1 cope; students who meet all three deadlines in the same fortnight of DP2 do not, regardless of how able they are. That is the single most useful thing an external tutor can do early, and it costs very little.

If Higher Level turns out not to be required, saying so is worth more than any revision session. Dropping from Higher Level to Standard Level is a decision with a last sensible date attached, set by the school rather than by the IB's deadlines, and it is a decision best taken on evidence rather than on nerve. We will give a view based on the student's written work and the published course demands. The school's DP coordinator makes the call.

sections.heading: What Chemistry tuition costs across these communities, and why crossing the road changes nothing
paragraphs: Start at the cheapest end, because that is where most families start. Online tutoring from university students and general platforms is published in Dubai from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that price the hour buys supervision and homework company. It very rarely buys somebody who has taught the current Diploma Chemistry course, and for a DP2 student with a data-question problem it is money spent on the wrong thing rather than money saved.

Move up one band and the figures change character. A qualified subject tutor working online is published in the AED 150 to 300 range; Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond. The premium end is thinner and louder: BartyED publishes AED 650 for its named tutors. Every one of those numbers was read from the provider's own page in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

In-home one-to-one is quoted separately because it is a different product. Bestimate reports AED 180 to 350 for a home visit and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 500, with travel inside the figure. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits. Notice what the second number is buying: roughly the same teaching time, plus a car.

Here is the part that answers the comparison this page is built on. None of those bands moves because a family lives in Dubai Hills Estate rather than Mudon. The hourly figure for online teaching is identical across every community in the table above, because there is no distance in it. The in-home figure is the only one that responds to geography, and it responds by going up as the drive gets longer. A parent in Remraam being quoted at the top of the in-home band is not being overcharged; they are being charged for Al Khail Road at six in the evening. Set against Dubai's school fees - KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion - a targeted block of specialist hours is a small line in a large budget, and it is the line most under a family's own control.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a group class: the arithmetic from a Dubailand villa
paragraphs: Put the three delivery options next to each other and the choice stops being about preference. An online hour starts when your child sits down. An in-home hour starts when the tutor arrives, which in this part of Dubai means twenty-five to forty-five minutes of Al Khail Road or Umm Suqeim Road each way at the time a Diploma student is free. Somebody pays for that time, and the published in-home bands show who.

The group option is worth taking seriously rather than dismissing. A small class of two to four students revising shared content, led by somebody competent, is a reasonable purchase for a confident student in the final term. It is a poor purchase for a student whose problem is specific, because the whole value of one-to-one Chemistry teaching is that the hour is spent on that student's actual gap. None of the providers we researched publishes a per-student group rate, so ask for the figure in writing before agreeing to anything.

The table compares the three on the terms that matter from a Dubailand address, and it is the clearest statement of why IB Gram runs the model it does. We deliver one-to-one lessons live online, to Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we operate only in India. That restriction is not a limitation we are hiding; it is what lets a family in Mudon work with the same Chemistry specialist a family in Dubai Hills Estate works with, at the same rate, in the same week.

One practical note on making online Chemistry work. The student needs a device with a real keyboard, a stable connection, a pen and paper for working, and a quiet room with the door shut. Chemistry involves drawing, so a cheap graphics tablet or a phone used as a document camera earns its cost within a month. Nothing else is required, and nobody needs laboratory apparatus at home: the investigation is done at school, under the school's supervision, which is where the IB expects it to happen.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the line a Chemistry tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is the component where good intentions cause real damage. It must be the student's own work. The IB's academic honesty rules treat work produced by somebody else as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the adult who helped. Two of the competitor pages we examined while researching this cluster sell completed internal assessments outright. We will not, and a family should treat any offer of that kind as a reason to walk away rather than a convenience.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and it is worth setting out precisely so that nobody has to guess. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria and what each one rewards. A tutor can discuss whether a proposed research question is answerable in the time and with the apparatus available, and can say plainly when it is too broad. A tutor can teach uncertainty treatment, error analysis, graphing conventions and how to evaluate a method. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it, in the same way a teacher gives feedback.

What a tutor may not do is write any part of it, redraft sentences into their own prose, generate the data, or hand over a structure that the student fills in. The distinction a parent can apply without knowing the rules in detail is this one: after the session, is the document still something the student could explain, defend and reproduce? If yes, the help was teaching. If no, it was something else, and the student is carrying the risk. Your child's subject teacher is the supervisor of record, and the school sets the internal deadlines; external support works around those, never instead of them.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to Theory of Knowledge, and families should expect it to be stated rather than implied. We put it on the page because the alternative - a vague promise of 'IA support' - is exactly how students end up in front of a school's academic honesty panel. A Chemistry investigation coached properly in DP1, with a narrow question and a clean uncertainty analysis, is worth more than a polished document the student cannot account for.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside Diploma Chemistry
paragraphs: Families arriving in Dubai Hills Estate from abroad are often surprised in their first August. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 the date for schools whose year begins in April. That means Diploma Chemistry is being studied alongside subjects that do not appear on any IB transcript and still occupy real timetable hours.

The organisational rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any tutoring material for those subjects may be described. We teach Arabic as a language and will say frankly where that boundary sits.

Why this belongs on a Chemistry page: because it is part of the timetable arithmetic. A DP2 student carrying six Diploma subjects, the core, and mandatory UAE subject hours has less discretionary time than the brochure implies, and a tutoring plan that ignores that will be abandoned by November. We would rather set one realistic weekly session that survives the whole year than three that collapse in the second month.

sections.heading: Starting Chemistry support from Dubai Hills Estate, with the limits stated
paragraphs: The process is short. You tell us the campus, the level, the exam session and what the last written work looked like. We find a Diploma Chemistry specialist whose availability overlaps your child's free evenings in Gulf Standard Time. The first session is a trial, and it is spent on a timed past paper rather than on introductions, because that is the only way to find out what is actually wrong. After it you get a written note naming the specific gaps and the number of hours they plausibly take.

Now the limits, because a page that lists only capabilities is not useful. Diploma Chemistry Higher Level specialists are the scarcest category we recruit for, and in any given week the person best matched to your child may not have an evening slot in the Gulf window. When that happens we say so and offer the options honestly: wait for a slot, take a different specialist, or take a weekend session instead of a weekday one. We would rather lose a booking than place a general science tutor on a Higher Level Chemistry problem and let a family find out in March.

A word on permits, since parents in Dubai ask and few pages answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time on the ministry's own service page. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Ask any tutor you consider, from any provider, whether they hold it.

Finally, the thing we will not do. We will not promise a grade, a point total or an improvement, and you should treat any tutor who does as a warning rather than a reassurance. What a good Chemistry tutor can promise is that the hour is spent on the right thing, that the work is marked honestly, and that you will be told early if the plan is not working. For a family in Dubai Hills Estate, Arabian Ranches, Motor City or anywhere else on these roads, that is the offer, and it is the same offer in every one of them.

process.title: Tell us the campus, the level and the session
process.description: A short form: which school, Standard or Higher Level, which exam session, and what the most recent piece of marked Chemistry work looked like. The last part is the most useful, because a marked past paper tells a specialist more in two minutes than a description does in ten.

process.title: We match a Diploma Chemistry specialist
process.description: We look for somebody who teaches the current course, at your child's level, with an evening slot that works in Gulf Standard Time after the bus reaches Dubai Hills Estate. If nobody suitable is free that week, we tell you rather than substituting a general science tutor.

process.title: A trial lesson spent on a past paper
process.description: The first session is free and it is a diagnosis. The student works a timed section while the tutor watches where the method breaks, then they mark it together against the published criteria. Families who have sat through introductory sessions elsewhere notice the difference immediately.

process.title: A written plan with hours attached

process.description: Lessons run to a schedule you set. Written answers are marked between sessions and the errors are logged by syllabus topic, so the final term's revision is aimed at the topics that are actually costing marks rather than at the whole course.

whyPoints.description: Choosing by distance narrows the pool to whoever will drive to your community. Choosing by subject and level widens it to every Diploma Chemistry teacher available. faqs.question: Does an IB Chemistry tutor cost more in Dubai Hills Estate than in Motor City or Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Not for online teaching. The published Dubai bands - roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB specialist - contain no travel, so they read identically in every community on these roads. The figure that does move is the in-home one. Bestimate reports AED 180 to 350 for a home visit and independent tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 500, and the longer the drive from Al Barsha out to DAMAC Hills or Remraam, the closer a quote sits to the top of that band. You are paying for Al Khail Road, not for Chemistry.

faqs.question: Which campuses near Dubai Hills Estate actually run IB Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Not the ones inside the community. Dubai Hills Estate families reach Diploma Chemistry at the Al Barsha and Al Quoz IB campuses, with Sobha Hartland and the Al Khail schools in the same travel ring. Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes, which widens the choice for younger children. Before you rely on any list, including ours, check the campus's current programme offer and its latest KHDA inspection outcome on the regulator's own site. School programme lists change between academic years more often than parents expect.

faqs.question: My child is at a British-curriculum school in this area and wants Chemistry HL. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: Only if the campus runs the Diploma. Many British-curriculum schools around Dubai Hills Estate take students through IGCSE and then into A Level, where Chemistry exists but Higher Level does not, because Higher Level is an IB designation. Families who want Diploma Chemistry specifically usually move campus at sixteen, and that decision is effectively made two years earlier in the Year 9 option block. If your child is in Year 9 or 10 now, ask both the current school and the target IB campus what subject combination each can actually timetable.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry papers does a Diploma student sit, and what is each worth?
faqs.answer: Two external papers plus one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 has a multiple-choice section and a data-based section; Paper 2 carries short-response and extended-response questions; the investigation is independent practical work written up by the student and marked by the school against published criteria. Higher Level papers run longer than Standard Level ones. We deliberately do not publish the percentage weightings here, because the IB revises subject guides on a cycle and we cannot show you a verifiable source for a current figure. Your child's subject guide or DP coordinator can confirm all of it in a minute.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter understand the theory but lose marks on the data question?
faqs.answer: Because the data-based question tests a different skill from the one she has been revising. It presents unfamiliar data and asks a precisely worded question about it, and most students answer by describing what the graph shows rather than by addressing the command term. The fix is mechanical and fast: twenty past data questions, with the command term underlined and the mark allocation read before any calculation begins. Most students move several marks within a month on this alone, which is why a diagnostic session starts with a timed paper rather than a conversation about confidence.

faqs.question: Is organic chemistry worth paying for separately?
faqs.answer: Usually it is worth paying for properly rather than separately. Students who say they cannot do organic chemistry have nearly always memorised individual reactions instead of learning to read a mechanism as a sequence of electron movements. Once the arrows mean something, the memorisation load drops sharply and the topic stops being a special case. That shift takes a few sessions with somebody who draws mechanisms properly on screen, and it does not happen by grinding through more past papers alone. Treat it as a teaching problem, not a revision-volume problem.

faqs.question: Can an IB Chemistry tutor look at the scientific investigation before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can explain what each assessment criterion rewards, say plainly whether a research question is answerable with the apparatus and time available, teach uncertainty treatment and graphing conventions, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write any part of it, redraft it into their own prose, or supply the data. The test a parent can apply is simple: after the session, could the student explain and defend every line? If not, the help went too far and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Chemistry tutor to a villa in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Dubai Hills Estate families are one-to-one and live online, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. That is a deliberate choice rather than a gap. It means a family in Mudon or Remraam works with the same Diploma Chemistry specialist as a family two minutes from the Al Barsha campuses, at the same rate, without anybody pricing forty minutes of evening traffic into the hour.

faqs.question: What time can a Chemistry session start if the school bus reaches Dubai Hills Estate at 16:10?
faqs.answer: A 16:45 start works for most families, and 17:00 is the common choice once a snack and a change of clothes are accounted for. Later than 18:30 tends to be counterproductive for quantitative work; a tired DP2 student makes arithmetic errors that look like knowledge gaps and waste the hour. Sessions are booked to Gulf Standard Time, so there is no conversion to get wrong. Families further out in Town Square or Remraam usually settle on 17:15 or 17:30, which is one of the few things the community genuinely changes.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL required for medicine at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: That is set by the receiving university, not by the school or by us, and it varies. Some faculties specify Chemistry at Higher Level; others accept Standard Level alongside a second science; some name a minimum subject grade rather than only a total. Open each target university's admissions page and write the subject and level requirement down before Year 11 ends. Where a UAE institution is on the list, also check the Ministry of Education equivalency route, because recognition of the qualification and admission to the programme are separate processes. Tutoring is not a requirement of either.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry sessions a week does a DP2 student here usually book?
faqs.answer: One session a week carries most students through DP2 if it starts early and the written work between sessions actually gets done. Two a week makes sense in the final term, or when Chemistry is one of two subjects in trouble and both need separate attention. Three is rarely a Chemistry decision; it is usually a timetable problem in disguise. A DP2 student in Dubai is carrying six subjects, the core, and mandatory UAE subject hours, and a plan that ignores that gets abandoned by November rather than adjusted.

faqs.question: Does my child need laboratory apparatus at home for online Chemistry lessons?
faqs.answer: No. The scientific investigation is carried out at school under the school's supervision, which is where the IB expects practical work to happen, and no legitimate tutoring arrangement moves it into a family kitchen. What helps at home is modest: a device with a real keyboard, a stable connection, pen and paper for working, and a quiet room. Chemistry involves drawing, so a cheap graphics tablet or a phone used as a document camera earns its cost within a month because the tutor can see the working as it is written.

faqs.question: Our family moved from an American-curriculum school. How far behind is the Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Rarely behind in content and often behind in assessment style. Students arriving from an American programme usually know more descriptive chemistry than expected and much less about how the Diploma asks questions: command terms, mark allocations, the data-based question format, and the expectation that an answer earns marks line by line. A diagnostic session on a past paper identifies which it is within the hour. The content gaps that do appear cluster in mole calculations and energetics, and both are a fixed number of hours rather than an open commitment.

faqs.question: Does a Chemistry tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit before charging us?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time on the ministry's own service page. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so nobody should quote you an amount.

faqs.question: Will Arabic and Islamic Education still be timetabled alongside Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes for both groups. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Chemistry plan this matters as timetable arithmetic: the discretionary hours a DP2 student has are fewer than the subject list suggests.

faqs.question: What should the first three Chemistry sessions produce?
faqs.answer: A timed past paper marked honestly, a written list of the specific gaps in priority order, and an estimate of the hours each one plausibly needs. If the honest answer is four hours rather than forty, the note should say four. By the end of the third session the student should have changed one concrete habit - underlining the command term, stating units, checking the sign on an enthalpy cycle - and have evidence it moved marks. Anything vaguer than that after three sessions is a reason to ask harder questions rather than to buy more hours.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-hills-.closingHeading: The same answer in Dubai Hills Estate, Arabian Ranches and everywhere between
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-hills-.closingBody: The comparison that opened this page closes it. Take the drive out and the answer is identical in all of them: a Diploma Chemistry specialist, one-to-one, live online, timed to Gulf Standard Time, on an evening that fits after the bus gets home. The first session is a free trial and it is spent on a past paper, so you will know within the hour whether this is the right help. If it is not, we will tell you that too.

intro.heading: Chemistry marks are decided by precision, and precision is teachable
paragraphs: Dubai Internet City is a workplace rather than a school district. It is a free zone in Al Sufouh housing the regional offices of large technology companies, bounded by Dubai Knowledge Park, Dubai Media City and the Red Line of the Metro, with residential supply in The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, Al Sufouh and the Marina towers. Most enquiries from this postcode come from a parent at work during the day, about a child at school somewhere else, which has a practical effect on how support gets arranged: the person organising it is not the person in the room at 18:00.

What those enquiries have in common is a question about precision rather than about content. The student understands the chemistry and the marks are not there. In marked Diploma scripts that gap almost always traces to one of four things: a bonding model held as categories rather than as explanations, an enthalpy sign applied by guesswork, an organic mechanism drawn with the arrow starting in the wrong place, or an equilibrium answer that recites a rule instead of arguing a position. None of those is a gap in knowledge, and all four are visible in a single marked paper.

The current chemistry guide organises content under Structure and Reactivity, three topics each, with HL material interleaved inside the topics rather than appended at the end. That structure rewards students who understand why a property follows from a model, and it punishes students who learned the properties as a list. It is also why a chemistry problem in the second year of the course frequently has its origin in the first: bonding explains reactivity, so a soft foundation in Structure 2 produces apparently random failures much later.

The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent of the grade under the current guide and is the component families most often ask for the wrong kind of help with. The line is simple and we keep it on every page. A tutor may teach how a research question is narrowed, how variables are controlled, how uncertainty is estimated, how an analysis is structured and how an evaluation argues. A tutor may read a draft the student wrote and reply with the questions an examiner would ask. A tutor may not write it, draft a section, rewrite the text or supply data. One provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments; the consequences of buying one land on the student.

IB Gram delivers chemistry support to Dubai families online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. For a household in this corridor the online format solves a specific problem rather than a general one: a parent who finishes work in the free zone at 18:00 does not need to be home to let a tutor in, and the session can start the moment the student is ready.

sections.heading: What a Diploma chemistry question is actually asking for
paragraphs: Chemistry papers are written in a controlled vocabulary and marked literally. The verb at the front of the question sets both the content and the length of the answer that will score. State wants a fact or a value with units and nothing else. Outline wants the key points briefly. Explain wants a chain of reasoning in which each link earns a mark. Deduce wants a conclusion visibly drawn from given information. Determine wants working and then a value with units. Describe wants an account without the reasoning, and compare wants both sides addressed within each point of comparison.

Students lose marks in both directions. Writing an explanation for a question that asked for a statement earns nothing extra and costs minutes that the back of the paper needed. Writing a statement where an explanation was wanted earns nothing at all. Across a full paper a capable student can surrender a noticeable number of marks without a single gap in chemistry, which is the most frustrating way to lose a grade and the easiest to repair. Three or four sessions with the mark scheme open is usually enough to change the habit permanently.

The second layer is the quantity actually requested. A question asking for a change in enthalpy and receiving an enthalpy is wrong. A question asking for a concentration and receiving a number of moles is wrong. A question specifying units, or a precision, or a particular form of an answer, means it. These are reading errors rather than chemistry errors, and the only reliable fix is deliberate practice at reading the stem twice before the pen moves.

The practical method is narrow. Take the student's own answers, set the published mark scheme beside them, and identify what the scheme awarded that the answer did not supply. Within a few sessions a student can predict the required answer shape from the verb and the mark allocation alone, which transfers to every question in every paper and to the other sciences as well.
bullets: The verb sets both content and length; read it before the chemistry
Match the number of scoring points to the mark allocation
Check the quantity requested: enthalpy change, not enthalpy
Units and precision are instructions, not suggestions

sections.heading: Bonding and structure: the model everything downstream depends on
paragraphs: Most apparently random chemistry failures in the second year of the Diploma trace back to bonding. A student who learned bonding as a set of categories, with properties attached to each as a list, can answer any question that names the category. The same student fails when a question describes a substance and expects the bonding to be inferred, or when a property has to be predicted for something unfamiliar. That is not a memory problem. It is a model problem, and it is repaired by working in the other direction: from structure to property, repeatedly, until the reasoning is automatic.

The chain to establish is short. What particles are present, what forces act between them, how strong those forces are relative to thermal energy, and therefore what the melting point, conductivity, solubility and hardness should look like. A student who can run that chain forwards can answer questions nobody has seen before. A student who cannot is dependent on the question being familiar, which is exactly what examination questions are designed not to be.

The table sets out the main bonding and structure types with the properties that follow and the error we see most often for each. It is not a revision list to memorise; it is a check on whether the reasoning works. The useful exercise with a student is to cover the property column, describe a substance, and ask them to produce the properties with the reason attached. Where they can only recall, the model is not there yet.

HL material deserves a specific note. Because the guide interleaves HL content inside each topic, HL bonding material tends to be taught at the end of the topic and then not revisited. It is the single most frequently under-rehearsed HL content we encounter, and the fix is organisational rather than intellectual: list it separately in the revision plan so it cannot be skipped by default.

sections.heading: Energetics: sign conventions, and why they cost so many marks
paragraphs: Energetics is where chemistry stops forgiving carelessness. The sign of an enthalpy change is not a decoration; it is the answer. A negative value means energy was released to the surroundings and a positive value means energy was absorbed from them, and a student who determines the magnitude correctly and attaches the wrong sign has produced a wrong answer that looks almost right. Examiners apply this strictly, and they are correct to, because the sign is the chemistry.

The recurring confusion is about perspective. A reaction that releases energy warms its surroundings, so the temperature of the solution rises while the enthalpy change of the reaction is negative. Students who have memorised rise means positive get this wrong every time, and no amount of additional content teaching helps because the error is in the frame rather than in the facts. The repair is to insist, in every calculation, that the student states whose energy is being described before writing a sign.

The second recurring issue is which mass is used in a calorimetry calculation. The mass of solution absorbing the energy, not the mass of the substance reacting, and a student who uses the wrong one produces an answer out by an order of magnitude without noticing. A habit of estimating the expected size of an answer before calculating catches this, and estimating is a skill worth teaching in its own right because it catches many other errors too.

Beyond the arithmetic, energetics is where the reasoning about spontaneity and driving forces begins, and at HL that reasoning becomes substantial. Students who treated the calculations as arithmetic exercises in the first year arrive at this material without the conceptual foundation it assumes, which is another instance of the same pattern: a second-year difficulty with a first-year cause.
bullets: State whose energy is being described before writing any sign

sections.heading: The organic sequence: functional groups, mechanisms and the arrow that starts in the wrong place
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where notation marks concentrate. A mechanism is a diagram that makes a claim, and the claim is made by where the arrow starts. An arrow drawn from an atom rather than from the electron pair it actually comes from is a different and wrong claim, and it is marked as such. Students find this harsh. It is also entirely mechanical to fix, which makes it one of the better returns available in the subject: a drill at the start of each session for a few weeks, and the habit holds.

The second organic issue is sequence rather than notation. Functional group chemistry is a map of what converts into what, under what conditions, and students who learn individual reactions in isolation cannot answer a question that asks for a two-step route. Building the map explicitly, as a diagram the student draws from memory rather than reads, is the difference between answering a familiar reaction question and answering a synthesis question. The map is small enough to be drawn from memory, and students who can do that find the whole topic shrinks.

The third is structural drawing. An organic structure drawn ambiguously, with a bond that could be read two ways or a group positioned unclearly, is marked on what the examiner can actually see. Teaching a student to draw deliberately slowly, with enough space, is unglamorous and it recovers marks. The same applies to naming: systematic names follow rules, and a student who guesses rather than applies them loses marks on questions they understood.

The table below maps the functional groups to the reaction types and the specific notation trap for each. Use it as a diagnostic rather than a revision list: a student who recognises their own recurring error in the right-hand column has found the next fortnight of work.

sections.heading: Equilibrium, acids and bases: arguing a position rather than reciting a rule
paragraphs: Equilibrium questions ask for an argument and most students supply a slogan. A change in conditions shifts a position, and a scoring answer names the change, states the direction of the shift, and explains why that direction follows. Students who have memorised the principle can usually state the direction and cannot explain it, which earns part of the mark and leaves the rest. The repair is to require three sentences in a fixed order every time, until the structure survives without prompting.

Acids and bases are where the arithmetic and the reasoning meet, and where students who are shaky on logarithms suffer twice. A concentration becomes a pH through a logarithmic relationship, and a student without fluency in logarithms is working two problems at once under examination pressure. This is one of the clearest cases where a chemistry difficulty has a mathematical cause, and where the honest recommendation is a short block of maths work rather than more chemistry teaching.

At HL the material extends into buffer behaviour and the reasoning about weak acids and bases, and here the precision demands rise again. A buffer explanation that says the buffer resists change has said nothing; one that identifies which species consumes added acid and which consumes added base has answered the question. We teach these as named arguments with named participants, because that is what the mark scheme is looking for.

The thread running through this section and the previous three is the same. Chemistry at Diploma level rewards reasoning that can be followed on paper. The student who writes the chain down scores; the student who knows it and compresses it into a conclusion does not. Most of what a chemistry tutor usefully does is make the chain visible, repeatedly, until writing it out is the student's default rather than an instruction they have to remember.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course: chemistry for students who changed school or system
paragraphs: The free zones in this part of Dubai have a relocation rhythm, and the consequence for chemistry is a steady stream of students joining a Diploma course part-way through from A Level, AP, CBSE or a national curriculum. These students are rarely uniformly behind. They arrive unevenly: ahead on some topics, absent on others, and frequently strong in calculation and weak in the reasoning the Diploma rewards, or the reverse. A general revision programme is the wrong purchase for them and it is what they are usually sold.

The right first step is an audit. One session, working through the specification topic by topic, establishing what was covered, to what depth, and whether the HL extensions were included. That produces a short written list of real gaps rather than an impression of being behind, and it typically reveals three or four items rather than a syllabus. It also prevents weeks of teaching material the student already holds, which is the most common waste in this situation.

The second step is comparing that list against the new school's teaching order, because what matters is not only what is missing but when the class will need it. A gap in a topic the department covered last term is urgent. A gap in a topic the department has not reached is something to time deliberately. That comparison requires the scheme of work, which is a routine request to a head of department and changes the quality of the plan substantially.

It is a starting hypothesis for the audit rather than a conclusion, because individual schools vary far more than curricula do. Students arriving from any system should be assessed on their own script rather than on their previous curriculum's reputation.

sections.heading: A free-zone household: the Metro, the working day and when sessions fit
paragraphs: The scheduling problem in this corridor is different from a residential neighbourhood's. Internet City is where the parent is, and the student is in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, The Greens or the Marina. That means the person arranging the tutoring is often unavailable at the hour it happens, which changes what the arrangement has to provide: written session notes rather than a doorstep conversation, a fixed slot that does not need confirming each week, and a clear record of what was covered.

The Red Line of the Metro serves this district and the tram runs through the Marina side, which matters less for tutoring than it does for school runs, but it shapes the afternoon. Students travelling back from Al Barsha or Jumeirah reach home across the same hours the free zone empties, and a session starting before 17:30 competes with that. For Marina and JBR students the exit is slower still. Online removes the journey entirely, which is the single largest reason blocks here complete rather than fragment.

What the student needs at their end is small: a hard surface, squared paper for graph work, their own calculator rather than a phone, the data booklet open, and headphones so an apartment with other people in it is not part of the session. The camera is angled at the page, because watching the working appear is the whole diagnostic method. For a parent who cannot be present, the recording and the written note are what substitute for having been in the room.

Ramadan shifts the pattern for a few weeks and Dubai schools adjust hours. We agree the revised timetable before the month starts, usually fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work set between them. Where a parent's own working hours change during the month, the session notes matter more than usual, and we write them accordingly.

sections.heading: The investigation, the Extended Essay, and the line we do not cross
paragraphs: Two pieces of assessed chemistry writing are produced under supervision: the scientific investigation and, for students who choose the subject, the Extended Essay. Both are the student's own work and both attract offers of help that cross a line. We state the line on every page because stating it is one of the few reliable ways a parent can tell providers apart in this market.

A tutor may teach how a research question is narrowed until it is answerable with available equipment and time. A tutor may teach how variables are identified and controlled, how uncertainty is estimated and propagated, how data is presented, how an analysis is structured, and how an evaluation identifies which limitation actually mattered rather than listing apologies. A tutor may read a draft the student wrote and respond with the questions an examiner would ask next. All of that is teaching.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, draft a section, rewrite the student's sentences into better ones, supply data, or provide a previous student's work as a template. One provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a published price. Buying that is an academic-malpractice trigger under the International Baccalaureate's own rules, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. We do not do it and we will not be asked twice.

Practically, the most common cause of a weak investigation is not weak writing but a research question that cannot be answered with school apparatus in the time available. The second is a data set too thin for the analysis attempted. Both are planning failures, both are cheap to prevent and expensive to rescue, and both are addressed before any data is collected. The school's internal deadlines are the dates the plan is built around, so we ask for them in writing at the start.

process.title: Send a marked script and the level
process.description: A recent marked paper tells us more in twenty minutes than a description does in a week. We are looking for which of four things is costing the marks: a bonding model that is not there, enthalpy sign errors, mechanism notation, or command-term length. Those four lead to four different plans and three of them are short.

process.title: Free trial lesson on real questions
process.description: The first session is free and runs on past-paper questions drawn from your child's own weak area rather than on a conversation about services. The tutor watches the working appear, which is where precision failures show themselves. A short written note follows, naming what is wrong and in what order to fix it, and it is yours regardless.

process.title: Ask the department for the scheme of work
process.description: The teaching order matters more than the guide's sequence, because a tutor working out of step with the class is competing rather than supporting. For a mid-course arrival this document is what turns an audit into a timetable, since it shows which gaps are urgent and which can be timed deliberately.

process.title: Fix a slot and accept written notes instead of doorsteps
process.description: One weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, set after the return from school rather than inside it. Because the parent in this corridor is often at work when the session runs, every lesson produces a written note of what was covered and what was set, and sessions are recorded. That record replaces the conversation a home visit would have provided.

process.title: Re-mark at week four and change course if needed
process.description: A second paper is sat and marked at week four and compared with the first. If the error pattern has not moved, we change approach or tutor rather than defending either. If the evidence says the gap is maths rather than chemistry, we say that too, because a term of chemistry teaching will not fix a logarithm problem.

whyPoints.title: Precision taught as a skill, not as a reminder
whyPoints.description: Notation drills, sign-convention routines and command-term discipline are built into the start of every session rather than mentioned once. These are the marks a capable chemistry student is actually losing, and because the fixes are mechanical they hold under examination conditions.

whyPoints.title: The bonding model rebuilt where it is missing
whyPoints.description: Apparently random second-year failures usually trace to a bonding model held as categories. We rebuild the chain from particles and forces to properties, and test it on unfamiliar substances rather than familiar ones, which is what examination questions are designed to do.

whyPoints.title: Mid-course arrivals audited before anything is taught
whyPoints.description: Relocation into this corridor is common and transfers arrive unevenly rather than uniformly behind. One audit session produces a short written gap list, which is cheaper and more accurate than a general revision programme sold on the assumption of broad weakness.

whyPoints.title: Built for a parent who is at work
whyPoints.description: Written notes after every session, recordings, a fixed slot that never needs reconfirming, and an explicit record of work set. The person organising tutoring in this district is usually not the person at home at 18:00, and the arrangement is designed around that.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We coach the investigation and the Extended Essay and we write neither. In a market where completed internal assessments are advertised at a price, publishing the limit is more useful to a parent than any claim about quality.

faqs.question: What does an IB chemistry tutor cost for a family working in Dubai Internet City?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more, and one premium provider publishing AED 650. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai rate table run about AED 600-1,200 for mid-band weekly support and AED 1,000-2,000 or more in an examination year. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour because the journey is inside the fee. Those are market figures with their sources attached rather than our price list; we quote after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our home if we live near the free zone?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we offer only in India. Chemistry sessions here are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. In this district that suits the household rather than inconveniencing it: the parent organising the tutoring is often still at work when the session runs, so a fixed slot, written session notes and a recording are more useful than a doorbell. Nothing is lost to traffic on the way in or the way out either.

faqs.question: Why do my child's chemistry errors look random across different topics?
faqs.answer: Usually because the bonding model is held as categories rather than as explanations. A student who learned bonding types with their properties attached as lists can answer any question that names the type, and fails whenever a substance is described and the bonding has to be inferred. The failures then appear scattered across topics because the cause is upstream of all of them. The repair runs in the other direction: from particles and forces to properties, tested on unfamiliar substances, until the chain is automatic. It takes a few weeks and it fixes a lot at once.

faqs.question: My child gets the right enthalpy number and the wrong sign. How is that fixed?
faqs.answer: By insisting that they state whose energy is being described before writing anything. A reaction releasing energy warms the surrounding solution, so the temperature rises while the enthalpy change of the reaction is negative. Students who memorised rise means positive get this wrong every time, and extra content teaching does nothing because the error is in the frame rather than in the facts. We also build the habit of estimating the expected magnitude first, which catches the related error of using the mass of the reacting substance instead of the mass of the solution.

faqs.question: How strictly are organic mechanism arrows marked?
faqs.answer: Strictly, because the arrow is the claim. An arrow must start from the electron pair that actually moves, so one drawn from a carbon atom rather than from a double bond, or from a nucleophile without its lone pair shown, is making a different and incorrect statement. Examiners mark what the diagram says. Students find this harsh and it is also entirely mechanical to fix: a short drill at the start of each session for a few weeks, with the student redrawing their own mechanisms, and the habit holds. It is one of the better returns available in the subject.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor can teach your child how to narrow a research question until it is answerable, how to read and evaluate sources, how to structure an argument, how to present data and how to handle a critical evaluation. A tutor can read a draft your child wrote and respond with the questions a supervisor or examiner would ask next. A tutor cannot write any part of it, draft a section, rewrite sentences into better ones or supply data. The essay is supervised in school, and the supervisor is the authority on what support is permitted in your child's case.

faqs.question: Our family relocated to Dubai mid-course. Where do you start?
faqs.answer: With an audit rather than with teaching. One session goes through the specification topic by topic, establishing what the previous school covered, to what depth, and whether HL extensions were included, then compares that with the new department's scheme of work. Transfers almost never arrive uniformly behind; they arrive unevenly, and the audit usually produces three or four real gaps rather than a syllabus. That is a far cheaper and more accurate starting point than a general revision programme, which is what students in this situation are most often sold.

faqs.question: Is a chemistry problem sometimes actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Often, and acids and bases is the clearest case. Converting a concentration to a pH requires logarithmic fluency, and a student without it is solving two problems at once under time pressure. Rate questions, equilibrium constants and energetics all sit on similar ground. When a marked script shows the chemistry reasoning intact and the arithmetic collapsing, the honest recommendation is a short block of maths work rather than more chemistry teaching. We say so when we see it, because selling chemistry sessions to fix a logarithm gap wastes a term.

faqs.question: How much extra content does HL Chemistry carry over SL?
faqs.answer: The HL course covers the same six topics under Structure and Reactivity with additional material inside each, so the difference is depth and rehearsal rather than a separate syllabus. The practical consequence is scheduling: HL content sits at the end of a topic and the class usually moves on before it is practised, which is why HL extensions are the most frequently under-rehearsed material we meet. A revision plan that lists HL items on their own lines, and revisits them deliberately, removes most of the problem without any extra teaching.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai Internet City teach Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The provision closest to the free zone sits in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, with a mix of full IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools offering the Diploma or A Level at sixth form. Rather than choose by reputation, ask the school two things: how many sets run HL Chemistry, and what the department's scheme of work looks like across the two years. The first tells you whether your child will have peers working on the same HL material; the second tells any tutor how to sequence support. We name schools on this page as context only and claim no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: What does a session actually look like for a student in The Greens or Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: The student sits at a hard surface with squared paper, their own calculator, the data booklet open and headphones on, with the camera angled at the page rather than the face. The tutor watches the working appear, which is where precision errors become visible as they happen. Mechanisms are drawn live on a shared whiteboard and can be rebuilt as many times as needed. Sessions are recorded, so an organic mechanism can be re-watched in the final term. A written note follows each session, which matters because the parent is often still at work.

faqs.question: How do you avoid teaching the same thing the school is teaching badly?
faqs.answer: By working from the department's scheme of work rather than from the guide's sequence. If the class is three weeks into the organic sequence, we support that, and we do not open equilibrium because it happens to be next in a textbook. Where the school's coverage of a topic has genuinely left a gap, we teach it from the model up rather than repeating the same explanation louder. The written coverage map we keep is the document that makes this visible, and parents can read it without needing to know any chemistry.

faqs.question: Which session do UAE Diploma students sit, and how should we plan around it?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the International Baccalaureate's own site is the authoritative source and should be checked directly or through the school's IB coordinator. For planning, the dates that shape a student's term are usually internal: the school's own deadlines for the investigation and the Extended Essay, which generally fall well before anything external. Build the plan around those, keep the heaviest coursework weeks clear of the mock series, and confirm every external date with the school.

faqs.question: What if the HL chemistry tutor we need is not free this term?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting a generalist. SL and mainstream HL matching is usually quick. Narrower requests, such as a specific HL extension or heavy mechanism work close to the papers, draw on a smaller group, and the honest options are a different time, a short wait for the right person, or a script-marking clinic in the meantime so the weeks still produce something. We also tell you where a tutor is based before you book. Filling a specialist slot with whoever is available is how families pay to be told what they already knew.

intro.heading: Chemistry money is spent late, broadly, and at the wrong rate
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station towards Expo City. Two IB schools and a British-curriculum school sit inside the district, with most secondary students travelling out to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan or Dubai South.

Chemistry has a distinctive spending pattern in this market, and it is not a flattering one. Families hire late, usually in the second term of DP2 when internal assessment deadlines and mocks have collided. They hire broadly, asking for chemistry rather than for a component. And they frequently hire at a premium rate for work that does not need one. Each of those three decisions multiplies the cost of the same outcome.

The subject does not require that. Chemistry mark loss is unusually concentrated, which means it is unusually cheap to fix once named. Organic mechanisms at Higher Level account for the largest single block, four to six sessions. Energetics sign conventions, which invalidate whole Hess cycles, take two. Equilibrium explanation that restates the shift instead of explaining it takes two or three. Weak acid calculations where strong acid arithmetic has been applied by habit take two or three.

Then there is the investigation at 20 per cent of the grade, where the cost profile inverts: one or two sessions before the research question is fixed can change the ceiling of the whole piece, and the same money spent after the data is collected buys presentation rather than marks. Knowing that distinction is worth more than any hourly rate comparison.

The third habit worth breaking is paying a premium rate for work that does not need one. Diagnosis from marked scripts, mechanism reasoning instruction and interrogating an investigation research question genuinely require somebody who knows the mark scheme and the limits of school glassware. Rule-and-check work after the rule has been taught does not, and practice supervision needs attention rather than expertise. Buying one rate for all three tasks costs more than splitting them, in either direction.

None of this requires buying tutoring years in advance. It requires knowing which windows are cheap, so that when a family does decide to spend, the money lands somewhere it buys more. Reading a marked script in DP1 is the mechanism: it tells you then what you would otherwise discover in February of DP2.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one chemistry tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. For mechanism work the shared screen is a real advantage: the student draws the arrow, the tutor corrects it as it is drawn, and both see the same molecule the same way up rather than from opposite sides of a notebook.

subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning and at Higher Level quantitative equilibrium work. The characteristic error is predicting the correct shift and then justifying it by restating the shift, which is circular and earns only the prediction mark. Two to three sessions.

sections.heading: What each chemistry block costs and buys
paragraphs: This is the table to see before any hourly rate is quoted, because in chemistry the block length varies far more than the rate. One problem is four to six sessions, four are two to three each, and one is a design conversation worth one or two sessions at the right moment and little at the wrong one.

The market rates, attributed and dated October 2026, so any quote can be judged. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

The useful discipline is the completion test rather than the rate. A block with a test ends when the work is done; a block with only an end date becomes a standing arrangement reviewed when the invoice becomes uncomfortable. Chemistry happens to have clean tests: an unfamiliar mechanism constructed unaided, a sign convention error absent from a full paper, a weak acid pH within range.

For wider household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, which makes tutoring the main variable line in most education budgets this year.

sections.heading: Why chemistry gets bought late, and what that costs
paragraphs: The timing pattern in this subject is remarkably consistent, and it is worth naming because the cure is free. Families hire a chemistry tutor in the second term of DP2, when the internal assessment is due, mocks are approaching and a report has arrived. At that moment every household in Dubai wants the same thing at the same hour.

The cost of hiring then is not a higher rate; it is a worse outcome for the same money. The investigation design is already fixed, so the cheapest decisive intervention has expired. Mechanism work now competes with four other deadlines for the student's attention, so six sessions achieve what four would have achieved in DP1. And the early-evening slots are contested, which in a southern corridor household with a long school run means the available times are the worst ones.

The alternative costs nothing but a calendar. The cheapest interventions in chemistry all sit early: criterion work in MYP, the transition block in the summer before DP1, mechanism reasoning in the first DP1 term, investigation design before the research question is fixed. Each of those is the same money spent at a point where it buys more.

This is not an argument for buying tutoring years in advance. It is an argument for knowing which windows are cheap, so that when a family does decide to spend, they spend into a window that works. Reading the marked script early is the mechanism: it tells you in DP1 what you would otherwise discover in DP2.

sections.heading: Mechanisms: the largest block and the clearest test
paragraphs: Organic mechanisms account for the biggest single share of recoverable Higher Level chemistry marks, and the reason is a mismatch between how students revise and what is examined. Students learn which reagent gives which product, because that is what a textbook table presents. The examination asks for the electron movement that produces it, and a mechanism with correct products and incorrect arrows earns very little, because the arrows are the chemistry being tested.

The method that works is reasoning from electron density rather than recognition. Where are the electrons, where are they attracted, what breaks, what forms, in which order. A student who can answer those five questions about an unfamiliar molecule can construct a mechanism they have never seen, which is precisely the skill the examination is built to separate. A student who cannot is dependent on recognition, and recognition fails exactly when the paper introduces something new.

Teaching it has a specific shape, and it is where online delivery is a genuine improvement rather than a substitute. The student draws, the tutor corrects the arrow as it is being drawn, and the correction lands at the moment the error is made. On paper between two people in a room, half the arrows are upside down from the tutor's viewpoint; on a shared annotated screen, both see the same molecule the same way up.

Expect four to six sessions for most Higher Level students, with a clean completion test: an unfamiliar mechanism constructed and justified without prompting. That is a defined block with a visible end point, which is how chemistry should be bought rather than as a standing weekly arrangement that nobody reviews until the May session has already happened.

sections.heading: The cheap fixes nobody asks for
paragraphs: Four chemistry problems cost two or three sessions each, and almost no family asks for them by name, because none of them sounds like a subject. Together they often account for more marks than a mechanism block does, and they fit a short weekday slot after a long school run, which makes them ideal for a household in this corridor.

Energetics sign conventions come first. An exothermic change reported with a positive enthalpy is treated by the scheme as a chemistry error rather than a presentation slip, and it frequently invalidates a Hess cycle built on top of it. Students find this harsh, which is why it survives: each instance looks like carelessness, so nobody fixes the underlying habit. Two sessions with a rule and a deliberate check.

Equilibrium explanation is second. A student predicts the correct shift and justifies it by restating the shift, which is circular and earns only the prediction mark. The scheme wants the change in the system named and the effect on the position of equilibrium derived from it. Two to three sessions. Weak acid calculations are third: strong acid arithmetic applied by habit produces a confident pH several units out, and the error is systematic rather than random, which makes it fast to correct.

Fourth is a stoichiometric checking routine. Inverted ratios and ignored limiting reagents produce clean wrong answers that look like misunderstanding and are not. Two sessions installing a verification habit usually ends them. None of these four requires new content, which is why they are the best value in the subject and the least often requested.

sections.heading: The investigation, costed by stage
paragraphs: The internal chemistry investigation carries 20 per cent of the grade, is marked by the school against lettered criteria and is moderated by the IB. Its cost profile is unlike anything else in the subject, because the same money buys very different amounts depending on when it is spent.

Before the research question is fixed, one or two sessions can change the ceiling of the whole piece. The commonest structural failure is a question depending on a change too small for school glassware to measure precisely, which caps the analysis and evaluation criteria before any data exists. Testing the question against the equipment actually available is an afternoon's work at the design stage and impossible three weeks later.

Before the laboratory session, the uncertainty plan can still be built into the method. A student who collects a single run per condition cannot subsequently produce an uncertainty analysis, and no amount of writing rescues it. That is a sequencing decision rather than a writing one, and it is worth more than any later polishing.

After the data is collected, the honest position is that the ceiling is set and the remaining scope is presentation and clarity. Help at that point has some value and is not worth a specialist rate, and any provider implying that late investigation support transforms a mark is selling comfort. The boundary also never moves: one operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the whole Diploma, and the consequence falls on the student. We write nothing, at any price. The test after a session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words.

sections.heading: Matching the rate to the task
paragraphs: The second commonest chemistry waste after buying late is buying at the wrong rate. Not every chemistry task needs a specialist, and paying AED 270 or more an hour for something that needs company rather than expertise is a straightforward transfer of money for no additional outcome.

Specialist rates are justified by diagnosis and by reasoning instruction. Reading two marked scripts and identifying that the loss is sign conventions rather than thermochemical understanding requires somebody who knows the scheme. Teaching mechanism reasoning from electron density requires somebody who can correct an arrow as it is drawn and explain why it was wrong. Interrogating an investigation research question requires knowing what a school laboratory can actually measure.

Mid-band rates are right for most of the short fixes, which are rule-and-check work once the rule is taught. Budget rates are genuinely appropriate for practice supervision, keeping a student working through question sets and providing company during revision, and there is no shame in using them for that. What a budget rate will not reliably deliver is diagnosis, which is the one thing that determines whether everything else is aimed correctly.

The practical rule is to buy diagnosis once at a specialist rate, then buy the execution at the rate the execution requires. Households that do this spend less overall than households who pick one rate and use it for everything, in either direction.

There is one exception worth stating, because it cuts against the rule. If a household can only manage a small number of sessions in total, put all of them at the specialist rate and aim them at the single highest-value target. Spreading a small budget across cheaper hours produces supervision rather than change, and supervision is only worth buying when the direction has already been set.
