sections.heading: Monthly budgets, and the fee context in Dubai
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a household budget. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is roughly double the money for half the number of contacts. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Put next to the rest of a Dubai education budget, one subject at the mid tier is a modest line and three subjects is not. That is the arithmetic behind the single most useful piece of advice on this page: buy one subject properly rather than three approximately. A weekly hour in chemistry, held for a term, with protected independent practice around it, outperforms thin coverage across chemistry, physics and mathematics at the same total cost.

The wider context has moved in families' favour for one year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's 2026-27 intake also adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

The last budgeting note is about where support should sit in the two years. Spending in DP1 is cheaper per unit of effect than spending in DP2, because the gaps are smaller, the specialists are available and the student has time to practise. Nearly every family spends more in DP2, for understandable reasons. Knowing that the pattern is expensive is the beginning of changing it.

sections.heading: Higher Level, medicine applications and the one thing nobody can sell you
paragraphs: Chemistry is the Diploma subject most often taken at Higher Level for a reason outside the Diploma: medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and related applications usually require it at the higher level of whichever system the student is in. That turns a chemistry grade into an application gate, and it changes the spending calculus, because a grade on a hard threshold is the narrow case where the specialist and even the premium band can be justified.

Requirements vary by university, by country and by intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas institutions. Read the individual programme page in the year your child applies, not two years earlier and not from a tutoring website, including this one. Any provider who tells you what a medical school requires without naming the school is guessing on your behalf about something checkable in five minutes.

Separately, the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process has its own requirements, and it is not the same thing as admissions. For the British track the published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source we could read, so no figure should be quoted to you without a moe.gov.ae reference. Equivalency is not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it.

The thing nobody can sell you is a grade. No tutor can guarantee a 7 in Higher Level chemistry, and any provider offering one is describing their marketing rather than their teaching. What can honestly be sold is specific: a diagnosis from the student's own marked work, a rate tier matched to the actual problem, mechanism teaching that generalises, an investigation coached within the rules, and a re-match if the fit is wrong after the first paid session. Those are testable, which is what makes them worth paying for.

faqs.question: How much should I actually pay for IB chemistry help in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem rather than the level. faqs.answer: Ask them to reason through a mechanism your child has not met, out loud, from first principles. Whether they reason or recall is visible within five minutes, and it is the single most informative thing you can watch. Follow it with two factual questions: how is the Internal Assessment marked and out of how many, and what is supplied in the data booklet. A specialist answers both immediately. A generalist talks about building confidence.

faqs.answer: Before the research question is fixed, which costs one or two sessions and preserves the full mark ceiling. After data collection it takes three or four sessions and some marks are already unreachable, because data that was never recorded cannot be recovered without repeating the practical. During the write-up it takes three to five and the ceiling is set. The single cheapest intervention in Diploma chemistry is the autumn conversation that replaces a broad question with a narrow one.

In a group of six the student reasoning wrongly is invisible until the test. If your child needs company and a timetable, a group class is a sensible purchase. Each works at the level the student takes, because the Higher Level extensions in organic chemistry and energetics are separate content rather than harder versions of the same material.

intro.heading: Three things decide a chemistry grade, and all three are teachable
paragraphs: IB Chemistry is organised into two integrated strands, structure and reactivity, rather than the old topic list, and it is assessed by two written papers plus a scientific investigation worth roughly twenty per cent. Across that structure, the marks a Production City student loses concentrate in a small number of places, and they are the same places almost every year: multi-step mole calculations, mechanistic notation in organic chemistry, energetics and equilibrium reasoning, and an investigation whose research question was chosen before anybody checked whether it could produce data.

That is good news for a family deciding what to buy. Chemistry is not a subject where a student needs everything revised. It is a subject where four specific capabilities carry a disproportionate share of the available marks, and where a student who is secure in all four will perform close to their understanding. One who is insecure in moles will underperform in every paper regardless of how well they understand bonding.

The mole is the gate. It appears in titrations, in gas calculations, in empirical formulae, in energetics, in equilibrium constants, and in the quantitative part of nearly every structured question. A student who has to think about it rather than doing it automatically spends time they need elsewhere, makes arithmetic slips under pressure, and loses marks that have nothing to do with chemical understanding. Fixing that is drill, and it works.

Organic chemistry is the second concentration, and the losses there are almost entirely notational. A correct product written without curly arrows, without a lone pair shown, without a named intermediate, scores a fraction of the available marks. The mark scheme is awarding the mechanism, not the outcome, which is a convention rather than an opinion, and once a student understands that the drawing is the answer their marks move quickly.

Dubai Production City has no IB World School inside it. Students travel to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, to the Al Barsha ring, or to Fairgreen International School to the south. Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. For chemistry the online format has a practical benefit: mechanisms drawn on a shared whiteboard are saved, so a student revising in the spring is reading their own corrected arrows from November.

We do not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be correct. UAE IB schools sit the May session; confirm windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Component structures and assessment criteria, which is what most of this page describes, are published in the subject guide your child's school already holds. Reviewed October 2026.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry entry route

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-produc.subjectsIntro: The chemistry content that generates the most requests in this cluster, with the specific place marks go missing. These notes come from marking scripts rather than from a syllabus summary.

subjects.name: Quantitative chemistry and the mole
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, molar volume, limiting reagents, percentage yield and atom economy. The losses are arithmetic under time pressure and unit confusion between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres. Making this automatic is the highest-return drill in the subject.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and periodic properties. Students state a trend correctly and lose the explanation marks by naming shielding without naming effective nuclear charge, or the reverse, when the mark scheme wants both.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and shapes of molecules. Shape questions are lost on the distinction between electron domain geometry and molecular shape, and on omitting the effect of lone pairs on bond angles.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess's law, bond enthalpies, and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign conventions cause most of the damage: an exothermic value written positive invalidates every subsequent step of an otherwise correct calculation.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory, activation energy and, at Higher Level, rate laws and the rate-determining step. Explanations lose marks when a student writes that particles have more energy without naming the proportion exceeding the activation energy.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier's principle and, at Higher Level, the equilibrium constant and its relationship to Gibbs free energy. The standard error is predicting a shift correctly and then failing to state the effect on the constant, which does not change with concentration.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.description: pH, strong and weak acids, titration curves and, at Higher Level, buffers and pKa. Buffer calculations are lost on setting up the ratio rather than on the arithmetic, and titration curve questions need the equivalence point distinguished from the half-equivalence point.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways and, at Higher Level, nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and the distinction between the two substitution routes. Marks are for curly arrows, lone pairs, charges and named intermediates, not for the product.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: A single internally assessed piece worth roughly twenty per cent, assessed across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design constrains every later criterion, which is why the question matters more than the write-up.

sections.heading: The mole is the gate, and it is pure drill
paragraphs: Of all the diagnostic work we do in chemistry, the most consistently revealing is a short set of mixed mole calculations under timing. A student who completes them automatically has a different problem from one who has to reconstruct the method each time, and the second student will underperform on both papers no matter how well they understand bonding or periodicity.

The reason is structural. Mole reasoning is assumed in titrations, gas calculations, empirical and molecular formulae, percentage yield, energetics, equilibrium constants and the quantitative parts of nearly every structured question. A student who spends ninety seconds working out which quantity to divide by which has spent ninety seconds they needed for the explanation question later in the paper, and will usually make an arithmetic slip while doing it.

The failures are predictable and almost never conceptual. Unit confusion between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, which costs a factor of a thousand. Forgetting to identify the limiting reagent before calculating yield. Dividing by the wrong molar mass because the formula was not written out. Losing a factor of two in a titration because the stoichiometric ratio was assumed to be one to one.

The fix is drill, which nobody finds appealing and which works. Short mixed sets, timed, every session, until the method is automatic rather than remembered. Four or five sessions does it for most students, and the effect shows up in marks across both papers rather than in one topic, which makes it the best-value hours a Production City family can buy in this subject.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry is a drawing discipline
paragraphs: The single most common misunderstanding in Diploma chemistry is that an organic question wants the product. It does not. It wants the mechanism, and the mark scheme awards the components of the drawing: the arrow starting from the right place, the lone pair shown, the charge marked, the intermediate named and drawn, the second arrow going where it should.

A student who writes the correct product and nothing else has usually earned one mark out of four. That is not a judgement on their chemistry, which may be sound; it is a marking convention, and once a student understands that the drawing is the answer their marks move fast. We treat organic sessions as practice in drawing rather than practice in predicting.

The specific conventions matter. An arrow begins at a lone pair or at a bond, never at an atom. A curly arrow shows the movement of an electron pair, so a half-arrow is a different claim. An intermediate in electrophilic addition carries a positive charge that must be drawn on the correct carbon, because the mark scheme distinguishes between a correct and an incorrect carbocation. At Higher Level, the distinction between the two nucleophilic substitution routes has to be shown through the drawn mechanism rather than asserted in a sentence.

Pathway questions add a second skill. Converting one functional group to another over two or three steps needs the reagents and conditions named, not just the intermediate compounds. Students write the structures and omit the conditions, which is half an answer. Building a one-page pathway map that the student draws themselves, repeatedly, is the exercise that fixes it.
bullets: Arrows begin at a lone pair or a bond, never at an atom
Charges and lone pairs are marked every time, not implied
Intermediates are drawn and named, with the charge on the correct atom
Higher Level substitution routes are distinguished by the drawing, not by a sentence

sections.heading: Energetics, equilibrium and the reasoning the mark scheme wants
paragraphs: Energetics and equilibrium produce a particular kind of lost mark: the student reaches the right conclusion and does not say the thing that earns the credit. Both topics are assessed through chains of reasoning, and the mark scheme awards the links rather than the destination.

In energetics, sign convention does most of the damage. An exothermic enthalpy change written as positive invalidates every subsequent step of an otherwise correct Hess's law calculation, and the student loses marks for a convention rather than for chemistry. Bond enthalpy calculations add a second trap: bonds broken are endothermic and bonds formed exothermic, and a student who sums them with consistent signs gets the right answer while one who mixes them loses the lot.

In equilibrium, the recurring error is answering only half the question. A student asked about increasing concentration predicts the shift correctly and then does not state what happens to the equilibrium constant, which does not change with concentration. Temperature is the only variable that alters the constant, and that distinction is worth marks on most equilibrium questions in some form.

Kinetics belongs here too. An explanation that says particles have more energy at higher temperature is not wrong but earns little, because the mark scheme wants the proportion of collisions exceeding the activation energy. Naming the mechanism of the change rather than describing the change is the general rule in all three topics, and once a student has it, their answers get shorter as well as better.
bullets: Write the sign convention before calculating, not after
Bonds broken endothermic, bonds formed exothermic, signs kept consistent
Only temperature changes the equilibrium constant; concentration and pressure do not
Kinetics explanations need the proportion exceeding activation energy, not just more energy
The mark scheme awards the links in the reasoning chain, not the conclusion

sections.heading: The investigation, and why the research question decides the mark
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is a single internally assessed piece worth roughly twenty per cent, assessed across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Almost no competitor page in this market names a single criterion, despite them being published in the subject guide every school holds.

In chemistry, research design fails in a specific way. A student picks a question they find interesting, such as the effect of a household variable on a reaction, without checking whether their apparatus can measure the dependent variable precisely enough to show a trend across the range available. The result is a flat dataset, which makes the data-analysis criterion hard and the conclusion criterion nearly impossible to satisfy well.

Testing the question before committing is the intervention, and it takes one session. What exactly is being measured, with what instrument, to what precision, across what range of the independent variable, with how many repeats, and will the expected variation exceed the uncertainty? A question that fails that test should be changed in week one rather than rescued in month four.

Our role is bounded and we state the boundary plainly. We teach what each criterion requires, interrogate the research question, discuss whether the method will produce usable data, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. We do not write, rewrite or complete any part of an investigation, nor generate data. One operator in our research sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750; the malpractice consequence of buying one falls on the student, not the seller.

sections.heading: Paper structure, command terms and time allocation
paragraphs: Chemistry is assessed by two written papers, one including multiple-choice and data-based work and the other extended response, plus the investigation. Students who are strong on content and weak on marks are usually losing them to command terms and to time allocation rather than to chemistry.

The command terms do specific jobs. State wants a fact and no reasoning. Outline wants a brief account. Describe wants an account of features or a sequence. Explain wants a mechanism or reason named. Deduce wants a conclusion drawn from given information with the reasoning shown. Suggest wants a plausible answer where more than one is defensible. A student who writes an explanation for a state question has spent three minutes earning one mark.

Time allocation follows from mark value. Roughly a minute per mark, glanced at before starting the question, is the habit that prevents a strong script thinning out towards the end. Students resist this because interesting questions attract attention disproportionately, which is exactly how a paper ends with two unattempted parts worth six marks.

Data-based questions deserve separate practice. They examine reading a table or graph, identifying a trend, and explaining it in chemical terms, and they reward precision about what the data does and does not show. A student who asserts a cause the data cannot support loses marks that a more cautious sentence would have earned. Writing what the data shows, then what it suggests, then what it cannot establish, is a three-sentence habit that scores reliably across both papers and takes very little practice to acquire.
bullets: State wants a fact; explain wants a named mechanism or reason
Deduce wants the reasoning shown, not just the conclusion
Allocate roughly a minute per mark and check the mark value first
Data-based questions reward precision about what the data supports
Command-term definitions are published in the subject guide the school holds

sections.heading: Past-paper work that produces improvement
paragraphs: Doing past papers is not a method. Marking them against the published mark scheme, under timing, with a categorised error log, is a method. Most students do the first part and then plateau after three or four papers, which families read as a ceiling on ability when it is a marking problem.

The mark scheme is diagnostic in a way a score is not. It shows that a particular line earned the method mark and the next did not, that an answer needed a unit to score, that a mechanism lost two marks for an arrow starting at an atom. A student who learns that half their losses are notational has a completely different plan from one whose losses cluster in equilibrium.

Sequence matters. Topic questions first, while the content is fresh from the school lesson. Then mixed sections under timing, because mixing exposes the traps that topic practice hides: a student doing a set of mechanism questions already knows the topic is mechanisms. Then full papers, late, when the student can finish one without exhausting themselves.

We do not reproduce or distribute IB past papers, mark schemes, subject guides or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. We work from papers the student or school legitimately holds and reference the official source. Any provider offering a downloadable library of IB material is distributing what it does not own, which is worth noticing. Your child's chemistry teacher can supply past papers through the school, and that channel is both legitimate and usually quicker than anything a tutor could arrange.

sections.heading: What chemistry support costs in Dubai, and which band buys what
paragraphs: The useful framing is which band each piece of work needs, because chemistry splits cleanly. Mole drill needs supervision and patience rather than specialist expertise, and budget or university-student tutors advertising from AED 45 an hour can do it competently. Mechanism notation and investigation criteria work need somebody who has marked against the published descriptors, which is the specialist band.

The Dubai bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, rising to AED 500 for specialist levels.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Diploma chemistry student with one weekly session sits in the upper two bands for most of DP2.

Context worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices. We publish no price list here and start with a free trial lesson and an honest conversation about which band the actual problem needs.

sections.heading: Honesty, practicals and the regulators
paragraphs: Chemistry is the subject where the essay-mill end of this market is most active, because an investigation is a discrete deliverable with a deadline. One operator in our competitor research sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is an academic malpractice finding against the student and it sits on their record rather than the seller's.

The legitimate line is clear. A tutor teaches the chemistry an investigation rests on, explains each criterion and what the descriptors require, interrogates the research question, discusses whether the method and repeats will support an uncertainty, and reads a draft the student wrote to say where it falls short of a criterion. A tutor never writes, rewrites, completes or supplies any part of the work, and never generates data.

On practical skills, online tutoring covers what is assessed: design, measurement choice, precision, repeats, uncertainty propagation, graph work and evaluation. It does not replace the hours a student spends handling apparatus, which is the school's responsibility. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes.

On regulation: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with no published fine schedule for working without one. IB Gram is not IB authorised, KHDA approved or ADEK approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit and has no UAE office.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter know the chemistry and still lose organic marks?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because she is writing the product instead of drawing the mechanism. The mark scheme awards the components of the drawing: the arrow starting from a lone pair or bond, the lone pair shown, the charge marked, the intermediate named and drawn on the correct atom. A correct product with nothing else usually earns one mark out of four. That is a marking convention rather than a judgement on her chemistry, and once she understands that the drawing is the answer her marks tend to move within a few sessions.

faqs.question: Is mole practice really worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value work in the subject, and it does not need the most expensive tutor. Mole reasoning is assumed in titrations, gas calculations, empirical formulae, percentage yield, energetics and equilibrium constants, so a student who is slow at it loses marks across both papers for reasons unrelated to chemical understanding. Four to six sessions of timed mixed drill usually makes it automatic. A budget or university-student tutor at AED 45-150 an hour can supervise that competently, and paying specialist rates for it is a common overspend.

faqs.question: What unit mistake costs chemistry students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, which is a factor of a thousand and therefore the kind of error that makes an answer obviously wrong without the student noticing under time pressure. The fix is mechanical: convert units as a separate written step before any arithmetic, every time, rather than doing it in the same line as the calculation. The companion trap is molar volume questions where the conditions are stated and students use a remembered value instead of the one given, which the mark scheme does not forgive.

faqs.question: How do we stop the investigation producing a flat dataset?
faqs.answer: Test the research question before any data is collected. Establish what exactly is being measured and with what instrument, the smallest change that instrument reads reliably, at least five well-spaced values of the independent variable, and whether the expected variation exceeds the uncertainty. If the predicted change is smaller than the instrument's precision, the data will read as noise no matter how carefully it is collected. That check takes one session in week one and prevents the most common way a chemistry investigation caps its own marks.

faqs.question: Which criteria is the chemistry investigation marked against?
faqs.answer: Criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, all published in the subject guide your child's school holds. Research design constrains everything after it, because a question the apparatus cannot answer precisely leaves nothing for the analysis criterion to work with. Evaluation needs stated limitations and realistic improvements rather than apologies. We teach what each descriptor asks for and give feedback on drafts the student wrote, and we never write, rewrite or complete any part of the work in any circumstance.

faqs.question: What goes wrong with energetics sign conventions?
faqs.answer: An exothermic enthalpy change written as positive invalidates every subsequent step of an otherwise correct Hess's law calculation, so a student loses marks for a convention rather than for chemistry. Bond enthalpy questions add a second layer: bonds broken are endothermic and bonds formed exothermic, and a student who mixes the signs loses the whole calculation while one who keeps them consistent gets it. The habit that fixes both is writing the sign convention down before starting rather than deciding it during the arithmetic.

faqs.question: Does the equilibrium constant change when we change concentration?
faqs.answer: No, and this is one of the most frequently dropped marks in the subject. Temperature is the only variable that alters the equilibrium constant. Changing concentration or pressure shifts the position of equilibrium, which is a different claim, and a student who predicts the shift correctly and then says the constant increased has given away marks they had earned. Most equilibrium questions test this distinction in some form, so the discipline is to answer both halves: what happens to the position, and what happens to the constant.

faqs.question: Should our son take chemistry at Higher or Standard for a medicine route?
faqs.answer: It is more content and genuinely different content rather than the same material examined harder. The Higher Level extensions in organic chemistry, energetics including entropy and Gibbs free energy, equilibrium constants and acid-base theory with buffers and pKa add material Standard Level students never meet. The practical implication is that a tutor should be matched to the level actually being taken. Check whether the target degree requires Higher Level chemistry before committing, since many medicine and some engineering routes specify it and the decision is hard to reverse.

faqs.question: Can online chemistry tutoring help with practical work?
faqs.answer: For the assessed parts, yes. What the investigation and the data-based paper questions examine is design, measurement choice, precision, repeats, uncertainty propagation, graph construction and evaluation, and all of those are paper skills that work well over video with a shared whiteboard. What online tutoring cannot replace is the hours spent physically handling apparatus, which remains the school's responsibility and which schools do. The useful division is that the lab teaches technique and the tutoring teaches what the criteria reward about that technique.

faqs.question: Our son's mock chemistry grade dropped. What should we look at?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for component marks rather than working from the grade. Notational losses in organic questions, content gaps clustered in equilibrium or acid-base theory, arithmetic slips in quantitative work and a script that thins towards the end are four different problems needing four different plans. Notation and arithmetic are the fastest to fix, often within four to six sessions. Content gaps take longer. A grade cannot distinguish them, and buying hours before you know which you have is how families spend twice what they needed to.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used in chemistry specifically?
faqs.answer: Marked against the published mark scheme rather than an answer key, under timing, and in sequence: topic questions while content is fresh, then mixed sections, then full papers late. Mixing matters particularly in chemistry, because a student working through a set of mechanism questions already knows the topic is mechanisms, which is exactly the clue the real paper withholds. Keep a categorised error log distinguishing notation, content, arithmetic and pacing, because the proportions in that log tell you what the next ten hours should be.

faqs.question: Will you supply IB chemistry past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material and we neither reproduce nor distribute them. We reference the official source, link to it, and work from papers your child or their school legitimately holds. Your child's chemistry teacher can supply past papers through the proper channel, which is the route to use. Any provider offering a downloadable library of IB material is distributing what it does not own, and that is worth noting for what else it might treat casually.

faqs.question: What does chemistry support cost across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: It depends which work you buy rather than how many weeks you book. Mole drill is four to six hours and can sit at the budget band from AED 45. Mechanism notation is four to eight hours at the specialist band of AED 200-450. Investigation criteria work is six to ten hours at the specialist band. A spring timed-paper block is ten to sixteen hours at the qualified band of AED 150-300. That is under forty targeted hours, which is a different purchase from a weekly arrangement running sixty to seventy.

faqs.question: Does your chemistry tutor come to our address in IMPZ?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For chemistry the online format keeps a shared whiteboard record of every mechanism drawn and corrected, which a student can revise from months later rather than reconstructing from a textbook diagram. Independent home tutors do operate in this area at roughly AED 180-350 an hour on published Dubai market rates, and for a younger child needing physical supervision they can be the better choice.

faqs.question: You have nobody free in our Tuesday slot. What do you actually do then?
faqs.answer: We give you a date rather than a substitute. Higher Level chemistry with investigation supervision in a specific evening slot is one of the thinner parts of our coverage, and two to five days is normal, longer near mocks and internal deadlines. Putting a biology or physics specialist in front of a chemistry student wastes the hours, because the marking conventions differ sharply between the three sciences. If the available specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-produc.closingBody: Chemistry is unusually diagnosable. Mole work automatic under timing, mechanisms drawn with the conventions the mark scheme awards, energetics and equilibrium reasoning stated link by link, and an investigation whose research question the apparatus can genuinely answer. A student secure in all four performs close to their understanding; one insecure in any of them underperforms for reasons that have nothing to do with chemistry. Start with a timed mole set and a recent marked script, take a free trial lesson, and let the evidence choose the first ten hours rather than the topic that produced the last bad mark.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-silico.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB chemistry at Higher and Standard Level and are matched to the level rather than the subject. For a calendar-led plan the useful tutor is one who asks which topics have been taught and when the school's investigation deadline falls, before proposing anything at all.

intro.heading: Chemistry has one slow booking and several fast ones
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry divides unusually cleanly into work that needs a term and work that needs a few hours, and the calendar punishes families who do not know which is which. The slow item is organic chemistry at Higher Level: mechanisms, stereochemistry and spectroscopic identification require the student to build a way of seeing reactions, and pattern recognition forms through exposure to enough examples over months rather than through concentrated effort over a fortnight.

The fast items are almost everything else. Learning what is in the data booklet and where is roughly a one-session job. Balancing half-equations in acidic and basic conditions is two. Hess cycles and sign conventions are two or three. Titration curves and buffers at Higher Level are about three, and the question types are highly predictable. Command terms are one session and improve both papers and the investigation at once.

The scheduling problem is that most schemes of work teach organic chemistry late, in DP2, which places the one item that needs duration into the term that also contains the scientific investigation deadline, the mock window and often university applications. A family that discovers this in January has a genuine difficulty; one that knew it in September booked the organic run while slots in the after-school window were still open.

The investigation itself carries 20 per cent of the grade and its deadline belongs to the school rather than to the board. Because every Diploma science sets one and the Extended Essay milestones sit nearby, the dates cluster. Asking the coordinator for all of them in September of DP1 is free and it is the most useful scheduling act available to a chemistry family on this corridor.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City, The Villa and Nad Al Sheba, chemistry lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format earns its place: the data booklet and the student's own working sit side by side on a shared screen, and a mechanism can be annotated arrow by arrow while both people watch.

What follows is the sequence in detail. Which topics arrive when. Why organic is the one early booking. How the investigation timeline runs backwards. Which chemistry gaps close late and which do not. And what the data booklet session is worth, which is more than almost anything else per hour spent.

One framing worth carrying forward. Chemistry is more forgiving than most Diploma subjects about a late start, and that is genuinely good news for a family arriving in the spring. Most of the course is procedural, the data booklet session works identically whenever it happens, and titration curves and half-equations close in a handful of hours. The single exception is Higher Level organic reasoning, and the only mistake that cannot be recovered is treating that exception as though it behaved like the rest of the subject.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-silico.subjectsIntro: This grid sorts Diploma chemistry by when it typically arrives and how long the repair takes. Use it to work out which bookings have to be made early and which can wait.

subjects.name: The data booklet
subjects.description: Provided in the examination and systematically under-used. Constants, equations, spectroscopic data and reference tables that students try to recall instead of locating. One session with a past paper beside the booklet, at any point in the two years, and the highest return per hour in the subject.

subjects.name: Mole and concentration calculations
subjects.description: Usually taught early in DP1. Amount of substance, concentration, gas volumes, limiting reagents, percentage yield. A finite set of procedures, so four sessions with marked practice produces fluency, and it should be closed in DP1 rather than carried forward.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Taught in DP1. Ionic, covalent and metallic models, intermolecular forces, and the link between structure and physical properties. Marks are lost in explanation rather than recall: a student names the force and does not say what it does to the property asked about.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles and bond enthalpies, with entropy and spontaneity added at Higher Level. Sign conventions are where marks disappear, and a drawn Hess cycle beats an attempted mental calculation every time. Two to three sessions.

subjects.name: Kinetics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, rate equations at HL
subjects.description: Rate measurement, collision theory and activation energy, with rate equations and mechanisms at Higher Level. Higher Level students quote orders from a table without reasoning from the data, which is an interpretation habit and responds to marked practice rather than content.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.levels: HL and SL, calculations at HL
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier reasoning and equilibrium constants. The commonest error is explaining a shift by restating the rule rather than reasoning about the specific system in the question, which earns a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.levels: HL and SL, buffers and curves at HL
subjects.description: Acid-base theory, pH, strong and weak behaviour, with buffers and titration curves at Higher Level. Titration curve questions reward reading the graph before calculating and are among the most predictable question types in the whole course.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, cells at HL
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrolysis, with electrochemical cells and electrode potentials at Higher Level. Balancing half-equations in acidic or basic conditions is procedural and highly drillable, so it responds quickly whenever it is tackled.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL, mechanisms at HL
subjects.description: Usually taught late. Functional groups, reaction types and synthetic routes, with mechanisms, stereochemistry and spectroscopic identification at Higher Level. The one part of the course that needs a term rather than a block, and therefore the booking to make early.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An independent investigation marked against published criteria, due in DP2 on a school-set date. Thin evaluation and a research question too broad for available apparatus are the expensive failures, and both are decided at the planning stage where correction is cheap.

sections.heading: The two-year chemistry sequence, and the collision it creates
paragraphs: Most schemes of work open Diploma chemistry with the quantitative material and with bonding, because stoichiometry and structure underpin everything afterwards. Energetics and kinetics commonly follow in DP1. Equilibrium, acids and bases and redox sit across the DP1 to DP2 boundary. Organic chemistry, and the Higher Level extensions throughout, generally come last. Your school may differ, and asking is one message.

That order is sensible teaching and awkward scheduling. It places organic chemistry, the one part of the course that needs months rather than weeks, into the term that also holds the scientific investigation deadline, the mock window and often university application deadlines. A student who has been coping adequately can appear to fall apart in that term without anything having changed about their ability.

The diagnostic a parent can apply is the same as in physics. If the student was fine until organic arrived, the problem is sequence and workload, and the response is a sustained organic run plus a calmer calendar. If the student has been losing the same kinds of marks since the first term of DP1, the problem is underneath the chemistry, usually in quantitative work or in explanation structure, and no amount of organic teaching will touch it.

The practical conclusion is that the organic booking has to be made before it is needed. The after-school window on Gulf Standard Time is the busiest part of the week across the UAE and fills by about October, so a family that waits until organic arrives is choosing from what is left. Asking the school in September when organic is taught, and booking the slot then, is the single most useful act available.

sections.heading: Why the organic booking cannot be made late
paragraphs: At Standard Level organic chemistry is largely functional groups, reaction types and synthetic routes, which is learnable content and responds to a block. At Higher Level the demand changes: mechanisms with curly arrows, stereochemistry and spectroscopic identification require a student to see why a reaction proceeds as it does, and that is a way of thinking rather than a set of facts.

Ways of thinking form through exposure to enough examples that the pattern becomes visible. A student shown twenty mechanisms across a term starts predicting the twenty-first. The same student shown twenty mechanisms in one week remembers a few and recognises none. This is why four-session organic blocks disappoint, and why families who buy one often conclude that tutoring does not work when the problem was the shape of the purchase rather than its quality.

That makes organic the one chemistry item where the calendar is unforgiving. If a family wants it addressed properly, the booking has to exist through the term in which the school teaches it, which means securing a weekly slot before the after-school window fills. A family calling in February about Higher Level organic mechanisms is calling for the thing that February cannot provide, however much they are willing to spend.

There is a partial alternative worth naming honestly. Spectroscopic identification sits at the junction of organic chemistry and the data booklet, and it is formulaic once learned, so it responds to a short block even late. A student weak at mechanisms but able to read spectra can still claim those marks reliably. So in a late conversation the right answer is often spectroscopy plus the recall-based organic marks, rather than an attempt at mechanistic reasoning.

sections.heading: The investigation timeline, counted back from the school's date
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the chemistry grade and its deadline belongs to the school. Every Diploma science sets one and the Extended Essay milestones sit nearby, so the dates cluster and three deadlines in one fortnight is routine rather than unlucky. Collecting all of them from the coordinator in September of DP1 is free, takes one request, and converts a predictable congestion into something that can be planned around.

Counting backwards gives the schedule. A complete draft two to three weeks before submission, so that feedback can be acted on. Data collection finished before that, with margin to repeat a run that fails. Method, apparatus and the uncertainty plan settled before any data is collected. And the research question narrowed earliest of all, because a question too broad for school apparatus produces data that cannot support a conclusion whatever else is done well.

For chemistry specifically, two planning errors recur. Choosing a reaction whose rate or yield cannot be measured reliably with school apparatus, and failing to think about uncertainty until the numbers are already recorded. Both are conversations rather than lessons, both belong at the front, and both are far cheaper to prevent than to patch. Two or three well-timed hours here outperform a term of content teaching placed badly.

The boundary is absolute and it matters more here than anywhere else in the course. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain each criterion, model a comparable investigation on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. One site competing for these queries sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750, which is a malpractice finding with a price attached.

sections.heading: Which chemistry gaps close late, and which do not
paragraphs: Chemistry is more forgiving than physics or English Literature about a late start, because so much of it is procedural. Half-equations in acidic and basic conditions, Hess cycles, titration curve reading, mole calculations and the qualitative reasoning behind equilibrium shifts are all finite sets of steps. A student either has the procedure or does not, and installing it takes sessions rather than terms whenever it is attempted.

The data booklet session is the extreme case. It is close to a free lesson, it claims marks in every component, and it works identically in September of DP1 or in April of DP2 because it is a matter of knowing what a reference document contains. Any late plan that does not start with it is leaving the cheapest marks in the subject on the table, and almost every late plan does exactly that.

What does not close late is Higher Level organic reasoning, for the reasons set out above. Nor does the habit of writing a proper chemical explanation, which is the ability to produce a chain where each step follows from the last and names the species or interaction involved. Students who have spent two years writing descriptions can be taught a structure and a checklist, which captures some of the marks, but not the underlying habit.

So an honest late plan for chemistry is: the data booklet and command terms first, then two or three procedural blocks chosen from the marked papers, then spectroscopic identification if organic is weak, then extended-response structure as a template rather than a habit. And an explicit exclusion: Higher Level mechanistic reasoning is not in scope in a short window, and the student should be told so at the start.

sections.heading: The data booklet session, and why it belongs first
paragraphs: A data booklet is provided in the chemistry examination. It carries constants, equations, spectroscopic data and reference tables, and it is the most under-used resource in the subject. Students spend examination minutes trying to recall things printed two pages away, and lose marks for approximations where an exact value was available. None of that is a knowledge problem and none of it needs a specialist to fix.

The reason it goes unaddressed is that it does not feel like chemistry. A session spent learning the structure of a reference document feels administrative, and both students and tutors would rather spend the hour on content. But the mark consequence recurs in every component, which makes it the highest return per hour anywhere in the course, and it is the same return whether the session happens in DP1 or three weeks before the papers.

The method is simple enough to describe here. Take a past paper. For every question, ask whether anything needed was in the booklet, then find it and note the page. After twenty questions the student has an internal map of the document and stops trying to remember what they can look up. Spectroscopic identification in particular becomes substantially more tractable, because the characteristic values are tabulated rather than memorised.

This is also where a shared screen earns its place. The booklet and the student's own attempt sit side by side at the same magnification, with the tutor able to point at a specific row while both look at it. Across a table, one person is reading a reference document upside down while the other turns pages, which is a small mechanical difference that materially changes how well the session works.

sections.heading: Paper components and the targeted drill for each
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry is assessed by two written papers plus the internally assessed scientific investigation, which carries 20 per cent of the grade. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 contains short-answer and extended-response questions. For exact weightings and durations at your child's level, use the school's copy of the subject guide, which is the authority.

The multiple-choice section loses marks to careless reading rather than to ignorance, and the drill is a timed set followed by analysis of every wrong answer, asking what the distractor was designed to catch. Most students find the same two or three traps recurring. The data-based section rewards graph reading, unit handling and uncertainty treatment, which are the same skills the investigation needs, so one block serves both.

Paper 2's short-answer calculations need a standard layout: formula written out, substitution shown, answer with units. A calculation compressed into two lines cannot be awarded method marks because the method is not visible to the examiner. Students do this to save time and lose more than they save, and teaching the layout is close to a single-session fix with a two-year payback.

Paper 2's extended-response questions are the Higher Level discriminator. They want a chain of chemical reasoning in which each step names the species or the interaction involved, and what arrives instead is a description that restates the question. Teaching the difference requires marked practice with the mark scheme visible until the student can see which of their own sentences earned nothing, which is a DP1 job done properly.

sections.heading: Higher Level chemistry and when the commitment bites
paragraphs: Higher Level chemistry adds content within both organising themes and raises the extended-response demand, and the two additions that most affect a calendar are organic mechanisms and the thermodynamics extension. Both are the slow kind of work. Choosing Higher Level is therefore implicitly a choice about how many months of support may be required, and the months fall in DP2 where they are hardest to find.

Whether that commitment is necessary depends on destination. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, chemical engineering and most life science programmes commonly require Higher Level chemistry or a Higher Level science, and some specify grades within it. Many other degrees do not require chemistry at all. Requirements are set course by course and change between admissions cycles, so read the admissions page for the specific course in the specific year.

For UAE routes, Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate matter from a university's own entry requirements. The sourced British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB Diploma we publish no points figure, because none has been read on an official Ministry source.

The advice that follows runs against our own interest. A student who does not need Higher Level chemistry and chose it for how it looks will consume months of tutoring hours on organic mechanisms that no application required. A confident Standard Level result in the right combination is often a better outcome and a far smaller bill. Ask the question before DP1 locks, because afterwards every answer costs more and takes longer.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and what we will not do
paragraphs: Send four things: the level, which topics have been taught so far, the school's internal deadline for the scientific investigation, and whether organic chemistry has been reached. That last question determines the whole plan, because it separates the booking that has to be made early from the ones that can wait. We then match a tutor to the level and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written note sorting the lost marks by cause rather than by topic: data booklet, command term, procedure, reasoning, or a genuine content gap. For most students the plan opens with a data booklet session and a four-session procedural block. For a Higher Level student entering the organic term, it is a sustained booking, and we will say so plainly rather than selling a block that cannot work.

The limits. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no IB, regulator or board approval. We publish no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than silence. We do not supply subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or data booklets as downloads.

And no grade promises. What the first month should produce is a child who can name which cause is costing them marks, a written note saying the same, and one visible habit change, usually reaching for the booklet rather than trying to recall, or writing working out in full. Grade movement takes longer than a month and nobody can honestly guarantee it at any price.

process.title: Ask when the school teaches organic chemistry
process.description: It is one message and it decides the whole plan, because organic at Higher Level is the only chemistry booking that needs a term rather than a block. Knowing the term means the weekly slot can be secured in September, before the after-school window on Gulf Standard Time fills around October.

process.title: Collect every science deadline in September of DP1
process.description: The chemistry investigation deadline, the other sciences, and the Extended Essay milestones. They cluster, and three in a fortnight is routine. One request to the coordinator turns a February emergency into something that can be spread, and it costs nothing at all.

process.title: Buy the data booklet session first
process.description: Take a past paper and, question by question, ask whether anything needed was printed in the booklet, then find it and note the page. After twenty questions the student stops trying to recall what they can look up. Highest return per hour in the course, and the same return at any point in the two years.

process.title: Sort two marked papers by cause
process.description: Data booklet, command term, procedure, reasoning, or genuine content gap. Most students show one dominant cause rather than a spread, and that single finding decides whether the plan is one session, four, or a term. It costs nothing and happens before any booking.

process.title: Schedule investigation support backwards
process.description: Complete draft two to three weeks before submission, data collection finished before that, method and uncertainty settled before any data, and the research question narrowed earliest of all. Two or three hours placed here beat a term of content teaching placed badly.

whyPoints.title: The slow booking is named
whyPoints.description: Higher Level organic chemistry needs a term because pattern recognition forms through exposure over months. Everything else in the subject closes in sessions. Saying which is which lets a family secure the one slot that matters in September instead of discovering the problem in February.

whyPoints.title: The sequence is mapped, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Most schemes teach organic last, placing the slow work in the term that also holds the investigation deadline and mocks. A student who collapses then has a sequence problem rather than a capability one, and the two need different plans and the same money.

whyPoints.title: Lost marks sorted by cause
whyPoints.description: Data booklet, command term, procedure, reasoning or content gap. A student losing marks for the first two looks exactly like one with a knowledge gap on a report, so the diagnosis sorts by cause and the plan follows from the evidence rather than from instinct.

whyPoints.title: An honest list of what closes late
whyPoints.description: The booklet, command terms, half-equations, Hess cycles, titration curves and spectroscopy all close late. Higher Level mechanistic reasoning does not. Stating the exclusion at the start is what makes a short plan succeed rather than feel like failure.

whyPoints.title: Investigation support with a written boundary
whyPoints.description: Question narrowing, criteria explanation, a comparable model on a different topic, and feedback on your child's own draft. No drafting, no completing, no supplied material. One site in this market sells finished internal assessments; that risk lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: A shared screen suits this subject
whyPoints.description: The data booklet and the student's working sit side by side at the same magnification, mechanisms can be annotated arrow by arrow, and a mark scheme can be opened beside an attempt. Across a table, somebody is reading a reference document upside down.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Silicon Oasis family book chemistry tuition for the organic term?
faqs.answer: In September, before the after-school window fills. Ask the school when its scheme of work teaches organic chemistry, because at Higher Level it is the one part of the course that needs a weekly booking across a term rather than a short block. Pattern recognition in mechanisms forms through exposure to enough examples over months, so a family calling in February is calling for the thing February cannot provide at any rate.

faqs.question: Why did my child cope with chemistry until organic chemistry started?
faqs.answer: Because the demand changes rather than merely increasing. Up to that point the course rewards procedures and recall, both of which respond to effort. Higher Level organic chemistry asks the student to see why a reaction proceeds as it does, which is a way of thinking built through exposure to many examples. A student who was fine until then usually has a sequence and workload problem rather than a capability one, and the response is a sustained organic run.

faqs.question: Which chemistry gaps can still be closed a month before the papers?
faqs.answer: More than families expect. Learning what the data booklet contains is roughly one session and claims marks in every component. Command terms are one session. Balancing half-equations in acidic and basic conditions is two. Hess cycles and sign conventions are two or three. Titration curves and buffers are about three and the question types are highly predictable. Spectroscopic identification is formulaic once learned, which makes it the late answer when organic is weak.

faqs.question: What is in the IB chemistry data booklet, and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Constants, equations, spectroscopic data and reference tables, all provided in the examination. It matters because students spend examination minutes trying to recall things printed two pages away and lose marks for approximations where an exact value was available. The fix is one session: take a past paper, ask question by question whether anything needed was in the booklet, find it and note the page. After twenty questions the habit changes permanently.

faqs.question: How much of the IB chemistry grade is the investigation, and who sets the deadline?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, and the school sets the deadline rather than the board. Every Diploma science sets one and the Extended Essay milestones sit nearby, so the dates cluster and three deadlines in a fortnight is routine. Ask the coordinator for all of them in September of DP1. Counting backwards, a complete draft should exist two to three weeks before submission so that feedback can be acted on rather than simply received.

faqs.question: Can a chemistry tutor help with the investigation close to the deadline?
faqs.answer: With feedback on what your child has written, yes; with producing any part of it, never. A tutor may explain each criterion, discuss systematic and random error, model a comparable investigation on a different topic, and read a draft and say where it falls short. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or supply any portion. The report is declared as the student's own work and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else falls on them.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to Cedre Villas or Academic City for chemistry lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For chemistry the online format is genuinely better: the data booklet and the student's own working sit side by side on a shared screen at the same magnification, a mechanism can be annotated arrow by arrow, and a mark scheme can be opened beside an attempt so the student sees which of their sentences earned nothing.

faqs.question: Is a four-session organic chemistry block worth buying?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, often yes, because the demand there is functional groups, reaction types and synthetic routes, which is learnable content. At Higher Level it usually disappoints, because mechanisms require pattern recognition formed over months and twenty mechanisms compressed into a fortnight produce recognition of a few rather than prediction of the next. If a short window is all that exists, spend it on spectroscopic identification and the recall-based organic marks instead.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand chemistry and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Usually command terms and working layout. State, outline, describe, explain, deduce and justify ask for different amounts, and answering the wrong amount either wastes time or loses marks. Separately, a calculation written in two compressed lines cannot be awarded method marks because the method is not visible. Each is roughly a one-session fix, each affects every component, and both look exactly like a knowledge gap when a report arrives.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics should be closed during DP1?
faqs.answer: Mole and concentration calculations first, because they are taught early, they are finite procedures that close in about four sessions, and carrying them into DP2 means they compete with organic chemistry for the same weeks. Then explanation structure in bonding, which is the habit that the Higher Level extended-response questions will later test. Energetics and Hess cycles can wait, because procedures close whenever they are attempted.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level chemistry commit us to a long tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: Potentially, and that is worth knowing before the level is chosen. The two Higher Level additions that most affect a calendar are organic mechanisms and the thermodynamics extension, and both are the slow kind of work falling in DP2. If a target course requires Higher Level chemistry, the commitment is justified. If none does, Higher Level chosen for how it looks will consume months of hours on mechanisms that no application required.

faqs.question: Can practical chemistry skills be taught without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: Most of the assessed practical reasoning can, because it is expressed in writing: choosing an appropriate method, distinguishing systematic from random error, explaining a repeat, and suggesting a specific rather than generic improvement. The laboratory belongs to the school, where the apparatus and technicians are, and a tutor should not pretend to replace it. What a tutor adds is the planning before the bench and honest interpretation afterwards.

faqs.question: Does weak mathematics hold back a chemistry grade?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is the commonest misdiagnosis in the subject. Mole and concentration work, gas law calculations, pH and equilibrium constants all depend on rearranging formulae, handling indices and standard form, and manipulating units. A student without fluency appears weak across several chemistry topics, because the same deficiency resurfaces with different chemical labels. Fixing the mathematics first can lift chemistry without anybody being paid to teach chemistry.

faqs.question: What should the first month of a chemistry plan change?
faqs.answer: Three things and no grade. Your child should be able to name which cause is costing them marks, stated as booklet, command term, procedure or reasoning. You should hold a written note saying the same. And one habit should visibly change, most often reaching for the data booklet rather than trying to recall, or writing working out in full so method marks can be awarded. Grade movement takes longer than a month.

faqs.question: Why are no IB chemistry session dates published on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around is the worst kind of error a tutoring page can make. UAE schools sit the May examinations. Your child's IB coordinator holds the real windows and, more importantly for planning, the internal investigation deadline that actually governs when chemistry tuition is worth buying.

The first session establishes where in the two-year calendar the student actually is, because that decides what the hours should do.

intro.heading: The chemistry year has three pressure points and they do not move
paragraphs: Chemistry in the Diploma has a shape, and most families meet it one crisis at a time rather than as a whole. The first pressure point is the investigation, worth 20% of the grade, whose school deadline usually falls in Year 12 or early Year 13 and which requires laboratory access the school controls. The second is organic chemistry, which in many schemes of work arrives in the second year and lands on a cohort already managing Extended Essay and university applications. The third is the May papers, which are fixed.

A plan that treats the subject as one long run-up to May will arrive after the first two have already happened. That is why this page is organised as a calendar rather than as a topic list. The content is the same content everywhere; what differs between a useful tutoring plan and an expensive one is whether the hours land where the deadlines are. For Dubai South families specifically, that means asking the school's IB coordinator two questions early: when is the investigation due, and when does the scheme of work reach organic.

The marks in chemistry are distributed in a way that rewards this planning. The investigation is 20% and can be secured months in advance. Paper 2 carries around 36% at Higher Level and rewards multi-step calculation discipline. Paper 1 awards nothing for method, so a correct mechanism with one arrow starting in the wrong place scores nothing. At Higher Level, Paper 3 covers data analysis and the option topic separately and is met last by nearly everybody.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script, the markband and the data booklet open on a shared screen and mechanisms drawn on a shared surface that is saved. For chemistry that persistence is useful in a specific way: a curly arrow drawn from the wrong lone pair in week three and again in week nine is visible on the record rather than recalled as carelessness.

One factual note. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the ratings. It does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Ask to see it, then ask whether they have taught Chemistry at the level your child is sitting. The permit licenses somebody to teach privately in the UAE; it says nothing about whether they have marked a Higher Level mechanism question, which is the question that decides whether the hours will be useful.
