programmes.name: Diploma Programme chemistry
programmes.description: Taken at Higher or Standard Level, with Papers 1 and 2 at both levels, Paper 3 added at Higher Level, and the scientific investigation worth 20%. Higher Level adds entropy and spontaneity, equilibrium calculations, transition metal chemistry and deeper organic content. The data booklet and periodic table are supplied in the examination, and most candidates have never located anything in them beforehand.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South Diploma candidates sit the May session. The dates that actually govern the chemistry year are internal: the investigation draft and submission deadlines, the laboratory access window, and the mock. Those come from the school and differ by several weeks between the Dubai Investments Park and Dubailand schools, which is why the first conversation is about dates rather than topics.

programmes.name: Middle Years Sciences
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria from A to D on a 0-8 scale, converted to a 1-7 grade. Criterion B rewards inquiring and designing and criterion D rewards reflecting on the impacts of science, so a student can hold a strong grade with good investigation design while quantitative chemistry lags. That gap shows up in Diploma mole calculations, where arithmetic and unit discipline decide the mark.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving from Middle Years Sciences into Diploma Chemistry in this cluster usually need a short quantitative block rather than content revision: moles, concentrations, limiting reagents and significant figures. Four to six sessions across the summer before Year 12 closes most of it, and skipping it costs a term of Year 12 while new content arrives on top.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 is the usual entry route. The gap to Diploma Chemistry is depth rather than breadth: IGCSE organic chemistry is nomenclature and reaction type, while Diploma organic requires mechanisms with electron movement shown correctly. Energetics and equilibrium also deepen substantially, from qualitative description to calculation.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools in the Al Furjan and Jebel Ali arc feed Diploma cohorts elsewhere in Dubai, so a student may change school and system at sixteen. That transition needs the gap written down over the summer, because Diploma Chemistry assumes a quantitative confidence the IGCSE course did not demand.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where chemistry is taken as one of the Diploma courses within the Career-related Programme, it is examined identically, investigation included. Students on this route sometimes have fewer timetabled contact hours for the same assessment, which makes laboratory access harder to arrange and independent practice between sessions more important rather than less.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is uncommon in this part of Dubai, so a family whose child takes chemistry within it has no local comparison for whether an investigation is on track. A specialist who has supervised the component elsewhere is the practical remedy, and online delivery is the only route to one from Dubai South.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The components and topics a Dubai South chemistry student needs work on, grouped by when in the two years they usually become urgent.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas volumes. The foundation everything quantitative rests on, and the place a weak Year 12 start does lasting damage. Marks are lost to unit slips between grams and moles and to early rounding that propagates through a multi-step chain to a rejected final answer.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and bonding
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends, hybridisation and intermolecular forces. The questions ask for explanation rather than recall: why a trend exists rather than what it is. Higher Level adds depth on orbital shapes and on the relationship between structure and physical property.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and calorimetry. Higher Level adds entropy and Gibbs free energy, which arrive late and are reliably rushed. Sign conventions cause more losses here than any calculation does, and a stated sign with a stated reason earns marks a bare number does not.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Le Chatelier qualitatively at both levels, with equilibrium constant calculations added at Higher Level. The Higher Level calculations arrive in the second year and are among the most improvable content in the course, because they are procedural: set up the table, substitute, solve, check the assumption.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and pH
subjects.description: Strong and weak acid behaviour, pH and the logarithmic scale, buffers and titration curves at Higher Level. Marks go on treating a weak acid as if it were strong, and on titration curve questions where the half-equivalence point and its relationship to the dissociation constant are not recognised.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrochemical cells and electrolysis, with electrode potentials added at Higher Level. Half-equations attempted without balancing charge score nothing, which is a mechanical check students skip under time pressure. Cell diagrams reward a learned convention rather than reasoning.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Nomenclature, functional groups, reaction types and, at Higher Level, mechanisms with curly arrows showing electron movement. An arrow starting from the wrong lone pair or bond earns nothing, and examiners do not award a half-drawn mechanism. The single largest source of lost Higher Level marks in the subject.

subjects.name: Spectroscopy and structure determination
subjects.description: Mass spectrometry, infrared and, at Higher Level, nuclear magnetic resonance. Entirely dependent on the data booklet, which supplies the characteristic absorptions and chemical shifts. A student who has never opened the relevant pages will lose marks that require only looking something up correctly.

subjects.name: Transition metals at Higher Level
subjects.description: Complex ions, ligands, colour and catalytic behaviour. Arrives late, is examined reliably, and responds well to a short focused block because the content is bounded. Marks go on naming the ligand arrangement and on explaining colour in terms of d-orbital splitting rather than describing it.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Worth 20% of the grade, marked on criteria rewarding a methodology addressing all relevant variables and processing that is correct and includes uncertainties. In chemistry it is additionally constrained by what the school laboratory can safely supply, which makes question selection a practical negotiation rather than a free choice.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: Data analysis questions plus the chosen option topic, examined separately from the core. Met last by almost every candidate and under-practised accordingly. The data-analysis question types repeat across sessions, which makes arriving unpractised a straightforward waste of accessible marks.

subjects.name: Calculation chains and significant figures
subjects.description: Not a syllabus topic but a marked skill. A multi-step calculation with a value rounded early produces a final answer the mark scheme will reject even when every step was right. Carrying full precision through and rounding only at the end is a two-session habit that recovers marks across every paper.

sections.heading: The two-year chemistry calendar and what each term holds
paragraphs: Chemistry is taught in an order, and the order has consequences for when tutoring is worth buying. Year 12 generally carries stoichiometry, atomic structure, bonding and the beginnings of energetics. Year 13 generally carries equilibrium, acids and bases, redox, organic chemistry and, at Higher Level, transition metals and entropy. That means the content most likely to be weak in March is content the student only met in January.

The planning consequence is counter-intuitive. The best time to buy chemistry support is Year 12, when the quantitative foundation is being laid and a weakness can be repaired slowly while the class is still introducing topics. The most common time to buy it is the spring of Year 13, when half the syllabus is three months old and the investigation has already been submitted. Both are useful; they are not equally useful per hour.

The investigation sits across this awkwardly. Its deadline is set by the school and typically falls while the student is still mid-course, which means the experiment has to be designed using the chemistry available so far rather than the chemistry they will know in May. That constraint is one of the reasons chemistry investigations go wrong: students pick a question whose analysis needs a topic they have not yet been taught.

The table lays the year out against what tutoring should do in each period. Place it against your own school's scheme of work rather than reading it as universal, because schools in this cluster reach organic chemistry at noticeably different points. Asking the department when organic lands, and when the laboratory is available for investigation work, converts this table from general advice into a plan.

sections.heading: The investigation, counted backwards and constrained by the laboratory
paragraphs: A chemistry investigation is not a free choice of question. It is a question that has to be answerable with reagents and equipment the school can safely supply, within a laboratory window the department controls, using analysis the student has already been taught. Those three constraints are the reason chemistry investigations go wrong more often than physics ones, and all three are known in advance.

Counted backwards from the school's submission date, the sequence runs: question negotiated against what the laboratory can supply, a pilot run to check that concentrations and timings produce a measurable change, booked laboratory time for the real data collection, processing with uncertainties, a complete draft in time for the one permitted round of substantive feedback, and submission. Students routinely skip the pilot and discover during real collection that the reaction is too fast or the change too small to measure.

The criteria reward specific things and they are published. The exploration criterion rewards a methodology addressing all relevant variables, which in chemistry usually means temperature control, concentration accuracy and the limits of the measuring equipment. The analysis criterion rewards processing that is correct and includes uncertainties, so a set of clean titration results with no error treatment caps the mark however neat the write-up is.

The boundary on help is firm. A tutor may teach the chemistry, discuss a proposed question and reject one the laboratory cannot support, insist on a pilot, explain each criterion with its mark allocation, and give feedback on a complete draft the student has written. A tutor may not write a section, supply data, rewrite the analysis or edit to completion. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; a malpractice finding falls on the student's Diploma, so that offer should be refused on sight.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, and why it arrives at the worst possible time
paragraphs: In most schemes of work organic chemistry lands in Year 13, frequently in the winter term. That places it on a cohort simultaneously finishing an Extended Essay, completing university applications and sitting mocks. It is also the topic with the least forgiving mark scheme in the subject, because a mechanism is either drawn correctly or it is not: an arrow starting from the wrong lone pair or the wrong bond earns nothing, and examiners do not award a half-drawn mechanism.

The failure mode is specific and it is not laziness. Students learn mechanisms as pictures to reproduce rather than as electron movements with a reason, which works until a question presents an unfamiliar substrate. At that point a student who memorised six diagrams has nothing to fall back on, while a student who can say where the electrons start and why will construct the right arrows for a reaction they have never seen. Teaching the second takes longer and survives the examination.

The remedy is volume with articulation. Each mechanism drawn repeatedly, with the origin of every arrow stated aloud before the pen moves, until the statement is automatic. Four to six sessions does this properly for Higher Level. Drawing on a shared digital surface matters here more than in most topics, because the same wrong arrow origin reappearing three weeks later is visible on the saved record rather than remembered as general carelessness.

There is a timing argument too. A student who previews organic nomenclature and the main reaction types over the summer before Year 13 arrives at the taught course with the vocabulary already in place, which converts a hard winter term into a manageable one. That is one of the better uses of a summer block in this subject, and it costs four to six sessions at a point in the year when nothing is competing for them.

sections.heading: Calculation chains, rounding and the marks that vanish quietly
paragraphs: Chemistry is full of multi-step calculations, and the mark scheme is unforgiving about the end of them. A student who rounds an intermediate value to three significant figures in step two will produce a final answer far enough from the accepted value that the accuracy mark is refused, even though every step of the method was correct. The method marks usually survive; the final mark does not, and in a multi-mark question that can be most of it.

The habit to build is simple and unnatural: carry full calculator precision through every intermediate step and round only the final stated answer, to the number of significant figures the question or the data justifies. Students round early because it looks tidy and because it feels like showing care. Naming that specifically, with a marked script in front of them where it happened, changes the habit faster than any general instruction to be careful.

The second quiet loss is units. A concentration quoted without mol per cubic decimetre, an enthalpy change without kilojoules per mole, a volume slipped between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres. These are checkable mechanically: writing the unit beside every quantity as it is written down catches nearly all of them. The third is the sign on an enthalpy or free energy change, where a stated sign with a stated reason earns marks that a bare number does not.

The fourth is balancing. Half-equations attempted without balancing charge, and ionic equations written with the species but not the charges reconciled, score nothing despite being nearly right. That is a mechanical check that takes seconds and gets skipped under time pressure. All four of these are visible on a marked Paper 2 script within a few minutes, which is why the first chemistry session reads a script rather than beginning a topic.

sections.heading: The data booklet and periodic table: what is supplied and what is not
paragraphs: Chemistry supplies more reference material in the examination than most subjects, and candidates routinely under-use it. The data booklet carries relationships, constants, characteristic infrared absorptions and nuclear magnetic resonance chemical shifts. The periodic table supplies relative atomic masses. A student who has never opened the relevant pages will lose marks on questions that require nothing more than looking something up correctly, and will waste time recalling things that were printed.

Spectroscopy is the clearest case. Infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance questions are essentially data-booklet exercises: match the absorption to the functional group, match the chemical shift to the environment, count the equivalent protons. A candidate fluent in those pages answers them quickly and reliably. A candidate meeting the pages for the first time under time pressure will guess. The difference is twenty minutes of reading at home, weeks earlier.

There is an equally important negative list: what the booklet does not supply. Definitions, mechanisms, qualitative explanations and the reasoning behind a trend all have to be known. Students who assume everything is provided arrive without having memorised the small set of things that are genuinely required, which is a worse error than the opposite one because it is invisible until the paper.

The practical action is a session spent with the booklet open, annotating which pages matter for which topic and which question types are effectively look-up exercises. It is unglamorous, it takes an hour, and it is among the highest-return hours available in the subject. The table below groups the common question types by whether the booklet answers them.

sections.heading: From the mock to May: the eight-week chemistry block
paragraphs: The spring of Year 13 is when most Dubai South families arrange chemistry support, and the plan that works is narrow. Eight weeks, two sessions a week, structured in four fortnights with a job each and a timed checkpoint at the end of each. It cannot cover the syllabus and should not try. What it can do is attack what the mock script exposes, in priority order, and convert content the student half-knows into marks.

Week one reads the script and teaches nothing. The findings that matter are whether the paper was finished, whether the losses are concentrated in a few topics or spread thinly, and whether marks went on chemistry the student does not know or on calculation discipline they do. Those three produce three different plans from the same grade, and teaching in the first hour makes the remaining fifteen sessions less accurate.

Chemistry has one legitimate exception to the no-new-content rule. Topics that arrived in January — frequently organic at Higher Level, or transition metals, or entropy — may genuinely not have been taught properly before the mock, in which case they are not revision but first teaching. Identifying which topics those are is part of week one, because a student cannot revise something they never covered and the distinction changes the plan entirely.

The final fortnight is whole papers and pacing. At Higher Level that has to include Paper 3, because its data-analysis and option content is examined separately and most candidates arrive never having attempted a whole one. A block that reaches the final fortnight without Paper 3 practice has left accessible marks on the table, and the table below places it deliberately rather than leaving it to whatever time remains.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the breaks and laboratory access
paragraphs: The UAE calendar interacts with chemistry in one way it does not with other subjects: laboratory access. Investigation data collection needs booked laboratory time with technician support, and that availability narrows during shortened school days and disappears during the breaks. A student planning to collect data in the spring break will find the laboratory closed, which is an obvious point that is nonetheless discovered late every year.

During Ramadan, school hours shorten and afternoon concentration drops. The practical adjustments for chemistry are to move sessions after iftar, shorten them from ninety minutes to sixty, and switch from new content to timed question practice, which costs less concentration per mark gained. Mechanism drill is a reasonable exception, because it is repetitive rather than demanding and holds up better late in the evening than a Hess cycle does.

The breaks are where the uninterrupted work belongs. A full timed Paper 2 marked and reviewed within forty-eight hours while the student still remembers their reasoning needs consecutive days, not a weekly hour. So does writing up an investigation whose data was collected earlier in term. The winter break of Year 13 is the single most valuable fortnight in the chemistry calendar and the one most often spent on nothing in particular.

For a Year 12 student the summer before Year 13 is the equivalent opportunity. Four to six sessions closing quantitative gaps and previewing organic nomenclature converts the hardest term of the course into an ordinary one. Nothing competes for the time, the student is rested, and the material is exactly the material that will arrive in January. In this cluster that block is the most under-booked thing we offer and the one that changes the most.

sections.heading: Shaping chemistry spend across two years, in AED
paragraphs: Because chemistry has three fixed pressure points, a flat weekly commitment across two years spends money in the wrong places. The sensible shape is a lighter Year 12 aimed at quantitative fluency, a concentrated block around the investigation, a summer block before Year 13 covering gaps and previewing organic, then a heavier spring for mechanisms, timed papers and Paper 3 at Higher Level.

The bands to budget against are published. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 a month for budget provision, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Published monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Hourly, the ladder is clear. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the budget end, both online and typically delivered by university students. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or more, and BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350, with independent tutors up to AED 500 once travel is in the hour.

In chemistry specifically the cheap hour is frequently the expensive one. A student losing marks to early rounding, missing units and misdrawn mechanisms needs somebody who recognises those as separate marked faults. A generalist will reteach the topic, which the student broadly has, and the next script will look the same. Every figure above belongs to the provider named; these are market bands, not an IB Gram price list, and our own conversation begins with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: When does organic chemistry arrive in the IB course?
faqs.answer: In most schemes of work it lands in Year 13, often in the winter term, which puts it on a cohort simultaneously finishing an Extended Essay, completing university applications and sitting mocks. Schools in this part of Dubai reach it at noticeably different points, so the only reliable answer comes from asking your child's department. The timing matters because organic has the least forgiving mark scheme in the subject and because a summer preview of nomenclature and reaction types converts a difficult winter term into an ordinary one.

faqs.question: Why do mechanism marks disappear entirely rather than partly?
faqs.answer: Because a curly arrow either starts from the correct lone pair or bond or it does not, and examiners do not award a half-drawn mechanism. A student who learned mechanisms as pictures to reproduce can handle the six they memorised and has nothing to fall back on when a question presents an unfamiliar substrate. A student who can say where the electrons start and why will construct correct arrows for a reaction they have never seen. Teaching the second takes four to six sessions and survives the examination hall.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Chemistry grade is the investigation?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Higher and Standard Level. It is marked on criteria that reward a methodology addressing all relevant variables and processing that is correct and includes uncertainties, so a set of clean titration results with no error treatment caps the mark however neat the report looks. In chemistry it carries an extra constraint: the question has to be answerable with reagents and equipment the school can safely supply, within laboratory time the department controls, using analysis the student has already been taught.

faqs.question: What does early rounding actually cost in a chemistry calculation?
faqs.answer: The accuracy mark on an otherwise correct question, which in a multi-mark calculation can be most of the available credit. Rounding an intermediate value to three significant figures in step two produces a final answer far enough from the accepted value that the mark scheme refuses it, even though every step of the method was right. The habit to build is carrying full calculator precision through and rounding only the final stated answer, to the significant figures the data justifies. It is a two-session fix.

faqs.question: Which pages of the chemistry data booklet matter most?
faqs.answer: The characteristic infrared absorption ranges and, at Higher Level, the nuclear magnetic resonance chemical shift ranges, because spectroscopy questions are effectively look-up exercises for a candidate who knows where to look and guesswork for one who does not. Relative atomic masses come from the periodic table. Equally important is the negative list: definitions, mechanisms and the reasoning behind a trend are not supplied and must be known. An hour spent annotating the booklet weeks in advance is among the highest-return revision actions in the subject.

faqs.question: Can my child collect investigation data during the spring break?
faqs.answer: Almost never, because the school laboratory will be closed and technician support unavailable. This is an obvious constraint that is nonetheless discovered late every year. Data collection has to be booked into term time, which means the question must be settled and the pilot run completed before the break rather than during it. What the breaks are genuinely good for is the write-up: processing data already collected, and drafting, both of which need consecutive uninterrupted days rather than a weekly hour.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level chemistry add for a Dubai South student?
faqs.answer: Content, a third paper and a higher analytical bar. It adds content, adds Paper 3, and raises the analytical demand of the markbands at the top. The additional content is entropy and spontaneity, equilibrium calculations, transition metal chemistry and deeper organic, and most of it arrives in Year 13 when time is already short. Paper 3 is the component that catches unprepared Higher Level candidates, because it examines data analysis and a chosen option separately from the core, so revising Papers 1 and 2 content does not prepare anyone for it.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai South student do in the summer before Year 13?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions closing quantitative gaps and previewing organic nomenclature and the main reaction types. Nothing competes for the time, the student is rested, and the material is exactly what will arrive in the hardest term of the course. In this cluster that block is the most under-booked thing we offer and the one that changes the most, because it converts a winter term carrying organic, mocks, the Extended Essay and applications into a term carrying three of those rather than four.

faqs.question: Why do half-equations score nothing when they look nearly right?
faqs.answer: Because a half-equation that balances atoms but not charge is not a valid equation, and the mark scheme treats it accordingly. Students lose these marks under time pressure, not through ignorance: the charge check takes seconds and gets skipped. The same applies to ionic equations where the species are right and the charges are never reconciled. Building the check into the writing habit, rather than leaving it as a final review step that never happens, is the fix and it takes about one session to establish.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to a Dubai South address?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script, the markband and the data booklet open on a shared screen and mechanisms drawn on a shared surface that is saved week to week. For chemistry that record earns its keep, because a wrong arrow origin recurring across three weeks becomes evidence rather than an impression.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start chemistry tutoring in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Year 12, and this is the opposite of when most families start. In the first year the quantitative foundation is being laid, the class is still introducing topics, and a weakness can be repaired slowly rather than patched. By the spring of Year 13 half the syllabus is three months old, the investigation has been submitted, and the same hours buy less. Both are worth doing. They are simply not equally valuable per hour, and the difference is large enough to be worth acting on.

faqs.question: What goes in the final fortnight of a chemistry plan?
faqs.answer: Whole papers and pacing, with nothing new attempted, and at Higher Level that must include Paper 3. Most Higher Level candidates arrive at May never having attempted a whole Paper 3, which leaves accessible marks behind because its data-analysis question types repeat across sessions. Three or four short sessions a week work better than two long ones at that stage, because concentration rather than available time is the limit. The night-before material should be a one-page list, not a textbook.

faqs.question: Can a tutor suggest my child's investigation question?
faqs.answer: A tutor may discuss a question the student proposes, reject one the laboratory cannot support or whose analysis needs chemistry not yet taught, and push until the question is answerable. What a tutor may not do is choose it on the student's behalf, supply data, write any section or edit a draft to completion. The permitted feedback is one round on one complete draft the student has written. A malpractice finding falls on the student's Diploma, which is why any offer of a finished investigation should be refused on sight.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change chemistry sessions in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and afternoon concentration drops, so sessions move later into the evening after iftar and shorten from ninety minutes to sixty. Content teaching gives way to timed question practice, which costs less concentration per mark gained. Mechanism drill is a reasonable exception, because it is repetitive rather than cognitively demanding and holds up late in the evening better than a Hess cycle does. Dropping from two sessions a week to one for the month, and moving heavy work into the spring break, usually works better than persisting.

faqs.question: What does chemistry support cost across two years in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the shape more than the rate. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, and qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. A plan that is lighter in Year 12, concentrated around the investigation and the summer, then heavier in the spring of Year 13 costs less than a flat weekly commitment. These are market bands from the providers named, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.answer: Most students on this page are in the Dubai Investments Park and Green Community cluster, where IB continuum provision sits alongside British and SABIS schools, or travel east to the Dubailand corridor for an IB continuum school. Those Dubailand schools supply most of the Higher Level chemistry demand in this corner of the emirate. KHDA publishes annual inspection ratings for every one of them on its own site, which is the document worth reading before an admissions conversation. intro.heading: Chemistry fails on a schedule
paragraphs: Chemistry has a more predictable failure pattern than any other Diploma science, and it is a calendar pattern rather than an ability one. The subject is taught in an order that compounds: stoichiometry early, then bonding and energetics built on it, then kinetics and equilibrium built on those, then organic chemistry late in the second year on top of everything. A student who leaves the first topic half-learned pays interest on it for two years.

That is why so many Sports City enquiries arrive in the same window. A student holds a 5 through the first year, meets organic chemistry in the second, and the grade collapses. The diagnosis families reach is that organic chemistry is hard. The actual diagnosis, most of the time, is that mole calculations were never secure, so every quantitative question in organic chemistry now has two obstacles instead of one.

The second predictable pressure is the scientific investigation, and its timing is less flexible than other coursework because it needs school laboratory access. An essay can be written at midnight. A chemistry investigation cannot be run at midnight, cannot be repeated after the laboratory timetable closes, and cannot be rescued by working harder in the final fortnight. Its research question has to be settled while there is still room for the data collection to fail once.

The third is the extra written paper at Higher Level, which adds both content and a paper type most students meet for the first time in a mock. Higher Level chemistry extends every topic rather than appending a few, so a student deciding between levels in the pre-Diploma year is choosing between two genuinely different workloads rather than between a long version and a short one.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For chemistry the online format has a concrete advantage: calculation layout is what the mark scheme pays for, and a shared screen lets a tutor watch the working appear line by line and stop at the step where the method broke.

The practical gain is also in matching. Diploma chemistry cohorts in this part of Dubailand are small, and the number of local tutors who have taught the Higher Level extensions and marked the extended papers is smaller. Matching by level and component rather than by driving distance is what makes a block in the second year worth buying at all.

What follows is the subject on a timeline: the syllabus in teaching order with the dependency each topic hides, why organic chemistry gets one pass and how to survive it, the investigation counted backwards from laboratory access, and what eight weeks before a paper should actually contain.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubai-sports.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is a small number of recurring demands dressed in different topics. Each entry below names what the topic assumes and where the paper withholds marks.

subjects.name: Stoichiometric relationships
subjects.description: Moles, molar mass, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas volumes. Every quantitative topic later in the course assumes this is automatic. Marks are lost to layout rather than to arithmetic: the relationship not written before substitution, so method marks are unavailable.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energies and periodic trends, with Higher Level extending into orbital detail. Trend questions require a reason, not a statement: 'ionisation energy increases' scores nothing without nuclear charge and shielding named.

subjects.name: Chemical bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, shapes of molecules and, at Higher Level, hybridisation and further structure. Students lose marks explaining boiling points by naming the bond type instead of the intermolecular force actually being overcome.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, calorimetry, Hess's law, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and spontaneity. Sign conventions decide the marks. An exothermic value given as positive loses the mark however correct the arithmetic behind it.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.description: Rate of reaction, collision theory, activation energy and, at Higher Level, rate laws and mechanisms. Explanation questions want a mechanism in words: more frequent successful collisions, not simply 'the reaction goes faster'.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Dynamic equilibrium, Le Chatelier's principle and, at Higher Level, the equilibrium constant and its calculations. The widest mark spread in the course. Students can define Le Chatelier and cannot apply it to a specific perturbation, which is a diagnosable gap in one session.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.description: Proton transfer, pH, strong and weak acids and, at Higher Level, buffers and titration curves. Logarithmic handling trips students who are otherwise sound, and titration curve questions reward reading specific features rather than describing the shape in general.

subjects.name: Redox processes
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrochemical cells and electrolysis, with Higher Level extending into cell potentials. Half-equations lose marks for unbalanced charge as often as unbalanced mass, and both checks take seconds once they are habitual.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Functional groups, nomenclature, reaction types and mechanisms, with substantially more mechanism work at Higher Level. Taught late, with one pass through it for most students. Mechanism marks depend on curly arrows drawn from the correct origin, which is a convention rather than an insight.

subjects.name: Measurement, analysis and the investigation
subjects.description: Uncertainty, error propagation, spectroscopic interpretation and the internally assessed investigation. Roughly half the investigation marks concern research design, analysis and evaluation rather than the result, which is why a sound experiment with a thin evaluation under-scores.

sections.heading: What an IB chemistry tutor in Dubai Sports City provides
paragraphs: An IB chemistry tutor in Dubai Sports City means one-to-one Diploma chemistry teaching arranged outside school for a student in or around the Sports City master plan, and IB Gram provides it live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is stated here rather than left to emerge after a deposit.

The skill a family is actually buying is sequencing. Chemistry is the Diploma science where the order of work matters most, because the topics are not independent. Teaching equilibrium to a student whose mole calculations are shaky produces a session that feels useful and a paper that does not improve. A tutor who diagnoses the dependency first will often spend the opening weeks of a block on material the student met eighteen months earlier.

The second skill is calculation layout. Chemistry mark schemes award method marks for the structure of the working — the relationship stated, the substitution shown, the units carried — and students who compute confidently in their heads lose marks they have earned. This is mechanical, it is teachable in about three weeks, and it is invisible to anyone who has not read a mark scheme alongside a marked script.

What is not provided is any help with producing the investigation. A tutor teaches the published criteria, questions the variable control, discusses whether the data supports the conclusion, and gives feedback on what the student has written. Writing, completing or producing any part of the report is a malpractice finding against the student, and pages competing for these searches that sell finished internal assessments are selling that risk to the candidate.

sections.heading: The syllabus in teaching order, and the debt each topic hides
paragraphs: Most schools teach Diploma chemistry in broadly the same order, and that order creates a specific pattern of accumulating dependency. Stoichiometry comes first because everything quantitative needs it. Atomic structure and bonding follow, then energetics, then kinetics and equilibrium, then acids and bases and redox, with organic chemistry and the heavier analysis work late in the second year.

Each of those transitions assumes the previous material is automatic rather than merely familiar. Energetics assumes moles. Equilibrium assumes both moles and an understanding of reversible processes from kinetics. Redox assumes charge balancing that was introduced in bonding. Organic chemistry assumes all of it and then adds its own conventions. Nothing in a school report tells a parent which assumption has failed.

The diagnostic that works is to take a question from a late topic and watch where the student stops. A student who stalls at the point of converting a concentration to a number of moles has a first-term problem, not an organic chemistry problem, and treating it as the latter wastes the block. This is the single most common misdiagnosis in Diploma chemistry and it costs families a term routinely.

The table below sets the teaching sequence against the dependency each stage hides and what should be secure before moving on. It is written to be used in the first Diploma year, when the checks are cheap, rather than in the second, when they are expensive. Each check takes a few minutes and can be run at home: give the student one question of that type, time it, and watch whether the answer arrives with hesitation or without. Hesitation is the signal, not a wrong answer, because a student who gets there slowly in a quiet room will not get there at all inside a timed paper with five other questions waiting.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry gets one pass, and it comes late
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is taught late and, for most students in Dubai schools, taught once. There is no second pass before the papers, because by the time it finishes the calendar has moved into mocks and then into the final weeks. Whatever a student understands at the end of that single pass is roughly what they take into the examination unless something is done deliberately.

That changes how it should be revised. The content divides cleanly into three kinds of knowledge: nomenclature and functional group recognition, which is memorisation; reaction types and conditions, which is organised memorisation; and mechanisms, which is convention plus reasoning. The first two respond to spaced repetition and can be built in the background from the week the topic starts. Only the third needs teaching.

Mechanism marks turn on conventions nobody states explicitly. A curly arrow has to start from a lone pair or a bond rather than from an atom. Charges have to appear on intermediates. The arrow has to point to where the electrons go, not to where the next atom is. Students who draw mechanisms that look right and score badly are almost always failing on these conventions rather than on the chemistry.

The practical recommendation for a Sports City family is to treat organic chemistry as a scheduling problem in advance. Start the memorisation work the week the school starts the topic rather than the week before the mock, and book any tutoring for the second half of the pass, when there is enough content for mechanism work to be meaningful. A block that arrives after the pass has finished is doing repair rather than teaching.

Reactions and conditions: organised memorisation, built in the background
Mechanisms: conventions taught explicitly, then practised

sections.heading: The investigation, counted backwards from laboratory access
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation is the component with the least flexible timeline in chemistry, because its middle requires a laboratory. A student cannot collect data at home, cannot repeat a failed run after the laboratory timetable closes, and cannot compensate for thin data by writing more. That makes the backwards count from the school deadline tighter than for coursework in other subjects.

Working backwards, the final week is formatting and a criterion check, with no chemistry happening. The fortnight before is analysis, uncertainty propagation and evaluation. Before that sits the data collection, which has to be scheduled with the school and should have room for one failure. Before that is the research question, and that is where a block earns most of its value, because an unworkable question discovered during data collection cannot be rescued.

Research questions fail in predictable ways. Too broad to be answered in the space available. Dependent on apparatus the school does not have. Involving a variable that cannot practically be controlled. Or producing data with so little variation that no meaningful conclusion is available. A specialist can identify all four in a single conversation, which is why that conversation should happen a term before submission and not a fortnight before.

The criteria themselves are published, and roughly half the available marks concern research design, analysis and evaluation rather than the result. A student who runs a competent experiment and writes two sentences of evaluation loses marks that no additional data would have recovered. Self-marking a draft against each criterion, with the mark ceiling for each made explicit, is the highest-return session on this component.

sections.heading: Eight weeks before a chemistry paper
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most Sports City families ask for, usually after a mock. In chemistry it has a reasonably well-defined best use, and it is not working through the syllabus from the beginning. The content is too large and the dependencies mean the early weeks would be spent on material that may already be secure.

A better eight weeks starts with a diagnosis of where the student stops rather than what they do not know. One session of mixed questions from late topics, watching for the point of failure, separates a stoichiometry problem from an equilibrium problem from a presentation problem. The remaining seven weeks then have a target rather than a syllabus.

If the diagnosis is calculation layout, three weeks fixes it and the remaining weeks go to the two most examinable weak topics. If it is stoichiometry, the first four weeks clear the debt and the rest consolidates the topics that depend on it. If it is organic mechanism conventions, that is two weeks of convention work followed by drilled practice. Each of those is a different eight weeks.

What eight weeks will not do is cover two years of chemistry, and a provider who accepts the booking on that basis is selling hope. The table sets out what each diagnosis implies, which is the version of this conversation worth having before any money changes hands.

One further point about the eight weeks: the omissions should be written down. A plan that names what it will not revise is a plan a student can follow without guilt, and guilt is what drives the unproductive pattern of re-reading everything lightly. Deciding in week one that spectroscopic detail and nomenclature will be handled by self-study, and that two named topics will be left alone, frees the sessions to do work that shows up on a paper.

sections.heading: Where chemistry marks are withheld
paragraphs: Chemistry mark schemes are specific about what they reward, and the reasons marks are withheld fall into a short and repeating list. Students who have never read a scheme alongside their own script are guessing at what earns credit, and the guessing is systematic rather than random.

The largest category is calculation presentation. The relationship not written before substitution, so method marks are unavailable. An intermediate value rounded and carried, so the accuracy mark goes. Units omitted. A concentration given in the wrong unit. Each is worth a mark, each repeats across the paper, and none is about chemistry.

The second is explanation specificity. A boiling-point question answered by naming the bond type instead of the intermediate force being overcome. A trend stated without nuclear charge and shielding named. 'The reaction is faster' offered where the scheme wants more frequent successful collisions. The chemistry is understood; the sentence does not contain the thing being marked.

The third is convention: half-equations unbalanced for charge, enthalpy signs reversed, curly arrows starting at atoms, oxidation states assigned without checking the total. All three categories are mechanical and all three respond to a few weeks of deliberate attention, which is why a first block should count them on a marked script before deciding to teach anything.

The counting exercise is worth doing at home before any tutor is involved. Take the last marked chemistry paper, go question by question, and put each lost mark into one of the three categories. If presentation and convention together account for most of the losses, the next block is a technique block and it will be shorter and cheaper than the content block a provider would otherwise propose. If genuine content gaps dominate, the block is longer and the expectations should be set accordingly from the start.
bullets: Write the relationship before substituting; method marks depend on it
Round once, at the end, and carry units through every line
Name the intermolecular force, not the bond type, for boiling points
Balance half-equations for charge as well as for mass
Check enthalpy signs before moving on from any energetics answer

sections.heading: Higher or Standard Level, and when that decision closes
paragraphs: Higher Level chemistry extends every topic rather than appending a few, and adds a further written paper. The practical consequence is that the Higher Level course is not the Standard Level course with more reading: the depth changes within the familiar topics, which is why students who coped with IGCSE chemistry comfortably can still find the extensions hard.

The decision is usually made in the pre-Diploma year from IGCSE or MYP grades, which predict imperfectly. A better predictor is quantitative confidence: how fluently a student handles proportional reasoning, unit conversion and logarithms. Chemistry at Higher Level punishes hesitation there in every topic simultaneously, and a previous science grade does not measure it.

For students already in the first Diploma year and struggling, the question is whether to move down, and the honest answer depends on the intended degree. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemistry-adjacent engineering courses frequently name Higher Level chemistry, and for those the work is to rebuild the quantitative skills and stay. Where no such requirement exists, a strong Standard Level grade generally reads better than a weak Higher Level one.

Whatever the decision, it should be made in the first year rather than the second, because a move after organic chemistry has started leaves a student consolidating a different syllabus under time pressure. The date that matters is the school's own, and a Sports City family should ask the department directly when a level change stops being possible.

sections.heading: What two years of chemistry support actually costs
paragraphs: Families usually ask for an hourly rate and then commit to something much larger, so it is worth looking at the two years as a whole. The published hourly bands in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium named end.

In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026, and none is IB Gram's price list.

Totalled across two years, the mid band at weekly sessions reaches several thousand dirhams, which is a real decision rather than an incidental one. Set against Dubai school fees — and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package — it is a smaller line item, but it is one worth spending deliberately rather than by default.

The deliberate version, in chemistry specifically, concentrates spending at two points: a short stoichiometry block in the first year, and a topic block in the second year once a mock has identified where the student stops. Those two together cost a fraction of two years of unmeasured weekly support and address the dependency pattern that causes the collapse in the first place.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and deliberate omissions
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Tutors are not described as examiners without evidence of current status, and examiner status is never presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content.

Three omissions here are deliberate. No IB session or results dates, because none could be verified from the IB itself. No syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes offered as downloads, because those belong to the boards and are referenced at source instead. And no success statistics, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method cannot be checked by the reader and therefore proves nothing.

The marked script matters more than the report, because the pattern of lost marks shows whether the problem is layout, stoichiometry, a specific topic or timing, and those need different blocks.

process.description: The trial session uses mixed questions from late topics and watches for the point of failure rather than testing knowledge topic by topic. A student who stalls converting a concentration to moles has a first-term problem, and diagnosing that correctly is what stops a block being spent in the wrong place.

process.description: Where the diagnosis points upstream, the opening weeks go to stoichiometry even though the presenting complaint was organic chemistry or equilibrium. That ordering is unintuitive for families and it is the difference between a block that moves a mark and one that produces pleasant sessions.

process.description: Questions are set from past papers and marked by the student against the published scheme during the session, with every withheld mark named. Categories are logged across weeks, so a convention that keeps failing — unsigned enthalpies, unbalanced charge — becomes visible rather than re-explained.

process.description: The target from session one is measured in writing at the halfway point. If the error log shows the same categories, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes at no cost. In an exam year, making that call at week four rather than week eight is the whole difference.

Finding where the student stops, rather than what they have not covered, is the first job of the trial session.

whyPoints.title: Calculation layout treated as marks

Students who compute confidently in their heads lose marks they have earned, and the habit takes about three weeks to change permanently.

faqs.question: Why did my child's chemistry grade collapse in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Usually because the syllabus compounds and a first-year debt has come due. Organic chemistry and equilibrium both assume mole calculations are automatic rather than merely familiar, so a student who was managing with slow stoichiometry now has two obstacles in every quantitative question. The diagnostic is to give a late-topic question and watch where they stop. If they stall converting a concentration to moles, the problem is from the opening term and treating it as organic chemistry wastes the block.

faqs.question: Can an IB chemistry tutor come to a home in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Published in-home rates in this market run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching. For chemistry the online screen is also the better surface, because calculation layout is what earns method marks and it can be watched line by line as it is written.

faqs.question: Which three chemistry calculations matter most at Diploma level?
faqs.answer: Moles from mass using molar mass, moles from concentration and volume for solutions, and limiting reagent or percentage yield work. Between them they underpin energetics, equilibrium, redox and much of organic chemistry. Each has a layout the mark scheme rewards: write the relationship, substitute with units, evaluate, then round once at the end. Installed as three templates and drilled under time, they take four to six sessions and remove a recurring loss across the whole course.

faqs.question: What makes organic chemistry mechanisms score badly even when the answer looks right?
faqs.answer: Conventions rather than chemistry. A curly arrow must start from a lone pair or a bond rather than from an atom, and must point to where the electrons go rather than towards the next atom. Charges have to appear on intermediates. Students who have learned mechanisms by copying finished diagrams reproduce the shape without the conventions and lose most of the available marks. Two weeks of explicit convention work followed by drilled practice usually resolves it.

faqs.question: When does the chemistry investigation need to be started?
faqs.answer: Ten weeks or more before the school deadline, because the middle of it requires laboratory access and a failed data run needs a slot to be repeated. Working backwards: the final week is formatting and a criterion check, the fortnight before is analysis and evaluation, and data collection sits six to eight weeks out with room for one failure. The research question has to be agreed before any of that, and an unworkable question discovered during collection cannot be rescued.

faqs.question: What actually changes between Standard and Higher Level chemistry in Year 12?
faqs.answer: It extends every topic rather than adding a few, and it carries a further written paper, so the depth increases inside familiar material. That is why students who found IGCSE chemistry comfortable can still find the extensions hard. The better predictor than a previous science grade is quantitative confidence: proportional reasoning, unit conversion and logarithms handled without hesitation. Higher Level punishes hesitation there in every topic at once rather than in one.

faqs.question: How much of the investigation mark is the experiment itself?
faqs.answer: Less than students assume. The published criteria cover research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and roughly half the available marks concern process and communication rather than the result. A competent experiment written up with two sentences of evaluation under-scores badly, and no amount of extra data recovers those marks. Self-marking a draft against each criterion, with the mark ceiling for each stated, is the highest-return hour available on this component.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry investigation write-up?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the variable control, discusses whether the data supports the conclusion and gives feedback on what the student has written. A tutor does not write, complete or produce any part of the report. That is an IB academic-honesty rule rather than a preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student. Providers selling finished internal assessments are selling the candidate a risk, not a service.

faqs.question: What should a student revise in the last eight weeks before chemistry papers?
faqs.answer: Whatever the diagnosis names, not the syllabus from the start. If the losses are layout and presentation, three weeks on that plus five on the two most examinable weak topics. If stoichiometry is not automatic, four weeks clearing it and four consolidating what sits on top. If mechanisms are the problem, two weeks of conventions then drilled pathways. Eight weeks cannot cover two years of chemistry, and a plan that pretends otherwise covers everything badly.

faqs.question: Why does equilibrium produce such a wide spread of marks?
faqs.answer: Because students learn Le Chatelier's principle as a statement and are then asked to apply it to a specific perturbation. Reciting that a system shifts to oppose a change is easy; deciding what happens to the yield when pressure rises in a particular reaction with a particular mole ratio is a different task. The gap is diagnosable in one session by asking for three specific perturbations in a row, and it closes with drilled application rather than with re-explanation.

faqs.question: My child is in the first Diploma year and coping. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: A short diagnostic is not premature and may be the cheapest intervention available. Chemistry's dependency structure means a first-year weakness that looks survivable becomes expensive in the second year, and the first year is when a stoichiometry debt can be cleared in four to six sessions without competing with new content. Acting then is a fraction of the cost of a second-year rescue, which is why the first-year enquiry is the one worth making.

faqs.question: Do enthalpy sign errors really cost that many marks?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter. An exothermic enthalpy change given as positive loses the mark however correct the arithmetic behind it, and the same convention recurs through calorimetry, Hess cycles and bond enthalpy calculations. Students treat it as a trivial slip and therefore never fix it, so it reappears in every series. The fix is procedural: check the sign before moving on from any energetics answer, every time, until it stops requiring thought.

faqs.question: What does a chemistry block cost across a Dubai exam year?
faqs.answer: Using Bestimate's published monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions, the specialist exam-year band runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month, and the mid band AED 600 to 1,200. Hourly figures behind them run from AED 33 to 65 at the university-student end up to AED 650 for premium named tutors, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase at AED 270. All are provider-published market rates read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics should be left out of a short revision plan?
faqs.answer: The ones that are both well understood and lightly examined, and the detail at the far end of topics the student will not reach in the time. That decision has to be explicit rather than accidental, because a plan aiming at full coverage in six weeks leaves the recoverable marks undrilled. Nomenclature can usually move to self-study. Spectroscopic detail is often a reasonable omission. What should never be cut is calculation layout, because it earns marks everywhere.

intro.heading: Who near Dubailand has actually taught this chemistry course?
paragraphs: This is the question underneath the search, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a list sorted by distance. IB Chemistry is a specific course with a specific assessment regime, and the useful qualification is not a chemistry degree but recent experience of teaching the Diploma course at the student's level. Those are different things. A chemistry graduate can explain equilibrium competently and still fail to notice that a student is answering describe questions when the paper asked for an explanation, which is where a large share of the marks go.

Scarcity here is not a Dubailand problem; it is a Dubai problem. Higher Level chemistry cohorts at individual schools are often small, which means the number of teachers in the emirate who have taken the course through to the final session recently is smaller than the number who teach science. Independent tutors then cluster where journeys are short, which in this city means the coastal corridor, Al Barsha and Business Bay rather than a villa belt forty minutes inland. Filtering by radius therefore narrows an already thin pool on exactly the wrong axis.

Dubailand makes the geography worse than most people assume. It is a development zone rather than a neighbourhood, running south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and taking in Arabian Ranches and its two later phases, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. Two families who both say they live in Dubailand can be twenty-five minutes apart in evening traffic, so a visiting specialist who works for one is often unavailable to the other at any usable hour.

There is a way to test a tutor's claim in one conversation, and it costs nothing. Ask which level they last taught, ask what the commonest loss is on organic mechanism questions, and ask what they would check first in a draft internal assessment. A specialist answers all three immediately and specifically. A generalist answers in terms of revision and confidence. That exchange is a better filter than any directory, and it works regardless of where either party lives.

IB Gram's position is straightforward. We do not send a tutor to a Dubailand address; home visits are a service we operate only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched on course and level, and the first session is a free trial with no card. Specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates, which is how a household in Town Square reaches a Higher Level chemistry specialist at all. A parent should hear that before paying rather than deduce it afterwards, because the alternative is a family discovering the delivery model from a dialling code.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubailand.programmesIntro: Chemistry reaches a Dubailand student at three stages, and the teaching problem is different at each. These notes say what each stage actually requires.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences marked against four criteria on a 0-8 scale, including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating. The chemistry strands build the habits the Diploma then assumes: balancing equations, reasoning about particles, and explaining rather than describing. Students lose marks by writing a good answer to a question the criterion did not ask.
programmes.countryNote: In this belt MYP students are home earlier than their Diploma siblings and have genuinely usable afternoon time. Families in Arabian Ranches 2 and 3 and Mudon ask for this stage most, often as transition work after a move between a British setting and an IB one.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry Standard Level
programmes.description: The full conceptual range at reduced depth, with written papers and an internal assessment worth 20 per cent. Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry carry the difficulty. The commonest avoidable loss is an equation that balances but omits the state symbols the markscheme requires.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level suits students who need a rigorous science within a broad Diploma rather than a chemistry-based degree. It is also the version that tolerates a shorter weekday session, because the problem sets are less extended than at Higher Level.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry Higher Level
programmes.description: A considerably larger syllabus with additional higher-level content, extended organic chemistry and spectroscopic analysis, and the same 20 per cent internal assessment. Confirm the current paper structure and weightings with the school's coordinator, since the IB science syllabuses were revised recently and no unverified figure belongs on a tutoring page.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level chemistry is a standard requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering applications, which is why Dubailand families often arrive asking for it specifically. Where a degree route is the reason, the level choice should be checked against published entry requirements in the first Diploma year.

programmes.name: The International GCSE route into DP Chemistry
programmes.description: Most students in this belt arrive from Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 rather than from MYP. The step up is in quantitative confidence and in the expectation that mechanisms are reasoned rather than recalled. A student who memorised reactions successfully at sixteen finds the Diploma asks why, repeatedly.
programmes.countryNote: The first Diploma term is where the gap shows, and it is the cheapest point at which to close it. By the second year the syllabus leaves no space to rebuild stoichiometric fluency, and attempting it then displaces revision the student also needs.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: Chemistry divides into strands with distinct failure patterns, which is what makes a precise diagnosis possible. These are the blocks Dubailand students most often need rebuilt.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas calculations. The foundation everything quantitative rests on, so a weakness here resurfaces in energetics, equilibrium and titration work. Usually a block of four or five sessions and worth doing before anything else.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energies and periodic trends. Marks are lost on trend explanations that name the trend without the cause, and at Higher Level on the detail of successive ionisation energies. Compact and well suited to a weekday session.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and shapes of molecules. Students confuse bond strength with intermolecular force strength when explaining boiling points, which is the single most repeated error in the strand.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign conventions are the reliable loss, and they are a discipline problem rather than a conceptual one, which means they close quickly.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory, catalysts and at Higher Level rate laws and mechanisms. Candidates describe rate changes without reference to collision frequency or activation energy, which is what the markscheme pays for in explanation questions.

subjects.name: Equilibrium and acids and bases
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning, equilibrium constants, pH, buffers and titration curves. The commonest error is applying Le Chatelier loosely to a catalyst or to an inert gas addition, which earns nothing. A substantial and high-value block.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half equations, electrolysis and at Higher Level cell potentials. Half equations that do not balance for charge are the standard loss, and the fix is procedural practice rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways and at Higher Level nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and reaction mechanisms with curly arrows. This is where Higher Level grades are decided, and where marks are lost to arrows drawn from the wrong place.

subjects.name: The internal assessment
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The band is largely determined by whether the research question produces data with measurable variation, which is settled before any practical work starts.

sections.heading: How to test whether a tutor really knows IB Chemistry
paragraphs: A parent cannot assess chemistry expertise directly, but they can assess specificity, and specificity is a reliable proxy. Three questions do the work. Which level did you last take through to the final session, and in which year? What is the commonest mark loss on organic mechanism questions? What would you check first in a draft internal assessment?

A specialist answers the first with a year and a level. They answer the second with something concrete: arrows drawn from the wrong species, nucleophiles not identified, intermediates omitted, or a mechanism recalled correctly but drawn without the charges. They answer the third by naming the research question and the data range, because that is what caps the band. None of those answers requires preparation from somebody who has taught the course.

A generalist answers differently, and the pattern is recognisable. The first answer becomes a statement about years of experience in chemistry. The second becomes a comment about students finding organic difficult. The third becomes advice about starting early and being organised. None of it is false and none of it is useful, because it would be the same answer for any science at any level.

This matters more in chemistry than in most subjects because the course has a particular structure: a quantitative foundation, a set of explanation strands where command terms decide the mark, and an organic section that behaves like a procedural skill. A tutor who has not worked that structure recently will default to covering content, which is the slowest and most expensive form of help available. The table below sets out what a specialist should be able to say about each strand.
