sections.heading: Organic chemistry is where the Higher Level grade is decided
paragraphs: At Higher Level, organic chemistry carries a disproportionate share of both the content and the difficulty, and it behaves unlike the rest of the course. Stoichiometry is arithmetic with chemistry attached. Equilibrium is reasoning about a system. Organic mechanisms are a procedural skill, closer to mathematics than to the descriptive strands, and they reward being taught as a procedure.

The mistake most students make is to memorise reactions. There are too many, and the papers do not ask for recall; they ask candidates to apply a mechanism to a molecule they have not seen. What a student needs instead is a small set of rules about where electrons come from and where they go, applied until the pattern is automatic. Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and the behaviour of carbonyl groups all follow from the same handful of ideas, and a student who holds those ideas can handle an unfamiliar substrate.

Marks are then lost in drawing rather than thinking. Arrows that start from an atom rather than from a bond or a lone pair. Charges omitted from intermediates. A mechanism that is chemically correct and incompletely annotated. These are conventions, and conventions are teachable in a defined number of sessions, which is why an organic block of six to eight sessions is one of the most reliable purchases available in this course.

The second half of the Higher Level organic challenge is synthesis and spectroscopy: building a route to a target molecule, and interpreting spectra to identify a structure. Both reward working backwards from the answer, a technique students rarely discover alone. A tutor who teaches the reverse-engineering habit changes how a student reads the whole paper, not just the organic questions.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level chemistry compared
paragraphs: The level decision is often made for degree reasons rather than for fit, and that is usually correct: Higher Level chemistry is a standard requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering. But a family should understand what they are committing to, because the gap between the two courses is wider in chemistry than in several other sciences.

The syllabus is larger at Higher Level, and the additional content is not evenly distributed. Organic chemistry expands substantially, spectroscopic analysis is added, and entropy and Gibbs free energy join the energetics strand. Equilibrium and kinetics both acquire quantitative treatment that Standard Level does not meet. The result is that the Higher Level course is more mathematical and less descriptive, and students who chose it on the strength of being good at remembering chemistry sometimes struggle for that reason.

The internal assessment carries 20 per cent at both levels, but the expectation of analytical depth differs. An investigation that is adequate at Standard Level may be thin at Higher Level in terms of uncertainty treatment and the sophistication of the analysis. A tutor working from a Standard Level mental model will approve work heading for a middling band, which is one of the reasons the level must be confirmed before matching rather than assumed.

Paper structure and weightings should come from the school's coordinator. The IB revised its science syllabuses recently, and ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no examination date, results date or paper weighting is published on this page that has not been verified. That is a deliberate position: an unsourced number repeated across many pages becomes many liabilities, and a parent acting on a wrong date has been actively misled.

sections.heading: The chemistry internal assessment, and the boundary around it
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in an individual investigation, and most of that band is decided at the design stage rather than the writing stage. A research question that produces data with no measurable variation, or a variable range too narrow to show a trend, caps the mark however carefully the report is written. A specialist can see that in one session; a student working alone often cannot see it until the data is collected.

So the useful sequence is testing before doing. Is the variable range wide enough to produce a visible effect? Will the uncertainty in the measurement swamp the thing being measured? Is there a quantity that can be plotted with a meaningful gradient? Does the chemistry behind the question go beyond a recipe from a textbook? Those four checks take one session and protect a term of work.

The write-up then rewards specific things: a clear and justified method, honest treatment of uncertainty, analysis that actually uses the data rather than describing it, and an evaluation that distinguishes random from systematic error and proposes improvements that would genuinely change the result. Evaluation is where students write generalities, and generalities score poorly. Naming a specific source of error with a specific consequence scores well.

The boundary is not negotiable. A tutor may test a research question, explain what each criterion rewards, teach uncertainty propagation and graphing, read a draft the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, and model an analysis on different data. A tutor must never carry out the investigation, write the report, or redraft it until the work is no longer the student's own. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum; that is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, whose diploma can be withheld.

sections.heading: What a chemistry specialist costs, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Price this subject by scarcity rather than by format. Chemistry has fewer specialists than mathematics and Higher Level fewer again, so the realistic bands sit above the market floor. The sourced figures: budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, travel included.

What a parent can verify matters more than the number. Three of the six most visible pages competing for these searches publish no price at all, and one asks the price question in its own FAQ list and then declines to answer it. Two of the three that do publish quote in US dollars. Against that, a figure with a named source and a date is checkable, and checkability is the whole reason this page lists who published what.

Two further things a parent can verify at no cost. First, the tutor's permit position: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Any licensing line item in a quote is charging for something free. Second, any examiner claim. Do not accept a description of a tutor as an IB examiner without evidence of current status, and be wary of any suggestion that examiner status grants access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it does not.

None of the figures above is an IB Gram price. Our answer to the cost question is a free trial lesson and a conversation, because the only figure that predicts anything is whether this specialist can name your child's loss pattern in one session. In this belt there is also no travel component in what we charge, since lessons run over live video and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across the internal assessment, Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: A chemistry student carries more than one piece of assessed personal work, and the same boundary applies to all of it. This section exists because one page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright, and a family comparing providers deserves to see the line drawn explicitly rather than left to inference.

What a tutor may do is substantial and genuinely valuable. Teach the chemistry. Explain what each assessment criterion asks for, in the criterion's own language. Test whether a research question or an Extended Essay topic will survive contact with real data or real sources. Read a draft the student has written and say where it is losing marks. Demonstrate an analysis, a titration calculation or a spectroscopic deduction on different material. Teach citation and referencing properly, which is a skill many students reach the Diploma without.

What a tutor must never do is produce the work. Not the investigation, not the report, not the Extended Essay, not the Theory of Knowledge essay, not a Personal Project. Nor edit a student's text until the reasoning and the voice are no longer theirs. Where a school requires an authentication declaration, the student signs it, and a tutor who crossed the line has put that signature at risk along with the diploma behind it.

The same discipline applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets or grade boundary tables; they are the board's copyright and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice in the same style. A provider advertising a download library has a problem a parent using it would be sharing.

sections.heading: Availability, fallback and the regulatory frame
paragraphs: Honest availability is part of the answer to the question this page is named after. Chemistry at Standard Level matches quickly. Higher Level matches well but not instantly, and a specific hour in the contested half past five to seven window may take longer than the subject itself. Higher Level organic specialists for a short-notice pre-series block are the narrowest request in this subject, and sometimes the right answer is a date rather than a substitute.

No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is why families discover one in week three. Our version is stated instead: where no specialist is genuinely free, we say so and give a date rather than putting a near-fit in front of a final-year Diploma student. And lessons are delivered by specialists who may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates, which a parent should be told at the outset.

The regulatory frame is worth knowing in outline. Private tuition runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tuition of their own school's students, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise; that reporting is press-sourced, so verify against the current ADEK text.

School regulation differs by emirate. Dubai is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education and inspects on six bands. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry HL much harder than SL, or just longer?
faqs.answer: Genuinely harder, and the gap is wider in chemistry than in some other sciences. Organic chemistry expands substantially, spectroscopic analysis is added, entropy and Gibbs free energy join energetics, and both equilibrium and kinetics acquire quantitative treatment Standard Level never meets. The course becomes more mathematical and less descriptive. Students who chose Higher Level because they were good at remembering chemistry sometimes struggle for exactly that reason, and the fix is usually calculation practice rather than more reading.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach the chemistry internal assessment legitimately?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may test whether a research question will produce data with measurable variation, explain what each criterion rewards, teach uncertainty propagation and graphing, read a draft the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, and model an analysis on different data. A tutor must never conduct the investigation, write the report or redraft it until the work is no longer the student's. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger and the student's diploma is what is at risk.

faqs.question: My child finds organic chemistry very difficult. Is that fixable before the session?
faqs.answer: Usually, and faster than parents expect, provided the approach changes. Students who find organic difficult have almost always been trying to memorise reactions, and there are too many to hold. Taught as a procedure with explicit arrow conventions and a small set of electron-movement rules, it becomes a skill that transfers to unfamiliar molecules. Six to eight focused sessions is the typical block. What will not work is rereading notes, because the papers test application rather than recall.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level chemistry work for medicine applications from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level chemistry is a standard requirement for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy routes, and for chemical engineering, which is why many Dubailand families request it specifically. What a tutoring page should not do is state a grade threshold for any particular university, because those change and vary by institution. Check published entry requirements directly during the first Diploma year, and treat that information as the constraint when deciding level and subject combination rather than discovering it in the second year.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics should be fixed first?
faqs.answer: Stoichiometry and the mole, every time. It is arithmetic with chemistry attached, it underpins energetics, equilibrium and titration work, and a gap there resurfaces for two years. Four or five sessions usually closes it. After that the sequence depends on the diagnosis: sign conventions in energetics close in about three sessions, half equations unbalanced for charge in three or four, and Le Chatelier reasoning in five or six. Organic is the largest block and should be scheduled rather than squeezed in.

faqs.question: What does an IB chemistry specialist charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Budget provision at AED 45 to 150 is rarely the right purchase for Higher Level chemistry. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Each figure names its publisher so a quote can be checked rather than trusted.

faqs.question: How are lab skills handled if our Dubailand sessions are online?
faqs.answer: The skills examined on paper can, and taught well. Identifying variables, criticising a method, reading an instrument scale, propagating uncertainty, plotting with error bars, finding a gradient and its uncertainty, and distinguishing random from systematic error all work better on a shared annotated document than at a bench. The laboratory work belongs to the school, which has the equipment, the technician and the safety framework. The most useful session of all is one where the student brings their own school practical data and has it processed properly.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a Higher Level chemistry tutor for this belt?
faqs.answer: Standard Level matches quickly. Higher Level matches well but not instantly, and the limiting factor is usually the hour rather than the subject, because the half past five to seven weekday window is contested across the whole city. Shifting a session twenty minutes later or taking a weekend morning normally resolves it. The narrowest request in this subject is a Higher Level organic specialist for a short-notice pre-series block, and where none is free we give a date rather than offering a near-fit.

faqs.question: Should I be impressed if a tutor says they are an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence of current status, and not at all if the claim comes with any suggestion of inside access. Examiner status does not grant access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content, and anybody implying that it does is making a claim that should end the conversation. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners where current status cannot be evidenced. What genuinely predicts usefulness is recent experience of teaching the course at the student's level, which is a question with a checkable answer.

faqs.question: Which exam session does a Dubailand IB chemistry candidate sit?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date that a parent plans around is a genuine harm; confirm dates with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications a sibling may be sitting, the UAE series are June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: Do you supply the IB chemistry data booklet and past papers?
faqs.answer: No. The data booklet, syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the IB's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued to the student, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. Be cautious of any provider advertising a paper library: that is an unresolved copyright problem, and a family using it is participating in it.

faqs.question: Should our Dubailand student use one tutor for chemistry and biology?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. The two courses share data-analysis and uncertainty skills, so a specialist strong in either often adds value in the other. Where it breaks down is at Higher Level, because Higher Level organic chemistry and Higher Level biology content are both large and neither tolerates a tutor whose knowledge is a year out of date. For a Standard Level pairing one tutor is often sensible; for two Higher Level sciences, two specialists usually serve better.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Ask the three questions, then book the hour
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IB chemistry tutor in Dubailand is worth hiring when they can tell you which level they last taught, what students lose marks on in organic mechanisms, and what they would check first in a draft investigation. Distance tells you none of that, and Higher Level specialists are scarce across Dubai rather than only in this belt, so a radius filter narrows the choice on the wrong axis. Book a free trial lesson with a specialist at the right level, use it as an interview and a diagnosis, and plan the organic block and the internal assessment deliberately.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emaar-beachf.tutorsIntro: Our chemistry tutors teach either Higher or Standard Level from the current subject guide and plan against the school's own calendar. Sessions concentrate on written working: mechanisms drawn out, calculations laid out in full, and evaluation written before the deadline rather than after.

intro.heading: Two years of chemistry, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry has a shape and almost every avoidable failure comes from ignoring it. The external papers sit at the end of DP2. The investigation's internal deadline falls months earlier, usually in DP1 or the first part of DP2, and it carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade. Mock examinations sit between them. The organic chemistry that defeats most students arrives in DP2 on a foundation laid in DP1. A tutor booked in October of DP1 and a tutor booked in January of DP2 are solving different problems, and treating them the same way wastes whichever time remains.

The current chemistry course is organised around two themes, structure and reactivity, each broken into sub-topics, with Higher Level adding depth inside each rather than a separate body of content. The IB revised the guide in recent years, so the first task is to establish which guide your child's cohort follows. Older revision books describe a different arrangement with an additional paper and option topics, and a student working from one of those spends hours on material that is no longer examined. The school can answer this in a sentence.

UAE schools sit the May session. The project this page belongs to could not confirm any IB examination or results date from the IB itself, because its site blocks automated retrieval, so no specific Diploma date appears here. That is a deliberate omission rather than a gap: a wrong date is worse than no date, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds the real calendar. What can be planned reliably is the sequence and the relative timing, and that is what the tables below set out.

Emaar Beachfront's own constraints determine when the sequence can actually run. The peninsula is reached by one road link, has no school and no tuition centre inside it, and its tower basements need a resident to clear visitor access. Children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30. Chemistry sessions involving mechanisms or multi-step calculations need a student who is awake, which makes 17:00 the honest weekday floor. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows is the two-year plan in usable form: what must be secure by the end of DP1, the investigation sequence from design to submission, where organic mechanisms belong and why they defeat students who arrive at them unprepared, a term-by-term revision order for DP2, how Ramadan and the school calendar reduce ten planned weeks to eight real ones, the honesty boundary on the investigation, and an honest assessment of what a January start in DP2 can achieve. Confirm every date and weighting with your school before you build a plan on it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emaar-beachf.programmesIntro: Chemistry is assessed differently at each IB stage, and the transferable skills are narrower than families assume. Here is what each stage rewards and what it leaves to the next one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Criterion-marked on knowledge and understanding, inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on science in context. The investigative habits built here map directly onto the Diploma investigation, which is why MYP students often handle that component better than students arriving from a written-examination system.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school runs MYP to Year 9 then switches to IGCSE, the criterion marking stops and a tiered written examination takes over. The design and evaluation habits remain the most useful thing a student carries forward.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: Structure and bonding, periodicity, stoichiometry and energetics are generally covered this year, and they are the foundation DP2 organic chemistry rests on. The investigation is often designed and sometimes completed during DP1. A student who finishes DP1 without secure bonding and mole work will not recover it while also learning mechanisms.
programmes.countryNote: The autumn term of DP1 is the cheapest point in two years to intervene, and the point at which almost nobody does, because the first reports have not yet exposed anything.

programmes.name: Diploma year two
programmes.description: Organic chemistry, kinetics, equilibrium and electron transfer typically land here, along with the mock window and the final papers. The content is heavier and the time is shorter, which is why the sequence matters more in DP2 than in any other year of school.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the May session. Internal deadlines for the investigation and for the other core components cluster ahead of it, so DP2 has fewer usable weeks than its length suggests.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with DP chemistry
programmes.description: Where chemistry is taken as one of the DP courses within a Career-related Programme, it is marked to full Diploma standards and the calendar is identical. Tutoring is therefore the same work on the same sequence, with the career-related study adding its own deadlines alongside.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across Dubai is narrow, so families in this cluster pursuing it generally choose between a small number of schools rather than between neighbourhoods.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emaar-beachf.subjectsIntro: These are the chemistry areas and adjacent subjects we are asked for most in this cluster. Each entry says where it sits in the two years and what goes wrong when it is met out of sequence.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Usually DP1 and the foundation for everything after it. Failures are almost always unit handling rather than the mole concept: grams against kilograms, cubic centimetres against cubic decimetres, concentration expressed three ways. A student carrying this weakness into DP2 titration and kinetics work compounds it.

subjects.name: Models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: DP1 content that determines whether DP2 organic chemistry is learnable. A student who understands bonding as a set of labels rather than as electron behaviour can pass DP1 assessments and then cannot reason about why a mechanism proceeds the way it does.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and spontaneity. Sign conventions cause most of the loss, and they cause it silently: a student with the wrong convention produces plausible numbers with the wrong sign and does not notice.

subjects.name: Kinetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Typically DP2. Students who apply a memorised rule rather than reasoning from the position of the system fail on any question that disturbs two variables at once. Higher Level rate law work adds algebraic demand that surfaces a mathematics weakness.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: The DP2 wall. Students who learned mechanisms as arrow patterns by shape can reproduce the examples they have seen and fail on an unfamiliar substrate, which is precisely what the paper supplies. Rebuilt from electron-pair reasoning, it becomes reconstructable rather than memorised.

subjects.name: Electron transfer and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, electrolysis and cells. The loss is mechanical: half-equations not balanced for charge, or electrons placed on the wrong side. A short block fixes it, and it is often left until the last fortnight when there is no room for a short block.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainty
subjects.description: Examinable in the data-based questions and scored again in the investigation's analysis criterion. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, and reading a gradient with its uncertainty. Taught thinly in many schools, which makes it unusually recoverable.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation carrying roughly a fifth of the grade, marked on criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Its internal deadline is the earliest hard date in the subject, and evaluation is where most of the lost marks sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside Higher Level chemistry. Logarithms, rearrangement and proportional reasoning are shared ground, so a chemistry calculation problem in equilibrium or kinetics work is often a mathematics problem in disguise.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual third science for students heading towards medicine or life sciences. The shared skills are uncertainty treatment, graph interpretation and the structure of an evaluation, so investigation coaching in chemistry generally improves the biology investigation too.

sections.heading: What has to be secure by the end of DP1
paragraphs: Three things, and they are not negotiable because DP2 assumes all three. First, unit handling in stoichiometry: grams and kilograms, cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, the three common ways concentration is expressed, and the ability to move between them without pausing. Second, bonding understood as electron behaviour rather than as a vocabulary of labels. Third, sign conventions in energetics, applied consistently enough that a wrong sign looks wrong to the student.

The reason these three matter more than any DP1 topic grade is that organic chemistry in DP2 is built on them. A mechanism is a sequence of electron movements justified by bonding and driven by energetics. A student who holds bonding as a set of definitions can answer DP1 questions about bonding and then cannot reason about why a nucleophile attacks where it does. The DP1 report will not reveal this, because DP1 assessments test the definitions, and that is exactly why the problem is discovered in DP2 when there is no time to fix it properly.

The practical test to apply at the end of DP1 is a short one. Give the student an unfamiliar calculation requiring two unit conversions, ask them to explain why a particular bond is polar from first principles, and ask them to predict the sign of an enthalpy change and say why. If any of the three is slow or uncertain, the autumn of DP2 should begin with repair work rather than with new content, however uncomfortable that is when the school has already moved on.

sections.heading: The investigation calendar, from design to submission
paragraphs: The investigation's internal deadline is the earliest hard date in Diploma chemistry and the one families discover latest. It carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade and is marked on criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because the marks are distributed across those areas rather than concentrated in one, the component is lost in pieces: a workable question with thin data, or good data with a two-line evaluation, or a conclusion the data does not support.

Working backwards from submission, the sequence is fixed. The research question has to be settled far enough ahead that apparatus can be checked and a pilot run attempted. Collection needs enough time for a repeat when something fails, which it usually does. Processing with uncertainty carried through has to happen before the conclusion is written, not alongside it. Evaluation has to be drafted while the method is still fresh. The final version needs a week of distance before it is submitted.

Most students compress this into the last fortnight and lose the evaluation marks because they are writing about a method they can no longer remember clearly. The intervention that works is a design session before the question is fixed, which is also the cheapest session in the whole component. Ask the school for the internal deadline in writing at the start of the year and count backwards from it; the dates below are a relative sequence, and the actual calendar belongs to your school.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms: the DP2 wall and when to meet it
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where Diploma chemistry grades are made and lost, and the reason is specific. Students are taught a set of mechanisms and they learn them as shapes: this arrow from here to there, in this arrangement. That works for every example they have seen. The papers then supply an unfamiliar substrate, and the student has no way to decide what happens, because they never learned why the electrons move. The result is a student who can reproduce three mechanisms perfectly and score poorly on the topic.

Rebuilding it is slower than learning it correctly the first time, which is the argument for securing bonding in DP1. The rebuild works from electron density: where are the electrons, where is the deficiency, what makes a leaving group leave, what stabilises an intermediate. A student who can answer those four questions about an unfamiliar molecule can construct a plausible mechanism, and a plausible mechanism constructed from reasoning scores where a half-remembered shape does not.

Timing matters. If mechanisms are met in DP2 with weak bonding underneath, the first four sessions should be bonding rather than mechanisms, even though that feels like going backwards while the school moves forwards. Families resist this and it is the right call: four sessions of foundation makes the next eight productive, while eight sessions of mechanism practice on weak foundations produces familiarity with those eight examples. The script from the first mock usually settles the argument, because it shows mechanism marks scoring well on seen reactions and poorly on unseen ones.

sections.heading: A term-by-term revision order for DP2
paragraphs: Revision order is not arbitrary and the default order is wrong. Most students revise in syllabus sequence, which means they spend the autumn on DP1 content they half-remember and arrive at the hardest DP2 material with the least time. The productive order is the opposite: stabilise what DP2 is currently teaching, because that content is both newest and heaviest, then return to DP1 material which recovers quickly because it was once secure.

Inside that, sequence by cost. Organic mechanisms first if they are unstable, because they carry the most marks and take the longest to rebuild. Then kinetics and equilibrium, which depend on reasoning habits rather than recall and so also take time. Then electron transfer and electrochemistry, which are mechanical and repair in a short block. Then DP1 material, which mostly needs reactivation rather than reteaching. Then whole papers under timing, from the midpoint of the final term onwards.

The measure throughout is the gap between the student's predicted mark and the real one on a timed component. A student who marks their own paper strictly against the official scheme and predicts within a few marks has internalised the examiner's logic and is ready for broad revision. A student whose prediction is consistently generous is not yet ready, and more content revision will not help. That audit happens every fortnight, which is what keeps the sequence honest rather than aspirational.

One warning about the default order. Starting in the autumn of DP2 with a full review of DP1 feels responsible and is usually the worst available choice, because it spends the freshest weeks on material that would have recovered quickly later while the heaviest new content arrives untouched. If a school's own revision programme runs in syllabus order, the private sessions should deliberately run against it rather than duplicating it, and that is a conversation worth having in the first week of term.

sections.heading: Ramadan, school trips and the weeks that actually exist
paragraphs: A ten-week plan is usually eight usable weeks, and knowing which eight changes what can honestly be promised. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the family day reorganises around iftar, which for a DP2 student can overlap the most important revision block of the two years. Mid-term breaks, Model United Nations trips, sports fixtures, university open days and the school's own mock window all compete for the same hours. None of this is an obstacle if it is planned for and all of it is disruptive if it is not.

The approach that works is to mark the unavailable weeks before fixing the plan. Ask the school for the calendar in writing in the first week of term, cross out what is gone, and build the sequence on the weeks that remain. For Ramadan specifically, decide the pattern in advance rather than improvising: a post-iftar session suits many students better than a 17:00 slot, and weekend mornings with reduced midweek frequency work for others. Cancelling for a month and resuming in the final fortnight does not work, because the content planned for those weeks has nowhere else to go.

There is a second reason to do this arithmetic early. A family who believes they have twenty sessions before the papers will plan for twenty and discover fourteen. A family who knows they have fourteen will choose differently: fewer topics, deeper, with the lowest-value items dropped deliberately rather than abandoned by accident. That choice is strictly better even though it feels like a smaller plan, and it is the single most useful conversation to have in the first session of a DP2 block.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary on a chemistry investigation
paragraphs: Chemistry has the most sensitive coursework position of the three sciences, because the data is quantitative and therefore easy to fabricate. The IB treats invented data as malpractice and the consequences fall on the student rather than on whoever supplied it. This market contains operations that sell completed internal assessments outright; one page researched for this project does so at a published price. A student who submits bought work risks the whole Diploma, and the school is obliged to report it.

The boundary is clear and worth stating in full. A tutor may explain what each lettered criterion requires and what distinguishes the bands. A tutor may test whether a research question is answerable with the apparatus available and whether the planned data volume can support a conclusion. A tutor may question the processing, point out that a table has no uncertainties, and ask whether the conclusion follows from the data. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give written feedback on structure, clarity and evidence.

A tutor may not design the experiment, supply or process the data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or produce a worked version for the student to adapt. Our tutors work on the first list and decline the second directly, and they will say so to a student who asks. The school supervises the investigation; a tutor supports the student's own work alongside that supervision and keeps the school's internal deadline as the schedule rather than inventing one.

sections.heading: What a January start in DP2 can and cannot do
paragraphs: Families often arrive in January of DP2 with a disappointing mock result and a reasonable question: is it too late? The honest answer is that it depends entirely on what the mock script shows, and that the available gain is real but bounded. A student losing marks to command terms, unit handling, sign conventions and unattempted final questions can move substantially, because those repair in weeks. A student who never secured bonding, cannot construct a mechanism and has no uncertainty technique has two years of foundation to rebuild in one term, and that is a different proposition.

What a January start can do well: stabilise one or two high-cost areas, install the technique habits that pay across every question, convert the investigation from a liability into a solid component if the deadline has not passed, and teach paper strategy so that the whole paper is attempted. Those four together typically move a grade. What it cannot do is cover the course again, and a tutor who offers that is selling hours.

The decision should be made from the script rather than from the grade. Send the marked mock, ask for the losses sorted by type with an estimate against each, and ask directly which items are not worth chasing in the time available. A good answer names things to abandon. Our trial lesson produces that document and you keep it whether or not you continue, because the honest version of this conversation is more useful to you than the encouraging version.

We cannot promise a grade and nobody who has marked a chemistry paper would. faqs.question: When should chemistry tutoring start for a Diploma student in Emaar Beachfront?
faqs.answer: The autumn of DP1 is the cheapest point and almost nobody uses it, because the first reports have not exposed anything yet. Securing unit handling, bonding as electron behaviour and energetics sign conventions in that term is what makes DP2 organic chemistry learnable. A student who reaches DP2 without those three is being asked to rebuild a foundation while also learning the heaviest content in the course, in the year with the least available time.

faqs.question: What is the earliest hard deadline in IB chemistry?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation's internal deadline, set by your school rather than by the IB, and usually falling well before the external papers. It carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade and is marked on criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Ask the school for the date in writing at the start of the year, because the coaching that helps most happens eight to ten weeks before it, at the point where the research question is still changeable.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well on seen reactions and badly on unseen ones?
faqs.answer: Because the mechanisms were learned as shapes rather than as reasoning. A student who memorises arrow patterns can reproduce every example they have been shown and has no way to decide what happens to an unfamiliar substrate, which is exactly what the papers supply. The rebuild works from electron density, leaving-group behaviour and intermediate stability. It is slower than learning it correctly the first time, which is the whole argument for securing bonding during DP1.

faqs.question: In what order should a DP2 student revise chemistry?
faqs.answer: Not in syllabus order. Stabilise what the school is currently teaching first, because that content is newest and heaviest, then return to DP1 material which recovers quickly because it was once secure. Within that, sequence by cost: mechanisms first if they are unstable, then kinetics and equilibrium reasoning, then electron transfer which is mechanical and fast, then reactivation of DP1 topics, then whole papers under timing from the midpoint of the final term.

faqs.question: How many usable weeks does a DP2 spring term actually have?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. Once mid-term breaks, trips, university open days, the mock window and the Ramadan adjustment are marked out, a ten-week plan is commonly eight real weeks. The useful response is to ask the school for the calendar in writing in week one and build the sequence on what remains, choosing fewer topics covered properly over more topics touched lightly. Fourteen known sessions are worth more than twenty assumed ones.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach the chemistry investigation without crossing IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor may explain the criteria and the band descriptors, test whether a research question is answerable with the school's apparatus, question the processing, point out missing uncertainties, ask whether the conclusion follows from the data, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the experiment, supply or process data, or write any part of the report. Invented data is malpractice in itself.

faqs.question: Is a January start in DP2 worth it?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the mock script shows, and the honest answer varies. A student losing marks to command terms, unit handling, sign conventions and unattempted final questions can move substantially, because those repair in weeks. A student who never secured bonding and cannot construct a mechanism has two years of foundation to rebuild in one term. Send the script, ask for the losses sorted by type, and ask directly which items are not worth chasing in the time available.

faqs.question: How should we handle the investigation deadline and revision at the same time?
faqs.answer: By separating them into different sessions and different weeks rather than alternating within a session. Investigation work needs ninety uninterrupted minutes and a clear head, which on this peninsula means a weekend morning. Revision runs on the weekday slot. Where the two collide, the investigation wins, because it is a fixed deadline carrying a fifth of the grade while revision has flexible timing. Plan the collision before it arrives rather than negotiating it in the week.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topic do students in this cluster find hardest?
faqs.answer: Organic mechanisms, with equilibrium close behind. Both fail for the same underlying reason: students apply a memorised rule instead of reasoning from the system in front of them, so any question that disturbs two things at once defeats them. Equilibrium is the cheaper repair of the two because the reasoning is narrower. Electron transfer looks hard and is actually mechanical, which makes it unusually good value in a short block late in the year.

faqs.question: Does uncertainty work matter as much in chemistry as in physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it pays twice. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and reading a gradient with its uncertainty are examinable in the data-based questions and scored again in the investigation's data analysis criterion. Many schools teach uncertainty as a formatting rule applied at the end of a calculation, which is why students drop it under pressure. Four to six sessions treating it as part of the chemistry makes it reconstructable rather than recalled.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL necessary for the medicine routes families here apply to?
faqs.answer: Decide on destination first. Medicine, chemical engineering, pharmacy and several life science routes commonly specify chemistry at Higher Level or treat it as strongly preferred, and those requirements are set by each receiving university and revised annually. Read the current rule on the named programme's own admissions page in Year 11. Where no target requires Higher Level, a strong Standard Level grade is worth more on a transcript than a modest Higher Level one in the same subject.

faqs.question: What should we send with the first enquiry?
faqs.answer: Level, the subject guide the school follows, the investigation's internal deadline, the most recent marked paper and the hours that genuinely exist after the school run. The deadline is the item most often left out and the one that most changes the plan, because design-stage coaching and draft review are different jobs belonging at different points. With those five things the trial lesson produces a plan; without them it produces a conversation.

faqs.question: Would the same tutor sensibly cover both science investigations?
faqs.answer: Only where that person genuinely teaches both at the required level, which is less common than families assume. The investigation skills transfer well, so a single tutor coaching both investigations can be efficient. Subject content does not transfer: a biologist taking chemistry will keep a student moving through DP1 and will struggle to diagnose a mechanism problem in DP2. Ask which components of each subject the tutor has taught at that level and expect two names if the answer is vague.

faqs.question: What hour works for chemistry sessions from this peninsula?
faqs.answer: 17:00 at the earliest on a weekday, 17:30 if the bus from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh runs late. Mechanisms and multi-step calculations need sustained attention, and a tired student makes errors that look like misunderstanding and get diagnosed as such. Weekend mornings carry the investigation work. Choosing the hour honestly matters more than choosing the tutor carefully and hoping the hour survives a term, which on a single-access peninsula it frequently does not.

intro.heading: The chemistry answer is better than the physics answer, and more deceptive
paragraphs: Chemistry is easier to staff than physics. More IB schools run more chemistry classes, more teachers accumulate Diploma experience in it, and an Emaar South family searching for a chemistry tutor will find more names than a family searching for a physicist. That sounds like good news and it carries a specific risk: a longer list of plausible candidates, most of whom cannot do the two things that decide a chemistry grade at Higher Level.

The first is marking an organic mechanism. In the Diploma, a curly arrow either starts from the correct lone pair or bond or it does not, and examiners do not award a half-drawn mechanism. Marking that properly requires knowing where the marks sit on each mechanism type, which is a teaching skill rather than a chemistry one. A competent chemist can draw mechanisms correctly and have no idea which part of a student's incorrect attempt would have scored.

The second is the investigation's analysis criterion, which rewards processing that is correct and includes uncertainties. A tutor who helps a student run clean titrations and write a tidy report, with no error propagation, has produced a mid-band piece of work and will not know why. The criterion carries six marks and the investigation carries 20% of the subject, which makes this the most expensive silent failure in the subject.

Add the Paper 3 option at Higher Level, which is school-chosen examined content taught in class, and the apparently wide pool narrows considerably. A tutor who has taught one option cannot teach another they have never delivered. So the honest answer for Emaar South is that chemistry help is findable and chemistry help that matches your child's actual papers requires asking two or three narrow questions first.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor is dispatched to an Emaar South address, which matters here because the community has no school in it and a visiting tutor would be absorbing a twenty-five to forty-five minute journey each way. Students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with mechanisms drawn on a shared surface that persists week to week.

One factual note. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the reports. It does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. It licenses teaching privately in the UAE; it says nothing whatever about whether the holder can mark a mechanism question, which is the competence this page is about and the one a parent can test in five minutes.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The chemistry components and topics where a specialist and a competent chemist diverge. Each note names what somebody who has taught the course knows that somebody who merely knows chemistry does not.

subjects.name: Organic mechanisms
subjects.description: A specialist knows where the marks sit on each mechanism type and can say which part of an incorrect attempt would have scored. A competent chemist draws them correctly and cannot mark them. Since examiners award nothing for a partially drawn mechanism, that distinction is the single largest one in the subject.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Worth 20%, with the analysis criterion rewarding processing that is correct and includes uncertainties. A specialist insists on uncertainty treatment before data collection. A generalist helps with clean titrations and a tidy report, which caps a six-mark criterion without anybody understanding why.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: Data analysis plus the school's chosen option topic, examined separately from the core. A specialist asks which option before agreeing to teach it. A generalist does not know the question exists, and a student taught only the core meets Paper 3 having never attempted a whole one.

subjects.name: Paper 2 at Higher Level
subjects.description: Around 36% of the grade and the component where multi-step calculation discipline decides the mark. Early rounding yields a final answer the scheme rejects even when every step was right. A specialist names that from a script in minutes; a generalist reteaches the topic.

subjects.name: Mole calculations and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The quantitative substrate under everything. Unit slips between grams and moles, and concentration errors between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, account for a large share of losses. Procedural, drillable, and the first thing a diagnostic session usually finds.

subjects.name: Energetics and entropy
subjects.levels: HL and SL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies, and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign conventions cause more losses than any calculation does, and a stated sign with a stated reason earns marks a bare number does not. Arrives late in most schemes of work.

subjects.name: Equilibrium at Higher Level
subjects.description: Equilibrium constant calculations added to the qualitative Le Chatelier work. Procedural once the method is learned: set up the table, substitute, solve, check the assumption. Among the most improvable Higher Level content precisely because it is a routine rather than an insight.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and buffers
subjects.levels: HL and SL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: pH and the logarithmic scale, weak acid behaviour, buffers and titration curves. The recurring loss is treating a weak acid as strong, and failing to recognise the half-equivalence point and its relationship to the dissociation constant on a curve.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half-equations, cells and electrolysis, with electrode potentials at Higher Level. Half-equations that balance atoms but not charge score nothing despite looking nearly right, and the charge check takes seconds and gets skipped under pressure.

subjects.name: Spectroscopy
subjects.levels: HL and SL, NMR at HL
subjects.description: Mass spectrometry, infrared and, at Higher Level, nuclear magnetic resonance. Almost entirely dependent on the data booklet, which supplies absorption ranges and chemical shifts. A student who has never opened those pages loses marks that require only looking something up correctly.

subjects.name: Transition metals at Higher Level
subjects.description: Complex ions, ligands, colour and catalysis. Arrives late, is examined reliably, and responds well to a short focused block because the content is bounded. Marks go on explaining colour through d-orbital splitting rather than describing it.

subjects.name: Calculation chains and significant figures
subjects.description: Not a syllabus topic but a marked skill. Carrying full precision through and rounding only the final stated answer is a two-session habit that recovers marks on every paper. A specialist treats it as a named fault; a generalist calls it carelessness.

sections.heading: Why a longer list of chemistry tutors is its own problem
paragraphs: In physics the difficulty is that almost nobody is available. In chemistry the difficulty is the opposite and subtler: plenty of people are available, most of them know chemistry properly, and a parent has no obvious way to tell which of them can prepare a Higher Level candidate. A short list forces careful questions. A long list invites a choice made on price, availability and manner, none of which predicts the thing that matters.

The structural reason the list is longer is straightforward. More IB schools run more chemistry classes than physics classes, so more teachers accumulate Diploma chemistry experience. Chemistry graduates also enter teaching at higher rates than physics graduates, whose alternatives are broader. Across this catchment the result is that an Emaar South family will find several plausible chemistry names and perhaps one plausible physics name.

What has not changed is the specificity of the work. Organic mechanism marking requires knowing where the marks sit on each mechanism type. The investigation's analysis criterion requires uncertainty treatment. Paper 3's option is school-chosen taught content. None of those is implied by a chemistry degree or by general teaching competence, and all three are testable in a few minutes with narrow questions.

So the recommendation for chemistry is different from the one for physics. In physics, calibrate your expectations to a very small pool and book early. In chemistry, assume you can find somebody and spend the saved effort on verification instead. The next section gives the test, and it works on us as readily as on anybody else.

sections.heading: The five-minute mechanism test
paragraphs: This is the single most useful thing on the page and it takes one session or one message. Ask the tutor to mark a mechanism question from a past paper that your child has already attempted and got wrong. Not to draw the correct mechanism, which any chemist can do, but to mark the student's attempt: how many marks it scored, which arrow lost which mark, and what the next mark up required.

A specialist does this immediately and in specific terms. They will say that the nucleophile's arrow starts from the lone pair rather than the atom, that the mark for the intermediate requires the formal charge shown, that the curly arrow for the leaving group has to come from the bond and not the atom, and that the question's two marks sit on those two features rather than on the overall product. That is mark-scheme knowledge and it is what a student needs.

A competent chemist who has not taught the course answers differently. They will explain the mechanism again, correctly and usefully, and will not be able to say which part of the student's attempt earned credit. That is not incompetence; it is the wrong competence, and it produces sessions in which a student understands mechanisms better and continues to score the same, because what they are doing wrong on paper was never named.

The same test generalises. Ask what the investigation's analysis criterion requires beyond correct processing, where the answer is uncertainties. Ask which Paper 3 option they have taught, to how many cohorts. Ask what they would set in the first session, where a component and a technique is the right answer and a topic is the wrong one. Four narrow questions, four short right answers, and most of the risk in this market filtered out before any money moves.

sections.heading: The two silent failures a chemistry generalist produces
paragraphs: Both are silent in the specific sense that nothing looks wrong until a mark arrives, which is why they survive a whole term. The first is mechanism work that improves understanding without improving scores. A student taught mechanisms as pictures to reproduce can handle the six they memorised and has nothing to fall back on when a question presents an unfamiliar substrate, which is precisely what examinations do. The remedy is volume with articulation: each mechanism drawn repeatedly with the origin of every arrow stated aloud before the pen moves.

The second is the investigation that looks excellent and scores in the middle. The analysis criterion rewards processing that is correct and includes uncertainties, and the exploration criterion rewards a methodology addressing all relevant variables. A tidy report built on clean titration data with no error propagation and no discussion of temperature control satisfies neither fully. Nobody involved sees a problem, because the chemistry is right and the presentation is good.

The compounding factor is timing. Both failures are only discovered when a mark comes back, and for the investigation that can be after submission, when nothing can be done. That is why the honest sequence puts uncertainty treatment before data collection rather than after, and why a specialist insists on a pilot run that students always want to skip.

What makes these worth a section rather than a line is that they are not the failures families watch for. Parents worry about whether a tutor knows the content. Content is the thing almost every candidate for the job does know. The failures that cost grades are located in mark allocation and assessment criteria, which is a narrower and less visible competence, and the only reliable way to check it is to ask for a wrong answer to be marked.

sections.heading: The Paper 3 option, and what transfers without it
paragraphs: Paper 3 at Higher Level has two halves: data-analysis questions every candidate sits, and an option topic chosen by the school and taught in class. The option is examined content and not interchangeable, so a tutor who has taught one cannot teach another they have never delivered. For an Emaar South family the first question to the department is therefore which option, in writing, before anybody is approached.

What transfers without an option match is substantial and worth knowing precisely, because it determines whether a shorter arrangement is useful or a holding pattern. The data-analysis half of Paper 3 is option-independent: it tests graph work, interpretation of processed data and uncertainty handling, all of which apply whatever the option. So does the whole of Paper 2, the whole of Paper 1, the investigation, and every bit of mechanism and calculation discipline.

That means a non-option specialist can genuinely work on the large majority of the subject. The honest limitation is a single component half, and describing it that precisely is more useful than either overstating a match or dismissing the tutor. A family facing a long wait for an exact option match should know that the available alternative covers most of the grade rather than nothing.

What nobody should accept is a vague assurance. If a provider says all options are covered, the follow-up is which option has this tutor taught, and to how many cohorts. Both answers are short. In a subject where the list of plausible names is long, that one question is what converts a plausible name into a verified one, and it is the question the length of the list makes people least likely to ask.

sections.heading: The laboratory problem no tutor can solve
paragraphs: A chemistry investigation is constrained in a way a physics or maths internal assessment is not, and it is worth saying plainly that this is outside any tutor's control. The question has to be answerable with reagents and equipment the school can safely supply, within laboratory time the department controls and schedules, using analysis the student has already been taught. Those three constraints belong to the school, and a tutor who implies otherwise is overselling.

What a tutor can do is work within them intelligently, which is most of the value. Negotiating a question against what the department will actually provide, rather than against what would be interesting, prevents the commonest failure: an investigation that cannot be run and has to be restarted weeks in. Insisting on a pilot run catches the second commonest, which is discovering during real data collection that the reaction is too fast or the change too small to measure.

The scheduling constraint has a particular bite for an Emaar South family, because laboratory time has to be in term and in school hours. It cannot happen in a school break, when the laboratory is closed and technicians are unavailable, and it cannot be moved to a weekend to suit a household's travel pattern. That means the data collection stage is the one part of the chemistry year that cannot be shifted into the slots this community otherwise relies on.

The practical consequence is a sequencing instruction rather than a tutoring one. Settle the question and run the pilot early enough that booked laboratory time in term is usable, then move the processing and writing into weekends and the winter break where the uninterrupted hours exist. Families who plan it that way finish comfortably. Families who leave the question open until the laboratory window is closing do not, whatever help they buy afterwards.

sections.heading: What we decline, and why it belongs on this page
paragraphs: A page competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. In chemistry that offer is more available than in most subjects, because the investigation is a document and a document can be supplied. An Emaar South family whose laboratory window is closing and whose deadline is approaching is exactly the family most likely to be offered one, which is why this section sits here rather than in a footnote.

Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. A finding can mean no grade awarded in that subject and, in serious cases, no Diploma at all. No price makes that a reasonable purchase, and the fact that an offer exists is useful information about everything else the provider claims, including their advice on where the boundaries sit.

What is permitted covers nearly all the useful work. A tutor may teach the chemistry the investigation rests on. A tutor may discuss a proposed question and reject one the laboratory cannot support or whose analysis needs chemistry not yet taught. A tutor may insist on a pilot. A tutor may explain each criterion with its mark allocation. A tutor may read a complete draft the student has written and give feedback on it.

What is not permitted is production: writing a section, supplying data, rewriting the analysis into better English, choosing the question on the student's behalf, or editing a draft to completion. The test is whether every line in the submitted document was produced by the student. IB Gram tutors teach, question and give feedback, and that boundary is explained to the student at the first session rather than discovered when a school runs an authenticity check.

sections.heading: What is available now and what has to wait
paragraphs: Disclosing this in advance is unusual in this market and it is more useful than a reassurance, particularly for a family whose investigation deadline or mock is approaching. Standard Level chemistry is reasonably covered and a match usually takes a few days. Higher Level core is moderate and can take up to a week. Higher Level with a specific Paper 3 option is thinner and can take a week or more depending on the option.

Three things are available sooner, and all three are genuinely useful rather than placeholders. Mechanism marking blocks, because they are option-independent and aimed at the largest single source of lost Higher Level marks. Calculation discipline blocks, which address early rounding, missing units, unstated signs and unbalanced charge, all of which are visible on a marked Paper 2 script and all of which are habits. And investigation supervision, which is better covered because the criteria are shared across the sciences.

When nothing suitable is free we say so and give a date. What we do not do is seat a general science tutor opposite a Higher Level chemistry candidate. In chemistry specifically that substitution is tempting because the person will be able to teach the content perfectly well, and that is exactly why it fails: the content is not what is costing the marks, and a term passes pleasantly with the script unchanged.

For an Emaar South family the planning implication is to ask early and to be specific about which part is urgent. A request that names the option, the weak component and the deadline gets a straight answer about timing. A request that says chemistry help needed gets a slower one from any provider, because the first thing anybody has to do is work out which of several quite different jobs is being asked for.

sections.heading: What the verified specialist costs, in published AED
paragraphs: The published Dubai bands place IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200-450 or more an hour on Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors online. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors. At the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online and typically delivered by university students.

In-home provision sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour. From Emaar South that figure sits at the top of its band because the journey is twenty-five to forty-five minutes each way. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one hour a week run AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

The chemistry-specific point is that the price ladder does not sort for the skill this page is about. A tutor at AED 270 may or may not be able to mark a mechanism, and a tutor at AED 150 may be able to. Price correlates with credentials, agency overhead and brand rather than with mark-scheme knowledge, which is why the four narrow questions are worth more than a rate comparison. In a subject with a long list of plausible names, that is the difference between choosing well and choosing expensively.

Every figure here belongs to the provider named and is published by them. None is an IB Gram price: our conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis, and the trial is where the mechanism test should be run. Three of the six most visible providers competing for these searches publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which no Emaar South household transacts in.
