faqs.question: Are there IB chemistry tutors available to Emaar South families?
faqs.answer: More than there are physics tutors, which makes verification the real task rather than patience. More IB schools run more chemistry classes, so more teachers accumulate Diploma chemistry experience, and a family here will usually find several plausible names. What a longer list does is invite a choice made on price, availability and manner, none of which predicts whether somebody can mark an organic mechanism or knows what the investigation's analysis criterion requires. Those are testable in a few minutes.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a chemistry tutor can mark a mechanism?
faqs.answer: Bring a mechanism question your child attempted and got wrong, and ask the tutor to mark it rather than draw the correct version. A specialist will say which arrow lost which mark, that the nucleophile's arrow must start from the lone pair rather than the atom, that the intermediate mark requires the formal charge shown, and what the next mark up needed. A competent chemist who has not taught the course will explain the mechanism again, correctly, without being able to allocate the marks.

faqs.question: Why do mechanism marks disappear completely rather than partly?
faqs.answer: Because examiners do not award a partially drawn mechanism. An arrow either starts from the correct lone pair or bond or it does not, and a student who learned mechanisms as pictures to reproduce can manage the ones they memorised and has nothing to fall back on when a question presents an unfamiliar substrate. The remedy is volume with articulation: each mechanism drawn repeatedly with the origin of every arrow stated aloud before the pen moves, until the statement is automatic.

faqs.question: What does the chemistry investigation's analysis criterion actually require?
faqs.answer: Processing that is correct and includes uncertainties, which is the part a generalist omits. A student who runs clean titrations and writes a tidy report with no error propagation has satisfied the chemistry and not the criterion, and it carries six marks inside a component worth 20% of the subject. The exploration criterion separately rewards a methodology addressing all relevant variables, which in chemistry usually means temperature control, concentration accuracy and the limits of the measuring equipment.

faqs.question: Does the Paper 3 option really change who can help?
faqs.answer: For half of Paper 3, yes. The option is school-chosen examined content taught in class, so a tutor who has taught one cannot teach another they have never delivered. Everything else transfers: Paper 1, Paper 2 at around 36% of the Higher Level grade, the data-analysis half of Paper 3, the whole investigation, and all mechanism and calculation work. That means a non-option specialist can cover most of the subject, and saying so precisely is more useful than overstating a match.

faqs.question: Can a tutor arrange laboratory time for my child's investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody implying otherwise is overselling. Reagents, equipment and laboratory scheduling belong to the school department, and the laboratory is closed during school breaks with technicians unavailable, so data collection has to happen in term time and cannot be moved to a weekend. What a tutor can do is negotiate the question against what the department will actually supply, insist on a pilot run that students always want to skip, and help plan the processing and writing into the hours that do exist.

faqs.question: Why can my child's investigation not be done in the spring break?
faqs.answer: Because the laboratory will be shut. This is an obvious constraint that is nonetheless discovered late every year, and in Emaar South it stings more because the breaks are when this community has usable hours. The workable sequence is to settle the question and run the pilot early enough that booked term-time laboratory hours are productive, then move the processing with uncertainties and the writing into weekend mornings and the winter break, which is where the uninterrupted stretches are.

faqs.question: What does early rounding cost in a chemistry calculation?
faqs.answer: The accuracy mark on an otherwise correct question, which in a multi-mark calculation is usually most of the available credit. Cutting an intermediate value to three significant figures in step two produces a final answer the scheme rejects even though the method was right. Students do it because it looks tidy. The habit to build is carrying full calculator precision through and rounding only the final stated answer. A specialist names this from a script; a generalist calls it carelessness.

faqs.question: Does A Level chemistry experience transfer to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Partly, and not in the places that cost marks. The underlying chemistry is the same, so an A Level teacher explains content reliably, and there is plenty of A Level experience in the British-curriculum schools around Al Furjan and Jebel Ali. What does not transfer is the IB's assessment architecture: the investigation criteria with their explicit uncertainty requirement, the Paper 3 option structure, and the mark allocation on Diploma mechanism questions. The characteristic failure is right chemistry aimed at the wrong target.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor to Emaar South homes?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script, markband and data booklet on screen and mechanisms drawn on a shared surface that is saved week to week. For chemistry that record earns its place: a wrong arrow origin recurring across three weeks becomes evidence rather than an impression of carelessness.

faqs.question: What is available immediately if no option specialist is free?
faqs.answer: Three things, all genuinely useful rather than placeholders. A mechanism marking block, which is option-independent and aimed at the largest single source of lost Higher Level marks. A calculation discipline block addressing early rounding, missing units, unstated signs and unbalanced charge, all visible on a marked Paper 2 script. And investigation supervision, which is better covered because the criteria are shared across the sciences. Paper 2 alone is around 36% of the Higher Level grade.

faqs.question: Should I be worried if a provider offers a completed investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the right response is to decline outright. Using a bought investigation is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student: a finding can mean no grade in the subject and, in serious cases, no Diploma. No price makes it reasonable. The existence of the offer is also information about that provider's advice on every other boundary, including what they will tell you is acceptable help on a draft, which is reason enough to go elsewhere.

faqs.question: Does paying more guarantee a chemistry tutor who can mark mechanisms?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the main practical finding of this page. Published bands put IB specialists at AED 200-450 or more an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650, while budget platforms advertise from AED 33-65. Price correlates with credentials, agency overhead and brand rather than with mark-scheme knowledge. A tutor at AED 270 may not be able to mark a mechanism and one at AED 150 may be. Ask the four questions instead.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics respond fastest to a short block?
faqs.answer: The procedural ones. Equilibrium constant calculations at Higher Level are a routine: set up the table, substitute, solve, check the assumption. Transition metals arrive late, are examined reliably and have bounded content. Mole and concentration work is drillable. Spectroscopy is largely a data-booklet exercise once a student knows which pages carry the absorption ranges and chemical shifts. Each of those is improvable in two or three sessions, which makes them the right targets when time or a specialist slot is scarce.

faqs.question: When should an Emaar South family book chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Earlier than they do, and the summer before Year 13 is the best moment. Nothing competes for the hours, the journey disappears, IGCSE-level and transition tutors are plentiful, and the material is exactly what will arrive in the hardest term: organic chemistry, equilibrium and energetics. Previewing organic nomenclature and reaction types over that summer converts a winter term carrying mechanisms, mocks, the Extended Essay and university applications into one carrying three of those rather than four.

faqs.question: What should the first chemistry session do?
faqs.answer: Read a marked Paper 2 script rather than teach. In chemistry the four commonest losses look identical from a grade: conceptual gaps, mechanism mark allocation, calculation discipline and procedural omissions such as unbalanced charge. Each needs different work and only one of them needs content teaching. Teaching in the first hour feels more productive and makes every later session less accurate, which matters particularly when a specialist slot has taken a week to arrange.

intro.heading: Chemistry marks are lost in specific places, and they can be named
paragraphs: There is a version of tutoring that consists of going over the topic again more slowly. It rarely changes a chemistry grade, because the problem is usually not that the student does not know the chemistry. The problem is that a correct idea arrives on the page in a form the mark scheme cannot reward. A student writes that the reaction gets faster; the examiner wanted the frequency of successful collisions. A student calculates the right number; the method mark went to the line of working they skipped.

That is why this page is built from the syllabus rather than from the neighbourhood. The current guide organises chemistry into six areas: Structure 1, models of the particulate nature of matter; Structure 2, models of bonding and structure; Structure 3, classification of matter; Reactivity 1, what drives chemical reactions; Reactivity 2, how much, how fast and how far; and Reactivity 3, what the mechanisms of chemical change are. Every mark your child will earn or lose sits inside one of those six, and a tutor who can say which one is the one worth paying for.

The assessment shape matters as much as the content. There are two written papers and one internal investigation. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and splits into a multiple-choice section and a set of data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is extended response. The investigation carries 20 per cent. Standard Level sits an hour and a half for each paper; Higher Level sits two hours for Paper 1 and two and a half for Paper 2. A data booklet is supplied, so recall of constants is not the skill being tested.

Students in this part of Dubai arrive at chemistry from two directions. Those who came up through the IB continuum schools in Emirates Hills and The Meadows have been assessed against criteria since they were eleven and are usually comfortable writing an explanation. Those who transferred in after Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 know more content than they think and have never been asked to sustain a two-page answer. Both need the same thing in the end, but not in the same order, which is the first question a tutor should ask.

Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not operate a UAE office and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are available only in India. What follows is the subject: the content map, the command-term traps, the three calculation areas that cost the most, the HL mechanisms, a worked eight-week past-paper programme, the investigation errors specific to chemistry, and what the Dubai market charges for this kind of help with the sources named.

Ask the school which sessions it offers rather than assuming, and verify any session date with the IB coordinator or on ibo.org before building a plan around it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emirates-hil.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is almost never the only thing being tutored in a household here. These are the combinations that actually appear, with what each pairing does to the week.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry HL
subjects.description: Six content areas with substantial additional material, a two-hour Paper 1 and a two-and-a-half-hour Paper 2. The additional work in electron-pair sharing reactions and in energy cycles is where HL candidates separate, and where students who learnt mechanisms as pictures rather than as electron movements come unstuck.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry SL
subjects.description: The same six areas at lower depth with an hour-and-a-half paper at each sitting. SL candidates lose most in the quantitative sections of Reactivity 2, because moles work at this level is examined through multi-step questions where one rounding error propagates to the final answer.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: The commonest partner subject in this cluster, especially among students aiming at medicine. The shared gain is data handling, and the shared risk is that both subjects demand precise causal language and students carry loose phrasing from one into the other.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Shares the assessment architecture exactly, so investigation technique learnt once transfers. The pairing is heavy on mathematics, and students taking both HL benefit from sessions sequenced so that uncertainty work happens in one subject and is applied in the other.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The pairing that makes HL Chemistry calculations feel routine. Logarithms arriving before the maths course has formalised them is the usual DP1 friction point, and ten minutes of algebra at the start of a chemistry session often saves the whole hour.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Entirely workable with chemistry, with one caveat. Students aiming at medicine, pharmacy or chemical engineering should read the named university's own stated prerequisite for the year of entry before settling the maths route in DP1.

subjects.name: IB Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Taken alongside chemistry by a number of students here and sharing much of its biochemistry vocabulary. Tutoring on data presentation and on justifying a conclusion from measured values pays into both subjects at once.

subjects.name: IB Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want a science without a second heavy quantitative load. It overlaps with chemistry in acid deposition, atmospheric systems and water quality, and the overlap is worth exploiting deliberately rather than by accident.

subjects.name: IB Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: A frequent request from this cluster and a demanding choice. The practical constraint is usually laboratory access, which is why essays that rely on a database or on secondary data often score better than ambitious bench work that cannot be controlled at school.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: The two years that decide whether HL Chemistry is realistic. The criterion worth watching is processing and evaluating, because it is where a student first has to defend a number rather than report it.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emirates-hil.regionsIntro: Where a student lives changes two things for chemistry: which school's laboratory and cohort they sit in, and the hour at which a session can realistically start. The notes below cover both.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Gated villa plots with long internal roads, so the bus run home is the binding constraint. HL Chemistry requests from here usually come in the second term of DP1, once the Reactivity 1 energetics work has been assessed for the first time.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Hosts an IB continuum school inside the community, and most chemistry students here have been assessed against MYP criteria for years. They write explanations comfortably and under-practise calculation, which is the opposite of the usual pattern.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: A large British-curriculum secondary sits inside Springs 3, so the chemistry work requested from this community is dominated by Cambridge 0620 technique and by students preparing to move into DP Chemistry the following September.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Often split across sectors, with one child taking DP Chemistry and a sibling taking A Level Chemistry. The two courses look similar and reward quite different answer structures, which is worth separating explicitly in back-to-back sessions.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Apartment living with short journeys, so earlier weekday slots are available. The limiting factor is a shared desk and background noise rather than traffic, and headphones make a measurable difference to a calculation-heavy hour.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Most secondary students travel out of community, typically towards Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. With door-to-door times of 35 to 45 minutes in evening traffic, a 5.30pm chemistry session is the realistic booking rather than a 4.30pm one.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Several of the larger DP cohorts this catchment feeds are taught here. Laboratory access for Extended Essay work is generally better at these campuses, which changes what is sensible to attempt in a chemistry essay.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Reached from Emirates Hills along Sheikh Zayed Road and a common destination for families moving from villa to apartment living. Chemistry students who move mid-DP keep the same tutor and the same slot, which is why the lessons are online.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs
schoolClusters.note: The schools inside or immediately beside these gates. They run both the IB continuum and IGCSE into A Level, which is why a single household can hold a DP Chemistry student working on Reactivity 2 and a Year 11 revising 0620 moles questions in the same week.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-emirates-hil.modesIntro: Three working patterns cover nearly every chemistry request from this cluster, and the right one is decided by the calendar rather than by preference.

modes.title: Weekly teaching alongside the school's scheme
modes.description: One session a week that follows the order the school is teaching in, consolidating what has just been covered and repairing what was rushed. Across two years this is what moves a chemistry grade, because every content area gets a second pass with marked written work in between rather than a single exposure.
bullets: A held Gulf Standard Time slot through the term
Content sequenced to the school's own order, not a generic plan
Written questions set between lessons and marked against the published scheme
A calculation set every fortnight so quantitative fluency never lapses

modes.title: Past-paper programmes by content area
modes.description: A block of work in which past questions are filtered to one content area and sat in sequence across several series. Students who have only ever sat whole papers are startled by how quickly a pattern emerges when they do ten Reactivity 2 questions in a row and see the same three traps repeat.
bullets: Questions filtered to one area, drawn from multiple series
Marked against the published scheme, with losses grouped by cause

modes.title: Investigation and Extended Essay feedback
modes.description: Short blocks around the student's own chemistry investigation or essay. The tutor challenges the research question before data is collected, explains what each criterion rewards, and responds to the student's own draft. The write-up stays entirely the student's work from start to finish.
bullets: Research question tested for control and measurability at the design stage

sections.heading: What an IB chemistry tutor in Emirates Hills does in the first three lessons
paragraphs: Lesson one is a marked script. Not a new topic, not a diagnostic quiz written by the tutor, but the most recent paper your child actually sat, read line by line against the published mark scheme. The output is a list of lost marks sorted by cause rather than a percentage, and in chemistry those causes fall into four reliable groups: content genuinely not known, chemistry understood but answered in the wrong register for the command term, calculation started correctly and abandoned before the final line, and questions left blank because the paper ran out of time.

Those four need completely different responses, which is why the sorting matters more than the total. Content gaps need teaching. Register problems need command-term work, which is quick and pays immediately. Abandoned calculations need method discipline, meaning every step written down even when the student can do it mentally. Unfinished papers need timing practice. A tutor who starts teaching before doing this sorting is guessing, and the family pays for the guess in weeks.

Lesson two takes the largest group and starts on it. If the loss is concentrated in Reactivity 2, the session covers amount of substance, rate and extent in that order, with a worked example and then questions the student does while the tutor watches. Watching matters: the moment a student stalls is far more informative than the written answer they eventually produce, and it cannot be seen in homework.

Lesson three closes the loop with a short timed set from the same area and a second marking against the scheme. By then the family has evidence rather than impressions, and the plan for the following six weeks writes itself. This sequence is identical whether the student lives inside the Emirates Hills gates, in The Meadows or along the Marina, because it is driven by the script rather than by the address.
bullets: Bring the most recent marked paper and the school's mark breakdown, not the report card
Expect losses to be grouped by cause, not reported as a percentage
Command-term errors are the cheapest marks on the paper to recover
Timing problems are fixed with a stopwatch, not with more content

sections.heading: The chemistry content map: Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3
paragraphs: The current guide is organised around two organising concepts rather than a numbered topic list, and a tutor still working from the older structure will teach correct chemistry in an order that matches no current paper. Structure asks what matter is: the particulate model and the mole, bonding and structure, and the classification of elements and organic compounds. Reactivity asks what matter does: what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and by what mechanisms.

That reorganisation has a real teaching consequence. Energetics and entropy now sit together under what drives chemical reactions, so a student who has met enthalpy but not entropy has half an answer to a spontaneity question. Equilibrium sits with rate and with amount of substance under how much, how fast and how far, which is why a question can move from a moles calculation into an equilibrium argument in the same part and catch out students who revised those as separate units.

Higher Level is not a different course. It is the same six areas with additional content, concentrated most visibly in energy cycles and in the electron-sharing and electron-pair-sharing reactions of Reactivity 3. An HL student who is struggling usually needs the additional material taught properly rather than the shared material revisited, and telling those two apart is the single most useful thing a first session can establish.

Use the table as a working map and confirm the detail through your school's IB coordinator, who holds the authoritative version of the guide. No tutoring page should be the final authority on a syllabus structure a grade depends on.

sections.heading: The command terms that decide whether a right answer scores
paragraphs: This is the part of chemistry tutoring that produces the fastest visible change, and almost nobody writing about IB chemistry online bothers with it. The IB mark scheme is built on command terms, and each one specifies a depth of answer. A student who explains when the question said state has wasted time. A student who states when the question said explain has lost the mark while knowing the answer perfectly. Both errors are invisible to the student and obvious on a marked script.

The pattern is learnable in about three sessions. State and identify want a short, unqualified answer. Outline wants a brief account without detail. Describe wants an account of events or features. Explain wants reasons or mechanisms, which means the word because, or its logical equivalent, has to appear. Deduce wants a conclusion reached from given information, so the information has to be referred to. Determine and calculate want a number with units and visible working. Discuss wants a balanced review, which means more than one position.

The practical method is a log. Every marked question gets its command term written next to the mark lost, and after two weeks a pattern appears: this student loses marks on explain and discuss, that one on deduce. The remedy is then specific rather than general, and it survives into the exam because the student starts reading the verb before the chemistry. It is the cheapest intervention available in this subject.

sections.heading: Moles, enthalpy and equilibrium: the three places grades quietly bleed
paragraphs: If a chemistry grade is being lost in a diffuse, hard-to-diagnose way, it is almost always in one of three quantitative areas. The first is amount of substance. Students can define a mole and still lose marks across a whole paper by rounding mid-calculation, dropping units between steps, or failing to identify the limiting reagent before dividing. The remedy is procedural, not conceptual: write the balanced equation, write what you have under each species, convert everything to moles before anything else happens, and never round until the final line.

The second is energetics. Sign conventions in enthalpy are the single most common source of a confidently wrong answer in Reactivity 1. An exothermic change releases energy and carries a negative enthalpy change, and a student who has absorbed that as a rule rather than as a consequence will invert it under pressure. Entropy compounds the problem, because it is frequently taught as disorder and then examined as a quantity that has to be combined with enthalpy to reach a conclusion about spontaneity. Questions that ask for a judgement about whether a reaction proceeds need both terms handled with their signs intact.

The third is extent of reaction. Equilibrium questions reward a particular discipline: identify the change, apply the shift, then explain the shift in terms of the system opposing the change rather than preferring an outcome. Students who have learnt a phrase about shifting to the right produce answers that sound right and score nothing. The ones who score write about what happens to the concentrations and why the system responds as it does.

All three respond to filtered past-paper work rather than to re-teaching. Ten questions from the same area in one sitting makes the repeated trap visible to the student, which is a different kind of learning from being told about it. That is the argument for the programme in the next section.
bullets: Convert to moles before anything else, and round only at the final line
Treat enthalpy signs as a consequence of energy flow, not as a rule to recall
Combine enthalpy and entropy when a question asks whether a reaction proceeds
Answer equilibrium questions through concentrations, not through direction alone
Always identify the limiting reagent before dividing by anything

sections.heading: Organic chemistry and the HL mechanisms
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where Higher Level separates most sharply from Standard, and where the difference between a student who has memorised and a student who understands becomes impossible to hide. Structure 3 introduces functional groups as a classification system, and Reactivity 3 asks what those groups do: proton transfer, electron transfer, electron sharing and electron-pair sharing. At HL, that last category is where full mechanisms are expected.

The failure is nearly always the same. Students learn mechanisms as pictures to reproduce rather than as accounts of where electrons go. The curly arrow is treated as decoration, so it starts in the wrong place, points at the wrong atom, or is omitted at the step that actually carries the mark. An examiner reading that cannot award credit for an intention; the arrow either shows the movement of an electron pair from a specific source to a specific destination or it does not.

The repair is slow but completely reliable. Draw the mechanism while narrating what is electron-rich and what is electron-poor. Identify the nucleophile and the electrophile out loud before drawing anything. Then draw the arrows and check each one by asking what pair of electrons is moving and from where. Students who do this for twenty mechanisms stop needing to do it, because the pattern generalises. Students who skip it have to memorise every new mechanism separately, and in an exam they will meet one they have not seen.

Reaction pathways deserve their own practice. A multi-step synthesis question tests whether the student can plan backwards from the target, and that is a different skill from reciting a single conversion. Working a set of pathway questions in sequence, with the target written first and the route constructed in reverse, is one of the highest-return exercises available in HL chemistry.

sections.heading: An eight-week past-paper programme that actually changes the score
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most families in this cluster arrive with, usually after a disappointing mock. The temptation is to cover everything. The programme below does the opposite: it measures first, narrows hard, and spends the last fortnight on the mechanics of sitting the paper rather than on chemistry.

Week one is measurement. A full Paper 1 and Paper 2 under real timing, marked by the tutor against the published scheme, with every lost mark tagged by content area and command term. The output is a table the family can read, and it almost always surprises them: the area the student complains about is rarely the area costing the most marks. Weeks two to five then take the two costliest areas and work them with filtered past questions drawn across several series, ten or more from the same area in a sitting, so the repeated trap becomes visible rather than described.

Weeks six and seven return to whole papers, one of each per week, with the mark scheme read aloud against the student's script afterwards. This is where command-term discipline is consolidated, because the student hears what the examiner was counting while their own wording is still fresh. The final week is deliberately light: timing, data booklet navigation, the order in which to attempt questions, and a short written checklist to run before handing a paper in.

One note on materials. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to the IB and are not reproduced or supplied here. They are referenced and accessed through your school or the board's own channels, which is both the legal position and the practical one, since a school holds the correct version for your child's session.

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation: the uncertainty nobody records
paragraphs: A fifth of the grade sits in one independent investigation, capped at 3,000 words, and chemistry investigations fail in ways that are specific to chemistry. The commonest is a titration-based study in which the student records a volume to two decimal places and never records the uncertainty of the glassware that produced it. The second commonest is a rate study with too few data points to establish a relationship, because the time available was spent on three repeats of one concentration instead of five concentrations.

Both are design problems, which means both are fixable only before data collection. That is the single most important scheduling point in this section: useful tutoring on an investigation happens at the planning stage. A tutor reading a finished draft can improve how it is written, but cannot create data that was never gathered. Families who come for investigation help two weeks before submission are usually asking for the one thing that cannot be delivered.

The things worth checking at design stage are concrete. Is there a single independent variable that can actually be varied over a sensible range? Are the controlled variables genuinely controllable in a school laboratory? Does the measurement have an uncertainty the student can state, and will the processed uncertainty be small enough for the result to mean anything? Is there an accepted value or a literature comparison available for the conclusion to be measured against? A no to the last question is not fatal, but it is worth knowing before the bench work starts.

The boundary is the same as everywhere else on this site, and it is not negotiable. A tutor explains what the criteria reward, challenges the research question, points at a graph that does not support the stated claim, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor never writes, completes or produces the report. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments outright; the person who carries the malpractice finding is your child, and the certificate is what is at risk.

sections.heading: What chemistry tutoring costs in Dubai, and what you can check yourself
paragraphs: Here is a useful way to read any tutoring price in this market: ask what you could verify independently. Almost nothing on the competing pages for these searches can be checked, because three of the six publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars. So the figures below are all attributed, in AED, with the provider that published them named, so that you can go and look.

What a parent can verify, and should: the hourly rate a provider advertises on its own site, the currency it quotes in, whether the rate includes VAT, whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and what the cancellation and replacement terms are in writing. What a parent cannot verify, and should discount accordingly: a satisfaction percentage without a sample size, a star rating a provider has awarded itself, a claim about examiner status with nothing to evidence it, and any promise about a grade.

On the numbers themselves: Bestimate's Dubai rate tables place a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Budget online tutoring, generally delivered by university students, is advertised from around AED 45 to 150. Published in-home one-to-one rates run AED 180 to 500, with monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appearing at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against an online package advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions.

Two things that belong in the same frame. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. And IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at all: lessons are one-to-one over live video, which is why the in-home column above is market context rather than an option on offer. The figures are market rates read in October 2026, not a price list; ask for a current quote and use the free first lesson before committing anything.

whyPoints.title: Taught from the current six-area guide
whyPoints.description: Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, in the order the current guide uses. A tutor working from an older topic list teaches correct chemistry in a sequence that no current paper follows, and the student revises against the wrong map.

whyPoints.title: Command terms treated as the mark scheme treats them
whyPoints.description: State, outline, explain, deduce, determine and discuss each specify a depth of answer. Logging which verbs cost marks and drilling those is the fastest visible improvement available in this subject.

whyPoints.title: Filtered past-paper work, not whole papers only
whyPoints.description: Ten questions from one content area in a sitting makes the repeated trap visible to the student. Whole papers measure; filtered sets fix. The programme uses both, in that order.

whyPoints.title: Investigation help at the design stage
whyPoints.description: Chemistry investigations fail on uncertainty never recorded and on too few data points. Both are design faults, so the useful conversation happens before the bench work, not two weeks before submission.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can go and verify
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate on this page names the provider that published it. No self-awarded ratings, no satisfaction percentages without a sample, no claims about grades achieved.

faqs.question: Which six content areas does the current IB Chemistry guide use?
faqs.answer: Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, including the nuclear atom, electron configurations, the mole and ideal gases. Structure 2 covers the ionic, covalent and metallic models of bonding. Structure 3 covers classification, both of elements in the periodic table and of organic compounds by functional group. Reactivity 1 asks what drives chemical reactions, bringing enthalpy and entropy together. Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far. Reactivity 3 asks what the mechanisms are. Higher Level covers the same six with additional content rather than different content.

faqs.question: Why does my child write correct chemistry and still lose the mark?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer does not match the command term. The IB mark scheme specifies a depth of response for each verb: state wants a short unqualified answer, explain wants causally linked reasons, deduce wants a conclusion that refers to the information given, determine wants a number with units and visible working, and discuss wants more than one position. A student who explains when the question said state loses time; one who states when it said explain loses the mark while knowing the answer. Logging the command term beside each lost mark makes the pattern visible within a fortnight.

faqs.question: What are the commonest moles calculation errors in IB Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Four, in order of frequency. Rounding mid-calculation and carrying the error to a confident wrong final answer. Dropping units between steps so that a correct number ends up attached to the wrong quantity. Dividing before identifying the limiting reagent, which gives a plausible answer to a different question. And skipping the substitution line, which forfeits method marks even when the final figure is right. The remedy is procedural rather than conceptual: balanced equation first, convert everything to moles before anything else, show every line, round only at the end.

faqs.question: How are enthalpy sign conventions examined in Reactivity 1?
faqs.answer: As a consequence of energy flow rather than as a rule to recall, which is why students who memorised it invert it under pressure. An exothermic change releases energy to the surroundings and carries a negative enthalpy change. Questions in this area frequently go further and ask for a judgement about whether a reaction proceeds, which needs enthalpy and entropy handled together with their signs intact. Entropy taught loosely as untidiness produces answers that read well and score nothing, because the mark is awarded for combining the two terms to reach the conclusion.

faqs.question: Why do equilibrium answers that sound right score nothing?
faqs.answer: Because they describe a direction instead of a mechanism. A student who has learnt a phrase about shifting to the right can produce a fluent sentence that the mark scheme cannot credit. What earns the mark is identifying the change imposed on the system, stating what happens to the concentrations involved, and explaining that the system responds so as to oppose the imposed change. Answered that way the chemistry is visible and the mark follows. This is one of the clearest cases in the subject where filtered past-paper practice beats re-teaching the topic.

faqs.question: How should HL organic mechanisms be learnt so they survive an exam?
faqs.answer: As accounts of electron movement, not as pictures to reproduce. The curly arrow has to start at a specific pair of electrons and point at a specific destination, and an examiner cannot credit an intention. The reliable method is to identify what is electron-rich and what is electron-poor before drawing anything, name the nucleophile and the electrophile out loud, then draw each arrow and check what pair is moving and from where. Students who do that for roughly twenty mechanisms stop needing to, because the pattern generalises to mechanisms they have never seen.

faqs.question: What goes wrong with titration-based chemistry investigations?
faqs.answer: The uncertainty of the glassware is almost never recorded. A student writes a volume to two decimal places, which looks precise, and never states the uncertainty of the burette or pipette that produced it, so the processed result has no meaningful error to compare against an accepted value. The second failure is a rate study with too few concentrations, because the available time went into repeats of one. Both are design faults, so they can only be fixed before data collection. Investigation help two weeks before submission cannot create data that was never gathered.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a chemistry tutor into Emirates Hills?
faqs.answer: No. Teaching for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only. There is no UAE office or centre. The practical reason is the specialism: command of HL Reactivity 3 mechanisms and of quantitative equilibrium is narrow, and a tutor who spends two hours driving for one hour of teaching cannot sustain a week built from that narrow a specialism. Removing the journey widens the pool to whoever is genuinely strongest at the hour you need.

faqs.question: What does an IB Chemistry specialist charge in Dubai in AED?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours, so you can check them. Bestimate's Dubai rate tables place a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Budget online tutoring is advertised from about AED 45 to 150. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour. These were read in October 2026 and are not IB Gram's price list, so ask for a current quote and use the free first lesson.

faqs.question: How does DP Chemistry differ from Cambridge 0620 in what it asks for?
faqs.answer: The content overlap is larger than students expect and the assessment overlap is smaller. Three demands are new: quantitative work carried through several steps without intermediate rounding, thermodynamic reasoning in which signs carry meaning, and extended explanation of mechanism rather than a short structured answer. A student who did well on 0620 Paper 4 often finds DP Paper 2 unfamiliar purely because of answer length. Six to eight weeks of focused work, ideally in the summer before DP1, closes most of the gap, and it is writing practice rather than content revision.

faqs.question: Is HL Chemistry realistic alongside Applications and Interpretation maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, with eyes open about where the friction will be. Logarithms and the manipulation of exponential relationships arrive in chemistry before that maths course has formalised them, so a few minutes of algebra at the start of a chemistry session often saves the hour. The more consequential question is admissions: medicine, pharmacy and chemical engineering courses state their own prerequisites and some name the mathematics route explicitly. Read the requirement on each university's own admissions pages for the year of entry before the DP1 choice is finalised rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a week do Emirates Hills families usually book?
faqs.answer: One a week through DP1 and DP2, rising to two for an eight-week block before mocks or the May session. One weekly hour is enough to give each content area a second pass with marked work in between, which is what actually moves a grade over two years. Two a week is for triage: one session teaching the costliest area and one sitting and reviewing filtered past questions. More than two is rarely productive, because the limiting factor becomes the time the student has to do and absorb the work set, not the teaching.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply IB past papers and mark schemes for chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to. Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the IB and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter; for unreleased material it is also an assessment-security matter. A tutor references them and works from what your child's school provides, which has the practical advantage of being the correct version for the session being sat. If a provider is handing out a library of board material, that tells you something about how else it operates.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade can eight weeks realistically move?
faqs.answer: Enough to be worth doing, and no honest tutor will put a number on it. What eight weeks reliably delivers is the recovery of marks lost to command-term mismatch, to abandoned calculations and to unfinished papers, because those are technique rather than knowledge. It also closes one or two content areas properly. What it does not do is cover six content areas from scratch. Any provider offering a specific grade improvement is selling a feeling, and no claim about outcomes appears anywhere on this site without a sample size and a method.

faqs.question: What happens if no HL Chemistry tutor is free at our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told before any booking, with the alternatives stated plainly. HL Chemistry at Gulf Standard Time evening slots is reasonably well covered, but a narrow request at an awkward hour, or one arriving in the fortnight before a May session, cannot always be met. In that case you are offered the nearest available specialist and the slot that genuinely exists, or an honest no. No competing provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is exactly why it is written here rather than discovered in the third week.

intro.heading: Three comparisons a chemistry family here makes, usually without the detail
paragraphs: Before a Green Community family hires a chemistry tutor, they have usually already made two or three decisions in the dark. Whether chemistry sits at Higher or Standard Level. Whether chemistry or biology is the safer science. And, for some, whether the IB Diploma or the A Level route at a nearby UK-curriculum school is the better place for a science-minded student. Each of those is answerable with specifics, and each is usually settled on impressions.

The Higher against Standard Level choice is the sharpest. Families treat it as a question of ambition, when it is really a question of what the extra content demands. Higher Level chemistry extends inside every area of the course - energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, organic, analytical - and adds a quantitative demand to work that was qualitative at Standard Level. The relevant test is not whether a student likes chemistry but whether they tolerate multi-step quantitative reasoning when the first step does not resolve cleanly.

The chemistry against biology comparison is the one most often decided on the wrong evidence. Students who found IGCSE biology easier choose biology, and discover that Diploma biology is content-dense and command-term unforgiving in ways IGCSE was not. Students who found IGCSE chemistry hard avoid chemistry, when their actual difficulty was mole arithmetic, which is a mathematics problem that follows them into biology statistics anyway.

The third comparison is local and real. Both routes exist within a short drive of Green Community: IB Diploma provision in Dubai Investments Park and The Sustainable City, and A Level provision at UK-curriculum schools in Jebel Ali and nearby. They assess chemistry differently and demand different things, and the decision deserves more than a preference for one school's atmosphere.

There is a fourth comparison worth making before any of the others, and it is about what to buy. A short decision review - three or four sessions that produce a timed diagnostic, an honest statement of the quantitative load at Higher Level, and a reading of the actual entry requirements for two or three target degree programmes - costs a fraction of a term of weekly tuition. Families here routinely skip the cheap purchase and buy the expensive one, then spend a year propping up a level that was never the right fit. Deciding first is both cheaper and more useful.

What this page does is put the chemistry detail behind each comparison, then describe where marks actually go at each level, what the investigation requires, and what the market charges. IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and laboratory work stays at school under the teacher's supervision as the IB requires.

One note on dates: Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and we cite them where relevant, while IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session and publishes no specific IB examination or results date.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-green-commun.subjectsIntro: The areas of Diploma chemistry that generate requests from this community, with how each one differs between Standard and Higher Level. The comparison is the point of this page, so the subject notes follow it.

subjects.name: Moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Identical in principle at both levels and more punishing at Higher, because the calculations sit inside longer multi-step questions. Set-up order decides marks: converting to moles after applying a ratio produces a plausible answer from the wrong proportion.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Standard Level asks what a force is and what it does; Higher Level asks for more quantitative consequences and finer distinctions. The shared loss is naming an intermolecular force without stating its physical effect.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermodynamics
subjects.description: Standard Level handles enthalpy cycles and calorimetry; Higher Level extends into entropy and spontaneity. Sign conventions decide marks at both levels, and an exothermic value written positive invalidates an otherwise flawless cycle.

subjects.name: Kinetics
subjects.description: Qualitative at Standard Level and quantitative at Higher, where rate expressions and orders of reaction arrive. Students describe what speeds a reaction up without explaining the effect on collision frequency, which halves the mark.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: Standard Level asks for the direction of a shift; Higher Level adds the equilibrium constant and calculation. The characteristic loss is stating the shift without the reasoning the question asked for.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and buffers
subjects.description: pH and strong-weak distinctions at Standard Level, buffers and fuller calculation at Higher. Buffer questions are procedural once understood, which makes them among the most reliable Higher Level marks available late.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: Half-equation balancing and cells at both levels, extended at Higher. Half-equation balancing is mechanical and therefore trainable quickly, which makes it one of the fastest gains in the second Diploma year.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Reaction types, reagents and conditions at both levels; Higher Level pushes further into mechanism. An arrow drawn from the wrong atom or bond loses the mark even beside a correct product, and that single convention accounts for a large share of Higher Level losses.

subjects.name: Analytical techniques
subjects.description: Spectroscopy and structure determination, where the skill is deduction from several pieces of evidence rather than recall. Students who read one spectrum in isolation miss the combination the question was built from.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The same criteria at both levels with a greater depth expectation at Higher. Chemistry investigations fail on feasibility more than on topic: a reagent, concentration or instrument the school does not hold, discovered during the practical.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level chemistry, compared on what differs
paragraphs: The useful comparison is not "more content" but what kind of content, because the Higher Level extensions change the type of thinking required rather than simply the volume. In energetics, Standard Level handles enthalpy cycles and calorimetry while Higher Level extends into entropy and spontaneity, which asks a student to reason about a quantity they cannot picture. In kinetics, what was qualitative becomes quantitative: rate expressions, orders of reaction, and calculations whose set-up is the marked part.

In equilibrium, Standard Level asks which way a system shifts and Higher Level asks by how much, through the equilibrium constant. In acids and bases, buffers arrive, which are procedural once understood and therefore a reliable source of marks. In organic chemistry, mechanism moves from peripheral to central, and the drawing conventions - arrow origin, intermediates shown, conditions stated with the reagent - start deciding the grade.

Taken together, the Higher Level demand is multi-step quantitative reasoning sustained through longer questions. That is why the honest test for a family is not enthusiasm for chemistry but tolerance for a calculation whose second step does not resolve cleanly. A student who stops at that point loses the later parts of nearly every long question, and that behaviour is harder to change than any single topic.

The counter-case for Standard Level deserves stating plainly, because families treat it as a retreat. A student who holds Standard Level chemistry securely, and uses the freed capacity on two Higher Level subjects they are strong in and an Extended Essay done properly, frequently finishes with a better points total than one stretched thinly across three Higher Level sciences. The Diploma is scored across six subjects and the core, not across one.

sections.heading: The step from IGCSE chemistry, described in specifics
paragraphs: Families are told the Diploma is a step up from IGCSE and rarely told where the step actually is. For chemistry it is in three identifiable places, and knowing them turns a vague warning into a term of useful preparation.

The first is organic chemistry. At IGCSE it is largely nomenclature, functional groups and uses, learned and recalled. In the Diploma it becomes mechanism: electrons moving, drawn with conventions that are marked as strictly as any calculation. A student who was comfortable naming compounds finds the subject has changed character rather than deepened, and that is why strong IGCSE candidates sometimes struggle first in this exact area.

The second is quantitative volume. Mole calculations exist at IGCSE and sit inside short questions. In the Diploma they sit inside longer multi-step problems where an early set-up error propagates silently to a plausible wrong answer. The arithmetic is not harder; the exposure to a single early mistake is much greater, which is why set-up order becomes a discipline rather than a preference.

The third is explanation depth. IGCSE frequently rewards a correct fact; the Diploma rewards the reasoning that connects facts. "Explain" means a causal chain, and a student whose default is a correct statement of chemistry loses the high-tariff marks consistently without identifying the pattern, because each individual loss looks like an unlucky question. All three of those are addressable in a term, and all three are much cheaper to address before the first Diploma report than after it.

sections.heading: Chemistry, biology or physics: choosing a Diploma science on the right evidence
paragraphs: Most students in this catchment take one or two Diploma sciences and choose them in MYP 5 or Year 11, usually on which IGCSE science felt easiest. That is weak evidence, because the three subjects change character between IGCSE and the Diploma in different directions.

Biology becomes content-dense and command-term unforgiving. The facts are accessible and the marks hang on connected accounts: a six-mark question answered as a list of true statements caps itself regardless of knowledge. Students who chose biology because it required no mathematics discover that the statistics and the data-handling in the investigation do, and that the writing demand is higher than IGCSE suggested.

Physics becomes a subject about causal explanation and uncertainty, where a correct formula without a chain of reasoning earns part marks at best, and where fields asks a student to hold an abstract model and a sign convention at once. Chemistry becomes a subject about mechanism conventions and multi-step quantitative set-up. Those are three different demands, and a student is rarely equally suited to all three.

The better evidence is a short diagnostic in each candidate subject at the standard the Diploma will demand, plus an honest look at the student's tolerance for each kind of work. A student who stops when a calculation gets messy will struggle more in Higher Level chemistry than in biology; one who cannot write a connected paragraph will struggle more in biology than in chemistry. And a student whose real weakness is mole arithmetic should know that it is a mathematics problem which will reappear as statistics in biology rather than disappearing.

sections.heading: Where chemistry marks go at each level, and what recovers them
paragraphs: At both levels the recurring losses are conventions rather than knowledge, which is good news because conventions respond to enforcement rather than to understanding. Four of them account for most of what a Green Community chemistry student leaves on the table.

Enthalpy sign is the cruellest, because every arithmetic step can be correct. An exothermic value written positive invalidates a cycle that is otherwise flawless, and the student sees no error to find. The fix is mechanical: write the sign before the magnitude, every time, even when it feels obvious. Four sessions of that enforcement normally removes it for good.

Mole set-up order is the most expensive. Applying a stoichiometric ratio before converting masses to moles yields an answer of plausible magnitude from the wrong proportion, and nothing on the script looks wrong. Enforcing masses-to-moles-first, without exception, is the single most valuable habit in the subject at either level.

Arrow origin is the Higher Level one. A curly arrow must start at a lone pair or at a bond, never at an atom label and never from nowhere, and an arrow from the wrong place loses the mark beside a correct product. Checking arrow origins on every mechanism drawn, every session, is what fixes it. The fourth is explanation depth: "explain" wants reasoning that connects facts, and a correct chemical statement where reasoning was asked earns part marks at best.

All four are visible on a single marked script, which is why the first session is spent reading rather than teaching. A tutor who starts explaining before marking is guessing at which of the four is costing the marks, and in chemistry the four have very different costs.

sections.heading: The investigation, and how feasibility differs from the other sciences
paragraphs: Every Diploma science carries an internally assessed investigation marked against criteria covering design, analysis, conclusion and evaluation. They fail differently by subject, and knowing the chemistry failure mode in advance saves a term.

Physics investigations fail on measurement precision: the expected effect is smaller than the instrument's uncertainty and the data cannot support any conclusion. Biology investigations fail on control of variables in living systems. Chemistry investigations fail on feasibility: the question requires a reagent, a concentration or a balance resolution the school laboratory does not hold, and this is discovered during the practical session rather than during the design.

So the first job on a chemistry investigation is a twenty-minute conversation rather than a lesson. What does the school actually have? Which concentrations are available? Is there a balance with the resolution this question needs? A question that survives those three checks is worth developing; one that does not should be replaced in week one, not in week six with a rushed substitute that leaves the evaluation criterion carrying the whole piece.

The second job is uncertainty derived rather than invented. Volumetric glassware has stated tolerances, a balance has a resolution, and a titration calculation propagates those through several operations. A plausible round number quoted as an uncertainty loses marks in the analysis criterion and again in the evaluation criterion, because the evaluation then has nothing real to engage with. And the boundary is firm: a tutor checks, explains, questions and marks; the student designs, runs and writes every word.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why chemistry carries the sharpest version of it
paragraphs: Chemistry has a particular academic-honesty exposure because the investigation produces data, and data can be adjusted in a way an essay cannot. A student who alters a reading to improve a trend has done something more serious than writing a weak conclusion, and the evaluation criterion exists partly to reward honesty about imperfect results.

So the first thing we say on any chemistry investigation is that unexpected data is not a failure. A result that contradicts the expectation is material for the evaluation criterion. A result that has been tidied is a malpractice exposure that can cost the Diploma. We say it in the first session rather than the last, because deadline pressure is when the temptation arrives.

The writing boundary is the same as in every subject. A tutor may teach the chemistry, explain each criterion and its mark ceiling, check feasibility, check uncertainty propagation, question whether the conclusion follows, check referencing conventions and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce data. Services in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which buys an investigation the student cannot defend.

Three further claims to set aside. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership. And we do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not evidenceable for individuals and is routinely used in this market to imply access to marking or grade boundaries that nobody has.

sections.heading: What chemistry tutoring costs here, compared across the bands
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors advertising to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

For chemistry the entry band does little that matters. Someone at the lower end can keep a student working through questions and cannot tell them that the arrow in their mechanism starts in the wrong place, or that their titration uncertainty was invented rather than derived. The real comparison is between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band, and the difference there is mostly a journey.

A second comparison is worth making, because families here face it. A decision review - a short block that settles whether chemistry belongs at Higher Level, or whether chemistry or biology is the right choice - costs a few sessions once. A term of weekly tuition propping up a level that was wrong for the student costs considerably more and does not fix the underlying mismatch. The cheap purchase is the one most families skip.

Monthly figures for planning: Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. sections.heading: Online chemistry from Green Community, and the laboratory question
paragraphs: The question every chemistry parent asks is whether a laboratory subject can be tutored over video, and the answer is that the laboratory part was never the tutor's job. Under IB rules practical work happens at school, with the school's apparatus, risk assessment and supervision. A tutor contributes the design beforehand and the analysis and writing afterwards, both of which are document and drawing work.

Mechanism teaching is the clearest case for the format. Organic chemistry is taught by drawing, and a shared screen where tutor and student draw on the same structure is at least as good as a sheet of paper between two chairs, with the advantage that the session is saved and reviewable. Arrow origins need to become automatic, and reviewing the same drawing a week later is part of how that happens.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, stated near the top of this page rather than left to be discovered, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

The honest limits: a student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better in person; a weak connection shortens the hour whatever the invoice says; a shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room; and no online tutor substitutes for laboratory time. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

sections.heading: Permits, and how to start with a comparison rather than a booking
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule. Never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

If the live question is the level or subject choice rather than a weakness, say so at the enquiry, because the right first purchase is different. Send the current level, the school, a photograph of the most recent marked assessment, and the two or three degree programmes your child has in view. The session that follows is a diagnostic plus a reading of the actual entry requirements, and it produces a written recommendation rather than a term of lessons.

If the live question is a weakness, send the level, the school, and whichever document is under pressure - a marked script or the current investigation draft. The first session reads it against the mark scheme and says plainly which of three positions you are in: convention errors recoverable in weeks, genuine content gaps needing a term, or both with a deadline too close to serve either properly.

Matching takes about a day for Standard Level chemistry and two or three for Higher Level in the second Diploma year, because the pool is narrow and a general science tutor in front of Higher Level organic work is worse than a short wait. The trial lesson is free, taught by the matched specialist, with no card details required. When nobody suitable has a slot at your hour we say so and offer alternatives rather than substituting.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level chemistry worth it for a Green Community student?
faqs.answer: It depends on tolerance for multi-step quantitative work rather than on enthusiasm for the subject. Higher Level extends inside every area: entropy in energetics, rate expressions in kinetics, the equilibrium constant, buffers, and extended organic mechanism. The common factor is reasoning sustained through longer questions, which punishes a student who stops when the second step does not resolve cleanly. Read the entry requirements for two or three target degree programmes first, because some specify a science at Higher Level and some do not.

faqs.question: Is taking chemistry at Standard Level a retreat?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it as one costs families points. The Diploma is scored across six subjects plus the core, not across one. A student who holds Standard Level chemistry securely, puts the freed capacity into two Higher Level subjects they are genuinely strong in, and writes an Extended Essay properly rather than in a weekend, frequently finishes with a better total than one stretched thinly across three Higher Level sciences. The relevant question is what the whole Diploma looks like, not how ambitious one line of it appears.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the step up from IGCSE chemistry?
faqs.answer: In three identifiable places. Organic chemistry changes character: at IGCSE it is names, groups and uses, and in the Diploma it is mechanism drawn to strict conventions. Mole calculations move from short self-contained questions into longer multi-step problems, where one early set-up error propagates silently to a plausible wrong answer. And explanation replaces recall, so "explain" wants reasoning that connects facts rather than a correct fact. All three are addressable in a term, and all three are cheaper to address before the first Diploma report.

faqs.question: Should my child choose chemistry or biology for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Decide it on what each subject actually demands rather than on which IGCSE science felt easier. Diploma biology is content-dense and command-term unforgiving: a six-mark question answered as a list of true statements caps itself. Diploma chemistry turns on mechanism conventions and multi-step quantitative set-up. A student who stops when a calculation gets messy will find chemistry harder; one who cannot write a connected paragraph will find biology harder. And a student whose real weakness is mole arithmetic should know it reappears as statistics in biology.

faqs.question: Can my child take both chemistry and biology at the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Many do, and the thing to plan for is not content but deadlines. Two sciences means two internally assessed investigations, usually with school deadlines in the same term as the Extended Essay and the mocks. Students with weak self-management find that term unmanageable regardless of how strong they are in either subject. If both sciences are taken, the investigations should be designed early and sequenced deliberately, with one substantially finished before the other begins in earnest.

faqs.question: How does IB chemistry compare with the A Level route available nearby?
faqs.answer: They examine chemistry differently and demand different things overall. A Levels take fewer subjects in greater depth with no Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay or Creativity, Activity, Service attached; the Diploma takes six subjects plus that core and scores out of 45. Practical work is assessed and reported differently by awarding body. Both routes exist within a short drive of Green Community, so read the specific entry requirements and the specification details from each school rather than relying on a general comparison between the systems.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose chemistry marks when the arithmetic is right?
faqs.answer: Most often the enthalpy sign or the mole set-up order. An exothermic value written positive invalidates a cycle in which every arithmetic step is correct, and the student sees no error to find. Applying a stoichiometric ratio before converting masses to moles yields an answer of plausible magnitude from the wrong proportion, again with nothing visibly wrong. Both are mechanical rules rather than concepts, and four sessions of strict enforcement - sign before magnitude, masses to moles first - normally removes them permanently.

faqs.question: What makes organic chemistry mechanism marks so unforgiving?
faqs.answer: The mark is for the movement of electrons, not for the product. A curly arrow must start at a lone pair or at a bond, never at an atom label and never from nowhere, and an arrow from the wrong place loses the mark even beside a correct product. Students who were never told this explicitly draw plausible arrows for a year without understanding why mechanism questions score low. Checking arrow origins on every mechanism drawn, every session, along with naming the reaction type and giving the reagent with its conditions, is the fix.

faqs.question: Why do chemistry investigations fail more often on feasibility than on topic?
faqs.answer: Because the question depends on what the school laboratory physically holds. A research question needing a particular reagent, a specific concentration, or a balance with enough resolution looks elegant on paper and cannot be run with the available apparatus. That is discovered during the practical session rather than during the design, and the rushed substitute written in week six leaves the evaluation criterion carrying the whole piece. A twenty-minute conversation with the teacher in week one prevents the entire sequence.

faqs.question: What should my child do if their chemistry data contradicts the expected result?
faqs.answer: Report it and evaluate it, which is what the criteria reward. Unexpected data is material for the evaluation criterion, not a failure to be corrected. A student who adjusts a reading to improve a trend has committed something considerably more serious than writing a weak conclusion, and it is a malpractice exposure that can cost the Diploma. We raise this in the first session on any investigation rather than the last, because deadline pressure is precisely when the temptation to tidy a result appears.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level chemistry tutor near Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Standard Level chemistry usually matches within a day. Higher Level in the second Diploma year takes two or three days, because the specialist pool is genuinely narrow and putting a general science tutor in front of Higher Level organic work is worse than a short wait. We state the expected wait at the enquiry rather than afterwards. A radius search from here for the same specialism commonly returns general science tutors, because Higher Level chemistry cohorts in this catchment are small.

faqs.question: Can online lessons teach organic chemistry mechanisms properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than sitting alongside. Organic chemistry is taught by drawing, and a shared screen where tutor and student draw on the same structure works at least as well as a sheet of paper between two chairs, with the advantage that the session is saved and can be reviewed a week later. Arrow origins need to become automatic rather than understood once, and reviewing the same drawing again is part of how that happens. Laboratory work remains the school's responsibility in any case.

faqs.question: Is a decision review cheaper than a term of chemistry tutoring?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and it is the purchase most families skip. Three or four sessions that settle whether chemistry belongs at Higher Level, or whether chemistry or biology is the better choice, cost a fraction of a term of weekly tuition propping up a level that was wrong for the student. The review produces a timed diagnostic at the standard the level will demand, an honest statement of the quantitative load, a reading of the actual degree entry requirements, and a written recommendation to take to the school.

faqs.question: Which chemistry marks are quickest to recover before the papers?
faqs.answer: Half-equation balancing and buffer calculations, because both are procedural: once the method is secure they are reliable rather than variable. After those, the conventions - enthalpy sign, mole set-up order, arrow origins, reagent with conditions - because they are mechanical and respond to enforcement within weeks. What will not move in the final stretch is a genuinely unfinished area of the syllabus, and an honest tutor says which of the two you are dealing with after reading one marked script.
