sections.heading: What a request for an IB chemistry tutor in JBR usually turns out to mean
paragraphs: In a first conversation, a parent describes chemistry as hard. Within ten minutes it resolves into something far more specific, and in this neighbourhood it resolves into one of four things almost every time. The student cannot do moles under time pressure. The student is memorising mechanisms. The student is at Higher Level and the additional material inside each theme was taught late and fast. Or the investigation has a research question the school laboratory cannot support.

Knowing which one you have is worth more than the first three sessions, because the four need different hours. Moles work is arithmetic discipline and the habit of writing down what is being asked before reaching for a relationship. Mechanism work is reasoning training. Higher Level content gaps are the easiest and cheapest of the four to close, which is exactly why they get left. Investigation trouble is a feasibility judgement and it has a hard deadline behind it.

The current syllabus organisation helps here, because it maps the four onto the course cleanly. Structure 1 is where the mole problems live. Reactivity 1 and 2 are where sign conventions and equilibrium calculation go wrong. Reactivity 3 is where mechanisms decide the grade. The investigation runs alongside all of it with its own clock. The table below sets the six themes out with what each one demands and where the Higher Level additions sit, which is the fastest way for a parent to place their child's difficulty.

sections.heading: The data booklet: what chemistry hands your child, and what it quietly does not
paragraphs: Chemistry candidates sit both written papers with the subject's data booklet available, and a remarkable number of students have never worked out what is in it. That ignorance costs marks in two opposite directions. Students memorise values that will be printed, wasting revision time on recall that earns nothing. And students assume something will be provided that is not, then lose the question entirely because they cannot proceed without it.

The fix is twenty minutes with the booklet open and a highlighter. Work through it section by section and write a single page listing what is given and what is not. Constants, the periodic table, standard enthalpy and electrode data, spectroscopic correlation tables and the characteristic infrared absorptions are the kinds of things supplied. What is not supplied is the ability to choose the right value, the reasoning that connects a spectral peak to a structural feature, or any of the mechanism types a student is expected to deploy.

There is a second and subtler point. Having a value supplied changes the question the examiner can ask. If a bond enthalpy is printed, the question will not be whether a student remembers it; it will be whether they can use it in a cycle with the correct signs. If an infrared absorption range is printed, the question is not what the range is but what the presence of that peak tells you about the molecule. Students who learn the booklet as a list of facts miss that the booklet reshapes the whole paper.

Do this once, in DP1, and it pays for two years. The table below is the checklist to work from, and the right-hand column is the point: for each item, decide whether the student needs recall or recognition, because those are two different kinds of revision and mixing them up is how a term of effort produces no grade movement.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: the term that decides a five from a seven
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is where Diploma chemistry grades separate, and the reason is uncomfortable. The subject is taught in a way that invites memorisation, and memorisation works until the examination uses a molecule the student has not seen. At that point a memorising student has nothing, while a reasoning student has everything they need, because the reasoning transfers and the picture does not.

The reasoning is learnable and it is not advanced. Where is the electron density. What is electron-poor and therefore liable to be attacked. Which bond is the weakest in this environment. What leaves, and what is left behind. A student who asks those four questions of any unfamiliar molecule will arrive at the right mechanism class most of the time, and will earn method credit even when the final product is wrong. A student reciting a learned arrow-pushing diagram earns nothing once the molecule changes.

Pathway questions are the second half of the problem and they have their own technique: plan backwards from the stated product rather than forwards from the starting material. Working backwards narrows the options at every step, because each functional group can only have arrived from a small number of precursors. Working forwards opens them, which is why students who start at the left-hand side of the question run out of time and confidence together.

This is also the part of chemistry where the delivery format genuinely helps. Arrow-pushing on a shared annotated canvas, with the tutor correcting an arrow the moment it is drawn wrongly, is more effective than the same conversation across a table, because the error is visible and fixable in the same second. For a JBR family that is the practical answer to whether online works for this subject: for mechanisms, it works better.

sections.heading: Moles, sign conventions and the arithmetic that quietly leaks marks
paragraphs: Quantitative chemistry loses more marks in this subject than conceptual chemistry does, and almost none of those losses are about understanding. They are about discipline: writing down the quantity being asked for before starting, keeping units attached to every line, carrying full precision until the final rounding, and respecting the sign convention that makes an exothermic enthalpy change negative.

The mole is the foundation and it is where a two-year problem usually begins. A student who converts between mass, moles, concentration and volume slowly will be slow in every quantitative question in both papers, and slowness in a timed paper reads as weakness. The remedy is unglamorous and it works: short, frequent, written conversions until the operation is automatic, which takes a few weeks rather than a term.

Sign conventions deserve their own paragraph because the cost is so disproportionate. An enthalpy calculation performed perfectly with the wrong sign scores nothing, and the same is true of several electrochemistry answers. Students who write the direction of energy flow in words beside each line almost never make the error; students who manipulate numbers without that annotation make it repeatedly, including in mocks where they have been warned.

The table below sets out the recurring quantitative losses with the component on which each usually appears. Use it to convert a vague report comment into a session objective, because a comment about weakness in calculations cannot be worked on and a comment about premature rounding in titration arithmetic can.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the experiments that actually work in a school laboratory
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade, a 3,000-word ceiling, and 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Those are the facts. The failure mode, in this city as everywhere, is feasibility: a student picks a question that sounds impressive and discovers in February that the school laboratory does not hold the reagent, that the reaction is too fast to time by hand, or that the apparatus cannot measure to the precision the analysis needs.

The investigations that work share characteristics. They vary one thing that can be varied in a controlled way with equipment a school actually owns. They produce enough data points to show a trend rather than two conditions to compare. They generate a measurement with a quantifiable uncertainty, because the evaluation criterion rewards a student who can say how much confidence their numbers deserve. And they can be repeated, which matters because the first run of any experiment usually teaches you how to run the second.

The investigations that fail are equally recognisable. Anything depending on an instrument the school does not have. Anything where the dependent variable is judged by eye. Anything with two data points. Anything requiring a reagent that cannot be obtained or safely handled at school level. And anything the student picked because it sounded like university chemistry, which almost always means the mathematics of the analysis is beyond the course.

The boundary on help has to be explicit here. A tutor may test feasibility, teach the chemistry the investigation needs, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, discuss uncertainty treatment, and read and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor may not design the investigation for the student, write any section, supply analysis to be inserted, or edit a draft until the work is no longer the student's own. Completed internal assessments are advertised for sale in this market at four-figure prices; that is a malpractice exposure that falls on the student, not a time saving.

sections.heading: Why Chemistry Higher Level is requested, and what to verify before relying on it
paragraphs: A large share of chemistry enquiries from JBR arrive attached to a plan: medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, chemical engineering, or a biomedical route. The parent has been told Higher Level Chemistry is needed, and usually that is correct in general terms. What is not safe is any specific claim about a specific university's requirement taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

Requirements are set by faculty and by programme, they differ between universities in the same city, and they change between admission cycles. A medical school may specify Chemistry at Higher Level with a minimum grade and a second science; an engineering programme may specify Chemistry or Physics; a biomedical science course may accept Standard Level with a particular mathematics course. The only reliable method is to open the admissions page for the specific programme at the specific university, read the line, and confirm it with the school's university counselling office in writing.

What a chemistry tutor can usefully do with that information is sequence the two years around it. A student needing a 6 or a 7 at Higher Level for a competitive route needs the Reactivity themes secure by the end of DP1, because the DP2 term where organic chemistry and the investigation collide is not a term in which to be learning energetics for the first time. That is a planning decision and it is made in September of DP1, not in January of DP2.

One further caution. Tutoring is not a requirement for university admission, for Ministry of Education equivalency, or for school progression, and anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a process that has published rules. sections.heading: The two-year chemistry rhythm against a Dubai calendar
paragraphs: Chemistry rewards planning more than most subjects because the content compounds and the independent work has a hard clock. Dubai schools sit the May session, the academic year runs from late August, and Ramadan falls inside it. Mapping the course onto that calendar, rather than onto an abstract two years, changes when tutoring is worth buying and what it should be doing.

DP1 autumn and spring are the Structure themes and the start of Reactivity. This is the cheapest window in the whole two years to fix a mole problem, and the one most often skipped because the grades still look acceptable. A weekly hour here is maintenance that prevents a DP2 crisis; the same hour in DP2 is crisis management at a higher rate.

The DP1 summer is when the investigation should be designed and, if the school allows, trialled. A question tested in June leaves room to change it; a question first considered in November of DP2 does not. Families who use those weeks get a better investigation and a calmer final year, and it is the single most valuable piece of scheduling advice on this page.

DP2 is where the pressure concentrates. Reactivity 3 and organic chemistry are usually taught in the same months as the investigation write-up and two or three other internal assessments, and for a JBR student that term also contains the longest commutes of the week. During Ramadan school days shorten and a post-Iftar slot is frequently the best chemistry hour of the day, particularly for mechanism work that needs an unhurried stretch. The table sets the rhythm out term by term.

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs around JBR, starting at the top of the market
paragraphs: Begin at the premium end, because that is where parents on a medical route are most likely to be pointed and it is worth knowing what the money is for. BartyED quotes AED 650 an hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. At that level you are paying for scarcity and for component-level specialism: somebody who has taught the current Reactivity themes, marked investigations against the four criteria and can read a mock script diagnostically. For a Higher Level student eight weeks from a mock, that is often the right purchase.

Below it the market steps down clearly. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. EdFlik publishes an entry tier at AED 45 to AED 65, and Tutopiya's comparison panel opens at AED 33 to AED 52, although that panel carries a revision date around twenty-one months old and should be read as historic. In-home visiting sits at AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's figures, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to AED 500. All of those were read in October 2026 on the providers' own pages.

Monthly, the picture is easier to budget against. Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour give AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Online packages around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits both appear in this market. For chemistry specifically the better value is almost always continuity in DP1 at a mid-tier rate rather than premium hours in DP2, because the subject compounds.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page. The sequence is a free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, then a quote once the level and the theme are known, because an hour of mole drilling and an hour of Higher Level mechanism reasoning are different products. For budget context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion; school fees are fixed this year and tutoring is the line still moving.

process.title: Name the level and the theme

process.title: A diagnostic trial in your real weekday slot
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details taken, held at the time the school run actually leaves open. The tutor sets an unaided conversion and an unfamiliar mechanism in the first fifteen minutes, which is the quickest way to find out whether the problem is arithmetic discipline, reasoning or content. You get that read in writing.

process.title: A plan mapped onto the school's calendar
process.description: Before the second session the tutor writes down the sequence, set against the school's theme order, its mock window and its investigation deadline. For a Higher Level student that plan usually puts investigation design in the DP1 summer and mechanism work in longer weekend sessions through the DP2 organic term.

process.title: Written notes, and a change of tutor if it is wrong
process.description: A short record after each session names what was covered, what the student did unaided and what remains open, and it can be shared with the school. Use it to decide whether to continue. If the match is not working, change tutor after two sessions; carrying a mismatch for a term is the expensive option in a subject that compounds.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the current syllabus, not an older one
whyPoints.description: The course has run on Structure and Reactivity themes since 2023, with Higher Level material inside each theme rather than in a separate block. A tutor or a revision guide working from the previous organisation teaches a different course, and in chemistry that mismatch is invisible until a mock exposes it.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms taught as reasoning, not pictures
whyPoints.description: Memorised arrow-pushing fails the moment the examination changes the molecule. Sessions build the four questions that handle anything unfamiliar: where the electron density is, what is electron-poor, which bond is weakest, what leaves. That reasoning transfers; a learned diagram does not.

whyPoints.title: Investigation feasibility checked first
whyPoints.description: Most failed chemistry investigations fail at the design stage, not the writing stage, because the school laboratory cannot support the question. We test feasibility before any experimental planning, which is the cheapest intervention available and the one almost nobody buys in time.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated out loud
whyPoints.description: Tutors test questions, teach the chemistry, explain the four criteria and comment on the student's own draft. They do not design the investigation, write any section, or edit to completion. Completed internal assessments are sold openly in this market at four-figure prices; that is a risk to a diploma, not a shortcut.

whyPoints.title: Rates traceable to the page that published them
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider and the month it was read, including the in-home band quoted only for comparison. Three of the six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all, and a rate without a source cannot be checked by the person spending the money.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand chemistry in class and lose marks in the paper?
faqs.answer: Usually because the losses are procedural rather than conceptual. Quantitative chemistry leaks marks through premature rounding, missing units, the wrong sign on an enthalpy change and slow mole conversions under timing, all of which look like weakness and are actually discipline. The fix is unglamorous: write the quantity being asked for before starting, keep units on every line, carry full precision to the end, and annotate the direction of energy flow in words beside each step of a cycle.

faqs.question: What are the six themes in the current IB Chemistry syllabus?
faqs.answer: The course runs on two concepts with three themes each. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level additional material sits inside each theme rather than in a separate block, which is why a pre-2023 revision guide describes a noticeably different course from the one your child is sitting.

faqs.question: Is the chemistry data booklet available in the examination?
faqs.answer: Yes, in both written papers, and most students have never audited what is in it. That costs marks twice over: time wasted memorising values that will be printed, and questions abandoned because something assumed to be supplied is not. Spend twenty minutes with the booklet in DP1 and write a single page listing what is given and what is not. Then revise accordingly, because recall and recognition are different kinds of practice.

faqs.question: My daughter has memorised the organic mechanisms. Why is she still losing marks?
faqs.answer: Because the examination changes the molecule. A memorised arrow-pushing diagram works on the compound it was learned from and collapses on an unfamiliar one, while a student reasoning from electron density handles anything the paper presents. Four questions do most of the work: where is the electron density, what is electron-poor and liable to be attacked, which bond is weakest in this environment, and what leaves. Those transfer, and they also earn method credit when the final product is wrong.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child's investigation question is actually doable?
faqs.answer: Test it against the laboratory rather than against how interesting it sounds. A workable question varies one thing in five or more controlled steps, uses equipment the school actually holds, produces a measurement with a stated instrumental uncertainty, can be repeated inside the available laboratory time, and needs only mathematics from inside the course. If any of those fails, the design criterion is damaged and everything downstream of it suffers. The DP1 summer is the right time to find this out.

faqs.question: How long should the chemistry scientific investigation be?
faqs.answer: Within a 3,000-word ceiling, and it is marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, at six marks each. It is worth 20 per cent of the grade. Students routinely spend their words on background reading and run short on evaluation, which is the criterion that most reliably separates a good report from an average one. Plan the evaluation at the start, as data is collected, rather than writing it in the final hour.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design the experiment for the investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can test whether a question is feasible, teach the chemistry it requires, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss how uncertainty should be treated, and read and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot design the investigation on the student's behalf, write any section, supply analysis to be inserted, or edit until the work is no longer the student's. That is a malpractice line under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, so it is not negotiable.

faqs.question: Should my child take the collaborative sciences project seriously?
faqs.answer: It is a ten-hour interdisciplinary project run across the science subjects as part of the practical scheme, and it is not externally assessed. Students and sometimes schools treat it as an administrative requirement, which wastes the opportunity. It is the one piece of investigative work in the whole course where a student can practise framing a question, controlling variables and handling uncertainty with no marks at stake, which makes it good preparation for the investigation that does count.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Chemistry much harder than Standard Level, or just longer?
faqs.answer: Both, and the additional material is the part most often taught in a hurry. Higher Level runs around 240 hours against 150 at Standard, sits longer versions of both papers, and extends each of the six themes rather than adding a separate block. In practice that means entropy and Gibbs energy, rate laws, buffers, further transition-element chemistry and further organic pathways. Students who reach the end of DP1 with the Structure themes insecure find the Higher Level DP2 term genuinely punishing.

faqs.question: My son is home at 16:40 from Al Barsha. Does chemistry work that late?
faqs.answer: Better than mathematics does, which is a useful thing to know when timetabling two subjects. Much of chemistry is recall, interpretation and drawing, and those survive tiredness reasonably well. What does not survive is mechanism work, which needs a student willing to be wrong on a page and to try again. Keep weekday hours for theme consolidation and put the organic and mechanism work at a weekend, particularly for the villa-belt commute where the return can reach fifty minutes.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma chemistry student start tutoring?
faqs.answer: The autumn of DP1, if the aim is value rather than rescue. Chemistry compounds: an insecure mole concept in October reappears in energetics, in equilibrium and in every organic calculation afterwards, so the cheapest intervention is the earliest one. The second high-value window is the DP1 summer, spent on investigation design. Hours bought in the spring of DP2 cost more, achieve less, and compete with four other internal assessments for the student's attention.

faqs.question: Do I need Higher Level Chemistry for medicine from a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Commonly yes, but verify the specific requirement rather than relying on any tutoring page, this one included. Medical schools set their own IB requirements, they differ between institutions in the same city, and they change between admission cycles. Open the admissions page for the exact programme, read the subject line, and confirm it in writing with your school's university counselling office. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission anywhere, and nobody should tell you it is.

faqs.question: Can online lessons really handle mechanism drawing and lab work?
faqs.answer: Mechanism drawing works better online than across a table, because a shared annotated canvas lets the tutor correct an arrow in the second it is drawn wrongly, with the whole sequence saved for revision afterwards. Laboratory work is different: the practical scheme belongs to the school and stays there. What a tutor contributes is the design thinking before the bench work and the analysis and evaluation afterwards, which is where most of the investigation marks sit anyway.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor come to our apartment in JBR?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. UAE lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared canvas for mechanisms, screen sharing for annotating the student's own script and saved worked solutions. The published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour appears on this page purely so the two formats can be compared on cost and tutor pool.

faqs.question: Does a chemistry tutor working with a Dubai student need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. It is granted free of charge for two years and applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are eligible. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level chemistry specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you before anything is paid. Standard Level chemistry is usually matched within the week. Higher Level with a specific Reactivity or investigation focus, in one fixed weekday slot, is the combination most likely to be unavailable at short notice, and in that case we offer the nearest workable time, propose a weekend session, or say plainly that we cannot staff it. An hour with someone who has not taught the current themes is worse value than no hour.

With those we can say whether the problem is mole discipline, mechanism reasoning, Higher Level content or an investigation that will not work, and whether we can staff your slot. Lessons run one to one on live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free, one per student, and no card details taken.

intro.heading: Diploma chemistry has two cliffs, and they arrive on schedule
paragraphs: Chemistry grades in the Diploma are decided at two predictable moments, and both are visible a term in advance. The first comes early in the course, when bonding and energetics stop being descriptive and start being quantitative. The second comes in the second year, when organic chemistry arrives and the subject becomes a set of mechanisms with conventions that have to be drawn exactly right. Students who were comfortable before each cliff are frequently not comfortable after it.

Because both are scheduled rather than random, they can be worked in advance. That is the whole argument for timing chemistry tutoring to the calendar instead of to the crisis. A family that starts six weeks before organic chemistry is taught is buying preparation. A family that starts six weeks after it was taught is buying repair, which takes longer and costs more, and competes for the weeks the investigation and the mocks have already claimed.

The other fixed edges are the internally assessed scientific investigation, which has a school-set deadline, and the mock window a term before the papers. In the final eight weeks nothing new should be taught, because new content there displaces the timed practice that converts knowledge into marks. Those four edges - two cliffs, one deadline, one mock window - are the whole plan.

There is a third edge that only chemistry families meet, and it is the reason the investigation deserves its own planning. A chemistry investigation depends on what the school laboratory physically holds: a reagent, a concentration, a balance with enough resolution. A research question that looks elegant on paper and cannot be run with the available apparatus is discovered during the practical session rather than during the design, and the substitute question written in a hurry is the one that costs the evaluation marks.

Geography is why this page also talks about delivery. Jebel Ali sits at the industrial western end of Dubai, around the port and the free zone, with its residential communities spread through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. A Higher Level chemistry specialist willing to drive to any of those at 5pm is a rare thing, and the further south the address, the rarer.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For chemistry that format works well, because mechanism teaching is drawing on a shared surface and investigation work is reading a document together. Laboratory work stays at school under the teacher's supervision, as the IB requires.

A note on dates. Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and we cite them where relevant. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publishes no specific IB examination or results date. The internal deadlines, which matter more to the plan, come from your school's Diploma coordinator.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of Diploma chemistry that generate requests from this part of Dubai, with the specific error each one produces on a marked script.

subjects.name: Moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The arithmetic underneath everything else. Marks go on set-up order rather than on calculation: students who convert to moles last instead of first produce a correct-looking answer from the wrong ratio and lose the whole question.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Intermolecular forces, shapes and the link between structure and physical property. The commonest loss is naming a force without explaining its effect, because the command term asked for a consequence rather than a label.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies and calorimetry. Sign conventions decide marks: an exothermic value written positive invalidates an otherwise flawless cycle, and the error is invisible to the student.

subjects.name: Kinetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Rate expressions, collision theory and the response of a system to change. Students describe what shifts without explaining why, and the marks sit in the why. Higher Level adds quantitative treatment that punishes vague reasoning.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH calculations, buffers at Higher Level, half-equations and electrochemistry. Half-equation balancing is procedural and therefore trainable, and it is one of the fastest mark gains available late in the course.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Reaction types, reagents, conditions and mechanisms. An arrow drawn from the wrong atom or bond loses the mark even when the product is right, and that single convention accounts for a large share of Higher Level losses.

subjects.name: Analytical techniques
subjects.description: Spectroscopy and structure determination, where the skill is deduction from several pieces of evidence rather than recall. Students who read one spectrum in isolation miss the combination the question was built around.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Internally assessed against criteria covering design, analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Chemistry drafts most often fail on a question the available apparatus cannot answer, or on a conclusion that reports a trend without the chemistry behind it.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data treatment
subjects.description: Resolution of volumetric glassware, propagation through a titration calculation, and uncertainty on a plotted result. Guessed rather than derived uncertainties cost marks on the papers and in the investigation at once.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: "State", "outline", "explain", "discuss" and "evaluate" set different depths. A correct chemical fact where "explain" was asked earns part marks at best, because the question wanted the reasoning that connects it.

sections.heading: The first cliff: when bonding and energetics turn quantitative
paragraphs: Early Diploma chemistry looks like an extension of IGCSE and then stops being one. Bonding moves from naming forces to explaining their quantitative consequences. Energetics moves from describing a reaction as exothermic to constructing an enthalpy cycle in which a single sign error destroys the answer. Students who were comfortable in the first weeks often report the subject becoming hard quite suddenly, and this is where.

Two specific conventions do most of the damage. The first is sign: enthalpy changes carry a sign that encodes direction, and writing an exothermic value positive invalidates a cycle that is otherwise flawless. The student cannot see the error, because every arithmetic step is right. The second is the mole set-up order. Converting to moles last rather than first produces an answer of plausible magnitude from the wrong stoichiometric ratio, and the mark is gone with no visible mistake to find.

Both are mechanical, which is good news: they respond to drilling rather than to understanding. Four sessions of enforced set-up order - masses to moles first, always, before any ratio is applied - removes most of the second problem permanently. Sign conventions take about the same, provided the tutor insists on the sign being written even when the student considers it obvious.

The timing argument matters here. A family that books four sessions in the weeks before energetics is taught in class pays for preparation. A family that books after the first energetics assessment pays for repair, and competes for the same weeks as the investigation. The school's scheme of work is usually available on request, and it tells you when the cliff arrives.

sections.heading: The second cliff: organic chemistry as a set of conventions
paragraphs: Organic chemistry at IGCSE is largely nomenclature, functional groups and uses. In the Diploma it becomes mechanism, and mechanism is drawn rather than written. That change catches out strong students, because the knowledge is present and the marks are allocated to the drawing conventions.

The decisive convention is arrow origin. A curly arrow starts at a lone pair or at a bond, not at an atom label, and not from thin air. An arrow drawn from the wrong place loses the mark even when the product written beside it is correct, because what the examiner is paying for is the movement of electrons. Students who were never told this explicitly draw plausible-looking arrows for a year and cannot understand why mechanism questions keep scoring low.

The second convention is conditions and reagent together. A reaction identified correctly but without its reagent, or with the reagent and no conditions, is an incomplete answer in a subject where the conditions often determine which product forms. The third is the mechanism-type label itself: naming the class of reaction earns marks that students routinely forgo by going straight to the product.

None of this needs a laboratory and all of it needs a shared drawing surface, which is why organic chemistry teaches well online. The drill is repetitive: draw the mechanism, state the type, give the reagent and conditions, then check the arrow origins. Done weekly through the second Diploma year, it converts organic chemistry from the hardest part of the paper into one of the most reliable.

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation, from feasibility to evaluation
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation is where a chemistry tutor can do the most legitimate good, and it fails in a way that is specific to the subject. Physics investigations fail on measurement. Chemistry investigations fail on feasibility: the research question requires a reagent, a concentration or an instrument the school laboratory does not hold, and nobody discovers this until the practical session.

So the first job is a feasibility check, and it is a conversation rather than a lesson. What does the school actually have? What concentrations are available? Is there a balance with the resolution this question needs? A question that survives those three questions is worth developing; one that does not should be replaced in week one rather than in week six with a rushed substitute.

The second job is uncertainty, derived rather than guessed. Volumetric glassware has stated tolerances, a balance has a resolution, and a titration calculation propagates those through several operations. A student who writes a plausible round number as their uncertainty loses marks in the analysis criterion and in the evaluation criterion, because the evaluation has nothing real to engage with.

The third job is the boundary, and it is firm. A tutor can narrow the question, check feasibility, teach the chemistry, explain each criterion and its ceiling, check propagation, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce or adjust data. Services in this market sell completed Internal Assessments, one advertising them at AED 3,750, and submitting bought work risks the entire Diploma.

sections.heading: Paper anatomy, and the habit each section punishes
paragraphs: Diploma chemistry is examined across papers that mix multiple-choice and data-based questions with extended written response. Each of those formats punishes a different habit, and treating them as one undifferentiated revision target is why a lot of late preparation produces no change.

Multiple-choice questions punish rushing. The distractors are built from the specific errors students make - a reversed sign, a ratio applied the wrong way, a unit mismatch - so an answer that feels obviously right is frequently the designed trap. The drill is to work the calculation rather than recognise the shape, which costs seconds and saves marks.

Data-based questions punish weak graph and uncertainty handling, and they reward a skill nobody revises: deciding what the data can and cannot support. A student who asserts proportionality from points whose uncertainty bars overlap has made a chemistry error. Linearisation, gradient units and physical interpretation of a gradient are all marked here.

Extended response punishes depth mismatch. "Explain" wants reasoning that connects facts; "discuss" wants both sides reaching somewhere; "evaluate" wants a judgement with evidence. A student whose default register is a statement of correct chemistry scores well on recall questions and loses consistently on the high-tariff ones. Separating the paper types in practice, rather than sitting whole papers only, is what exposes which of the three is costing the marks.

The practical implication is that whole-paper practice is the wrong starting point late in the course. Sitting a complete paper tells you the total and hides the cause. Working twenty multiple-choice questions, then four data-based questions, then four extended-response questions as separate exercises tells you which of the three formats is leaking marks, and that is what the following sessions should target.

sections.heading: What chemistry tutoring costs in Dubai, and what you are buying at each level
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026, attributed to whoever published them. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

For Diploma chemistry the entry band does very little. Someone at AED 50 an hour can keep a student working through questions; they cannot tell them that the arrow in their mechanism starts in the wrong place, or that their titration uncertainty was invented. The decision in chemistry is almost always between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band, and the difference between those two is mostly the journey.

Monthly figures are often more useful for a household plan. Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

None of these are IB Gram prices; this page has no rate card, because the fee depends on level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The bands exist so a quote can be judged against something published. Three of the pages currently ranking for this search publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams.

sections.heading: Online chemistry from a Jebel Ali address, including the laboratory question
paragraphs: The question every chemistry parent asks is whether a subject with a laboratory can be tutored over video. The answer is that the laboratory part was never the tutor's job. Under IB rules the practical work happens at school, with the school's apparatus, risk assessment and supervision. What a tutor contributes is the design before the practical and the analysis and writing after it, both of which are document and drawing work.

Mechanism teaching is the clearest case. Organic chemistry is taught by drawing, and a shared screen where tutor and student draw on the same structure is at least as good as a sheet of paper between two chairs, with the advantage that the whole session is saved and can be reviewed. Uncertainty work, graph interrogation and criterion-by-criterion review of a draft are all document work too.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, stated here near the top rather than discovered after a booking, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

The genuine limitations: a student who will not begin work without an adult present does better in person; a weak connection shortens the hour whatever the clock says; a shared study space in a Discovery Gardens apartment undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room; and nobody online substitutes for laboratory time. If one of those describes your household, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in chemistry, where the risk is highest
paragraphs: Chemistry carries a particular academic-honesty risk because the investigation produces data, and data can be altered in a way an essay cannot. A student who adjusts a reading to improve a trend has committed a more serious act than one who writes a weak conclusion, and the evaluation criterion exists partly to reward honesty about imperfect results.

So the first thing a good chemistry tutor teaches about the investigation is that unexpected data is not a failure. A result that does not match the expectation is material for the evaluation criterion. A result that has been tidied is a malpractice exposure that can cost the Diploma. We say that explicitly in the first session on any investigation, because students under deadline pressure are the ones who reach for the eraser.

The boundary on writing is the same as in every subject and worth restating. A tutor may teach the chemistry, explain each criterion and its mark ceiling, check feasibility, check uncertainty propagation, question whether the conclusion follows, check referencing conventions and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce data. There are services selling completed Internal Assessments in this market at AED 3,750, and that transaction is worse value than it looks.

The other claims to discount: we are not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy; we claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership; we do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not evidenceable for individuals and is routinely used to imply access to marking that nobody has; and we promise no grade, points total or improvement figure.

sections.heading: Starting, whichever cliff you are standing on
paragraphs: Send the level - Higher or Standard - the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked assessment, or the current investigation draft if that is the live deadline. If you know which unit the class is about to start, say so: a request that arrives six weeks before organic chemistry gets a different and cheaper plan than one that arrives six weeks after.

The first session is diagnostic. The tutor reads the script against the mark scheme and tells you plainly which of three positions you are in: convention errors recoverable in weeks, genuine content gaps needing a term, or both with a deadline too close to serve either properly. The third answer determines what gets sacrificed, and it is better heard in the first session than in April.

Matching takes about a day for Standard Level chemistry. Higher Level in the second Diploma year can take two or three days, because the pool is narrow and a general science tutor in front of a Higher Level organic paper is worse than a short delay. We tell you the expected wait at the enquiry.

When no suitable chemistry specialist has a slot at the hour you need, we say so and offer the real alternatives: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot frees up, or an honest recommendation to hire locally with the permit question in hand. No competitor in this market publishes its unavailable case, which is why it is written here rather than left to a delayed reply.

process.title: Tell us the level and the next unit
process.description: Higher or Standard, and what the class is about to start. Work timed to arrive before energetics or organic chemistry is preparation; the same work after the unit is repair, and repair competes with the investigation for the same weeks.

process.title: Send a marked script or the investigation draft
process.description: A photograph is enough. Chemistry is diagnosable from a script: sign conventions, mole set-up order, arrow origins and explanation depth all show within two or three questions, and they are different problems with different timescales.

process.title: Chemistry specialist matched at that level
process.description: Never a general science tutor. Standard Level usually matches within a day; Higher Level in the second Diploma year can take two or three, and we tell you which case applies before you start waiting for someone.

process.title: Free diagnostic trial lesson online
process.description: A real one-to-one lesson with the matched specialist on the document you sent, ending in a written note of what it showed and what the first month should target. No card details and no package to commit to beforehand.

process.title: Weekly slot, re-cut at each edge
process.description: The same tutor at the same Gulf Standard Time hour, with the plan rewritten at the investigation deadline, after the mocks and again eight weeks out. Slots shift for Ramadan and exam weeks as a calendar change.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the two cliffs
whyPoints.description: Energetics in the first year and organic mechanisms in the second decide most chemistry grades, and both arrive on a schedule the school publishes. Preparation before a unit costs less and achieves more than repair after it.

whyPoints.title: Conventions drilled, not discussed
whyPoints.description: Enthalpy signs, mole set-up order, arrow origins, reagent and conditions: these are mechanical rules that respond to enforcement. Most chemistry marks a Jebel Ali student loses are convention marks rather than knowledge marks.

whyPoints.title: Feasibility checked before the investigation starts
whyPoints.description: Chemistry investigations fail on apparatus and reagents the school does not hold, discovered in week six. A thirty-minute feasibility conversation in week one prevents the rushed substitute that costs the evaluation criterion.

whyPoints.title: Honesty about data taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Unexpected results are material for the evaluation criterion, not a problem to be tidied. We say that in the first investigation session, because deadline pressure is when the temptation appears.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names its publisher and the month we read it. Three of the pages ranking for this search publish no price, and two quote US dollars to families paying in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: The earliest usable hour
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from about 4pm Gulf Standard Time because nobody is driving to Jebel Ali or Emaar South. Mechanism drawing is precision work, and precision work at 6.30pm after a cross-city drive is not where marks come from.

faqs.question: When does Diploma chemistry get hard for students in this catchment?
faqs.answer: At two predictable points. The first is early in the course, when bonding and energetics turn quantitative and sign conventions and mole set-up order start deciding marks. The second is in the second year, when organic chemistry arrives and the subject becomes mechanism drawing with conventions that must be exact. Both are scheduled rather than random, which means both can be worked before they arrive. The school's scheme of work tells you when, and that is the single most useful document a chemistry parent can ask for.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose mechanism marks when the product is correct?
faqs.answer: Because the mark is for the movement of electrons rather than for the product. A curly arrow must start at a lone pair or at a bond, not at an atom label and not from thin air, and an arrow drawn from the wrong place loses the mark even beside a correct product. Students who were never told this explicitly draw plausible arrows for a year without understanding why mechanism questions score low. Checking arrow origins on every mechanism drawn, every session, fixes it within weeks.

faqs.question: My child finds organic chemistry very difficult. Is that fixable before the papers?
faqs.answer: It is one of the more fixable parts of the course, because so much of it is convention rather than insight. The drill is repetitive: state the reaction type, name the reagent precisely, give the conditions, draw the mechanism, then check every arrow origin and every intermediate. Done weekly, organic chemistry moves from being the most feared part of the paper to one of the more reliable, because the marks are allocated to things that can be made automatic. Starting before the unit is taught is better still.

faqs.question: What does a chemistry tutor do about the laboratory work?
faqs.answer: Nothing, by design. Under IB rules the practical work happens at school with the school's apparatus, risk assessment and supervision. What a tutor contributes sits either side of it: checking the research question is feasible with what the laboratory actually holds, teaching the chemistry the investigation needs, deriving uncertainty from glassware tolerance and balance resolution rather than guessing it, and testing whether the conclusion follows from the data collected. All of that is document and drawing work, which is why it transfers to video well.

faqs.question: Why do chemistry investigations go wrong in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Feasibility, more often than anything else. The research question needs a reagent, a concentration or an instrument resolution the school laboratory does not hold, and this is discovered during the practical session rather than during the design. The student then substitutes a rushed question with little room for real evaluation, and the evaluation criterion is where the marks were. A thirty-minute conversation with the teacher about available apparatus, in week one, prevents the whole sequence.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the chemistry IA without breaching IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor can narrow the research question, check feasibility against the school's apparatus, teach the chemistry involved, explain each criterion and its mark ceiling, check whether uncertainties were derived or invented, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, check referencing, and mark the draft against the descriptors. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce or adjust data. Every sentence must be typed by your child, and no result should ever be tidied.

faqs.question: Does the enthalpy sign really cost whole questions?
faqs.answer: It does, and it is one of the cruellest losses in the subject, because every arithmetic step can be correct. An enthalpy change carries a sign that encodes direction, so an exothermic value written positive invalidates a cycle that is otherwise flawless, and the student sees no error to find. The fix is mechanical: write the sign before the magnitude, every time, even when it feels obvious. Four sessions of that enforcement typically removes the problem permanently, and it is the cheapest chemistry mark available.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the last eight weeks before the chemistry papers?
faqs.answer: Timed papers and mechanism drills, with no new content. Full papers under real conditions, including the data-based sections, marked by someone who is not the student against the official scheme. Separately, mechanism and half-equation drills, because both are procedural and therefore the fastest marks available late. Introducing new chemistry in this window displaces the practice that converts existing knowledge into marks, which is why a late content push so often leaves the result unchanged.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level chemistry worth it if my child wants medicine?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements differ by university and by country, and the only reliable method is to read the requirements for two or three specific programmes directly rather than relying on a general rule. Separately, school-leaving certificates generally need Ministry of Education equivalency before a UAE university application, and no IB points threshold appears in the source we have read, so verify that on moe.gov.ae rather than trusting a figure quoted on a tutoring page. We make no claim about admission outcomes and tutoring is not a requirement for any of it.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a Higher Level chemistry tutor near Green Community?
faqs.answer: Standard Level chemistry usually matches within a day. Higher Level in the second Diploma year takes two or three, because the specialist pool is genuinely narrow and putting a general science tutor in front of Higher Level organic work is worse than a short wait. We state the expected wait at the enquiry rather than afterwards. A radius search from Green Community, Dubai South or Emaar South for the same specialism commonly returns general science tutors only, which is the supply problem online delivery solves.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take chemistry and biology for the same Diploma student?
faqs.answer: We would usually say no, and the reason is specific. Chemistry at Higher Level turns on mechanism conventions and quantitative set-up; biology turns on command-term discipline and the structure of extended answers. They are taught by different specialists in most schools for good reason, and the match we make is for component-level knowledge of one mark scheme. Chemistry and physics share more ground through the mathematics. Tell us both subjects and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits or two is better.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB chemistry exam dates on this page?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one almost all UAE schools enter candidates for and goes no further. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we cite those where relevant. The dates that drive your term plan are internal anyway - the investigation deadline, the Extended Essay deadline, the mock window - and your school's Diploma coordinator holds all three.

faqs.question: How should chemistry sessions change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Keep the frequency and shorten the session. What decays fastest in chemistry when sessions stop is quantitative fluency: mole set-up, unit conversion, rearranging relationships. Two shorter sessions a week hold that better than one long one while a student is fasting, and a complete pause usually means relearning in the first week back. The hour itself typically moves to early afternoon or post-iftar. Because nobody is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of a commute.

faqs.question: What does the free chemistry trial lesson produce?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis that is yours whether or not you continue. The matched specialist, not a salesperson, teaches a real one-to-one lesson online on the marked script or investigation draft you sent, and finishes by writing down what the document showed: whether the losses are sign conventions, mole set-up order, arrow origins, explanation depth, or genuinely unfinished content, and what the first month should target. No card details are required to book it and there is no package to agree beforehand.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jlt.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Chemistry to JLT families over live video. Ask each of them two pricing questions before anything else: what an hour includes beyond the hour, and whether marking between sessions is inside the rate or billed separately. The answers vary more than the headline rates do.

intro.heading: Why two chemistry tutors at the same hourly rate are not the same purchase
paragraphs: A family in Jumeirah Lakes Towers comparing chemistry tutors is usually comparing two numbers on two websites, and the numbers are not describing the same product. One AED 200 hour is a tutor reteaching last week's lesson from a textbook. Another AED 200 hour is a specialist reading your child's marked Paper 2, naming the three command terms that cost the marks, and rebuilding one organic mechanism until the student can draw the curly arrows without prompting. Those are different purchases at an identical price, and nothing on either website tells you which you are buying.

That matters more in chemistry than in most subjects, because chemistry marks are lost in a small number of very specific places. Organic mechanisms. Equilibrium reasoning that has to be argued rather than calculated. Energetics sign conventions. Data-based questions where an unfamiliar table has to be interpreted rather than recalled. Bonding explanations that describe a model without saying which model is being used and why. A tutor who covers the syllabus broadly will spend your money on the ninety per cent of the course your child can already do.

The second reason to start from cost is that this search cluster refuses to. Of the Dubai tutoring pages reviewed in October 2026, three published no hourly figure at all, two quoted in US dollars, and one of them contradicted its own prices between two sections of the same page. The best-ranking page in the set asks the price question in its own FAQ list and then declines to answer it. So the figures on this page are published competitor rates with the provider named and the month they were read, which is information you can check rather than a rate card you have to trust.

Being honest about our own side of it: IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, because the rate depends on level and on what the brief actually needs, and a single number would mislead you. What we do publish is the market, the comparison, and the free trial lesson that lets you judge an hour before paying for one. We also do not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE. Visiting tuition is a service we run only in India, and the in-home dirham figures quoted further down are other providers' rates, included because the comparison is the argument.

The rest of the page follows the money. What an hour contains at each published band. Where the chemistry course actually eats hours. The five ways a JLT budget leaks. A term-by-term map of a two-year Diploma spend. The formats compared for a tower address. The extras nobody lists until the invoice. And the two rules, one about permits and one about academic honesty, that quietly change what you should be willing to pay for.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: What a chemistry hour should cost depends partly on which programme your child is in, because the work is different. A Middle Years student needs criterion-aware science support; a Diploma student in the final year needs component-level examination work, which is the most expensive thing on the market and the most worth paying for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences are assessed against four criteria each marked out of eight, covering knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Chemistry usually sits inside an integrated sciences course rather than standing alone, so the quantity of formal chemical calculation a student has met by MYP 5 varies a great deal between schools.
programmes.countryNote: For a JLT family the cost question at this stage is whether to spend at all. Middle Years science support is cheaper per hour than Diploma work and is often better value, because fixing mole calculations and bonding language at fourteen removes the expensive remedial work at seventeen. A short block before the Diploma choice is made costs less than a year of catching up afterwards.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry sits in Group 4 at Standard or Higher Level. The current guide organises content around structure and reactivity rather than around traditional topic headings, assessed through a multiple-choice paper, a data-based paper, an extended-response paper and an internally assessed scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma chemistry is the most expensive tutoring any JLT family buys, and the spending should be unevenly distributed across the two years rather than spread as a flat weekly cost. The expensive terms are the one containing the investigation and the one before the examinations. The cheap terms are the two in between, where a short monthly review is usually enough.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a core of personal and professional skills. Where chemistry is taken inside it, the course content and the assessment are the same as for a Diploma candidate, including the scientific investigation and the three written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run this route. If your child is on it, budget for chemistry as though it were a Diploma subject, because it is, but expect the surrounding timetable to give fewer deadline reminders. The investigation is the item that slips, and a slipped investigation is the most expensive thing to rescue late.

programmes.name: The route in from IGCSE
programmes.description: British-curriculum schools around JLT run Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1, or chemistry inside a co-ordinated or double award. Each ends in terminal written papers, with an alternative-to-practical component in the Cambridge route, and covers moles, bonding and basic organic chemistry at a descriptive level.
programmes.countryNote: The step from IGCSE to Diploma chemistry is the cheapest problem to fix and the one families most often pay to fix late. IGCSE treats bonding and energetics descriptively; the Diploma asks which model is being applied and why. A six-session bridging block in the summer before Year 12 costs a fraction of a remedial year and is the single best-value chemistry spend available to a JLT family.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: Chemistry hours are not evenly valuable. The list below names the parts of the course where paid time pays back, with the places marks leave the page, so you can direct the spending at a component instead of buying general chemistry help by the hour.

subjects.name: Structure 1: particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: The mole concept, formulae, empirical and molecular determination, solution concentration and the ideal gas relationship. Cheap to fix and expensive to leave: almost every later calculation in the course runs through a mole step, so a student shaky here loses marks in topics they otherwise understand. Two or three focused hours usually settles it.

subjects.name: Structure 2: models of bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, Lewis formulae, shapes and polarity, and at Higher Level formal charge and molecular orbital ideas. Marks go on explanations that describe a property without naming the bonding model used. This is argument practice rather than content revision, which means it needs a tutor rather than a textbook.

subjects.name: Structure 3: classification of matter
subjects.description: Periodicity, trends down groups and across periods, and an introduction to the functional groups and homologous series that organic chemistry then builds on. Students lose marks by stating a trend without a reason, and by explaining periodicity through one factor when the mark scheme requires two competing ones.

subjects.name: Reactivity 1: what drives reactions
subjects.description: Energetics and thermochemistry: enthalpy changes, calorimetry, bond enthalpies, Hess cycles and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs energy. The reliable loss is sign convention, closely followed by Hess cycle arithmetic where one arrow is reversed and not negated. Highly trainable, and worth paying for before the first mock rather than after it.

subjects.name: Reactivity 2: how much, how fast, how far
subjects.description: Reaction rates, equilibrium, acids and bases, buffers at Higher Level, and the quantitative treatment of each. Equilibrium questions are argued rather than calculated, which is where strong mathematical students drop marks. The command term decides the answer shape, and students who write the correct chemistry under the wrong command term score poorly.

subjects.name: Reactivity 3: mechanisms of chemical change
subjects.description: Oxidation and reduction, electrochemistry, and organic reaction mechanisms with the full curly-arrow treatment at Higher Level. This is the most expensive part of the course in tutoring hours and the part most worth buying, because mechanisms cannot be memorised usefully and have to be drawn repeatedly with feedback on each attempt.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: multiple choice
subjects.description: Whole-syllabus multiple choice with no credit for working, sat with a data booklet and no calculator in some configurations. It rewards pace, elimination and confident unit reasoning. Students who have only practised long-form questions run out of time, and the fix is timed sets rather than more content, which makes it one of the cheapest components to improve.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data-based questions
subjects.description: Questions built on unfamiliar data and experimental contexts, drawing on the skills tools rather than on recall. It asks the student to read a method, judge it, process data and comment on a graph. It cannot be revised from a textbook, which is precisely why it is worth paid hours: the skill only develops against feedback.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: Short and long written questions mixing calculation with explanation. Command terms carry the marks, and Higher Level questions chain more steps than Standard Level ones. The most common expensive mistake is buying content revision when the marks are being lost to answer shape, which is a different and much shorter piece of work.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation marked against four criteria out of twenty-four marks and carrying a fifth of the subject grade. It is the single largest block of tutoring hours most chemistry students need, and the cost rises steeply the later it starts, because a question that cannot produce a trend has to be rebuilt from the beginning.

subjects.name: Practical and data skills
subjects.description: Experimental technique, spreadsheet and graphing work, and the mathematics the course assumes, all examined inside Paper 1B and assessed inside the investigation. Because they are never a separate revision topic, they are the thing students skip, and deliberate practice on them returns more marks per paid hour than any content topic.

All three run online over live video with a shared whiteboard, and the differences between them are about what the hour contains rather than about where anybody sits.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, the standing cost
modes.description: A fixed weekly slot running alongside the school's scheme of work, used for the week's marked problems and the topic the class is currently in. This is the predictable line in a household budget and the one families over-buy, because the middle terms of the Diploma rarely need a full weekly hour of chemistry.

modes.title: Mechanism and component blocks
modes.description: A short run of sessions aimed at one thing: organic mechanisms, equilibrium argument, energetics sign conventions, or Paper 1B data skills. sections.heading: What an hour of IB Chemistry actually contains at each published band
paragraphs: Lead with the monthly number rather than the hourly one, because that is the figure a household budget is built on. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates, for a single weekly hour, run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Packages seen in the market sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the numbers to compare.

Convert them back to hours and the published spread becomes visible. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour; Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's premium named tutors at AED 650. In-home one-to-one is published at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by home tutors generally, with travel inside the rate.

The useful question is not which band is cheapest but what each one contains. At the bottom, the hour is usually a general tutor working through the textbook chapter the class has just covered, which is reteaching rather than diagnosis. In the middle band the tutor knows the syllabus and can name the components. At the top, you are paying for component-level work and for someone who will read a marked script before the session. The step that matters for chemistry is the one into the middle band, because mechanism feedback requires subject knowledge the budget band does not reliably have.

Ask three questions of any quote, whatever the number attached to it. Is marking between sessions inside the rate or billed separately? Is the rate per sixty minutes or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? And what happens to the fee if you stop after one session? The answers move the real cost more than the headline rate does, and the providers who answer them crisply are usually the ones worth hiring.

sections.heading: Where chemistry hours pay back, component by component
paragraphs: Spending evenly across a syllabus is the most common way to waste money on chemistry. The course does not lose marks evenly. A student can be secure across most of structure and reactivity and give away a grade in two identifiable places, and those two places are where paid hours belong. The rest the school teaches well enough, and paying to hear it again is paying for reassurance.

The highest return per hour is organic mechanisms. They cannot be memorised in any useful way, because the examination asks the student to apply the pattern to a molecule they have not seen. The only training that works is drawing them repeatedly with someone correcting the arrows, the charges and the intermediates on each attempt. That is a feedback loop, and feedback loops are the one thing a textbook, a video and a group class all fail to provide.

The second highest is Paper 1B data work, for the same reason in a different disguise. The paper presents an unfamiliar method and asks the student to judge it, process the numbers and comment on the pattern. There is nothing to revise. The skill grows only against worked feedback, and it is examined in both papers and assessed inside the investigation, so improvement there pays three times.

The lowest return per paid hour is content recall. Periodicity trends, functional group names, the list of intermolecular forces: all of it is in the student's notes and all of it can be drilled alone with a reliable self-test routine. If a tutor is spending your hour on recall, you are paying specialist rates for something a flashcard app does better. sections.heading: Five ways a JLT chemistry budget leaks
paragraphs: The first leak is buying the subject instead of the component. A parent books chemistry help because the grade dropped, the tutor starts at the beginning of the syllabus, and six weeks go by before anyone looks at the marked script that would have identified the problem in twenty minutes. The fix costs nothing: send the last two marked assessments before the first session and insist the trial lesson starts there.

The second is paying for a group class in a subject that needs individual correction. Group tuition is genuinely cheaper per student and genuinely works for content delivery. It does not work for mechanisms, because eight students drawing eight different wrong arrows cannot each be corrected inside an hour. Families who buy a group chemistry class for mechanism work usually buy private hours afterwards as well, which is the expensive route to the same place.

The third is the investigation bought late. A research question that cannot produce a trend has to be rebuilt, and a rebuild four weeks from the deadline costs several times what a single viability hour would have cost at the start. This is the leak that most often doubles a chemistry budget, and it is entirely avoidable with one session booked before any apparatus is touched.

The fourth is the travel premium paid without measuring what it bought. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. From a tower address that premium buys a journey through two arterial roads and a visitor parking process, and it narrows the available pool to whoever can complete that journey by seven. The fifth leak is the quietest: paying a weekly standing rate through the two middle terms of the Diploma, when a monthly review would hold the ground just as well and the money would be better saved for the examination term.

sections.heading: Two years of Diploma chemistry with the spending mapped out
paragraphs: Chemistry spending should be lumpy, and most families make it flat. A flat weekly rate across two years feels disciplined and is usually the wrong shape, because the course has two expensive terms and several cheap ones. Mapping the spend against the terms lets you buy more in the terms that matter without raising the total.

The first term of Year 12 is a bridging term. Students arriving from IGCSE meet a course that asks which bonding model applies and why, where IGCSE asked them to describe a property. A short block here is cheap and prevents the most expensive pattern in the subject, which is a student who understands each lesson and cannot assemble an argument from it. The second term is usually quiet, and a fortnightly review is enough.

The investigation term is the first peak. Budget for a viability hour, two or three processing and analysis sessions, and criterion feedback on drafts. The term after it is the second quiet period and the one families most often overspend in, because the habit of a weekly session has been established and nobody questions it. This is the term to drop to monthly and bank the difference.

The final two terms are the second peak and the one worth funding properly. Past papers under timed conditions, mark-scheme-by-mark-scheme review, mechanism blocks, and Paper 1B sets. Study leave shortens the school day and opens the mornings, which is the only period of the two years when the best hours are available, and buying more sessions then returns more per dirham than buying them in any other term.
