sections.heading: Group class, centre, visiting tutor or online one-to-one, priced for a tower
paragraphs: The format decision is a cost decision and it is usually made on convenience instead. Four options are realistically available to a JLT family, and each buys something different for a different number. Setting them side by side with the published rates attached makes the comparison honest, which is more than most pages in this search result do.

A tuition centre group class is the cheapest per student and the easiest to schedule because it runs on a fixed timetable. For chemistry content delivery it is reasonable value. For mechanisms, equilibrium argument and Paper 1B skills it is not, because none of those can be corrected individually inside a group hour. The hidden cost is the journey to the centre, which from JLT means an evening car trip in both directions.

A visiting private tutor is the most expensive per hour at the published AED 180 to 500 range, and the premium is travel rather than teaching. It also imposes the hardest constraint on your choice of tutor, because the pool shrinks to those who can reach a tower by a workable time. In Higher Level chemistry that pool is small at any price. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so this row of the comparison describes the market rather than something we sell.

Online one-to-one is priced in the middle of the published range, carries no travel in either direction, and leaves the choice of tutor open. For chemistry specifically it has a technical advantage that is easy to miss: mechanism work, spreadsheet analysis and graph interpretation all happen on a screen anyway, so a shared annotated whiteboard is not a substitute for the real thing but the natural medium for it. The fourth option, a recorded course or video library, is cheapest of all and provides no feedback loop, which is the one thing chemistry marks actually require.

sections.heading: The extras that move the real cost after you have agreed a rate
paragraphs: An agreed hourly rate is not the price. Several things attach to it, and in the Dubai market they are disclosed inconsistently, which is why two tutors at AED 220 can produce invoices that differ by a third. Ask about each of the following before the first paid session rather than after the first invoice.

Marking between sessions is the biggest variable. A tutor who marks a timed paper section between lessons, writes a short diagnostic note and arrives with a plan is doing substantial unpaid or separately charged work. Some rates include it, some bill it, some simply do not offer it. For chemistry it matters: Paper 1B improvement depends on written feedback on attempts the student made alone, which has to be marked by someone.

Then the mechanical questions. Is the rate per sixty minutes or per lesson, and is a lesson fifty minutes? Is a cancellation inside twenty-four hours charged? Is the first session discounted or free, and if free, what condition is attached to it? Are session notes and annotated solutions provided afterwards, or does the whiteboard disappear when the call ends? Is there a charge for switching tutors if the first match is wrong?

A last one specific to this subject. Do not pay for past papers, mark schemes, subject guides or grade-boundary tables. Those are the examination boards' copyright material and nobody should be selling them to you. A tutor should reference them, cite the official source and link to it, which costs nothing. Our own position is the same: we point to the boards' own pages rather than supplying their documents, and we do not charge for materials we have no right to distribute.

sections.heading: Two rules that change what you should be willing to pay for
paragraphs: The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The application route is MoHRE's own Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time.

That has a direct price consequence. An informal arrangement at AED 80 an hour arranged through a building group chat is only cheap if the person holds the permit, because individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any page quoting you a figure as quoting something unverified. Ask the question, and ask it before money changes hands rather than after.

There is a second rule in the same area. A teacher at your child's own school tutoring your own child is the arrangement families ask for most and the one that carries the most exposure. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Check the current policy document before relying on it, but do not build a plan around that arrangement.

The second rule is about what the money may legitimately buy. A tutor may teach the investigation criteria, discuss whether a research question is viable, explain uncertainty handling and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor must never write the investigation, supply data or rewrite a paragraph into final form. One page in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student. If a quote includes producing assessed work, the price is irrelevant because the product is unusable.

sections.heading: What to send, and what the free trial should prove before you pay
paragraphs: Start by making the brief specific enough to price. Send the level, Standard or Higher, the school and year group, the topics covered so far, and the component where marks are going. Add photographs of the last two marked assessments with annotations visible. A tutor who has read marked work before the trial can say in the first ten minutes whether the problem is content, answer shape or method, and that is the information you are actually shopping for.

The trial lesson then has a job, and it is not rapport. Watch whether the tutor works from your child's own lost marks or from a generic worksheet. Watch whether your child talks. Ask the tutor to name, out loud, the component they would work on first and why. A tutor who cannot name it after reading a marked script is not the specialist the top band is charging for. The trial is free, runs in full, and takes no payment and no card details.

Then agree the shape rather than an open-ended booking. A named weakness, a block length, and what happens between sessions. Blocks make the total knowable in advance, which is the single most effective budget control available to a tutoring family, and they end naturally when the error pattern changes rather than continuing because the slot exists.

If no specialist is free in your window, we say so and offer an alternative time or a date rather than substituting a general science tutor into a chemistry brief. Higher Level chemistry in an early-evening Gulf Standard Time slot is one of our most contested combinations. Disclosing that is worth more to you than concealing it, because a mismatched hour at any rate is the most expensive hour on this page.

process.title: Write a brief specific enough to price
process.description: Level, school, year group, topics covered and the component where the marks are going. Two or three lines is enough. A vague brief gets a vague quote and a generalist, and the generalist costs the same per hour as the specialist while moving less, which is the most expensive outcome available.

process.title: Send marked work before the first session
process.description: The last two marked assessments and the most recent mock, annotations visible. Phone photographs are fine. This converts the trial from an introduction into a diagnosis, and it is the single cheapest thing you can do to improve the value of everything you buy afterwards.

process.title: Ask the three pricing questions
process.description: Is marking between sessions inside the rate? Is the rate per sixty minutes or per lesson? What happens if you stop after one session? These three answers move the real cost more than the headline rate does, and a provider who answers them crisply is usually worth hiring.

process.title: Use the free trial as an audition
process.description: A full lesson online with no payment and no card details. Judge two things: whether the tutor starts from your child's own errors, and whether your child speaks during the hour. Ask the tutor to name the first component they would target. Both signals are visible inside twenty minutes.

process.title: Buy a block, not an open booking
process.description: Agree a named weakness and a number of sessions, so the total is knowable before you commit. Blocks end when the error pattern changes rather than running until someone cancels, which is what keeps a chemistry budget from drifting through the quiet middle terms of the Diploma.

process.title: Review the spend every six weeks
process.description: Check whether the named losses have stopped appearing in marked work. If they have, move the focus or pause. If six weeks have produced no change in the pattern, change the approach or the tutor rather than renewing by default. This review is where most of the saving actually happens.

whyPoints.title: Attributed figures, not a rate card you must trust
whyPoints.description: Every dirham range on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. We publish the market rather than inventing a benchmark, because three of the pages competing for this search publish no price at all and a number you cannot check is worth nothing to a family making a decision.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Lessons run online over live video, so nothing in what you pay is a journey. Published in-home rates in Dubai carry travel inside the figure, which is why they sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour. Removing that also removes the constraint that the tutor must live near enough to reach a JLT tower.

whyPoints.title: Component-level matching
whyPoints.description: Chemistry marks are lost in specific places: mechanisms, equilibrium argument, data questions, sign conventions. We match a tutor who has taught the component rather than the subject, because paying specialist rates for general chemistry revision is the most common way money leaves a tutoring budget without a grade moving.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Where the brief is a named weakness, we price it as a block of sessions with an end point tied to the error pattern rather than an open weekly commitment. That makes the total knowable before you start and stops the quiet middle terms of the Diploma absorbing money that the examination term needs.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty limits
whyPoints.description: Investigation support means teaching the criteria, checking viability and giving written feedback on your child's own drafts. It never means writing it, supplying data or rewriting a paragraph into final form. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that product is unusable at any price and we will not supply it.

whyPoints.title: An honest no when the slot is full
whyPoints.description: Higher Level chemistry in an early-evening Gulf Standard Time window is one of our most contested combinations. When it is full we say so and offer an alternative time rather than putting a generalist into the brief, because a mismatched hour is the most expensive purchase in this whole market.

faqs.question: What does an IB Chemistry tutor cost per hour for a family in JLT?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026 span a wide range. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work at AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED's premium named tutors at AED 650. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Those are other providers' published numbers, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying for chemistry by the hour?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the package matches the term you are in. Market packages sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end up to AED 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. A package is good value in the investigation term and the final term, and poor value in the two quiet middle terms when a fortnightly review would hold the ground for a fraction of the cost.

faqs.question: Which part of IB Chemistry is worth paying a specialist rate for?
faqs.answer: Organic mechanisms first, then Paper 1B data-based questions. Both share a feature that justifies the cost: they cannot be improved by reading. Mechanisms have to be drawn repeatedly against someone correcting the arrows, charges and intermediates on each attempt, and data questions use unfamiliar methods the student must learn to judge. Both need a feedback loop, and a feedback loop is the one thing a textbook, a video library and a group class all fail to provide. Content recall sits at the other end: that is in your child's notes already and should not consume paid hours.

faqs.question: Is a group chemistry class at a Dubai centre cheaper in practice?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, yes, and reasonable value for content delivery and pace. It does not work for the parts of chemistry that cost marks. Eight students drawing eight different wrong mechanisms cannot each be corrected inside an hour, and equilibrium argument needs the tutor to read one student's sentence and rewrite it with them. Families who buy group classes for mechanism work usually buy private hours afterwards as well, which is the expensive route to the same destination. Add the JLT car journey in both directions when comparing the real cost.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way chemistry tutoring money gets wasted?
faqs.answer: Buying the subject instead of the component. A grade drops, a tutor is booked, the tutor starts at the beginning of the syllabus, and six weeks pass before anyone reads the marked script that would have identified the problem in twenty minutes. The remedy costs nothing: send the last two marked assessments before the first session and insist the trial lesson starts from them. The second most common is starting the scientific investigation late, which turns a few hours of supervision into a rebuild.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium buy anything extra for a tower address?
faqs.answer: It buys a journey. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and for a JLT tower that journey means two arterial roads in the afternoon direction plus a visitor parking process. The teaching hour is the same hour. The real cost is not the money but the narrowing of choice: only tutors who can complete that journey by a workable evening time are available to you, and in Higher Level chemistry that is a short list. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: Should we pay for chemistry support in the quiet middle terms of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually less than families do. The two terms between the bridging period and the investigation are the ones where a weekly slot continues out of habit rather than need. Dropping to a fortnightly review in those terms holds the ground just as well for most students and banks the difference for the final term, where timed papers and mark-scheme review return more per dirham than any other period. The exception is a student with an unresolved structural weakness, such as mole calculations, which should be fixed immediately whatever term it is.

faqs.question: How much tutoring does the chemistry scientific investigation actually need?
faqs.answer: Bought early, a handful of hours: one session testing whether the research question can produce a trend, two or three on data processing and graphing, and written feedback on drafts against the four criteria. Bought late it becomes a rebuild, because a question whose independent variable cannot be varied usefully has to be replaced and the data recollected. That is the point at which chemistry budgets most often double. The investigation carries a fifth of the subject grade, so the early hour is the highest-value booking in the course.

faqs.question: What extras should I ask about before agreeing a chemistry tutor's rate?
faqs.answer: Five things. Whether marking between sessions is inside the rate or billed separately, since Paper 1B progress depends on written feedback on work the student did alone. Whether the rate is per sixty minutes or per lesson, and how long a lesson is. Whether a late cancellation is charged. Whether annotated solutions and session notes are provided afterwards. And whether switching tutors costs anything if the first match is wrong. Those answers move the real total more than the headline hourly figure does.

faqs.question: Do chemistry tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does that affect the price?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published. So an informal arrangement at AED 80 an hour through a building chat group is only genuinely cheap if the permit exists.

faqs.question: Can I buy only mechanism help rather than a whole chemistry course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the better purchase. A block of six to ten sessions on organic mechanisms alone, with timed question sets attempted between lessons and every arrow corrected during them, costs a knowable total and ends when the error pattern changes. Buying a block rather than an open weekly booking is the most effective budget control available to a tutoring family, because the end point is defined before you start rather than decided by whoever remembers to cancel first.

faqs.question: Will paying more get my child a higher chemistry grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and any provider promising a grade for a price should be treated with real scepticism. What the higher bands buy is subject depth: a tutor who can name the component where marks are going after reading one marked script, and who has taught Higher Level mechanisms to examination. That is worth paying for. What the top band does not buy is certainty, and claims about guaranteed improvement are a warning sign rather than a selling point. Judge the hour in the free trial instead of judging the number on the website.

faqs.question: Do you charge for past papers, mark schemes or the subject guide?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. Past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables are the examination boards' copyright material, and supplying them is not something a tutoring service has the right to sell. A tutor should reference them, cite the official source and link to it. We point families to the boards' own published pages instead, which costs nothing and keeps you on the version that is current rather than a copy of uncertain date.

faqs.question: Is the free chemistry trial really free, and what condition is attached to it?
faqs.answer: It is a full lesson, online, with no payment taken and no card details required, and the condition is simply one trial per student so the slot can be offered to the next family. Use it as an audition rather than a meeting. Ask the tutor to name the component they would target first and why, watch whether they work from your child's marked script or from a generic worksheet, and watch whether your child talks during the hour. A silent trial is a signal worth acting on straight away.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest high-value chemistry spend for a JLT family?
faqs.answer: A short bridging block in the summer before Year 12, for a student moving from IGCSE chemistry into the Diploma. IGCSE asks students to describe properties; the Diploma asks which bonding or energetic model applies and why. Six sessions covering that shift, plus a check on mole and solution method, costs a fraction of the remedial work families buy in October when the first marked assessment comes back. It is the clearest case in this subject of early money being worth several times late money.

faqs.question: What happens if no chemistry specialist is free at the time we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you and offer either an alternative time or a date when the slot opens. Higher Level chemistry in an early-evening Gulf Standard Time window is one of the most contested combinations we handle. We will not substitute a general science tutor into a Higher Level chemistry brief, because a mismatched specialist costs a term of a two-year programme and that term cannot be bought back at any rate. If the wait is long, we say how long rather than leaving the enquiry open.

intro.heading: A Diploma Chemistry student is running three clocks, and only one of them is the exam
paragraphs: Families in Jumeirah 1 usually look for chemistry help after a single trigger: a DP1 report, a DP2 mock, or a sentence from a school coordinator about the investigation. The useful first question is not what topic is hard. It is which deadline is closest, because a Diploma Chemistry student is simultaneously bound by three different calendars, each set by a different party, and the one that is closest decides what the next six sessions do.

The first clock belongs to the school. Internal deadlines for the scientific investigation, the first draft, the final submission, mock weeks, and the point at which predicted grades are agreed are all set by the school's own Diploma coordinator, published in a handbook, and often earlier than parents expect. The investigation is worth 20 per cent of the grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria, so a school deadline in the spring of DP1 is not a soft date to be negotiated.

The second clock is the examination session. UAE schools sit the May session, and the written assessment is Paper 1 - a multiple-choice section and a data-based section together worth 36 per cent - plus Paper 2 at 44 per cent. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and a wrong date on a revision plan is worse than no date. Every IB date on a plan should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the official timetable.

The third clock is the university cycle, and it runs earliest of the three. Applications to UK, US and many Gulf universities are submitted in the autumn of DP2 on the basis of a predicted grade, which is produced from DP1 results and the autumn mock. That means the chemistry grade that gets a student an offer is largely decided a full academic year before the paper is sat. A family that understands this plans chemistry support in DP1 rather than in February of DP2.

Jumeirah 1 students mostly commute to their Diploma school. Jumeirah Baccalaureate School is inside the district; the rest of this page's chemistry cohort travels to Raffles World Academy or Emirates International School in the Umm Suqeim cluster, or inland to Dubai International Academy and Dubai American Academy. Buses get home between 15:45 and 16:45, so a 17:00 session works on a good day and 18:30 works every day. Over a two-year course, the slot that holds is worth more than the slot that is ideal.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 1 address, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. For chemistry the trade is favourable: mechanisms are drawn and redrawn on a shared whiteboard while the question stays visible, the data booklet sits open beside them, and the session can be rewatched the night before a mock. What is removed is the drive and the requirement that the right chemist happens to live nearby.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: Chemistry reaches a Jumeirah 1 student through one of a few routes, and the route determines which deadline bites first. The five stages below are set out with what Dubai schools actually do about timing, which is the part a revision plan has to respect.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, with chemistry inside it
programmes.description: Chemistry taught as part of integrated sciences and assessed against four MYP criteria rather than a content list. Students become competent at designing investigations and processing data, which transfers directly into the Diploma's scientific investigation. The gap is content: a strong MYP student may arrive in DP1 without having met the mole as a working tool, which is the single most consequential absence in the subject.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB continuum schools, including Jumeirah Baccalaureate School and Raffles World Academy, run MYP straight into the Diploma, and the October of DP1 is when the mole gap becomes visible. Families here often read it as a sudden collapse in ability. It is a predictable curriculum seam, and six weeks of concentrated work on moles, concentration and limiting reagents usually closes it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry 0620 or 4CH1 before the Diploma
programmes.description: The British-school route. More content taught than MYP, with a practical component and reasonable mole arithmetic, but almost no work on uncertainty and none on the kind of extended reasoning Paper 2 wants. Students from here are strong on recall and weak on justification: they can state Le Chatelier's principle and lose the marks for applying it to an unfamiliar equilibrium.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah College, Dubai College and the British schools in the Al Safa and Al Sufouh cluster run IGCSE into A Level rather than into the Diploma, so a Jumeirah 1 student moving onto the Diploma route has normally changed school too. New teacher, new scheme of work and a new assessment model in one September, with the investigation arriving before anyone has settled.

programmes.name: Diploma Chemistry Standard Level
programmes.description: Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3 at Standard Level, with Paper 1 of ninety minutes, Paper 2 of ninety minutes and the 24-mark scientific investigation. The data booklet is provided in both papers, which changes what has to be memorised and what has to be found quickly. Standard Level penalises imprecision heavily: an answer that describes a trend without naming the cause earns nothing.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level Chemistry is the usual Dubai choice for a student whose Higher Levels are elsewhere but who needs a science for a UAE or international application. The decision to stay at Standard Level or move up is normally taken in the February of DP1, which is also when the investigation planning starts, so the two conversations belong together.

programmes.name: Diploma Chemistry Higher Level
programmes.description: The same six units with additional depth, a two-hour Paper 1 and a two-and-a-half-hour Paper 2. The extensions concentrate in energetics and thermodynamics, equilibrium calculations, acid-base theory and organic mechanisms, where Higher Level expects curly arrows drawn correctly and intermediates named. Extended-response questions reward sustained reasoning across four or five marks rather than a single correct statement.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students applying to medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or chemical engineering generally need Chemistry at Higher Level, and the predicted grade for those applications is set in the autumn of DP2. That makes DP1 chemistry support an application decision rather than a remedial one, which is the opposite of how most families schedule it.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are assessed alongside the six subjects and contribute up to three points on the diploma total. A chemistry Extended Essay needs a research question narrow enough to answer with school apparatus, and it competes directly for laboratory time with the scientific investigation, which is why the two have to be planned in the same conversation.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set internal Extended Essay milestones well before the submission window, typically with a full draft due in DP2 autumn. For a chemistry essay the experimental work therefore has to be completed in DP1 summer term, which is exactly when Jumeirah families travel. Fixing the laboratory dates before the holiday is the most practical scheduling advice on this page.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the subject of this page, and the rest of the grid is the company it usually keeps. A Diploma timetable is bought whole, and the three subjects a chemistry student most often needs help with alongside it are predictable enough to list honestly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure 1-3 and Reactivity 1-3 on the current guide. Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44, the scientific investigation at 20. Teaching concentrates on mole arithmetic, sign conventions, equilibrium reasoning and organic mechanisms drawn to mark-scheme standard.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Taken with Chemistry by nearly every medicine applicant in Dubai, and the two investigations fall in the same window, which is a scheduling problem rather than an academic one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, the same assessment shape as Chemistry, and a shared set of data-handling skills. A student who has learned uncertainty propagation in one subject carries it into the other, which makes the pairing cheaper to support than it looks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route that carries Higher Level Chemistry comfortably: logarithms for pH work, exponential relationships for rates, and algebraic confidence for equilibrium expressions. Students lose marks in unstructured questions, where nothing signals which tool is wanted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Workable with Chemistry, with one caveat. The logarithmic work behind pH and the exponential treatment of rate have to be taught rather than assumed, and that usually costs two or three extra sessions in DP1 rather than causing a problem later.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and a scientific investigation of the same shape. Chosen in Dubai as a third science by students who want a lighter load and then discovered to have real data-handling demands of its own.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary option satisfying either group 3 or group 4. Shares a surprising amount of chemistry - buffering, nutrient cycling, pollution load - so a chemistry tutor can often support it without a separate match.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and three internal assessment commentaries. Frequently the sixth subject for a science-heavy Dubai student, and its commentary deadlines collide with the investigation more often than anyone plans for.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and the HL essay. Science students tend to underrate Paper 1 because it is a timed skill rather than a body of content that can be revised.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three points on the total. Support here is process coaching only: framing a knowledge question, narrowing a research question until school apparatus can answer it, and reading a draft to ask what the evidence does not yet support.

sections.heading: The three clocks a Diploma Chemistry student is running at once
paragraphs: A Diploma Chemistry student in Dubai is bound by three separate calendars, and the one a family notices is rarely the one that matters most. The school sets internal deadlines for the scientific investigation and the Extended Essay, publishes mock weeks, and fixes the point at which predicted grades are agreed. The IB sets the examination session. The universities set the application window, which opens in the autumn of DP2 and closes long before any paper is written.

Of the three, the university clock runs earliest and is the one most often missed. An application submitted in autumn of DP2 carries a predicted grade that the school derives from DP1 results and the DP2 autumn mock. A family that plans chemistry support for February of DP2 has already passed the point where the grade on the offer letter was decided. Support that begins in DP1 is cheaper, calmer and influences the number that actually travels with the application.

The school clock is the one most often underestimated. Internal investigation deadlines in Dubai schools commonly fall in DP1 spring or DP2 early autumn, well ahead of the IB's own upload window, because the department needs time to mark and moderate. Those dates are in the Diploma handbook. Reading them in September and writing them into a calendar is a twenty-minute job that removes most of the emergencies this subject generates.

The examination clock is the one we deliberately say least about. UAE schools sit the May session, and the structure is fixed: Paper 1 with a multiple-choice section and a data-based section at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent, and the investigation at 20. Specific IB session and results dates are not published on these pages, because the IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and a plan built on a wrong date is worse than a plan built on none. The Diploma coordinator holds the official timetable and is the right source.

sections.heading: DP1 term by term: what chemistry should be secure by when
paragraphs: DP1 is where chemistry grades are actually built, and it is almost always the year families do not buy support in. The content sequence varies between Dubai schools, but the dependencies do not: nothing in Reactivity works without the mole, nothing in equilibrium works without a secure grasp of dynamic reversibility, and nothing in organic chemistry survives without functional-group recognition becoming automatic.

By the end of the first term, mole arithmetic should be a tool rather than a topic. That means a student can convert between mass, moles, concentration and volume without hesitating, can identify a limiting reagent in an unfamiliar equation, and can carry a percentage yield calculation to a sensible number of significant figures. Students arriving from MYP Sciences frequently cannot do this in October, and it is the single highest-value repair in the subject because every later unit depends on it.

By the end of the second term, bonding and structure should be secure enough to predict rather than recall - shapes, polarity, intermolecular forces and the reasoning that links structure to physical property. Energetics should be arriving, and with it the sign convention that costs more marks than any other single idea in Standard Level chemistry. An exothermic change has a negative enthalpy value, and a student who writes it positive has lost the mark regardless of the arithmetic.

By the end of DP1, equilibrium and the beginning of organic chemistry should be in place, and the investigation should have a research question, a method and ideally its data. A student entering DP2 with the investigation unplanned is carrying 20 per cent of the grade into the busiest academic year of their school life, alongside university applications and the autumn mock that sets their prediction.

sections.heading: DP2 autumn: mocks, the investigation and the application in one term
paragraphs: The autumn term of DP2 is the hardest term of the Diploma, and chemistry is usually one of three subjects making the same demand at once. The mock sits in it. The investigation's final internal deadline often sits in it. The university application sits in it. And the predicted grade, which is the number that actually reaches an admissions office, is agreed from that mock during it.

The practical consequence is that DP2 autumn is a bad term to start from scratch and a good term to consolidate. Sessions in this window should be spent on assessment technique rather than content: writing justification to the standard Paper 2 credits, using the data booklet as a tool rather than a reference, and converting correct chemistry into a written form a mark scheme can award. A student who already knows the content gains more from six sessions here than from twenty in February.

The investigation needs a different kind of hour. By DP2 autumn the data should exist, and what remains is processing, uncertainty, the conclusion and the evaluation - criteria B, C and D, eighteen of the available twenty-four marks. Those are the criteria students lose most on, usually because the evaluation reads as a list of apologies rather than an assessment of how the method limited the conclusion. That can be coached without a tutor writing a word of it.

Jumeirah 1 households feel this term physically. Two school runs, a mock timetable, an application portal and an investigation draft inside twelve weeks is a scheduling problem before it is an academic one. The arrangement that survives is one protected hour a week at a fixed time, taught online so no journey is attached to it, with work set and marked in between. An ambitious three-hour week agreed in September is usually two hours by October and nothing by November.

sections.heading: The last ten weeks, counted backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Ten weeks before the written papers, the available moves narrow and that is helpful rather than discouraging. Content cannot be rebuilt wholesale, so the question becomes which parts of chemistry repay late attention and which do not. The plan below allocates those weeks and, more importantly, names the evidence that each phase worked, because a revision plan without evidence is a wish list.

The first three weeks go to the topic triage set out in the next section. Two topics, chosen because they carry marks and respond to late work, are rebuilt properly. Everything else is consolidated rather than retaught. The temptation at this point is to cover everything lightly, and it reliably produces a student who recognises all of the course and can answer none of it under time pressure.

Weeks four to seven are the data booklet and Paper 1B. The booklet is provided in the examination, which means marks are available for using it quickly and are lost by students who have revised as though they had to memorise it. Knowing where the bond enthalpies are, which constants are given and what is deliberately absent is a skill that takes two sessions and is worth more than a third rewrite of organic mechanisms. Paper 1B's data questions are the component least drilled at school.

The last three weeks are full timed papers and cold repeats. Two complete papers under exam conditions, marked against the published scheme, with errors reported by cause rather than as a total. Then questions the student failed earlier in the block, returning unannounced, to prove a repair held. A student who has never finished a Paper 2 inside the time will not finish the real one, and ten weeks is more than enough to fix that specifically.

sections.heading: Which chemistry topics repay late work, and which do not
paragraphs: Not every chemistry topic responds equally to attention ten weeks out, and treating them as equal is how a final term gets wasted. Some topics are procedural: once the method is secure, the marks follow reliably and quickly. Others are conceptual networks that take months to build and cannot be assembled in a fortnight. A good late-stage plan is honest about which is which.

The procedural topics repay late work handsomely. Mole and concentration arithmetic is the clearest case: it is mechanical, it appears across both papers, and a student who tightens it gains marks in units they have not revisited. Enthalpy calculations with correct sign conventions are the same. So is titration arithmetic, pH calculation for strong acids and bases, and reading the data booklet fluently. None of these require new understanding, only reliable execution.

The conceptual topics are different. Bonding and structure as a predictive framework, equilibrium as dynamic reasoning rather than a recalled principle, and the Higher Level organic mechanisms taken as a connected system all take sustained time. Ten weeks out, the right move with these is consolidation: secure what is already partly there, practise the question types that recur, and accept that a student who has never understood why an equilibrium shifts will not come to understand it in week nine.

The triage is not a counsel of despair. It is what lets a student arrive at the paper with two topics genuinely repaired rather than ten topics lightly revisited. A marked mock is the input: the topics where the student lost the most marks and which sit in the procedural column become the two priorities, and everything else is consolidated. That decision takes one session and shapes the other nineteen.

sections.heading: The UAE school calendar against a chemistry revision plan
paragraphs: A revision plan that ignores the local calendar fails in contact with it. The Dubai academic year carries a winter break in December, a spring break, National Day at the start of December, and Ramadan, during which school days are shortened across the emirate. A ten-week block placed without reference to those is a six-week block with four weeks of optimism attached.

Ramadan is the one that most changes the shape of a week. School hours shorten, families eat late, and the useful study window moves. A session that worked at 17:00 in January often works better after Iftar in Ramadan, and a student who tries to hold the old slot generally ends up tired rather than ahead. The honest planning move is to shift the slot deliberately and keep the frequency, rather than pausing and hoping to catch up afterwards.

The breaks cut both ways. A December or spring break with no homework competing for the evening is the best available window for covering ground, and three or four sessions inside one week of a break achieve more than three weeks of term-time hours. But a break is also when Jumeirah families travel, often across time zones, and a plan that assumes availability it does not have simply loses those sessions. Agreeing in advance which weeks are working weeks is a five-minute conversation with real value.

The mandatory UAE subjects also sit inside the week and are frequently left out of parents' mental arithmetic. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and advises that no mandatory subject lesson should be shorter than 25 minutes. Those hours are real timetable hours, and they are part of why a Diploma week is fuller than the six subjects suggest.

sections.heading: What chemistry support costs across two Diploma years, not one term
paragraphs: Begin at the top of the Dubai market, because that is the band families reach for in a panic and it is worth knowing what it does and does not buy. Premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 an hour and above. At that rate, ten final-term sessions is a five-figure commitment in dirhams, and what it buys is late-stage technique from someone very experienced. What it cannot buy is the DP1 foundation that should already be there.

Below that, the IB and IGCSE specialist band runs at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with monthly estimates for exam-year specialist support around AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more on two sessions a week. A qualified subject teacher working online is quoted at about AED 150 to 300 an hour, roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on one weekly session. Budget online tutoring, usually university students, is advertised from about AED 45 to 150. All of these are published market figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

Spread across two years the arithmetic changes shape. One weekly hour with a qualified subject teacher across both Diploma years, at the middle of that band, is a steady monthly figure rather than a crisis payment, and it covers the DP1 foundation, the investigation planning and the final block. Families who buy nothing in DP1 and then buy premium hours in DP2 spring commonly spend more in total for a worse result, because they are paying the highest rate in the market for the work that was cheapest to do early.

Context helps. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, and the gap above the online band is travel rather than teaching. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; they are a service we offer only in India, and chemistry here is taught online with a free trial lesson first and nothing payable before it.

sections.heading: The investigation deadline is set by the school, not by the IB
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent of the Diploma Chemistry grade, is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each, and has a report length capped at 3,000 words. Those are the IB's parameters. The dates are not: the school sets the internal deadlines for the plan, the draft and the final submission, because the department must mark and moderate before anything is uploaded. Those dates are in the Diploma handbook, and they are the ones a family should write into a calendar in September.

The supervisor is the student's own chemistry teacher, who provides subject guidance and authenticates that the work is the student's own. That authentication is the reason the boundary around a tutor's help is firm rather than a matter of taste. A tutor may narrow a research question until the school's apparatus can actually answer it, point out that a chosen variable is not controllable, plan the number of repeats needed to justify an uncertainty, explain what each criterion rewards, and read a draft to ask which claim the data does not support.

A tutor may not supply the research question as a finished thing, process the data, write or rewrite any section, or correct a draft repeatedly until it is right. The student makes every change. This is not caution for its own sake: the research behind these pages found a site in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is a route to a candidate losing their diploma rather than a cheaper form of tutoring.

Where students actually lose investigation marks is predictable and coachable. Criterion A goes when the research question is too broad to answer with the apparatus available. Criterion B goes when uncertainties are not propagated or error bars are absent. Criterion C goes when the conclusion claims more than the data supports, or does not compare the result with an accepted value. Criterion D goes when the evaluation lists apologies instead of explaining how a specific methodological limitation affected the specific conclusion. All four can be improved without a tutor writing a sentence.

sections.heading: Retakes, remarks and the November option, in the right order
paragraphs: Results day produces three decisions and they have to be taken in order. The first is whether any single component looks anomalous against everything else the student has produced. A chemistry grade two below every mock and every internal assessment is the case where a remark is worth considering, and the request goes through the school within the review window the IB sets. A grade consistent with the student's mocks is almost never changed by a remark, and paying for one is usually buying disappointment.

The second decision is whether a retake makes sense. The IB runs a November session as well as a May one, and candidates do retake in a later session. A retake is a reasonable choice when the student has a specific, diagnosable failure - one component, one term of missed teaching, an illness during the paper - and poor value when the grade reflects two years of partial understanding, because the same six months will produce the same result without a changed plan.

The third decision is about the offer. University offers made on predicted grades have conditions, and those conditions are negotiated with the institution rather than with the IB. Some will accept a November retake; some will defer entry; some will not. That conversation belongs with the school's university counsellor in the first week after results, not a month later, and it determines whether a retake is useful at all.

No specific IB session or results date appears on this page, deliberately. Those dates should be taken from the school's Diploma coordinator or from the IB directly, and confirmed rather than assumed, because a retake entry missed by a week cannot be recovered. What a tutor can do is start a retake plan from a marked script rather than from the grade, because the component that failed is the one the next six months should be built around.

process.title: Send the handbook dates and a marked script
process.description: Two things make the first session useful: the school's published internal deadlines for the investigation and the Extended Essay, and a photograph of the last marked chemistry paper. One tells us which clock is closest, the other tells us whether the losses are content, technique or arithmetic. A grade alone tells us neither.

process.title: A short call to identify the binding deadline
process.description: Twenty minutes to establish the level, the school, the next deadline on the handbook and whether a university application is in play. The output is a decision about what the next six sessions are for, written as a sentence a parent can repeat, rather than a general plan to improve at chemistry.

process.title: A free trial lesson on the student's own question
process.description: One lesson, nothing payable, no card details, built around a question the student has already lost marks on. It shows whether the tutor knows the current guide and whether the hour works for the student. If either answer is no, a different tutor is proposed rather than the same one defended.

process.title: A plan dated against the school's calendar
process.description: A short written plan that uses the school's own deadline dates rather than generic ones: which topics are being rebuilt, where the investigation work sits, when the two review papers happen and which week the full timed papers fall in. Short enough to be checked in four weeks instead of reinterpreted.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marking in between
process.description: A fixed weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time, with work set at the end of each session and marked before the next. The marking is where the plan corrects itself, because errors get classified by cause. Sessions with nothing between them deliver roughly a third of the gain for the same fee.

process.title: A review at the end of each term
process.description: At each school assessment point the plan is tested against the result. If the triaged topics have moved, the next priorities are chosen. If they have not, the diagnosis was wrong and it changes, rather than the student being asked for more effort against the same plan.

whyPoints.title: We plan against your school's dates
whyPoints.description: The deadlines that bind a Diploma Chemistry student are set by the school's coordinator, not by a generic calendar, and they are published in the handbook. Sessions are planned from those dates and from the university application window, because those are the clocks that decide the grade that reaches an admissions office.

whyPoints.title: DP1 is the cheap year
whyPoints.description: Mole arithmetic, sign conventions and justification style are inexpensive to install in DP1 autumn and expensive to repair in DP2 spring. Families who buy nothing in the first year and premium hours in the second commonly spend more in total for a worse result, which is worth saying before anything is booked.

whyPoints.title: Topic triage instead of covering everything
whyPoints.description: Ten weeks out, some chemistry repays late work and some does not. Procedural topics - moles, enthalpy, titration, data booklet fluency - are rebuilt. Conceptual networks are consolidated. Two topics genuinely repaired beats ten lightly revisited, and the marked mock decides which two.

whyPoints.title: A hard boundary on the investigation
whyPoints.description: A tutor narrows a research question, plans repeats, explains criteria and asks questions about a draft. A tutor does not process data, write sections or correct a draft until it is right. The boundary is stated before booking because the school supervisor authenticates the work and the candidate carries the risk.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates we cannot verify
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this site are taken from the boards' own published pages. IB session and results dates are not published here, because they could not be verified against the IB directly. The Diploma coordinator holds the official timetable and is the right source for them.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what IB Gram is not
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no accreditation from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, no UAE office, no school partnerships, and no in-home service anywhere in the UAE. All of that is checkable, which is why it is written down.

faqs.question: Which chemistry units should be secure by the end of DP1?
faqs.answer: By the end of the first Diploma year a student should be able to use the mole as a tool rather than recall it as a topic, predict shape and polarity from structure instead of remembering examples, apply enthalpy sign conventions consistently, and reason about an unfamiliar equilibrium rather than quoting Le Chatelier's principle. Functional-group recognition should be becoming automatic. The investigation should have a research question and ideally its data. A student entering the second year without mole fluency is carrying a gap that every subsequent unit will widen, which is why the first term of DP1 is the cheapest place in the whole course to intervene.

faqs.question: What falls due in DP2 autumn, and in what order?
faqs.answer: Three things collide in one term. The autumn mock, which is the main evidence for the predicted grade. The investigation's final internal deadline, set by the school rather than the IB, because the department needs time to mark and moderate. And the university application, submitted on the strength of that prediction. The order matters: the prediction is produced from the mock, the application carries the prediction, and the investigation competes for the same weeks. Support in this term is best spent on assessment technique and on the processing, conclusion and evaluation criteria of the investigation, rather than on new content.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics are worth working on ten weeks out?
faqs.answer: The procedural ones, because they convert into marks quickly and reliably. Mole and concentration arithmetic first, since it appears across both papers and tightening it gains marks in units that are not being revised. Enthalpy calculations with correct signs. Titration arithmetic and pH for strong acids and bases. And fluency with the data booklet, which is provided in the examination, so marks go to the student who can find a bond enthalpy without searching mid-question. None of these require new understanding, only reliable execution, which is exactly what ten weeks can deliver.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics are not worth starting late?
faqs.answer: The conceptual networks. Bonding and structure used as a predictive framework, equilibrium understood as dynamic rather than recalled as a principle, and Higher Level organic mechanisms taken as a connected system all take months to build. Ten weeks out the sensible move with these is consolidation: secure what is partly there, practise the recurring question shapes, and accept that a student who has never grasped why an equilibrium shifts will not grasp it in week nine. Spreading the final block thinly across everything produces a student who recognises the whole course and can answer none of it under time pressure.

faqs.question: Who sets my child's investigation deadline?
faqs.answer: The school. The IB sets the parameters - 20 per cent of the grade, 24 marks across four criteria, a 3,000-word cap on the report - but the dates for the plan, the draft and the final submission are set by the school's Diploma coordinator and the chemistry department, because they have to mark and moderate before anything is uploaded. Those dates appear in the Diploma handbook and in Dubai schools commonly fall in DP1 spring or DP2 early autumn. Writing them into a family calendar in September removes most of the emergencies this part of the course generates.

faqs.question: How long does the chemistry investigation take, start to finish?
faqs.answer: Plan for a term rather than a fortnight. Narrowing a research question until the school's apparatus can answer it usually takes two or three attempts. Trialling the method reveals that the first version does not produce a measurable change, which is normal and is why trials exist. Data collection needs enough repeats to justify an uncertainty. Then processing, graphing with error bars, the conclusion and the evaluation. Compressed into three weeks, the criteria that suffer are A and D - research design and evaluation - which together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school calendar leave usable revision weeks?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a ten-week plan assumes, which is why the plan should be built against the actual calendar. The year carries National Day at the start of December, a winter break, a spring break, and Ramadan with shortened school days across the emirate. Breaks are genuinely valuable for covering ground, because nothing competes for the evening, but they are also when Jumeirah families travel. Agreeing in advance which weeks are working weeks converts an optimistic ten-week block into a real six or seven-week one, which is a better basis for deciding what can be achieved.

faqs.question: What should a chemistry revision plan do about Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Move the slot and keep the frequency, rather than pausing. School days shorten across Dubai, meals are late, and the productive study window shifts, so a session that worked at 17:00 in January often works better after Iftar. Students who try to hold the old slot generally end up tired rather than ahead. Because lessons are online there is no travel attached to a late session, which makes the shift practical. Pausing for the month and planning to catch up afterwards tends to cost four weeks that the final block then has to absorb, usually at the expense of full timed papers.

faqs.question: What does two years of chemistry support cost, rather than one term?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour with a qualified subject teacher online is quoted in Dubai at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, which is about AED 600 to 1,200 a month, sustained across both Diploma years. An exam-year specialist at two sessions a week is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above monthly. Premium named tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above per hour. Families who buy nothing in DP1 and then premium hours in DP2 often spend more in total for a worse outcome, because they are paying the top of the market for work that was cheapest to do early. These are published market bands read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Is a premium examiner-led rate worth it in the final term?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a specific job. At AED 500 to 650 an hour and above, what a very experienced teacher brings is late-stage technique: how an extended response should be structured, which answer shapes the scheme credits, how to allocate time across a paper. That is real value for a student whose content is already secure. It is poor value for a student with a mole gap, because the highest rate in the market is being spent on the work a DP1 session would have done. Also treat examiner descriptions carefully: current examiner status is a specific claim and should be evidenced rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Can my child retake chemistry in a later session?
faqs.answer: Yes. The IB runs a November session as well as a May one, and candidates do retake in a later session through their school. Whether it is worth doing depends on the diagnosis. A retake makes sense where the failure is specific and identifiable - one component, a term of missed teaching, illness during the paper. It is poor value where the grade reflects two years of partial understanding, because the same six months will produce the same result unless the plan changes. The first conversation after results should be with the school's university counsellor, because some offers accept a November retake and some do not.

faqs.question: When is a remark worth requesting?
faqs.answer: When a single component is clearly out of line with everything else the student produced. A chemistry grade two below every mock, every internal assessment and the teacher's own expectation is the case worth reviewing, and the request goes through the school inside the review window. A grade consistent with the student's mock performance is very rarely changed, and requesting a remark then is usually buying a delay and a disappointment. The school's Diploma coordinator can say what the review options and deadlines are for that session, and those dates should be confirmed rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our home in Jumeirah 1 for chemistry?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. Diploma Chemistry for a Jumeirah 1 family is taught online, one-to-one, over live video, with the question, the data booklet and a shared whiteboard all on screen. Mechanisms are drawn and redrawn without anyone recopying the question, and the session can be rewatched the night before a mock. The Dubai in-home market exists and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the premium above online rates reflecting travel rather than teaching, which is a useful comparison when weighing the two.

faqs.question: What time can a chemistry session start on a Jumeirah 1 school night?
faqs.answer: Most Diploma students living in Jumeirah 1 travel to Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh or Al Barsha and reach home between 15:45 and 16:45, later when the beach road or Sheikh Zayed Road is slow. That makes 16:00 unrealistic, 17:00 workable on most days, and 18:30 dependable including late buses and a sibling's pick-up. Since lessons are online there is no journey attached, so the booked hour is the taught hour. Across a two-year course the slot that holds every week is worth considerably more than the slot that looks ideal in September.

faqs.question: Which Jumeirah 1 schools run Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Jumeirah Baccalaureate School runs the full IB continuum inside the district itself. Beyond that, a Jumeirah 1 family's realistic options are Raffles World Academy and Emirates International School in the Umm Suqeim and Umm Al Sheif cluster, and Dubai International Academy, Dubai American Academy and the other Al Barsha campuses inland. The International Baccalaureate accounts for about 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, against 37 per cent for UK curriculum, so Diploma Chemistry is taught in a limited set of schools here. Which campus a student attends changes the opening weeks of tutoring more than their ability does.

faqs.question: How do I verify a tutor holds the UAE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask to see it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services, under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, there is no good reason for a UAE-based tutor not to hold one. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any page quoting a figure with caution.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingHeading: Send the handbook dates, and we will work backwards from them
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingBody: If your child is taking Diploma Chemistry from a Jumeirah 1 address, the most useful first step is to send the school's published internal deadlines alongside the last marked chemistry paper. From those two documents it is possible to say which of the three clocks is closest, whether the losses are content or technique, and which two topics in the triage are worth the next ten weeks. Take the free trial lesson on one of your child's own questions, with nothing payable and no card details, and a short plan dated against the school's own calendar comes back before anything is booked. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Chemistry at Standard and Higher Level on the current syllabus, covering Paper 1A multiple choice with the data booklet, Paper 1B data analysis, Paper 2 extended response and the scientific investigation.

intro.heading: The cheapest useful thing a Jumeirah 2 family can do about chemistry
paragraphs: Start with the options that cost nothing, because in this subject two of them work surprisingly often. The first is the school's own chemistry department. Most Diploma schools in the Jumeirah and Al Safa ring run a weekly subject clinic, and a Higher Level student who attends it for a term with specific questions written down beforehand usually closes two or three topic gaps without anybody paying for an hour. Families skip it because it is at 7:30am or 3:30pm and inconvenient, which is a different objection from it not working.

The second free option is the student's own marked scripts. A Diploma chemistry student accumulates a dozen marked tests across two years and almost none of them get read twice. Sitting down with three of them and sorting the lost marks into four piles — did not know the content, knew it but wrote no reasoning, arithmetic slip, misread the question — produces a diagnosis a tutor would charge for, and parents can do it in an evening. In our experience the second pile is the largest, which changes what you should buy.

The third option costs a little: past papers marked honestly against the published mark scheme. The fourth is a small group, where a centre class at roughly AED 80 to 200 per student per hour works well if everyone in the group has the same gap and badly if they do not. Only after those four does one-to-one tuition become the obvious answer, and then it is worth buying properly rather than cheaply.

Here is the published market, lowest first, as of October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student tier. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level rates at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors to AED 500. BartyED sits at around AED 650. On a monthly basis Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a budget weekly hour, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Monthly packages in this market run near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. The first lesson is a free trial, with no card details requested beforehand, and the honest purpose of that lesson is to tell you which of the five options above your child actually needs.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: Chemistry is taught in three distinct forms across the schools serving Jumeirah 2, and the price of support tracks the assessment rather than the difficulty.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Two years at Standard or Higher Level on the syllabus introduced in 2023 and first examined in 2025. Content is organised as Structure 1 to 3 — models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and classification of matter — and Reactivity 1 to 3 — what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade, Paper 2 is 44%, and the internally assessed scientific investigation is 20%.
programmes.countryNote: IB students make up 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places. For a Jumeirah 2 household the practical effect is bigger Higher Level chemistry sets, and bigger sets are precisely where a student who writes correct chemistry with no reasoning stops being noticed.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Chemistry sits inside integrated sciences and is assessed against four criteria rather than by examination. There are no weightings and no papers, so a parent gets no numerical warning before the Diploma begins. Support here is cheaper per month and considerably better value, because the skills that decide Higher Level chemistry — ratio reasoning, significant figures, unit tracking — are taught in these years or not at all.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim ring run MYP into the Diploma. The cheapest chemistry intervention available to a family in this district is a handful of hours in the MYP 5 summer on mole reasoning, bought at the budget band rather than the specialist one.

programmes.name: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry
programmes.description: The British-curriculum route at 16, examined entirely by written paper with practical skills tested through an alternative-to-practical component rather than coursework. Mole calculations, titration arithmetic and percentage yield are the components where marks concentrate, and they are the same components that decide whether Diploma chemistry feels manageable two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Published rates sit a band below IB throughout: Unitors quotes IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200. A family in Jumeirah 2 planning for Higher Level chemistry should treat Year 11 as the cheap window, because the same mole-reasoning work costs the IGCSE rate now and the specialist IB rate in eighteen months.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in this catchment, with organic chemistry taught in greater depth than at Diploma Standard Level and a practical component assessed by written paper or endorsement depending on the board. Support is usually quoted at the same specialist band as IB because the content depth is comparable.
programmes.countryNote: The budget difference is structural rather than about price. An A Level chemistry plan can be built almost entirely from past papers, while a Diploma plan has to fund investigation supervision as well, so the same AED total buys more paper practice on the A Level route.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is almost never the only booking a Jumeirah 2 family makes. These are the subjects most often added, and what each one assesses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1A multiple choice with the data booklet, Paper 1B data analysis, Paper 2 extended response, plus a scientific investigation worth 20%. The largest single source of lost marks is correct chemistry written without the reasoning step the mark scheme asks for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual companion for medicine applicants. Its investigation is assessed against the same four criteria as chemistry's, so investigation coaching bought once transfers, which is one of very few real economies in a Diploma budget.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Taken with chemistry by engineering applicants. The shared skill is quantitative discipline: significant figures, units, uncertainty, and writing working in the order an examiner reads it rather than the order a student thinks it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The subject that quietly decides whether Higher Level chemistry is painful. Logarithms for pH, exponentials for rate constants and algebraic rearrangement under a square root all appear in chemistry before the maths course has finished teaching them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Adequate for Standard Level chemistry and thin for Higher Level, particularly in the energetics and equilibrium material. A student on this combination typically needs more chemistry hours rather than fewer, which should be in the budget from the start.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Chosen instead of a second demanding science by students who want a lighter quantitative load. Pairs well with Chemistry HL for a student whose target courses need one strong science rather than two.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, assessed by a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition. It adds no chemistry content but competes for the same weeks as the investigation, which is why a chemistry plan has to be written against the school's whole assessment calendar.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece often written in chemistry here. Supervision belongs to the school. What a tutor can legitimately add is feedback on the student's own drafts and help thinking through experimental design, never any part of the writing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Booked alongside chemistry more often than expected, usually because the same student who writes chemistry without reasoning also writes essays without analysis. The underlying habit is identical and improving it once improves both grades.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.regionsTitle: Jumeirah 2 and the districts that share its schools
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.regionsIntro: Diploma chemistry cohorts here are drawn from a continuous coastal strip, so families several streets apart are often working to the same internal deadlines.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2
regions.note: Villa streets between Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road. No Diploma school inside the district, so chemistry students travel inland to Al Safa or along the coast to Al Sufouh each day.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: North-east towards City Walk and La Mer, nearest to Emirates International School Jumeirah. The shortest Diploma commute in the cluster and the one case where an in-home arrangement is logistically simple.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: South-west towards Al Safa 2 and the Jumeirah English Speaking School catchment. Shares Beach Road with Jumeirah 2 and the same late-afternoon constraint.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Immediately inland, and the densest school cluster near Jumeirah 2. Group chemistry classes in this area fill fastest, which is why they are also the ones most likely to contain students with four different gaps.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
