sections.heading: Price steps in the Dubai chemistry market, read from the bottom
paragraphs: Reading a rate card from the cheapest end tells you more than reading it from the top, because each step upward should buy something nameable. At AED 33 to 52 an hour, which is Tutopiya's published starting point, you are buying somebody who studied the subject recently and can answer questions about it. That is genuinely useful for a student who has fallen behind on content and knows it. At AED 45 to 65, EdFlik's published range, the same thing with more structure.

The step to AED 150, where Unitors begins its IGCSE pricing, buys a trained teacher who has taught the specification to a class and knows which questions the cohort gets wrong. The step to AED 200, Unitors' IB starting point, buys the same thing for the Diploma. The step to around AED 270, TutorChase's quoted rate, and into Bestimate's AED 200 to 450 specialist band, buys somebody who has read the published assessment criteria for the scientific investigation and marked work against them. That is a real distinction and it is the one worth paying for in this subject.

Above AED 450 the nameable thing gets harder to name. BartyED's published AED 650 is a real rate for a real service, but a family deciding between forty hours at AED 300 and eighteen hours at AED 650 should normally take the forty, because chemistry marks accumulate with contact time and with the number of marked papers, not with the reputation attached to the hour.

The in-home rows sit apart from this ladder because they bundle a car journey into the rate. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500. The difference against an equivalent online rate is roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour and it pays for driving, not for chemistry. All of these figures were published by the providers named and are dated October 2026. None of them is our price.

sections.heading: The current chemistry syllabus, Structure and Reactivity
paragraphs: The syllabus introduced in 2023 and first examined in 2025 abandoned the old option topics and reorganised everything into two strands. Structure 1 covers models of the particulate nature of matter, including the mole concept and atomic structure. Structure 2 covers models of bonding and structure — ionic, covalent and metallic models and the behaviour that follows from them. Structure 3 covers classification of matter, including the periodic table and the organic families. Reactivity 1 asks what drives chemical reactions, which is the energetics and thermodynamics material. Reactivity 2 asks how much, how fast and how far, which is equilibrium and kinetics. Reactivity 3 asks what the mechanisms of chemical change are, covering redox, acid-base and organic mechanisms.

Assessment is Paper 1 at 36% of the final grade, split into Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data-based questions, with the data booklet available; Paper 2 at 44%, short and extended response; and the scientific investigation at 20%. Higher Level candidates sit the same components over longer durations and across additional content in both strands rather than in a separate option paper.

Two practical consequences follow for a Jumeirah 2 student. First, the reorganisation means older revision material maps imperfectly onto the current course, and a tutor working from pre-2023 notes will spend hours on emphases that have moved. Ask directly whether a prospective tutor teaches the current structure, by name. Second, because the strands are integrated rather than compartmentalised, a weakness in Structure 1 mole reasoning reappears in Reactivity 2 equilibrium calculations and again in Reactivity 3 redox titrations. One cheap gap, closed once, pays three times.

The data booklet deserves a mention of its own. Students lose marks by not knowing what is in it, so they memorise constants that are provided and fail to look up values that are. Twenty minutes with the booklet and a highlighter is one of the highest-return unpaid activities in the subject.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry and the mechanisms students get wrong
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is the topic Jumeirah 2 parents name most often when they call, and the complaint is nearly always the same: the student can recite the reactions and cannot answer the question. That is a diagnosable pattern rather than a vague difficulty. The marks in Reactivity 3 go to the mechanism — which bond breaks, where the electrons go, what the intermediate is — and students who have learned reagent-to-product pairs by rote have memorised the two ends of a process whose middle is what gets assessed.

The specific failures recur. Curly arrows drawn from the atom rather than from the electron pair or the bond, which loses the mark even when the overall mechanism is right. Nucleophilic substitution answered without saying whether it proceeds through one step or two, when the halogenoalkane's structure is the entire point of the question. Electrophilic addition to an alkene written without the carbocation intermediate. Condensation and hydrolysis confused in both directions. Isomerism questions where the student identifies the type correctly and then draws two structures that are in fact the same molecule.

All of these respond quickly to teaching because they are notation and reasoning problems, not knowledge problems. A student who already knows the reactions can usually be moved up a band in four to six focused hours, which makes organic chemistry one of the cheaper things to fix in this subject. The expensive problems are the quantitative ones: a student who is genuinely unsure about moles needs weeks, not hours, and should be bought at the lower rate for longer rather than at the specialist rate briefly.

A warning about how organic chemistry gets sold. It is the topic most often named in advertising because it is the topic parents fear, and a provider who leads with it is leading with your anxiety rather than with your child's diagnosis. Ask for the marked script to be read first. If organic chemistry is not where the marks are going, do not buy hours on it.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: twenty-four marks and four criteria
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is 20% of the chemistry grade. It is one independent piece of experimental work, reported in no more than 3,000 words, assessed against four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Twenty-four marks in total. If a family has a small chemistry budget, this is where it belongs, and it should be spent before any data is collected rather than after the draft exists.

What goes wrong is consistent across cohorts. Research design loses marks because the question is too broad to produce a measurable relationship, or because the controlled variables are listed without a stated reason for controlling each one. Evaluation loses marks because students write a list of weaknesses rather than explaining how each weakness would push the result in a particular direction and by roughly how much. Data analysis and conclusion are usually the stronger two, which is the opposite of what most parents assume.

The chemistry-specific version of good design is worth stating. A titration investigation needs enough repeats for a meaningful mean and a stated tolerance for concordant titres. A rates investigation needs a concentration range wide enough to show a trend and a method of timing that does not depend on judging a colour change by eye. An energetics investigation needs the heat loss to the surroundings acknowledged in the design rather than apologised for in the evaluation. These are the decisions six hours of supervision buys.

The boundary is absolute and we state it to the student in the first session. A tutor may interrogate the research question, teach uncertainty handling, explain what each criterion rewards and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the investigation. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750; for the student that is a malpractice finding that can cost the whole Diploma, which is a much larger loss than twenty-four marks.

sections.heading: A two-year chemistry budget for a Jumeirah 2 household
paragraphs: Set the tutoring figure beside the school fee and the numbers stop feeling abstract. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within AED 2.5 billion in total. For a Jumeirah 2 family that fee freeze is the first year in some time where a tutoring line can be added without a fee rise absorbing it.

A sensible two-year chemistry plan on the figures above comes to somewhere between AED 7,000 and AED 20,000 depending on the band chosen and whether the school is doing its job. That is a real amount of money and it deserves the same scrutiny as any other annual household commitment. The cheapest effective version — a diagnostic block, an investigation block, and a weekly exam-term slot in the final spring — lands near the bottom of that range. The most common version, which is panic buying at the specialist rate in the final three months, lands near the top and achieves less.

Two line items that families forget. Private candidate exam entry, if a student ends up entering outside their school, is a separate cost paid to the centre rather than to a tutor. And a second subject: almost nobody buys chemistry alone, so the honest budget question is what three sciences plus maths will cost together, not what chemistry costs.

We do not publish a fixed price list on these pages, because the rate varies with level, subject and session length and an invented figure would be worse than none. We quote in AED in writing before anything is booked, we do not take card details before the free trial, and we will say when a cheaper option would do the same work.

sections.heading: Scheduling chemistry around the Jumeirah 2 week and Ramadan
paragraphs: Chemistry sessions in this district run later than any other subject, for a practical reason: Diploma students carry the heaviest afternoon co-curricular load, and the schools they attend finish between 3:05pm and 3:20pm with commitments often running to 4:30pm. A Jumeirah 2 Higher Level student is frequently not available before 5:30pm, and families who book a 4pm slot discover within a month that it collides with something immovable.

The Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road corridors are slowest between 4pm and 5:30pm, which is exactly the window an arriving tutor would need. Because our lessons run over live video, that hour is simply not a factor: a 6pm or 7pm start costs nothing extra, holds reliably and does not require anybody to leave early to beat traffic. Families travelling between the UAE and abroad in the long breaks keep the same slot, adjusted for the time difference, rather than pausing for a month.

Ramadan reshapes everything. School hours shorten, the household rhythm moves around iftar, and an afternoon slot that worked in February stops working entirely. Most families in this district move chemistry to a post-iftar evening session, and a smaller number move to a short mid-morning slot at the weekend. The useful discipline is to agree the Ramadan arrangement in writing before the month starts rather than improvising week by week, because the weeks that get improvised are the weeks that get skipped.

One more calendar note specific to the Diploma. The internal deadline for the scientific investigation differs by months between schools in the Jumeirah and Al Sufouh ring, and at some schools it falls in the final term of the first Diploma year rather than in the second. Ask the chemistry teacher for that date in writing at the start of the first year. It is the single most important date in a chemistry budget and almost no family knows it when they first call.

sections.heading: Medicine and engineering applications: when Higher Level chemistry is not optional
paragraphs: A significant share of the chemistry enquiries from this district are really university enquiries. The question behind them is whether Standard Level will be accepted, and the answer depends entirely on the target country and course rather than on anything a tutor can influence. Most medicine programmes in the United Kingdom require Chemistry at Higher Level, usually at a specified grade, and many require a second science or mathematics alongside it. Engineering programmes generally want Physics at Higher Level with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, with chemistry optional.

The decision point is early. Subject changes between Higher and Standard Level are normally possible only in the first term of the first Diploma year, so a student who discovers in the second year that their target course needed Higher Level chemistry has run out of options other than a gap year. The practical advice for a Jumeirah 2 family is to read the prerequisite pages of six target programmes during the first autumn term, write down the Higher Level requirements, and treat that list as the subject plan.

What this changes about buying tuition is the timing rather than the amount. A student who must hold Higher Level chemistry for medicine cannot afford to drift through the first year and catch up in the second, because the first year contains the investigation and the foundation that the second year's content assumes. Those are the families for whom a steady modest arrangement across both years genuinely beats a large block at the end.

A caution that matters. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and nobody can promise a university place. Any provider who attaches an outcome to a price in this context is selling something they cannot deliver, and in a medicine application the stakes make that a particularly expensive thing to believe. We will tell you what a plan can realistically address and what it cannot.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what a tutor's permit means
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain the regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits at emirate level.

For an individual tutor the relevant body is MoHRE rather than any education regulator. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different matter again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a six-month maximum to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and does not describe itself as having approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any page claiming such approval should be asked for the number.

One rule worth knowing even in Dubai. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. The principle applies generally: do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them for a fee.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to get IB chemistry help in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: The school's own chemistry clinic, attended for a term with questions written down beforehand, costs nothing and closes two or three topic gaps for a committed student. After that, sorting three marked scripts into content errors, missing reasoning, arithmetic slips and misread questions gives you a diagnosis a tutor would charge for. A centre group class at roughly AED 80 to 200 per student per hour is next, and it works only if everyone in the group shares the same gap. One-to-one tuition is the fourth step, not the first.

faqs.question: What does an IB chemistry tutor charge in Dubai, from the lowest band up?
faqs.answer: Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student tier. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist rates at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED sits at around AED 650. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 with independent tutors. Those are market figures published in October 2026, not our prices.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics should a Jumeirah 2 parent actually pay to fix?
faqs.answer: Notation and reasoning problems, because they move fastest. A student who can recite organic reactions but cannot draw a mechanism usually improves a band in four to six focused hours: curly arrows from the bond rather than the atom, substitution answered as one step or two, a carbocation intermediate shown in electrophilic addition. Genuine mole-reasoning weakness is the expensive case and needs weeks rather than hours, so buy it at a lower band for longer. Pay for a marked script to be read before you pay for any topic.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry assessed on the current syllabus?
faqs.answer: Content is organised as Structure 1 to 3 — the particulate nature of matter, bonding and structure, and classification of matter — and Reactivity 1 to 3 — what drives reactions, how much and how fast and how far, and mechanisms of chemical change. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and splits into multiple choice and data-based sections with the data booklet available. Paper 2, short and extended response, is 44%. The internally assessed scientific investigation is 20%. Higher Level sits the same components over longer durations with additional content in both strands.

faqs.question: Why does the scientific investigation deserve the first part of a chemistry budget?
faqs.answer: It is 20% of the final grade, assessed against four criteria worth six marks each, and it cannot be changed after submission. Six hours at the design stage, before any data is collected, routinely moves a student up a band on research design and evaluation. Students lose marks by asking a question too broad to produce a relationship and by listing weaknesses instead of explaining how each would shift the result. Money spent on chemistry after the submission date cannot touch that fifth of the grade at all.

faqs.question: Will a chemistry tutor help write my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. A tutor may interrogate the research question, teach uncertainty handling, explain what each assessment criterion rewards and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, which is an academic-integrity breach and for the student a malpractice finding that can cost the whole Diploma. We state this boundary to the student in the first session.

faqs.question: Is a small group chemistry class good value in the Al Safa area?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the group shares one gap. Four students who all struggle with equilibrium calculations get close to one-to-one value at roughly a third of the price. Four students with four different weaknesses get a lecture, and the one whose problem is organic mechanisms sits through ninety minutes of titration arithmetic. Ask the centre what the group's common topic is before enrolling, and ask how many are in it. Group classes in the Al Safa cluster fill quickly, which is also why they are frequently mixed.

faqs.question: Does the published hourly rate for chemistry tuition include VAT?
faqs.answer: Providers differ and it is worth settling before the first invoice rather than after. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring page's assurance. What we will do is quote our own figure in AED in writing and say whether that figure is the total payable. The single useful question to put to any provider is whether the number quoted is the number that appears on the invoice.

intro.heading: Jumeirah 3 or the next community over: the chemistry does not change
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IB chemistry tutor in Jumeirah 3 frequently search twice, once with their own community name and once with the one next door, because a neighbour in Umm Suqeim or Al Safa has recommended someone and the family wants to know whether distance matters. The useful answer is that for Chemistry it matters less than for any other Group 4 subject, and here is why: the subject is taught almost entirely through worked reasoning on a shared screen. Mechanisms are drawn, not demonstrated. Equilibrium problems are argued through, not performed. A whiteboard the student can annotate beats a kitchen table, and the drive between communities buys nothing.

What does change between these communities is logistics, and this page sets that out in a table rather than pretending otherwise. A Jumeirah 3 family whose child is bussed to Al Barsha gets home later than a Jumeirah 2 family whose child walks out of school in Al Safa. A villa in Al Manara with two children at two schools has two different pick-up times to work around. Those differences move a session by thirty or forty minutes; they do not change which tutor your child should have, and they are the entire practical content of most area-based tutoring pages in this market.

The second comparison worth making is between communities and the thing families actually compare them against, which is the local tutor pool. Hiring within a two-kilometre radius means choosing from whoever happens to live nearby and has a free weekday evening. Hiring a specialist online means choosing from everyone who has taught HL organic chemistry to candidates sitting the current guide. For a subject where the difference between a 5 and a 7 is usually mechanism fluency and uncertainty handling rather than general enthusiasm, the second pool is the one worth drawing from.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. Nothing on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at a villa in Jumeirah 3, Umm Suqeim or anywhere else in Dubai. What we do offer is a Chemistry specialist, a fixed weekly time that works around the school run, and a written diagnostic after the first free lesson.

The rest of the page is chemistry. It covers how the current subject guide is organised and assessed, the four topics where Jumeirah-strip students most reliably lose marks, how Higher Level differs from Standard Level in ways that change how many hours are needed, what the internally assessed investigation is marked on, how Dubai's published tutoring rates compare across delivery models, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons that sit alongside the Diploma in every Dubai private school and quietly eat into the week.

sections.heading: This community against the next one over, compared honestly
paragraphs: The direct answer: for online Chemistry tuition, moving between Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara and Al Wasl changes the time a session can start by up to about forty minutes and changes nothing else. The tutor pool is identical. The materials are identical. The price is identical, because no part of it pays for a car. Any page that tells you a neighbourhood has its own dedicated tutors is describing a sales territory rather than a teaching reality.

Where real differences exist, they come from schools rather than streets. A student at an IB continuum school in Umm Suqeim has a different internal deadline calendar from a student bussed to Al Barsha, and a different one again from a Year 11 student at a selective British school in Al Sufouh who will sit IGCSE and then A Level. Two families living two hundred metres apart in Jumeirah 3 can therefore need completely different tutoring plans, which is the opposite of how area pages usually describe the market.

The second real difference is sibling logistics. Families in Al Manara and Jumeirah 2 frequently have two children at two schools, and the window where both are home and neither is at football is narrow. An online slot can be split: forty minutes for one child, forty for the other, back to back, with one tutor and no travel between them. That arrangement is impractical for a visiting tutor and routine for a video session.

The honest conclusion is the one in the heading of this page. The answer is the same either way, so choose on subject specialism and on whether the tutor has taught the current guide at the level your child sits, not on which community the tutor lives in. sections.heading: How the current Chemistry guide is organised, and what that changed
paragraphs: DP Chemistry is now taught under two headings rather than eleven topics. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, molecular structure and bonding, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives a reaction, how much, how fast and how far it goes, and the mechanisms by which chemical change happens. Higher Level material sits inside those same headings rather than in a separate block, and the old option topics are gone.

That reorganisation matters for tutoring in a specific way. A student who revises by topic list will revise bonding on Monday and intermolecular forces on Thursday and never connect them, which is exactly the connection Paper 2 asks about. Sessions therefore work across the structure and reactivity boundary deliberately: why does this bonding model predict that solubility, why does that entropy change follow from this structure. Marks in the extended-response paper are awarded for the link, not the recall.

Assessment is two papers and the investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% and contains multiple choice plus a data-based section on an unseen experiment; Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response; the internally assessed scientific investigation is the remaining 20%, marked in school against IB criteria and externally moderated. A data booklet is provided in the examination, which changes revision priorities: knowing where a value lives and what it implies is worth more than memorising it.

Higher Level is wider and deeper in the same framework, and the practical consequence is hours rather than difficulty. HL students meet additional content inside each heading and sit longer papers, so the same weekly hour covers proportionally less ground. A family moving a child from SL to HL in DP1 should expect the tutoring requirement to rise by roughly half, not to stay flat. Confirm the exact structure for your child's cohort with their DP coordinator, who holds the version of the guide in force for that intake.

sections.heading: The four places Chemistry marks disappear on this strip
paragraphs: Organic mechanisms come first, and they are the clearest divider between a 5 and a 7. Students learn the names of mechanisms and then draw arrows that start in the wrong place, from an atom rather than from a lone pair or a bond. An examiner marking a mechanism is reading the arrows, not the label, so the fix is to draw mechanisms repeatedly while someone questions each arrow aloud. That is an ideal use of a shared screen and a poor use of a textbook.

Energetics is second. Enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy work is mostly sign management, and a student who has not internalised the conventions will produce a numerically correct magnitude with the wrong sign and lose the mark. Hess cycles are where this shows: the arithmetic is simple, the direction of each arrow is not. A tutor who makes the student narrate each step catches the error pattern in a single session.

Third is equilibrium and reasoning under Le Chatelier. The common failure is describing a shift rather than explaining it in terms of the quantity that changed and the system's response, and then applying the same sentence to a question about rate instead of position. Chemistry Paper 2 pays for the distinction. Fourth is quantitative care: significant figures, units, and uncertainties carried through a multi-step calculation. None of these is a knowledge gap and all four are trainable within a term.

There is a fifth that only appears in the internal investigation, and it is a design failure rather than a chemistry failure. A research question with an independent variable that cannot be cleanly controlled, or with too few levels to establish a relationship, caps the grade before the first measurement. Students who come to a tutor after data collection have usually lost marks that nobody can recover, which is why the clinic begins with the question.

sections.heading: The investigation: criteria, marks, and what a tutor will not do
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation carries 20% of the Chemistry grade and is marked against four criteria worth six marks each, twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Naming those criteria and their mark allocation is unusual in this market, and it should not be. A parent who knows the split can ask a tutor a precise question, which is where in those four does my child lose marks, and get a precise answer instead of reassurance.

Research design is decided before any chemistry happens: a focused question, clearly identified variables, a method that controls the rest, and a justified range and number of measurements. Data analysis rewards correct processing with uncertainties carried through to the final result and graphs that show the relationship. Conclusion must answer the research question using the data and compare it with accepted chemistry. Evaluation must weigh weaknesses by their impact on the result rather than cataloguing everything that could have gone better.

The boundary on a tutor's role is not negotiable, and it is worth being explicit because this market contains businesses selling finished coursework at four-figure prices. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards, challenges a research question, teaches uncertainty handling on the student's own measurements, and reads a draft and responds with questions. A tutor does not supply text, does not restructure a report, and does not hand over a method. The work must be the student's own; under IB academic-honesty rules the consequence of anything else falls on the candidate.

In practice, feedback sounds like interrogation rather than correction. What was your independent variable, and how did you keep the others constant? Does your uncertainty allow the claim you have made? Which of your weaknesses actually changed the result, and which merely annoyed you? A student who answers those and then revises their own report has learned the criterion and kept authorship intact, which is the only version of this that is safe.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what a Jumeirah 3 family is actually buying
paragraphs: Rates published by Dubai providers during 2026 group into bands. Budget online tutoring, often delivered by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to AED 300. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 with travel included in the price. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors at about AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in the same period ran near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures taken from provider rate cards and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, not an IB Gram price list; we quote after the free diagnostic lesson.

The comparison that matters is not the hourly number but what the hour contains. An hour with a Chemistry HL specialist who diagnoses an arrow-pushing error in the first fifteen minutes is a different product from an hour of general science support at a lower rate, and families who have bought both usually describe the cheaper one as the more expensive. The second variable is continuity: a lower rate with a rotating tutor costs a month of re-diagnosis every time the person changes.

In-home pricing carries a structural cost that no rate card shows. A tutor travelling into the Jumeirah strip for a 4.30pm lesson spends an hour or more in a car for a sixty-minute session, and that time is paid for somewhere, either in the rate or in the shrinking of the pool prepared to accept the booking. It also pushes sessions late, which is why visiting arrangements in this area cluster at 7pm and at weekend mornings.

One more honest note about cost and timing. Specialist availability in Chemistry thins in the weeks before an examination session, so the same specialist is both cheaper and more available in October than in March. Families who begin weekly work early get a better match for less; families who start late pay a premium for whoever is free. Anything advertised as free should state its conditions on the same screen: our trial is one lesson, with no card details and no obligation.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects that sit alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's guidance required those arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a DP student in Jumeirah 3 this is not a footnote. It is timetable time that sits alongside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service, and it is a frequent reason a Chemistry HL student says there is no room left in the week.

The organisation of those lessons is prescribed in detail. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details are useful when a parent is reading a timetable. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should be shorter than twenty-five minutes. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly.

For tutoring purposes, the practical consequence is scheduling rather than content. Count the mandatory lessons when you work out how much homework time a Chemistry HL student genuinely has, and set the weekly session where it does not collide with the subjects that carry the nearest deadline. Where families want support in Arabic itself, note that for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so any tutoring there follows the school's own material.

sections.heading: Starting from the Jumeirah strip, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is deliberately short. Send the year group, the level, the two or three Chemistry areas causing trouble, the school and the next assessed deadline. We propose one or two specialists and a slot in Gulf Standard Time. The first lesson is free and diagnostic: the student works problems aloud while the tutor records where each error occurs, and you receive a written summary of the error pattern with an honest estimate of what a term can move.

Availability deserves a straight answer, because most pages in this market imply infinite supply. Chemistry HL specialists with current experience of the Structure and Reactivity guide are a narrow pool, and in the two months before an examination session that pool is mostly committed. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred time, we say so, and offer either a specialist in another time zone whose evening matches your afternoon or a place for the next slot that opens. We will not seat a general science tutor in a Chemistry HL slot and describe them as a specialist.

What progress looks like after four sessions is checkable. Mechanism arrows start in the right place without prompting. Hess cycle answers carry the correct sign the first time. The student can state which of the four investigation criteria is weakest in their own draft. Timed Paper 2 sections are finished rather than abandoned. If none of that has happened, the match is wrong, and changing tutor early is cheaper than persevering politely for a term.

Families across Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara and Al Wasl compete for the same 4pm to 6pm weekday windows, so the slot is the scarce resource rather than the tutor. Booking it before the term starts is worth more than adding hours in April, and one reliable weekly session over twelve weeks outperforms a crammed fortnight on every measure we can observe.

whyPoints.title: One slot that works for two children
whyPoints.description: Back-to-back forty-minute sessions for siblings at different schools are routine online and impractical for a visiting tutor. Families in Al Manara and Jumeirah 2 use this constantly, with one tutor and no gap spent travelling between them.

whyPoints.title: The criteria named, not implied
whyPoints.description: We tell you that the investigation is four criteria of six marks each and which one your child is losing. A parent who knows the split can hold any tutor, including ours, to a specific account instead of accepting general reassurance.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Draft feedback arrives as questions. No text supplied, no method handed over, no report restructured. That keeps your child's work theirs, which matters because the academic-honesty consequence of the alternative falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted after a diagnosis
whyPoints.description: We publish what the Dubai market charges by model and source it, then quote our own fee once the level and frequency are known. No package is proposed before a tutor has seen the student work, because the right length is a finding rather than a guess.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my Chemistry tutor is based in Jumeirah 3 or somewhere else in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For online Chemistry tuition it makes no practical difference. Lessons run over live video on a shared whiteboard, so the only thing a tutor's location affects is the time zone they teach in, and our UAE sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time either way. What does matter is whether they have taught Structure and Reactivity at the level your child sits, and whether they can diagnose a mechanism error quickly. Choosing on postcode rather than specialism is the single most common way families here spend a term without moving a grade.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL noticeably harder than SL, or just longer?
faqs.answer: Both, but the difference families underestimate is volume. Higher Level sits inside the same Structure and Reactivity framework with additional depth in each heading and longer papers, so a weekly hour covers proportionally less of the course. The mathematical demand also rises: equilibrium algebra, pH and buffer work and thermodynamics need fluent rearrangement. A student moving from SL to HL should expect the tutoring requirement to rise by roughly half, and the limiting factor is usually algebra rather than chemistry.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep losing marks on organic mechanisms?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the arrows start in the wrong place. Students learn mechanism names and then draw arrows from an atom instead of from a lone pair or a bond, and an examiner marks what the arrows show rather than the label above them. The fix is repetition with interrogation: the student draws, the tutor questions every arrow's origin, and the pattern corrects within a few sessions. It is one of the clearest cases where a shared screen is better than a textbook, because the error is visible as it happens.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Chemistry investigation without crossing IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside firm limits. A tutor may explain what each of the four criteria rewards, challenge the research question for feasibility, teach uncertainty propagation using the student's own titration or calorimetry results, and read a draft and reply with questions. A tutor may not supply text, hand over a method, process the data or restructure the report. The investigation is 20% of the grade and is externally moderated, so work that is not the student's own puts the candidate's registration at risk, not the tutor's.

faqs.question: What are the four Chemistry investigation criteria worth?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation carry six marks each, twenty-four in total, marked in school against IB criteria and then externally moderated. Research design is where most of the loss happens, because a question with too few concentrations or temperatures to show a trend caps everything after it. Data analysis rewards uncertainties carried to the final value. Conclusion must compare the result with accepted chemistry rather than quote a literature value. Evaluation must weigh weaknesses by their effect on the number, not list them.

faqs.question: My daughter is at a school in Al Barsha but we live in Jumeirah 3. Does the commute affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Only the start time. A bus from the Al Barsha schools back to the Jumeirah strip usually makes 4pm the earliest realistic weekday slot, and 4.30pm safer in the winter term when traffic is heavier. Nothing else changes: the tutor, the materials and the rate are the same as for a family whose child walks home in Umm Suqeim at 3.30pm. Because the session is online, a late bus costs ten minutes of the lesson rather than the whole booking, which is the usual failure mode for a visiting arrangement.

faqs.question: How many hours of Chemistry tuition does a DP2 student typically need after poor mocks?
faqs.answer: Most families in this position book eight to twelve hours over six to eight weeks, split between a repair block on the two weakest areas and timed paper work. Mechanisms and energetics usually account for the repair; equilibrium and quantitative care are handled inside paper practice. If mocks revealed a content gap across several Reactivity headings rather than a technique gap, the honest figure is higher and the first diagnostic lesson will say so. We would rather lose a booking than describe four hours as sufficient when it is not.

faqs.question: Do Dubai private schools really require Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited. For a Chemistry HL student the effect is on available homework time, which is worth counting honestly before adding a second weekly tuition slot.

faqs.question: Which UAE universities expect Chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set by each university and revised regularly, so read the programme page for the exact intake year rather than trusting any tutoring site, including this one. Broadly, medicine, pharmacy, dentistry and several engineering routes in the UAE and abroad look for Chemistry at Higher Level, often with Biology or Physics alongside. Tutoring cannot change an admissions rule, and anyone implying otherwise is selling false urgency. What a tutor can do is make HL Chemistry survivable where it is the entry requirement standing in the way.

faqs.question: What does the Chemistry data booklet change about revision?
faqs.answer: It shifts the priority from memorising values to knowing where they live and what they imply. A student with a provided booklet does not need to recall a bond enthalpy, but does need to recognise which value the question wants, read it accurately and use it with the right sign. Revision time therefore moves towards interpretation and away from rote learning, and sessions include deliberate booklet navigation under time pressure, because hunting for a value during an examination costs minutes a student needs for the extended-response answers.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Chemistry and Biology for a medicine applicant?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and for the investigation it is efficient: both subjects are marked on the same four criteria, so uncertainty handling and evaluation can be taught once and applied twice. For content, most families split the subjects after the first month, because deep organic chemistry and deep physiology compete for the same hour. We say which arrangement fits after the diagnostic rather than defaulting to two slots, and some students need only the shared investigation work alongside one subject-specific weekly session.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday Chemistry session start during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Most families on the Jumeirah strip move to a post-Iftar slot and shorten sessions to 45 or 60 minutes, which works better during fasting than a long weekend block. Some prefer a late-morning weekend session instead and drop weekday work for the month. Both are workable because nobody is driving to a lesson. What we advise against is changing tutor or format in the fortnight before a paper, when continuity is worth more than any improvement a new teaching style might bring.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Chemistry tutor before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Four questions sort most of the market. Which level and which guide version have you actually taught, and for how many cohorts? Show me how you would correct a wrong arrow in a nucleophilic substitution mechanism. Which of the four investigation criteria do students most often lose, and why? And what will you do in the first fifteen minutes with my child to find out what is wrong? Vague answers to the last two are the reliable signal, more so than any claim about qualifications.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class a reasonable alternative for Chemistry?
faqs.answer: It can work for broad revision at a lower cost per hour, with two caveats worth checking before paying. First, group size and composition: a class mixing Higher and Standard Level students teaches to the middle, and HL content is where the harder marks sit. Second, mechanisms and the investigation are individual problems, and a group cannot interrogate one student's arrows for ten minutes. Many Jumeirah 3 families use a centre for general revision and a single weekly one-to-one session for the specific repair work.

intro.heading: Why a chemistry specialist is harder to find than a maths one
paragraphs: Every subject on a Diploma timetable has a different supply curve, and chemistry sits at the thin end of it. Mathematics teachers are relatively plentiful, because mathematics is taught to every student in every school. Chemistry at Higher Level is taught to a small subset of a small subset: around 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school pupils follow the IB at all, and only some of those take chemistry, and only some of those take it at Higher Level. The pool of adults who have taught it to examination standard is correspondingly small.

Now narrow that pool to people living within a short drive of Jumeirah Golf Estates, a community of a few thousand households wrapped around two golf courses, and then narrow it again to those free at the one hour your child is neither at school nor at training in Dubai Sports City. The expected count is below one. That is not a judgement about the neighbourhood; it is what happens when you intersect three small sets.

This matters more in chemistry than in most subjects because the syllabus has specific, non-obvious conventions that a generalist does not know. The current guide is organised around Structure and Reactivity rather than the older topic numbering, and a tutor working from an outdated organisation will teach content in the wrong relationships. Mechanism answers have required conventions: curly arrows starting from the right place, lone pairs shown, intermediates drawn. The data booklet is provided in the examination and students are expected to navigate it fluently. None of that is guessable from general chemistry knowledge.

So IB Gram's answer to the question in the search box is to stop asking it geographically. Your child is matched to a chemist who teaches that level, wherever they are, and the lesson happens one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We state that before you book rather than after.

One further thing a parent should know before shortlisting anybody. Families almost always ring about organic chemistry, because it looks hardest on the page, and a marked script frequently shows the real problem one layer down: mole calculations that are not reliable under time pressure. Fixing those is four sessions and it improves energetics, equilibrium and every titration analysis at once, whereas starting with organic leaves the foundation untouched and the same marks lost in three other places.

The rest of this page is the detail you would use to test whether anyone — us or anybody else — actually knows the subject. It covers the syllabus organisation, where mechanism marks go, how the data booklet is examined, the four criteria of the internally assessed investigation, what Higher Level chemistry is actually needed for, and the market's published rates with attribution.

programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than examined, with chemistry taught either within integrated sciences or as a discipline depending on the school and the year group. Students arrive into Diploma Chemistry with reasonable inquiry skills and, frequently, thin quantitative chemistry: moles work, in particular, is often met properly for the first time in Year 12.

A student arriving from Cambridge 0620 has usually done more stoichiometry; a student arriving from the Middle Years Programme has usually done more investigation design. Both are useful and neither covers the whole gap.

programmes.name: The handover into Chemistry Higher Level
programmes.description: The cheapest intervention available in this subject. Students entering Chemistry Higher Level need secure mole calculations, confident unit conversion, and the ability to read a chemical equation as a ratio rather than as a sentence. Four sessions on stoichiometry in the summer before Year 12 removes a disproportionate share of the Year 13 repair work we are later asked for.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-gol.subjectsIntro: Chemistry divides into parts that fail in distinct ways, and a specialist can name which one a student is in from a single marked script. These are the parts tuition is actually bought for.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas calculations. The load-bearing skill in the whole subject: weakness here reappears in energetics, equilibrium and titration analysis. Usually four sessions and the highest-value block available.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energy trends and periodic behaviour, with extension at Higher Level into transition metals and complex ions. Students lose marks explaining trends in terms of size alone where the mark scheme wants nuclear charge and shielding named together.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces, shapes of molecules and hybridisation at Higher Level. The common failure is loose vocabulary: answers about bond strength where the question is about intermolecular forces, which loses the mark entirely.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess's law, bond enthalpies and, at Higher Level, entropy and Gibbs energy. Sign conventions are where the marks go, and a student who is fluent with moles finds this section considerably easier than one who is not.

subjects.name: Kinetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Rate expressions, collision theory, dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier reasoning, with rate laws and the equilibrium constant extended at Higher Level. Le Chatelier answers lose marks by stating a direction without naming the change that caused the shift.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and redox
subjects.description: pH, strong and weak behaviour, buffers and electrochemistry, extended at Higher Level into pKa calculation and electrode potentials. Buffer calculations are the single most commonly muddled Higher Level item and they are efficient to tutor because the procedure is fixed.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways and, at Higher Level, nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and the drawing conventions that carry the marks. This is where most Higher Level session count goes and where a generalist is most visibly out of their depth.

subjects.name: Spectroscopy and structure determination
subjects.description: Mass spectrometry, infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance data interpreted together to deduce a structure. Entirely dependent on fluent data-booklet use, and one of the most teachable areas in the subject once the procedure is explicit.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.description: Processing titration and calorimetry data, propagating uncertainty and judging whether a conclusion is supported. Assessed in its own right and taught unevenly, which makes two or three dedicated sessions one of the better returns in the course.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: A student-designed investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria. The high-value support is before data collection, interrogating the research question and the control of variables, and then on analysis afterwards, always as feedback on the student's own work.

sections.heading: The honest answer about local chemistry supply
paragraphs: Take the numbers seriously for a moment. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. Of the IB cohort, a fraction take chemistry; of those, a fraction take it at Higher Level. The absolute number of adults in the emirate who teach Higher Level IB Chemistry is small, and nearly all of them are employed full time at the schools that offer it.

Intersect that with Jumeirah Golf Estates and the arithmetic becomes stark. A few thousand households, and the requirement that the person be free between 6.30pm and 8.15pm on a specific weekday. Families discover this empirically, after two or three disappointing trial lessons with capable people who turn out to be teaching from a different syllabus organisation or a different board entirely.

There is a related trap. Research across sixty-odd competitor pages in this market in October 2026 found providers listing twenty-five or more schools as clients with no apparent relationship, agencies routing UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, and one page showing a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. A claim of local chemistry coverage costs a provider nothing to make and is almost impossible for a parent to check.

So the three questions worth asking anybody, including us, are concrete. Which school do you teach chemistry at, and at what level? Which parts of the current Structure and Reactivity organisation have you taught most recently? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Those answers are checkable. A pin on a map is not. The table sets out how a chemistry match typically resolves for a family in this part of New Dubai, including what we say when the answer is no.

sections.heading: Structure and Reactivity: the syllabus as it is now
paragraphs: A quick test of whether somebody knows this subject: ask how the syllabus is organised. The current guide is built in two halves. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far they go, and what the mechanisms of chemical change are. Higher Level extends within each of those areas rather than bolting on separate options.

That organisation is not cosmetic. It deliberately links ideas that the older topic-numbered structure kept apart, so a question can move from bonding to intermolecular forces to a physical property to a reaction rate inside a single extended response. A tutor teaching from the old organisation will cover the same facts in relationships the examination no longer assumes, and the student will keep being surprised by the connections questions ask for.

The practical consequence for a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent is that currency matters more in chemistry than in most subjects. Somebody who taught this course four years ago and has not taught it since knows a different course. It is a fair and non-confrontational question to ask at a trial: which parts of Structure and Reactivity have you taught in the last two years?

Confirm the detail against your school's own subject guide rather than against any tutoring page, including this one. Science guides are periodically revised, schools work from the version their cohort sits, and the version your child sits is the only one that matters.

sections.heading: Organic mechanisms: where the Higher Level grade is decided
paragraphs: If one part of Higher Level chemistry accounts for the gap between a 5 and a 7, it is organic mechanisms. The reason is that the marks are not only for knowing what happens. They are for showing it according to convention: curly arrows beginning at a lone pair or a bond rather than at an atom, arrows ending where the electron density goes, intermediates drawn with charges shown, and the distinction between homolytic and heterolytic fission made visible.

Students who have learned organic chemistry as a set of outcomes — this reagent gives that product — can answer a recall question and lose almost everything on a mechanism question, because the product was never the point. That failure mode is invisible in classwork and brutal in a mark scheme. It is also entirely fixable, because conventions are learnable in a way that intuition is not.

The second half of the work is pathway construction. A question that asks how to convert one molecule into another two steps away requires the student to hold a map of transformations and the conditions attached to each. Students who are given a pathway diagram memorise it and cannot reconstruct it; students who build their own map, badly at first, can. So a good tutor refuses to hand the map over, which is slower and works.

Spectroscopy belongs with this. Mass spectrometry, infrared and nuclear magnetic resonance data are interpreted together to deduce a structure, and the whole procedure depends on fluent use of the data booklet provided in the examination. That is the subject of the next section, and it is the part most students are quietly guessing at.

sections.heading: The data booklet is an examined skill
paragraphs: Chemistry candidates are given a data booklet in the examination containing constants, bond enthalpies, electronegativity values, spectroscopic data and acid dissociation information. Because it is provided, students and sometimes schools treat it as a safety net. The examination treats it as a tool a competent chemist uses fluently, and the difference shows up in timing.

A student who knows exactly which page holds the infrared absorption ranges, which holds the proton environments for nuclear magnetic resonance, and which holds the bond enthalpies, answers a structure-determination question in six minutes. A student who has to search answers it in fourteen, or runs out of time and guesses. That is a difference of several marks on a paper, produced by nothing more than familiarity.

There is a second-order skill as well: knowing what the booklet does not contain, so that time is not wasted looking. And a third: understanding why a value is given to a particular precision, which is what governs the significant figures in the answer. Both of those are teachable in a session and almost never taught explicitly.

A practical note on materials, because this is where some providers in this market cross a line. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, data booklets, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Tutors reference them and link to the official source, and a student should be working from the copy their school provides. A provider offering a folder containing all of it is telling you something about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks, four criteria
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation contributes 20 per cent of the chemistry grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm the current criteria and allocations with your school, because the science guides were restructured relatively recently and the version your child's cohort sits is the one that counts.

In chemistry the design criterion is where a project is usually won or lost, and it is settled before any measurement is taken. A titration-based investigation with too few concentrations, or a calorimetry investigation where heat loss cannot be controlled or even estimated, produces a capped mark that no amount of later writing improves. Three sessions at that stage, before school laboratory time is used, is a small block with a large effect.

The evaluation criterion is where otherwise strong chemists lose marks. It asks for honest, specific limitation of the method: not that more repeats would have helped, but that heat loss to the surroundings introduced a systematic error of roughly a known magnitude, and what that does to the conclusion drawn. That is a taught skill, and it is the single most coachable part of the report.

The boundary is firm. A tutor may question the research question, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, explain what each criterion rewards, mark a draft against the criteria, and teach uncertainty convention and referencing. A tutor may not write any part of the report, rewrite the student's prose, supply a research question as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line. One operator in this market was found selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Is Chemistry Higher Level actually required?
paragraphs: This question drives a lot of unnecessary stress in Jumeirah Golf Estates households, usually because an answer has been inherited from a friend rather than read from a university page. The accurate position is that it depends entirely on the degree and the institution, and that the only reliable source is the published entry requirement for the specific course under consideration.

Medicine commonly expects chemistry, often at Higher Level, and often alongside biology. Engineering more often specifies physics and mathematics. Pharmacy, dentistry and veterinary routes frequently specify chemistry. Many other degrees, including most business, humanities and design courses, do not require it at all. Students sometimes carry Chemistry Higher Level for two painful years for a plan that never needed it, which is worth checking in Year 11 rather than Year 13.

For families considering UAE universities, there is a separate process that is not a subject-choice matter and not a tutoring matter. Equivalency of the school-leaving certificate is performed by the Ministry of Education. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the American track, English requires IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB there is an equivalency figure circulating on tutoring sites and we are not repeating it, because we have not read it on a Ministry of Education source. If somebody quotes you an IB points threshold, ask where on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority it appears. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

Budget online tuition is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150, one platform listing from AED 33 to AED 52.

For chemistry the budget band is a poor match. Supervision does not resolve a mechanism convention or a buffer calculation, and the gap will not surface until a mock. The specialist band is where this subject lives, and the informative comparison is the block: four or five sessions for stoichiometry, six to eight for organic and mechanisms, two or three for data analysis, three plus two around the investigation.

In-home visits in Dubai are advertised at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with one provider publishing AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. For chemistry the premium is hard to justify, partly because of the travel and partly because mechanism work is better done on a shared screen, where arrows can be drawn, erased and redrawn where both people can see them.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach chemistry privately in the UAE
paragraphs: Because the specialist pool is so small, parents in this situation sometimes consider approaching the school directly, which makes the permit position worth knowing precisely. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted and we do not quote one.

The boundary that applies directly here: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. This is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording. Whatever the precise text, the practical rule is clear — do not engage your child's own chemistry teacher as a paid private tutor, however scarce chemists are.

And what nobody holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We also do not describe any tutor as a current IB examiner, because that status cannot be evidenced from a website and should never be implied to confer access to marking or grade boundaries.
