dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-living-legen.programmesIntro: Chemistry reaches a student here at three stages, and the sensible spend differs at each.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences marked against four criteria on a 0-8 scale. The chemistry strands build the habits the Diploma assumes: balancing equations, reasoning about particles, and explaining rather than describing. The budget or lower qualified band is appropriate here, and specialist rates are premature.
programmes.countryNote: Younger students from this community attend nearby schools in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam, with short journeys and usable afternoon time. Work at AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's estimate is both affordable and effective at this stage, which is the cheapest intervention available to a family here.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry Standard Level
programmes.description: The full conceptual range at reduced depth, with written papers and an internal assessment worth 20 per cent. Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry carry the difficulty. The qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour is usually the right level, with the specialist band reserved for the final months.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level work is more tolerant of a shorter weekday session, which matters in a community where students commute and arrive home after four. That makes it the cheaper of the two levels to support properly, not just the easier one.

programmes.name: IB Chemistry Higher Level
programmes.description: A considerably larger syllabus with extended organic chemistry, spectroscopic analysis, entropy and Gibbs free energy, plus quantitative equilibrium and kinetics. Confirm the current paper structure and weightings with the school's coordinator, since the IB science syllabuses were revised recently and no unverified figure belongs on a tutoring page.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level chemistry is a standard requirement for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering applications, which is why families here commit real budget to it. It is also where the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and upward is genuinely justified rather than merely charged.

programmes.name: The International GCSE route in
programmes.description: Most students here arrive from Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. The step up is in quantitative confidence and in the expectation that mechanisms are reasoned rather than recalled. A student who memorised reactions successfully at sixteen finds the Diploma asks why, repeatedly.
programmes.countryNote: The first Diploma term is the cheapest point at which to close that gap. By the second year the syllabus leaves no space to rebuild stoichiometric fluency, and attempting it then displaces revision the student also needs, which effectively doubles the cost of the same work.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-living-legen.subjectsIntro: Chemistry divides into blocks with distinct failure patterns and distinct costs. These notes say what each block typically takes in sessions, which is how a budget should be built.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield and gas calculations. The foundation everything quantitative rests on, so a gap here resurfaces in energetics, equilibrium and titration work. Four or five sessions, and the first thing to buy.

subjects.name: Atomic structure and periodicity
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Electron configuration, ionisation energies and periodic trends. Marks are lost on trend explanations that name the trend without the cause. Compact and inexpensive: three or four sessions typically closes it.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, intermolecular forces and molecular shapes. Students confuse bond strength with intermolecular force strength when explaining boiling points, which is the most repeated error in the strand. Three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Enthalpy changes, Hess cycles and bond enthalpies, with entropy and Gibbs free energy at Higher Level. Sign conventions are the reliable loss and they are a discipline problem, which makes this a cheap block: around three sessions.

subjects.name: Chemical kinetics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Rate, collision theory, catalysts, and rate laws and mechanisms at Higher Level. Candidates describe rate changes without reference to collision frequency or activation energy, which is what the explanation marks are for. Three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Equilibrium, acids and bases
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Le Chatelier reasoning, equilibrium constants, pH, buffers and titration curves. The common error is applying Le Chatelier loosely to a catalyst or an inert gas addition. A larger block, five or six sessions, and high value.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Oxidation states, half equations, electrolysis, and cell potentials at Higher Level. Half equations unbalanced for charge are the standard loss, and the fix is procedural practice. Three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and mechanisms
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Functional groups, reaction pathways, and at Higher Level nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition, mechanisms and spectroscopy. The largest block at six to eight sessions and the one where Higher Level grades are decided.

subjects.name: The internal assessment
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Four to six sessions, front-loaded at the research-question stage, which is where most of the band is actually determined.

sections.heading: Why chemistry costs more than mathematics to support
paragraphs: A family comparing quotes across subjects reasonably asks why chemistry sits higher. The answer is supply, and it is worth stating plainly rather than leaving as an impression that somebody is charging what they can get away with.

Mathematics is the best-supplied tutoring subject in Dubai. A great many people can teach it competently at Standard Level, and quite a few at Higher Level in both routes. Chemistry is thinner at every level and markedly thinner at Higher Level, because Higher Level cohorts at individual schools are often small. That means the number of teachers across the emirate who have taken the course through a final session recently is smaller than the number who teach science generally, and smaller again for those fluent in organic mechanisms and spectroscopy.

Scarcity does two things to price. It raises the floor, so the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 is where chemistry starts rather than where it peaks. And it compresses availability, so the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and upward is often the realistic option for Higher Level work rather than a premium upgrade. A family budgeting chemistry at mathematics rates will either not find a specialist or will end up with a generalist who cannot diagnose a mechanism loss.

The honest counterweight is that chemistry support converts efficiently when correctly sequenced, because the subject divides into blocks with identifiable failures and finite work attached. A well-chosen six-session organic block does more than a term of general revision, which means the higher hourly rate can still produce a lower total cost. sections.heading: Three purchases, in the order that returns most
paragraphs: Chemistry budgets fail from sequencing more often than from rate. A family buys weekly general support in September, continues it until March, and finds the grade roughly where it started. The sessions were not wasted exactly, but they were spent on coverage when the student needed three specific things in a specific order.

First purchase: a diagnosis. Two or three sessions working from marked papers, identifying whether the loss is quantitative, conventional, linguistic or organic. This is cheap, fast and it determines everything after it. A family that skips it is paying a specialist to guess, which is the most expensive form of guessing available.

Second purchase: the foundation, if that is where the diagnosis points. Stoichiometry and the mole underpin energetics, equilibrium, titration work and much of organic analysis, so a gap there resurfaces everywhere and makes every later block slower. Four or five sessions closes it in most cases. Students and parents resist this because it feels like going backwards, and it is the single highest-return block in the course.

Third purchase: organic chemistry, which at Higher Level is where the grade is decided. Six to eight sessions taught as a procedure rather than a memory task. Only after those three does general revision earn its rate, and by then the student needs much less of it, which is the point: correct sequencing reduces the total number of hours rather than merely rearranging them. sections.heading: What the organic block actually buys
paragraphs: Of all the chemistry purchases available, the organic block is the one most worth understanding before paying for it, because it is the largest and the most frequently mis-taught. At Higher Level organic chemistry carries a disproportionate share of both content and difficulty, and it behaves unlike the rest of the course.

The mistake students make is treating it as material to memorise. There are too many reactions, and the papers do not ask for recall; they ask candidates to apply a mechanism to a molecule they have not seen before. What a student needs instead is a small set of rules about where electrons come from and where they go, drilled on unfamiliar substrates until the pattern is automatic. Nucleophilic substitution, electrophilic addition and carbonyl behaviour all follow from the same handful of ideas.

Marks are then lost in the drawing rather than the thinking, which is why this block converts so reliably. Arrows that start from an atom rather than from a bond or a lone pair. Charges omitted from intermediates. A mechanism chemically correct and incompletely annotated. These are conventions, and conventions can be taught in a defined number of sessions, which is what makes a six-to-eight session block a purchase with a predictable return rather than an open-ended commitment.

The second half of the Higher Level organic challenge is synthesis and spectroscopy: building a route to a target molecule and interpreting spectra to identify a structure. Both reward working backwards from the answer, a technique students rarely discover alone. A tutor who teaches that habit changes how a student reads the entire paper, not only the organic questions, which is why this block often improves performance in strands nobody targeted.

sections.heading: The costs a gated community adds and nobody quotes
paragraphs: Any in-home quote for Living Legends carries costs that do not appear in the hourly figure, and a family comparing options should add them in. A visiting tutor must clear a gate, which depending on the arrangement means pre-registration by the household, being met, collecting a pass, or waiting while security confirms. Then parking. Then locating the villa or tower entrance in a community arranged around a golf course.

The direct cost is teaching minutes. A session booked for six that begins at ten past has delivered fifty minutes against a sixty-minute fee. At two sessions a week across roughly thirty-six school weeks, consistent ten-minute losses come to about twelve hours of tuition paid for and not received. At the in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour that is a substantial figure, and it arrives in pieces small enough that most families never total it.

The indirect costs are reliability and choice. A specialist delayed on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at twenty past has effectively halved a session, and that recurs often enough to erode an arrangement by the second term. Meanwhile the pool of chemistry specialists willing to make this journey twice a week at the contested evening hour is very small, so a family chooses from fewer people and pays the top of the band to those who agree.

Set against that, in-home has a legitimate case for some students: a child under roughly Year 5, or a student with significant attention difficulties, for whom physical presence does real work. A Diploma chemistry student working through mechanisms and spectra on a screen is not in that category. IB Gram does not sell UAE home visits at all, so this is reported as the market rather than offered; the service exists only in India.

sections.heading: Budgeting chemistry across two Diploma years
paragraphs: Families want a total, and the honest way to build one is to price the blocks rather than multiply a monthly figure by twenty-four months. Chemistry suits that approach because the blocks are discrete and finite, which is unusual among Diploma subjects and should be used.

Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give the reference points: AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. Market packages include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. For a two-year Diploma those monthly figures compound quickly if left as a standing arrangement.

A block-based plan looks different and usually costs less. A diagnosis and a foundation block in the first year. An organic block in the second. An internal assessment block placed around the school's deadline, ideally inside a holiday. A pre-session technique run in the final months. Between those, nothing, or a lighter weekly slot if the student benefits from the rhythm. That plan has gaps in it on purpose, and the gaps are where the student consolidates independently, which is the part that actually produces the grade.

A standing weekly arrangement across both Diploma years is the right choice in one situation: where a student needs the external structure to work at all. That is a legitimate reason and it should be chosen deliberately rather than drifted into. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the following academic year, which makes tuition the variable line in a household education budget and worth deciding on purpose.

sections.heading: Where chemistry money is wasted in this community
paragraphs: Four patterns recur, and all four are avoidable with information a family already has or can obtain free. None of them is about being overcharged per hour.

The first is buying general revision before a diagnosis. It is the default purchase in this market, it bills monthly, and it converts slowly because most of the hours address content the student already holds. The second is paying the in-home premium for a Diploma student, which in a gated community buys a journey, a gate wait and a reduced choice of specialist.

The third is buying the organic block before the foundation. Organic chemistry at Higher Level leans on quantitative confidence and on comfort with structure and bonding, so a student without secure stoichiometry struggles through an expensive block that would have been straightforward two months later. The fourth is leaving the internal assessment until the drafting stage, by which point the research question is fixed and most of the band is already determined.

There is a fifth that is specific to high-stakes subjects. Paying a premium for claimed examiner status without evidence. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and any suggestion that examiner status grants access to marking, boundaries or paper content should end a conversation rather than justify a higher rate. What genuinely predicts usefulness is recent experience of teaching the course at the student's level, which costs nothing to ask about and can be checked in a single conversation before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: What no chemistry budget can buy
paragraphs: A page about cost should state where money stops working, because the alternative implies that spending and outcome are the same variable.

No provider can promise a grade, at any band. Grades depend on the work the student does between sessions, on what a particular session's papers ask, and on where boundaries fall, and nobody selling tuition controls any of those. We publish no grade promise, no improvement promise and no refund tied to an outcome. We publish no satisfaction or results statistic either, because a figure without the number of students, the date and the method is not evidence, and most such figures in this market carry none of the three.

No budget buys assessed work, and this matters more in chemistry than almost anywhere because the internal assessment is a fifth of the grade. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum. That is an IB malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, whose diploma can be withheld. A tutor may test a research question, explain criteria, teach uncertainty treatment and graphing, read a draft the student wrote and show where it loses marks, and model an analysis on different data. A tutor must never conduct the investigation or write the report.

No budget buys board material either. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets and grade boundary tables are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice. And no amount of tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for a university place or for school progression; any page implying otherwise is manufacturing pressure around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and honest availability
paragraphs: One cost should be zero and occasionally is not. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system. A licensing line item in any quote is charging for something free.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any amount quoted anywhere is unverified. There is also a conduct rule worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise. That reporting is press-sourced, so verify against the current ADEK document.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

On availability, Standard Level chemistry matches quickly and Higher Level matches well but not instantly. The narrowest request is a Higher Level organic specialist for a short-notice pre-session block, and where none is free we give a date rather than putting a near-fit in front of a final-year student. No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere. Specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates, and nobody is sent to a UAE address.

faqs.question: Why does an IB chemistry tutor cost more than a maths tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Supply rather than marketing. Mathematics is the best-supplied tutoring subject here, with many competent teachers at Standard Level and a reasonable number at Higher Level. Chemistry is thinner at every level and markedly thinner at Higher Level, because Higher Level cohorts at individual schools are often small, so the pool of teachers who have taken the course through a final session recently is small city-wide. Scarcity raises the floor, which is why the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 is where chemistry starts rather than peaks.

faqs.question: What should a Living Legends family buy first for chemistry?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, and it is the cheapest purchase available. Two or three sessions working from marked papers establishes whether the loss is quantitative, conventional, linguistic or organic, and that answer determines everything after it. Buying general weekly revision first is the default in this market and converts slowly, because most of the hours address content the student already holds. A family that skips the diagnosis is paying a specialist rate for guesswork, which is the most expensive form of guessing on offer.

faqs.question: How much is the organic chemistry block likely to cost?
faqs.answer: Six to eight sessions is the usual size, at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and upward per hour for Higher Level work, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate putting examination-year specialist support at AED 200 to 450 plus. It is the largest single chemistry purchase and the most reliable, because mechanisms are a procedural skill taught through explicit rules about where electrons come from, and the marks lost are drawing conventions rather than understanding. It also improves performance in strands nobody targeted.

faqs.question: Is stoichiometry worth paying for if it feels like going backwards?
faqs.answer: It is the highest-return block in the course. Moles, concentration, limiting reagents and gas calculations underpin energetics, equilibrium, titration work and much of organic analysis, so a weakness there resurfaces everywhere and makes every later block slower and therefore more expensive. Four or five sessions closes it in most cases. Students and parents resist it because it looks like revisiting earlier material, and skipping it is why expensive organic blocks sometimes disappoint.

faqs.question: What does an in-home chemistry visit really cost in a gated community?
faqs.answer: More than the quoted rate. In-home tuition is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and on top of that premium the gate and the arterial road remove minutes. A session booked for six that starts at ten past is a sixty-minute fee for fifty minutes. At two sessions a week across thirty-six school weeks, consistent losses of that size approach twelve hours of tuition bought and not received.

faqs.question: How should we budget chemistry across both Diploma years?
faqs.answer: By pricing blocks rather than multiplying a monthly figure by twenty-four. A diagnosis and a foundation block in the first year, an organic block in the second, an internal assessment block around the school's deadline, and a short pre-session technique run. Between those, gaps on purpose, because that is where the student consolidates independently. Bestimate's monthly reference points are AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support, which compounds fast if left standing.

faqs.question: Is a weekly chemistry slot across two years ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one situation: where a student needs external structure to work at all. That is a legitimate reason and it should be chosen deliberately rather than drifted into, because the cost across two Diploma years is substantial. For a student who works independently between sessions, a block plan achieves more for less, since chemistry divides cleanly into discrete pieces with finite work attached. The honest test is whether work actually happens in the gaps.

faqs.question: Should we pay more for a tutor who says they are an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence of current status, and not at all if the claim implies inside access. Examiner status does not grant access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content, and anybody suggesting otherwise is making a claim that should end the conversation rather than justify a premium. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners where current status cannot be evidenced. What genuinely predicts usefulness is recent experience of teaching the course at the student's level, which is checkable.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade is the internal assessment worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent in all IB science courses, with the written papers carrying the remaining 80 per cent. The exact number of papers and the split between them should be confirmed with the school's coordinator, since the IB science syllabuses were revised recently and no unverified figure belongs on a tutoring page. Practically, that 20 per cent has a fixed school deadline and is the part a student most directly controls, which is why it deserves budget earlier than most families allocate it.

faqs.question: When is internal assessment support worth paying for?
faqs.answer: At the research-question stage, well before drafting. Most of the band is decided by whether the question produces data with measurable variation and whether the uncertainty will swamp the effect being measured. One session testing that protects a term of work. Support bought at the drafting stage, which is when most families think of it, arrives after the decisive choice has been made. Four to six sessions placed around the school's deadline, ideally inside a holiday, is the usual shape.

faqs.question: Will any provider refund us if the chemistry grade does not improve?
faqs.answer: No reputable one should offer that, and we do not. A refund tied to an outcome is a promise with no mechanism, because grades depend on the work done between sessions, on what the papers ask and on where boundaries fall. What protects a family's money instead is a free full-length trial lesson with no card, a per-session arrangement rather than a locked package, and a written diagnostic to measure progress against. Those are checkable commitments rather than claims.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level chemistry justify the specialist rate for medicine applications?
faqs.answer: For most families aiming at medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or chemical engineering, yes, because Higher Level chemistry is a standard requirement and the grade usually needs to be specific. What a tutoring page should not do is state a threshold for any particular university, because those vary and change; check published entry requirements directly in the first Diploma year. The budget conclusion is that the organic block and the internal assessment are the two purchases least worth economising on in that situation.

faqs.question: Will the fee include past papers and the data booklet?
faqs.answer: No, because those are not ours to supply. The IB data booklet, syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued to the student, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. A provider advertising a paper library is offering an unresolved problem rather than value.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Higher Level chemistry specialist be booked from here?
faqs.answer: Standard Level matches quickly and Higher Level matches well but not instantly, with the contested half past five to seven weekday window usually the limiting factor rather than the subject. Shifting twenty minutes later or taking a weekend morning normally resolves it. The narrowest request in this subject is a Higher Level organic specialist for a short-notice pre-session block, and where none is genuinely free we give a date rather than putting a near-fit in front of a final-year Diploma student.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-meydan.tutorsIntro: The profiles below teach Diploma Chemistry as it is now assessed, including the data-based section of Paper 1 and the four published investigation criteria. Each works one-to-one online in a slot that survives a Meydan weekday, and you meet the person before any payment.

intro.heading: The question behind the search is not distance
paragraphs: A parent typing this search is usually asking one thing: is there anybody near us who genuinely knows this course. It is a fair question and the honest answer is uncomfortable. Diploma Chemistry was restructured, and the content a student meets now is organised into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3 rather than the numbered topic list that preceded it. The assessment changed with it. Paper 1 now contains a data-based section alongside the multiple-choice section, and the old practical scheme of work and group project have gone, replaced by a single scientific investigation marked against four published criteria.

None of that is obscure. It is in the subject guide and every chemistry teacher in a Nad Al Sheba school works to it daily. The trouble is that a large part of the tutoring market does not. A tutor who taught Diploma Chemistry competently five years ago, has not taught it since, and advertises on the strength of that experience will describe a paper structure your child does not sit. They will often be an excellent chemist. They will still send a DP2 student into a data-based section they have never practised.

Distance is almost irrelevant to this problem and Meydan makes that unusually clear. There is no secondary school inside Meydan. The cohort sits in Nad Al Sheba, where North London Collegiate School Dubai, Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Kent College Dubai are clustered, or across Ras Al Khor Road at Hartland International School and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. Whether a tutor lives ten minutes from your villa or in a different time zone has no bearing on whether they know what criterion D asks for. The second fact bears on your child's grade. The first does not.

So this page is built around verification rather than reassurance. There is a section that gives you three questions to put to any chemistry tutor, ours included, with the answers you should expect. There is a component-by-component map of where the marks sit. There is an honest account of where Meydan students actually lose chemistry marks, which is less about memory than about the way long-answer credit is awarded. And there is a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not touch on the investigation, because that boundary is where the real risk in this subject lives.

On delivery: IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. That service runs only in India. Chemistry support for Meydan families is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, a past paper visible to both sides and a recording the student keeps. The reason is the same reason the syllabus question matters. The people who know this course well are a small group, and selecting from them on the basis of who can cross Ras Al Khor Road by six o'clock throws away the only criterion that counts.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-meydan.programmesIntro: Chemistry sits inside a programme, and the programme sets what a tutor should be able to describe without hesitating. A Meydan family may be at any point from an MYP sciences class to a DP2 student with an investigation deadline on the horizon.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Chemistry
programmes.description: Assessed on Paper 1, Paper 2 and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 holds a multiple-choice section and a data-based section; Paper 2 is structured long answer and carries 44%. The content is organised under Structure, covering models of the particulate nature of matter and bonding, and Reactivity, covering what drives and controls reactions. Higher Level runs to 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard, with the extra depth loaded onto energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms.
programmes.countryNote: In Meydan this is what most families are looking for, since the Nad Al Sheba IB schools run the full continuum. Ask the school which section the class is currently inside, then ask a prospective tutor to describe it. The two answers should match without translation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Sciences is marked against four criteria out of eight each, covering knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on science in context. No external chemistry paper exists. The practical consequence is that a student can hold a strong MYP science grade with limited stoichiometric fluency, because criterion A rewards explanation and the Diploma rewards a calculation that survives scrutiny.
programmes.countryNote: Meydan students at the continuum schools in Nad Al Sheba usually discover this in the first term of DP1. A short block on moles, concentration and limiting reagents in MYP 5 is the most efficient chemistry help a Dubai family can buy, and it is almost never bought then.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry as the entry route
programmes.description: Many Meydan students arrive at Diploma Chemistry from Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 rather than the MYP, often after Years 10 and 11 at Repton School Dubai or Kent College Dubai. IGCSE chemistry rewards recall of reactions and trends; the Diploma asks why a trend exists and demands that the reasoning be visible. A student who scored highly through memorisation frequently finds DP1 tests marking them down for answers they consider correct.
programmes.countryNote: For families on this route the useful purchase is a short bridging block over the summer before DP1, not a term of rescue work in November. Dubai providers charge their usual rate in July for work that is substantially easier then.

programmes.name: Certificate and Career-related study
programmes.description: A smaller group takes Diploma Chemistry as a single certificate course or alongside the Career-related Programme. The subject assessment is identical, investigation included, but without Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay the weekly load looks very different and a sensible tutoring commitment is correspondingly lighter.
programmes.countryNote: For a Meydan household this usually means one subject needs attention rather than a whole timetable, so the honest recommendation is a short block and a review rather than a standing weekly slot.

sections.heading: Three questions that reveal whether a tutor knows this course
paragraphs: You do not need to be a chemist to test this. You need three questions and the patience to listen to the shape of the answer rather than its confidence. Ask first how the course content is organised. The answer you want describes Structure and Reactivity, three sections each, covering models of matter and bonding on one side and what drives and controls reactions on the other. An answer that recites numbered topics from the previous structure is describing a course your child is not sitting, and the person giving it has not opened the current subject guide.

Ask second what sits inside Paper 1. The answer should mention both the multiple-choice section and the data-based section, because Paper 1 is no longer a single multiple-choice exercise and the data-based questions are where procedural marks are won and lost. A tutor who treats Paper 1 as pure multiple choice will drill content recall and never touch uncertainty, significant figures or graph interpretation, which is a systematic gap rather than an oversight.

Ask third what the internal assessment is and how it is marked. The current answer is a single scientific investigation, 24 marks across four criteria of six, roughly a fifth of the subject grade, with a 3,000-word ceiling and a deadline set by the school rather than by the IB. A tutor who mentions a practical scheme of work or a group project is working from a scheme that has been replaced. That matters practically: it is the difference between advising your child on a report that exists and one that does not.

Put all three to us as well. The reason this page opens with a test rather than a claim is that every provider in this market writes the same adjectives, and a parent cannot distinguish between them on copy. Three questions and ten minutes on a free trial call distinguishes them completely. Keep the answers in writing if you can, because a tutor who gives a vague answer in conversation tends to give a precise one once it is being recorded.

sections.heading: Where the chemistry marks actually sit
paragraphs: Paper 2 is the largest pot of marks in the subject at 44% of the grade, and it is structured long answer. The published mark schemes award credit in pieces: the principle stated, the substitution shown, the conclusion drawn. A student who writes a correct final value with no visible reasoning collects a fraction of what was available, and this is the most common single reason a confident chemist underperforms on paper. It is also the most tutorable thing in the subject, and the part cheap tutoring touches least, because marking a long answer properly takes longer than teaching the content did.

Paper 1 carries 36% and does two jobs. The multiple-choice section penalises speed and misread stems rather than ignorance; most students fix it by sitting timed sets alone. The data-based section is different. It asks for uncertainty treatment, gradient work, unit handling and judgement about anomalies, and those are procedural skills that transfer directly to the investigation. A revision plan that treats Paper 1 as one block almost always drills the half that needs no help.

The scientific investigation holds the remaining 20%. Four criteria, six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The school marks it and the school sets the deadline. Criterion D, evaluation, is where marks most reliably disappear, because students name a limitation without explaining what effect it had on the result. That is a teachable move and a single session can change it, provided a draft already exists for the conversation to be about.

The upshot for a Meydan family planning a year is that the money should move. DP1 is content plus one or two investigation reviews. The mock window buys diagnosis. DP2 buys timed Paper 2 marking and data-based practice. A household that keeps buying the same sixty-minute content hour for two years will spend more and get less than one that changes format twice.

sections.heading: Where Meydan students lose chemistry marks, specifically
paragraphs: Organic mechanisms are the most common collapse point, and the reason is diagnosable. Students learn the products of a reaction and not the movement of electrons, so they can state what forms but not justify why, and Higher Level questions ask for the justification. The repair is mechanical rather than mysterious: draw the mechanism repeatedly, with the curly arrows placed and explained, until the pattern generalises. It is slow work and it responds well to a weekly hour, which makes it one of the better uses of money in the whole course.

Equilibrium and energetics fail differently. Here students can usually do the calculation and cannot explain the direction of a shift in words that earn the mark. A question asking why a yield changes when the temperature rises wants the enthalpy change referenced and the shift stated as a consequence. Students write the conclusion and omit the because, and the mark scheme pays for the because. Once a student has seen three marked examples of their own writing fail on this point, it generally stops happening.

Acids, bases and the pH family cause trouble for a reason that is not chemical. The mathematics of logarithms frequently arrives in the chemistry class before the maths class has covered it properly, so a student who understands the chemistry stalls on the arithmetic and concludes they do not understand the chemistry. This is why Chemistry and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are so often tutored together in Dubai, and why a chemistry tutor who notices the real problem is worth more than one who drills pH questions.

Finally there is the school-specific element. The Nad Al Sheba schools and the Hartland schools run different internal calendars, so two Meydan students in the same community can be examined on different sections in the same month. A tutor who asks which section the class is inside, rather than assuming a standard sequence, avoids a term of teaching slightly ahead or slightly behind the class. That single question is worth asking in the first session.

sections.heading: Does a nearby tutor beat a specialist on a screen?
paragraphs: This is the trade the search is really about, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales one. A tutor who lives in Nad Al Sheba or District One can sit at your table, which is genuinely valuable for a younger student who will not work without a person present. For a DP2 chemistry student, the thing that moves the grade is somebody who can look at a marked Paper 2 answer and say precisely which of the available marks was not earned and why. Those two qualities are unrelated, and in a pool this small they rarely coexist in the same person within driving distance.

Meydan sharpens it further. The drive in from Al Quoz or along Al Khail Road between four and six o'clock is substantial, so a local tutor's earliest offer is often later than the hour a family wants, and the set of specialists who clear both the subject bar and the commute bar is very small. Online delivery removes the commute from the selection criteria and leaves only the subject bar, which is the one that affects the grade. That is the argument in full. It is logistical, not technological.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and that is worth saying before a parent spends time asking. Home visits are a service we run only in India. What we sell to Meydan families is one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time: shared whiteboard, the same past paper on both screens, mechanisms drawn as they are explained, and a recording the student can return to the night before a test. A kitchen table does one thing better, which is hold a reluctant student still. Both facts are true and you should weigh them rather than be sold one.

The market prices the difference openly enough. Published Dubai rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's table showing 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking 200 to 500. The spread between the two formats is travel. Unitors states an IB rate from AED 200 and TutorChase lists AED 270; those are their published figures, read in October 2026, and not ours.

sections.heading: What a chemistry tutor may and may not touch on the investigation
paragraphs: The scientific investigation must be the student's own work. The school authenticates it, it carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade, and a breach is an academic-honesty matter whose consequences land on the student rather than the tutor. Stating the boundary precisely is therefore not legal decoration. It is the most useful thing a provider can publish about this part of the course, and in a search results page where one competitor advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price, it is also a meaningful difference.

A tutor may teach the chemistry the investigation depends on. A tutor may ask whether a research question can be answered with the apparatus available in a school laboratory, whether the independent variable is genuinely controllable, and whether the planned range will produce a trend worth analysing at all. A tutor may explain what criterion B expects from uncertainty and anomaly treatment, show the published criteria wording, and read the student's own draft to say which criterion is not yet satisfied. A tutor may point at an evaluation paragraph and note that a limitation has been named without its effect being explained.

A tutor may not select the research question, write or part-write the report, supply data, redraw the student's graphs, rewrite a conclusion or edit a draft into a finished state. IB Gram provides none of those things and will decline to. If a provider in this market has quoted you a price for a completed investigation, that is what is being sold, and the exposure it creates for your child is worth understanding before any money changes hands.

The same line runs through the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Questioning, teaching and feedback on the student's own work are legitimate and genuinely valuable. Production is not, and no amount of careful wording changes that.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and what a parent can verify alone
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every school a Meydan chemistry student attends falls under it. The national picture is wider than most tutoring pages admit: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

Tutoring itself is a different file. The private tuition work permit comes from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services system. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so nobody should be quoting you one.

That gives a Meydan parent a second cheap verification to run alongside the syllabus questions. Ask any prospective chemistry tutor, ours included, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, and ask to see it. It is free to obtain, so there is no reason for a working tutor to lack one. Separately, a provider operating from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which has its own initial-approval step, a six-month window to complete the licence steps and an annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

For the avoidance of doubt: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this site should be read as claiming one. We are an independent platform matching families with subject specialists and teaching online. Explaining what a regulator does is useful. Implying it stands behind us would not be.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside a Diploma science load
paragraphs: A Meydan family running a Diploma timetable is also running a mandatory one, and it takes real space out of the week. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a DP1 student already carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and a chemistry investigation, those periods are the reason the evening is narrower than the timetable suggests.

The organisation rules are explicit. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Social Studies for Arab students is taught primarily in Arabic, while non-Arabs take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold the appropriate KHDA approval.

Timing is counted in 40-minute lesson units. Schools may vary the length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. There is a content constraint too: for these subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which rules out the supplementary-workbook approach a family might sensibly take in chemistry.

The practical conclusion is about scheduling rather than content. Map the whole week, including the mandatory periods and whatever sport or activity the student does, before choosing a chemistry slot. A slot chosen from the full picture survives the term; one chosen from the chemistry timetable alone usually gets moved three times and then dropped.

sections.heading: Starting from Meydan, with the limits said out loud
paragraphs: Begin with a conversation rather than a booking. Tell us the school in Nad Al Sheba or across Ras Al Khor Road, the level, which section the class is currently inside, the current grades and the hour that genuinely works. We will say whether a Diploma Chemistry specialist is free in that window. If the answer is no, you get the no, because the alternative is a generalist at a specialist rate and that is the substitution this market makes most often.

Then take the free trial lesson with the person who would actually teach your child. There is no card, no commitment and no automatic enrolment. Use it to run the three questions from earlier in this page. A tutor who names the six sections, describes both halves of Paper 1 and explains the four investigation criteria without prompting has told you more in five minutes than any provider's copy can.

Coverage limits are worth saying plainly because nobody else does. The group of people who can teach the current Diploma Chemistry course and mark its long-answer papers accurately is small, and the late-afternoon Gulf window is the most requested in the country. Sometimes the honest answer is a different hour, sometimes a different day, sometimes a fortnight's wait. You will get which, with a date.

After that the working pattern is simple and deliberately unexciting. Weekly sessions aimed at a named target, a written note each time, a format review twice a year, and an explicit decision after the mock window about moving from content work to timed paper marking. The plan drives the money rather than the calendar driving it.

faqs.question: Is there actually anyone near Meydan who knows the current IB Chemistry course?
faqs.answer: Proximity is the wrong filter, and in Meydan it is an especially poor one because there is no secondary school inside the community. The real question is whether a tutor can describe the content as Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, name both halves of Paper 1, and explain the four investigation criteria. People who can do that are a small group nationally, and restricting them to those who can drive to your villa by six o'clock makes the group much smaller without improving it. We select on the syllabus answer and teach online.

faqs.question: How can a parent who is not a chemist check a tutor's syllabus knowledge?
faqs.answer: Three questions, no chemistry required. Ask how the content is organised; you want Structure and Reactivity, three sections each. Ask what is inside Paper 1; you want both the multiple-choice and the data-based sections named. Ask what the internal assessment is; you want one scientific investigation, 24 marks over four criteria, a 3,000-word ceiling and a school-set deadline. An answer that lists numbered topics, calls Paper 1 pure multiple choice, or mentions a group project is describing a course your child does not sit.

faqs.question: What changed when the Diploma Chemistry course was reorganised?
faqs.answer: The content was regrouped under Structure, which covers models of the particulate nature of matter and bonding, and Reactivity, which covers what drives and controls reactions, replacing the previous numbered topic list. Paper 1 gained a data-based section alongside the multiple-choice section. The old practical scheme of work and group project were replaced by a single scientific investigation marked against four published criteria. None of that is obscure to a school teacher, but a tutor who last taught the subject under the previous guide will describe the wrong paper structure confidently.

faqs.question: Why does my child get the right answer in chemistry and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 2 pays for reasoning, not for answers. It carries 44% of the grade and the mark schemes award credit separately for the principle stated, the substitution shown and the conclusion drawn. A correct final value with no visible working collects a fraction of what was available. This is the most fixable problem in the subject and the one cheap tutoring addresses least, because marking a long answer properly takes longer than teaching the content did. Sit a timed section, then mark it with the student watching.

faqs.question: Is the data-based part of Paper 1 worth tutoring separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is routinely skipped. Paper 1 carries 36% and contains two unrelated challenges. The multiple-choice section responds to timed practice a student can do alone. The data-based section asks for uncertainty treatment, gradient work, unit handling and judgement about anomalies, which are procedural skills that also transfer straight into the investigation. A revision block aimed at Paper 1 as a single entity almost always drills content and leaves the procedural half untouched, so ask for it to be timetabled explicitly.

faqs.question: My child understands organic chemistry in class and collapses in tests. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the products have been learnt and the electron movement has not. A student can state what forms without being able to justify why, and Higher Level questions ask for the justification. The repair is unglamorous and reliable: draw mechanisms repeatedly, with curly arrows placed and explained aloud, until the pattern generalises across reaction types. It is slow work that suits a weekly hour, which makes it one of the better-value purchases in the course. Expect several weeks rather than one session.

faqs.question: Is a pH problem in chemistry really a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes. Logarithms turn up in the chemistry class on acids and bases before the mathematics course has covered them securely, so a student who grasps the chemistry stalls on the arithmetic and concludes the chemistry is beyond them. A tutor who spots that treats the algebra directly rather than drilling more pH questions. It is one of the main reasons Chemistry and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are tutored together so often in Dubai, and it is worth raising in the first session.

faqs.question: How much of the chemistry grade does the scientific investigation carry?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth of the subject grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report has a 3,000-word ceiling, the school marks it, and the school sets the submission deadline rather than the IB. Criterion D, evaluation, is where marks most reliably disappear, because students name a limitation without explaining what effect it had on the result. That is teachable, and often a single session once a draft exists is enough to change it.

faqs.question: May a chemistry tutor suggest my child's investigation research question?
faqs.answer: No. The student chooses it. A tutor may question whether the chosen question can be answered with school apparatus, whether the independent variable is genuinely controllable and whether the planned range will produce a trend worth analysing, and those questions are where most of the value sits. What a tutor may not do is select the question, supply data, redraw graphs, write any part of the report or edit a draft into a finished state. IB Gram provides none of those. The school authenticates the work and the consequence of a breach falls on your child.

faqs.question: Does a Meydan family get a better chemistry tutor by paying for home visits?
faqs.answer: You get a person in the room, which matters for a younger or reluctant student and does not by itself improve subject depth. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutoring, and the spread is travel. Meydan adds a specific cost: the approach from Al Quoz or Al Khail Road between four and six means a local tutor's earliest offer is usually later than you wanted. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

faqs.question: Which schools do Meydan chemistry students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Meydan has no school inside it, so the cohort forms elsewhere. The nearest belt is Nad Al Sheba, with North London Collegiate School Dubai, Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Kent College Dubai within a short drive. Across Ras Al Khor Road families use Hartland International School, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, Deira International School and Dubai English Speaking College. Each sets its own investigation deadline and works through the course sections in its own order. These schools are named as context only; no affiliation is implied.

faqs.question: Does the course section my child's class is on actually matter to a tutor?
faqs.answer: It matters more than almost anything else in the first session. Schools in this corridor sequence the six sections differently, so two Meydan students in the same community can be assessed on different material in the same month. A tutor who asks which section the class is inside can align with the school's teaching; one who assumes a standard order spends a term slightly ahead or slightly behind, which feels like poor teaching to the student and is really a planning failure. Ask your science coordinator and pass the answer on.

faqs.question: Can you promise my child a 7 in Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, and treat any provider who does with suspicion. Nobody controls the paper, the mark scheme, the grade boundaries or the amount of work a student does between sessions, so a promised grade is a sales device rather than a professional judgement. What a tutor can do is name the specific gap, evidence it from a marked script and say what closing it would take in hours. Several pages in this market publish outcome percentages with no sample size, date or method attached. Ask for the method and see what arrives.

faqs.question: Does an online chemistry tutor need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason for a tutor working with UAE families to lack one, so ask to see it. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions a week does a Higher Level student need?
faqs.answer: One well-aimed hour is the normal starting point, and the honest answer is that frequency matters less than target. A weekly hour on organic mechanisms through the autumn of DP2 does more than two scattered hours covering whatever came up that week. Around the mock window the useful shape changes: one ninety-minute timed section with the marking done together usually beats two sixty-minute content lessons. Expect to change format twice across the two years rather than to increase frequency, and read the session notes before you decide.

faqs.question: What if no Diploma Chemistry specialist is free in our Meydan slot?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. The group of people who teach the current Structure and Reactivity course and mark its long-answer papers accurately is small, and the late-afternoon Gulf window is the most requested in the country. Sometimes the answer is another hour, sometimes another weekday, sometimes a fortnight's wait. What we will not do is put a generalist in the slot and charge the specialist rate for them. No competitor page we examined in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Mizhar: the Chemistry tutor problem is identical in all three
paragraphs: Parents in Mirdif usually start this search after a mock. The Chemistry grade comes back a 4 or a 5, the student insists they revised, and nobody in the house can tell whether the problem is the content, the command terms or the data questions. The next step is a Google search for an IB Chemistry tutor in Mirdif, and the results look reassuringly local. Most of them are not. Scroll the listings and you find agency pages that name every Dubai community in a footer, freelance adverts posted from Al Nahda, and marketplaces quoting US dollars.

The honest position is worth stating early, because it changes what you should be comparing. Dubai's IB Diploma Chemistry teaching pool is concentrated where the IB schools are concentrated, and that is mostly the western and central corridor: Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim, Nad Al Sheba, Dubai Hills. Mirdif has strong schools, but it sits on the eastern side of the city, and a tutor who lives in Al Barsha is looking at a 35 to 50 minute drive each way at 4pm. That tutor either declines, or charges for the travel, or arrives at 5:30pm when your child is already tired.

Now cross Algeria Street into Al Warqa, or carry on to Al Mizhar or Al Khawaneej. The arithmetic does not change. The same handful of Chemistry HL specialists are the same distance away; the drive is five minutes longer or shorter and the premium is the same. This is the point of this page. Families often assume their area is uniquely badly served and that moving the search one neighbourhood over will turn up someone better. It will not, because the constraint is not your postcode. The constraint is how few people in this city teach Diploma Chemistry to examination standard.

Once you accept that, the sensible question changes from "who is near me" to "who actually knows this syllabus". That is a question online tuition answers properly. IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB Chemistry tuition to Mirdif over live video, which means the tutor is selected for the course your child sits rather than for the road between their flat and yours. A student taking Chemistry HL with a weak grasp of equilibrium gets a tutor who teaches equilibrium, not whoever was free and local. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only.

The rest of this page compares the two options properly, with the AED figures the rest of this market refuses to publish, the assessment structure your child is being marked against, and a Diploma year counted backwards from the examination session so you can see where the next eight weeks have to go. dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: Mirdif families arrive at Diploma Chemistry by several routes. Some children come through a full IB continuum school, some transfer in from IGCSE at a British-curriculum school in the eastern suburbs, and some arrive mid-DP1 from abroad. The three programmes below are the ones that matter for this page, and each one needs a different first lesson.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma is where Chemistry becomes a named, externally examined subject at Higher or Standard Level. Students sit Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, and Paper 2, which is structured and extended response. Alongside the papers sits the scientific investigation, an independent piece of practical work worth a fifth of the final grade. The Diploma also carries Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, which compete for the same evenings as Chemistry revision.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB cohort is a minority of the private-school population at roughly 7%, which is precisely why Diploma Chemistry teachers are thin on the ground in the eastern suburbs. Mirdif students more often sit the Diploma at a school a drive away rather than at the end of their own street, so timetables vary by school and so does the internal deadline for the investigation draft.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria rather than against papers, and that difference catches Mirdif students out when they reach DP1. A child can score a 7 in MYP Science on strong investigations and reflective writing, then meet Diploma Chemistry Paper 1 and discover they have never been asked to answer forty multiple-choice questions in ninety minutes. The repair work is mechanical: calculation fluency, moles, mark-scheme literacy and timed practice.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Mirdif and Al Mizhar run MYP to Year 11 and then offer both the Diploma and A Levels. Families in the eastern suburbs therefore face a real choice at 16, and the Chemistry question is a large part of it. A student who liked MYP Science for the practical work usually prefers the Diploma; one who wants depth in two subjects often prefers A Levels.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.description: Not every student sitting IB Chemistry is doing the full Diploma. Course candidates take individual Diploma subjects and receive certificates rather than the Diploma itself, which suits students who want Chemistry at Higher Level for a medicine or engineering application without the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge load. The Chemistry syllabus, the papers and the investigation are identical; only the surrounding requirements differ.
programmes.countryNote: Course-candidate Chemistry is worth knowing about in Mirdif, where several students move in from American-curriculum or CBSE schools partway through secondary. For Ministry of Education equivalency, what the certificate route can and cannot carry is a question for the ministry's own attestation channel rather than for a tutor, and we point parents there rather than guessing.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is the subject on this page, but almost no Mirdif family books one subject in isolation. A Diploma Chemistry student is usually also wrestling with Maths AA and often Physics or Biology. subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The page subject. HL adds depth across most topics and a longer Paper 2. Marks are lost most reliably on equilibrium, entropy and spontaneity, the organic mechanisms that need arrows drawn correctly, and the data-based section where students round early and lose the final significant-figure mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion to Chemistry HL. Students who struggle with the logarithm work in pH calculations are often the same students struggling with logarithms in AA. Fixing the maths usually fixes two grades, which is why we check for it in the first Chemistry lesson.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Taken alongside Chemistry by most engineering applicants in Dubai. The shared weakness is uncertainty and error analysis: a student who cannot propagate uncertainties loses marks in both subjects' practical work and in both data-based papers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The medicine route pairs Biology with Chemistry HL. Biology rewards precise terminology where Chemistry rewards calculation, and students who learn one habit often carry it into the wrong paper. Command-term practice is the fix, and it transfers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by Chemistry SL students heading for life sciences or business. The statistics content is heavier than in AA, and the graphic-display-calculator work is examinable, so calculator fluency is part of the tutoring rather than an afterthought.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries the Individual Oral and the HL essay. Mirdif's cohort includes many students for whom English is a second or third language, and extended-response marks in Chemistry improve when written expression improves.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A common third subject for students who keep Chemistry SL. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, and the deadline pattern collides with the Chemistry investigation in DP1, which is a planning problem worth solving early.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Sometimes taken instead of Chemistry by students who find the calculation load heavy. Worth discussing honestly before a subject change, because dropping Chemistry closes several UAE and UK degree routes that a parent may not have considered.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai schools and sat alongside the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision. Oral assessment carries real weight, and preparation is conversational rather than written, which is a different kind of session.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Not a Chemistry course, but the TOK exhibition and essay land in the same months as the scientific investigation. Our support is structural: how to read the prescribed title, how to build an argument, and where the assessment instrument actually awards marks.

sections.heading: Mirdif against the next neighbourhood over: the comparison in full
paragraphs: Start with the claim this page makes and then test it. A parent in Mirdif searching for a Chemistry tutor is working from a reasonable assumption: that their area is underserved and that a neighbouring community might be better covered. The table below sets Mirdif beside the four communities that ring it and compares the things that actually determine whether a tutor turns up and whether they know the syllabus.

What the comparison shows is that the variables families worry about move very little across the cluster, and the variable that matters does not move at all. Drive time to Dubai's IB-heavy districts varies by around fifteen minutes across the whole eastern suburb belt. The realistic earliest start for an in-home session varies by perhaps forty-five minutes depending on school and school-run arrangements. The number of IB Diploma Chemistry specialists living within half an hour is small everywhere, because the IB schools that employ them are elsewhere.

This is not an argument that Mirdif is a poor place to raise a Diploma student. It is a good one, with real schools and short runs to several more. It is an argument that geography is the wrong axis to optimise. If you would not accept a Chemistry teacher at your child's school on the grounds that they live nearby, the same standard should apply to the tutor you pay for. Online delivery removes the postcode from the decision entirely, which is why families in Al Khawaneej moved first and families in Mirdif are moving now.

sections.heading: The IB Chemistry course your child is actually being marked on
paragraphs: Before any tutoring decision, it helps to know what the final grade is made of. IB Diploma Chemistry is assessed through two written papers and one piece of independent practical work. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and comes in two parts: a multiple-choice section sat without a data booklet question bank, and a data-based section that asks students to read graphs, tables and spectra. Paper 2 carries 44% and is where extended response marks live. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%.

That distribution is the single most useful fact on this page, because it tells you where tutoring hours should go. A student who is strong on recall and weak on analysis is losing marks in the smaller paper and the investigation, which together are more than half the grade. A student who panics in extended response is losing them in the larger paper. These are different problems with different remedies, and a tutor who starts with content revision rather than with the student's marked mock is guessing.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework. The HL syllabus goes deeper across most topics and the papers are longer, which changes the pacing demand as much as the content demand. A Mirdif student who moved from MYP Sciences into Chemistry HL often has the conceptual grasp and not the examination stamina. That is fixable, but only with whole papers under timed conditions, which almost no student does voluntarily.

sections.heading: Where Chemistry marks actually go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: Ask a student why their Chemistry grade is a 4 and they will say they find it hard. Ask the mark scheme and it gives names. In our experience with Dubai Diploma cohorts, the losses cluster in a small number of predictable places, and almost all of them are procedural rather than conceptual. A tutor's first job is to find which of these apply, which takes one lesson with the marked paper in front of both of them.

Moles and stoichiometry come first, because everything downstream depends on them. A student who hesitates converting between mass, moles and concentration will be slow on every calculation question in both papers, and slowness in Paper 1A costs marks even when the chemistry is right. Equilibrium follows: the arithmetic is manageable but the reasoning about shifts, and the distinction between rate and position, is where answers become vague and vague answers score nothing.

Then there is organic chemistry, where the marks are in the detail of mechanisms rather than in the product. Arrows that start in the wrong place, missing lone pairs, missing charges: each is a mark, and a student who arrives at the right product by the wrong route often scores one mark out of four. Energetics and entropy catch students who learned a formula and not a sign convention, so an answer comes out negative when it should be positive and the reasoning behind it was never secure. And in the data-based section, the recurring loss is significant figures and units, which is the cheapest set of marks on the paper to recover and the easiest to keep losing week after week.
bullets: Moles and stoichiometry: accuracy is fine, speed is not, and speed is examinable
Equilibrium: confusing the position of equilibrium with the rate of reaction
Organic mechanisms: arrow origin, lone pairs and formal charge each carry marks
Energetics and entropy: sign conventions applied by habit rather than by reasoning
Data analysis: premature rounding, missing units, uncertainties left untreated

sections.heading: What Chemistry tuition costs across eastern Dubai, in AED
paragraphs: Most of this market will not print a number. Three of the six strongest pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and two of the remaining three quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Mirdif family budgets in. So here is the market, in dirhams, with the source of each band named. These are market rates in Dubai, not IB Gram's price list; our own pricing follows a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many sessions the student actually needs.

Read the table from the bottom rather than the top, because the interesting question is not what the premium tier costs but what the difference buys. Between a budget online tutor at AED 45 to 150 an hour and a Diploma subject specialist at AED 200 to 450, the gap is roughly a hundred and fifty dirhams an hour. What that gap pays for is syllabus-specific judgement: knowing that the data-based section rewards a particular habit, knowing which organic mechanisms recur, knowing what a school's internal investigation deadline usually means in practice. For a student two terms from the examination session, that judgement is worth more than the hourly difference.

The in-home band is the one to look at hardest from Mirdif. Market in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour include travel, and in the eastern suburbs the travel component is real. A parent paying the top of that band for a Chemistry HL specialist to drive from Al Barsha is paying a premium for geography, not for teaching. The same money spent on online delivery buys either more sessions or a better-matched tutor, and the comparison in the next section makes the trade explicit.
