sections.heading: Online against a tutor who drives to Mirdif
paragraphs: This is the comparison that decides the question, so it deserves a table rather than a paragraph of advocacy. Set aside the marketing on both sides and compare four things: what you pay, how much of the hour is teaching, how large a pool the tutor is drawn from, and what happens when something changes. In the eastern suburbs, each of those four favours online delivery for a different reason.

On cost, the in-home premium in Dubai is visible in the market bands above: roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour over the online equivalent, and the gap widens the further east you live. On teaching time, a tutor who has driven forty minutes through 4pm traffic arrives with less patience than they left with, and a session that starts at 5:15pm competes with dinner, prayer times and a tired fifteen-year-old. On pool size, the difference is not marginal: online, a Mirdif family chooses from every Chemistry specialist available on the platform rather than from those willing to make the drive.

The fourth point is the one parents raise last and value most. Schedules in Dubai move. Travel, examinations, Ramadan timings, a school trip. An online session can shift to a post-Iftar slot or to a Saturday morning without renegotiating a driving arrangement, and a student abroad for a fortnight can keep the same tutor. What online does not give you is a person in the room, and for some younger students that matters. For a Diploma Chemistry student working on paper technique, it rarely does. To be plain about it: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so the choice here is between our online delivery and a local in-home arrangement you would make yourself.

sections.heading: The Diploma Chemistry year counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody else in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is what a parent in October actually needs. UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and the useful way to plan is backwards from it rather than forwards from today. The table below counts back through the milestones that matter for Chemistry specifically, naming who sets each one, because the mistake families make is assuming the IB sets every deadline when in fact the school sets most of the ones that bite.

Two cautions before you use it. First, we do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB sets the session and publishes its own dates, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, which are the ones that govern the investigation. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including ours. Second, the internal deadlines are the ones that move: a school may pull an investigation draft deadline forward by a month with three weeks' notice, and a student who has not started is then in real trouble.

Read practically, the table says that Chemistry tutoring has two natural entry points. The first is early in DP1, when the investigation question is being chosen and the moles-and-stoichiometry foundation is still fixable cheaply. The second is immediately after the DP2 mock, when there is a marked paper to work from and roughly eight to twelve weeks of usable time. Starting between those points works; starting after the Easter break before the session is a triage exercise, and an honest tutor will tell you which topics are being abandoned.

sections.heading: KHDA, the eastern-suburbs schools, and what an inspection band tells you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In practice that means annual inspection against a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, published school by school. For a Mirdif parent choosing between schools, or trying to work out whether a Chemistry problem is the student or the provision, those reports are the most useful free document available.

They need reading carefully, though. A school's overall band is an average across phases and subjects, and a strong secondary science department can sit inside a school rated Good, just as a weak one can sit inside a school rated Outstanding. What matters for Chemistry is the secondary science commentary and the attainment and progress judgements for the relevant phase, not the headline word. Mirdif and Al Mizhar families comparing schools across the eastern suburbs should read those sections side by side rather than comparing single words.

Scale is worth knowing too. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula. KHDA's published enrolment shares for that year put the UK curriculum largest at 37 per cent, Indian next at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. That last share explains the shape of this page. IB families are a minority in a very large market, so IB-specific teaching capacity is concentrated rather than spread, and a neighbourhood without an IB continuum school will not have IB Chemistry teachers living in it in any number.

One more thing to be clear about. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or licensed by any UAE education authority, and neither is any individual tutor in the sense that phrase implies. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any tutoring service telling you its tutors are KHDA approved is either describing something else or saying something untrue, and that is worth testing before you pay anyone.

sections.heading: Academic honesty and the Chemistry investigation: the line, drawn
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is a fifth of the Chemistry grade and the single most common place where tutoring crosses a line it should not cross. At least one operator ranking for these queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not a grey area. Submitting work that is not your own is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the Diploma, not on the website that sold it.

So here is what a tutor may do. They may help the student understand the assessment criteria. They may question a research question until it becomes measurable. They may point out that a planned method will generate four data points when the analysis needs more. They may read a draft the student has written and say where the evaluation is thin, where the uncertainty treatment is missing, and where a claim outruns the data. They may teach the chemistry the investigation depends on, and they may teach how to write a scientific evaluation in general terms.

And here is what a tutor may not do. They may not choose the research question. They may not supply a method. They may not provide or invent data. They may not write, rewrite or edit the student's text into its final form. They may not supply a worked example so close to the student's investigation that copying it is the obvious next step. We state these boundaries to the student directly in the first session, because a fifteen-year-old under deadline pressure is entitled to know where the line is before they are standing on it.

The same applies to the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay for students taking Chemistry as part of the full Diploma. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. We reference them and link to the official source, which is both the lawful position and the more useful one, since the official version is the current version.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside Diploma Chemistry
paragraphs: Something that catches families new to Dubai: the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the Diploma, not instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Chemistry HL student in Mirdif, that is real timetable pressure in a year that is already full.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

Two practical consequences for a Chemistry tutoring plan. First, the mandatory subjects occupy periods that in another country might be free study, so the evening is doing more work than you think and a ninety-minute weekly session may be better than two sixties. Second, KHDA requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking of a school rather than of a tutoring service. For the mandatory subjects, KHDA also states that the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so tutoring in those subjects is a narrower activity than tutoring in Chemistry.

sections.heading: Getting started from Mirdif, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is short and the first step costs nothing. You tell us the board, the subject, the level and the problem as the school has described it, and then you add the detail that actually helps: the mock grade, which topics the student says they hate, and what time the school day ends. From a Mirdif address that last point does real work, because it sets the window a session can occupy without competing with the drive home.

We then propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson. The trial is a diagnosis, not a sales call. The tutor should finish it able to tell you which of the loss patterns from earlier on this page apply to your child, and you should finish it knowing whether your child will talk to this person for an hour a week. If the answer is no, we propose someone else. A match that the student tolerates rather than respects does not survive the second term.

Now the honest part, which most of this market leaves out. Diploma Chemistry specialists are a limited resource and sometimes the right one is not available at the time you want. When that happens we say so rather than substituting a general science tutor and hoping. Usually the resolution is a different slot, occasionally a different week, and sometimes a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus to Gulf Standard Time. What we do not do is put a Biology graduate in front of a Chemistry HL student because the diary was tidier that way.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Chemistry HL and Chemistry SL are different jobs, and a student arriving from MYP Sciences needs different first lessons from one arriving from IGCSE. Send the school, the level, the mock grade and the topics the student names as weak. It takes two minutes and it changes who we propose.

process.title: We match on the course, not the commute
process.description: Because lessons are online, the shortlist is drawn from every Chemistry specialist available rather than from those willing to drive to the eastern suburbs. We tell you who the tutor is, what they teach and why they fit this particular gap before any lesson is booked.

process.title: Free trial lesson as a diagnosis
process.description: The first session is free and its job is to find the problem. The tutor works through a piece of the student's own marked work and reports back on what is actually losing marks. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose someone else; nothing is booked on the strength of one hopeful conversation.

process.title: Fix the session time around the school run
process.description: Mirdif school days end anywhere between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the drive home from Dubai Festival City or Academic City can take a chunk out of the afternoon. We set a slot that works in term time and revisit it for Ramadan, examination weeks and travel rather than assuming it holds all year.

process.title: Work between sessions, reviewed in the next one
process.description: Each session ends with a named piece of practice, usually past-paper questions on the topic just covered. The following session starts with that work marked against the published criteria. This is the part that converts attendance into a grade change, and it is the part students skip.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the clock
process.description: Every few weeks we check the plan against where the student is in the Diploma year: investigation deadline, mock, final revision block. The plan changes when the calendar changes, and a block that has done its job ends rather than renewing by default.

whyPoints.title: The pool is the point
whyPoints.description: A Mirdif family working with a local in-home tutor chooses from those who will drive east at 4pm. Online, the choice is every Chemistry HL and SL specialist available. That is the entire argument of this page, and it holds identically in Al Warqa, Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej.

whyPoints.title: AED figures published, with sources
whyPoints.description: Most pages in this market quote nothing or quote US dollars. We publish the Dubai market bands in dirhams with the provider that published each one named and the month we read it. Those are market rates, not our price list; our own pricing follows the free trial.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes before motivation
whyPoints.description: Encouragement is not a method. Our tutors start from the student's marked paper, name the loss pattern, and work on it. Command terms, significant figures and mechanism arrows are unglamorous and they are where a 5 becomes a 6.

whyPoints.title: The investigation line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the Chemistry grade is the student's own practical work, and we tell the student in the first session exactly what we will and will not do with it. Teaching, questioning and feedback on their own draft; never writing, never data, never a method handed over.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed for credibility
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA does and link to its own material. We do not describe IB Gram or any tutor as KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, because none of those things is true of us and the phrase is the most common untruth in this market.

whyPoints.title: Availability told straight
whyPoints.description: When the right Chemistry specialist is not free at the time you want, we say so and offer a real alternative rather than a nearby substitute. A general science tutor in front of a Chemistry HL student wastes a term, and the term is the one thing nobody gets back.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB Chemistry tutor in Mirdif, or will my child be taught from somewhere else?
faqs.answer: Taught from somewhere else, and that is deliberate. Diploma Chemistry specialists in Dubai are clustered around the schools that employ them, which are mostly in the western and central districts rather than the eastern suburbs. Rather than offering whoever is willing to drive to Mirdif, we match your child to a tutor who teaches the Chemistry course they are sitting and deliver the lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. The practical gain is a specialist instead of a generalist, and a session that can start at four rather than a quarter to five.

faqs.question: Would I find a better Chemistry tutor if I searched in Al Warqa or Al Mizhar instead?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most useful thing on this page. The communities ringing Mirdif draw on the same small supply of IB Diploma Chemistry teachers, because those teachers live near the IB schools that employ them. Moving your search one neighbourhood east or north changes the drive time by five to fifteen minutes and changes the number of available specialists by approximately zero. Al Khawaneej is marginally worse served and Al Rashidiya marginally closer to town, and neither difference produces a better Chemistry tutor. The axis worth optimising is syllabus knowledge, not distance.

faqs.question: What does IB Chemistry tutoring cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates, read in October 2026, run roughly as follows. Budget online tutors, usually university students, advertise from AED 45 to 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to 300. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 500 because the figure includes travel. Those are other providers' published figures, each attributed in the rate table on this page, not IB Gram's prices. Our own pricing follows a free trial lesson and depends on how many sessions the student genuinely needs.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry weighted between the papers and the investigation?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 carries 44% and holds the structured and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation, the student's own independent practical work, carries the remaining 20%. The distribution matters for planning because it shows that analysis and practical work together are worth more than half the grade. A revision plan built only on content recall is aimed at the smaller part of the paper, which is why we start from a marked mock rather than from the first chapter of the textbook.

faqs.question: Is IB Chemistry at Higher Level much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is deeper rather than simply longer, and the difference students feel first is stamina. The Higher Level syllabus extends most topics and the papers run longer, so a student who could hold concentration for a Standard Level paper finds the back end of a Higher Level one expensive. Content-wise, the extra depth bites hardest in energetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry. In our experience, students arriving from MYP Sciences have the conceptual grounding and lack examination pacing, which only improves by sitting whole papers under timed conditions rather than by doing more topic questions.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on help with the Chemistry scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits we state to the student in the first session. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, push a research question until it is narrow enough to measure at school, point out that a method will not generate enough data to analyse, teach the chemistry involved, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot choose the question, supply the method, provide data, or write or edit the text into its final form. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct under IB rules and the student bears the consequence.

faqs.question: My child says organic chemistry is impossible. Is that fixable before the exams?
faqs.answer: Usually, because the problem is rarely the concepts. Marks in organic chemistry sit in the detail of mechanisms: where the arrow starts, whether lone pairs are shown, whether formal charges are marked. A student who draws the right product by the wrong route still loses most of the available marks, and nobody has told them that. Six to eight focused sessions on mechanism conventions, with past-paper questions marked against the published criteria between sessions, moves this reliably. It is procedural work, which is why it responds to practice faster than, say, entropy does.

faqs.question: What time can a Chemistry session realistically start in Mirdif on a school day?
faqs.answer: Online, four o'clock works for most families. Eastern-suburbs school days typically end between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and if the school is in Mirdif itself the student is home shortly after. If the school is in Dubai Festival City or Academic City, add the drive. With an in-home tutor coming from Dubai's IB-heavy districts, a realistic start is closer to a quarter to five in Mirdif and a quarter past five in Al Khawaneej, because the tutor is in the same 4pm traffic. That forty-five minutes is the difference between an alert student and a tired one.

faqs.question: Which schools around Mirdif offer IB Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The eastern suburbs mix curricula, so this needs checking school by school rather than assuming. Uptown International School runs an IB continuum in Mirdif itself, and Deira International School in Dubai Festival City is the best-known Diploma provider that Mirdif and Al Mizhar families drive to. Several neighbouring schools run IGCSE to sixteen and then offer A Levels rather than the Diploma. KHDA publishes current curricula and inspection outcomes for every Dubai private school on its own site, and that listing rather than any tutoring website is where to confirm what a school offers this year.

faqs.question: Are your tutors KHDA approved?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest will tell you theirs are. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai, and IB Gram does not hold one or claim one. Individual private tutors in the UAE need a different thing: a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. If a service advertises KHDA-approved tutors, ask which permit and which number. In this market that phrase is usually either confused or untrue.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and should I check?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated: MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Asking a prospective tutor directly is reasonable and a permitted tutor will not mind.

faqs.question: Can my child keep the same Chemistry tutor during Ramadan and when we travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearer advantages of online delivery. During Ramadan sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, which works because there is no journey to renegotiate at either end. When a family travels, the lesson follows the student rather than the address, so a fortnight in Europe or India does not cost a fortnight of Chemistry. The one thing worth agreeing in advance is the time zone the session is pinned to, so that a student abroad is not sitting a Chemistry lesson at six in the morning.

faqs.question: My child's mock Chemistry grade was a 4 and the exams are two terms away. Is that recoverable?
faqs.answer: Two terms is a workable amount of time, and a 4 usually hides two or three specific losses rather than a general failure. The first session should be spent marking the mock with the student, question by question, to find whether the problem is calculation speed, command-term reading, mechanism detail or the data-based section. From there, a weekly session with marked practice between sessions is the normal plan. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is selling something. What is reasonable to expect is a clear list of what is costing marks, within one lesson.

faqs.question: What happens if no Chemistry specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not the market norm. Diploma Chemistry teaching capacity is genuinely limited, and when the right tutor's diary is full the options are a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a general science tutor in front of a Chemistry Higher Level student to keep a booking. If none of the alternatives suits, we say so and you have lost nothing but an email, since the trial lesson is free and comes first.

faqs.question: Do IB Chemistry students in the UAE sit the May session or November?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools overwhelmingly sit the May session, which fits an academic year running from late August or early September. A November session exists and is used in parts of the world where the school year runs the other way round, and occasionally by individual candidates. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the IB holds those and we will not have a parent act on a date from a tutoring site. Your child's Diploma coordinator has the school's version of the calendar, including the internal investigation deadlines that matter most.

faqs.question: How many Chemistry sessions a week does a Mirdif Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one session a week and that is usually right. One well-used hour, with marked practice between sessions, repairs topic gaps steadily and leaves the student time for the other five subjects. Two or three sessions a week makes sense in a defined block: six to ten weeks before the examination session, or a short period around the scientific investigation. Open-ended twice-weekly tutoring across two years tends to produce dependence rather than independence, and it is also the version that costs the most for the least.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-mirdif.closingHeading: Start with a free trial lesson, from Mirdif or anywhere east of it
dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-mirdif.closingBody: The comparison on this page points one way. Whether you live in Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Mizhar or Al Khawaneej, the number of IB Diploma Chemistry specialists who will drive to your door is small, and it is the same small number in each case. Choosing the tutor on syllabus knowledge instead of distance costs nothing extra and changes the lesson materially. Tell us the level, the mock grade and the topics your child names as weak, and we will propose a Chemistry tutor and run the first session free. If the match is wrong, say so and we will propose someone else.

intro.heading: The real question is not the hourly rate
paragraphs: A chemistry quote in Dubai means almost nothing on its own. Two tutors can both charge AED 220 an hour and deliver work that differs by a grade boundary, because the rate reflects what the market will bear in a given district rather than what the tutor can teach. The useful questions are different: how many hours will this take, how much of the grade are those hours aimed at, and what am I paying for that I would get anyway.

Start from the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most MBR City families begin. EdFlik advertises budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that price the tutor is usually a university student, and for a Year 9 or MYP chemistry student needing homework support that can be entirely adequate. For a Higher Level DP2 student who needs organic mechanisms taught properly, it is not, and the eight weeks spent discovering that cost more than the saving.

One step up, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150 — the only competitor in this market with a published hourly rate at all. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 once travel is in the number. BartyED, at the top, publishes AED 650. Three of the six main competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and one of them has a frequently asked question that asks the price and then declines to answer it.

What those figures do not tell you is total cost. A weekly hour at AED 220 is roughly AED 950 a month. A DP Chemistry student who starts in DP1 term two and runs one session a week to the May session of DP2 is buying around sixty hours. A student who starts in DP2 February needs two or three sessions a week for ten weeks to cover the same ground badly, which is twenty-five to thirty hours in a compressed block, at a higher effective rate because specialist availability in the spring is tight. The second route is cheaper on paper and worse on both grade and money.

The delivery position, stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Mohammed Bin Rashid City or anywhere else in the UAE. Visiting tutors are an India-only service. Chemistry here is one-to-one live video in Gulf Standard Time, which removes the travel premium from the price and removes driving distance from the tutor pool. Both of those are cost arguments as much as quality ones.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-mohammed-bin.programmesIntro: Chemistry appears at three levels across the schools MBR City families use, and the cost profile of each is different because the assessment load is different. The notes below say what each stage demands and what that usually means in hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry sits in Group 4 at Standard or Higher Level, organised into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, with a Scientific Investigation worth 20% of the grade. Higher Level adds depth inside the same themes and a longer Paper 2. This is the stage where tuition spending concentrates, and the stage where it is most often misdirected towards coursework rather than Paper 2 technique.
programmes.countryNote: Across the MBR City catchment, DP Chemistry cohorts in a single Dubai IB school are often small, since IB accounted for roughly 7% of Dubai private-school pupils in 2024-25. A small cohort means less peer material to work from and a sharper fall if a student slips, which is the usual trigger for a family in District One or Sobha Hartland to start pricing tutors in DP1 term two.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry is taught inside MYP Sciences and assessed against four criteria rather than by examination. Hours at this stage are cheaper and more effective per dirham than hours in DP2, because the work is habit-forming — balancing equations reliably, handling moles without a calculator crutch, writing a method that someone else could repeat.
programmes.countryNote: The continuum schools in Sobha Hartland run MYP straight into DP, so a student may reach DP1 without having sat a timed chemistry examination. Families who buy a short MYP5 block to build examination habits usually spend less in DP2 than families who wait, which is the clearest cost argument in the whole sequence.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry, for comparison
programmes.description: The British-curriculum schools around MBR City run IGCSE Chemistry at Core or Extended, under Cambridge syllabus 0620 or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent. Rates at this stage are lower across the market — Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200 — because the content ceiling is lower and the tutor pool larger.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing if your child will move from a British school in Sobha Hartland into a DP Chemistry course. The IGCSE-to-DP gap in chemistry is concentrated in energetics and organic mechanisms, and closing it over a summer costs materially less than closing it in DP1 term one while new content arrives weekly.

programmes.name: A Level Chemistry, for comparison
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route at the British schools in this district. Content overlaps heavily with DP Chemistry but the assessment model differs: A Level weights externally assessed practical skills more heavily, DP places 20% on a single student-designed investigation. Market rates are similar, with Bestimate grouping IB and A Level specialists in the same AED 200 to 450+ band.
programmes.countryNote: For an MBR City family choosing between the British school and the IB continuum school two minutes away, the cost of support is roughly equal. The difference is where it falls: a DP family spends on investigation supervision in DP2 term one, an A Level family spends on practical examination preparation. Plan the budget around the model your child's school enters them for.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-mohammed-bin.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is rarely tutored alone, and a second subject changes the monthly figure more than most families anticipate. Below are the courses MBR City families most often add, with what each one assesses and where the marks go missing.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3. Marks are lost most reliably on moles in multi-step calculations, on organic mechanism arrows drawn from memory rather than from reasoning, and on data-based questions where the uncertainty is ignored.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual companion for medicine-track students. Shares the data and measurement strand with chemistry, so a single block of sessions on data handling serves both subjects and halves the cost of fixing it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares energetics and the particulate model with chemistry. Students sitting both often carry one laboratory habit across two investigations, which the criteria reward in one subject and penalise in the other.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Logarithms, exponentials and rearrangement underpin kinetics and equilibrium. A chemistry student who looks weak on equilibrium calculations is frequently weak on logs, which is a cheaper problem to solve.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The lighter route, common where AA is oversubscribed. Statistical treatment helps with the Scientific Investigation; the thinner algebra leaves gaps in kinetics that need closing deliberately rather than hoped away.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Counts for Group 3 or Group 4. Relevant for a student who is finding chemistry the wrong fit in DP1 term one, while a change of course is still permitted by the school.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Offered at some Dubai IB schools as a Group 4 option with substantial biochemistry. Students who move into it from chemistry usually need a short block on energetics rather than a full programme.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Chemistry students draw on TOK when asked how far a model can be trusted. Assessed separately, but a chemistry tutor who can explain why a reaction mechanism is a useful account rather than a photograph makes the essay less abstract.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: Needs a question with a measurable dependent variable and a method the school's laboratory can actually run. Most of the cost of a chemistry EE is incurred because the question was agreed too loosely in the first place.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent. Lower market rate, larger tutor pool, and the stage at which mole calculations should become automatic. Fixing them here is far cheaper than fixing them in DP2.

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition actually costs an MBR City family per month
paragraphs: Hourly rates are a poor planning tool because nobody buys an hour. Families buy a term. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put the budget end at AED 240 to 600 a month, the middle at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those two in-home numbers are the most instructive figures on this page. Four two-hour visits a month is eight hours for roughly AED 1,700, or about AED 210 an hour. Eight online sessions a month at AED 799 is eight hours at around AED 100 an hour. The teaching in both cases may be comparable. The difference is largely a car, parked outside a villa in District One for ninety minutes either side of the lesson, which the family is paying for whether it is itemised or not.

For a Higher Level DP2 chemistry student, plan against the AED 1,000 to 2,000 monthly band and then ask what reduces it. Two things reliably do. Starting earlier, so the hours are spread rather than compressed. And buying the right component — Paper 2 carries 44% of the grade, and hours spent there are worth more than hours spent on the investigation, which carries 20% and absorbs most of the attention because it has a deadline attached.

sections.heading: Where chemistry tuition money gets wasted
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the waste we see in Dubai chemistry engagements, and all four are avoidable without spending more.

The first is buying a generalist for a Higher Level course. A science graduate can carry a student through Structure 1 and 2 convincingly and then stall on organic mechanisms, which arrive later and carry more marks. The family has by then paid for twelve sessions and still needs the specialist. The fix is to test the specific weakness in the trial lesson: ask the tutor to walk through a nucleophilic substitution mechanism and explain why the arrows go where they go. A chemistry specialist does it from reasoning. A generalist recites it.

The second is paying for content when the problem is timing. A student who knows the chemistry and scores poorly on Paper 2 is not short of teaching, they are short of practice under a clock. Content sessions at AED 250 an hour do not fix that, and three terms of them have been sold on exactly that misdiagnosis. A marked mock paper read properly tells you which problem you have in one session.

The third is spending on the investigation at the expense of the papers. The Scientific Investigation is 20% of the grade, has a visible deadline and produces a document a parent can see, so it attracts attention out of proportion to its weight. Paper 2 is 44%, has no deadline and produces nothing visible until results day. Families who split their hours by grade weighting rather than by anxiety get more for the same money.

The fourth is starting late. A DP2 February start costs more per hour because specialist availability in the spring is tight, needs more sessions per week, and covers less ground because the student is simultaneously revising five other subjects. The same total spend in DP1 term two buys a better outcome. This is the least popular piece of advice on this page and the most reliable.
bullets: Test organic mechanism reasoning in the trial lesson, not after twelve sessions
Diagnose timing versus content from a marked mock before buying a programme
Split hours by grade weighting: Paper 2 is 44%, the investigation is 20%
A DP1 start costs fewer total hours than a DP2 rescue block

sections.heading: What the extra money buys between SL and HL Chemistry
paragraphs: Higher Level Chemistry costs more to support than Standard Level, and it is worth knowing why rather than accepting it as a surcharge. The themes are the same — Structure 1 to 3, Reactivity 1 to 3 — and the Scientific Investigation is identical in weight and word limit. What differs is the depth inside each theme and the length of the papers.

The practical consequence is that Higher Level students need more hours on fewer topics. Organic chemistry at Higher Level goes beyond recognising a mechanism to predicting products and reasoning about selectivity. Energetics extends into entropy and spontaneity. Equilibrium acquires quantitative treatment that depends on logarithmic manipulation a student may not have met in their maths course yet. None of those are more hours of the same teaching; they are a different kind of teaching, which is what the specialist band is actually pricing.

For a family deciding whether Higher Level is worth it, the question is not difficulty but destination. Medicine, chemical engineering and most natural-sciences routes expect Higher Level Chemistry. A business or economics route does not. Taking Higher Level for safety and then needing two sessions a week to survive it is an expensive form of insurance, and dropping to Standard Level in DP1 term one — while the school still permits a change — is sometimes the single best financial decision available.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of what you already pay
paragraphs: Tuition spending looks different alongside the rest of a Dubai education bill. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat. Tutoring is the part of the bill that still moves, which is an argument for deciding how much of it you want rather than discovering the number later.

The Dubai market itself is growing rather than contracting. The emirate had 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, across seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of pupils, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

Those figures matter to a chemistry budget in one specific way. IB is a small share of a large market, so IB-specialist supply is thin relative to British-curriculum supply, and thin supply is what sustains the AED 200 to 450 specialist band. More IB schools opening does not immediately produce more Higher Level chemistry tutors. It produces more families looking for them, which is a reason to secure a slot before the spring rather than during it.

The table puts tutoring next to the other items so you can see the proportion. School-fee figures vary enormously by school and are not published here as a band; ask the school, or check the fee listed on KHDA's own school pages.

sections.heading: What the in-home travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: The gap between the online package and the in-home package in this market is roughly AED 110 an hour. It is worth asking what that buys, because the answer is not more teaching.

It buys presence. For a younger child who will not sit still for a screen, that is a real product and worth paying for. For a DP2 chemistry student working on equilibrium calculations, it buys a person in the room and costs a specialist. The tutor who can be in District One at 17:00 on a Tuesday is drawn from the set of chemistry teachers living within a drivable radius who are free at that hour. The tutor on a video call is drawn from the set of DP Chemistry specialists free at that hour, which is a much larger set and includes people who teach Higher Level organic chemistry every week.

There is a second cost that rarely appears in a quote. A visiting tutor's travel time is either billed or absorbed into the rate, and in either case the family pays it. A forty-minute round trip through Al Khail Road at 17:00 is a real economic cost whoever carries it. Online, that cost does not exist, and the saving is available to spend on a better-matched tutor instead.

To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. The in-home figures quoted here are what the Dubai market charges for a service we do not sell, included because the comparison is the whole argument.

sections.heading: Paying for help with the Scientific Investigation, and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation carries 20% of the DP Chemistry grade, caps at 3,000 words, and is assessed against four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks. It is also the component families are most willing to pay for, which is exactly why the boundary needs stating in a section about money.

What a tutor can legitimately be paid to do: interrogate the research question until it has one controllable variable and a measurable outcome the school laboratory can actually deliver; teach uncertainty treatment and error propagation; explain why an evaluation that lists limitations without weighing them scores poorly; and give feedback on the student's own draft against each criterion by letter.

What no amount of money should buy: a written or part-written report, sentences rewritten into the tutor's prose, a research question supplied wholesale, processed data, or a produced evaluation. IB Gram does not sell any of that. One Dubai-facing site in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price, and buying one is an academic-honesty breach whose consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

There is a timing argument buried in this too. Investigation support bought in DP1 term three, while the question is still being chosen, costs a handful of sessions and prevents the expensive problem. Investigation support bought a fortnight before the school's submission deadline is triage on a question that cannot now be changed, data that cannot now be re-collected, and a word count already over the ceiling. Families pay several times more for the second version and get fewer marks for it, which is the clearest example on this page of cost following timing rather than rate.

The parent's test costs nothing. Ask your child to talk you through their own evaluation section, out loud, without the document. If they can explain why each limitation matters and what they would change, the help they bought was teaching. If they cannot, you have paid for a risk rather than a grade.

sections.heading: What you can verify about a chemistry tutor for nothing
paragraphs: Before you spend anything, four checks are free and all four are skipped more often than not.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app and e-services. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, a tutor without one has no cost-based excuse. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific figure you see quoted.

The accreditation claims. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual tutor does not hold one and cannot. A provider presenting an endorsement from KHDA should be asked for the permit number, which KHDA's own listings will corroborate. IB Gram does not hold one and does not claim to.

The rate's source. Ask where a quoted market comparison comes from. Every AED figure on this page names its publisher, which no researched competitor page in this market does for a single figure. A provider who cannot say where their comparison came from is comparing themselves to nothing.

And the ratings. Review markup that a provider writes about itself is not evidence. Two pages in this market display different review totals in different sections of the same page, and one shows a five-star average from twenty reviews next to a claim of far more students. Ask to speak to a current family instead.

sections.heading: Agreeing a chemistry plan, and what we will not sell you
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the school, the year, the level and the two evening windows that survive your district's school run. We match a DP Chemistry specialist. The first lesson is free, taught by the proposed tutor on a live topic — bring the question your child is actually stuck on. Only then do we discuss a rate, because the right number depends on level, session length and how many weeks are left.

Three things we will decline. We will not sell a long programme to a family who needs a diagnostic block; if four sessions will tell you what is wrong, four sessions is what we will propose. We will not sell investigation writing, at any price. And we will not quote a package that depends on a grade outcome, because no tutor can promise one and any provider who does is selling you something they cannot deliver.

Two practical details families ask about before agreeing anything. Cancellation: tell us before the day and the session moves rather than disappears, because a slot lost to a school trip should not cost you an hour. And frequency: the number of sessions a week is yours to change term by term, which matters most in the final block when some students need three and some need one plus a lot of unsupervised timed practice.

If no Higher Level chemistry specialist is free in your window, we say so. That is a narrow request in a specific evening slot and it is sometimes unavailable, particularly in the spring. The options then are a different weekday, a weekend morning, or a wait. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is itself worth noticing.

process.title: Say what you have been quoted

process.title: Send the last marked assessment
process.description: A marked chemistry paper with per-question marks visible is worth more than any placement test. It usually shows within one reading whether the problem is content, calculation or timing, and those three have very different costs attached.

process.description: The DP2 mock changes the plan. Triage comes from the student's own marked paper, and the final weeks move to timed papers only. If fewer hours are needed at that point, we reduce them.

whyPoints.description: There are no IB Gram home visits in the UAE and no UAE office. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, MoE or IB accreditation and do not imply one, and we promise no grade. Knowing the limits before you pay is part of what you are buying.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Chemistry tutor in Mohammed Bin Rashid City cost?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates for an IB subject specialist run roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 200 to 450 or more. Qualified online subject tutors start lower, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Budget online options are advertised from AED 33 to 65 at Tutopiya and EdFlik. Those are the providers' own figures rather than IB Gram prices. We quote after a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on Standard or Higher Level, session length, and how many weeks remain before the May session.

faqs.question: What should I budget per month for DP2 chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session put the budget end at AED 240 to 600, the middle band at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. For a Higher Level DP2 student, plan against the top band. Two things reliably reduce it: starting in DP1 so the hours spread across twenty months instead of compressing into ten weeks, and spending the hours on Paper 2, which carries 44% of the grade, rather than on the investigation, which carries 20% but has a visible deadline.

faqs.question: Why is there such a wide gap between the cheapest and most expensive chemistry tutors in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the published spread runs from about AED 33 to AED 650 an hour and covers genuinely different products. At the bottom the tutor is usually a university student, which can be perfectly adequate for MYP homework support. In the middle sits a qualified subject tutor. At AED 200 to 450 sits a specialist who can teach Higher Level organic chemistry and mark to examiner standard. The premium band above that buys reputation more than additional capability for most students. The mistake is paying budget rates for a Higher Level course and discovering the ceiling in week twelve.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than paying per hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the arithmetic is worth doing. An online package advertised in this market at AED 799 a month for eight sessions works out at around AED 100 per session hour. An in-home package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits works out at around AED 210 an hour. The second is not more teaching; the difference is largely travel, which the family pays for whether it appears on the invoice or not. Check what happens to unused sessions, whether the rate holds if you reduce frequency, and whether the named tutor is guaranteed.

faqs.question: Where do families in District One and Sobha Hartland waste money on chemistry tuition?
faqs.answer: Four places. Buying a generalist for a Higher Level course, then needing a specialist anyway after twelve paid sessions. Paying for content sessions when the real problem is paper timing, which a marked mock would have shown in one session. Spending disproportionately on the Scientific Investigation, which is 20% of the grade, because it has a deadline, while Paper 2 at 44% goes untouched. And starting in DP2 February, which needs more sessions per week at tighter availability and covers less ground than the same spend in DP1 would have.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level chemistry support cost more than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, and for a reason rather than as a surcharge. Both levels share the same themes and the same 20% investigation, and both weight Paper 1 at 36% and Paper 2 at 44%. The difference is depth: Higher Level organic chemistry moves from recognising mechanisms to predicting products and reasoning about selectivity, energetics extends into entropy and spontaneity, and equilibrium becomes quantitative in a way that depends on logarithms. That is a different kind of teaching rather than more of the same, and it is what the specialist band prices. If the destination does not require Higher Level, that is worth revisiting early.

faqs.question: Is online chemistry tuition cheaper than a tutor who visits the villa?
faqs.answer: On published market figures, yes, and the gap is roughly AED 110 an hour between the online and in-home packages advertised in Dubai. The saving is travel, which is a real economic cost whoever absorbs it. The more important difference is the tutor pool: a visiting tutor must live within a drivable radius and be free at 17:00, while an online specialist only has to be free at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, so the in-home figures here describe the market rather than anything we sell.

faqs.question: How many chemistry sessions will my child actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most quotes assume, if the diagnosis is right. A student whose problem is Paper 2 timing may need a block of six timed-paper sessions rather than a term of content teaching. A student with a genuine gap in organic chemistry needs a longer run, because mechanisms have to be built rather than revised. The way to find out is a short diagnostic block of four to six sessions starting from the student's own marked assessment. We will propose that rather than a programme where it is the honest answer.

faqs.question: Can a chemistry tutor help with the Internal Assessment, and what does that cost?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help within clear limits, and the cost is usually a short block rather than a programme. Legitimate work includes stress-testing the research question until it has one controllable variable, teaching uncertainty and error propagation, and giving feedback on your child's own draft against the four criteria of six marks each. What no fee should ever buy is a written or part-written report, rewritten sentences, a supplied question or processed data. The work must be the student's own, and an academic-honesty breach falls on the student rather than on whoever was paid.

faqs.question: Should I be paying extra for a tutor who holds the UAE tuition permit?
faqs.answer: No, because the permit costs the tutor nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app and e-services. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, a tutor has no financial reason to be without one. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Does a quoted chemistry rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that would need a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not in a position to give, and a confident answer without one would be worth nothing to you. What you can reasonably ask any provider is simply whether the number they quoted is what will leave your account, and whether a tax registration number appears on the invoice. A provider who cannot answer that clearly about their own pricing is a provider to be careful with.

faqs.question: Are chemistry tutoring rates in Dubai higher closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: Effective cost rises, though not usually because a rate card changes. Specialist availability tightens in the spring, so the tutors still free in a specific evening slot are fewer and often more expensive. Families also buy two or three sessions a week instead of one, which multiplies the monthly figure. And compressed teaching covers less ground per hour, because the student is revising five other subjects at the same time. The same total spend placed in DP1 term two buys more. Securing a slot before the final term is the practical response.

faqs.question: How does the cost of chemistry tuition compare with Dubai school fees?
faqs.answer: School fees are the larger and now the more stable number. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Fees vary enormously by school, so check the figure published for your own school rather than a band. Tutoring is the part of the bill that still moves, which makes it the part worth planning. One weekly specialist hour sits around AED 860 to 1,950 a month on published rates; two weekly hours roughly doubles it.

faqs.question: What can I check about a chemistry tutor without paying anything?
faqs.answer: Four things, all free. Whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which costs nothing to obtain so there is no excuse for its absence. Whether any KHDA claim is real, since only training institutes with premises hold an Educational Services Permit and an individual tutor cannot. Where any quoted market rate came from, with a URL and a date. And whether review claims are backed by real, countable reviews rather than self-written markup, which two pages in this market display inconsistently within a single page.

faqs.question: What happens if we start chemistry tuition and it is not working?
faqs.answer: Say so and the tutor changes, without a negotiation. A chemistry student who does not trust their tutor will not ask the question they are embarrassed about, and that question is usually the one holding the grade down. The free trial exists to surface a poor fit before money moves, but it does not catch everything and a mismatch four weeks in is not a reason to persist. We would also rather reduce your hours than keep selling them if the diagnosis turns out to have been wrong.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a short block rather than a whole term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many families it is the right purchase. A four to six session diagnostic block starting from the student's own marked assessment will usually establish whether the problem is content, calculation or timing, and will produce a written list of gaps with their grade weighting attached. Families often come out of that block needing fewer hours than the programme they were originally quoted. There is no obligation to continue, and if the block shows the school's own support is sufficient we will tell you that.

intro.heading: The step up, and the booklet nobody reads properly
paragraphs: A student who came out of IGCSE Chemistry 0620 with a 7 or an 8 and is sitting at a 4 in DP1 has not become worse at chemistry. They have met a different subject wearing the same name, and almost nobody warns them. The topics overlap heavily — moles, bonding, energetics, organic chemistry, acids and bases all appear in both — but what is asked of a student within each topic changes substantially, and the change is specific enough to list.

At IGCSE, a bonding question usually asks for a classification and a diagram. At Diploma level it asks which intermolecular force operates and why, in language precise enough to distinguish between candidates. At IGCSE, organic chemistry is functional groups and reaction types. At Diploma level it is mechanisms, with marks awarded for electron movement rather than for the product. At IGCSE, a calculation is usually one step with clean numbers. At Diploma level it is multi-step, often with the quantity being asked for buried two operations away from anything given.

That is a predictable transition and a tutor's first job is to name which part of it a student has not made. Doing so takes one marked paper. A student losing marks on Paper 2 extended response because mechanisms are drawn without curly arrows has a different problem from one whose Paper 1 multiple-choice score is low because definitions are approximate, and the two produce opposite revision plans. Buying the wrong one is how a family spends a term improving the component that was already working.

The second thing this page covers is the data booklet, which IB Chemistry candidates have in the examination and which most students use badly. It provides a defined set of values and relationships. Everything outside it has to be recalled. Students routinely spend revision time memorising what will be printed in front of them and arrive without the content that is not there, which is a symmetrical and entirely avoidable waste. Twenty minutes marking up the current booklet converts a vague anxiety about formulae into a short finite list, and a further twenty minutes being timed on finding a specific value in it stops a student losing minutes to the index under pressure.

Motor City's position is worth stating because it shapes the practical side. GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so students here meet 0620 first and then commute out across the Dubailand corridor if they move to the Diploma. That makes the IGCSE-to-Diploma comparison a live local question rather than an abstract one. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, sessions run 45 or 60 minutes to 21:00, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-motor-city.subjectsIntro: The Diploma Chemistry topics most requested from the Motor City area, each with a note on how the demand differs from the IGCSE version of the same topic. That difference is the diagnosis.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and the mole
subjects.description: At IGCSE, usually one clean step. At Diploma level, multi-step with limiting reagents, percentage yield and atom economy, and the quantity asked for often two operations from anything given. A weakness here presents as a problem in whichever topic is current.

subjects.name: Bonding and structure
subjects.description: At IGCSE, classification and a diagram. At Diploma level, precise language about which intermolecular force operates and why, molecular shapes, and at Higher Level hybridisation and formal charge. The marks sit in the explanation rather than in the label.

subjects.name: Energetics and thermochemistry
subjects.description: At IGCSE, exothermic or endothermic with a simple calculation. At Diploma level, Hess cycles, bond enthalpies and at Higher Level entropy and Gibbs free energy. Sign errors dominate: a cycle built correctly and traversed the wrong way gives a confidently wrong answer.

subjects.name: Equilibrium
subjects.description: At IGCSE, Le Chatelier reasoning in words. At Diploma level the same reasoning with greater precision, extending at Higher Level to equilibrium constants and calculations. Students lose marks setting up initial and equilibrium concentrations rather than on the algebra.

subjects.name: Acids and bases
subjects.description: At IGCSE, pH scale and neutralisation. At Diploma level, Brønsted-Lowry theory, strength against concentration, and at Higher Level weak acid and base calculations, buffers and titration curve analysis. Confusing strength with concentration survives from IGCSE and costs marks.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: At IGCSE, functional groups and reaction types. At Diploma level, mechanisms with marks for electron movement: curly arrows from the correct source, lone pairs shown, intermediates charged. Higher Level adds elimination, condensation and multi-step pathways.

subjects.name: Redox and electrochemistry
subjects.description: At IGCSE, oxidation and reduction with simple half-equations. At Diploma level, oxidation states, balancing in acidic or basic conditions, voltaic and electrolytic cells, and at Higher Level standard electrode potentials. Balancing is procedural and either secure or lost.

subjects.name: Periodicity
subjects.description: At IGCSE, group trends described. At Diploma level, trends explained through shielding and effective nuclear charge, with Higher Level extending into transition metal chemistry, complex ions and colour. Explanation questions want the mechanism of the trend, not the trend.

subjects.name: Data analysis and spectroscopy
subjects.description: Largely new at Diploma level. Infrared, mass spectrometry and at Higher Level nuclear magnetic resonance used to deduce structures. Rewards a systematic routine — molecular formula first, then functional groups, then assembly — rather than inspired guessing.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Replaces the IGCSE alternative-to-practical paper with something considerably larger: 20% of the grade, 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Chemistry investigations fail most often at research design, on feasibility in a school laboratory.

sections.heading: The step from IGCSE 0620 to Diploma Chemistry, topic by topic
paragraphs: This is the most predictable difficulty in the subject and the one families are least warned about. The topic lists overlap heavily, which is exactly why the step catches students out: a chapter heading looks familiar and the questions underneath it are not. A student who scored well at IGCSE and is struggling in DP1 is usually not behind on content but behind on what the content is now for.

Four shifts account for most of it. The first is multi-step calculation: at IGCSE a stoichiometry question typically runs one operation with convenient numbers, while at Diploma level the quantity being asked for sits two or three operations away from anything given, with limiting reagents and yield in between. The second is precision of language: bonding and periodicity questions move from classification and description to explanation in terms of shielding, effective nuclear charge and specific intermolecular forces, and loose wording loses marks that a correct idea would otherwise earn.

The third is mechanisms. IGCSE organic chemistry is functional groups and reaction types; Diploma organic chemistry is electron movement, with marks allocated to curly arrows starting at the correct bond or lone pair, lone pairs drawn, and intermediates carrying the right charge. A student who learned organic chemistry as a set of outcomes writes the correct product and scores little. The fourth is the arrival of spectroscopy, which is largely new and rewards a systematic deduction routine.

Naming which of the four a student has not made is a one-paper job and it changes the whole plan. It is also far cheaper to do in the holiday before DP1 than in the term after the first assessment, because at that point the student is behind on new content as well as adapting to new demands. Eight to ten sessions before DP1 begins closes most of the gap; the same work in November takes longer.

sections.heading: The data booklet: what it gives and what it does not
paragraphs: IB Chemistry candidates have a data booklet in the examination, and it is the most under-exploited resource in the subject. It provides a defined set of values and relationships. Everything outside that set has to be recalled. Those two sentences should shape a student's entire approach to memorisation, and for most students they do not, because nobody has sat down with the booklet and marked it up.

The failure runs in both directions and is equally expensive each way. Students spend revision hours memorising content that will be printed in front of them, which is wasted effort. And they arrive without content that is not in the booklet, which is lost marks. The remedy is twenty minutes with the current booklet, a highlighter and a list: this is given, therefore I do not memorise it; this is not, therefore it goes on the recall schedule.

There is a second skill beyond knowing what is in it, which is finding things in it quickly. A student fumbling through the booklet under time pressure on Paper 2 is losing minutes that have nothing to do with chemistry. Deliberate practice — being asked for a specific value and timed on retrieving it — fixes that in about twenty minutes and pays for the rest of the course.

The same logic applies to the periodic table provided in the examination. It gives relative atomic masses, which removes a memorisation task, and it gives group and period positions, which supports periodicity reasoning if the student is used to reading it that way. What it does not give is the explanation a periodicity question asks for, and that is the part students assume the table will carry.

sections.heading: Reading a component profile as a diagnosis
paragraphs: A chemistry grade is a weighted sum of three components: Paper 1 at 36%, split between multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 at 44% extended response, and the scientific investigation at 20%. The combination of strengths and weaknesses across those three is a diagnosis, and it is far more useful than the overall grade. Two students on the same 4 can need entirely different work.

Strong Paper 1 and weak Paper 2 is the commonest profile and points at extended-response technique: the student knows the content and cannot deploy it at length, usually because mechanisms are drawn loosely or because explanations describe rather than explain. Weak Paper 1 and strong Paper 2 points the other way, at approximate definitions and slow recall, and responds to short daily multiple-choice practice rather than to more teaching.

Strong papers with a weak investigation is a criterion problem, not a chemistry problem, and the work is reading the published descriptors and rewriting against them — though only if the investigation has not yet been submitted, because after submission it is closed. A profile weak across all three usually means a content gap that is wider than a short block can address, and the honest response is to say so and propose a realistic target rather than take the booking on the implied one.

The reason to insist on this is that the wrong diagnosis produces confidently wasted money. A student with weak Paper 1 and strong Paper 2 who is given extended-response coaching will improve at something they were already good at. Reading the profile takes five minutes with a marked script and it is the first thing the free diagnostic lesson does.

sections.heading: Which topics repay study time fastest
paragraphs: Not all chemistry revision is equally productive, and with a finite number of evenings it is worth knowing which topics give marks back quickest. The efficient ones share two features: the content is bounded, and the question types are predictable. The inefficient ones are open-ended, or they depend on a technique the student has not got.

Among the most efficient is redox balancing in acidic and basic conditions. It is procedural, it appears reliably, and it is either secure or lost — so two or three sessions converts a standing loss into a standing gain. Oxidation state assignment is similar. So is the spectroscopy deduction routine: a fixed sequence applied to every question, learnable in two sessions, and it turns a topic students fear into one they can approach systematically.

Mechanism drill sits in the middle: it takes four to six weeks rather than two sessions, because drawing is a motor skill built by repetition, but the payoff is large because organic chemistry carries substantial extended-response marks. Energetics sign discipline is quick — one procedural rule, write the direction on the cycle before computing — and removes a category of confidently wrong answers.

The least efficient use of a limited number of sessions is broad content review across several topics, which is what most families instinctively buy. It feels thorough and it spreads attention so thinly that nothing becomes secure. Where a content gap genuinely spans the syllabus, the answer is a longer plan rather than a faster one, and a provider who agrees to cover everything in six sessions is agreeing to something that cannot be done.

sections.heading: Four ways to get chemistry help, compared
paragraphs: Before paying anyone, it is worth comparing the options honestly, because two of the four are free and one of those is frequently the right answer. A Motor City family with a Year 12 student struggling in chemistry has school support, peer study, group tuition and one-to-one specialist help available, and the best choice depends on what is actually wrong.

School support — a subject clinic, a lunchtime session, an open door — is free, delivered by someone who knows the scheme of work and the internal deadlines, and should be the first thing tried. Its limits are time and individual attention: a teacher running a clinic for twelve students cannot read one student's error pattern across a term. Peer study is also free and genuinely effective for recall work, because testing each other on definitions and the recall list is exactly the activity that builds reproduction. It is poor for diagnosis, because peers reinforce each other's misconceptions.

Group tuition at a centre is the cheapest paid option per hour and suits a student whose problem is structure and routine rather than a specific error. It cannot see an individual error pattern, because the teaching is pitched at the group. One-to-one specialist help is the most expensive per hour and buys the thing the other three cannot: somebody reading this student's marked script and naming the specific repeating failure.

Which leads to a sequencing recommendation rather than a sales pitch. Try the school clinic first. Set up peer testing for the recall list. Then buy one-to-one help for the one thing the marked script identifies, and buy it as a defined block rather than an open commitment. That ordering costs the least and works most often, and we say it despite it reducing what we sell.

sections.heading: What chemistry support costs by component
paragraphs: Costing chemistry by component rather than by term exposes the real decision, which is which component to fix. The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end.

Applied to the blocks this page describes, the arithmetic in the table below is straightforward and the point of showing it is to make the choice visible. A transition block before DP1 is the single best-value purchase in the subject and almost nobody buys it. A mechanism drill block is the best-value purchase in DP2. A broad content review is the most expensive thing on the list per mark recovered, and it is the one most often requested.

There is a reason to spend at the specialist band rather than the entry band for chemistry specifically. Marking mechanism work requires somebody who knows that the arrow has to originate at a bond or a lone pair and that the intermediate needs its charge, and marking an investigation draft requires somebody who has read the criterion descriptors. A tutor at the entry band may explain the chemistry competently and be unable to do either, which is precisely what the money is for.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page because level, component and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson rather than preceding it.
