sections.heading: The investigation, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade, 24 marks, four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. In chemistry the component fails most often at research design, and specifically on feasibility — a question requiring apparatus the school does not have, or variables that cannot be held constant to the precision the analysis needs, or too few data points to support the intended processing.

That makes the early check the valuable one, and it is an hour that cannot be bought back later. Before any data is collected: can the method be run with the equipment actually available, can the variables be controlled to the needed precision, and will the number of data points support the processing the student intends. One session answers all three, and it is the highest-value hour available in a 20% component.

Data analysis in chemistry means propagating uncertainty from the instruments — balance, pipette, thermometer — through to the derived quantity, which many students omit entirely. Conclusion requires comparison with accepted literature values rather than a restatement of the result. Evaluation requires specific methodological limitations and realistic targeted improvements: an instrument resolution limit expressed as a percentage uncertainty scores, while human error and a shortage of time score nothing.

The honesty line is strict and this market does not always respect it. At least one site ranking for UAE IB searches sells completed Internal Assessments; submitting purchased work is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. A tutor may interrogate the research question, check the method's feasibility, teach uncertainty propagation, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, and read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion a passage fails. A tutor may not design the investigation, process the data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or edit prose to a standard the student could not produce. Every submitted word is the student's.

faqs.question: My child got an 8 in IGCSE chemistry and is at a 4 in DP1. What happened?
faqs.answer: They met a different subject with the same topic headings. Four shifts account for most of it: stoichiometry moves from one clean step to multi-step problems with limiting reagents and yield; bonding and periodicity move from classification to explanation in terms of shielding and specific intermolecular forces; organic chemistry moves from functional groups to mechanisms marked on electron movement; and spectroscopy arrives largely new. A marked paper identifies which of the four has not been made, and eight to ten sessions usually closes it.

faqs.question: What does the IB Chemistry data booklet actually provide?
faqs.answer: A defined set of values and relationships, and nothing beyond it — so everything outside the booklet has to be recalled. The common error runs both ways and is expensive each way: students memorise content that will be printed in front of them and arrive without content that is not there. Twenty minutes with the current booklet and a highlighter separates the two and produces a finite recall list. A further twenty minutes of timed retrieval practice stops a student losing minutes hunting for a value under pressure.

faqs.question: How do we tell which chemistry component is the problem?
faqs.answer: Read the profile rather than the grade. Paper 1 is 36% and splits into multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 is 44% extended response, and the investigation is 20%. Strong Paper 1 with weak Paper 2 means the content is known and cannot be deployed at length, so the work is extended-response structure and mechanism drill. Weak Paper 1 with strong Paper 2 means approximate definitions and slow recall, which responds to short daily practice instead. Two students on the same 4 need opposite blocks.

faqs.question: Why are mechanism marks lost when the product is right?
faqs.answer: Because the product is not what is being marked. A mechanism question allocates marks to electron movement: a curly arrow starting at the correct bond or lone pair, lone pairs drawn on the nucleophile, intermediates shown with the right charge, and each step separated rather than collapsed. A student who learned organic chemistry as a set of outcomes writes the correct product and scores little. The fix is drawing from blank paper, ten mechanisms a session, marked on the arrows, over four to six weeks.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics give marks back fastest?
faqs.answer: Redox balancing in acidic and basic conditions, at two to three sessions, because it is procedural and appears reliably. Oxidation state assignment, at one to two. The spectroscopy deduction routine, at two sessions, which turns a feared topic into a systematic one. Energetics sign discipline, at two, which removes a whole category of confidently wrong answers. Mechanism drill takes longer at four to six weeks but has the largest payoff because organic chemistry carries substantial extended-response marks.

faqs.question: Should we try the school's chemistry clinic before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first thing we suggest. A school subject clinic is free, run by somebody who knows the scheme of work and the internal deadlines, and often enough on its own. Its limit is individual attention: a teacher running a clinic for a dozen students cannot read one student's error pattern across a term. Peer testing is also free and genuinely effective for the recall list, because testing each other on definitions is exactly the activity that builds reproduction rather than recognition.

faqs.question: Is group tuition at a Dubai centre worth considering for chemistry?
faqs.answer: For a student whose problem is structure and routine rather than a specific error, yes — it is the cheapest paid option per hour and the discipline of a fixed class helps some students considerably. What it cannot do is see an individual error pattern, because the teaching is pitched at the group, so a student losing marks because their mechanism arrows start in the wrong place will keep losing them. Where the marked script names a specific repeating failure, one-to-one is what addresses it.

faqs.question: When is the best time to prepare for Diploma Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The long holiday before DP1, which is the single best-value purchase in the subject and one that almost nobody makes. Eight to ten sessions on multi-step stoichiometry, precision in bonding and periodicity language, mechanism drawing and the spectroscopy routine closes most of the transition gap before the student is also trying to keep up with new content. The same work in November takes longer and costs more, because by then they are behind on two things at once.

faqs.question: What usually goes wrong with a chemistry investigation?
faqs.answer: Feasibility, at the research design stage. A student proposes a question needing apparatus the school does not have, or variables that cannot be held constant to the precision the analysis requires, or too few data points to support the processing they intend. The data then cannot justify a conclusion however carefully the report is written, and research design and conclusion both suffer. One session checking the method against real laboratory constraints before any data is collected is the highest-value hour in a 20% component.

faqs.question: Can anything be done about the investigation after it is submitted?
faqs.answer: No, and that matters for how a late-arriving family should spend. The scientific investigation is 20% of the chemistry grade, marked in school and moderated externally, and it closes on the school's submission date. After that the movable things are Paper 1 recall, Paper 2 extended-response technique and residual content. So the diagnostic note written for a student in DP2 term five lists what has closed as well as what has not, rather than selling hours against work that is already finished.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Chemistry need a particular mathematics course?
faqs.answer: It does not formally specify one, but the calculation load is lighter than physics and heavier than biology, and students on Applications and Interpretation generally cope. What matters more is procedural reliability: rearranging expressions, handling logarithms for pH work at Higher Level, and carrying units through a multi-step calculation. Those are habits rather than course content, and a student who is secure on them manages Higher Level Chemistry with either mathematics course. Check the degree requirement separately, since many science routes specify Analysis and Approaches for other reasons.

faqs.question: What time can a chemistry session start from Motor City?
faqs.answer: About 18:00 for Diploma students. GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so IB students commute out across the Dubailand corridor and are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30. Online sessions run to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, which lets a 45-minute mechanism drill session and a full-hour marked paper session sit on different evenings in the same week. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00, which suits drill work well.

IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service for us. For Higher Level Chemistry the online format also widens the pool considerably, because the number of people who have taught buffer calculations and the extended mechanism set is small enough that filtering by driving distance leaves very little.

faqs.answer: At published bands, a mechanism drill block of six sessions is roughly AED 900-1,800 at the AED 150-300 qualified band or AED 1,200-2,700 at the AED 200-450 specialist band. A redox block of three sessions is AED 450-1,350, and the spectroscopy routine at two sessions is AED 300-900. A transition block of nine sessions before DP1 is AED 1,350-4,050 and is the best value in the subject. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026; we quote after the free diagnostic lesson.

intro.heading: Chemistry is chosen by comparison and lost on execution
paragraphs: Most Diploma chemistry problems start with a choice made for the wrong reason. A student picks chemistry over physics because it seemed less mathematical, or over biology because it seemed more respected, and discovers in the second term that it carries a dense calculation load and a mechanism-drawing discipline neither of the others requires. That mismatch is worth naming early, because it is fixable in Year 12 and expensive to discover in Year 13.

Mudon adds the familiar constraint. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand, villas and townhouses across Al Salam, Rahat, Arabella, Naseem and Mudon Views, with no secondary school inside its own boundary. Diploma students travel to Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, GEMS International School Al Khail, Nord Anglia in Al Barsha South or Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City. Evenings are short, and the local tutor pool is concentrated around Motor City and Dubai Sports City, where generalists outnumber Higher Level chemistry specialists heavily.

The comparison that matters more than geography is between the three sciences. Chemistry sits between physics and biology on mathematical demand and above both on precision of notation. A chemistry answer that is conceptually right and sloppily written loses marks in a way that a biology answer often does not: an unbalanced equation, a missing state symbol, a curly arrow starting from the wrong place. Those are mechanical losses, which makes them the fastest to repair.

The second comparison is Higher against Standard Level. Higher Level adds content and an additional paper, and the areas it adds are not evenly distributed in difficulty. Organic chemistry, equilibrium and the energetics extension carry most of the Higher Level losses in marked scripts, and a student who is comfortable with the core can still be defeated by the extension. Knowing that shapes which topics a plan touches first.

The third comparison is the one families make without evidence, which is one neighbourhood against the next for availability. It feels as though a larger community must have more tutors, and across Dubailand that is only loosely true. What determines supply is whether a community has a Diploma school inside it, and almost none here do. Arabian Ranches 2 is the exception, and even there Higher Level chemistry specialists are scarce. The table further down this page sets that out community by community, because the conclusion is the same in every row and it is worth seeing why.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so a session can sit early for a student home from Arabian Ranches or after eight where both parents commute. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon door. The practical work stays with the school and its laboratory; what a session does is prepare the design and interrogate the write-up, which is where the assessed marks sit.

sections.heading: Chemistry compared with the other two sciences
paragraphs: Students choose a science at fifteen on the basis of which teacher they liked and which subject sounded useful, and then live with the consequence for two years. The comparison that would actually help them is rarely made, so here it is. Physics is the most mathematical of the three and the least dependent on memorised detail. Biology is the least mathematical and the most dependent on precise terminology and volume of recall. Chemistry sits between them and adds a demand neither of the others makes, which is notational precision in the answer itself.

That third demand is the one that catches people. In biology a conceptually correct answer written loosely often collects most of its marks. In chemistry it does not: an unbalanced equation is wrong, a missing state symbol loses a mark where the scheme required it, and a mechanism drawn with arrows pointing from the wrong species is simply incorrect even when the student knows what happens. Chemistry rewards tidiness in a way that surprises students who were strong at IGCSE science.

The calculation load is the second surprise. Moles work runs through the whole course, equilibrium and energetics add logarithms and proportional reasoning, and kinetics asks for graphical interpretation. A student who chose chemistry to avoid physics mathematics finds a comparable amount of it distributed more thinly and therefore harder to avoid.

None of this makes chemistry the wrong choice. It makes it a choice with a known shape, and a student who understands that shape in the first term plans differently from one who discovers it in a mock. sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level chemistry
paragraphs: Higher Level chemistry adds content and an additional paper, and the added content is not evenly difficult. The extensions in energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases and organic chemistry account for most of the losses visible in marked Higher Level scripts, while the extensions in some other areas cause comparatively little trouble. A plan that treats the extension as one undifferentiated block spends time badly.

What does not change between the levels is the examination style. Standard Level questions are phrased the same way, demand the same notation and punish the same sloppiness. Students and sometimes parents assume Standard Level is a gentler form of assessment on narrower content; it is the same form of assessment on narrower content. A technique problem therefore travels with a student who drops a level, and dropping does not fix it.

Where dropping genuinely helps is load. A student carrying Higher Level chemistry alongside Higher Level biology and Higher Level mathematics, which is a common medicine-track combination in this belt, is carrying three heavy internal assessments on overlapping deadlines as well as three content loads. Doing two of those well is a better outcome than doing three adequately, and that trade is worth making deliberately in Year 12 rather than by collapse in Year 13.

The decision belongs with the school. The question to ask is which university routes are realistically in view, checked against each institution's own published entry profile, since requirements differ between countries and change between cycles. A tutor should not be the source of that information.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry: the topic every parent in this belt names
paragraphs: Organic chemistry is the single most requested topic in Diploma chemistry tutoring in Dubai, and the reason is consistent. Students try to memorise reactions as pairs of starting material and product, which produces a list that grows beyond memory and collapses under an unfamiliar question. The subject only becomes manageable when mechanisms rather than outcomes are what is learned.

The practical shift is small and the effect is large. Group reactions by mechanism type rather than by functional group, so that a student who understands nucleophilic substitution recognises it whatever the substrate. Then drill the arrows: every curly arrow starts from a lone pair or a bond and ends where the electrons go, and an arrow drawn from a positive centre is simply wrong regardless of whether the product is right.

Drawing under time is the part students skip. Mechanisms practised slowly at a desk feel learned and then fail in a paper, because the recall required is motor as much as conceptual. Twenty mechanisms a week, timed, each checked for arrow origin and destination, changes performance inside a month. This is the clearest example in the Diploma of a topic where the right kind of practice beats more explanation.

The second common failure in organic chemistry is nomenclature, which costs easy marks and is purely mechanical. Students who cannot name a branched compound reliably lose marks at the start of questions and then lose confidence for the rest of them, and the repair is a fortnight of short naming exercises rather than anything conceptual.

Nomenclature is mechanical, cheap to fix and costs marks at the start of questions

sections.heading: The calculation cluster: moles, energetics, equilibrium and kinetics
paragraphs: A second cluster of losses sits in the calculation topics, and they fail together because they share underlying skills. Moles work runs through everything, and a student who is slow at it under time loses marks in stoichiometry, in titrations, in energetics and in the investigation's analysis. Speed here is not a luxury; it is what leaves time for the harder parts of a paper.

Energetics introduces sign conventions, which cause more errors than the arithmetic does. Exothermic and endothermic sign handling, Hess cycle direction and bond enthalpy conventions all have to be automatic, and a student who thinks about them each time will make an error under pressure. The repair is a short set of sign-only exercises, stripped of context so that only the convention is being tested.

Equilibrium and kinetics add logarithms and graphical interpretation. The common failure is not understanding the chemistry but being unable to manipulate the mathematics quickly enough to reach the chemistry. A student who cannot handle logarithms confidently cannot access several Higher Level questions at all, and that is a mathematics intervention rather than a chemistry one.

The diagnostic test a parent can apply is simple. Take a question the student lost marks on, strip the chemistry, and ask them to do the algebra alone. If the algebra fails in isolation, the hour belongs to manipulation practice. If it succeeds, the problem lies in the chemistry reasoning or in how the answer was written, and the hour belongs elsewhere.

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation against the physics one
paragraphs: All the Diploma sciences share the same investigation criteria, which makes the comparison between them useful. A physics investigation usually fails on uncertainty treatment. A biology investigation usually fails on controlling biological variability. A chemistry investigation most often fails on scope: a research question that cannot be measured reliably with school equipment in the time available.

Design therefore sets the ceiling here more than in the other two sciences. A question with one clear independent variable, a dependent variable that can be measured with the apparatus the department holds, and a realistic number of repeats can score across every criterion. A question requiring equipment the school does not have, or a reaction too fast or too slow to time accurately, cannot be rescued by effort.

Analysis carries most of the mathematical marks. Uncertainties have to be propagated through calculations rather than mentioned, concentrations recalculated rather than assumed, graphs chosen so the relationship is visible, and anomalies addressed rather than quietly removed. Chemistry students who have never been taught propagation lose these marks silently and usually blame the experiment.

Evaluation is the criterion most often written as a conclusion. It asks for specific, chemistry-based limitations and realistic improvements: a named source of systematic error, a reason the measurement drifted, a change that would actually address it. A tutor can explain each descriptor and mark the student's own draft against it. Drafting, rewriting or supplying data is not permitted, and the investigation is authenticated by the teacher.
bullets: Chemistry investigations fail most often on scope rather than on analysis
The department's actual apparatus constrains what a question can be
Uncertainties must be propagated, not mentioned in a sentence
Evaluation wants a named systematic error and a change that addresses it

sections.heading: Mudon against its neighbours for chemistry help
paragraphs: Availability of Higher Level chemistry help varies across this belt, and not in the way distance suggests. The tutors advertising locally are concentrated around Motor City and Dubai Sports City, and most cover several sciences at IGCSE level with Diploma work as an extension rather than a specialism. That is a reasonable business model and a poor match for a student at a 4 in Chemistry Higher Level.

Compare the communities on what a family can actually get. DAMAC Hills has a school inside the community and so the shortest travel, but Jebel Ali School takes students through Year 11, which means Diploma chemistry families there have usually moved a child elsewhere for sixth form. Remraam has South View School on its edge and a predominantly IGCSE cohort. Arabian Ranches 2 has the belt's nearest Diploma provision and therefore the thickest Diploma demand, which attracts more capable tutors but still not many Higher Level chemistry specialists.

Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3 are the thinnest, because they combine a Diploma-age population with no school and no established tutor cluster. Town Square is thinner again. In every one of those cases the answer to the availability question is the same, which is the point: choose the tutor by level and option, and let the lesson arrive over video.

The cost comparison runs the same way. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, and from Mudon that loading sits at the upper end because the pool is elsewhere.

sections.heading: What a chemistry tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: The boundary is the same across the Diploma and worth stating in chemistry terms. On a past paper a tutor may show a model answer and a model mechanism, because the paper is practice. On the scientific investigation, the Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, the work is assessed and must be the student's own, authenticated by the teacher. A malpractice finding does not reduce a mark; it can remove the Diploma.

The permitted actions are specific. Teaching the chemistry behind an investigation. Explaining what each criterion rewards and asking the questions it implies. Saying that a proposed reaction is too fast to time reliably or that a concentration range will not produce a measurable difference. Working uncertainty propagation through the student's own measured data. Marking a draft the student wrote against the published descriptors and naming where it falls short.

The prohibited actions are equally specific. Drafting any part of the text. Rewriting a section. Editing a document to completion. Supplying a worked write-up to adapt. Providing data the student did not collect, which in a chemistry investigation is a particular temptation when an experiment has failed and a deadline is near. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and that is the offer to refuse.

Board material carries its own rule. IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers; sessions reference and link to the official pages rather than circulating copies, and nobody has access to unreleased material whatever is claimed.
bullets: Model mechanisms belong to practice papers, never to assessed coursework

sections.heading: What chemistry tuition costs, and the permit position
paragraphs: Chemistry requests land in the specialist band, because credible Higher Level coverage is scarcer than general science coverage. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Below that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

On the legal side, an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute instead, renewed annually. IB Gram has no UAE premises, holds no such permit, and does not attach a regulator's name to its tutors. For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

process.title: Name the level, the option and the school
process.description: Higher or Standard Level, the option the school teaches, and the school itself. Option content differs between Dubai schools and preparation aimed at the wrong one is wasted. The school also determines the practical programme the investigation depends on.

process.title: Send a marked paper and the investigation status
process.description: A marked response paper shows whether the losses are notation, calculation or reasoning, and knowing whether the investigation is unstarted, measured or drafted shows where recoverable marks sit. Two facts in one message make a specific proposal possible.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a chemistry specialist
process.description: A trial over live video at no cost and before any payment, with the student doing most of the work. The test afterwards is whether the tutor named something specific, such as arrow direction in mechanisms or sign conventions in energetics. If not, ask for a different tutor.

process.title: Fix the slot around the Dubailand run
process.description: Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time. Early evening suits a student home from Arabian Ranches; after eight suits households where both parents commute. Because nobody drives to Naseem or Arabella, the slot can move within the evening or after Iftar during Ramadan at no cost.

process.title: Review by topic cluster every few weeks
process.description: Session notes name the cluster worked on, the error pattern and the next target. Every four to six weeks the plan is checked against the investigation deadline and which cluster still holds recoverable marks, so the hour follows the marks rather than the textbook order.

whyPoints.title: The subject comparison is made honestly
whyPoints.description: Chemistry carries a heavier calculation load and a stricter notation demand than students expect when they choose it. Saying so costs nothing and prevents a two-year mismatch that a tutoring hour cannot fix later.

whyPoints.title: Notation is drilled every session, not taught once
whyPoints.description: Unbalanced equations, missing state symbols and loose arrow direction are mechanical losses, which makes them the fastest marks in the course to recover. Ten minutes of every hour, regardless of topic, is enough to close them.

whyPoints.title: Organic chemistry is drilled under time
whyPoints.description: Mechanisms practised slowly at a desk feel learned and fail in a paper, because the recall required is partly motor. Twenty timed mechanisms a week, each checked for arrow origin and destination, changes performance inside a month.

whyPoints.title: Maths failures are separated from chemistry failures
whyPoints.description: Strip the chemistry from a lost question and test the algebra alone. If it fails in isolation the hour belongs to manipulation practice, not to another pass through equilibrium. Misdiagnosing this wastes a term, and it happens constantly.

whyPoints.title: The laboratory limit is stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Online lessons cannot run an experiment. They prepare the design, interrogate the analysis and give criterion feedback on the write-up, which is where the investigation's marks sit. Claiming more would be the easiest sentence to write and the least honest one.

whyPoints.title: No regulator names used as credentials
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration, no board affiliation and no UAE office. Where a page in this market attaches a regulator's name to its tutors, that is a claim to check rather than a qualification.

faqs.question: Is chemistry harder than physics or biology at Diploma level?
faqs.answer: Harder in a different way rather than overall. Physics is the most mathematical and the least dependent on recall. Biology is the least mathematical and the most dependent on volume of terminology. Chemistry sits between them and adds a demand neither makes, which is notational precision in the answer itself: an unbalanced equation is wrong, a missing state symbol loses a mark, and a mechanism with arrows from the wrong species is incorrect even when the product is right. Students strong at IGCSE science are often surprised by that.

faqs.question: My daughter finds organic chemistry impossible. What actually fixes it?
faqs.answer: Changing what she is trying to learn. Most students memorise reactions as pairs of starting material and product, which produces a list that outgrows memory and collapses on an unfamiliar question. The shift is to learn mechanisms and group reactions by mechanism type rather than by functional group, so that recognising nucleophilic substitution works whatever the substrate. Then drill arrows under a timer, checking origin and destination every time, because the recall needed in a paper is partly motor. A month of that changes performance measurably.

faqs.question: Why does a correct chemistry answer still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because chemistry marks presentation in a way biology often does not. The recurring losses are mechanical: an equation left unbalanced, state symbols omitted where the scheme required them, a concentration given without units, significant figures carried inconsistently, and curly arrows drawn from a positive centre rather than from a lone pair or bond. Each is small and each is reliable. Ten minutes of notation drilling in every session, regardless of the topic being taught, recovers marks the student had already earned conceptually.

faqs.question: Should a Mudon student drop Chemistry HL to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Only for the right reason. The question styles and notation demands are identical at both levels, so a technique problem travels with the student and dropping will not fix it. Where dropping genuinely helps is load, particularly for someone carrying Higher Level chemistry alongside Higher Level biology and Higher Level mathematics, a common medicine-track combination in this belt. Three heavy internal assessments on overlapping deadlines is a real problem. Doing two well beats doing three adequately, and the decision belongs with the school, checked against published university entry profiles.

faqs.question: What does the chemistry investigation usually fail on?
faqs.answer: Scope, more often than analysis. A research question that cannot be measured reliably with the apparatus the department holds, or a reaction too fast or too slow to time accurately, cannot be rescued however carefully the work is done, because the criteria assess the investigation rather than the effort. Design therefore sets the ceiling. One clear independent variable, a dependent variable measurable with available equipment, and a realistic number of repeats is the shape that can score across every criterion. Interrogating the question before the laboratory is the highest-value session available.

faqs.question: Are energetics mistakes usually about maths or about chemistry?
faqs.answer: About sign conventions, which is neither exactly. Exothermic and endothermic signs, Hess cycle direction and bond enthalpy conventions have to be automatic, and a student who reasons them out each time will err under pressure. The repair is a short set of sign-only exercises with the context stripped away, so only the convention is being tested. Separately, if logarithms or rearrangement fail when the chemistry is removed from a question, the hour belongs to manipulation practice rather than to another pass through the topic.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check uncertainty propagation in my son's chemistry data?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the first things worth covering because it is assessed and seldom taught thoroughly. Uncertainties have to be propagated through calculations rather than mentioned in a sentence, and the method differs for sums, products and powers. Working it through on his own measured numbers rather than on a textbook example means the method is learned on data he recognises. What a tutor must not do is supply data he did not collect or write any part of the analysis for him.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics should an exam-term plan cover first?
faqs.answer: Whichever two or three carry the heaviest recoverable loss in his own marked scripts, which in Higher Level is most often organic chemistry, equilibrium and the energetics extension. Those three account for a large share of the losses visible across scripts, and all three respond to practice rather than to further explanation. Low-density topics should be left alone deliberately near a session: a topic worth a couple of marks a paper is not worth three weeks however shaky it feels, and saying so is part of an honest plan.

faqs.question: How does Diploma chemistry differ from IGCSE chemistry?
faqs.answer: In two places mainly. The volume of calculation rises sharply, with moles work running through everything and equilibrium and kinetics adding logarithms and graphical interpretation. And the expectation shifts from stating a product to justifying a mechanism, which is a different kind of thinking rather than more of the same. Students arriving at a Diploma class in Arabian Ranches or Al Khail come from several boards, so the class is very unevenly prepared. Six to eight sessions across the summer before Year 12 evens that out cheaply.

faqs.question: Is a chemistry Extended Essay a sensible choice?
faqs.answer: It can be strong and it is unforgiving, mostly for practical reasons. The research question has to be answerable safely with equipment the school actually holds, in measurements a student can take reliably, and within the word limit. Most weak chemistry Extended Essays are not badly written; they ask something the available apparatus could never answer. One or two sessions interrogating the question before any work begins is worth more than ten afterwards. The essay must be entirely the student's own work, authenticated by the supervisor.

faqs.question: Does the option topic matter for a chemistry plan?
faqs.answer: Enough that revising the wrong one wastes weeks. Schools choose which option to teach, so two Diploma chemistry students in Dubai can sit the same core and completely different option questions. Any paper preparation that includes the option has to match the school's choice, and a revision guide bought online may cover content the student will never be examined on. Name the school and the option when you enquire. It also tells us what the practical programme and available equipment look like, which shapes what the investigation can attempt.

faqs.question: How much does a Higher Level chemistry tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Chemistry sits in the specialist band because credible Higher Level coverage is scarcer than general science coverage. Named IB and IGCSE specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table at AED 200 to 450 or more, while premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. These are published market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level chemistry help so thin around Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Because the local demand cannot sustain a specialist. Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 and Town Square combine a Diploma-age population with no school inside the community and no established tutor cluster, so the people advertising locally are based around Motor City and Dubai Sports City and cover several sciences at IGCSE level with Diploma work as an extension. That is a sensible business model and a poor match for a student at a 4 in Chemistry Higher Level. Choosing by level and option rather than by distance resolves it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write up the investigation if the experiment goes wrong?
faqs.answer: No, and the temptation is exactly why the boundary is stated here. When an experiment fails close to a deadline, the offer families sometimes receive is for someone to supply workable data or draft the write-up. Both are malpractice and both risk the Diploma rather than the mark. What a tutor can legitimately do is help interpret the data that exists, check whether a different graph reveals a relationship a direct plot hides, and coach an honest evaluation that names the systematic error. Failed experiments, well evaluated, score better than families expect.
